Wow, a really big Christmas hit! Dad is retired-twice!-and said he'd love to have some suspenders to wear instead of belts.  Naturally, he gained weight right after he retired, but has been losing for the last year, and he is in-between sizes (I'm jealous actually, it's so much easier for him to lose than for my mom or me!).  So I started looking for suspenders on amazon, because it's my favorite, most reliable online shopping 'store'.  I found three sets which I thought might fit the bill.  Most sets which weren't obviously shoddy had button fasteners.  I don't know much about men's pants, other than jeans or suits (but not tuxedos) or Army Uniform pants (Dad was a Chaplain for 20 yrs-I'm an Army brat). I was fairly sure buttons wouldn't work, especially for his jeans! There was one pair which was 'convertible' between built in button fasteners & removable clamps (alligator clips? don't know what you call them!). I almost got those, but on second thought, figured the clamps might remove themselves from the suspenders before the pants! Not a good result...more like a good nightmare, lol! So I looked at clamp-only styles, and to be honest, many of them looked pretty wimpy!Then I ran across these, noticing the patriotic 'flag' striping first of all.  Then I read the details-very strong, sturdy construction, powerful clips for 'dungarees' (very old style description of jeans :), and a decent price. Though not made in the USA, I decided to give them a try...and Dad loves them!  Honestly, if they weren't tagged 'Made in China', I'd never have thought it! I usually have a low opinion of stuff made in China, but these are heavy duty, rugged, sturdy clip on suspenders with real leather at the back. Dad joked about being careful where he fastened the clamps...his sense of humor leaves a bit to be desired...but his point is a good one.  I think these suspenders would hold up a shower curtain or fabric curtains just as well as jeans! Once he got them adjusted, they were very comfortable, and he has worn them practically every day since he got them.  This company also makes a pair which is identical, except it's designed to look like a yellow carpenter's tape measure.  Might get those for his birthday, or father's day....  The clamps have a nice 'cover' over them to give them a slightly less "utility guy" look.  It's nice, but a bit stiff to open & close at first.  If your hands get numb or are arthritic, you might need to have someone else open and close them a few times to loosen them up for you.  Don't get your finger caught between clamp and cover, either, it'll hurt.  This is not the best comparison, but adjusting the suspenders for looks (they had to be even-mom's got a sharp eye, and the old military precision from years of uniforms causes dad to be conscious of the same thing.) and for comfort is a little like adjusting a new bra.  You want it to look nice, wear evenly, etc. but if you have one shoulder even a bit higher than the other (or other reasons I won't go into here-lol), you have to decide whether it's worth the discomfort. The biggest difference is that the suspenders are generally seen by everybody when you wear them.  I'm assuming any of you who wear bras don't habitually wear them outside your clothing :)  I highly recommend these! If you're looking for tuxedo suspenders, or something for dates or church, etc., these might be a bit too casual, but for everyday wear & casual dress, when wearing pants which won't get snagged by the clamps, these are an excellent, high quality choice.  The price was just right too.  Kinda makes me want to wear suspenders...nah.  I don't like shoulder straps THAT much!

This is a great watch. I bought it as an upgrade to the el cheapo Walmart watches about 5 years ago and have worn it every day since.  It has never needed a new battery and the only thing I have had to do is replace the band a few times, as I am particularly hard on watches.  I love the features on this watch. I use the two time zone feature a lot because we live right next to the CST/EST border and my parents live in the other time zone.  I also love that it has 3 alarms, a timer, and the night feature where it will turn the backlight on with any button push; great for setting the watch in the dark.All this makes for a great watch, but what impressed me most is what happened a few months ago. We were doing laundry and the watch somehow got mixed in with the laundry.  This watch went through an entire wash cycle, then was in the dryer for an entire cycle as well.  I think maybe it was in a jeans pocket.  As soon as I saw it I was sure it would be toast, but to my surprise it was still working and keeping perfect time.  I have worn it ever since and also have a new respect for Timex.  I will likely buy Timex watches from now on.

The FEATURES of this watch are great, which is why I've bought several of them.  HOWEVER, like "clockwork," (pardon the pun) this watch breaks after 11 months.  The center button that turns on the Indiglo light and turns off the alarm stops working.You might think I just got a bad model.  It happens.  HOWEVER, every single Expedition I have purchased has had the Indiglo button go bad after 11 months.  Just how foolish am I?  I've purchased 5 of these things.  EVERY SINGLE ONE has had the button go bad after 11 months.  Shame on me for being so gullible as to buy 5 of these.  I've essentially paid $150 for a $30 watch.Forget about getting any service from Timex.  By the time you've paid for shipping and repair, you could just buy a new one.  (which I did, 5 times)  Alas, the FEATURES and design of the watch are great, just what I wanted, but SHAME ON TIMEX for intentionally building obsolescence into a watch that COULD have been a great value and recommendation for the company.  Instead, Timex has abandoned their old mantra of "takes a licking and keeps on ticking" and replaced it with poor service and the intention of bilking their customers.Soon I will be making a video of my shameful watch collection and posting it on youtube.  Amazon should change the purchase price on this watch to a RENTAL price.  Obviously I will be searching for a different, more reliable watch brand that has the same features as the Expedition.Shame, shame.  Ironically, my 90 year old father is still wearing a Timex he purchased in 1960, and it still works.UPDATE: My last one croaked, right on time as usual.  The indiglo light doesn't work, and now there's no sound on the alarm.  Caused me to miss an important meeting.  How is it, that others here haven't had the same problems??  I'm a writer, so I don't mistreat my watches AT ALL.

This watch is efficient, tough, and sleek.  It's not over the top, but it has everything you need.  Time, stopwatch, countdown timer, and alarms.The light is solid, and will stay on if you hold down the button.  This sucker is DURABLE.  I've had one before and only had to buy a new one because last one got lost somehow.
This is the second watch I buy for this same model...I like its color, the screen and its bigger numbers, the dual time feature as I travel a lot...

I wanted a digital watch with a leather band instead of the crappy plastic band that comes with most of them. This watch fits the bill at a decent price. my only quibble is I wish the face were a bit larger so I can see it without using my reading glasses.

The official description of this product doesn't mention the type of band closure, and it is not shown in the picture. I relied on information provided by other reviewers and chose this watch because several of them mentioned the Velcro closure. I never would have purchased this product if I had known about the metal buckle.
summary: My strap has a metal buckle--not Velcro

reviewText: I now have two of these.  My original has seen all sorts of activities including yard work, sprinkler adjustments, digging weeds, and splashes from kayak paddles.  The sharp looking and comfortable band started to deteriorate after several years of sub-tropical sweat, though the watch itself still functioned fine.  The watch face has a few scratches, but then it's seen plenty of action.  Instead of trying to find the correct replacment band and also wondering about how much more battery life I have, I felt replacement parts put me close enough, money-wise, to warrant the purchase a new and identical watch, keeping the old version for particularly nasty situations.  I've read about concerns over splits and other sport applications, but these didn't concern or apply to me.  This watch has also been my alarm clock for work and when on vacations.  It's a good looking watch and a great band, and even if I won millions, I'd still wear this watch.

I have had this watch for over 4 years, and have travelled all over the world with it. I like it because it is slim, and not obtrusive. Mine has been very water resistant ( I have freedived/snorkelled  to 25ft with this watch on (over 50 dives), with no ill effect). I also windsurf and surf with this watch on; no water problems.I have had to replace the band twice, but that probably is due to salt water wear, and rubbing against wetsuits.

Love this watch.  Nothing fancy, but it has all the features I want at a low cost.  This is the third that I've purchased over the years. I purchased this most recent one because the battery was low on the last one and the watch was pretty beat up and abused.  My only complaint is that the "crystal" (hardly a true crystal) scratches easily, but what do you expect for this price?  I like the dark green color of this most recent model and the fake leather band is quite nice.
summary: I like it so much I've purchased three in my lifetime

reviewText: My hubby is hard to please, believe me.  He loves this watch.  Perfect for his daily swim work-outs.  He says:  "It's simple and does what I want it to do.  I like the color and I like the leather band which is holding up well.  It is vastly improved from the previous Timex "water resistant" watches." I'm so pleased that I finally bought him something for his birthday that he really likes.
Leaked after first swim in the pool. My last expedition survived hundreds of swims. Will be returning asap. Not sure if i'll go timex again.

One would think that a watch that is supposed to be water resistant to 100 meters would be able to be rinsed off while washing your hands.  This is not an isolated incident because I had the same exact watch with the same problem.  I only thought it was my bad with the first watch for not aligning the rubber seal on the back cover when changing the battery.  I love the design and look of this watch.  The mode and selection are very intuitive.  The band is not hard plastic (this was an important requirement for me). It is an attractive watch.  I don't even need to check the back to see if it is made in China.  I'm sure of it.  Can anything of good quality come out of China?  How can the label say water resistant to 100 meters? The good news is that the warranty is 1 year.  I wonder how much effort it will take to get it replaced though.  I'll probably get a customer support agent in India.  I'll probably take the replacement.  I don't know why I keep going back.  Perhaps I should look for a Timex Anonymous meeting!

I have had three of these. All of them have lasted two to three years. I am a farmer and very tough on watches. They do not wear out. They keep going until I accidentally damage one on farm equipment.

Bought this watch three months ago prior to a military deployment, used it for two months, primarily to keep time while runnning and doing timed exercises. The band broke right after finishing a run at the loop where it connects to the watch. I've had similar watches in the past that have been treated much less delicately and have had no issues. A real disappointment.
This watch replaces an identical one I purchased about 10 yr ago. Old band was worn out and lens a bit beat up so I ordered a new one. This is a great watch. Survived backpacking in Alaska.
summary: Great watch for outside and garden

reviewText: Practical, inexpensive, alarms, stopwatch, timer, large numbers, appreciated by seniors, what's not to like? Some complained about the strap and that watch was too small. I liked the strap and thought size was just right. Of course, if you think watches are jewelry this watch isn't for you.
I had one for about 2 years and I beat it up but it still worked great until the batteries ran out. It lasted longer than I expected. Buying on amazon was cheaper than at miejer...
summary: Old one died after 2 years, bought new one

reviewText: This is my work watch and is worn every time I am working or doing something that I do not want to ruin my dress watch.
This is my third or fourth one.  I use them till the battery runs out and I buy a new one. I have Rollex and Omega watches but this is my favorite everyday watch.

Love this product it's the perfect size, smaller so its not super bulky and in the way. Lights up in the dark, extremely waterproof don't have to remember to take it off before the shower. Great look and extremely durable I live by these!

ExcellentThe watch has a good price.  It is a light and thin sports watch which can be worn all the time.The watchband looks better than plastic. My last one lasted many years before the front face got scratched.Could not find the watch at stores any more.

All features exactly as described & what my adult son needed. Works great, easy to set all the bells & whistles. Not too large or too small. Low profile allows his shirt cuff to slide over it & leather band is long enough. Another happy customer. Fast FREE delivery, & Amazon donated to my chosen charity [...]
Light stopped working after two months.  It worked initially but has since stopped.  Replaced battery but no improvement. What is the warranty with this watch?

I like a watch that keeps accurate time.  This Timex does a great job, being off only a couple of seconds in a months time. My only complaint is that the alarm is so weak that it is impossible to hear in a room with background noise such as a TV. This may be a defect in my watch only, but it is a defect that is disappointing to me.

I had bought 2 of these roughly 10 years ago.  I coach youth soccer and loved not only the Chrono feature but the timer feature.It allowed me to time players at practice yet also time the game.  It is also one of the easiest watch's to operate.The first one the band wore out and I lost it on a business trip.  The second one I crushed the crystal.  I have bought several Timex watch's since looking for this watch again.  My last Timex broke Sat. during a game so I looked on Amazon.  Son of a gun, here is the watch I was looking for.  There were a couple in the Amazon Warehouse so I bought two.Using Amazon Prime, I received the watch's Tuesday.I highly recommend this watch
I have used Timex watches for years, and have always found them to be tough, waterproof, easy to set, cheap, and well designed.

I liked the functionality especially the countdown timer & the alarms. However, it didn't last. I was just in Mexico & condensation formed under the watch glass on a humid day. I did NOT go scuba diving while I was there. Now, the watch in useless.I would recommend the cheaper Casio which lasted almost 2 years for me until the band broke.

This is the only watch I have and have replaced a few times over the years after scratches and battery changes.  This is not a negative, I travel frequently and the watch gets abused.  It stands the test of time.The only downside is the instructions.  It comes in micro print on a folder paper.  Would much prefer to be given a web link to a real PDF manual.
Shopped this watch on price too replace an older model that had finally given up the ghost.  Great fast service and the best price I could find.

Just as discribed with fast shipping. Timex is one company that is still making a quaility product at a good price. I'm hard on watches working with my hands on cars, houses and just doing what ever it takes to get a job done. I usually wear one out ever 3-4 years which is about how long the battery last so I just replace it with the same trusted item a TIMEX
summary: Takes a lickin and keeps on tickin

reviewText: Love this watch.  Have had an identical one for years that got scratched.  Buying this one because the old one was so functional and I already know how to work all the buttons.

Good price, Tells time as well as one that cost ten times as much. Came quickly, easy to set up. (I'm over 60 and did it with out the instructions). Looks good, easy to operate, Don't know how long the strap is going to last can't tell if it is leather or not but it is pretty thin. This one replaces an Iron-man I had for about 12 years.

Had same watch couple of years ago, got beat up after years of wear and tear.  Bought a cheap look a like barley lasted a year.  It has all the functions I need, timer, stopwatch, second clock and the modes and setting are easy to use.  The band is tough but comfortable and stylish.
Supposed to be good down to 100M..... Just don't take a shower with it on!!! I did and fogged up and stooped working!!!

I have been using this same watch forover  twenty-five years, because it does everything, but can take abuse from an active lifestyle.  I don't need to worry if it gets scratched, I replace the watchband when it's worn out, and I replace the batteries every couple of years when the light dims or the alarm becomes barely audible.  I seriously don't know how many I've had, in various colors and "styles," but it has been unchanged for over two decades, save colors of bezel and watchband.  I get alot of grief from family and friends for wearing a "cheap" watch.  However, this watch does it all, and is a "one watch" for all activities and work.  I do everything, except scubadive, with this watch, and have snorkeled with several deeper than I can recommend, and it chugs along, wakes me the next morning with the three ear-piercing alarms that a couple of wives have grown to loathe.  When I bump it against a wall or workbench, I don't even look at it to see if it's alright.  I set it at work from a GMT/UTC source, and I am no longer as compulsive about it as when I was in the military, because I know it's always tight and accurate, which can not be said for watches costing oodles more.  This is a warfighter, active, let's go, be ontime appendage.  NO Gucci boys or lady-boys, please.
summary: My eight or ninth of same watch...

reviewText: I have bought this model of Timex for the last 20 years. Great watch.  It takes a lick'in and keeps on tick'in. When the battery starts to run down, I just buy another one.

I bought one of these six or seven years ago.  It's been through one new battery, today I bought its second new band, and I have no plans ever to replace it.  The fact that the exact same model (judging by the picture) is still being sold after all this time says something about its popularity and quality.

I've had an older version of this watch for several years and loved it. So when I damaged it, I just wanted the same watch again. This is an upgraded version of the older model and works equally well and is easy to program. It even had  a snooze timer, meaning it will beep again 5 minutes after a timer goes off. I'm totally satisfied with it. It also keeps perfect time, never more than a second off in many months.

I've ordered this watch twice in recent months. In both watches, the light burned out upon my accidentally hitting a second button quickly after hitting the light button. Other than that, the watch is very accurate, it has useful and easy-to-use features, and a comfortable band. Earlier incarnations of this watch did not seem to have the light-burn-out gltich.
summary: Excellent except for light burn-out bug

reviewText: Been using this model of Timex for several years and it's a great all around time piece. I was disappointed in that the last watch wrist brand broke after 11 months. Other than that it's a great watch.

I don't feel the need to proclaim $$ from my wrist, but you truly get what you pay for.  NOT!  This is one of those times when less is definitely more.  I get all the functions I want (and more); I can read the time easily, and I didn't spend a fortune.  Plus, it was delivered to my door!  Can anyone please explain to me the down side?

Within 2 weeks of using this watch the Indiglo (dial lighting) feature stopped working permanently.  That feature is one of the main reasons I bought this watch--so I can read the time in low light situations.  I was traveling outside the U.S. at the time, and continue to do so.  Repairing or replacing the watch while traveling overseas is costly--more time, trouble, and expense than it's worth.  Also, the wristband is already begin to unravel at the seams after just a few weeks of usage.  Timex' warranty information states the warranty is void if the watch wasn't purchased from an authorized dealer.  It appears the Amazon retailer I purchased this watch from is not an authorized dealer, so it wouldn't even help to make a claim for repair/replacement under the warranty.  More damaging than the lost money is being stuck with a defective watch that can't be easily fixed or replaced outside the U.S.  An overall disappointing purchase.
This is the third watch of this model I have purchased. The watches are running strong - bands tend to wear out after 3 years.

The indiglo stopped working almost exactly 2 months after purchase.  Figuring it was a battery, I took it to a store to get it changed.  The tech wasn't able to even get the battery out without causing a tampered appearance.  I also tried and succeeded, but the battery holster never unclipped as the instructions state.  This is the first time I've ever been disappointed with a Timex watch.  I don't think Timex will take this as defective any longer.
summary: Indiglo stopped working within 2 months, battery difficult to remove.

reviewText: I have been using this style watch for many years now. I will continue as long as they keep making it.
summary: Has been my choice of watch for years!

reviewText: I received my first Timex Expedition about ten years ago as a gift from my wife. I was involved in law enforcement at the time, and wore that watch every day. I really enjoyed the low profile, and ease of use. Also, these watches can really take a beating. I have been involved in several physical altercations while wearing my watch, and never had a problem with it. After ten years, and only one battery replacement, I have finally decided to replace my old trustworthy Timex Expedition, with another Timex Expedition. For what you will spend on this watch, you won't be disappointed.
Accurate, easy to use, INDIGLO is nice.  A good watch for working outside.  Has timer and two alarm settings, and more.

everything about this little digital watch works and fits just the way it should.  The interface is much more logical and easier to operate that the version I got about 10 years ago  as you'd expect.  Displays are easy to read with the added benefit of a simple indiglo; attractive in my mind and it certainly looks just like the display and the band is light, easy to adjust, and comfortable even when playing tennis or biking.  Not a lot of extreme features but everything that I want to be more accessible than my smart phone is "at hand".
summary: Well designed, attractive, and exactly as advertised.

reviewText: My husband loves this watch.  He is very hard on watches, but insists on buying this same watch each time a new one is needed.  Don't get me wrong, the watch has NEVER failed, but the face gets very scratched up because of his work.  Comfortable band.

I got this for my husband who works construction and needs a watch that will hold up in the conditions.  Compared to the Timex Ironman, which he has also used, the band on this one isn't as strong, but can easily be changed.  I like the price of this better.  A good watch that will last a long time.
This is my 3rd or fourth one of these. I use them for physical work around the farm. I have dress watches but they won't put up with the abuse.

The display is exactly as shown, AND the watch keeps great time, but advertised as a Man's Watch when the size of theband and face seem more aappropriate for a boy is the reason for only 3 Stars. You just can not judge size online, so I thought this would be a decent sized watch, but it really is tiny. On the other hand, it lights up great and is waterproof as advertised, so I would recommend it as a great Boy Scout watch or perfect for people whose watches get caught in machinery at work because it is more like a small bracelet.
Keeps perfect time. Feels great. I love how it blinks bright flashes when alarm goes off to wake up. Highly recommended

I think I'm on my 6th one of these watches, NOT because they are poorly made; on the contrary - they have to stand up to 24-hour-a-day use and abuse and, oh my goodness! how they do that! I actually keep an extra on hand just in case I manage to destroy the one I'm using. I have never had a watch so amazing before, and if they ever stop making this model, I am going to be seriously lost since I can't imagine going a day without it. I rely upon it so much that I find it almost impossible to exchange it for a dress-up watch - even for my own wedding - and I was the bride!!!The 3 alarms are vital to my lifestyle, as are the 2 timezone settings. The Indiglo light is essential because I am often working in darker rooms, and I love that it shows not only hours and minutes, but the day of the week, month and day, and seconds. I don't own a bedroom alarm clock; my watch has done that duty without fail since the first one I purchased. The description says the strap is leather and nylon, but it seems to me that it is entirely leather except for possibly the 2 cross-bands which hold down the tail end of the strap.Sometimes the Indiglo button will stop working and the setting-knobs will become difficult to push in. I have found that, in all cases, this was caused by an accumulation of dirt and lint under the bases of the knobs. It is almost impossible to access these areas without cracking the plastic ring around the face, so have a jeweler clean those places when he replaces your battery. (The batteries last for years but, as a warning, be aware that 2 of my watches were completely ruined because I made the mistake of getting the battery changed at Wally World, and the employees broke the 4 setting-knobs when they misaligned the backs before replacing them on the watches. Use a professional jeweler instead. You can also request a yellow Timex return-box from the jewelry counter at Wally World, and probably other places too. Then you can send the watch to Timex to have the battery replaced or any other problem resolved.)
Extremely quick service with Amazon Prime. This watch is a replacement for one just like it that I used for years in rugged circumstances, so I anticipate great service from it.
Nothing fancy but it does have a bit more appeal than the usual Ironman with the black plastic strap. It works like all Ironman watches,solid. Its not a dress watch but functionable and durable

I've worn one of these watches 24/7, 365 days a year for the last 8 years or so.  My only problem with it is the bands wear out after a couple years of hard use.  However, I work in a fairly rough environment and never take it off to shower, swim, or anything.  Since the bands aren't cheap, and after a couple years the face is scratched up a bit, so replacing it is my best option.  I have one that is over 3 years old with a broken band on my dresser, keeping perfect time.My old eyes like the large digits.

I like the two time zones, and keep one set to GMT/Zulu.  It comes in very handy when going through 4 timezones in a week.  A third zone would be better so I could track local time, zulu, and back in the states.  As far as durability goes, some of the color is worn off the buttons, and there are a few lite scratches on the face.  Neither of these is a problem.The major problem is that the Indiglo died after a few months.  My Ironman with the side button still glows like champ, but the Expedition's front mounted Indiglo button got harder and harder to push to make it light up.  It might have been the Afghan dust?  At least with the side mounted button I can push as hard as I like without crushing my wrist bones.  I did like the feature where it continued to glow for a few seconds after lighting it up.I'll probably buy another one, because I really love the two time zones (and multiple alarms).

This deserves 5 stars for the price, features and comfort. I primarily use it during my brew sessions and when I go jogging. It's also decent looking enough to wear for casual engagements. It has both a timer and stopwatch. I destroyed one after 5 years and I'm purchasing another.
summary: Great price for what you get

reviewText: This is a very simple but versatile watch. Third of this type and have liked the previous ones. Works very well as expected and holds up well in everyday use.
I like the handsome style, the lighted dial for use at night, the alarm for appointments, and the chronograph for timed workouts.
summary: Just bought my fourth watch of the exact same type.

reviewText: He needed a new all around watch and is very happy with this one. He tends to be a bit hard on watches, and where others have been banged around and broken(or the alarm gets stuck and you can't change the alarm timer), it is still doing well.
summary: A small gift for my outdoorsy husband.

reviewText: This is a watch I got to tell the time (duh) and for its stopwatch.  It is light and comfortable.  I have had several Ironman watches but the plastic bands cracked and broke or the Velro band just wore out or got dirty fairly fast.  I hope this is not the case on this band and watch.

This watch if fine did everything I need it to do. But the band is horrible, used it for work I tend to sweat a lot from my arms  because my job is fast pace but sweat will mess this band up fast. Even with trying to clean it regularly the thing tore up in less then 5 months.
summary: watch if fine the band blows.

reviewText: I enjoy this watch mainly because it is light, small, and has all the basic features I need. I wanted a watch with a nylon strap that did not use Velcro. This watch feels great against my wrist especially when it is warm outside, and securely stays strapped while I work or exercise.  My only complaint is that this watch is not exceptionally durable compared to my other watches. I have owned my watch for 5 years, and it shows some scratches. The Nylon strap is worn out and faded, but it still works. I understand that this is the price of having light-weight material. I would buy this watch again since it is perfect for my everyday activities and work-outs.
This watch was on sale and got it for a very good price. It is almost exactly like my old Timex Expedition and so I love it. Easy to use and looks so much better than my several year old watch.
summary: Watch to Replace My Old Expedition

reviewText: I have had this watch for about 9 months and have been very happy with it. It is extremely accurate, requiring maybe three or four under 5 second adjustments in the time I have owned it. The large display is easy to read, although the viewing angle window may be a bit smaller than with other watches, esp. in night mode. The band is still in great shape, unlike the plastic/resin bands that crack quickly. There are some small scratches on the face from the times I have occasionally set the watch face down on a hard surface. So that is partly my fault, though a slightly raised rim around the face would prevent it from happening. Having three separate alarms is wonderful. I only wish there was a ONE TIME option in addition to the DAILY, WKDAYS and WKENDS alarm options. Another wish is for the TIMER to be 99 Hours instead of just 24, but no watch has ever had every feature I wanted. And I would likely purchase this watch again.

Lasted for over 4 years.  I cannot think of anything negative to write abut this item. I was going to buy another when the batteries gave out during a business trip but needed a watch IMMEDIATELY.  I never took it off my wrist (yes, slept, showered, etc.) and it was a faithful companion on many trips in all types of inclement weather.  "took a lickin' and kept on tickin'

I wear a Rolex a couple times a year to show off but prefer my Timex Expedition digitals.  Why?  Because they  feature 2  Time zones, an  Alarm, Timer, Lap Counter, and they LIGHT UP in the dark up to boot. I  mean for under $50 you have all bases covered!  I mean Dick Tracy never had it so good.I have 3 or 4 of the Expedition model and I beat them to death!  How?  Washing and working on the car soaking them, messing in the garden and getting dirt on them, throwing them on the dresser etc etc.The Timex motto used to be ."takes a licking and keeps on ticking!"  Believe it!  This is a quality product and is made the way things used to be made "in the day"  Fear not!  Buy this watch!  You can thank me later.
summary: My Rolex Presidential or my Timex?

reviewText: I hope they never stop making these. On average I buy one of these every two years. Not because they die. But because eventually I scratch it up beyond recognition from abusing the heck out of it. For the price this watch is the best. Ill keep buying them as long as they are available

I returned this watch immediately for one simple reason.  The phrase "99-lap counter" in the description was not clear to me, and I bought it expecting to be able to review the lap times.  That isn't possible, and should be made clear in the description because it is such a common feature on sporting watches.  I had otherwise been looking forward to using this watch, and still think it's a great watch, but I need lap recall with the lap counter.

This will be my last Timex purchase.  After having many Timex watches through the years, I was greatly disappointed in this purchase, in Amazon, and with Timex.  The watch is described as waterproof, but it is not.  I never immersed the watch in water, yet water got into the case while I showered and now it does not function properly.  Obviously wearing the watch in the shower would not be strong enough water pressure to break the water barrier seal.I discovered the watch was not waterproof more than 30 days after the purchase so Amazon will not allow me to return it.  Timex will not honor the warranty even though I purchased it just 6 weeks ago since I did not purchase it on their webpage.  Timex insists I need to return it to my place of purchase.My warning to everyone is check ALL functions of any devices purchased from Amazon so you don’t end up with a paperweight like I did.  At least I can use the band on my next watch.

i've always considered timex one of the best watches on the market. this one is awesome. it is bright when illuminated. the illumination button is placed in the front and not on the side which is a smart design. durable wrist band. all in all awesome

I've owned the expedition watch for 10+ years having purchased from stores in all other cases.  I made my first and last purchase via Amazon in May and every item including this watch have failed and were either returned or I've had to replace going to a REAL store.  AMAZON = cheap cheap cheap, rip offs.

I have had this for several years.  The Indigo lasted about a year.  The leather band is fine.  Using this as a running watch has a drawback - it is hard to cut on and off so that you have to be very focused on starting and stopping.  There is a delay of a second or two to get this done.  The start and stop are two different controls.  The good part of that is that you are unlikely to accidentally stop the watch.  I use a cheap watch with easily accessible on/off switch and separate lap timer.  Despite years, I still find it cumbersome to try to use this for jogging.  As to general functions and looks, I still like if and wear it often.
summary: OK performer for most things except jogging.

reviewText: I purchased this watch for my husband who has been wearing the same one for probably 20 years. It has all the features he needs, is not too big, so yes he loves it.
summary: Been wearing this watch for years.

reviewText: This is a replacement of the exact same watch I used for almost 10 years.  Some of the control buttons were getting hard to use - probably due to dirt accumulated during that time.  I was very happy to find the same watch still available.  I'm all set for the next 10 years.

This watch suits me just fine!  I just recently purchased this watch for the third straight time! The two previous watches lasted me about two or three years each. As long as Timex keeps selling this watch I'll continue to buy it.

I first got this watch a few months ago and it worked great! It has three alarms, a stopwatch, the date, two time zones, and a timer! It has a great value BUT it will cease to work if any buttons are pressed underwater. If you want a good watch with nothing too fancy on it then you'll like this. So far I have failed to keep this watch working for more than one month. Remember, "When all else fails, read the directions

I am a destroyer of watches. I use them in outdoor work and they get smashed, exposed to the elements, and are forced to wake me at ungodly hours and alert me of events every few minutes every day. I can kill a Casio of similar price range in a day or two. These watches seem to last longer and are less finicky than their more expensive Ironman counterparts. The watch is soft, wide and leather so it is comfortable when sweating and moving the wrist a great deal to climb or support oneself. The screen is large but attractive, good for fast glances at whatever info is needed from the screen, but it isn't such an ugly monster that I mind wearing it out of the forest. The functions are intuitive and the buttons are easy to manipulate, but I have had not trouble with accidentally bumping the buttons. Chrono lets me know everytime a set interval passes, a counter tells me how time has passed overall, there are 3 alarms that can be set for varies types of days (e.g. weekend, daily), and of course 12 and 24 hour time.
summary: sturdy, comfortable, all the functions I need

reviewText: I have always used Timex. Thought I would get this one through Amazon. I bought this the end of January. Taking a shower and noticed it was  on set time. It wouldn't change from that screen. Then it pops back to the time but you cant leave that screen.Keeps changing on its own. Tried to return it and Amazon says the return time has ran out. Nice guess I better start buying local instead of wasting my money online.
I have had this same watch in the past and wanted a replacement to wear for work. I work in construction and do not want anything too bulky on my wrist.
summary: Great low cost low profile work watch

reviewText: Timex has been around a long time, and I've owned a few.  I remember forgetting to take one off while scuba diving in St Lucia, looking down to see it using its 'Indiglo' feature, and being surprised that it worked at 25 meters under water.  This newer version, the Expedition, is much the same, but improved, with a magnifying crystal that makes the numbers a bit larger and easier to read.  A good buy.

After a few years of not having a watch, I began searching for a watch that met my visual and feature requirements.  This Timex T48042 watch fits my desires perfectly.The watch screen is large enough to easily read, and the layout of it is also very good.  It shows the time in large digits, while also displaying the day and the date in smaller digits.  It has a stopwatch/lap function with a 99+ lap function.  When the 99th lap is reached, the lap counter resets to 0, but the timer continues to time accordingly.  It has a large "Indiglo" button directly below the screen which provides ample light in darkness to read the entire screen with ease.The watch band is very comfortable and has 9 holes for fitting.  The inside of the band (the part that touches the wrist) has a very soft material, I'm guessing that it is nylon according to the product description, stitched to it, which makes the watch quite comfortable.  The outside of the band is a combination of brown leather and black nylon, which gives it a very nice look and feel to it.  The watch head is a forest green and the buttons are a greenish-tan color.  Overall, the colors work beautiful together and was one of the reasons I was attracted to this watch.The watch is not waterproof, but it is water resistant to approximately 100m.  So be careful if getting near water with this watch as water may manage to get inside the watch.  I have not has any problem, but I am relatively careful when near water with this watch.I, personally, have not found any cons or problems with this watch.  It is well built and should last quite a while if taken care of.Overall, I am very satisfied with this watch.  The functionality, colors, and feel work very well together, and it is a pleasure to own and wear.  I fully recommend this watch.
summary: The Timex T49042 is a great watch!!  I am very, very satisfied!

reviewText: I have bought this watch before.  They usually last me about 4 years.  Strap does wear out but I buy replacement straps.  Good watch for the price.  I will continue to buy them in the future.
summary: Times Men's Expedition Green Resin Case watch

reviewText: I have had this model of watch for about 15 years. I had no idea it was still being manufactured. Seven years ago I lost it in a river, amazingly found it a few months later, and it was still working. I have replaced several bands and it is a little beat up, but it keeps on ticking. Just last week it started malfunctioning, but I think that is due to a depleted battery. I *almost* hope it will die for good so I'll have an excuse to replace it! $1.66/year is not a bad price for a watch! I gave it four stars because the face tends to scratch easily. (But scrubbing it with toothpaste or baking soda helps improve readability despite scratches.)

I've purchased Timex Ironman Watches for the past 30 years. No more.  When I needed to replace my Ironman in early 2013 and saw the Expedition I thought, "This is a nice looking alternative."  The Expedition looks nice, but is a piece of junk.  Historically the Ironman stood up to diving to the bottom of pools, steam rooms, saunas, anything.  After years of use they would give up, and I would buy a new Timex watch.  I'd become a loyal customer. So I was fooled into thinking I would get the same quality from the Expedition, but no.  Like the other reviewers that gave the Timex Expedition low ratings, I found that it leaks with just a dip into water, and the band falls apart with just a tug.  I even returned the first one I purchased for another.  Same crap workmanship.  Same results.  I won't even bother buying another Timex Ironman.  They've lost my trust.
summary: Would Like to Have Rated With A Zero

reviewText: I have been using the Timex Expedition watches for years and rarely have any problems. The battery lasts for about 3 years but the buttons used to access the different screens tend to become difficult after 2 years. Overall, it is a very good watch and I will continue to buy more as time goes on. (No pun intended)
I really like the Timex watches but would recommend the version with velcro strap; the nylon strap on this model wears out very quickly (in a matter of a few months).
summary: Good, but the strap wears out very quickly

reviewText: Bought this as a supplement/replacement for the same watch I bought 10+ years ago, which is still going strong but has gotten beat up from very heavy use, including underwater use. I love this watch because it does everything I need - 3 alarms, chronograph, timer, & indiglo, so I can always see the functions in the dark. I particularly like the 2 time zone feature, which is terrific when traveling. You can press a button to quickly check the time at home when you are in a different time zone.
My dad seemed to like it a lot. The color is nice and would go with just about anything. He can wear it outside to work or out to dinner and be fine.

This is a great watch for the money (or for any money, for that matter).My father gave it to me after he received another one. He is a carpenter and used it on construction sites for several years, in all weather conditions.I have used it for several years now as my gym/running watch. It has been drenched in sweat many times over, and still keeps going. I have not even had to change the battery after about 4 or 5 years.Great watch. I have paid 200 dollars for watches that have not been NEARLY as reliable.

I bought this watch retail for $35 because as a clinician, I need to wash my hands all day. The watch is working out alright, but the watchband is lousy. It bleeds brown die all over my white clothes and papers. Why would Timex put a band that does not tolerate getting wet on a watch that is designed to be water resistant?

It is a solid and rugged performer. I've had one for a few years and giving it four because they have done nothing to improve it, while others have added temp and/or altitude sensing. For a watch labeled "Expedition," it should do more than just tell you the time, date, and provide a stopwatch.

I have always bought Timex Expeditions. They're not horribly expensive, but they work for years. This watch has a nice face and leather band, and looks very classy. The leather band is best not immersed in water (even though the watch itself is very good with water), so if you need to use it in water consider an Expedition with a velcro band (I personally hate rubber bands).

I have worn out half-a-dozen of these watches over the years.  Often the watch body outlives 2 pairs of straps.  Once I had the plastic receiving hole for the strap retaining spring break.  When they become scratched to the point that they are unreadable, I replace them.  Overall, it is pretty good when used as a utilitarian watch for outdoor activities and work (construction). It has large numbers so it is easily visible and the backlight is great for nighttime use.  Battery life is good and the water resistance has never proven to be a problem, even when working in water all day and worn during SCUBA diving.  The face and body are not very scratch resistant, so I take it off when doing mechanic work.  The major drawback of this watch is the poor quality of the straps.  I have tried several versions.  The fabric and velcro is the worst, it wears on my skin and doesn't dry quickly.  The black and brown leather strap looks much nicer, dries more quickly, and doesn't bother my skin, but also doesn't last as long.

I love this watch its light and just the right size and shape. I hate big watches. The options are great and easy to use. I lost the first one while at work and got a second the best part they are relatively cheap.  I am hard on equipment and this watch cuts the mustard.

I have owned this specific watch for over 6 years now and only had to change the battery in it a couple years back. I've worn it through: school, work, sleep, shower, swimming, it's gotten whacked into door frames and just bounced the collision off. Any time it gets scratched or dinged, I just put a little elbow grease into it and all the marks go away, and can hardly notice any left behind scratches in the screen. When this watch hits a wall or a frame, the wall or frame is what gets hurt by the whack, not the watch. This is THE BEST watch I have ever owned and will be buying another one now that this watch has reached its limit of my cruelty. The band is amazing and comfortable. The case doesn't detract from the watches comfortableness. This watch is THE watch. Any other I might own, would only ever be a backup.

reviewerName: Norman C. Murphy "Retired Psychologist and Pr...
reviewText: This is an outstanding watch with featurs for easily use, plenty of alarms, chronograph, and timer for many practical and aports uses.

This is my second Timex Men's Expedition Digital Chrono Watch. I still have the first one, which I bought about three years ago, and it still works. I only bought this one because the band on the first one was getting a bit worn and I wanted a new one. I keep the old one as a backup.  These watches last and last. They are easy to use and tell perfect time. I have tried many men's digital watches over the years, but Timex makes the best ones. They are even better than the expensive designer digital watches sold at major department stores (those have batteries that die after less than a year). You cannot go wrong with this watch, guys.
summary: Seriously the best men's digital watch ever made

reviewText: Just replaced my last Timex Expedition.  Love this watch.  all the right features and looks great.  i do a lot of construction work and may last Expedition took a beating until the buttons no longer worked all the time.  but the watch still worked great even after a couple of years of abuse.  So i'm back to get another tough, good looking watch.  Well done Timex.
The ease of access and comfort  of use with this Timex was paramount because, my son is an adult who has Autism. Nothing wrong with using an old friend to tell time by.
summary: My Son Loves An Old Standby

reviewText: This is a great watch.  I am very hard on them and this watch last, unless you crack the lens and go swimming like I did.  The ban has a nice leather look to it, although I am not sure if it is leather or not.  The inside of the ban is cloth, so I never get hot or sweaty wearing it.  I love the large dial with easy to read numbers.  I use the Chrono features when I cook.  The Light does it job with a very light touch.  Over this is a good looking and very functional watch.
summary: This is a great watch. I am very hard on them and ...

reviewText: I've had this watch for about a year now and it's falling apart.  Strings are hanging off of it, the strap keeps falling off and the face of the watch has several deep scratches on it.  And I don't put it through much more than just wearing it every day. The strap notches are spaced about 1 cm apart, which for my wrist either means I wear it skin tight or loose and floppy.That being said, it has been a great cheap "interim" watch.  It's not at all dressy-looking, but it has a big, clear display, lots of features, and it doesn't beep when you press anything (that drives me crazy!).  Also, the watch face is a bit slimmer than other comparable designs (1 cm), and it's lightweight.  If you can find this for $25 or less, you probably won't be disappointed.  If you're looking for a permanent or rugged watch, this probably isn't it.

I replaced the same watch with the new one; I obviously like the watch.  It has the right size and functions for me,and I like the way it looks. I dropped my first one and can no longer work the buttons to change the time, thus when DST arrived, I was out of luck.  It has good life to the battery; the alarm keeps chiming away each day at the wrong time.  So, hopefully it was my clutziness, not the watch that caused the problem.  It has a great looking and comfortable band, but I did find the weak spot is the second loop for the strap, which gets a lot of wear over time.

Love this watch.  I had the same model for a few years.  The light died.  A new battery did not help so I got a new one.The new one is exactly the same as the old one.  It's nice to see a company keep a good product for a few years rather than feeling the need to 'improve it' every year.One bad thing, the same light failed on my new watch after about 6 months that failed on my old watch.  I think it is the button.  Don't know if I'm unlucky or if this is a problem of the series.
summary: Second purchase of the same model

reviewText: This watch has a countdown timer that I use at work and that many watches don't have so it is perfect for what I need.
Don't feel right without it. Gives me what I need and more for a very good price. love the Indiglo!
It works great.  I had a hard time finding one at the retail stores, so came to Amazon and found one right away.  I've been using them for years and love 'em.

I bought this idential watch about 5 years ago and wore it almost every day until the band started to wear out and finally the battery went dead.  I was very pleased to find they still sell this model and it's the exact same one as before. I like the leather strap and the watch looks good, not grossly tech looking like a lot of the other brands and it's easy to use.

This is my 3rd one of these. They last at least 4-5 years. They have all the functions I use, especially the countdown timer. Easy to read in the dark or light. Buttons are easy to push without accidental activation like some other watches. The bands will have to be washed from time to time because they seem to absorb your sweat and will stink if you don't
summary: If they discontinue these I will die.

reviewText: very functional.... too short a time to ensure durability...my last one was the same model and it lasted for years of every day activity including swimming..

I bought this watch because of the cheap price and I do like the size and appearance.  I am very rough on watches and jewelry but I like to wear a watch when I am working in my yard and around the house.  It takes a beating.  When it stops working I order another one.  I have had three and when this one stops I will order another "disposable" watch.
summary: great for wearning for yard work

reviewText: I have owned this watch for several years now. It has withstood severe heat and cold. I wear it as a stop watch when I work out. It can withstand the shock of running and the band is very comfortable. Recommend anyone needing a quality time peace for a reasonable price, BUY THIS IMMEDIATELY.

If you don't need the ego boost of an expensive watch, buy a Timex. It keeps the time just fine and the new band is quite nice. You can give the money you save to a worthwhile charity (I won't presume to suggest where that might be). I once  had a lovely women sitting next to me on a airplane ask if I was a college teacher (I am). When I asked her how she guessed she said it was the beard and the Timex watch. So, (if you are a male) all you have to do is grow a beard and wear a Timex and women will assume you are a PhD.  They should hire me to do their advertising.RSF

This watch is a replacement for the exact same watch that I have had for over ten years.  It has all the functionality  I need with multiple alarms and time zones.I was glad to find that Timex still made this model.
Watch was smaller than my husband was wanting but it only took a couple of days and he now likes the slightly smaller size.  Great looking to replace one he lost that was similar.  Price was right!!

This is the second one that I bought so far, the only reason it's my second one is the last one got lost. I've had no problems with either of the watches, the band will stink if you workout and take a shower with it though.

I own two of these watches, the first was purchased five years ago and is still running in my sock draw with a destroyed band.  The present one has been going for two years and the watch band is looking a little frayed which is why I'm here looking at a replacement watch.  The replacement band cost about $15 and a new watch is $30, so I'll have two working watches in my sock draw soon.  All the buttons continue to work and the watch has three alarms which I set and use as a 'snooze' function when traveling.  Great watch at a great price and the accuracy is excellent (off by about a minute/year on both watches but in opposite directions).
I just wish the back ground wasn't green.  Otherwise, perfect size and weight.  This is my second, the first lasted forever!

Band broke in less than three months. Very disappointing. I bought five of these watches as gifts. Two still have bands intact. Neither of those were ever worn (too small). The other ones were used as daily watches.  All those bands have failed. Very disappointing.

The watch fell apart after 15 months continuous use. I wore it everyday and only took it off to wash arm. I slept with it on because I wake up in the middle of the night and sometimes want to check the time with the indiglo LED backlight tells me the time. The watch also comes with an alarm you can set. Very nice. What sucks about this watch and why I gave it a 2 stars is because it is a watch, therefore it must go around your wrist. But if it can't it's not a watch, but a clock. So now I can't use it for what it's used for. I bet the interior mechanics will still work for years. Why couldn't they get their product correct. Strap started to mold, but I guess that's because dirt got trapped on it, but watch broke at where the cloth strap attaches to metal part. For those of you wondering what to do with your watch once the strap breaks off, you can use a string to tie it through and make it into a necklace. Buying a new watch doesn't justify the price when the mechanics still work.
summary: Watch fell apart after 15 months continuous use

reviewText: I have bought three of this watch.  I buy them because I like the big numbers and the Indiglo.  Also, they keep very good time.  However, I often need to know the time in the dark and that is a problem.  The button on the face to light up the dial gets polluted with sweat, grease, dirt, blood, whatever and it stops working.  The rest of the watch is fine but the light stops working.I never use the chronograph, I never use the time zones, I don't care about laps.  I want time, day and date in big numbers and I want to read it in the dark.  The features are useless to me but the light must work and this light works for a while; until it gets dirty.
summary: Good watch, it doesn't like to get dirty...I do

reviewText: It has a good strong alarm, and the three alarms with daily/weekday/weekend options are very handy. Also not a huge watch, very well-sized for smaller arms like mine. I had one for a couple of years that finally go too scratched up. I replaced it with another, and after one diop in the pool the crystal completely fogged up. So much for the 100 mete, good for anything up to and including snorkel diving!

I wear my watch 24/7 for 7 years, I am a watch's worst nightmare as TV ads used to say " it takes a licking and keeps on ticking"( I'm dating my self here)When the band goes bad, it's a hard decision to make; new watch ? new band?When the battery dies the decision is easy, for $ 30 dollars you can't go wtrong.
summary: I replaced my old Timex Men's T48042 Expedition Digital Chrono Brown Nylon Strap Watch when it diedI

reviewText: I had one of these for many years. Loved it. After so much use I finally had to replace it, due to the face having gotten so badly scratched. I went through a couple bands, as well. I bought a replacement of the exact same watch (since the previous one had lasted through every rigorous trial I had put it!) and after less than a month the strap broke! Right at the spring bar. The "leather" just tore right in half.I bought a replacement bandB003OQ8AS6and they shipped meTimex Expedition 16 20mm Replacement Watchband!! The wrong band that is way too big.Now I have to return the new band, wait for the refund, buy a new band and hope they send the correct one this time. *Sigh* Back in my pocket to get scratched some more; poor new watch.

I have owned this watch for over four years now, and it still has the original battery.  I just replaced the original strap; it started getting loose due to a clasp hole stretch.  This watch has been on my wrist for about 16 hours a day 365 days a year, and I love it.  I can time tasks, set an alarm, and see the time in the dark.  Moreover, this watch is set up to my time at work, and it stays true to the second, even after four years.  I am in true awe of this watch and will immediately replace it with the same once it ceases to work, which should be some time.
summary: Superb Watch After Years of Use

reviewText: Watch good size.  Not very large as most digital watches r today.  The screen is darker than todays dig watch screens.  This is an indigo screen.  Know what u r buying!  BAND IS EASILY REPLACEABLE.

Within a few weeks there were many scuffs on the watch face.  It had gotten to the point where I had to angle my wrist in a certain position to be able to see the time.The leather band literally disintegrated after 8 months of wear.
summary: Not as durable as I was led to believe

reviewText: I have been a fan of Timex digital watches for years because unlike other brands there is a great selection of smaller, light weight designs.  When I obliterated my "Iron Man" recently I was once again in the market for a digital, but this time I wanted something that looked less like a runner's watch and more like a conventional watch with the functionality I needed.I am happy to say, the Timex Men's Outdoor Performance Chrono Alarm Timer Expedition Watch #T48042 fit the bill perfectly. It is small, for those of us with small bone structure it will not overwhelm your wrist, and stylish, it has the functionality but also fits better than my previous digital watches in a business environment.There is one great change from my earlier watches.  For backpacking or any time you need to check the time at night the Indiglo button has been moved to the front and it is much easier to light up the watch face.

Honestly, I thought I was missing something so I read the directions twice. No. I wasn't...there's no indication that you can review split times. After going online to see if there was some other soul that cracked the code, I was disappointed to read other reviews on this topic. Then I actually called Timex because I thought that this was such a strange oversight. NO DATA RECALL. What's the point of taking splits if you can't review the split after the event is completed? I don't get it. I guess that Timex assumes that you will glance at the display during the 10 second delay with a notepad and pen in hand and record the splits as you take them. Well, this watch isn't going to the San Diego Rock and Roll marathon with me. It's going back to Target. Try again Timex. I was a big fan of your watches, but you lost me on this one. Not good. A waste of my time, money, and gas.
summary: No split recall--are you kidding me?

reviewText: I have had this watch over 5 years, but this brand "timex expedition" for more than 20 years. The only time I get a new one is for more alarm settings. This one has three. I have a busy schedule and 3 different alarms (with snooze) helps me keep on time. The battery last long and is easy to change. It's a popular battery so you should get a fresh one every time you buy. When the next watch comes out with 4 or more alarms, I'll buy that too. (hint to manufacture).
Bought this for a choosy relative who LOVED it.  He especially liked the light feature.  Really happy with the purchase!

I'm hard on watches -- They usually get scratched faces way before they stop working.  I buy this model because it has an alarm, 2 time zones, backlighting, and a timer that I frequently use when I'm grilling.I knocked this down a couple of stars because months after it arrived I discovered the backlighting does not work.
summary: I've bought this model several times over the years

reviewText: My husband had one of this same exact watch, it eventually just got too worn...  I replaced it for him, and yes he loves it... but the band on this replacement just did not last very long... less than a year and now he is not using it, and I guess I'll have to get a generic replacement band.. even though part of his "like/love" of the watch is the band.  :)
summary: Husband loves the watch, but the band did not last very long.

reviewText: This watch delivers superlative value for the money. It keeps good time, lights up when you push a button, gives two time zones, and can swim underwater. It enjoys snorkeling and hiking both, and can tell you what time it is even if your spelunking down 100 feet below light.

I bought this watch for the stopwatch function.  It has the option to time "laps" not just "splits".  In the lap mode, it will show you the elapased time for several seconds, and then revert to the current lap time under way.  In that mode you don't need 2 watches to time the same race car/boat/plane/whatever.  I do wish the buttons were a little bigger, and the watchband was not leather.  The band tends to develop an "odor" after awhile.  I guess that's why I have a purpose built digital stopwatch when I'm racing.
The recipient really liked this watch.  Perfect for an active person who likes to be outdoors.  Easy to see and operate.
I had almost given up hope for finding a basic, readable digital watch.  This fits the bill perfectly.  Just what I was looking for.
Looks good, works without a problem.I am not a watch person but I like this watch a lot for its simplicity and effectiveness.

I first purchased this model at a PX in Afghanistan and am now on the third one after the band on my second one (acuired in Iraq) gave up the ghost.  It is light-weight, goes through metal detectors without having to be removed, survives water and sand, and keeps great time.  As a no-nonsense timepiece it can't be beat.  My law partner has put away his fancy, expensive watch and purchased this model out of envy for its utility.  Now that I've retired from the Army I expect this watch to last much longer since its face will not be etched by blowing sand or other flying junk.

This is my third Expedition watch in nearly twenty years. Mind you, they don't break but I loose them. This is a GREAT product. It's good looking enough for every day and as tough as you will ever need a everyday watch to be. You really cannot go wrong here.

I've owned two of these watches.  The first (which I loved, hence my purchase of #2) lasted me probably 5 years, and accompanied me through several scuba dives at 90ft depth.  The second which I purchased maybe 3 months ago, did not survive a single dive to 30ft.  I'm not sure what change in materials or manufacturing Timex has made, but they've taken a fantastic '5-star' watch, and turned it into a watch that's great for everyday use, as long as you're not around water.  They've also lost me as a customer.
watch itself is very good but the strap let it down, the strap lasted only a matter of months before breaking

I ordered this watch from Amazon.  It is supposed to be waterproof.  The first time I showered with it, water seeped inside, obscuring the screen.  I returned it to Amazon and asked for a replacement.  The replacement arrived with a dead battery!  I returned that and asked for a refund.  Amazon then charged me a RESTOCKING FEE!  They sent me a defective item TWICE and are trying to CHARGE me to restock a defective item!  Unbelievable.  Needless to say this has been a big hassle.  Now I have to try to find a way to actually contact someone form Amazon to ask that they refund the restocking fee.  There is, of course no phone number or email address anywhere on the website where I can register a complaint.

It's advertised to be an adventure/sports watch.  I used it for exercise and activities that involved sweat.  After a while the watch band came unglued where it's attached to the watch.  I replaced it with another band and it's fine.  The watch itself is good, though I'm constantly turning on the light by accident whenever the watch is lightly pressed against something.
this is my 3rd timex expedition.  ( over a 20 year time frame)  i wasn't real happy with the velco band on my second one,  but i see they got rid of that and returned to the conventional attachement.
I like the back light & it tells good  time

I've been wearing Timex Expedition watches for a long, long time, and I love them.  Three alarms, great backlight, easy-to-set timer, just generally awesome.This new model, though, it not my all-time favorite.  Yeah, about that backlight?  It would be really nice if the Indiglo button wasn't so enormous that the slightest pressure puts the watch into night mode.  It's still a great watch, but that huge button (the black one beneath the display) didn't stick out so far.Also, I have no opinion about the band--I immediately remove and replace it.
summary: Great watch with one annoying flaw

reviewText: I have been using this same watch for 15 years, replacing them when the battery wears out-Normally 2 years.The Velcro on the watchband wears out in a year so I replace them as needed.I was surprised to read reviews from other Amazon customers that this watch was not very waterproofThat has never been a failure that I have experienced in the past.Clearly Timex has started building an inferior watch and not bothering to test them before shipment.This is a great watch with countdown timer, Chronograph, Alarm, and a bright light.Too bad Timex cares less about quality than in the past
summary: RATED 100 meter Waterproof ! Leaked when exposed to my 1 meter swimming pool.

reviewText: this was exactly what my husband wanted.  Very please with purchase.  We always find what we want at Amazon!
This watch has really stood the test of time.  My husband repeatedly buys this watch. But they seem to last forever, years.  I am surprised it is still available.  Great watch.

I bought this watch 25+ years ago while serving in the army. It has seen more abuse on my wrist than any machine should be exposed to. I have replaced batteries and bands over the years and never has it failed me. If you are looking for a watch that will last, this one will. The only reason I am getting a new one is because I finally ground the lense so bad that I can barely read it. The watch still works! If you want something perfect, good luck. If you want a watch that will take some abuse and keep working, this one does!

I work 3rd shift outside year round so I need a watch that can and will stand up to abuse. For starters the velcro band is very comfortable and sturdy. The watch is so light that you will forget you're wearing it. The display is fairly large and easy to read. Not to mention that the greenish background makes it easy to read even in sunlight.  The only  thing I'm not enjoying anout the watch is the plastic case, but hey if anything happens I won't be upset like I would if it were my Citizen...Anyway buy this watch, you won't regret it.

I have had this watch for 4+ years and it died today.  It appears that water leaked into the housing and corroded the terminals that provide data to the LCD screen...thus making it so a 3 and a 9 look the same.  However, I am confident that this was an old age problem and not a Timex problem.  FYI the waterproof is only supposed to last a few years at most on all watches.1) Durable- It endured a ton of scuffs and scratches on the plastic front and did not hinder the viewing of digits.  While taking this watch apart to diagnose it, its guts are VERY solidly put together...even the battery took a few minutes to get out.  The buttons never started "sticking" like most other (cheap) watches do after old age.2) Sleek- Numbers are large and easy to read.  No watch should be without a date and day-of-the week display and this one is no exception.  The face is MEDIUM sized...great for people like me with smaller wrists (man) or people who don't want to create an eye-sore on their wrist.  The face is covered with a silvery tan paint that eventually flaked off, but the plastic underneath it was also tan colored.  That made it so it looked the same even after the paint came off.  The buttons are wide and easy to push.3)Great battery life- The quoted duration of the battery is only 3.2 years, according to [...].  I have not had to change the battery yet after 4+ years.4)Band - The only partially bad thing I can say about it is that the band is Velcro.  Velcro loses it's "grip" after being taken on-and-off 400 times.  Thus you will have to replace the strap every year or so for about  5-10 dollars if you want that firm grip again.  I still think the band is the best I ever used because it is easy on/off and doesn't snap like metal, tear like leather, or lose springs like those latchless metal ones.  Completely worth the cost of replacement.I am definitely planning on buying another one of this watch.  Absolutely love it.  The fact that it is only $28 and free shipping is even better.EDIT:  I did purchase another one of these a little under 2 years ago...same story...face is scuffed up but display still easily readable.  Paint is just now starting to peel.  I'm also adding info about changing the strap since someone asked about it in the comments.The bands are sold at Kohl's (department store) and I think I saw them at walmart. If you can't find them at walmart or don't have a kohl's, just try various watch stores and jewelery counters- look for them on spinning carousels on the counters. The strap is held in to the body by 2 silver spring-loaded bars on the back. I take a very small flat head and push the spring half in and working it out until the spring comes free (careful because the spring bar will shoot out- replacement band comes with 2 new spring bars so don't worry if you lose them). Repeat for the other spring bar. When looking for the replacement band, be sure to take the old one with you. Some bands have a slightly thicker "stretchy" part than others and this can make it a pain to change out (it's possible though). I think the one I get is labeled as "6-8 mm" but I'm not positive. Thinking about it, 6-8 is the one the "petite" version of this watch comes with (smaller face- what I wear)..8-10 mm might be what comes on the regular version. You then install the replacement in the reverse order as removal...hold the stretchy part in the slot then put the spring bar over it and make sure its ends gets in the holes.PS: The replacement band also comes with picture instructions but we all know given instructions usually aren't very user friendly.Cost of replacement band: 7[...]. Total time to change out band: < 5 minutes.EDIT: 3 years after original review.RE: Can I change the battery?Of course you can change the battery. There's 4 tiny Phillips screws on the back and the back (stainless steel) will come off once they are removed. You might need a small flathead driver to pry the backing off since it is meant to be watertight. It can take a bit of fanaggling (as I mentioned in the review the guts are put together really well) but the battery is replaceable.PS - Once you change the battery I'm pretty sure you can not put the watch underwater anymore. I know you can get waterproofing redone professionally (watch repair shop) though. I'm really paranoid about "waterproof" watches so I never took mine swimming or showering at all. It would occasionally get splashed on while I was washing my hands but that was it.And in case anyone is wondering...I'm still wearing the same watch (second one) with the original battery- 3 years old now.

I just received this watch yesterday from amazon and i really love it. Ive been buying Timex watches for 31 years  starting when i was 14 when i purchased a Timex mercy windup watch. I also had purchased the other watch like this one with the green face and brown leather band(T48042).this past month (which i like also)and really love the expedition series as well and the Ironman triathlon 30 lap watches. To be honest i really didn't know if i would like the fast wrap band because i have never owned one but i liked the color of the watch, the functions and features it has so i decided to give it a try. At first when i got it i wasn't too impressed with the band but i put it on and wore it all day long and it really grew on me . the fastwrap is completely adjustable and it gives you the ability to have a perfect fit band so as a result it doesn't move and stays right in the center of your wrist unlike a normal band that may not fit your wrist exactly right but rides slightly up on  your wrist where you have adjust it back to the center when you have to look at it. the velco is strong and i have no doubt it will hold . I liked it so much i ordered a couple more velcro straps from Timex so Im set  a good bit of time. This watch  has your standard time with the day of the week ,date(month and day), a chronograph, a 24 hour timer, 3 alarms you can set to weekdays,weekends or daily ,its 100meters water resistant , a indiglo light and a night mode when you hold in the Indiglo button for 4 seconds where any button you push with turn the light on and its disengages after 8 hours. also for your information  the Velcro replacement band number from Timex is (Q7B802GZ) and they make a black &blue; leather replacement band (Q7B798GZ).In closing its a fantastic watch and i will defiantly buy it again when this one and my other one breaks.
summary: A great watch for everyday use!!

reviewText: My husband loves this watch!  This is his second ( he lost the first) and had to have an exact replacement!

I've depended on Timex, or Timex clone watches, for decades. This one replaces a Coleman which had all the features I like: two time zones, 24 hour international time, alarm, Indiglo, large numbers in the display, water and shock resistant, countdown timer, back lighting, lightweight and inexpensive. This watch has all those features and more (the watch is smaller, but the display has even larger numbers, has 3 alarms). It comes with a nylon/velcro fastwrap band, which I prefer, despite its tendency to fray sleeve cuffs. The watch is intuitive and easy to set up if one has familiarity with digital watches; I haven't needed to consult the instruction sheet. I'm not a diver, so only need water resistance. And, it was inexpensive, a terrific value!
summary: Just what I was looking for

reviewText: I bought several watches of this style knowing that I would look them over, read the manuels then decide which one to keep. This is one I Kept.I like the vecro band and the 3 alarms. I use the alarms to remind myself that it is bedtime or time to take a pill

I had one of these for 3 years that had been through it all and was still working great but the velcro was pretty worn out on the strap. I dove into the lake one day and when I came up it was gone. I figured I'd get another since it worked so well and lasted so long before. That was the end of April. Two weeks after I got the new watch I was swimming and later noticed that water had leaked in behind the lens. Soon it fogged up so bad i couldn't read it. Luckily it was still within the Amazon Prime 30 day return period. I sent it back and got another. That was the end of May. Now it's mid August and the same thing has happened and I can't return it to Amazon. Hopefully I can find my original warranty info to return it. Mind you I am not a diver, never went deeper than regular diving off the boat depth (10ft max) and never banged it or anything. I assume the manufacturing of these has degraded as it's supposed to be 'water resistant' to 100 meters which is ridiculously deep. It's a bummer that a product that used to be so solid has turned to crap. 2 failures in a row under very mild conditions is more than coincidence. If I don't get a warranty replacement from Timex I definitely won't be buying another after this.

Love this watch.  Summers we live on a boat and I needed something that was minimally waterproof, reasonably reliable, reasonably cheap.
