reviewText: I have used these sunglasses for years but they are hard to find in stores. These are the exact same as what I have used before and shipping was quick. I bought enough to last a few years and keep one in each of my cars.

My husband loves these because they shade his eyes well and are easy to use by placing in his shirt pocket when going in and outdoors.  He likes the grey colored lenses better than green and they fit well behind his glasses.  He has used these for years and now Amazon is the only place we can find them.  Handle with care as they scratch easily.
summary: Comfort; fit and color are great.  Scratches easily.

reviewText: Full wrap-around shading; fits behind your glasses rather than in front.It would be even better if it were polarized.
Been looking for these fro some time .Glad to find them and get them quickly. They are very fine quality

Nothing wrong with the glasses, but they are too BIG.  If there is a smaller size, I want to send these back and exchange them for the smaller size.  SUGGESTION:  Indicate in inches or in metric the dimensions of each size so the consumer can know ahead of time what to choose.

I bought a pair of instant sunglasses at Walgreens about 5 years ago, and have not been able to find replacement pairs since in any store. My order was filled/completed in a manner of days. The product was very well packaged for transit. I made sure to order multiple pairs of the instant sunglasses and am very pleased with the product.

I have bought these instant sunglasses for years from where I bought my glasses.  I no longer get my glasses there and my eye doctor does not sell these.  I love them for the fact that they are easy to slip on with one hand and they wrap around the sides blocking out most of the bright sun light.
I have several of these. I only wish the smaller size was available in grey, but still love them. x
They work great.
They were as advertised and work great. The only thing that you could do better is to make them concave so they don't touch your eyelashes.
summary: Work great. threw away all my sunglasses. put a couple pair in the car and am never without complete coverage even from the side

reviewText: I was a bit concerned because the size was "large" and I was buying for my Old Mother. They fit perfectly and she is happy -- not small feat. Thank you so much!!
summary: Great price and just what my mom needed. Thanks!!!

reviewText: This is my third Vibralite 2 (in a 5 year period) which I use primarily for the countdown timer. However, I noticed the following changes from the previous models:1) there are no 10 and 5 minute remaining time warnings, which for my usage is an improvement, since I didn't need them;2) when resetting for another countdown session, it defaults to the last setting rather than 0, a feature similar to one found in the Vibralite 3, but which does not automatically restart and requires pressing the start/stop button. Again, for my requirements this is an improvement.Next time: Now that Android watches are becoming available, I doubt that I will purchase this product again. Perhaps Vibralite will develop an Android version.
summary: 2014 New feature or failure of countdown timer?

reviewText: Vibrates fine.Alarm is fine.But I want it to vibrate me every 20 minutes.You have to set 20 minutes in the countdown timer and then it goes to 0. Then you have to painfully set 20 minutes again. You can't even hit start again.Vibralite 3 does this and even automatically restarts but unfortunately it wasn't clear for Vibralite 2.
This version of the Vibralite series is very easy to use and has all the functions I need to be awakened gently by the two alarms with the vibration mode.  Others sleeping nearby don't even hear it.

It does what I bought it for, and it does it well, so it gets 3 stars.  I bought this watch so I could wear earplugs and still wake up to an alarm.However, the design is not elegant.  As one other reviewer noted (possibly for the vibralite 3), it is way too easy to turn the vibrate feature off - a single button changes between vibrate/beep/silence modes.  However, it doesn't seem like I can accidently hit this button, so it is forgivable, though worrying.An example of the rough design is function of the button that changes vibrate/beep/silence modes.  It has four settings: beep, vibrate, beep&vibrate;, and off.  When cycling through these modes, the watch vibrates & beeps for vibrate & beep mode, BUT ONLY WHEN TURNING THIS MODE OFF!  It would make sense (and I believe this was the intention of the designers) if when you turn on vibrate mode, it vibrates to confirm this.  But it only vibrates to confirm that you have just turned vibrate mode OFF.  Fortunately, there is a visual indicator to indicate the mode, so this is only disappointing, and not disastrous.There are other annoying things that standard digital watches have had right for many years, like:After using a different function (like stopwatch), mode button takes you right back to time display.When I turn on the light, it turns off as soon as I press any button - so forget about trying to set the watch in the dark - EVERY button turns the light off.I'm guess they were first to market with this concept, because I couldn't find any competitors at all.Bottom line, without competition, I would still buy this watch.
summary: Vibrating alarm feature works great, but rough design.

reviewText: If you are planning to use this watch for a recurring countdown timer for medical purposes, move on to another model.  This one has a countdown timer, but it only runs once and must be continually reset.  The product description is misleading for this model.  Beyond that, it works well.
summary: Does Not Auto-Repeat the Countdown Timer Despite Claims

reviewText: My husband is a pilot who flies international.  He needed a silent alarm to wake him up when he took his turn napping on the plane to Europe.  After using this watch several times now for this purpose, he couldn't be happier.  The vibration is strong enough to wake him without waking anyone else.  And he likes that it is easy to turn off.  The design is simple enough that it is fine to wear with his uniform.  Since it arrived quickly after ordering, well-packaged and in perfect condition, we are both very pleased!

This was the same model of a Vibralite 2 that I have used for a few years. I had to replace it because it no longer held the wristband clip because of deterioration of the plastic housing. It still functions fine.I need a vibratory watch because I can no longer hear the alarm frequencies. This watch exceeds my expectations.

I have to get up early for rowing practice and my husband is a light sleeper, so this product has been great to have.  The watch itself is ugly and rather big and clunky -- I would not wear it around town or anything -- but it works well.  I have never accidentally switched it off by pressing the button.  I do use a backup alarm, but have never had to use it because the vibrating alarm failed.  Try it.

This item just arrived yesterday and I am very disappionted.The watchband is very rigid, rather uncomfortable, and bites or digs into any loose skin one may have on their wrist; over time I could imagine it becoming more supple, but it is made of cheap 'sneaker sole' rubber so I doubt it.The vibrating alarm is not very strong, and the duration is only 20 seconds.  Although there are two alarms that could be set to go off a minute or two apart I found that if the watch is worn too tightly or too loosely the vibrations seems to get dampened.  My comforter, with the watch worn loosely, seemed to absorb most of the vibration.This item may be good if used for medication reminders or some other use for the waking hours, but it is by no means an alarm clock, (placing an old cell phone under the covers would be more effective) and I would suggest expecting to invest in a new band if it is to be worn for any length of time.Unfortunately I purchased this item through a 'sponsored link' (eseasongear.com) and not an Amazon vendor.  I failed to read the 'terms and conditions' which state that any opened item is not returnable. I guess I need to be more careful with whom I do business in the future, and to remember BUYER BEWARE...
summary: Vibralite2 - Not for waking up even light sleepers

reviewText: I bought this originally 2 years ago for a trip to europe so I could sleep with ear plugs in a hostel and still wake up on time. It serves this function quite well. What the others have said about the design flaws are true, but not fatal errors.I still use this watch as an alarm on a regular basis. It is pretty big, and if I tighten it to the smallest hole it still moves around a bit on my wrist. It isn't so loose, however, that I can't feel the vibration. The vibration is also really loud. if you were using it because you didn't want to wake another person in the room, it might not work for that purpose.I've had it for 2 years now and it's still going strong. Good watch that does what it says it does.
summary: wakes me up, which is what I wanted it for

reviewText: It is a great watch but the vibrate alarm can be shut off by any button.  I use it to wake me in the morning and if you hit the wronge button it won't wake you again.

I like it, it vibrates quite hard, has always woken me up (and not my wife).  And it doesn't deactivate if you push the shutoff buttons before the alarm goes off, as one reader wrote, as long as you have it on the right setting.  However, the digital face is extremely hard to read because the lettering is so small.  I literally had to use a magnifying glass to set mine.  Setting the alarm is also pretty complicated.  But in terms of the vibration, it's great.
summary: Vibralite 2 works well, hard to read

reviewText: My boyfriend is a pilot and this watch is the newest latest greatest product that all his pilot buddies are getting. We are happy with it so far. The only problem that we have with it is that the buttons are hard to push. When you are turning off an alarm every fifteen minutes this can be a real pain. I am sure that it would cause problems with someone who does not have a lot of strength in their hands.There is also an alarm function that this watch is suppose to have that it just does not. I cannot remember the specifics (the watch is currently with my boyfriend doing rescue missions in Louisiana).We have looked at other products and despite the small issues that we have had with it, this one was by the best. The vibrating alert that can be set at so many different intervals really makes this product stand out.

Postive: It wakes me up without waking my wife up.Negative: After I changed the battery it had a tendency to leak and then not work properly. I have replaced the plastic watch band three times.Overall: Useful

My girlfriend bought me the stainless Vibralite3 watch as a gift. I am a pilot and I wanted to have a watch that would have the silent vibrating alarms, as audible timer alarms (used for holding procedures) are rather inaudible in a noisy airplane.The watch fell apart - the face bezel came unscrewed and then fell off. Before it fell off, it was just loose enough to make an audible rattling sound whenever the watch vibrated. The vibrations were strong enough, but the buttons were extremely hard to push and had no feel to them. Also, I never got the automatic 'flick of the wrist' light function to work. Night-owls, don't bother: whenever you push a button it turns off the night-light so you can't see what's happening!!!I'm looking for a new vibrating watch - perhaps a Casio G- Shock. Hopefully someone at Timex finally gets the idea to start producing a vibrating digital watch.-Danny V. ON, Canada
summary: A Pilot Says "Great Idea, Poorly Implemented"

reviewText: I bought this watch because I needed a dual-alarm watch to remind my wife to take medication twice a day while we traveled.With sound vibration and light options the alarm can be discrete (vib) or very noticeable - all three.  The 24-hour countdown feature also sets off the alarm and automatically resets.  With a little planning you can set the dual alarms and the countdown timer and get as many alarm reminders as you need per day.I thought that using the vibe feature twice a day every day would eat batteries, but I have had the watch 1 3/4 years now and the battery is finally getting a little weak.  The water resistant feature works, I've accidently dunked the watch a few time.  Now to clean it I put it under the faucet.  The only drawbacks are that the watch is big and with time the silver coating wears off to reveal a whit plastic underneath.  It's not too noticable.  It is perfect for my needs and I highly recommend it.

I am very happy with this watch as it has exactly everything that I needed. The best part is that it has auto-countdown timer that works without any hassle.  I use it mainly for daily medication (multiple dose) reminder and it works wonderfully with its built-in vibration mode.  The timer warns you twice, with a single vibe (or beep), before going off when it reaches the end time: First, at 10 minutes prior, then at 5 minutes prior and finally going off at the 0.  It resets the countdown automatically as set before right then without you having to do anything (except maybe stop the vibration/beeping with one touch before it stops automatically).  And if you wanted to reset the timer for the next reminder soon after finishing the activity you are using the timer for, it's easily done manually.It's handsome in looks. Has indigo background as the light feature. With 2nd zone clock, it's very handy when travelling without having to change the main clock.Perfect for those who need silent reminders throughout the day and have hearing impairment, or do not want to disturb others with beeps.  Works wonderfully for medicine reminders with multiple doses throughout the day.  It also has two separate alarm clocks.
summary: Great product at a great price!

reviewText: These seem to be made much bigger but it worked for what I needed.
Great suit,excellent valueLandscaper and outdoorsman keeps me completely dryRuns a little big to fit over clothingWould highly recommend
Light, stops wind, not real rugged and no pockets, but does keep you dry even in heavy rain. So I recommend them
This suit came "as shown" on site (color, size). I've only gotten to try out the jacket and it works great!

The Frogg Toggs work well.  I'm dry as can be during rainy camping outings.  The only issue I have is no jacket pockets.  Often I just wear the jacket and it is a nuisance not to have pockets to put my hands in or items in. Same with the pants, although there are pass through pockets when I wear pockeless shorts during warm , rainy weather no pockets! Otherwise a terrific product at a fair price.
My son took the rain coat on a trip to Brazil and found it quite useful.  The lightweight garment fit nicely into the luggage weight requirements for the trip.
the suit was just what i needed. it was cold and raining this morning ,i put the suit on and made it to work dry and not so cold, cause the suit killed most of the wind.

The Frogg Toggs are well made and hopefully will do the job..just looking for something to keep my dry in sudden rain storm.  Was looking  for them to pack into smaller bundle.  Read all the reviews and this wasn't mentioned.  Ordered a small, and it is plenty big to cover anything that I might be wearing.  I was concerned as I am  5 lbs. over the weight for a small.

On the positive side, this suit kept me clean and dry during a very wet camping trip.  The negatives were 1.)  Sitting by and campfire led to the pants melting around the knees.  2.) It is not very durable as sitting on rough surfaces or walking thru brush caused tears in the suit.  3.)  There are no pockets in the jacket.  There should be!  4.)  There are only through pockets in the pants.  Who wants an opening to the inside on a rainsuit?  Pants pockets would be a better option.

This suit is not as easy to put on as my other frogg togg suits, but its bright color is the main reason for buying it. I am out on a CDL range with beginner drivers around, so I wanted them to see me. It works great, just like the ones we use for our motorcyles, but the fasteners are just seem to be over-engineered. I highly recommend Frogg Toggs to anyone who has to be out in the weather, especially in hot climates. Even if you get wet, then put them on, they breathe enough that you can actually dry out under them. You don't feel like you are trapped in a sauna.
Great fit and kept me completely dry during a rain storm. I would recommend to any one who has to who has to work out in the rain.

My husband had a pair of these and the zipper broke.  I got ready to buy a good rain suit and thought it was probably just a fluke about the zipper.  BUT - the third time I wore mine, the zipper on MY jacket broke.Loved them at first - they were lightweight and didn't make me sweat inside them, and they blocked wind and water.  Shame about the zipper because it negates all the benefits!I won't buy anything made by them again.
summary: Nice and waterproof - until the zipper breaks.

reviewText: The very first time I took mine out of the package and tried it on, two of the seams separated. I used the contact form on Frogg Toggs' website to request a return authorization. They didn't respond. I then phoned the company. They gave me a second number to call. I left a message there. Once again, no response. I won't be buying any more Frogg Toggs products.
summary: Junk, with customer service to match

reviewText: I purchased this rain suit after doing a lot of comparison shopping.  I decided that for the price, it was a great deal, but it turned out to be a great disappointment.  First of all, the material is very unusual looking for being waterproof.  Think fortified paper towel.  I didn't even bother to test how effective it was though because the jacket fit like a hot air balloon.  The chest area was fine, but the sleeves were large beyond reason.  Generous fit is one thing, but I probably could have fit my body through the sleeves. I had to send it back.

Just received a set of the camo pro action mossy oak breakup XXL yesterday. They look OK. (I like the camo pattern)I normally wear XL size, I can tell you that the XXL Jacket is not what I would consider a generous cut (like some of the others may have implied). The stuff sack that comes with it is totally useless since it is far to small to accomodate the XXL jacket and pants (it might be OK for a small or even a medium) the zipper appears to be plastic (at least it won't rust) and the snaps do pull apart very easily in the vertical plane. They seem to be a bit more sturdy in the horizontal plane.I think if you are looking for something for very occasional use in light winds they will probalbly be OK.

The jacket is too short. Needs to be longer, even a parka style with cinching waist would help, just to provide extra coverage. An XL on a 5'8" male and can't sit down with out the jacket lifting in the back leaving an area to get wet.  Can't lift arms over head for any normal activity with out jacket raising up as well.  Cinching doesn't help either.  No pockets in jacket or pants, which stinks but is probably for waterproofing purposes.  The jacket on the zipper also seems to leak pretty bad, left a wet spot all the way down the front of my shirt.  The compactness and weight are great.

Today I ordered a new set in camo so I can use them hunting, but the original set I have in bright blue is still going strong.  I can't believe the use I got out of these for the small amount of $ paid.It's replaced some things for me. Wading jackets, rain coats, and 2 expensive wind shirts don't even get used much anymore.  The pants are fine, but I've only wore them a few times to social events like football games - and they work great. Normally I carry my stocking foot waders which become my rain pants, so the pants don't get used a lot.Mostly I wear the coat - 100 times? yes, at least that many. I wasn't a real believer AT FIRST.  Eventually, I've come to the point above...it's replaced a lot of other gear I'd normally take - and I've come to trust it.  I've never really been a fan of such gaudy colors in the wild...but I got tired of waiting on it to fall apart, so I ordered the camo today...the older bright blue set will go to my jeep full time now, which it will replace a much more expensive goretex paclite jacket there too...and the whole blue suit will take up less room and weigh less than the Lowe Alpline jacket by itself.This is one of those things I just accept - like how amazing overnight mail around the world is..or even the internet...this silly fabric seems flimsy and not very durable...till you actually put it to the test.  I've accepted the fact I can't figure out why it's so good, light, breathable, and durable...it just is. And now I have 2 suits.

I bought this just before my third trimester when the back pain from lifting a 30 lb two-year-old all day long became absolutely unbearable.  It wasn't quite what I was expecting, and came nowhere near giving me the support in my back and belly that I was looking for.  It helped a teeny tiny bit, but the construction is such that it just can't provide much support (it's a little heavier-weight than a bra, with no additional elastic).I bought the other one, by loving comfort, and was thrilled.  It's a little bit more intimidating, perhaps, and less, uh, sexy, but it really works in all the ways that this one didn't.  It slings my belly up nicely and takes over the work for my pained muscles.  Ahhhhh.
summary: Better than nothing, but not the best choice....

reviewText: This maternity belt might fit someone else better than it fit me , but it would roll and not stay in place when I wore it. I am an XL or size 16-18 maybe I was just to big for it.

I bought this for my wife to use during and after her pregnancy.  She wore it every day and said she couldn't have lived without it.  She had a c-section and this seemed to help hold everything "inside."  I would recommend it for anyone to use during pregnancy or afterwards.  Great deal too.
Helps ease back pain and is hidden underneath clothes.  Use it almost every day. Would recommend to anyone to use.

Based on the sizing instructions I ordered a s/m. I am 5'1" pre-pregnancy size 8, pregnancy size 10/M.  I received this band today and am nothing but uncomfortable; it is too tight and rolls anytime I move.  I'm not sure I will be able to wear this all day much less find any relief from a heavy belly.  I would definitely recommend ordering a size larger than sizing chart suggests.  The seller shipped promptly, accurately and was timely.

I went and ordered the maternity belt they instead sent me the wrong thing. I contacted them the day my order arrived and told them they sent me the wrong thing. They perceeded ro tell me they couldnt find my order ask for my order number. I gave it to them and have never heard back. Been stuck with the wrong product now for 3 months.

I bought a medium, which is what I would normally wear. I bought it for a race at 25 weeks. It was too big, barely stayed above my hips on the smallest position. The other end just flapped because there is no way to velcro it if you are not that big yet. I'll try it again when I'm bigger and hope it works better.
This product is very supportive to the belly weight. I pulled my ligaments under by baby belly and I was having pain from the weight of the baby belly. I would recommend this product.
The maternity support didn't stay in place.  It kept bunching up in one spot and didn't help my back at all!  I would not reccommend anyone to waste their money on this product.

I got this belt second hand from a friend & it's a good thing I didn't waste my money. At first I thought I liked it until I figured out that it was the thing irritating my skin.  The velcro is sown into the seams so it pokes out causing it to scratch & irritate your skin.  It's not worth the little support it gives.

I ordered this to help support my belly when running early on in my pregnancy in a large. It didn't help any at first but as I get bigger it seems to do a good job. I should have ordered a small size then ordered the larger when I needed it.
summary: Seems to be good (I run and need extra support)

reviewText: I bought this in a S/M at 5 months. I am 5'9" and went from 135-184 during pregnancy. This belt worked great for back pain and belly support. It also helped to hold up my maternity pants that slid down a lot.  I would have loved for it to come in a dark blue as to blend in with my jeans. Maybe they will make that color in the future.
I like it. It does what it is supposed to do. The only drawback is that if its not placed just right it rolls down your back

Very disappointed. I bought this in hopes of relief from pain and pressure after I pulled a pelvic muscle at about 30 weeks pregnant. It has not helped me and has been annoying. The L-XL is too large but the S-M was too small. The material folds and rolls under my clothes and there's nowhere for the extra flap of material in front to go. I get sweaty underneath it and it's difficult to get my underwear back under it after using the bathroom---which I'm obviously doing frequently at 34 weeks! This was the only pregnancy belt available at the shop I went to. I wish I'd had the chance to try on others to compare.
summary: Awkward to use and not supportive enough

reviewText: There were a few things I didn't like about this product. While the material was a lot more comfortable than other supports I tried on, it tended to bunch and roll which meant the full support was all but gone. Also, it was a little larger than expected and stretched out a little. I could only wear it for a few hours a day before it became a pain, but for those few hours it was soooooo much better. I would recommend this product to a friend, and actually lent it to my sister in law.
summary: Worked great at relieving some back pain

reviewText: I don't like that when I put it up, is rolls down and does not support my belly or my back how is supposed to do.

The package said the l/xl was meant "Pre-pregnancy dress size 14-20. Pre-pregnancy waist size 28"-34"." I was a pre-pregnancy waist size 44" and hips almost ten inches bigger. Yes I'm a bigger girl. But this stretches and gives me nice support. I don't know how I would make it through the third trimester without it.I couldn't walk and was super tired and immediately after putting it on I felt better and my SPD stopped acting up. Don't know how I made it through my first pregnancy without a support belt.It fits nicely under clothes. Good especially if you will be doing a lot of running around or standing. I got a little crampy when I sat down. so I had to open it.On another note I also bought the postpartum support belt (same brand/packaging style) but that seems to run a little big! I am returning it because it nearly fits me now at 30 weeks! That means it won't last long postpartum.

A friend of mine bought this item for me and at first I thought that "wasted" her money. I noticed that she bought it for me in L-XL and of course I thought this will never ever fit me, after all my pre-pregnancy size was a 4. Well, I was sooo wrong! Into my 3rd trimester, I developed discomfort in my lower abdomen and back. I decided to try this belt and it was a awesome! I've been able to continue working out, walking, etc... because of this belt. I love it!! My only suggestion is to buy the bigger size.

I bought this belt because in my 3rd trimester I started having back pains, and my doctor recomended a back brace to help.  This gives you NO support.  it is made out of a bathing suit like fabric, and when you pull it tight to velcro shut it rolls down in the back where you are supposed to get 'back support'....(I think I am putting it on right, but then again there are no directions on how to position it on your belly)..... AND to top things off it is considered a personal care item and you cannot return it. BUYER BEWARE !
summary: BUYER BEWARE: no support, no directions, cant return!

reviewText: This product is very thin and stretchy.  If you are looking for some serious support, this is not for you.
summary: Not much support at all.  Don't waste your money

reviewText: Product is flimsy and rolls up in back so its not smooth under clothing. I was hoping for something more rigid as it appears in the photo.

I'm 25 weeks pregnant with my second child and had an immediate need for relief from back pain and pelvic pressure from my growing belly (I actually had to purchase this in a local store because I was so miserable).  In my first pregnancy, I didn't get this bad until about week 38 or 39, so I didn't need the extra support.  2 things helped this time: 1) going for walks or stretching, and 2) wearing this support belt.  Yes, it can bunch and roll when you sit, but it doesn't bother me.  I need the support when I'm standing, and that's when it works best.  It's very comfortable and I hardly notice it's there, doesn't leave marks on my belly or anything.  I would agree that the size small/medium is more of a small.  I'm small framed and was around 112-115 lbs pre-pregnancy and now I'm around 130 lbs, 5'4", if that helps your sizing yourself.  Whatever you do, if you're in pain, invest in one of these belts.  It really helps alleviate back pain and instantly improves posture.
summary: significantly reduces pregnancy back pain, and improves posture!

reviewText: THIS WAS THE ABSOLUTE WORSE PURCHASE. I RETURNED IT BECAUSE IT WAS VERY FLEMSY AND CHEAPLY MADE. OFFERED ME ABSOLUTELY NO SUPPORT AT ALL.
summary: VERY FLEMSY AND CHEAPLY MADE. OFFERED NO SUPPORT AT ALL

reviewText: This item worked ok for me. I feel like the sizing might have been a little bit off on this product. My pregnant belly is very small as compared to most. Someone of normal size would need to get a larger one.

This certainly serves the intended function, though I will say that the velcro could have been a little better placed- I have to be careful not to catch it on my clothing when I pull it tight, and I do need to readjust throughout the day as the material stretches out, so this leaves more of the "hook" side of the hook & loop (velcro) exposed, either on my skin or on my clothing depending on how I wear it.

I'm 22.5 weeks pregnant and was suffering from a lot of back muscle pain caused by a lack of support and change in my posture.  I bought this and was skeptical at first as it is pretty thin.  This IS NOT a heavy duty back support like you'd get from a weight lifting belt.  It basically lifts the uteras and underbelly just enough to relieve some of the pain/discomfort.  I've only gained 10 lbs and am certainly not big, so it will be interesting to see if this continues to work as I get bigger.  But it has been a lifesaver for me lately.The funny thing is...I've been wearing this backwards.  I'm not much for directions so I pulled it out of the packaging and used it the way I thought it should go, which is velcro in the back.  It felt great and did what I wanted.  Once I figured out I was wearing it opposite the way the manufacturer recommended I turned it around - didn't work as well.  I'll continue to wear it backwards and let it relieve my backpain and give me support when I exercise.
summary: wore it backwards for a week and it worked great!

reviewText: If I could have given this no stars I would have. This product in L-XL only fits a pre-pregnancy 28"-34" waist. And in sizes that only goes up to a 18. So now I'm on the search for something a little bit bigger.  So if your pre-pregnancy size is any bigger then a 16 on the safe side, dont waste your money or time by getting this.
summary: not for the full figured mothers-to-be

reviewText: I wouldn't recommend it. As many of the reviews noted, it's pretty flimsy and doesn't feel like it's providing much support.

Ordered the Maternity Support in Nude from ANB BABY.#1:  Love the product!  I'm in my 7th month and jogging almost everyday.  My first run with the product I noticed a difference in the way I feel.  Less heaviness in the belly, less strain in my lower back.  Only wish I would have ordered it sooner!#2:  Fast shipping, got it before I expected to.  Impeccable packaging.  Quite pleased.
very comfortable.

I bought this to see if it would help with my pelvis and ligament pain, but it seems to be more of a belly-supporter, which I don't really need. Anyway, I've been trying to wear it for a few days and just can't get it to fit comfortably below my belly. The velcro is stiff, but not stiff enough to keep from wrinkling and buckling, so it's not completely smooth under clothing; it will also make a crinkling noise when you try to adjust it or if you're bending over. The stretchy material seemed nice at first, but it doesn't lend much support AT ALL.

My wife is having twins and she is 24 weeks pregnant.  The small/medium was too small and the large/xlarge which we ordered is waaay too big.  For all the money Medala makes you would think they could offer more than 2 sizes.  The quality is good, but be sure of the fit before you order!
summary: Too big, other size too small

reviewText: I hated this support belt! It was absolutely useless.  Even when I was hardly showing this "support" did nothing for me. Now I'm stuck with it because it is a personal and health item. So I'm out $40(incl shipping)and stuck with a peice of spandex with velcro on it. I recommend you by pass this product and buy the Loving Comfort Maternity Support which was cheaper and even though there are more peices to it you can actually feel a difference in you back, legs, and abdomin and overall it is a much better product.

This product does not come with instructions, so it takes some time to get the positioning right.My doctor told me to get this product, and said it would help relieve pressure on the bladder and ligament pain.Here's what i have discovered:This band needs to be worn higher than you would think. I thought it would go under the belly, as to hold the belly up (as in the photo). Instead, it works best to use it on the belly (about 2-3 inches higher than the photo).It does not help with bladder pressure at all. If anything, it makes you have to pee more...but you're already peeing so much anyway, who cares.It works WONDERS for ligament pain. Before getting this, I could not function on my feet at all. Walking around the grocery store or down the street, or even standing and cooking for too long in the kitchen would send me screaming and crying in pain. Like super bad stabbing pain that could only be soothed by getting into the fetal position. Everyone told me it was normal...but it hurt so bad. When i wear the band, I dont have that pain at all. i can go for an hour long walk, go grocery shopping, ANYTHING. It's fabulous!It has helped with stretch marks. I think. I say that because when i take the band off i can feel the pain of my skin stretching, which i don't feel when it's on. i'm not an expert on stretch marks.I haven't noticed that it helps with back pain, but i have preexisting back issues so it may work for the everyday person.I wear mine pretty much all day every day, right on my skin, under my stretchy pants (aren't stretchy pants wonderful? The BEST part of being pregnant...). I have not tried wearing it on top of clothing. My doctor warned not to wear it while laying down and sleeping.I also have never washed mine, because I don't want to have to do laundry without wearing it. That would probably suck.I hope this helps. I would definitely buy it again...and it's SO worth the price. It would get another star if it helped with the bladder or back.EDIT: Also, I bought the L/XL and i have a 7.5 month weight of 250lbs. It's huge.

According to the sizing guide, I should be a S/M, so that's the one I started with.  To my shock, it was nowhere near closing...so I changed to the L/XL.  Hey this isn't a vanity issue, I just need some relief.  Unfortunately, this one didn't work either.  It was way, way too big!  I almost wrapped it twice around me and proceeded to do a half day of work at my home office.Which leads to my next point:  this product is not made for sitting, which is a shame, because I just can't take the thing on and off, as I go through my day.  Who has time for that?  It rolled and bunched, defeating the purpose of getting a belt that is supposed to be more discreet under clothing.Maybe I'm just one of those weird pregnant women whose belly is proportionally too big for her frame.  I do get the feeling that if they had a belt that fit me, it would help ease my back strain...while standing, that is.

Tonight will serve as the big test, but I purchased this belt this morning from a hospital pharmacy following unsuccessful amd desperate searches at Walmart, CVS, and Walgreens. I put the item over my a tank but below my work clothing and felt minor relief as my back was already in excruciating pain. As the day unfolded and I adjusted the belt to the inside Velcro tab for a tighter fit I felt major relief. I purchased the s/m and had a pre-pregnancy weight of 107-108 lbs at 5'3" and am 36 weeks with my first child. I gained 39 lbs as directed by my doctor. Most of the weight is localized to my stomach; hence the marked back and plausible sciatic nerve pain. It bunches slightly, but was not majorly impactful to me. I recommend this item.
summary: Grab this if you're in pain- worth it!

reviewText: I've never written a review before and to be honest I didnt read the reviews on this item before I bought it. But I also hurt myself at work and the back pain was getting worse especially going into my third trimester. This back support made a big difference for me, it does work and I would recomend it. I only gave it 4 stars cause it does roll down a little on the sides of the back. Other than that its great and does its job.

I really like this product so far.  I have a condition called distasis recti, which is a separation of the abdominal wall. Something very common in woman but in most women it heals, even after pregnancy. The abdominal weakness can cause a lot of muscle strain and back discomfort. Well, check and check...I am there!  So I order this because I really like Medela's post partum support (and my mom convince me to try a belly/back support) and I already feel more comfortable (I hate when she's right).I ordered the s/m as I am 5'3", normally about 112lbs and currently about 130lbs at 5 months pregnant but all belly and it fits well. Some reviewers complain of rolling but since I wear it below the waist band of my pants, it prevents the bottom from rolling. The top doesn't roll much because I am carrying mostly in front, not so much all around I guess. Some people required more support but this is great for me. In fact have been wearing it most of the time since I received it and noticed a major difference in discomfort from when I forget to put it on. It does do a bit of shifting on mor active days but the pain it saves me from, it's worth it.  A great purchase for me.

This band is a basic band for those needing added daily support.  However, it rolls a bit and definitely does not provide enough support for jogging.  I would recommend the Gabriella for those looking for a workout support during pregnancy.
From the picture the band looks thicker. However when I got it it is thiner and tends to roll up as I moved not giving real support. Very disappointed.

This item is misleading because it runs VERY small.  I am a pre-pregnancy size 6 and I ordered the s/m size based on the waistline.....WRONG!  I am in my 35th week of pregnancy and this thing barely would fit around my lower abdomen.  Not only does it run small, but it also fold and wrinkles anytime I move so it is not much help.  If you are shorter or petite, the waistband is VERY wide in the back and can be ill-fitting (does not conform to the curve of your spine). It is definately made for taller, longer-torso women (aka 6 ft. models). I would go with another type of support if given another chance.
summary: Not the best maternity support item

reviewText: I'm 33-weeks pregnant with my third daughter, during my previous pregnancies I had very mild back pain but never enough to make me feel I needed to buy one of these support bands. But this time was different, about 3 or 4 weeks ago I started having really bad lower-back pain, and 2 weeks ago it got so bad that I wanted to cry every time I had to take a few steps. I was so desperate to get something that helped with the pain that I stopped at a Babies R Us store and bought the cheapest support band they had (the Medela one) without even checking reviews. I've been using it every day and I'm VERY happy with the results, my back pain is completely gone, and because I don't hurt my back during the day I'm sleeping better at night.I want to say that the first few days after I started using it I still had some mild pain at the end of the day, but nothing compared to the pain I had before so I thought I could live with that, but after using the band for 2 weeks (from the moment I wake up to the moment I go to bed) my back feels great, I have no pain at all. I was able to take my kids trick-or-treating last Sunday and walk with them for more than one hour with no pain.I have not had problems with the band not staying in place or bunching up; I was a size 8 pre-pregnancy and I bought the size S/M and it was the right size. The reason I give it 4 stars and not 5 is because you can clearly see the band through the clothes, and also, both the website description and the box description show an "extra support panel" in the middle of the band and it's just not there, the band I have does NOT have it. But this support band definitely works.
summary: This thing WORKS, my back pain is completely gone

reviewText: I read the other reviews and thought I should order the lg/xl. Well, I guess I really didn't need that size, Med would have worked also. It gave me great support and eased the low back pain. I think it works excellent!
We sent the maternity support to my sister and she is so glad she has received it, her back pain just disappeared, It really works, so far :)

At the beginning of my third trimester I started pulling muscles in my groin due to the unbelievable weight of my growing tummy. It got to where I wouldn't leave the house and I would cry everytime I had to get up because the pain was excrutiating. Out of desperation I bought this product and it has made a huge difference for me. I highly recommend it to reduce and relieve back/groin pain in late pregnancy.

I purchased this watch in December for my blind friend. It only worked for 5 months I changed the battery which only lasted 5 months  and the time still going crazy. The blind person is so upset as he taught that this gift would be very helpful to him it turned out to be more of a hindrance. The time keeps going to military time when pressed and the talking voice could hardly be heard.

My father, who just turned 80, has been going blind for 20 years. Now that he is showing some signs of senility, he is obsessed with the time. This watch is loud enough for him to hear without being loud enough to drive everyone else crazy. Wearing this watch, he can sit and listen to TV while checking the time every few minutes. The whole family loves this watch!
summary: I'm a hero to my blind father

reviewText: Didn't get this to wear. Just keep it on my desk to keep me apprised of the march of time.
The battery did not work upon arrival, it was difficult to find a replacement also very difficult to set up.

This review is for the Tel-Time VI, not the only watch that this search engine recognises, the VII. Actually, while the battery held up this watch kept decent time. For disabled folks, it can be pretty important to keep 'systems' in place so that getting around and generally functioning well is not impacted. Well don't lose the instructions or the person that can read them for you; the only place on line that offers them wants you to pay for the instructions, and it is likely that those instructions are for a completely different watch. So essentially your $25 is being spent to have a talking watch until the battery dies. There is no website for Tel-Time, contact is either a well-guarded secret or just isn't going to happen. Economically, if you toss one of these out every several months and have to buy a new one, getting a more expensive watch from another company that isn't in fear of having to back their product with some "customer service" (it is outrageous that this term has become a joke), is a money-saver. I personally recommend almost anything else. Unless, of course, someone writes in and informs me that there is another company that finds it even more humorous to move the furniture around.
summary: Tel-Time DARES you to find the instructions...

reviewText: This watch is very dark in color. Buttons are small, hard to see, and complicTed to use. The readout is tiny and dark  The instructions are also hard to read. And the watch and strap look like cheap plastic. It's really hard to say anything complimentary about this product. Not recommended.
summary: Not practical for people with poor vision

reviewText: I didn't realize that I didn't get the watch I had ordered until the review came up. I received the square one with buttons on the side. It was a very good watch - but hard for my wife to use.

This watch is basically the same watch in appearance as the Economical Square Talking Watch but the clarity of the voice was much better than the Economical Square Talking Watch.  Also the paperwork included an inspection ticket showing that it was inspected on the same date as the shipment was processed.  I assume they were checking for whether the watch battery was still good.

I bought other talking watches which did not please my Dad.  He needed a watch that told the time clearly and loud enough for him to understand which Tel-Time Talking Watch did. I am pleased with the puchase and the price, as well.

The first watch I received was defective.  I told them and they sent me a # to send it back.  No Problem!  A few days later I received a new one and its working fine.  I love it and I'd buy from this Company again.

I got this for my Grandma because she has trouble seeing. The problem is, the voice on it is not very clear at all.  So now, instead of asking me what time the microwave clock shows, she pushes the button on the watch and asks me what time the watch says.  Half the time I can't even understand what it said. One more problem is that the buttons and their labels are super small and hard for most elderly people to work.

Purchased this watch for my elderly, visually impaired mother.  The voice is clear, but the activation buttons are small and she touches the wrong ones when "seeing" what time it is.  I think this watch would be good for someone a little younger who is visually impaired.

I bought this for my wife who recently lost her eyesight and, with luck, seems to be getting it back.  Still, it could be months, years, or never before it's to the point where she could read a watch.  This has been great for her making one more step towards independence after her loss of vision.  These kinds of watches are definitely worthwhile to anyone that cannot see well enough to read a wristwatch.

I work construction so I like the use the Talking Watch at work since its made from plastic and the arm band is rubber, its hard to damage it. The watch has a feature where it can call out the time per hour. I use that feature mostly. It allows me the option of knowing what time of day it is while not having to actually look at the watch. With that feature, I can also buckle the watch to a belt loop instead of my wrist and still monitor the passage of time.
summary: Talking Watch for the Construction Worker

reviewText: This watch is awesome. My brother, whom is currently blind, loves being able to stay on top of the time. It's comfortable and well made although very well priced!!!

This watch was accurate and the voice was easy to hear. The issue was the small button which was too hard for my mother to push. buttons were to small to activate for an older person. When I returned the product with the same message with asking for recomedation and no one contacted me bck
this is an awsome purchase (especialy for those that are blind or have low vision) my only negitive comment is that there's no volume control so it's sometimes hard to hear.

bought for husband, do not buy the zipper slips down and I had to fix and it still falls. :(

The watch mechanism itself is great, but if I can't wear it on my wrist, it's useless.  Although it looks good at first, the cheap plastic that holds the face to the strap gets worn out, stretches, and then eventually doesn't hold onto the face and buttons any longer.  I wear this watch only to the gym, so I put it on and take it off 4-5 times a week, which is apparently too much stress for the watch band.  Because the band is such an intricate part of the design-- the side buttons are incorporated into it-- it can't be replaced. I have to get a new watch.I've had $9.99 Casios that lasted 10 years... For $35, I think this watch should last a lot longer than the year or so I've gotten out of it.  Very poor design by Timex.  (Though very clever that this design flaw is not covered under the warranty.)  Two stars instead of 1 because it was a 5 star item for about 6 months.

I've used this model watch for the past three years of my cross-country career and have thoroughly enjoyed it.  It's very light and not bulky at all - something every runner looks for in a watch.  Along with that, the interval timer really comes in handy when doing timed work outs or when  simply doing crunches.  The fit is so comfortable and does not cut or chafe.  Also, the battery life is outstanding (+ 1 year).Though, I have had a few issues.  I broke off the band that keeps the excess watch strap in place - though that may be my own doing from the roughness of the sports I play.  Also, I've had to return the watch for a replacement due to water damage.  Sure, it was covered by the warranty - but it's still a hassle to deal with if the problem comes up - though, I've only experienced this when steam gets into the watch or while swimming in high pressure circumstances - like when diving.That being said, when I lost the watch - I immediately replaced it with the same model.  If you're looking of a light, sleek, and versatile watch this will definitely do.
It is easy to use and easy to read, comfortable to wear. I think I would recommend it to a friend.

I had previously reviewed my other green version of this same wathc and was disappointed because it fogged up and stopped working because I swam with it with my kids.  I was hesitant to buy another one based on the reviews but I did finally go ahead and buy the black and silver version.  It has been fine through swimming the gym etc.  I wear it every day and it has been great.  No problems.

This watch has a large display and easy-to-use functions.  I get a lot of compliments on the unique band.  It's small enough to look feminine yet still sporty.  I can't think of anything I would like to change about it.

This watch fits just right, with a securing knob that holds the band in place, which is nice. The best thing about this watch is that it's dummy proof - it's easy to operate and you don't have to go digging for the instruction booklet if you don't remember how to do something. The watch will tell you how. I've gotten it pretty wet (swimming) a couple of times, and it still works, so the waterproofing is fine. The size is just right for a regular women's wrist.

I love the watch itself, but will not buy another one because the band just does not last. It comes off of the side buttons that hold it, and thus, cannot be used, or replaced. If Timex would fix the band, it would be perfect, but without the band, it's worthless after 4-6 months.

I've owned this watch for approximately 3 years and wear it everyday, everywhere, except in the shower. Within this time period, I've had to change the battery once.  There have been no problems with paint wearing off (I have the all black one with black/gray strap).  I do have some scratches on the face, but nothing too noticable.I just bought a replacement (same watch, TIMEX Ironman 50-lap) on Amazon because the band on my current one is about to snap. As far as I can tell, there are no replacement bands for this particular watch. I saw this for 25$ on Amazon, so couldn't pass up on this price, even though I know the band won't last as long as the watch itself. I've owned many Timex watches in the past, and the bands always break off at the same location.  I decided this is a pretty good deal (with free shipping). I may pay for an extended 4 year warranty, with my past experiences with the bands. UPDATE, 2 years later the band on this watch is starting to break.06Sept2013: Previous watch lasted 2 years (band is breaking ,and 1 battery change). I bought the same watch today. The band around the watch face comes apart (one of the plastic probes that holds the band to the watch face has broke). Spent 40$ on replacement. Wish Timex would make a replacement band for this watch.
summary: Great watch, but band won't last

reviewText: I bought this watch and three weeks later it filled up with water when I was swimming (definitely not below 100m) and it died.  Now I have to pay $8 to have it fixed and it won't come back for up to a month.  A water resistant watch should be able to be used in water.  And it only was submerged on maybe 5 occasions during that time frame. The customer service representative tried to tell me that I likely pushed buttons while I was underwater, but I know I didn't.  Since then, I've heard other people tell me that the same has happened with their Timexes.

The very first time I took it in the water after it was only 3 months old, it broke. AND the warranty does not cover water damage despite the fact that it is advertised as such. This is the 2nd timex watch that did this and I didn't even push any buttons on it. I thought the first time was a fluke. Piece of crap. Clearly, no one at Timex has ever actually used this watch.

Second update: The watch was repaired and returned with a new strap. Based on the new strap, which is much sturdier, I now give this watch at least 4 stars as it's help up wonderfully.Update: I went swimming at the public pool yesterday and by the time I left, the watch wasn't working and condensation could be seen in it. It's still under warranty, but I now have to spend about $15 ($7 to ship there, plus another $7 to have it shipped back) to get it fixed. This watch has caused way too much frustration!Previous review: This is my third Ironman watch and of the three, this one is my favorite when it comes to the actual watch. (The stopwatch portion offers more options than my previous versions and it's less bulky, so it's a bit more feminine than my others.) But I bought it in January and the watch band  has been driving me nuts since February. The resin that wraps around the four buttons is really thin and keeps popping off. I'm constantly squeezing the band to pop it back into the slots near the buttons that are supposed to anchor the watch to the strap.So far I haven't lost the watch but I'm afraid it's only a matter of time before the band becomes detached at three of the buttons and simply falls off.
summary: Update: Bought in January, it leaked and quit in July. Band is awful

reviewText: I purchased this watch a few weeks ago to do interval running. It allows you to set intervals of different durations and it beeps when each interval ends. Everything works well, the only problem I have with this watch is that the alarm sound is not very loud. It is possible to miss when it beeps if you are crossing a busy road or are slightly distracted. The manual is easy to comprehend and the buttons are easy to opperate. This is a good product for the price and I rarely take it off, it is really water proof.

I searched and searched and couldn't decide on what watch to get. I run about 25 miles a week and wanted something to help me keep track on time to do intervals etc. Plus I wanted the watch to be attractive enough to wear on a daily basis so I would get into the habit of putting it on consistently.I really like the watch. I also give tests at work so the timer comes in handy to stop the testing.I'm not one that uses all the bells and whistles but this one is easy enough to get the items I need going.Plus the the price, I am satisfied.

i work with preschoolers, and i was looking for a watch that's durable and waterproof/resistant.  i found this watch at target and loved it.  this watch has been through a lot of wear this year.  from kids tugging on it with all their might to constant hand-washing and to swimming in the bay, this watch has surpassed my test.  i brought this traveling with me and i really liked the duo-time function and three alarm settings which was good as morning and medication reminders.  the date is always visible which is perfect for a person like me who's always asking, "what's today's date?" and the light function was handy in the dark (my kids loved pressing on the button to see the green light during nap time).  i'm not a gadget person, but i really appreciated all the simple day-day functions that's easy to use.  for those who are into sports, there's a timer and many other useful functions.  only the printing on the face is fading, but everything still works after a year of use (i.e. battery, buttons, light, listed functions).  i highly recommend this watch!

For the first year that I had this watch, it was great. Good features, nice style, no complaints.Then after about a year, the watchband started becoming detached from the watch face! It seems like it snaps on there, but also has some glue holding it in place. Once the glue started to fail, the watchband kept popping off of the buttons - first just one segment, eventually three with the fourth weakening. I had some luck reattaching the band with rubber cement, but it's definitely not as good, not to mention it looks lousy.Stylistically, the non-detachable watchband looks great, but it just isn't durable, and you can't replace it, so once it breaks this watch is useless. I'm very disappointed to be looking at retiring a Timex Ironman within two years of purchase when, back in the day, my Ironman watch lasted me ten years until I lost it.
summary: Good watch, but not the durability I expect

reviewText: After losing my first timex women's watch and destroying my second timex women's watch, I could not find another watch with interval training other than my gps watch. With that said, I decided to buy another timex women's watch. Third time is a charm.

I bought this watch in January.  Last weekend I had it in the pool for less then 15 mins and the watch doesn't work any more, that's only 6 months.  I bought it because I like to spent time in the pool and know what time it is.  If you don't get it wet it's an ok watch.
This watch immediatly broke I give 1 star. What a waste of money! I gave it to my dog. It was not waterproof took it for a swim. borken bad horrble rip off

Short story:  great watch with great features (two time zones, multiple alarms, countdown timer, plus standard stopwatch, time/date)... but the band sucks and is NOT replaceable.Unlike other reviewers, I have no problems with water, even though I wear mine in the shower daily and pool a time or two per week for laps (consistently for 18 months now).  I love the countdown and repeat timers to set my pace and keep my workout moving (or cooking reminders, or naps:).  Indiglo is a bit hard to read in dim light, but lights up very well in darkness.  Buttons are easy to use and well labeled.The watch band, however, sucks.  The sides of the band, where it wraps around the face of the watch, separated after only two weeks' use.  I've re-glued it multiple times; when stretched into place, it stays (sort of), but still pops out often, which is irritating if not problematic.  After about one year of use, the small ring which holds the tail against the watch strap broke, so I'm left with a flapping band--which makes the watch fly off at the least provocation.  And the band is not replaceable, at least not locally.I like the look and function of the watch; Timex just needs to do something about the band.

I'm very pleased with this sleek and contemporary-looking new Ironman - much more attractive than my original Ironman ladies' watch! It also comes in several case/band color combinations besides the silver case/black band I chose. With summer just starting, I haven't put this new model to the water immersion test yet, but hopefully Timex hasn't sacrificed the durability and practicality of the original in this redesign.
summary: The Timex Ironman gets an Extreme Makeover

reviewText: This watch is the greatest watch I've ever owned! Every day during track and field practice my coaches and team mates all rely on the interval timers. I also make use of the watch for swimming intervals, as well as using it as a stop watch for races. Great buy!

update: today is july 5th i bought this in october previous year. for whatever reason the watch went blank. i don't press the button when under water. the face has not been harmed. but it is no longer working. returning under warranty. will let you know what happens. other than this current issue- watch has been great.the buttons are big, but if i sleep with the watch i don't accidentally reset anything. i like the look. simple and sleek. i like the resin strap - i know some people complain about the rigidity but i haven't been bothered at all. when my arm gets sweaty or wet the strap stays put, doesn't rub or get loose.i feel like i got alot of watch for the price - 50 laps plus memory. b/c the warranty doesn't cover the strap or the paint on the face i am more careful with it. i read other reviews that the paint wore off or the strap broke. I haven't had mine long enough for that to be an issue.if i wear the watch too long - say 3 days straight without taking it off, my wrist starts to itch where the buckle is. i don't consider that a negative though. i have to take it off eventually right?i like the watch - i would have given it a 5 star, but there is always room for improvement.
It's perfect in every way, except it broke after a year.  No!  The bit that holds the face onto the strap broke.  Poo.

From the pool, to the bike, to the run; this watch does it all.  Even when not racing this watch is a great daily wear and easy to navigate through all the options.Multiple time zones and alarms make it easy as a traveler's watch and fits small wrists nicely.

Like other reviewers, I've been very disappointed with the quality of the watchband for the current version of this watch. The watch itself is excellent - easy to use, visible display, lots of helpful features. But the buckle snapped off the band within a month of purchase. I expected better from Timex (and have been very pleased with previous versions of this watch).
Watch is every thing it says, but you cannot find new bands anywhere.  Try one of Timex's many other models

Despite claims, this watch is NOT waterproof.  The whole reason I bought it is so I could wear it in the pool.  After only a few swims it began taking on water and shorted out.  I would NOT recommend this watch if you plan on getting it wet.
I bought this watch to play tennis in. It's comfortable, lightweight & cool-looking! Plus, the price was right-Amazon's price was the best on the web!
Got this as a replacement for my other watch. Lightweight. Have had a dozen people ask me whaere I found it. So many compliments.

This is my second Timex Women's Ironman watch. The first I had for like 2.5 years and somehow I lost it during a trip. I like it because even though it's small and light weight, the screen and numbers are big enough. I like it particularly because it has the intervals function which I use for running as I do 5/1 runs. This seemed to be the most economical watch that included the 2 interval function and it works great. I only use it for running and exercising. I have no complaints about the strap or fading as I don't use it in the water all that much, only occasionally.

The watch serves its purpose. The time reads well and it has a light on it, so when you travel and there is no light in the room, it is easy to see the time. It is a comfortable watch to wear.  I would buy again.
This watch is more comfortable due to the band design allowing the wrist to breath.  The style is more femine than most. It has all the functions needed and the price is right.
summary: Comfortable sports watch.  Great functions and price.

reviewText: this is probably one of the lightest/smallest watches with an interval timer feature, which is why I got it.  It's also pretty cheap.  It has a decent number of other options as well.  This particular seller had the cheapest price with the most recent model.  very quality.

I wear my sports watch every day and but it through pretty rigorous conditions.  My first Timex Ironman is still going strong, but the color and some of the other aesthetics have worn off over time.  What prompted me to buy another watch was that the plastic holder which keeps the band close to the wrist broke.  (I have a small wrist, so the flopping band became a nuisance.)  I have been pleased with the performance of the watch and have had no issues.  It's a great watch for the price.

I swam in this watch one time and the watch now has condensation in it. I had thrown away the packaging, so now I'm stuck. The watch is light and nice for running, but not a triathlon watch as it is marketed.

I've had this watch for few years now. I had to replace the battery a handful of times but besides that the watch looks and operates as good as new. Good quality with great design, this watch has served me well through a few marathons!

I have worn Timex sports' watches for several years now.  However, I am now considering switching to a different brand.  I purchased an older model Timex Women's Ironman watch in DEC of 2007.  The band kept popping off the top and bottom of the watch, forcing me to buy a new one.  I went with the T59201, hoping the new band design would be better.  I have had no problems with the band.  It is now the watch, itself, that is the problem!I purchased the T59201 in JUL 10.  After wearing it to the waterpark one day, I noticed water inside the watch.  The watchface became so clouded over with condensation that the watch was useless.  Timex did send me a replacement watch in about 3 weeks.  I have worn this watch lap swimming twice.  Today, AGAIN, I noticed water in the watch.  AGAIN, the face is clouding over.  AGAIN, I now have to send the watch back.  Third time a charm?  I don't think so.  I will be asking for a different make of watch.

I purchased this watch for three reasons: 2 time zones, backlighting, constant display of day of week/month & day.  Did not disappoint. Looks cool. I bought this watch on the basis of the other earlier reviews -- very accurate account of the features and performance.  I wear it for everyday use.

I am a fairly new runner and have been building up my pace and mileage by doing the run/walk method of training.  I wanted a watch that had interval timers for this purpose.  I didn't want to spend a lot, and thought this watch would be perfect.  It's a great little watch...looks nice, has the features I want...BUT the problem is I cannot HEAR the chime  while I am running!  I tried turning my music down super low and still couldn't hear it, if a car drives by...can't hear it.  The tone of the chime just blends right in with any sounds in the environment.  I hate running without music, so this is really disappointing.  I have gone running with a friend of mine and can hear her watch's interval alarms with no problem over my music. I guess I will have to keeping looking at it to know when to walk, and that's what I wanted to avoid.  One of these days I will invest in a Garmin for running.
summary: Bought this watch for the interval timers

reviewText: When you wear the watch in the rain or very short exposure to water, it's fine.  When you swim for a half hour, it leaks through the Indiglo button and fogs up the screen.  The Indiglo consequently stops working temporarily (for now).  I returned the first one I ordered that had this defect.  This issue occured in the first month of use, the very first time I swam with the watch.I got a new one and the exact same thing happened.  Too much time has elapsed for me to return it to Amazon now so I'm thinking about returning it to Timex.  Regardless, the quality-control on these watches seems to have plummeted.  It's good looking but it doesn't 'keep on ticking.'

I purchased this watch at Wal-Mart, and after a month or two the strap separated from the watch on the side of the buckle. It pulled away from the watch where the two upper buttons are located. The watch could be hooked back into the strap; but the strap remained loose and the upper part of the watch separated from it frequently. This continued for another month or so until today, when the watch popped completely out of the strap and was lost somewhere. This is a terrible design and I would never purchase another one.

I've worn the women's ironman for years, but this version does not have a good strap. It pulls away from the buttons and looks junky and gets grimy. And the strap cannot be replaced with other non-ironman straps. I won't buy this again.

This watch is perfect for running or any type of exercise! I haven't had it for long, and typically only wear it during a workout, but it's great. The timer and interval function are perfect, and it's relatively easy to use. I've just started to get into running so I like to set run/walk times and I love that it tells you how many intervals you have done. Great watch!

Great watch in general, however my particular one experienced some kind of leakage and subsequent water failure after 7 months. I swim regularly, but the watch is designed to handle that (you know, the swim part of the ironman). Failure was sudden. All was fine, then suddenly 7 months later after one workout, I noticed some clouding of the display which appeared to be due to moisture. Was gone by the next morning. After the next workout though, display was totally blank and remained so. So, I am disappointed.So now I face trying to deal with the timex warranty (thanks to amazon's records I do have the proof of purchase), sending them my watch under unclear instructions, with $7, to some PO box and hope they will send me a "reconditioned" watch, which may be "similar" to this one, eventually (no timeline in the pdf file). Or I can just buy a new watch with one click and be done.  The real question in the latter case is, will I opt for *this* watch again. Unclear.Good luck.
summary: Failed due to swimming after 7 months...

reviewText: I really love this watch.  It is so light and comfortable that I hardly notice it is on.  It is great for swimming and coaching.  I like how the numbers are large and very readable.  I recommend this for any active woman!
I love the features and slender case of this watch.  It is just what I needed.

After less than five minutes in the shallow end of a swimming pool (just hanging out, not swimming), my timex got water in the face and immediately stopped working.  The watch says "Triathlon" on the face - but it appears it would have never made it through a triathlon!  I trust the Timex brand, so I'm hoping Timex will repair or replace the watch for me.

Don't Bother - Avoid the InsanityI have had my heart broken by too many of these styles of ironman watch. The watch itself is Good, but the wristband does not last longer than a year. Then you are stuck with a watch that works but is un-wearable because there is no way to replace this type of band. NO Band Available.I know because I have 5 watches (so obviously I liked the watch mechanism) - At first I thought it was just a fluke that the wristbands broke. But I finally remembered - a definition of insanity is repeating the same action over and over and expecting different results.Now some of my watches are still ticking away in a drawer because there are No replacement wrist bands. It doesn't matter how great the watch is - if you can't wear it.
I have now owned two of these watches. Neither was waterproof. Both leaked! One watch lasted one swim. The other watch died after three swims.

Returning watch I purchased 1 month ago (water ruined display) even though supposed to be water resistant to 100 meters. In pulling up my order history by the word "watch" I saw that I've ordered a watch a year for the past 6 years. Most have lasted about a year, but this last one only one month. Works well until the display fails due to moisture.
summary: Bought 6 of these exact watches. 13 months is longest any have lasted.

reviewText: I purchased this watch in Jan 2012 and have been wearing it practically every day since.  Showers, swimming, hiking, the watch did stand up (at least on the exterior). I had 3 alarms set a day for various purposes and this little watch was exactly what I needed. Unfortunately, I noticed this weekend (2 months after Timex's warranty ended) that some of the LED bars that make up the numbers have stopped working, along with one of the alarms.  That's just too close to warranty-end for multiple things to go wrong.  I had honestly expected to get 2 years out of this watch and not 1.
summary: Decent watch, only good for a year.

reviewText: I am on my 3rd watch for this model. I would have given up long ago, but the store where it was purchased traded out the watch for me 2 times. I this model. I don't wear the watch when swimming, so that isn't the issue. Everything else continues to work, only the indiglo dies. If it happens with this third watch, I will be replacing it with another brand.

I loved the watch, but recently the part that hooks the band together fell off. I have reconnected it several times. However, it keeps coming a part. I guess I will see if a watch store can help me. I have only had the watch for 3 months.

I've been very pleased with this watch in that it's sporty but not manly and is very versatile.  I can wear it to work or out casually as it goes with most attire.  Since I travel between the east and west coasts, the dual time zone feature is great.  I'm new to running which is why I got the watch, and I like the chrono feature and use the alarm regularly, but I haven't been able to figure out the best use of the other features as the directions are not user friendly and setting the functions is not intuitive.  That aside, I'm very happy with the product and found I got great value for the price.
summary: Great watch with a learning curve

reviewText: Love this watch.  I've had it for two years with no issues.  I had read about the band falling apart and haven't had any problems at all.  When I push the buttons, I make sure to brace my opposite finger on the watch and not the band.  Maybe this has helped me avoid the catastrophic band failure.I use it for both swimming and run/walk workouts.  Love that I can set an interval timer for my run/walk workouts.Will buy another one if this one ever fails.
summary: Great watch for swim training & running

reviewText: There is only one thing wrong with this watch, IMHO: It lasts only a few years before I manage to kill it. During that time, however, it goes swimming, gardening, hiking, camping, and even scuba diving. It gets dunked in the water, shoved in the dirt, clunked with rocks, stuffed in a pack, crammed in a pocket with keys.... I can wash it in the shower or sink, and it doesn't retains dirts or mildew. FEATURES I USE MOST: two-time-zone feature for traveling; countdown for laps is also good for cooking, reminding myself to get up from the computer for breaks; three alarm settings rouses me from my computer when I'm so overfocused that I don't get up the first two times; indiglo helps me see it in a movie or a tent; and I can take it absolutely anywhere without worrying about breakdowns or killing it in the pool. It has also got a thin watchband, so I can get away with it with almost anything you'd wear in the PNW (except an interview). DON'T REPLACE THE BATTERY YOURSELF. You'd think it'd be a no-brainer, but I killed my last one this way.
summary: I'm on my third one: my favorite everyday/outdoors watch

reviewText: I love this watch.  I actually own two of these.  I work in the medical field, more specifically in MRI, and I feel lost if I don't wear a watch everyday.  I have to wear a digital watch working in MRI and I can't imagine that there would be any better a watch than this one for the money!

Works well and is nice looking and comfortable on the wrist.  I've had similar models before, and I've always liked it.  The colors for this one are nice.  The only thing that is a little weird are the buttons.  They don't depress very much, so I can't always tell by feel whether I've actually pressed them or not.

It's a nice, understated watch and the yellow button gives it some pizzazz, without making it look too funky.  I wish the alarm was a bit louder though ... if your wearing headphones and doing interval training, it might be a tad difficult to hear the alarm go off, if you enjoy listening to your ipod kind of loud.
summary: A nice watch ... it counts your repititions when you're in "timer" mode

reviewText: I love this watch for several reasons: 1. I am a nurse and wanted a watch that I could wear to work and also be able to wash/disinfect it. I wash it with warm soapy water after every shift. 2. The display is easy to see. 3. Also, as a nurse it's easy to see the seconds. 4. I love that it has an alarm. I use it for so many things like timing my dinner if I'm busy doing something else and may not hear the oven alarm; I set the alarm to remind my son to take his medication at the same time everyday; I set the alarm to give me a warning that it's almost time to pick up the kids from school; etc. 5. I also use the timer a lot to time my workouts. 6. It's comfortable. 7. It displays the date and can also be set for military time which we use at the hospital. 8. It's versatile and great for everyday use. 9. I had the same watch and when the battery died I took it to one place where they said that the battery couldn't be replaced (don't know if that was really true, I never got to take it anywhere else because I lost the watch.) I was going to get something different but after looking at a lot of other watches I ended up getting the same one because it has everything I need!

I bought this watch 5yrs ago as a way to keep up with my newborn twins nightly feedings.  (which, between the indiglo light and the multiple timers worked very well!)  I wore it 24/7, overnight, and in the shower.  The band died at about one year, and I chucked the timepiece in my nightstand.  4yrs later I started running and wanted something to keep track of my intervals.  The timepiece still worked, so I bought some industrial strength, sticky-backed velcro and a piece of elastic legband from a craft/sewing store.
