I cut out a circle of velcro and stuck it to the back of the watch, stuck a matching velcro circle on the band, and then added some velcro to the ends of the wristband so that I could adjust it to fit my wrist.  It's not pretty, and I have to wear the timepiece on the inside of my wrist so that it doesn't catch on anything, but it's worked beautifully for running all year.  This week the battery has finally died (after 5yrs - not bad), so I will probably break down and buy another one.
summary: A fix for the wimpy band

reviewText: This watch is great, unless you need a loud alarm. The alarm and timer beeps at a very high pitch and not very loudly. It is sleek, comfortable to wear and very easy to set. I especially like the up / down options when setting time / alarm / timer and the "restart" option for the timer. Personally I bought it for refereeing soccer but the alarm at the end of the timer countdown is way too soft to hear on the pitch. So I'd recommend the watch, but not if you plan to rely on it as an alarm clock or timer.
summary: Comfortable, easy to set but alarm is too soft

reviewText: Received quickly from Amazon.  For a button-challenged, programming-challenged person, the way to set starts and splits is a little hard to figure out.  Most of the watches that set for starts and splits are this way. It looks great, though.  I wear it with dress-up clothes as well as when I'm running.  Very light and comfortable.

This watch is extremely comfortable and very easy to read.  I have little wrists and I usually have a difficult time finding quality running watches that fit.  The buttons are also fairly easy to navigate.I have had this watch for about a year and I have super-glued the strap back to the face of the watch twice.  Because of the odd shape of the strap and how the face hooks into the middle of it, it started to come unhinged not too long after I purchased it, but the super glue has helped in holding it together.  I also have never quite understood the lap feature of the watch.  The laps are hard to recall and you have to store them to memory before you see them, rather than scrolling through after you stop the timer.
This watch was for my wife.  She wanted a watch she could see the time and date without looking hard to see it.  She loves it!
summary: Timex Ironman Digital Watch Mid-Size T59201

reviewText: This is my second watch in two years. On my first one, the band broke after about a year. I love the look of this watch and so I bought another one. My second broke last week after about 10 months. Apparently, it is not very water resistant while swimming laps! At first, the display fogged up but dried out after a day or so. When I went swimming again, the display fogged up again and the watch quit working all together. I've had many Timex watches over the years but, am pretty disappointed in this one.

This is the perfect watch for me. I tend not to take it off very much...so works great for shower etc. Also, very comfortable band and lightweight. I have not used the functions very much on it yet. Also like the size and readability of the display. Definitely, a great watch for a cheap price!

I first purchased this watch May 2010.  It lasted a few months.  I clicked the start button while underwater and broke the water-resistant seal.  I was later able to find online that this was a known problem.  I purchased the watch again because I love the look and feel and how it performs when it's working.  I've only had it a few months and did not use it while swimming.  While running in 20 degree weather, the face started clouding over again like the seal was broken.  Since then, the watch has gotten slower and slower and is still cloudy on its face.  Would love the watch if I could actually get it to work more than 3 months at a time.
summary: Watch Didn't Last More than 3 Months

reviewText: I wear my watch during workouts...it's comfortable, not at all bulky.  Great product, great watch!
this watch is not at all water resistant,firstly only lasted 4  months before water broke  it later I got the same watch and it broke after being submerged

This is the 10th Timex Ironman watch I've purchased since 1987, and it will be my very last.  Timex has begun using "chi chi" watch bands.  Well, my wife looked down at her christmas present after only 4 months, and the watch WAS GONE FROM THE BAND!  What a piece of garbage, I'm out $35 !!If you use Timex Ironman watches, you know that the plastic bands eventually fail.  What are you going to do when this band fails?  NOTHING AT ALL, YOU'RE GONNA HAVE TO THROW IT AWAY !!!I'd rather own a happy meal than this watch.  From now on, I'm going to buy the Ladies Expedition model, which uses standard watch bands.  TIMEX THIS IS MY LAST IRON MAN PURCHASE !!!
summary: Nonstandard Band; Watch Fell off; Wasted $35!

reviewText: This is my third or fourth watch of this type. It's a great watch, but the band will fail well before the watch does.
summary: Love the watch, hate the band

reviewText: We purchased this watch for our daughter as she entered her senior year and the fall cross country season.  She finally admitted that a watch could help her track her summer training runs, since she had taken up to keeping a running journal.  The TIMEX WOMEN's IRONMAN watch is easy to use.  She (17 year old) has had no issues or problems.  The big thing with teens is not to look like a geek with a huge ugly watch.  I'm sure if this had a nice pink strap it would have been a home run; otherwise, it's a good option for the girl runner who is not keen to wearing a watch.
summary: Good runners watch for high school girl runner

reviewText: I think 5 Stars describes a watch so perfect that I hesitate with the highest rating! I would certainly give this watch 4.5 Stars for it fits, works and looks very nice on my mother's wrist. She has become quite the devoted swimmer at 82 and before she had this other ugly watch with large display and very cheap looking (probably because we got it for free with one of those magazine deals!). I bought it as a gift but knew better of the many uses she would find for it in the coming year. The bottom line? She likes it, looks good wearing it and for $5 Dollars we have extended the warranty (if anything goes wrong she gets a replacement) for an additional 4 years from Timex (information included on the very large paper that came with the watch instructions). She is happy and when Big Mama is happy all is well in my world. Timex is reliable and the price quite appealing. 4.5 Stars for  the Timex Women's Ironman Triathlon Sleek 50/100 Watch #T59201 (What a Title for such a cute little thing!).

I just bought this watch to use as a countdown timer for sailboat racing.  It is easy to use and read, but what it found out is that the location of the start/split button on the bottom of the face is far too easy to bump.  It was stopped when I didn't want it to be and I had to restart it.  The next time I looked at it it was stopped again.  Not good when you're trying to time something.  I tried four times and each time I looked at it it was stopped.  I think for running it is probably fine, but for activities where it might get bumped it's no good.  I am going to try to take it back and get something with a start/reset button that is more difficult to bump.

This is the most ideal watch. It's slim bands make it stylish and comfortable, its features are easy to use, the digital screen is easy to see, and better yet, it is waterproof so there is never any need to take it off. Because of these reasons, I have bought this watch three times in a row. My reason for needing to buy a knew one having nothing to do with the mechanics, but the fact that I had worn the band out from extreme use I never take it off and am extremely active). I will continue to buy this watch until it no longer is carried....which I hope is many years from now.
summary: Most dependable watch I've ever owned

reviewText: Just contact Timex Group UK. You can send the watch in and get a new strap - much cheaper than a new watch!
summary: You can get a new strap!

reviewText: I bought this watch as a replacement for the same watch that I bought a few years ago.  It has served me well for running and other activities for several years.  Lightweight watch which does not slip and fits well.

This is the third time I have purchased this same watch for my teen daughter in the past five years.  She wears the watch all the time including showers and swimming.  The only problems we have ever encountered were a cracked lens when she miscalculated and hit the edge of the pool during backstroke and a broken band after 3 yrs of nonstop wear. A great value for the price!

I got one of these on clearance probably 5 or 6 years ago and it has been great.  I am just now needing to get a replacement for it and I put it through its paces; road running, ultra trail running, pool swimming, open water swimming, triathlons.  The straps did begin to pull away from the watch buttons about a year ago but that was something I could live with.  Here is to hoping the design and craftsmanship has not changed over the last few years.  I am looking forward to another 5 years with this watch.
summary: Probably the only watch I will ever own from now on

reviewText: I have been a devoted Timex fan for 15 + years. I am on my SECOND watch of this model. The first lasted for about 6 months before the watch part broke away from the band, my current one lasted for 1 MONTH before this same thing happend! I can still use it just snap it back into place but I have almost lost the watch part NUMEROUS times! One time in particular I was on a run and keeping track of my miles via the lap button on the Chrono, on my first mile I pressed the button to log the mile and the watch part popped out and I lost it in my layers of jacket and gloves. I found it of course but added time to my run and had to just carry the watch by itself.Let me say that I LOVE the interval timers and having the capability of 3 alarms and 2 time zones those alone made me buy my second one, I couldn't find another watch on the market that had those features. I have now found SOLEUS watches (they have the same features and more)Womens Soleus 10K Chronograph 30 lap Mid Watchesyou may pay $10 more, but get the same features and hopefully a longer life out of your watch!

I bought this watch to help pace myself for competition runs. I mostly use it to help with 400 meter workouts so I can either stay consistent or time myself to go a little faster. I've never owned a watch like this, so the settings were a little confusing and I'm still getting used to the chronos and lap time settings.Its a little bigger than I expected, but I'm short and petite so most watches look pretty big on me.It's a great watch if you're even just beginning, or an avid athlete.
This watch lasted 5 weeks and shorted out when in water. Do not buy it if you plan on it getting wet other then that it works great.

I bought this watch to replace one of the same model that I purchased roughly 6 years ago, which had frozen up and stopped responding to the buttons. I assumed it had just reached its maximum life span (whadya want from a $40 watch?). But shortly after the new watch arrived, the screen went completely blank, which makes me wonder if all it needed all along was a new battery - if/when the same happens with this one, I'll try battery replacement before getting a whole new watch! Anyway, the first watch saw me through 6 years of almost daily wear, served as my alarm clock, timed everything from runs to restaurant wait times...and never missed a beat. I got this one two months ago, and so far, it's every bit as good as the first model. The buttons are big enough that even clumsy frostbitten fingers can manage them, the controls are intuitive, and the display is clear and easy-to-read. I've seen a number of complaints about water resistance in the reviews, and I can't speak to that - I used my old Timex Ironman Triathlon to time lap swims (on my wrist/in the water) and never had any problems, but I haven't tried it with this one yet. (And if the directions say not to press the buttons underwater, I probably *won't* try it with this one.) I would also agree that the strap for this one feels a little more brittle than the strap for the first one, BUT I haven't seen any hints of cracking or breaking (again: my original Timex Ironman Triathlon went 6 years without any strap breakage whatsoever). I've also seen some complaints about discoloration and the shiny finish on the face rubbing off. All I can say to that is: it's a SPORTS watch, not a fashion statement. Yes, the light edges of the strap get a little discolored. And yes, the shiny finish on my last one (the purple model) rubbed off over time (the silver on the face of this one is a matte finish, so I don't know if the same thing will happen)...it's FAR more important to me that the thing works properly and lasts a long time. Which, in my experience, it does! :-)

I'm on my second one of these, and I only had to replace the first one because I fell down stairs and the band became damaged, but held up for a good 3 or 4 months after it happened. Very sturdy and the battery lasts forever. The only criticism I can give it is that the lighter colored parts of the band discolor after a while, particularly on the inside of the wrist, but for a watch I can wear all the time, I'm extremely happy with it. It's sleek enough that I don't feel awkward wearing a sports watch all the time.

The Timex Women's T59201 Ironman is a great watch in terms of features. I've been buying them for years, but the quality is getting worse and worse. I used to have a problem with the bands breaking after about a year, but now I'm lucky to have one four months before the indiglo goes out. Target keeps replacing them for free, but I've got to find a higher quality watch with all the Ironman's features. Such a waste.
summary: Save your receipt. It won't work for long!

reviewText: This watch is advertised as a "triathlon" watch by Timex. It took on water the first time I took it in the pool! Timex customer service told me that you can't press the buttons when the watch is in the water!Does anyone at Timex know what a triathlon is? I'm sorry, but if you call a watch a triathlon watch it means people are going to buy it to use swimming (getting splits, etc.) and they're going to need to press the buttons while the watch is wet! False advertising by Timex. They should be ashamed!

Love this watch!  I use it nearly every day during my marathon training.  It's perfect for timed intervals, stores up to 50 workouts, and has 3 alarms to ensure I get out of bed and on the trails when I'm less that inspired to roll out of bed.  The strap actually fits my narrow wrist, which is hard to do, and since it's not fabric, it doesn't get damp and stinky after a run or swim.  The only drawback is that the beeps are a little soft as compared to those on past Timex watches I've owned, but overall I would really recommend this model.  It's a bargain for the price!

I started using Ironman watches eight years ago, when I started long distance running. These have all the functions I need for training. I wouldn't be without one. I've had this particular model for the past two years, and my only complaint it that the "beep" for the interval timer is way too quiet. I called customer service about this and they said that that's the way it is. It's fine if you are in a controlled environment, but outdoors, where I do my training, there is lots of other noise, especially from traffic.  The interval signals can't be easily heard. Likewise in colder weather, if I'm wearing a hat, the signals can't be heard. I compensate by glancing at my watch frequently but really, that shouldn't be necessary.My first running watch was a man's Ironman 100 lap (8 years ago)and it was loud enough. The woman's models are not.  Would love if you could improve this feature!

Love the watch design, but the warranty requires me to return it to the merchant instead of Amazon. Due to costs to send the watch for repair, it makes more sense to buy a new watch - but this time not from Amazon. (It doesn't seem to help to pay extra for the protection plan). I like Amazon for many things, but now I've decided to not buy watches from them anymore.
summary: Condensation under lens in less than 5 months

reviewText: The watch is easy to use and works for every day and for tracking exercise. I love the interval timers. Great value!

I just bought this watch and have been wearing it for a couple weeks now.  As a 5'3" cyclist and runner I love it.  Very intuitive functionality, lightweight and the watch face is not big like some other sport watches w. similar functionality making it ideal for those w. smaller wrists.  However, despite claiming to be water resistant to 100m it is NOT water resistant at all!  I wore it on a cycling ride where it happened to shower (not even rain) and after 2 hrs the watch case fogged all up! The fog inside the watch face went away after about 4 hrs but it was annoying.  I will be keeping it since otherwise it seems to be an awesome sport watch but if you are a swimmer I definitely would not be getting this watch until Timex fixes this problem.
summary: Great watch but NOT water resistant!

reviewText: This is my third Timex Ironman, and the second of this variety.  After 2 solid years of wear, the band broke - but I didn't expect it to last forever like a metal watch band.  I went back to this option because of the interval timer, which is essential for me when running (or starting again post-baby!).  So easy to set, reset, etc. once you get past the first time or two - you do need the directions so DO NOT throw them away.  After the first few times, you can chuck them. :-)
summary: The best watch for running intervals!

reviewText: My wife's running watch broke, so I bought her this.  It was well reviewed, and has lived up to expectations.  It did break a week after I gave it to my wife, Amazon is great at returns, so I will not ding the product for what is hopefully a bad watch from the bunch.  I recommend this product, not expensive, and you get a lot of great features.

I've had two ironman watches - I loved the design and ease of use, but both lasted less than a year. My advice - get it if you really like the look & the features, but don't expect it to last.  Like many others' stories, the band on the first ironman broke around 10 months.  My second one just got water condensation inside after 5 months. It was fine with swimming 2 or 3 times a month, then suddenly let in water and broke. Since I really like this watch, I may put up with it a 3rd time at $30-$35 on amazon. But if anyone finds a more durable, lightweight, multi-function, good looking watch - I'll be first in line to try it.
summary: The disposable watch- love it when it works but not durable

reviewText: I love it. It is light weight, sleek looking , comfortable and has great features!

I bought this watch because I needed an interval timer to help me train for my marathon. This watch was perfect. There are probably more expensive watches out there that have more features, but for the price I paid, I was more than happy with this watch. It's light and small on your wrist.

I bought this watch and loved it because I could set multiple time intervals; it was perfect for my runs. Within a week of owning it I jumped in the pool with it, it fogged up immediately. I waited for days for the condensation to disappear, not being able to see the intervals while running. About 5 days after I wore it in the pool it just completely died. I would not buy this watch again, love the features but not worth the risk of it failing when wet.

I've had the watch for 11 months. It still functions very well, but the silver paint started chipping off after only a few months, making it look sloppy and cheap. It would look better ultimately if they just featured the grey plastic and ditched the silver accent paint.

My family and I have four Timex Ironman watches among us.  One by one these things have stopped being waterproof.At first they are fantastic (thus, the number of them that we own).  The features are great and they are waterproof - for a while.  None of these has ever been abused, just worn and never in water deeper than 10 feet (a mere 3.3 meters).  One of them, worn into a swimming pool, came out full of water and completely non-functional.  Fortunately it was under warranty, but it still cost $7 to have repaired/replaced.  Two others are older than one year, but less than two, and have started becoming foggy after swimming (pool, not ocean).  The fog evaporates after an hour or so, indicating that water can not only get in, but that it can get out.  The last is only six months old and fine so far, but I do not expect it to last much longer--it too will likely leak just after the warranty expires.For the cost of these things and the claim that they are "waterproof to 100 m," they are incredibly unreliable long-term.
summary: Waterproof only for a limited period of time.

reviewText: I love this watch.  It is lightweight yet sturdy.  Even I can figure out how to set the alarms and use the timer.  I love that it has a light so I can see it in the dark.  The only downside is that I have to get a new one every 3-4 years because the band wears out.  Also, I would not recommend getting a light-colored band because they tend to get dingy looking.
I love the look of this watch.  It's tough and athletic, while being stylish and feminine. I only wish the band were a bit more comfortable.  It slides around a bit... but I'm getting used to it.
No email addresses, no phone numbers, no resolution from Amazon. Forwarded to my c/c company to recoup payment.
summary: Item Never Received - Zero Customer Support From Amazon

reviewText: I like this product, it's lightweight, easy to read, backlighting is cool.  The only issue I had was that it didn't come with any directions on how to set any of the modes.  However, the watch was user friendly enough that I was able to figure most of them out.

I bought this watch a few years ago and loved everything about it. Just recently the sides came up done and even super glue wouldn't fix the problem. I finally gave in and decided to buy a new one. I thought about trading up for a different model. However, the other model just didn't do it. I had problems with it and ended up sending it back to get this one again.My favorite features:Easy to useLight works greatThe three alarms allow you to customize when you need them (weekdays, weekends, daily). This made it nice cause I never had to worry about turning the alarm back on after a weekend.Buttons are really easy to use and figure out. I never had a problem changing features or actually  pushing any of the buttons.

I had one that lasted eight years and then I needed to replace it - understandable.  I was very happy for how long it lasted.  Then I had gone through four in the last three years due to the sealing on the watch.  After a short time, when swimming, water seeped in and created a foggy screen making it difficult to view the time.  With each replacement watch in the last three years, each one performed for a shorter amount of time than the one previous.  Too bad I love the watch and it's three alarms, but I don't think I will replace my most recent watch.  It's time to find a better performing watch for swimming.

The watch's warranty makes you pay 7$ for shipping and handling if it has a manufacturing problem, which it usually has when inmersed in water for the first time. That in itself is a great business for Timex. Then the watch works pretty good for up to a year when the band falls apart and the water goes in. It is very disappointing.

Overall its not bad, but do have some issues with the starting and stopping of the chrono, and I am not new to the timex ironman.  Have not yet figured out if its user error or an issue with the design.  Would probably say I was happier with my old timex ironman which was the basic ironman

The button labels on this watch are so small, I simply could not even read them.  The picture of the watch on this site must be blown up several times because it led me to believe the labels were clear and visible. Well, they are not. I sent this back.

I have just ordered my third watch like this.  They last about 2 years, and my second one isn't dead yet, but the top right corner display is starting to disintegrate and I don't want to be without one.  I am not complaining about the two year lifespan because I wear it ALL the time. In the shower, windsurfing, swimming, etc.  I take some pretty good falls while windsurfing and everything keeps working.  Yes, most of the silver has come off around the face and the face has lots of small scratches on it but the band is fine, the three alarms are great, the chrono is terrific.  In short, I love the features and the style, yes I wish it could take the beating I give it a little longer, but I didn't pay that much for it.That being said, I am sticking with the black band even though I like the other colors.  Lighter colors get grungy.  Also, I agree with the person who said they would like to just have the plain gray resin around the face.Also, I love that Amazon tells me when I last bought the watch, when I go to order a new one.  Thanks, Amazon!

I'm not a hard-core runner, but wanted to train to run my first 5k. This watch was easy to use and did exactly what I needed it to. I wish it was a bit smaller still, as I have tiny wrists and even the ladies size was a bit big, but it's not heavy and works great.
Great watch except that the finish is coming  off without much wear.  Numbers are easy to see.  I like the fact that it is waterproof!

I love my new running watch. It has all of the features I needed to track my running progress. The chime for the interval timer gets muffled under all of my layers. I am sure it will be more audible as the weather warms and the layers come off.

I bought this because I wanted a watch that easily kept track of my spilts for the Chicago Marathon. It is super easy to store and recall. It doesn't have a ton of extras, but you can get your average pace, spilts, overall time. It has been sturdy and fits my small wrist well. Loved it on the big day and continue to use it regularly.

I love this watch. Simple. Durable. Affordable. Need I say more?I will only because I love this watch. As I train for my very first marathon, it's nice to have a simple watch that helps me train without a lot of figuring out. This watch is a great tool when incorporating Jeff Galloway's run walk methods. It helps to keep track of different running intervals continuously, hands-free. When you do need to stop or restart the timer, the controls are simple enough to maneuver without peeling your eyes off the road.As a first-time runner, it's nice to have found an uncomplicated solution.Update: It's now been two years since I purchased this watch and it's in great shape. I run at least once a week for a long distance and I've yet to experience any deterioration in the strap. Here are a few points: I use this watch only when I run so I don't end up causing undue wear and tear - sure it's waterproof so I could wear it into the shower, but why would I? When I strap it to my wrist, I wear it loose - mostly because my wrists tend to swell during my runs, but perhaps the leeway reduces strain in the resin. Finally, I don't refasten the strap when I take it off. I'm too lazy to do so - maybe this allows the material to dry in a relaxed state preventing cracking?Simply put, I still love this watch to pieces!
keep setting watch & it returns to another time/date.  directions impossible to read so small.  too bulky to wear at the card table, but like it when it works
always do love Timex and have had 3-4 - this model looks lovely but it is not quite as comfortable as my last Times.

I swim three days per week and wanted a watch I could see underwater- this works great, I also like that I can hit the button to light it up if I wake up at night and want to know the time.I'm not into all the bells and whistles but somehow set the timer to chime hourly, which I find I like, (keeps me on track at work and seems to make it go faster!) The directions on settings was difficult for me- though my husband figured them out pretty easily- next I'll use it to keep count of my laps or pre set a timer so I'll know when the time I wanted to work out is up.I have small wrists and this fits fine and doesn't look too bulky, though if you want to make a glittery fashion statement, this is not the watch for you.Well worth the money.

I have had 2 of these.  Timex replaced the first under warranty because it took on water while swimming.  The second one has done the same and Timex will not replace.  They told me that if you push any of the buttons in the water or ever change the battery that the water resistance is compromised.  Once it takes in water, it fries the watch and stops working.  Since this in an ironman triathalon watch designed to time laps, it defeats the purpose of having the watch.

I've had another Timex Irinman watch before so I knew I would want one just the same except with a plastic armband, the last one I had was Velcro and tore up everything. Anyways I love thier watches because:1. It's waterproof.2. 3 different alarms.3. Timer and stopwatch. I probably use the timer at least three times daily for different stuff here at college.4. Two or more timezones. I work with a travelling kids camp in the summer and I lived being able to just hold down a button and have the right timezone!There are probably more reasons I love this watch but I think you can see you get what you pay for and this is an excellent watch.Plus black matches everything girls!
I have been very happy with this watch. It is a great watch to have when I am out running.
Too many buttons blows my mind.  I wanted something easy and this had too many different buttons to push and then I just all confused and I only wear it now for the time.

I love the options it has, although I don't use any of the sports features. I just need mom stuff, the 3 alarms,the day and the date,and the night light. It's comfortable to wear. It's durable, water resistant and not bad lookin. But around the face the color has worn off and makes it look old and needs to be replaced. I have had several of these watches because I can't find any other with the features I need, and they all have the same wearing problem around the face.
summary: I like it but, the coloring wears off.

reviewText: Although my first Ironman watch, exactly like this, fell apart, I abused it by wearing it daily and wore it in the water.  So, I was happy to purchas another one.

I purchased this watch about six months ago and while on vacation last month, the watch stopped working.  I assumed that the battery had died and I finally took it to have the battery replaced.  The battery had corroded (Keep in mind that this is a Timex Woman's Ironman Triathlon watch.  I of course wore it in the water for swimming and certainly didn't expect a corroded battery, especially after such a short time.  Unfortunately, it is outside of the Timex warranty period.I had purchased this watch after another Timex Triathlon watch strap broke and the strap could not be replaced.So, now I have two useless watches from Timex that were poorly manufactured (likely in China, although the watches don't indicate where they were made).  I certainly won't be purchasing another Timex sports watch.
summary: Buyer beware! - Watch battery corroded in six months time.

reviewText: This product was absolutely amazing and totally worth it.  I have seen it in several watch stores and it has always been at least ten dollars more.  It arrived on time and everything in perfect condition. I have not had any problems with it at all and would highly recommend purchasing your items from here.

At least this is what I would like to think. I absolutely loved my watch. I thought it fit and looked great. I loved the easy button for the light up display as I often run at night. However, the first time I decided to try out my watch in the water it got water inside. I was so disappointed, but thought it may dry out. However, the next day it just got worse until the whole watch was ruined. I am think of purchasing another, but I may always be afraid to take it in the water!

I had been looking for a watch that had interval timing for easy run/walk timing.  This watch works great for that!  It only has 2 interval settings but that's enough for what I do.  The chrono timer is also helpful and all the timers are easy to use.  The reason I only gave this watch a 4 star rating is because I'm not that fond of the watch band.  It is very stiff and not as comfortable to wear as other sport watches I've had in the past.  I read lots of reviews about this watch and many people said that the band breaks easily.  But I really needed the interval timing aspect of the watch so I went ahead and purchased it.  It's doing fine so far.  I just try not to jerk on it so much when taking it off.  I could see that it would break easier if you aren't patient taking it off your wrist.

I LOVE this watch...except that less than 10 months after purchase, the band is detaching from the face in more than one spot.  The detaching band is interfering with using the watch buttons to start/stop time and change modes.  I don't wear my watch for swimming, showers, baths, or any other prolonged water activities.  The most water exposure it's had is when I give my kiddos baths, and it's supposed to be water resistant anyway!!  I have purchased many of these watches, and this one leaves me looking for a new brand of stopwatch.  As a PE teacher, I wear this watch ALL of the time...how disappointing.
All I had hoped for. Nice smaller size, great runners watch. Timex ironman is a trustworthy watch. Bought for a gift, she loved it.

Pros:It has all the main features you want in a decent running watch:50 laps, savable memory, splits.It has a relatively small face which is good for women, especially petite ones.Cons:It doesn't last more than a year, maybe a year and a half.  The piece that tucks the band is usually the first to go, then the band falls off, which can't be replaced.  If the battery dies it is almost impossible to replace it without ruining the waterproof seal, which then busts the whole watch when you get it wet.  And the last round I bought about a year ago seemed to have a bad indiglow that breaks after two months.  I thought it was bad luck, but then my friend had the same problem with the one she bought around the same time, went through the hassle of returning it, and the new one broke as well.  I am hoping this is fixed now, as I didn't have the problem with the previous 7 watches I owned.I've used this style of watch for the past 10 years.  I can't find another watch that has the features as well as the small face so I keep buying it. (If anyone knows of another watch please let me know). My husband went through a bunch of more expensive Nike watches that also broke after a year or, so I figure spending $50 a yar for a watch is better than $100.  It is a shame because I know Timex knows how to make watches that last.  The same friend mentioned above had a Timex that she bought 20 years ago that lasted for 10 years, with replaceable bands, all the features, and a small face, but they no longer make that model.  I guess you don't sell as many watches that way.
summary: I have owned at least 8 of these

reviewText: This was a gift for my daughter.  She loved it. She said the watch looked alot nicer when we actually got it.  The picture online didn't do it justice.

In under six months with normal use (3 or 4 runs a week and a couple of dunks in a swimming pool) this watch is no longer waterproof and the band has stretched to the point that the watch face won't stay connected.  It is very easy to use and very comfortable, but it is almost at the point where it has become worthless.  I will look for a different watch next time.

It was exactly what I expected and haven't had any issues with it since purchasing. It seems a little more bulky then the one I had before (I thought it was the same type), but it really isn't an issue.

I havent owned this long but I wasn't overly thrilled about it at first... its the women's size but still pretty bulky for a watch, you would have thought with technology the Timex models would be getting smaller, but its just as thick (almost half an inch) as my old Timex Expedition watch from 2001 (which died on me years ago but I just found it recently).  I like the functions... hopefully I just get used to the bulk on my wrist again...
I bought this to replace my old, broken one, and I just love this watch! It's sleek and sporty and stylish, all at the same time. The buttons work well, easy to use, and has multiple handy functions.
summary: Perfect! The one I was looking for!

reviewText: I had an identical one before but I think it died down.  I still believe in the Timex quality watches so I replaced it with identical one.  It works fine and easy to program.  Definitely recommend it to anyone who needs the use of a timer and other bells and whistles.

El reloj es excelente, muy practico para trotar y llevar las cuentas de la vueltas. Pudiera ser mas comodo de usar, pues trae muchas funciones y los pocos botones que trae le hace algo complicado de manejar.
summary: Buen reloj, algo complicado de usar

reviewText: This is my all time favorite running watch.  Started wearing it in the 90s when I was training with the Galloway Group for my first marathon.  Recommended my them because of the 2 timing alarms.  Perfect for walk/run training.  Also like size.  No longer do marathons but still prefer this watch.  Garmins etc are wonderful for very serious runners....think it will even do your grocery shopping::)).  Give me this watch!

It's a Timex!  That means it keeps surprisingly accurate time for an inexpensive watch.  At first I thought the strap was going to be its weak point; but it has held up like a champ for nearly three years of daily wear as in 7days a week daily.  The crystal is slightly recessed, which has kept it scratch free in all that time.  However, the bevel has no fared as will.  Most of the silver coating over the plastic housing has worn off.  It there were some safe way to replace it, this watch would be invincible.  And best of all the battery shows no signs of wearing out yet.It looks nice on the wrist and is light and airy, removing one of the biggest complaints about a resin strap, that it is stiff and sweaty.  I will soon be replacing it with another.  Perhaps I will go for a different color this time........

I had a similar watch for about 6 years that I absolutely loved; the soft plastic band finally broke, so I treated myself to a new one.  I was glad to see the same type of watch was still available from Timex at a moderate price; the design is even nicer, since it has a sleeker, more feminine design.  The alarm has been terrific especially when I travel.  The digital face has big numbers that are very easy to read -- even at night, with the Indiglo feature.  I would definitely buy this watch again -- and again.Timex Unisex Ironman Triathlon Sleek 50/100 Watch #T54281
This is my third one as its cheaper to buy a new one than replace the batteries.  Nice and light and great for running.

I'm 42 and haven't worn a watch in a very long time. This was purchased specifically for it's timer/interval timer function which I use for timing meditation/Reiki treatments. I have the timer pre-set for 20 minutes to meditate, then once the alarm goes off, I switch over to the Interval Timer which is set up (both intervals) for 2 minutes so it simply chimes every 2 minutes until I turn it off. I think the alarm/timer chime is delicate enough to be used for meditation (Compared to other products like kitchen timers.) and so it is serving my intended purpose quite nicely.As a watch? Eh. I think it's bulky and uncomfortable to wear on my wrist. As an alarm clock, the alarm isn't very loud or aggressive (which is why I like to use it for meditation) but when I've slept with the watch on my wrist and my arm is under the pillow, I don't hear the alarm.

I love this watch and is my second one, unfortunately both watches had the strap fail on them in less that two years. I sent Timex an email and they didn't reply. I love the functions on the watch and the simple look to it so am sad about this default. I am uncertain if I will buy Timex again.

I use this watch when I am diving, and it is great. Still works after it has been down 60+ ft in the ocean (didn't get any deeper) and it was easy to figure out- took me around 10 minutes to get most the functions (change time, timer, alarms, ect) without the instruction book.
summary: Easy to use and lives up to its claims

reviewText: I like the looks of this watch.  It's not expensive and is user friendly if you read the instructions.  I would recommend this watch.
Serves it function well. Fit is less than perfect as the plastic band does not lay flat under the wrist at the buckle.

I wanted a rugged watch that I could wear to play tennis and also wear at the beach. This watch fills the bill! The style is sporty but practical. So far I love it! The gray color that I selected goes with everything. It is also easy to set.
summary: My Timex Women's Ironman Watch is a Winner

reviewText: My skin is sensitive and so have to wear jewelry that won't break me out - have been wearing some version of this type of sports watch for years now - this is my second on this exact watch - have never had any issues with it - the other one's battery finally died and I had bonked it hard enough to crack small vulnerable area just above the start/stop button and so just bought a new one.  It's not super big but still easy to ready - has a lot of features - 1/2 of them I don't even use, but I like an alarm and timer and this has both.  It's easy to set - I recommend it.

The Women's Ironman Triathlon watch is a good watch.  It works well keeping track of my laps and timing.  There are 2 major issues with this watch for me.One, the band is not really comfortable.  It is made of some kind of rubbery material that makes my wrist sweat!  Also, the band is difficult to fasten because of the rather stiff nature of the material.  The end of the band wants to keep "popping up" and you have to make sure to slide the loop over it each time.  This is an inconvience when all you want to do is get on the track and get moving.Issue #2 is the indiglow factor.  When I push the indiglow to see the time in the dark, the numbers are illuminated but they are illuminated in such a way that makes them difficult to see!  I was familiar with a Timex watch that would illuminate the face of the watch - literally flood it with light so that you could easily see and read the information.  I was very disappointed with this feature of the watch.Keeps great time and it is easy to operate - so I give it 3 stars.Given an opportunity to buy this watch  again, I would opt out.  I am sure there are watches much more suited to the runner/walker's needs.

Love everything about it.  I'm 72 and this is my third one.  Going to take out the extended warrantee on this one as this is my third one.  Lost the first after about 4 years, the second the band broke after 3 years.  So hopefully the warrantee situation with fulfill my needs.  It's comfortable, give accurate information and I love the 'night light'.

I purchased this watch at the same time i purchased a men's tri watch for my husband as a gift. When i tried to use my watch for the first time, the battery was dead. I contacted Amazon customer service and they refunded me teh amount for a new battery... however, it appears the battery is not the problem, as the watch has never worked for me. Disappointing, because i tried to contact Amazon customer service regarding this issue several times with no response. So i am left with a non-functioning piece of equipment. Very disappointing.
The BEST watch!  Feels great, fits great, looks great and is very user friendly.  Very good for a woman who has a small wrist, and very easy to use.  Love it!

Very good watch that works well for sports.It is not too bulky and the buttons are easy to operate.  I have been using this for timing walks and jogging and it has ben fine.  Also has held up well in swimming.I do rinse it off quickly though in clean water after I use it to make sure chlorine and perspiration does not damage it somehow (more precaution than actually having and problem with it.)

I've used this watch in training and triathlons for three years now.  For the price, I think that's a reasonable life expectancy.  The watch is light, comfortable, attractive, simple to use, and has all the functions I've needed.  After about two years the band began to discolor and to stretch, so that it now sometimes falls off.  Replacement bands are not available, which is a shame since the watch itself still works fine.  However - look at price - this is an extremely affordable watch which has given me several years of reliable service.  If I want something more, I need to be willing to pay more.  I am asking for the same watch for my birthday!

I love the watch. I've been wearing it for about three weeks now and the only complaint I have is that some of the print on the wrist part of the watch has worn off (this is where it says "50 Feet etc" I don't know what else it says since I can't read it). It's not an integral part of the watch at all, so really no loss to me. The watch is perfect for my needs. Fast as heck delivery time.

I've been using this sport watch for almost a year in and out of the water.  It provides all of the basic timing functions I need for running, biking, and swimming - including lap timing and various ways to view your splits.So far, it has proved to be water resistant in pools, lakes, and showers.I also really like the way the band is secured.  It has a sliding ring to hold the end of the band down.  The cool thing is that the ring has a little nub that fits into a hole at the end of the band to keep it in place.

I initially purchased a watch for myself.  I like to wear my watch 24-hours a day, and am an active person, so needed something which could withstand some punishment.  About the only time I take my watch off during the day is if I'm typing on a laptop on a desk.  I also like to lift my hand in the middle of the night to see what time it is without having to roll over, so for the value, this has been a great watch for me.My daughter started first grade and was always asking me what time it was.  I began looking for a watch for her, but after a while, decided to give her my old watch and buy myself a new one.  This watch fits her wrist as well, and has worked great for her.  This summer, however, her watch did take on some moisture after some pool time.  Her watch is about 3-years old.

I bought one of these over 3 years ago and am buying a replacement. The keeper for the watch band recently broke and the silver paint on the face has mostly worn off. No problems with leakage and I am impressed that the battery has lasted over 3 years.  I like the overall look of the watch because it is functional yet, feminine. I think it would be hard to find a better watch for the price if you are looking for a sports watch.  I'm hopeful that Timex has fixed the leaking watch  problem that other reviewers have experienced.

This watch survived six weeks of anthropological field work in The Gambia (West Africa) during the rainy season.  Sweat, dirt, and downpour did not destroy it.  The "alarm" feature can be set on "repeat," sounding in intervals, which is very useful for behavioral observations or for athletic activities.  In "civilian" life, it's terrific for timing runs.  It fit the wrists of both members of the lab team.  The only damage suffered was that the silver paint around the face chipped away (it's gray underneath, so hardly noticeable) and the plastic face got scratched.
summary: Durable, easy to use, and comfortable

reviewText: I love this watch!  I just began running again after 10 years and joined a running group training for the half-marathon.  This watch is great for the Galloway method of training, esp. the alternating timers. I can set it for 2 minutes running and 1 minute walking with continuous or interrupted repeats.  Easy to use and program!

Bought this for interval training so I could set a 2 minute/1 minute pace and it worked for that. Other than that, nothing too exciting but it worked for what I wanted at the time. I think anything under the 50-lap doesn't do the intervals. Found that out the hard way by buying and then returning the 30-lap watch.
So far so good with this watch. Size is perfect, comfortable, and does everything I need it to do. Just got it so idk how long it will last.
this watch is perfect for me.  It is just the right size, the wrist band is great.
As a new runner, I needed a product that would be easy to use but still help with my interval training.  I have been VERY happy with this watch as I transition between running and swimming.

Writing this after seeing the pictures someone posted that are not favorable to this watch.  I've worn this watch pre-fishing and in fishing tournaments for many years - from high 90's to freezing cold weather.  Watch looks like it is brand new.  Can't imagine what the individual that posted the pictures did to the watch to cause the damage but I've never had any problems with mine.  It is the best watch for fishing tournaments that I've owned.  My husband bought me an expensive watch to wear in these events but the metal band gets, and stays, cold in winter/late fall/early spring events.  This watch does not get cold, is very light, band drys quickly, and waterproof.  Tried other watches with nylon bands but they stayed wet far after the rain/snow stopped.  Also this watch is easy to set up/program alarms, etc.  I fish in several different states/time zones and can change zones with a 5 second press of the center button.  The chime helps me to track the hours in a tournament and alarms are extremely easy to set and turn on and off.  I don't have a negative to say about this watch - it is extremely good.

I love this watch. It's perfect for swim workouts and aquathlon races -- takes splits, can do intervals, etc. I use a different product with a heartrate monitor for my runs, but can't use it for my swims (since heartrate monitors can't transmit under water, and also, the unit itself is not waterproof). This Timex has an audible chime under water, and it's easy to set the various functions. It stores your workout splits so you can recall them later when logging your workout. I also love the 3 alarms - my schedule is different every day, so I use the alarms to remind me when to leave work for school, when to leave to pick up my son, etc. I had lost my first watch (same model), but never found another watch that had all the features I wanted for a reasonable price. This is my second one!!
summary: Perfect for swim workouts and aquathlon races

reviewText: I bought this watch to wear to work in a hospital setting.  I love everything about it.  The size is just right for a woman...big enough to clearly read the face, but not so big that it looks bulky or masculine.  It is also water resistant which is important when frequent handwashing is part of the job.  I would definitely recommend this watch.
summary: Exactly what I was looking for!

reviewText: I was looking for a workout watch that wouldn't be the smaller version of those gargantuan men's watches. Ended up settling on this watch because of the sleek style, but the functionality and features are just as impressive. Operation is straightforward and easy to figure out.

I bought this watch towards the beginning of the summer and it's been on my wrist ever since.  It is still working absolutely great and I've wore it through two triathlons, numerous pool workouts, hundreds of showers, to the lake, etc.  It is a very great watch!

I recently purchased a Timex Women's Ironman Triathlon Watch. I would recommend this purchase. I have had very good experiences with my prior Timex Ironman for Women's watches. They last and last and last. The band wears out before the watch. I am not sure about the water resistent feature as I don't swim or bathe with the watch on. I wear the band loose so that it won't tear as other people have reported. All over a good watch.

I have been a faithful Timex purchaser and love their IRONMAN Watches and fell in love w/the new sleek design. Now Im not a "Triathlon runner" but I am a "TRIATHLON MOM" With 2 boys ages 2 and almost 4; Running around chasing and cleaning dishes and muddy shoes! This watch is awesome! I however am always finding myself having to buy a new WATCH when my band breaks or tears. I cant find a replacement. Only if TIMEX offered it on their website. The band/strap on this watch is different where it wraps/loops around the buttons on the sides.  Love the watch, thou the  band will give out first!

I received this as a Christmas gift in 2010.  It lasted less than 2 months before it was no longer waterproof.  It would cloud up and stop working.  It would begin working again once it dried out.  This is worthless!

Excellent watch and well worth the money!  Makes my sailboat racing that much more efficient and very comfortable to wear d/t it's small size and light weight!!  One thing I would like to see in a watch this size though, would be to have the real time showing in the corner while the timer is going both in the main window at the same time, so I don't have to go back and forth and take the chance of interrupting the timer.
summary: Definitely well worth the money...a very nice watch!

reviewText: I actually just bought my second one of these watches.  My other one lasted just over a year.  The band became separated from the watch face in a few months, and finally, the little strap that holds the band in place finally broke so I am forced to replace the watch.  Despite these issues, I am buying another one because of all the features; it has the interval setting which I use regularly in my training, and the multi-time settings allow me to easily change times when I travel through time zones. It is easy to read in the pool when I'm doing laps and great for time keeping . Nevertheless, I wish this watch had lasted longer and was of more durable construction, which is why I'm just giving it 3 stars.
summary: Great watch, though not great longevity

reviewText: This is an ideal watch for those athletically minded. I decided to purchase the Women's version because of my smaller size, but it has not affected my manhood any! The features on the watch are especially for those training in longer distance running. You can find an interval timer along with regular chronometer.I'm still learning what this mini computer can do. Perhaps the only drawback on this is the stop/start button which is a little difficult to activate, and might have been better placed on the outside of the watch.

I have had this Ironman watch for about a year. I have been really happy with the interval timer function and the watch in general, but it has not held up to a year of regular use. I wear it probably about 75% of my waking hours. I take it off, of course, to sleep, shower, and swim, but I do wear it when I run, bike, hit the weight room, and at work. In a year's time, the band has broken because it is very thin where it wraps around the watch face, and over time it has become slightly brittle and worn out. The strap is also highly susceptible to discoloration (soaks up dyes from clothing like a sponge) but I imagine that this is a problem with many similar watches. Another problem I've had is the indiglo function ceasing to work within a few months of purchasing the watch. Now pressing the indiglo button just makes the screen go blank. I wear the watch a lot but am pretty careful with it, so I have been surprised by how quickly it has worn out.
summary: Well designed but doesn't stand up to use

reviewText: I've uploaded several photos so you can see for yourself why I gave this watch only 1 star. Timex Ironman are my favorite watches, and I have owned several over the years (currently I own the Timex Ironman 30 Lap and it's great -- no problems with it whatsoever). But this one ... such a disappointment and ONLY because the resin strap/band is a piece of junk and the 'paint job' on face wore off almost immediately. The timepiece itself is fantastic. No problems there, but after the nice silver paint wore off, the little loop that prevents the excess band from catching on your clothing split and fell off (not a piece you can find & replace). Then the band started cracking in many places and the problem is not just aesthetic. Eventually it's going to fall apart completely and I won't be able to wear it again. The band is not replaceable. Such a bummer. A great watch but the poor quality band ruins it. BTW - I've owned this watch for 1-2 years and wear it constantly, including in the shower. So I've definitely *used* it, but this is marketed as a *triathlon* watch so I would expect it to be able to stand up to things like water.
summary: Don't buy it unless you want a disposable watch

reviewText: I really like the functionality of the Ironman watches. I like this one in particular because it's on the smaller side. The watch features 3 alarms (with day-of-the-week options), 2 different count-down alarms (and one allows you to set multiple successive count downs of varying lengths), a stopwatch and 2 timezones. It's very easy to use, and gives instructions on how to set various things. I liked this watch so much that I bought a second after the first one broke.Unfortunately, every one of the Ironman watches I've owned have failed in the exact same way - the band. There are little rubber tabs that fit into the watch case, and they are the only thing that connects the band to the watch. If the rubber tabs get stretched or torn, then the watch case falls out. To be fair, the band is definitely comfortable, and the curvature of the band makes it fit sturdily without being too tight.The bands have lasted between 3-14 months, so I've been buying a new $30-$40 watch once a year (or so) for the past 6 years. I've been unable to find watch band replacements, and I'm not sure that I could do it myself anyway. The warranty specifically says that it does not cover any problems with the band of the watch. At this point, there's a clear financial incentive for Timex to pair awesome watches with bad bands. If you search the reviews for Ironman watches, so many people just buy a new watch when the watchband breaks, rather than try to get the band replaced. I'm boycotting the Ironman watches because of this.It looks like the Timex Expedition has most of the features I want, so that's what I'm going to get next.

I love this watch, although its not the prettiest thing.  It has all the functions I need and then some I'll never need.  I love the practicality, the dual time zones, the multi-functional alarms.  I can set an alarm to go off every week-day when my son gets out of school, and a separate timer that goes off only on Thursdays at a different time (early days).  I can even set a third alarm if I need to!The only real downer is that the paint/color or the silver part started rubbing off after a while which makes it look really cheap, and I am not fond of the neon yellow color for the top right light button.
summary: Fantastic Funtions, Great Watch, color comes off

reviewText: I've had Timex Ironman watches for years, but this band style is really prone to breakage.No issues with the watch performance, just the plastic band, which pops apart.It didn't happen immediately, so your mileage may vary.I got enough use out of it that I would not return it for being outright defective; it's just a poor and flimsy band style.

I love this watch.  I'm on my third one.  I wear it ALL the time.  The biggest reason I've replaced is the band wears out after 3 years or so of daily wear.  I use it in running.  There's an interval timer (I run via Galloway method: run-walk-run) so this is VERY helpful.  I also use it as my daily alarm clock (3 alarms) on it.  I use the timer for my kids bedtime.  It's a great all purpose watch.Love it and will buy another in 3-5 years.
Very nice watch with just the features I need. This is my second one. I would still be using the first one but I lost it!
I got this for my wife for interval training when her Garmin 405cx acts up.  Nice and small/light for women and she liked that it was relatively easy to use.
Very nice watch for price. Meets my gym and exercise needs.Instructions are difficult to read. Font is light on a light background. Why can't they just use black font on white background.
summary: Timex Women's Ironman Triathlon Sleek 50 Lap Watch

reviewText: The watch arrived and as I was setting the time, one of the buttons and its spring completely fell off!  I thought sports watches were supposed to be sturdy.  This was a new watch, I hadn't even worn it once.  Amazon processed my refund promptly.
the watch does everything I need it to do so I can track my intervals, know my pace, etc.  Now, if it had a GPS built in, it would be perfect!!

This is a great watch for keeping track of my busy life. I use it for exercising, reminders, even cooking. It's easy to use and very reliable. I've been using this same model for about ten years now.Just two quibbles: the bands are always the first thing to go. It'd be nice if there was a way to easily replace it rather than buying a whole new watch. I realize it's not very expensive: I just hate wasting resources like that.The other quibble is it would be great to have two timers. I exercise the same amount of time each day and it'd be nice if I didn't have to reset that just because I was timing something on the stove.Otherwise, this is a very nice watch. It's sporty but cute enough to wear with my regular clothes. It even does military time, which I prefer.
summary: This is the fourth or fifth time I've bought this watch

reviewText: I loved the looks of the watch and it probably is a wonderful watch but I found the directions to its functions very confusing and complicated. I sent it back because I neither have the time to wade through all the directions nor do i want to have to consult the directions every time I go for a run.

I initially purchased this watch from Amazon about 8 months ago.  I was happy to have an easy way to monitor my lap time and count laps while swimming.  But after just a few months use, the watch fogged up and quit working.Since it was still under warranty I sent it in for repair.  Timex replaced the watch, stating that the original watch could not be repaired.Okay fine.By the time I got the new watch, swimming season was over.I got back in the pool for the first time 3 days ago.  When I got home I noticed my watch was fogged over and within hours the thing just died.It is a pity because I really liked the watch.  But I won't be wasting my money on this one again.

I bought this watch as a gift for my wife 2 years ago, and the, as others had reported, the band broke.  Others report that it is more expensive to have it repaired than simply buying a new one.  My wife liked it so much, that she insisted on having the same thing- regardless of the band. This would be a 5 star review if there didn't seem to be a systemic problem with the band

Great price and a great watch for workouts.  Easy to use.  Battery was a bit tough to replce (don't leave the chronographer running - it quickly wears the battery out), but other than that - I would highly recommend the watch.

Prior to purchasing this watch, I owned two Timex Women's Ironman watches. I replaced each of the watches after numerous years of wear--only when the battery or the band broke. I've been very pleased with the Timex Ironman watches, and so I decided to purchase yet another Timex Ironman.Needless to say, I am *very* disappointed with the design of the Timex Women's T59201 Ironman Triathlon Watch. After just a few months of wear, the face of the watch completely popped out from the band; when I went to look at the time, the face of the watch had completely slipped out from the band and so all that was attached to my wrist was the watchband. Fortunately I was able to locate the face, which had fallen on the carpet in another room in my house.I then tried supergluing the face of the watch to the band. Unfortunately, the glue has failed on numerous occassions. I hate to throw out the watch, as I haven't owned it for that long. But it such a pain to keep checking the watch to make sure that the face is still connected to the band. I am often to reconnect one of the four prongs thats secures the face to the band.Timex has gone careless in their design over the years. I used to be a faithful fan of Timex Ironman watches, but I no longer am a fan.
summary: Crappy Design - Hope You Don't Lose the Face of Your Watch

reviewText: I love this watch but have had to return it to times two times for the indigo button not working. Timex has been great and had fixed it for free, but it still was a hassle.I do wear this watch all the time. So I am definitely very rough on it. It takes showers with me etc.The heartrate function is great! Especially now that I am pregnant and need to keep my heart rate from going too high.

I received the watch on a Friday, learned how to program it Friday night.  Took it for a swim Saturday afternoon. By Saturday night the watch no longer worked.  My swim was  a simple lap pool, I might have gone 5 feet under with flip turns, and yet it cannot withstand it.  Does not live up to it's water resistance as advertised
I needed a durable watch to take to Kenya, Africa.  So far it has meet all my expectations.  Easy to operate, alarm is loud enough and fits nicely on my smaller wrist.
I wear this watch almost all of the time now.  I was switching out watches for work and working out, but recently started wearing it at work.  Love it!!

I started out with 2 stars and then the more I thought about it I chose 4.I purchased two of these for my daughters. The most they do is swim at a pool. Both watches got condensation within two months after we purchased them. One was replace through Amazon, the other repaired through Timex. The new watch from Amazon has worked great for the last year. The one repaired through Timex had the same problem about 8 months later. I expressed my disappointment with the repair to Timex and they sent a brand new watch to me and a prepaid box to send the old one back.So I'm on the fence. When the watches work, they work. When they have issues Timex does stand behind them and so I upped my rating to 4 stars. While I did have some minor problems they were easily fixed.
Easy to setup. Great colors. Size is perfect. Love this watch. I run on a bi-daily basis. Definitely a must have. And, not too expensive!
Great product but if your in the military the bands crack within two years but I keep buying them because they are very durable.

this watch is great! i was looking for a watch to match my new ecco running shoes and this one is perfect. i especially like the alarms. when the alarm goes off it is just like a snooze button buzzing again 5min. later. i have it set for when it is time to leave my house for work, clock in for work & when i clock out from work. i love it! i saved around $8.00 buying it from amazon and the service was terrific. thanks

This is the 4th or 5th watch in this series that I've owned. This one allows for multiple interval timing. Fantastic!I 'did' the Chicago marathon this past fall. The group that I train with runs for 3 minutes and then walks for 2 minutes on all of our training runs. This watch alternates these intervals, sounding an alarm after each! The buttons are intuitive, making it easy to use even with quite a few features.The silver and black color combo has held up much better another black and metallic green Timex watch from another line did (The metallic green on the watch face scraped off). The band has openings which is nice (your wrist doesn't get sweaty). Good value.
love the design and how it fits in your wrist.colour is great too. great for counting laps when running
summary: VERY GOOD - GREAT DESIGN AND FIT

reviewText: It works great, I've went swimming with it many times and its definitely water proof. I read some reviews about people's watches breaking as soon as they got wet, but I've never had a problem. You can't push any buttons why in the water, but I really like it, good for athletic people!
Exactly what I expected.  Glad that Timex has an excellent standard and that they don't change up an excellent product.
summary: Love this watch and glad to have it in different colors

reviewText: I have had this watch for only a month, but so far have not had any of the problems I read about in other reviews.  No problem with the band.  No problem in the pool (though I am careful to not push buttons while underwater).  For $32 it was just what I wanted.
I have had my watch for one year and the band is already cracked (the watch itself is great).  The band is such that it cannot be replaced therefore the watch must be replaced.  What a waste!

I ordered this watch because I am starting to run again, and interval training works for me. The old Timex VO2 max had dual linked timers that were perfect for interval training. Timex has since buried endless iterations of the linked timer feature in it's Iron Man series - it's pretty hard to know when you are getting the "real" linked timer feature in a watch. This one doesn't have it. There are two interval timers, but they do not cycle continuously. After one round they shut off, and you have to start it again - annoying! Unfortunately, Timex seems to be the only manufacturer that even has this feature = which is why I guess they feel so comfortable jerking their clients around with misleading product descriptions....

After 10 months, the watch still works fine after daily use.  Only complaint functionally is that the large, exposed buttons are easy to press accidentally, but no biggie.  But cosmetically, the watch doesn't last.  The silver finish around the face has rubbed off & the plastic face is scratched up (see my posted photos).  I've also owned a light purple version of this watch, which looked even worse after a year - the band discolored and wouldn't come clean.  So, though the watch works fine, I'll be replacing it because it now looks ugly.  I find that Timex watches have a lifespan of a year or less - sure, they keep ticking, but they really look awful after a few months.  So, I've been replacing my watches every year.  Maybe this time I'll learn my lesson and try another brand.
summary: Functional, but its looks don't last

reviewText: We have had several of these watches through the years. They don't last forever but they work great and well priced.

This watch is amazing.  It has the time, a chrono timer that can store up to 50 laps, a timer that runs down to zero, an interval timer and three alarms that you can set by the day, by weekdays, by weekends.  This is the most practical and useful watch I've ever had.  It's very easy user-friendly; I was able to set it while I was doing a flip-turn.  It's cool because you can even use multiple timers at the same time and they have different beeps.  It was great for using during my workout.  I set it for the interval time and the overall timer, then I didn't have to worry about looking at my watch all of the time.  The beep is loud enough to hear when I'm working out.  The watch face has large numbers and lights up very nicely in the dark.  It's sleek design fits nicely on my very small wrist.  It also has a rubber thing that helps keep the watch flap secured.  I would highly recommend this product to everyone.  It is definitely worth the value.

This watch does exactly what it says it does. I had a previous Timex which I also loved. Works great in and out of the water so it is perfect for Triathlon. Would highly recommend this watch for the active person who needs to time there runs, swims, etc.

This is a good watch just for basic every day use.  I would NOT recommend it for someone that wants to use it for running or tri training IF you are over 40 and need reading glasses for small print. If you need reading glasses and have not used this particular watch before, the small print around the inside edge of the glass is very difficult or near impossible to read - without glasses - which you will not have while running or swimming.  Some of the lap times and other things are also difficult to read, especially while you are out running and are looking at the numbers on the fly.  Also, the layout of the functions and which buttons do what has never seemed intuitive to me on this particular model.  With some functions the 2 buttons on the right side do the same thing and you must press a button on the top left to get to a function that you need.  It's more difficult to press the button on the top left side while you are running, especially if you wear the band a little loose.  When you press the buttons on the left side with the band not fastened super tight, then the whole watch shifts on your arm which makes it seem like you have to chase it down your arm til it hits your wrist bone to catch it.  There are 4 buttons on the sides plus the large button on the bottom of the face.  Don't know why they couldn't have just shifted some of the functions to work with the other buttons available.  Just not a great design.Also, the band on this watch is molded onto the watch.  If your band breaks you will not be able to replace just the band.  The whole watch will be garbage.  The basic time, date, alarm is all fine for every day use.  For running or tri training I would recommend shopping around for something else, especially if you are someone who wears reading glasses these days.  I've noticed some of the other models do have print now around the face of the watch on the outside of the glass area.  I'm looking into some of those now just for running.  This one I will continue to use just for every day wear.  But for running I will be looking into getting some other model, and may have to go with a larger Men's model just to get numbers that are easier to read while running even though I would prefer a Women's model.  They just don't seem to make some of the Women's models with all the goodies that the men's models get or they make the numbers cramped to fit into the smaller face.Overall, good watch for basic every day use.  Not so good for running and not so good for over 40 eyesight.  Design with some functions really could be better.

I love this watch but after having my 3rd one go belly-up (I did say I loved it, so yes, I have bought it 3x) I am going to have to find a different model digital watch.Background:  I am a scientist and need a digital watch for work.What I love about this watch:-It has 24h time-It gives me both day of the week and date (while my coworkers get confused about what day it is, I never do!)-Love the timer-Love the alarms and indiglo-It looks nicer than your average digital watch.  I like both the black and light blue.What I don't love about this watch:-It's easy for the little ring that holds the strap in place to crack and break off.  This maybe the result of my wearing latex gloves at work and having to take them on/off over the watch numerous times each day.  But I still don't think it should do that.  A ponytail band does a decent job in lieu of the ring, but it kind of looks stupid.-My second watch died as soon as I went swimming in it.  In 5ft of water.  For an IronMan watch, I thought that was odd.-The faceplate on my third watch has completely detached from the strap.  It's ridiculous.  I'm going to have to crazy glue the watch to the strap and I shouldn't have to do that.  And I've only owned it since August (It's now November.)  I haven't treated this watch any different from the others.Bottom line:  I like the IronMan features, but the "sleek design" is not durable enough for me. :(
summary: Great features but not very durable

reviewText: I love this watch.  In fact, I just bought my second one.  It has a 50 lap timer, countdown timer, two alarms, two time settings and a good back light feature.  I have one complaint - the strap wears out and I don't think you can replace just the strap.  I wear this watch all the time - even sleeping and showering so I know it takes a beating.  I just wish you didn't have to replace the whole watch each time the strap wears out.
summary: Great watch, but strap wears out too quickly

reviewText: If you are a fan of the walk/run training of Jeff Galloway, this type of watch (with two interval timers) is essential. Just set the interval timers and switch from walking to running (or vice versa) every time you here the watch chime. I like the compact size of the watch. My only beef is that the chime is pretty quiet and I have to really listen for it. If you like to run with music, it would be hard to hear.

I've had my watch for probably 3 or 4 years now. I can't remember because I don't concern myself with it. I wear it everywhere. My parakeet is also inlove with it as a head-scratching post. I bought it to replace a similar watch given to me by my husband when we were expecting our son 9.5 years ago. (The ingiglo feature finally gave out.) The alarm features on the first watch were the best and I wanted that again! I could take a nap anywhere I needed to -- Contrary to some reviews, the alarm is more than enough to wake me up. Later on, it was just plain handy to have a timer, alarm, etc. right on my wrist wherever I went without the bulk of the big watches I'd seen before. Now, my 9.5-year-old son wants a watch with an alarm/timer so that he can remember to come home on time, so I'm getting him this because it's not as bulky, once again, as the men's watches.My only complaint is that it only has 3 alarms (my previous one had five), but that's just an inconvenience, not really a problem. I liked the fact that I had three consistent alarms and two variable, but I've learned to live with three total.

This watch is perfect for that Mother on the go. I use it for the gym, appointments, wake- up alarm, almost anything! I love the feel of the band, not sticky even when I am sweating. The light is perfect. No problems in the dark. The selections of colors, make this watch the most trendy of all. Good luck buying Amazon shoppers, if your looking for a watch for your wife and she is on the go like me this is the one.
I use this product as part of my training regieme.  It has helped me be the lean mean running machine that I am today.Becky.

I would have given this watch 5 stars, but the band sometimes comes loose from the strap that is designed to hold it securely in place. I lost my first Ironman Timex this way and had to buy another.I'm in Iraq right now, and I love the way it keeps my current time and the stateside time. I can easily toggle between the different time zones, and when I'm visiting the states, I just hold down the button for 5 seconds, and my secondary time, becomes my primary time.I also like the fact that I can set 3 different alarm times.
