It doesn't ring very loud, so I don't suggest using it to wake you up. I use it to remind me to do daily tasks.You will not be disappointed with this purchase.
I love my Timex ironman triathlon!  It's such a cool, functional watch.  It's light-weight, comfortable and easy to use.

I am about to purchase my fourth ironman watch by Timex.  The band separates from the face of the watch every time.  Repeat: every time.  While I'm peeved each time I have to buy a new one, I still do. They last about one to two years.  At ~ $35 a pop, I just have to consider it a disposable watch.  This watch provides me with exactly what I'm looking for:  interval timing for my run/walk method of running, time, date, an alarm, a sporty look, and so light weight and comfortable that I never take it off.  Literally, never.  Until the band breaks -again - of course.  If you can accept that you are purchasing a product with a limited life-span - it's a great watch.

I've had this watch for about a month and so far, so good. I train in the ocean twice a week and this watch fits comfortably under my wetsuit without damaging it. I've also used this watch on my bike-run workouts and the watch itself is lightweight and doesn't chafe. The numbers are easy to read and the I love the feature that saves the workouts for that day. Perfect watch for me.

I got my watch before a trip to another time zone so I could keep track of the different times and the time it took to fly, etc.  It worked perfectly!  It has 2 time zones and it's very easy to switch back and forth between the 2.  The Chrono function allowed me to keep track of each leg of my trip along with a running total by using the Lap feature.  After reading the instructions I found all of the functions easy to use.The title says it is a 50-Lap memory watch, which is correct, but some of the information in the Amazon description and the instruction manual say 100-Lap, which is not correct.It's sporty but pretty sleek and feminine so it still looks nice on your wrist.  I've had it for a month and I have not noticed any visible signs of wear and tear.I think I read a review that mentioned the Chrono function is off by a few seconds when you press the Lap button, which can be a problem for serious athletes who need to keep close track of times.  However, when I used the feature I noticed that it's NOT actually off, it just appears to pause for a few seconds and then when the time shows up again it has accurately kept track of the time so I don't think it's an issue.Overall I'm very pleased with this watch and it has been great for my purpose!
Perfect size and weight for my interval training and long runs. I've had ironman before and this one more than lives up to my expectation and then some.

Timex Women's Ironman Triathlon Sleek 50/100 Watch #T59201I have really enjoyed this watch.  I have been wearing it nonstop since I bought it four months ago. I am deployed to Iraq, so I wear it everyday - in the shower, running, at the gym, at work, sleeping, swimming laps, etc.  (I literally don't take it off ever.) I don't even notice it's there.  It has one small crack and scratch from a not so graceful jump off a truck, but no problems otherwise.  It is extremely comfortable, nice small size, great features.  My only issue with it is that the alarm is somewhat soft and very high-pitched.  I have decreased high-frequency hearing (thanks to US Army), so I don't hear it unless I pay close attention.

This watch is great if you don't need GPS.  I got it over a year ago to help me with intervals during running practice, and it has worked great for the purpose.  I like its design and even like wearing it as an everyday watch.The face tells the date and time, with hours and even seconds.  I've mostly used the interval setting to create two intervals of different lengths; when time is up there's a subtle beep to tell you that a new interval has begun.  The sound is pretty quiet so if you are wearing headphones and listening to music you might not hear it.  There's also a stopwatch option, and a night light.  Controls are pretty easy.  I haven't used it in a pool so I don't know how watertight it is. Unlike other reviewers, I haven't had any issues with the wristband.

I literally never take this watch off. I wear it to shower, swim, workout, sleep, everything. I even wear it to formal affairs. I love the different time zones (great for friends who are studying abroad), the multiple alarms, saving workouts, the timer, and the separate interval timer (they must've had fartleks in mind when they made the watch).The band is the only gripe I have with this watch. I purchased one a few years ago, but the strap came apart from the watch face when I wiped out while surfing. Water got into the head, and the display shut off.I've had so many Ironman watches that I just replaced the broken watch with the exact same model. I literally NEVER take it off - only when a friends need a chronograph - and I discovered this morning that the band is splitting and cracking on the underside. It's been over 18 months that I've had this watch, so maybe it's just wear and tear, but I seem to like the fabric band better.I'm asking for a new Ironman for Christmas before this strap breaks and I'm naked without a watch!

I bought the Casio STR300 to replace a ten year old Timex Ironman that was recently stolen. I went to the Casio because the entry level Ironman no longer does splits in the stop watch mode. Over all I've found the Casio to be a worthy replacement for keeping track of my time when I run, swim or bike.The good:First and foremost, sixty split times! That's a lot of splits, but essential for someone like me that is presently training for a triathlon by swimming laps in a pool.Second, one thing that I really like about the Casio over and above my old Timex is the way that after an hour passes by in the stop watch mode, I don't lose the hundredths of a second from the face of the watch. Once my old Timex would hit the one hour mark, the hundredths of a second numbers would disappear to make room for an hours column. Casio avoids this by putting the hours above the minutes so that it doesn't have to shift the minutes over to make room. I think is a very clever solution.Third, the price, this watch is packed with features for less than the entry level Timex Ironman. Granted, most of the features are lost on me. I'm hearing impaired so I don't really care about the five alarms. Nor do I use the countdown mode. But I don't have a whole lot of money and this watch is worth every penny that I paid for it.The bad:The build quality of this watch seems inferior to the Timex Ironman series. Maybe it just feels different and will last just as long. I won't know that until ten years down the line. If this Casio is still going, then I'll change my mind on this point.I find the button to trigger a split difficult to press. With my old Timex, it was pretty easy to hit the split button while doing a flip-kick at the end of the pool to turn around. With this thing, I miss more often than not. Often times I have to stop swimming and hit the button a few times to get it. This may be user error on my part and perhaps given enough time I will learn to hit the button in just the right way. I've only had this problem underwater. When running or cycling, hitting the button is pretty easy. If the button were as easy to hit as my old Timex was, I'd probably have given this watch 5 starts.

I've had this watch for around 5-6 months. My previous watch, a Timex, lasted a few years but eventually died due to water seal failure. I can't yet comment on the long-term durability of this watch as I haven't used it much in water/outdoors. Anyway, here's the rundown:Hardware- Very cool, perhaps even futuristic-looking body and digits. Main reason why I bought it and I'm satisfied with it.- Color is nice and looks almost identical to the picture, although the strap is slightly darker than shown.- Strap is hard but not stiff. It takes a little getting used to and if worn super tight the buckle will bite into skin. So I wear it looser, and it doesn't usually slip.- This is a small watch. Both the strap and face are small. I have a thin wrist so it fits me fine but adults with thicker wrists will have trouble keeping it on.- Button placement is unconventional but I like it. My gripe with the buttons in that the top and bottom buttons -- start/stop and lap, respectively -- are difficult to push. These are used for other functions, namely cycling through hour/minute so it can be frustrating when setting alarms and such.- The light is possibly my biggest gripe with the watch, second only to the buttons. It's an okay light -- kind of greenish -- but lasts for just two seconds... what!? Massive inconvenience when trying to set up a stopwatch or timer in a dark area. This would not be a good watch to get if you expect to use it in dark locations often.- Good water-resistance, although testing was limited.Software- The watch display is broken into three compartments, designated by two horizontal blue lines. Check out the picture to see what I'm talking about. What this means is that features are displayed in the top two compartments and the time is displayed in the bottom compartment. This is GREAT. So I can be setting my alarm and still know what the current time is. The only section the "universal time" is not displayed is when I'm flipping through pace records (see below).- There are six "sections," if you will. Sections can be navigated by pressing the bottom left button and a beep is heard. When I finish cycling through, a beep of a higher pitch is heard to signify that I've reached the first section. This is a great, subtle feature.- Sections are (in order): Time/Date/Year, Stopwatch, Records, Timer, Alarm, Time (same as first but no date/year)--- Time/Date/Year: What you'd expect. Watch supports both 12-hour and 24-hour. No apparent support for multiple clocks, which is kind of irritating but not a big deal.--- Stopwatch: Noticeable beeps for starting (three fast beeps) and stopping (one long beep) which is nice. There's some kind of lap feature but I haven't used it much.--- Records: I haven't used this at all. I'm not a runner. :) Looks like it saves Stopwatch history and orders it by date. It appears to store a lot of records (28 at least).--- Timer: Your typical timer except seconds can't be set, gah! This is a bizarre and annoying restriction. Other than that the timer is fine.--- Alarm: There are five alarms, which is great. When an alarm is activated a little icon is displayed all throughout the watch. The first (and only first) alarm appears to have a snooze setting, but I haven't used it. The alarm sound is a simple beep rhythm: 2 beeps, pause, 2 beeps, pause, etc. When I had it on while I slept I had trouble hearing it. It's loud enough to be heard normally but it was too quiet when under covers. That was easily fixed when I placed it on a counter beside my bed. My only complaint here is that the alarm lasts for a measly ten seconds.--- Time: Looks like this is just a cosmetic feature for those who don't want a crowded display. Personally I think it's silly.Outstanding Pros- Slick appearance, color; neat button placement.- Time is always visible when browsing through watch.- Stopwatch/records could prove useful if I ever take up running. ;)- Beeps are intelligently designed.- Lots of alarms.Outstanding Cons- Top/bottom buttons difficult to press.- Light duration is a joke.- Can't specify seconds in timer.- Alarm noise could last a little longer.Overall: Great consumer watch for the price. I might be irked if it costed more, but $21 is a steal.Hope this review helped! Let me know if there's anything specific you'd like to look at.

I've been using a Palm Pilot since before I started regularly wearing a watch, so my review is a bit biased toward the idea that humans cannot live well under the pressure of modern demands without an external brain extension.That said, this watch is one of the best things I've ever bought for myself. Its benefits far outweigh its drawbacks.Those drawbacks are:* Tiny, tiny screen. Can be hard to read. Not for use by people with poor close-up vision! A magnifying glass, either physical or software (like Teal Magnify) helps with this.* BIG. I am a small-boned woman, and the watch face is as wide as my arm. I have gotten compliments on how stylish it looks, but I've also been mocked for strapping a boat anchor to my wrist. Main issue for me has been that it is too big to slide under the cuff of a long-sleeved shirt.* Short battery life. I forgot to charge it three nights in a row, and had to restore all my data from a backup the next day. (Fortunately, that process is really easy -- just keep it synced to your PC or Mac and data loss on the watch is no reason to panic.) It really does need to be charged at least every other day. On the other hand, if you have a cell phone, a Palm Pilot, or other device that needs frequent charging, the watch can just be added to those habits; it's possible to find equipment to charge it from a wall outlet, a USB port, or even a car lighter port.* NOT AT ALL water-resistant. This is not a watch you can put on and forget about. You cannot leave it on in the shower, or fail to protect it in heavy rain.Those issues aside, the thing is just outright useful. It will run most software made for the Palm, excepting software for OS 5. There isn't much software made specifically for it, but what is out there is good.Its main benefit it that it's strapped to you, all day every day, so unlike a larger full-size Pilot, it won't be in your purse or the pocket of your other jacket at home when you need it. It doesn't really have enough memory to fill some of the functions I demand of my T|T3 (English-Japanese-Spanish dictionaries & translation, Mapopolis, Office file editing and storage) but it has plenty of room for daily things: multiple alarms that actually tell you WHY your watch just went off (through datebook), phone numbers, email addresses, birthday reminders, a game or an ebook for emergency entertainment, and Handy Shopper -- shopping list freeware I can't do without any more.For example, imagine that you've just discovered you're out of salt. You don't have to find a pen and dig out a grocery list; just make note of it on your wrist. Next time you're in the grocery store, that item will show up with all the others you've put in at the touch of a drop-down menu. Or imagine you've called Information for a number but can't find a pen. Why bother? Jot it down on your wrist. Thought of something you need to do tomorrow? Friend just told you title and author of a book you want to read? No matter what the datum is, no matter where you are, you can finally track all of this on the spot. No more writing phone numbers on your hands and trying to remember not to wash them off until you get home!Seriously. It has too many drawbacks to succeed as a casual purchase; most watches perform specialized watch functions better, and most Palm Pilots perform serious palmtop data-crunching or -storage better. but in those two little niches -- stuff you want to write down now before it can be forgotten and stuff you need to be reminded of with text instead of just something going "beepbeepbeep" -- this thing really shines. And the more you remember to use it, the less you'll ever be able to do without it again.

****14-month followup****The good: Case, strap, and screen all in great shape despite daily wear. Has survived miscellaneous drops and brief immersions in water with no apparent damage or effect.The annoying: Needs charging daily. The screen is still small! When I ride my bike on a bumpy road, the Palm OS crashes, and if I don't notice quickly and reset it, the battery goes dead (and then I have to re-enter all the setup data, and reload it). Lately it has been crashing badly (total restart) every couple of days, for no apparent reason.********Below is the original Nov. 2005 review:I bought the Abacus PDA a couple of weeks ago, mainly to replace the shredded memo pad I'd been trying to keep in my pocket, and to synchronize smoothly with my Microsoft Outlook system at work. Overall, it's everything I expected and it has become my almost-constant companion.  A few specific comments:- Battery life: The biggest problem with it. The battery life bar shows empty after two days, even though I only use the PDA function a couple minutes a day. Maybe it's like a gas gauge, and you really have another day before it dies? If you set it so the LCD display turns off when not in PDA mode (instead of showing the watch face), the life goes to about 4 days. By having the watch application running, you can see the time by simply pressing the enter button. Charging seems very fast, however, and it doesn't seem like you have to have it plugged into a computer to charge. Sadly, it did not charge from my laptop; it had to be plugged into AC.- The watch is pretty big. Notice that nowhere are the dimensions shown in the specs? The actual size (ignoring the band) is 2.25" long x 1.88" wide by 0.50" thick, more or less. It's also quite heavy, with the stainless case. Display is 1" square. It looks kind of bulky on my fairly large wrist; it would look absurd on my wife's slender wrist. But those of you who carry purses everywhere can get a normal-size PDA.- Entering data is hard with the tiny screen. Amazingly, the keyboard works pretty well, though I had to run the digitizer calibration option a couple times before the letters I hit lined up with the ones on the screen. However, they're hard to see in dim light, and the touch screen doesn't respond as predictably as I'd like, sometimes giving a letter and sometimes not. I tried Jot briefly, with moderate success, and may try it more later.- You can look things up entirely with the buttons (no stylus), which is great.- I wish it was waterproof; I have to take it off at the health club, etc. But I've dropped it on concrete, banged it into a bunch of things (it's a lot bigger than my old watch, after all), and washed my hands while wearing it (oops!), getting it wet, all with no apparent damage.- Syncronization with Outlook was a breeze to set up, and takes only a couple of seconds. Now I have about 500 contacts, my schedule, and a dozen lists on my wrist. Plus a calculator. Cool!
summary: Effective and well-designed, but could be even better (w/1 year followup)

I have always been interested in the coolest gadget watches and over the years I have had the pleasure of owning some great ones including one of the rare Casio Scientific calculator watches, the remote control watch as well as the Casio WristCamera Color (which I use even today)So the WristPDA was a natural progression for me. I had been interested in it since it was announced a couple of years back but the pricing (> $200) kind of held be back!. But the moment I saw the price drop on Amazon, well, I pushed the button and now I have this cool one too!First off, I should make it clear that overall I am well satisfied by this great little gadget. For the price I paid (79.99 at amazon) I think it is well worth the money!The only thing I was worried about while waiting for it to arrive was its size on my wrist (since I have a small'ish wrist, my WristCamera watch felt a little too bulky for comfortable use). Anyway I am glad to report that even though the Abacus is not small by any standards, its sleek design definitely does not feel bulky at all and it looks real nice on my wrist!!Since it is Palm OS powered, usage of this watch is quite similar to the usual Palm powered PDA's (the grayscale versions). The Font, although quite small, is crystal clear to read and I did not have difficulty in using any application. The included stylus although completely functional does feel uncomfortable if you use it for long. I recommend a full size stylus whenever possible.I was able to find and load quite a lot of standard applications onto this watch. Just look for the grayscale versions with support for Palm OS 4.x. Most of the freeware games work as well (although the ones dependent on the Hard keys on a standard PDA may need to be tweaked).The IrDA functions work well too and I was able to sync my cellphone addressbook with the WristPDA quite easily with a few clicks.The Handwriting recognition (Jot) is amazing as well. Infact it is so good and fast at recognizing NORMAL writing style, Initially I had difficulty 'unlearning' the special Grafitti style letter writing used by older PDA's. But if you are a Grafitti fan, then the wristPDA does support that mode as well.I only have 2 concerns with this watch:- The first one is the relative lack of any protection for the sensitive touch-screen face of the watch. For a normal PDA, there is an option of a case/pouch. But as a watch, the face is always exposed and there is a high probability of scratches/nicks from the elements. I now use a PDA screen protector film (cut to size) for reducing this problem.- The second one is the lack of any water resistance. Even rain is supposed to be dangerous for the watch! So be careful while singing in the shower with this watch :-)The other minor issue I have is the mandatory 2 day recharge period. But hey the watch is not doing anything in the night... might as well recharge it!But overall I think Abacus/Amazon deserves a hand in making such a great piece of equipment for a relatively affordable price.

Its kinda cool for a PDA on your wrist, but the battery doesn't last for more than a day at most...  I'd use it more if I didn't need to charge it every night.  Plus all the data (at least on mine) gets erased if the battery dies.  It was a nice try, but not good enough.

Being a long-time PalmOS user, I have become dependent on having my device with me.  This beauty is small (very, very small) for a PDA; but it is a bit large for a wristwatch.  Coworkers who have seen me wearing it but did not know its function have mentioned that they were impressed with the size of the digits when the Abacus is in "watch mode" - and commented that their assumption was that I chose the watch for that purpose.  Ha!  Little did they know!Most of the apps that I crave to have with me (e.g. RPN, Planetarium, and the OliveTree Bible reader) work perfectly.  Besides the standard main apps - which are somewhat enhanced with large fonts - there is a watch application with system prefs that permit selection of alternatives.There are a few downsides, but you have to expect some compromises in a device this tiny.  The battery really needs to be recharged daily.  This is not so much the problem that it might seem when you consider that it can charge from a standard USB cable connected to your PC.  The recharge time is short (less than an hour a day) and I have not found it to be a problem, though I was concerned at first.  Once you get past the very small display, the only other obstacle is the lack of a Graffiti area.  This is offset by the fact that Jot is provided in ROM and it is quite functional.I really would not recommend this as one's only PDA, or for a first time PalmOS user (mostly because the display is too small for extended use); but if you're like me you never want to be without your trusty Palm. Existing Palm V users will be impressed to know that the Abacus has nearly the same OS version and RAM plus a faster processor.Regrettably, some of the apps that I might want to use - BugMe and MessagEase - do not get along with Jot.  Although Jot can be turned off, I find the Abacus to be more useful when sitting in traffic if leave Jot turned on.Overall, I am now hooked on the Abacus.  My most important information and applications are always conveniently with me.  Yeah... its geeky; but no more so than carrying around a stupid cell phone!

reviewText: I received my Fossil Abacus watch a few weeks ago and have been using it every day ever since.  Software compatibility with Palm Pilot apps is excellent.  Basically, anything that can run on version 4.0 of the Palm OS can run on this watch.  Only drawback (if you want to call it that) is that this watch has the full 160x160 display of the Palm Pilot shrunk down to the size of a quarter - and as many apps use small fonts in the first place, you probably need good eyesight if you plan on using this as more than just a watch.I currently run Weasel Reader, a free and open source eBook reader that uses it's own open zTxt format.  Written for a full-sized Palm Pilot, the text sized ends up very small on the Abacus in order to fit about 40 chars by 20 lines on a watch display.  I have about 5 books stored on the watch and at about 100-200k each, that's hardly 1/8 of the available memory.  I have no trouble reading books this way but in direct sunlight, it sometimes requires trying different angles to get a good view.The watch face is an actual touch-screen, which by itself is exceedingly cool in a watch, and within the watch band there's a small stylus (an extra is included in the box) - but it's a little tedious to use and I usually use a normal PDA stylus instead.USB hotsync is amazingly fast for this watch.  A few megabytes transfer over in a few seconds.  Another cool aspect is the watch uses a standard mini USB port for _BOTH_ data transfer and recharging!  That's right, plug your watch into any computer with a USB port and within an hour, it's fully charged up for a couple more days.For developers, Fossil provides an SDK that can be used with either Codewarrior or the free (and superior) IDE that Palm OS Developers Suite from PalmSource.  One of the unique features of this SDK is that a developer can create their own watch faces, which are simply programs that are called every minute to update the screen.  This opens up a lot of interesting possibilities such as a watch face that shows moon phases, tides, or perhaps randomly generated graphic designs, especially with it's 160x160 16-grayscale display.
summary: It's a Palm PIlot on a watch, what more do you need to know?

reviewText: I really like this watch, but battery ruins all the fun. 18 hours is about the most I can get out of it. I've had this watch for about a month and it's been an indispensable tool (I owned a Philips Nino running Windows CE before this). With this watch/PDA, you don't have to worry about carrying your bulky PDA  to every meeting or to your Doctor's office for checking your availability or be reminded of your upcoming tasks. If you need a basic palm PDA on your wrist for everyday use, this is one of the very few products out there for you. BTW, don't forget to install Avantgo on it! I get my free daily New York Times, CNET news, local weather forcast, movie and book reviews, and much more on my wrist PDA every morning when I synch with my desktop! Wassup is another handy add-on written exclusively for this watch.Pros:-Has all the essential PDA functionality in a small form factor-Syncs flawlessly with MS outlook (I've checked outlook 2000 and 2003)-Very speedy USB sync (a matter of seconds on USB 2!)-Can run quite a few of the available Palm programs on its 160x160, 16 gray level screen (Note that it's running the older Palm OS ver 4.1)-It also updates my home computer outlook with my work computer when I synch at home after synching at work.-It'll be with you everywhere! (Remember the last time you were forced to be somewhere you didn't want to be and you were bored out of your mind wishing you had something to read or to play with?)-Surprisingly, I found the included tiny stylus pretty handy and practical!Cons:-Short battery life: If you want to use its PDA function on a daily basis, you HAVE to charge it almost everyday! However I don't find it inconvenient as I synch it with my desktop through USB port everyday (as you do with any other PDA) and it packs enough juice through the same USB cable if you leave it connected for a while.-The touch screen is hard to operate (sometimes it misses even precisely targeted stylus taps) but hey what did you expect from such a tiny screen?-It takes quite a few keystrokes to navigate from the watch mode to say your calendar-The audio beep is weak-A little bulky especially if you have a smaller frame, however it draws a lot of attention and gives you an opportunity to brag about it!Conclusion: I just paid $80 for this gadget on Amazon and for that price it's been worth every penny. I hope that Fossil continues working on this promising watch and have improved models out. I'll be buying one for sure!

reviewText: The winder truly is silent (unlike some others I've tried). It has a really neat way of holding onto the watch by simply pressing a button, although it's important to center the watch. Otherwise the winder becomes out of balance and the winder makes a thumping noise from going too far in one direction. The winding motion is bi-directional and is a very accurate winding motion similar to wearing the watch naturally. I don't think it would make a very reasonable traveling winder though because of it's size and the fact it has no cover to protect a watch in transit. Although if you're traveling with a large suitcase and can spare the room it would be nice to have once you arrived at your destination. Wolf Designs offers some really nice Winding Boxes at very reasonable prices at (...) but I believe they deal with dealers and Jewelers only. I have no problem recommending this winder though. You can always go by a (...)to see one in person. I bought the 3 year replacement agreement just because Sharper Image is so good about honoring them worldwide. I would avoid "cheapie" bargain winding boxes. They are NO VALUE AT ALL. Plastic gears and junky motors that burn up in a few days to a few weeks and an "Oh well..." type of attitude about replacing them. Of course who'd want another one. This winder shows that you don't have to drop a bundle for a name brand to get a decent product that does exactly what it's suppose to do. Sometimes they can be had at quite a bargain at Sharper Image.com/outlet. Although you're pretty much stuck with a 90 day warranty if you go that route. It always nice later on to be able to walk into ANY Sharper Image store and have them replace something right there on the spot just by pulling your phone number up in the computer. And no, I'm not a Sharper Image junkie. It's just once in a while they come up with something that really fits the bill. God help 'em if brushed aluminum and plastic ever get outlawed. Although in this case the brushed aluminum and black leather go really well together. The 6 minute cycle per hour is a good setting for Rolexes and most Swiss time pieces.

reviewText: I've had 5.10's for the last 10 years now and most recently a pair of these shoes (~4 years old).  They are spectacular for long climbing days or indoor where you don't want to keep taking them on and off.  The toe and edge are very good on small holds, but not quite like a pair of elf shoes would be.  They smear very very well, and I have no problem stemming, chimney-ing or doing crack jams with them.  They can be slightly loose for heel hooks, but really they are designed for comfort and too tight a heel isn't comfy long term.I only climb up to 5.11 indoor and 10s and 11s outdoor, so you can use that info to put this in context.I am sorry to see all the bad reviews just on sizing.  Yes, climbing shoes are snug, and generally you have to break them in, so they are not comfy on the first try.  My last pair of Spires took 3 weeks to shape to my foot, but they were a glove thereafter.  Read up on climbing shoe sizing before you buy, or go to a walk in store.  It's worth getting it right once, then you can buy easier online.My sizing suggestion for this type of shoe is to have your big toe bent, but your second toe just firmly touching.  For 5.10s, that is usually the same as your street shoe size +- 1/2 size.  All toes bent should be reserved for elf shoes in my opinion, and no toes bent is for beginners and long scrambles.
summary: Great grip, comfortable enough to leave on between climbs

reviewText: I buy lots of watches here on Amazon.  Mostly for gifts for friends in Thailand.  I always find a great price range and nice looking watches.  Shop here before you buy. Nice watch.

I needed a watch for swimming laps as there is no clock near the pool and I refuse to bring my phone to the pool. I initially bought a more expensive waterproof one that lasted less than six months before needing a new battery. When I replaced the battery, there went the water resistance and I wound up destroying the watch.I was at Target shopping for a new watch. This one caught my eye since it says it has a ten year battery. I figured that even if it was on the shelf for a year or two, I should be good for about seven or eight years. It is water resistant like the description says. I have had this watch for over a year and a half and I swim 2-3 times a week. I swim at night so I "charge" up the glow in the dark areas in bright light before I start swimming and I don't have a problem seeing the time when I take breaks to see what time it is. If I don't "charge" it up first, it is difficult (but not impossible) to see the time in the low light of the pool area.The only time I wear a watch is when I am swimming or when I am on a plane, so this watch does not get daily use (my cellphone is my watch). As other reviewers have mentioned, the black metal guard does scratch up - it did so after a few months. Before I went on my last trip, I took a black Sharpie to the silver spots showing through, which worked for a few weeks. By then I was back to only using it swimming so I really don't care.Some reviewers complain that it is a modern watch so it should have light like most modern watches. Well, if it had a light, it would not be a "10 year battery" watch - its battery would be depleted by the light so it would not last 10 years. That is why it does not have a light. I understand the trade-off so I don't have a problem with that.Another reviewer complained it lost time. Mine has not lost any noticeable time. The only time I have changed the time on it is for daylight savings time and for time zone changes when I travel.This loses a half a star for the fact that it is difficult to read in low-light situations if it is not "charged up". They could have put a little more of that glow-in-the dark stuff on the hour hand. It also lost a half of a star for the (minor) scratches on the guard and the fact that it isn't that pretty of a watch - but I am not complaining about that one since I bought it for function, not aesthetics - if I really wanted a pretty watch that badly, I would have bought a woman's watch instead of a man's watch. It is a masculine watch. Women's watched tend to be dainty and don't hold up to my swimming along with the hot tub.Like most analog watches with a date window, you have to manually change the date at the end of the month if the month does not have 31 days since it automatically cycles through its 31 days. It is not smart enough to know the month has 28, 29, 30, or 31 days - but it is an analog watch - there is no computer in it. It does not get any dings for something that is within the limitations of the type of watch it is. If you don't want to change the date (which is easy to do), don't get an analog watch or get an analog watch without a date window.A reviewer did complain that the instructions were difficult. I can't say anything about the instructions. I never read them. This watch works like every other analog watch I have ever owned. You pull out the metal knob halfway to change the date and all the way to change the time. The date will only change if you turn it in one direction. The time will change in both directions. If you have ever had an analog watch before, you won't have a problem.A major plus of this watch is its price. It is cheap and it will last you a long time.

The lighted and large display (for the light, one must push a button) is easily read, though I believe Timex has a newer model that has a 'night-light' feature which doesn't depend on you pushing a button to light the display.  That would be my next watch whenever this one goes out.  The control buttons are easy to find and push, though the printing to tell what they do are tiny and barely legible to my 44 yo myopic eyes without a magnifier.  So, I've learned to memorize what each button does through repetition.  The watch is easy to use intuitively, and I highly recommend it.

As always, Timex Ironman watches are great. I had my old one over 10 years and many marathons, 1/2 marathons, etc. Bought this one for my daughter in law, also a runner...She will get many years of use. The only problem was the delivery, it took over 7 days before the order was shipped and than waited another  week+ for delivery
summary: Great Timex Ironman watch, Poor delivery

reviewText: I have several of these Timex Watches. They are familiar and easy to use. I am looking forward to wearing the white in the summer months.
Great watch.  I have it in another color, too.  It's only annoying when you have to change times and have to check the brochure for the sequence of moves.
This watch is exactly what I needed. It is for travel purposes when I can't wear my nice watch! Recommend it!
really love this watch. lightweight and goes with everything. easy to use and reasonable on price. recommend to anyonewho is wondering
So, far I really like this watch. I'm sure the white will get dirty and change colors but so far so good.
This is exactly what i was looking for - a watch that looks good and is easy to use.  I used it for my first marathon and it was fantastic, however, I didn't use the 'laps' feature.

I love this watch! It serves many needs for me. I use the stop watch often, and use the alarm clock feature as a back up, when traveling. I also enjoy having the indigo light, for seeing the time in dark places.
Love the way it fits. Love the way it feels. Love the way it looks! Couldn't be happier with this purchase!!!

I really like this watch. It does exactly what I wanted it to and it is very cute. However, the band disappointed me a little. It does get dirty pretty easily. I have found that a Mr. Clean Magic Eraser does the trick for cleaning it up though!

Good bang for your buck, I'm wearing it daily and use it while swimming laps.  Best inexpensive sports watch I ever had,  very comfortable to wear and reliable.  Wish it also tracks heart rate and calorie consumption.
summary: Best sports watch I ever have

reviewText: I love the Timex Ironman watches. I have found them to be reliable, easy to set with a great face display which is easy to read at a glance. I got this one mainly because of the silver face bezel and the white band to wear for special occasions where I didn't want one that was so bold in size or color. I love the way the strap loop is designed to catch in the strap hole to prevent slipping around. I really like this watch a lot and it is just what I wanted for a second watch.
summary: Timex Women's T5K515 Ironman / White Resin Strap Watch

reviewText: I received this about a week ago and so far have worn it everyday.  I really like it for when I'm dressed super casual, i.e. jeans and a hoodie, or when I'm working out.  I'm hoping the band doesn't turn green like others said theirs did.  So far it is a great watch!

I received my Timex T5E951 about 2 months ago.  Very functional and easy to use.  I love it.  I had no problem with it so far.  The numbers are VERY sharp and the indiglo light is a very nice improvement over the old system (light in the corner).  The wrist band has a locking system that prevents the end from sticking out, and that was a good surprise!!!  The picture on amazon.com is not very accurate as far as color though.  I would recommend a peak at the Timex website for more accurate pictures.
I purchased his watch to wear when hiking. It is lightweight, waterproof, has light to view time in darkness and is very durable.

I've purchased this watch three times now--bought the first one eight years ago, repurchased when the silver part fell off, and again when i lost it at a cross country meet.. the functions are simple to use and convenient, small enough to be unassuming. I wear it every day, almost never take it off, which is probably why the silver part fell off on the first one... waterproof, mostly, and comfortable. it's not exactly stylish, but since i rely on it so much, that's not really my main concern.
Metal piece on watch band that keeps it around the wrist broke the first day I wore it very disappointed!!!!!
summary: watch band broke the first day

reviewText: This watch does all that I need this type to do.  Great for the out doors and late night.  The timer is tops.

Sure this watch isn't the highest quality, but it's at a good price and has great functionality, durability and looks. I love this for running, hiking, swimming, and I even dove with it once and it held up beautifully.

Nice watch! great price too! Packaged properly and received quickly.  I broke the band on my old version of this watch and I thought it would be cheaper to buy a new one (at this price) than to track down a replacement band.  I'm glad I did it and I would purchase from this vendor again.  Very pleased with the transaction.

I has always loved and have purchased this Timex watch over the years! I have never seen this color option and love it! I will continue to look for this watch in the years to come. It's a great product.

My digital watch broke while I was deployed and I could conveniently order this one.  It arrived pretty quickly.  I chose Timex because the one I had before this worked forever (but this one is cuter because of the light blue accent).  The functional part of the old watch still worked but the band that held the strap broke so I used duck tape on the old one until this arrived.  I still use it now and it matched my AF blue uniform :)
I love these watches and this makes shopping so easy. Have worn these for many years. Easy to set and use.

I have owned 2 other Ironman watches. The strap designs were different, and the straps stretched over time, failing to stay around the watch face. I like the features and easy use of Ironman watches, so I hope this one lasts better.
I like this watch, but I wish that it was a little bit bigger... I do use a magic eraser to clean the white bands.

I have owned several Ironman watches by Timex going back ages.  They used to be so complicated to use, but I needed the features it offers.  The Indiglo is better, hoping it will lead to longer battery life.  The stopwatch (chronograph) is much, much easier to use because this one tells you how to reset it, rather than guessing.  But what I am delighted about most of all is that the numbers are clearer on the face than ever before.  As far as alarms go, I can now tell which ones are on and which ones are off, as the watch TELLS me.  I always wear the bands out, so I give these watches a lot of wear and tear, feeling that I am getting my money's worth.  This watch fills the bill and the color choice was fabulous on the Amazon site.
summary: Easiest Ironman watch I have ever owned

reviewText: I am used to the wider band so this did not make my cut. This band is that of the typical ladies' band. I sold it to my clinical and she loves it!
I have used it for 2 month and so far have no issues using it in the pool. I wish the lap number was bigger so easier to read under water. Overall, a good quality sports watch.
summary: good quality, no issues for swimming.

reviewText: It is the perfect size for my 10 year old son, and a great watch. I always wear an Timex Ironman watch.
summary: Perfect for my 10 year old son.

reviewText: I had this watch in blue. The wrist band broke after 2 years, but I suppose that's acceptable for the price. I bought this same watch in white and the band is discolored. I'm a nurse so it gets soap, foam, and all sorts of other stuff on it. I thought this would stand up to heavy duty use but no luck. I'll get a darker color next time. I gave it 4 stars because I do recommend the watch, just not in white.

This is a really nice and easy to use watch especially for the money.  I bought it for my 11 year old daughter and it is perfect for her.  The buttons are easy to use and very intuitive.  We did not even need to use the instructions to figure everything out.  Would definitely buy again.

Returned this when I realized it couldn't do what I wanted which is beep at intervals. It's fine for a basic watch but doesn't do anything extraordinary. Got the Timex T59201 50-lap which does the interval training that I wanted.

I'm addicted to this watch and let me tell you--I use and abuse it.  It's been on my wrist for 2yrs10mos; honestly I can recall less than a dozen times I've had it off.  This watch has been to Burning Man (extremely harsh conditions) and around the world (18 countries, 35 cities).  It's been on hikes and runs.  It's been submersed without abandon.  I use nearly every single function, constantly.  I have never had another sport-type watch and yet I didn't have to read the instructions in order to use it.  I find the functions very intuitive.When I say I use the functions I don't mean that I used the timer once to hard-boil some eggs.  I mean that I actually USE all the functions ALL DAY LONG.  I consult all three time zones daily because I have/had a husband in Iraq and have friends and family abroad.  I use the chrono/lap four times per day to monitor the baby's naps.  I use the timer at least six times/day for the laundry, heating bottles, and with the "repeat at end" function to remind me to drink water every two hours.  (I could use a 2nd timer, to be honest.)  I use the alarms and love that they can be set for only weekdays, only weekends, or every day.  (What a great idea!)  I use the nightlight every night since the baby is up at least once and, naturally, I open one bleary eye to check the time.  Regarding the night light I wish the light stayed on a little longer and I find the flick light function to be worthless.  You'll break bones in your wrist flicking it hard enough to make the light come on.This watch has been on the slopes and in rainstorms, pools, hot tubs, and the ocean.  It's been on my wrist for every shower I've ever taken and submersed in dishwater twice a day.  The highest compliment I can give the water-resistance feature is that I have never hesitated before doing something while wearing the watch.  I just assumed it would work and it did.  I have never had a water problem with it.I replaced the battery once, I think.  (Maybe twice?)  I haven't had the band breakage issues that others have had, possibly because I never take it off and thus never "stress" the band.  The silver paint around the face began to wear off shortly after I got it and it's looking pretty WT right about now but the plastic under the paint is sort of a metallic-ish tan/silver so it's not really too noticeable to other people unless they are really looking at my watch.  Demerits for that.The styling is definitely "sporty" and it doesn't translate well to dress clothes.  I covet those Tissot/TAG/etc metal casual watches but to be honest, I can't do without the precision chrono and timer let alone the awesomeness of never having to remember what day of the week (or month) it is because I can always just look at my wrist.  Why doesn't Timex make one of these in metal?  I don't mind the digital display, just sometimes would like something other than resin and rubber.After 2yrs10mos the band finally broke when my daughter pulled on it.  I'm ordering the exact same style and would pay ten time this much for the amount of use and functionality I got out of it.  Highly recommend.

I was very selective buying a watch because I had specific things I wanted and a price limit.So far I am very pleased with the watch and I haven't taken it off since I bought it several weeks ago.I love the timer, alarms (although I can't hear it if I'm sleeping but it's great for daily reminders), the chrono (I use for timing myself so I take shorter showers), and of course, keeping track of time.Finally: I LOVE that I can take it swimming, bathing, hand washing and all sorts of water shenanigans and it still works!Odd personal note: The sporty yet feminine look is oddly inspirational to work out (but that's just me).CONCERN:  I really like the little band that keeps the strap in place, but it looks a little fragile... It has (thankfully) stayed together but I have read reviews where this strap has broken and I can see this as a strong possibility.  :(
summary: I searched for hours for a watch that did what I want for what I could afford... And I picked this one.

reviewText: Great bargain. These do not go out of style. Timex stays current. Not oversized and great quality. Great for active people.

I've had Timex 30 Lap Ironman watches for years. My last one finally died (even with replacing the battery) after many years. These last - and for around $30, you can't go wrong. It's lightweight, has a durable strap and buttons are easy to press. The white one looks nice enough that it works as an accessory and not just looking like a typical sport watch. I have small wrists and this watch fits and looks great. I wear it daily and use it primarily for timing long distance runs, using the 'split' function. Love it.
summary: Bang for your buck, looks great too

reviewText: Works great, looks great and feels good on my wrist.  This is my second Ironman, the first one bit the dust after 10 years of good use, but the band finally broke in two.  I love the indigo lighting on this one.  Have not yet been in the water with it, but it won't be long now.
Has all the standard Ironman watch functions. The white strap is new and different from previous Timex watches. Nice watch!
I was looking for a durable inexpensive watch for a high school runner.  This was perfect and a great price.

I got this watch a little over a year ago and I was very satisfied with the product. The white band does begin to show a little bit of discoloration over time but its not too bad at all. As a disclaimer I will acknowledge that I don't treat the watch very well, so to speak. I wear it every single day, without fail, and anything I do, I do with the watch on, and that includes swimming in the ocean. Considering all I've done in this watch i'm highly impressed with how well the color holds up. For the most part, it is still very white. Aside from the white maintaining itself, I really like the look of the watch. The face of the watch is a good size that fits well on a small size wrist and the band easily adjusts to even the smallest wrist. Additionally, it can be worn with all attires, even fancy (okay maybe not to a black tie wedding, but you get the point.) It doesn't have the typical "sport watch" appearance and therefore works perfectly for everyday wear. However, if you use a watch this frequently, expect it to last only about a year, which is not bad at all considering the low price you pay for it. My watch is no longer water proof, but this only happened after a full year's use. Maybe it would still be water proof had i not swam in the ocean with it, etc. Additionally, the top silver piece has fallen off (in the ocean) but again, that probably isn't a common occurrence. All of the functions still work perfectly. Overall, a great buy, as long as you are aware you will be buying a new one after a year.

I'd give this 4.5 if I could, but that's not an option so I'll go with the "I love it" rating.  It's inexpensive, it's easy to set and to use, it's lightweight and very comfortable, it does everything you need, you can shower and swim and exercise and use power tools, no matter what you do you won't worry about damaging it.  I"m on my second, I wore the first for maybe five years but the strap broke a few years ago while I was living abroad and it was faster and cheaper to order a new watch from Amazon than to replace the strap. The only reason I lower my review is that the purple color is some sort of surface paint that has started to chip, this didn't happen on my earlier watch so I don't know if they changed the formula or I did something unusual.
I got this watch for my wife.  We have always liked the ironman watches.  She likes the color and functionality.
summary: nice price for a nice watch

reviewText: My wife has worn various Timex Ironman watches (with black bands) for 30 years and she's been extremely happy with the quality of the product.  I recently gave her this Ironman watch with the white band. After wearing it only 15-20 times, parts of the white band have turned grey and she will no longer wear it because it is so unsightly.  We tried scrubbing and using the Mr. Clean Magic Eraser as recommended by another reviewer, all to no avail.  This watch is therefore worthless and gathers dust in the back of a drawer. Our advice is simply this:  Do not buy the watch with the white band or you will regret it after only wearing it for a few months.
summary: Band turned grey in spots after only 20 wearings

reviewText: This Timex Ironman 30-Lap Watch (Mid-Size) is perfect for athletes at any level. It is stylish and very easy to use.  The main features of this watch are the 30-lap memory, 100-hour chronograph with lap and split options, on-the-fly lap recall, and water resistance down to 100m. This is very useful for running, biking and swimming. For marathon runner, you can track your pace each mile (since it has 30 memory vs 26.2 miles total distance of marathon race). It also have countdown timer, 3 alarms, and 3 different time zone settings.The only two downside to this watch:1. If your wrist is relatively larger, you might want to get the full size watch (vs this mid-size/unisex watch)2. The strap on this watch can be made stronger or thicker (if not careful when taking the watch off and yanked the strap, it will break)Have a great race!Sidarta Tanu
summary: Perfect for running, biking or swimming. Get full size version if you have larger wrist.

reviewText: Good morning, I bought this item years ago and it lasted for a good while until I went into the steam room. I had done this multiple times before, but I guess this was one time too many. When I called to get it fixed through the lifetime warranty, it would have ended up costing more to fix it than it would be to just buy a new one.
After wearing this for just a few weeks, the band broke. The watch is still keeping time, but that isn't helpful when you can no longer wear it on your wrist.
summary: Band broke after a few weeks

reviewText: This watch DOES NOT have interval timers.  I will be sending back and getting a watch with interval timers.  I believe the product description said it does have the interval timers.  It does not!
I bought this for my wife because her $4,100 diver's watch got water in it.Cost $601.00 to repair. This new watch will be her new "go-to" diver's watch!

This is the 3rd Timex Women's Ironman Watch I've owned. The first one was the smaller version and I found the buttons hard to press when I was swimming laps at the pool. The 30-lap version has buttons that are MUCH easier to press in a kick turn. The second Timex Ironman watch I owned was a 30-lap version with a blue/grey band. The band broke after about 2-3 years of CONSTANT use and abuse. This one, my third one, has worked beautifully. I have noticed, like other reviewers, that the band gets dirty easily. The white resin band seems to soak up the blue coloring from my jeans and it is a stubborn stain. My other colored resin bands did not have this issue.Still, this is one of my favorite things I own. I know, it's simple, but it's great. It's reliable, easy to use, simple and versatile. I use this watch for timing fitness laps (run/bike/swim), I use it as a kitchen timer, I use it as an alarm clock, oh, and as a watch too. You can easily toggle between two time settings in case you care to track two time zones or toggle between standard and military time format.I recommend this product.
summary: Good for timing laps at the pool!

reviewText: I have trouble seeing the date on most watches, and I don't like the design of the digital watches I had been getting.  This one is attractive AND visible.  It certainly does the job!  Not to say I'm not looking for a more dressy band somewhere, but I haven't found that combination yet and this one will do.
summary: Nice to have a day and date before my eyes when writing a check :)

reviewText: easy to set, clear dial, many functions.Bought it for nursing classes, needed a second hand for taking blood pressures.

I just started triathlon training and needed a watch to swim with.  This watch is easy to read and use.  The day and date is easy to read across the top.  There are many functions: stopwatch, timer, alarms etc.  It can also be set to military time.  I definitely needed to read the directions, but it's easy to use once you figure it out.  The watch is a good fit; I was worried it would be bulky, but it is sleek and fits great.

This watch is great...I love the looks.  That is until about 3 months after I bought it.  The band has turned green!  It's been about 6 months now, and I'm looking into a Casio b/c I can't stand looking at the green band anymore.

I love this watch. Have traveled all over the world (Asia, Africa, Latin America) and this watch is the perfect companion. Lasts about 2 years--well, it's plastic, after all--but it's reliable, looks OK even at the office, and doesn't break the bank to replace.
My wife wanted a simple and easy to use watch that gave her the time a date.  Perfect for her
it nice, but need to make the nick bigger for those how have a big one, like how has blood sugar or blood pressure

I ordered these from Rock Ridge Sales, Inc. through Amazon and was very pleased with the service and shipping efficiency  plus their willness to make sure I was happy with my purchase.  I would recommend them to anybody and would be happy to repeat the transaction as many times that it takes as I need them.  Thanks so much.  B. Carli
summary: Silver and Gold  colored Deluxe eye glass holders

reviewText: This chain was exactly what i was looking for. Its the perfect length, its elegant and it looks like a necklace holding your glasses. Truly happy with my purchase! Thank you!!

It took me forever to find a good chain for my glasses. Some were too thin, too cheap, to expensive, too short... It was especially hard to find one online without being about to pick it up. This one is perfect. It's simple, heavy enough to be sturdy and durable, long enough to hand properly without strangling me or resting too low, and (best of all) it's a really good price. Finally!

Great for the price. I was afraid the links would be weak or open b/c of the cheap price but they arent. The chain is light weight but holds up well. I just use it in the house so i dont miss place my glasses constantly.

I am OK with this chain, but not thrilled.  It is a little light, but the problem was not that.  The problem was that the loops come apart under slight pressure, and you will be faced with pulling them apart with needle nose pliers.  That is a drag.  But if you squeeze the loops tightly together, one after one, it will work out for you.

The eye glass holder is great. I can't go grocery shopping without them. Keeps my glasses handy so I can read labels and lets me take my glasses off so I can see to walk. Makes my life so much easier.
These worked out fine for me didn't break some people complained about length but they were just right size to me

I like the chain but I find it a little short in length. I have another chain and I like that longer length better. Personal preference, I guess. It is light weight and does the job just fine.  Happy to have an extra eye glass chain.
summary: Eyeglass chain- works just fine for me.

reviewText: Very poor quality product: it broke in only 2 days. Now I am buying the string ones hoping they will last longer...

I needed to get a simple chain for my step mom because she kept losing her glasses.  I just wanted a cheap one cause it was more as a joke then anything.  This chain though it came in a cheap cardboard packaging, actually was pretty good.  Its not like some durable NASA made metal, but it does the job.  I recommend it for anyone who just needs a simple chain that is inexpensive so you don't lose your reading glasses or something.

This was total junk.  It didnt come in the pictured package, just a plastic baggie.  Within the first 5 mintues of wearing, one of the chains completly broke off in two, then another link detatched from the glass grip.  I will be asking for a refund so I can search for something better.
summary: Total Junk - broke in 2 places w/in 5 minutes

reviewText: Chains are on the short side and inexpensive looking. They do the job, but they  are a little short.  I would order more if they were longer.

This eyeglass chain is exactly what I was seeking.  It is simple, well made, and in excellent taste.  If you want a classy but very reasonably priced eyeglass holder that isn't flashy or gaudy, this is for you.

ive been told that glasses chains are really outdated but WHATEVER. i lose my glasses all the time because I take them off and set them somewhere. all those old ladies who used to use glasses ch ains were on to something, its very useful. This is a nice simple clain. nothing bad to say about it, does what i wanted it to
this was bought as a gift. The little girl is a bratz fanatic and she loved it because we hadn't seen anyone else with it..

Love this dash mat!  I was hoping the dash mat would lay totally flat on the dash once it rested from being shipped but that never happened. It's not perfect (hence the 4-star rating) but it's still great looking and protects the dash from cracking or so that is my hope.  The dash mat is available in both standard or with the "heads up" feature but be sure to specify when ordering.  I would recommend this dash mat.
summary: Embroidered C5 Logo Corvette Dash Mat

reviewText: I actually love them. They fit all of my needs but you need to know that you actually have to wear shoes on under the boots. Because of that, the boots are stretched out every time you put them on. As such, my boots now have some holes at the seams which actually defeats the purpose.
summary: Now, I gave this a four out of five but...

reviewText: The rubber in these boots crumbled, literally rotted away, before I had a chance to wear them even once.  If you buy them, plan on wearing them during the first month after purchase.

I purchased these boots for my husband since his first pair were falling apart--THEY WERE AT LEAST 10 YEARS OLD! He is in the contracting business and needs quality "rain and mud boots" and this product does the job!!  These boot slip right over his shoes and are an easy on and  off.
Nice quality material however do not purchase if you intend on wearing work boots as you will never get them on or off, even if you go 3-4 sizes too large
Only place I could find these boots in my size for a great price! Good job. I love my boots.

The Workbrutes arrived in excellent condition and on time as I'd requested an expidited delivery.  No problem with the boots.  I was purchasing these to replace a pair of Totes that had torn.  I was hoping to get something lighter in weight as they are being used for motorcycle riding so storage space is always a priority and these boots do take some room.
Wouldn't fit over my work boots...I had return them.  They didn't seem to stretch out enough to fit. Thanks for the quick response...........

I bought these to keep at the barn so I could slip my gym shoes into them and a) have warm shoes to do chores b) keep the barn mess out of my car and c) have boots tall enough to handle deep mud and snow.It didn't work out quite like I planned. My nike shox wouldn't slip in the boot. The only thing that I can wear that will slip in are ballet flats. But who is going to wear those to a barn?! Also, the boots are pretty flimsy and they don't stay up right when you are trying to put them on. It's a hassel. They feel plenty big in the foot area, but the ankle is small and it catches the heel of the shoe you are trying to insert. Gah! Annoying!This would possibly work better if you bought a size that is significantly larger than your normal size? On the plus side, I like the light weight rubber and the tread was good.
summary: Fair price for the boot you are getting

reviewText: You won't be disappointed with this purchase.  They keep the feet dry and the rubber thickness is excellent.  Will definitely purchase more in the future.

I purchased these boots to go over my sneakers to work in the yard to keep grass and dirt from getting into my shoes and socks. They work great for that. The only thing is they are heavier than I expected, and a little hard to get on and off.

So far, these boots have survived a few New England snowstorms with no wear & tear. At age 76, with some hip bursitis, I find that leaving an old pair of shoes inside them, and then putting on this assembly with the help of a really long (plastic) shoehorn, works wonders with my own wear & tear. Your feet won't get cold for a very long time when you wear this double-layered combination out in the snow. Buy and enjoy!

I wear American size 10, medium shoes--without exception. THIS is the size I needed. I bought a pair of these in Large which should have been correct, but I could only fit smaller/lighter style shoes, like a pair of boat shoes. I could not get some of my dress shoes into the large.  My Keen Detroit boots (10) will go in with a fight. Width seems to be the problem rather than length in this case.

My boyfriend really wanted these - he works outdoors in extreme temperatures and his father use to wear them when he was a child so he always wanted a pair (Aaah, lol).  The only place I could find these wherein they weren't astronomically priced were on Amazon and they fit over his work boots.  He loves them.

Tried and tried to find good old fashioned overshoes and couldn't find them anywhere locally. Of course Amazon came to the rescue and I'm so happy to have found these boots for my Dad. He's hard to buy for once he has a particular item in mind. And no one in our area had just plain boots that he could slip over his shoes.The quality of the boots is good. the finish is good and the simple button closure is helpful - easy on and easily fastened.
summary: Sturdy and just what my Dad wanted!

reviewerName: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
reviewText: I wear a 10 1/2 shoe and boot. I ordered the XL Workbrute - my gym shoes slip right in, even when I'm wearing them. There's about 1" of space in front of the toe.  Boots - I had to force the boot in before putting it on (took some work) - after the boot was in place, I rolled down the top to expose the laces, etc.  I slipped my foot it, laced up the boot, then rolled up the PVC over-boot. There was about 1/2" of open space in front of the boot.There was no was a smaller boot would have fit over the boots. Tried it with my Browning hiking boots and my work boots.
summary: Fantastic product - just pick the right size!

reviewText: These work boots work well when we need to ptotect out leather boots from chemicals or rain or wading through water and mud.
they were huge and we returned them-they are meant to go over heavy work boots not shoessorry they didn't work.

Product does exactly as it was advertised to do. The only significant issue I had was not actually with the product but, the actual sizing. I pretty much had to guess that the size shoe I was wearing on the particularly rainy day would fit into the overshoe. The sizing chart does not leave much room for error. Sized up properly, an excellent product indeed.
So far very handy and haven't even used them as they are intended. Use as a wintertime sandal for quick trips outside onto snow covered driveway or backyard. Should last a good long time.

The rubber boots were great, just one problem, they were too small. I had to return them & shipping costs were almost as expensive as the boots themselves. Had I bought them from a store I would have exchanged them for a larger pair (if available). That wasn't an option. That's the down side of buying online plus the time involved getting the merchandise.

The watch is waterproof and worked great. My main issue with the watch is that the band was too small for an adult wrist. I had to keep it in my pocket or attached to a belt loop and that defeated the purpose of the purchase. I had to let my daughter wear it and was always asking her for the time.

I have 3 GPS watches and this one is my favorite and most frustrating one.  Let's start with the good.- Tons of features.  Like many Suunto watches, this one is loaded.  Compass (which works well despite other reviews), altimeter, barometer.  All of those features work well, as well as my Suunto Advizor.  All this and it's waterproof.- Mostly sturdy build.  Maybe too sturdy - the strap is quite stiff.- I have the X9mi version which has inverted lcd shades and a red backlight (doesn't mess with night vision).  Both neat features.Now the bad.- Battery life is mediocre with GPS running - this is compared to modern GPS watches (remember this thing came out almost a decade ago).- GPS reception and fix speed is not great.  I had to modify mine a bit to get an improvement - and it actually worked fairly well.  I took a length of 6 inches of insulated wire I took from an old cable.  I stripped about 1 inch on one end and actually tied it to the GPS' ring antenna on the left side. With this wire hanging out of the watch my fix speeds are greatly improved and I can pick up and lock to 2 or 3 more satellites.  My position screen now normally shows 5/5/ or 6/6 for satellites in use where before I'd have 3 or 4 locked on.  In everyday use the watch doesn't look any different because I wrap the remaining cable into the rubber edge of the strap around the back.  When I want to use the GPS I just unwrap it and let it hang out.  Not ideal, but it works for me.- Bezel tends to come loose or break.  I'm on my second one and I just tonight epoxied it on to the watch face because it came off on one end and cracked in the middle.  My first one popped off and broke within a year and a half of purchase, but Suunto replaced it at no charge.  My watch is well out of warranty now and as I understand I would have to send it in to Suunto now to get fixed which I'm sure would cost more than I'm willing to pay.With my GPS antenna mod, I think I'll get new life out of this watch.  I'd pretty much given up on it until that mod because of the GPS issues.  I'm somewhat excited about it's new lease on life.If you're thinking of this watch as a running watch, I'd look elsewhere.  It's not designed for that, and is not nearly as useful as some Garmin, Soleus, New Balance, Nike, TomTom, Schwinn, Timex, Polar, or you name it GPS running watch for that purpose.  If you're gonna spend time hiking and want to be able to upload waypoints and routes, then take a look at this one over most of those others.
summary: Mostly a great watch, Bezel design and GPS implementation could be better

Conversation with friends and especially by looking at this DVD convinces me that Aikido will work only if :(1). you are extremely big and strong (like Steven Seagal) or very fast like Murohei Uyeshiba, where the speed will substitute for his strength. In my view it is misleading to say that Aikido proceeds on the basis of the path of least resistance. This DVD also has not disabused my long held belief that most masters of female martial arts are rather ugly. For example, none of  10 of the top pioneering women in Aikido is gorgeous and beautiful, in the ordinary sense of the words. I am happy to give this album 1 star.

This is the only DVD of its kind that I know of.  It is a series of interviews with women who have reached black belt or teacher level in Aikido. As a woman doing Aikido I found it very helpful and interesting, as I struggle to find my own style and expression in a sport dominated largely by the male expression of the art.  A male friend of ours who runs his own dojo also found it very helpful because he could relate first hand to the journey of the teachers and the struggles they experienced in setting up and establishing a dojo.  He also found it insightful because it gave him a deeper understanding the struggles that females have in developing and expressing the art.

An unexpectedly inspiration! In spite of the recent Hollywood stereotype of sexy women with Ninja skills I think of martial arts as primarily the domain of men so it's refreshing to find real women practicing and teaching others Akido.  This video gave me insight not only into the practice of Akido but into my position in society as a woman in a leadership position.  I recommend this video for anyone, male or female, who wants to deepen their understanding of how this martial art offers not just a physical but a psychological training field.

Normally I don't try to engage in debates with other reviewers, but as a person who has practiced korean karate, taijiquan and aikido for many of my nearly fifty years on this planet, I have to take issue with Mr. Hariman's comments, as well as his review of the DVD under discussion here.While many tai chi teachers that emphasis health and well-being over fighting applications, I have met at least three who produced students that are more than capable of holding their own in a fight.  The same applies to aikido. While the emphasis in many dojo is on the art as a spiritual practice, I have met several aikido practitioners who are able to quickly take another's balance, and bring him or her under control (or simply throw them into a wall, if need be) - its' just that the development of fighting skill is not the only goal of practice.  While I would concede that both arts require at least a minimum of physical (as well as mental and emotional) conditioning before a student is able to apply the techniques of these arts at speed and under pressure, the student gains that conditioning (and builds the necessary skills) through disciplined practice (and rational analysis of technique) over time.The thing is that this process does take time: if one is physically weak to begin with, one year of practice is not nearly enough to gain a fighting level of skill at either art (and I would argue that this goes for korean karate as well).  With all due respect, Mr. Hariman's review betrays a rather shallow understanding of the arts in question, as well as a desire for 'quick and easy' results.  I would suggest that he take the time to find a teacher that he can trust and have confidence in, whatever the art, and commit himself to three-five years of practice with an open mind, and see.  He might be surprised.That said I enjoyed watching Malory Graham's documentary.  It presents a well-balanced view of the styles of practice and personal experiences of the senior women yudansha (black belt level practitioners) who studied the art under the major Japanese shihan (master instructors, like Yoshimitsu Yamada, T.K. Chiba,  and the late Mitusunari Kanai) active in the United States Aikido Federation over the past couple of decades.  if I had a criticism, it would be that the presentation would have benefited from discussions of the internal mechanics of receiving an attack and taking another's balance, or demonstrations of advanced modes of practice like kaeshiwaza (reversals), both of which may have gone a long way to allay the issues raised by skeptics like Mr. Hariman.  I share my copy with women students in the dojo I practice in, particularly beginners, for whom I hope it serves as a inspiration and a spur to more dedicated practice in these difficult times.

These are pretty solid all-around climbing shoes, especially if you value comfort and wearability over super-high performance.  They are very stylish--I love the red color--and unusually comfortable for climbing shoes.  There was literally no break-in period, and right out of the box I could wear them for hours without any discomfort.  They are cushier and more sneaker-like than many other climbing shoes.  I would recommend them, especially for a first pair of climbing shoes, or for anyone who wants comfortable shoes with decent performance that they can stand in all day.  But I don't love them as much as I wanted to.  For comfort, I still actually prefer my worn old Five Ten Spires, and for performance I prefer my new La Sportiva Katana Lace-Ups.Good stuff:ComfortStyleDecent but not spectacular climbing performanceNot so good stuff:Stiffness--These shoes are kind of stiff, and less flexible than I want them to be.  I slip more than in my old shoes because I can't feel the rock as well with my toes.Stickiness--The rubber on these is not quite as sticky as the Stealth C4 rubber on my old Spires.  (Still good, but not as good).Breathability--These are lined and made of synthetic material, so they are hotter and less breathable than the butter-soft unlined suede of my old Five Ten Spires.  The Spires conformed perfectly to my foot after a while, and I don't think the Sirens will do that.Performance--There's always a trade-off between comfort and performance.  These are fine, but they are not great for toe-hooks and they are not great for overhangs.  If you are a beginner, you probably won't care about that.  I don't love them for smearing either.  If you're looking for more aggressive shoes to push you to the next level, I'd go with the La Sportiva Katanas--but they are more expensive and much harder to break in.I saw that some other people have complained about durability.  I haven't had any problems with that so far, but I have only been climbing in these for about a month (twice a week).Bottom line:  If you're going with comfort and wearability over really high performance, you will not be sorry to buy these shoes.  But I'd really recommend checking out the Five Ten Spires, which I actually prefer because they are stickier, more breathable, more flexible, and really long-lasting even if they are not as pretty.  If you're going for high performance, you may want something with a more aggressive (and less comfortable) shape.Sizing:  If you're buying these shoes, you're probably picking comfort over performance, so it doesn't seem worth it to put yourself through agony to try to wear shoes that are way too small.  I did originally try a half size smaller than my normal street shoe size and climbed in them about 3 times before realizing that the synthetic material just wasn't stretching.  Now I have my normal street shoe size, and the fit is just right.
summary: Wearable right out of the box
