Well, it doesn't have advanced features such as a chrono function but you certainly will be happy enough (as I am) wearing this thing. It has the right size, and it is lighweight. Recommended.
Not only is this watch fashionable, but my husband had worn it every day since I bought it last year as a Xmas gift.
I've owned this watch for over a decade. No frills, absolutely indestructible, and very accurate. It's a great basic timepiece.

This watch may seem somewhat expensive since it is a black plastic basic time/date watch, but for what it is, it's perfect.  The plastic used to make the case is very high quality, the rubber used for the strap is very durable, but at the same time is comfortable/flexible/soft.  The many holes in the strap help keep your wrist from getting too sweaty, the numbers are big and easy to read, the accuracy of the watch is very impressive (loses maybe a minute or two per year), it's lightweight and it has a mineral crystal cover.  As an added bonus, the watch is not overly big/bulky...I have pretty small wrists and this watch doesn't look out of place when I wear it (note...the reviewer who posted his pics has REALLY tiny wrists...this is definitely not a big watch).  Also, this thing looks surprisingly classy for a plastic watch...I'm not saying you should wear it if you end up on the cover of Forbes mind you, but it really does look nice.I've had this watch for about 3 years now (haven't had to replace battery yet) and have been completely satisfied with it. If you are looking to purchase a simple but reliable/high-quality watch that can be worn anywhere,  this is probably the best one you can buy.
summary: The best black plastic watch money can buy!

reviewText: This is by far the best watch I've ever owned.  It was a bit expensive compared to the others I have used in the past but It was so worth the $.

I just wanted a basic, understated, durable watch and thought this would fill the bill. It has. It's beautiful in a minimalist sort of way, with fluorescent numbers and hands, and a whisper quiet mechanism. Setting the time and date is simple and it keeps perfect time. The cover of the watch casing and the wrist band appear to be made of the same tough, black rubber, and enough holes are punched in the band to keep my wrist from sweating.One aesthetic note: The face of the watch looks more elegant than the photos here. I think they either removed the crystal to reduce reflections in the photo or used a polarizing filter. Be advised that the clearly visible inner ring encircling the numbers in the photo is actually a 45-degree-ish beveled surface that completely disappears when the crystal is in place.

I'm a real fan of Victorinox and Wenger.  I have quite a few from the old Marlboro Country Store watches to a few Victorinox automatics.  This is a decent little watch.  Its build really makes it looks like it should be a freebie with some purchase.  An inexpensive plastic case and a very thin, somewhat brittle plastic band.  I have it only to collect it and don't wear it often.  Truthfully, this is something that should be labeled "Timex" and cost $40.  It's a decent watch, just like a Timex.  The price is all wrong though.  It is waaaay to expensive.  As an example, I just bought a Victorinox 25792 Automatic watch with a Swiss ETA self-winding movement and sapphire crystals front and rear.  It has a titanium case.  I paid $259 from Amazon.  That makes my Renegade look like I should have found it in a cereal box. This is truly just a watch whose only real attraction is the brand. With it's easily scratched glass crystal (not even mineral) and easily scratched case, I would call it disposable and would not price it above $40 on Amazon.
summary: An inexpensive watch with a big price tag.

reviewText: I wear this watch while working out, out on a date, in the shower, bicycling, motorcycling, in the office, at home, etc.  You get the point! This is a fantastic all-purpose watch.  The numbers and hands glow when you step inside a room with low lighting. I receive compliments from watch enthusiasts. Great product! I lost the first one I bought and now I'm purchasing a second.

I am on my third one in 17 years.  If one stops working I immediately buy another!  I absolutely LOVE this watch. Both my previous watches died because moisture got into them - one my fault and one the battery replacer! The face design is the most eligant I have ever seen, yet basic and functional.  You would have to pay thousands of dollars for a watch as eligant(see Bell & Ross!). I wear it 24/7, only removing it if I am crawling under a car or working on a lawn mower. I gouged the case and scratched the crystal doing these things so I am more careful now. I have never had to replace a strap yet- they wear like iron yet are very comfortable!  At night I charge the luminous hands under a light for a few seconds and I can see the hands until the wee hours. I keep it set using the U.S.Naval Observatory Master Clock - so I know it is accuate to a few seconds / year! I intend to have this watch model all my life - Swiss Army willing!
summary: I Love My Swiss Army Renegade!

reviewText: I was surprised to find less than stellar reviews for this watch.  I had previously reviewed this item in a slightly different model, though this is the same kind that I currently own.  Aesthetically, I find it to be perfectly designed.  It's fairly simple, isn't too flashy and yet looks very elegant.I've had this watch for a few of years now, and it holds up to the test.  There is such a thing as actually taking care of the stuff you own.  I mean, I wear this everyday and I'm not any kind of construction worker or anything, but what kinds of things do you have to do in order to screw up a watch?  Take it off when you shower, don't use it as a door stop, and playing catch with it is probably not a good idea.Over time, a few scuffs have appeared and a slight scratch on the watch face, but they're just a sign of use.  Nothing is taken away aesthetically... and yes, I still am using the original leather strap that came with it, the second strap loop is still in place, and I have never had to take it into the shop and never had a single issue with it.I give this watch my complete endorsement.  Don't buy a butt-ugly Fossil watch, you'll be a million times happier by having purchased this one.

Bought for my wife for Christmas to replace a returned watch then was much smaller than pictured(Claude Bernard).  She loves the watch, only problem was the battery gave out 2 weeks after we recd it.  $6 later up and running perfectly.

I purchased this watch in 2007 from the Central Department Store, an authorized dealer, in Bangkok.  Every nine months after that it required a new battery, and then finally stopped.  To get it moving again, I was told, would cost about as much as a new watch.  Five years of use, $60 worth of batteries, and I have a watch that won't move.  For the estimated $300 that I paid for it, I am sorely disappointed.

I chose this watch as a gift for my eldest son's college graduation.  He is a watch collector and has some lovely pieces, but had expressed interest in this one for a more casual look.  I researched it and all reviews were quite positive.  I need to add to the trend, this watch is handsome, I am told it is quite comfortable, it is so easy to read with its clear face and the crystal has prevented damage to the face with my son's hobbies.  This is a great item!
This is a perfect watch and looks great. The price was very good on Amazon compared to retail and the watch will last a long time.

I have had this watch for a few years now. The battery and it has lasted a very long time. It still has the original battery in it. I think this is highly unusual, as I replaced batteries in my  other watches at least once in the last two years. I would definitely get another Swiss Army watch if I needed one.

I have owned a few Swiss Army watches over the years, all have served me well with the exception of this watch I ordered.  I will never order thru Amazon again.  When I opened the box, the contents were not neatly organized, almost as if the watch had been ordered and returned or packaged carelessly.  The watch looked like a fake, I sent a photo I took of the back case to the contact information I found on the Swiss Army website, they stated they could not confirm if the watch was a fake.  The watch has since stopped working properly, the second hand jumps 5 seconds at a time, very weird right?!  And the back case has corroded as if it is made of a plated cheap carbon steel.  Wow!  my first sense was the watch was a fake, and 2 years later I cannot return it, I have hardly worn it and it is worthless!

December, 15,2011; Got this watch as a gift. The first one died after 3 weeks. The jeweler gave me a new one after it was evident that Swiss Army was taking months to repair it. The new one is also failing. It just stops for no reason; battery checks ok.Quartz watches in general are way over priced. The best movement only costs about $20.00. You are paying for the case and the huge mark up.Anyway, no more Swiss Army watches for me.June 23, 2012 (6 months later) This watch continues to be a piece of garbage. The date indicator advances randomly. I would send it back to Swiss army, but the are absolutely awful for customer service and I simply don't want to aggravate myself dealing with these people. This one is going in the trash.
summary: First one defective, second one also defective

reviewText: This watch is everything I expected it would be. It's the real deal, a Victorinox, which I consider the "authentic" Swiss Army watch. I had a Wenger before, and there's no comparison. The quality is fantastic. It is not a small watch, but I have thin wrists and it fits me perfectly. The dial is extremely easy to read. I am extremely pleased and highly recommend this watch. You will not be disappointed.

For those who say it has scratches.. this watch is not made with sapphire glass. I personally I own a new Victorinox. So please Next time read about a watch. Your old watch which you wore for ''X'' years and never had scratches is made with sapphire glass or better!

I bought this watch last year to replace another Swiss Army watch that I had since 1987. I was very pleased with my original watch and it always amazed me that the glass (or crystal actually) never got a scratch even after nearly 18 years of use. My new watch however now has deep scratches after only a year of use... It's a nice watch, but I'm disappointed with the poor quality of the crystal.
summary: They don't make them like they used to...

reviewText: Terrible Product, Terrible Customer ServiceI recieved my product in the mail and tried it on for the first time and the rubber band tore. It said it was water proof and i ran it across an open faucet briefly and it got water inside the plate. I wrote to customer service to send a replacement twice before they would even respond. They say they have an apparent 30 day warranty. When they finally got back to me, they told me to take a picture of the broken watch and send it to a seperate email. Twice again I try to get in contact with them and they claim to have sent a replacement. It has been 18 days and nothing
This is a really nice looking watch.  But the one I had lost 3 seconds a day.  Three seconds a day is pretty bad.  I got my money back.

I have gone through 2 leather bands in 3 years. The watch currently is sitting on my kitchen counter - requiring a THIRD replacement.The watch itself is simple and elegant. No problems with time. It's almost perfect except for the problem with leather band replacement and the associated costs.Note; the leather watch band has two loops and the loose one is guaranteed to come off with normal wear and tear in the first 6 months (IMHO).The band itself seems good for 1.5 years based on my normal wear and tear experience. Give or take.As for replacement leather bands' direct from manufacturer. BE PREPARED for the cost. It seems unreasonable to me.In April - they seem to be putting out another model of this same watch with a "rubber band". That almost sounds like a joke; but I can assure you its' not - it's actually rubber!You ask me; Swiss should be replacing my leather band and spending more money on the quality of their bands. The watch itself; perfect!~tb
summary: Be prepared for additional expenses on this one!

reviewText: There isn't much to this watch but I find it very handsome.  It can be casual yet looks good with a suit, too.  I have worn it daily for about 4 years now.  I have replaced the band once but not because it broke.  I also sent it back to Swiss Army to have the battery changed.  I love this watch and plan to wear it as long as it continues to work.
The seller, Mr. Watch, sent me a broken watch and then stiffed me on the return because of a technicality on their return policy. Don't buy from Mr. Watch, unless you want a shiny, $200 paper-weight.
Super durable water proof sports watch that performs great and looks good to boot.  I highly recommend this product.  Try it for yourself.

I have to say that this is my first watch with this kind of a band and I love it. It feels secure very comfortable and the illumination on the "dial" works great! I have to say that the customer service was wonderful when after only a month of owning the watch it froze on me. They told me to contact Freestyle directly because of the lifetime warranty and if I had any problems that they would help me resolve any issues. Freestyle told me to send it it and within two weeks I have my watch back working properly without costing me anything except the postage to send it in. I hope now it will last me a long long time. Great for workouts and camping.

This watch was a great price but it arrived with no setup instructions. I have found it very difficult to set because freestyle does not have instructions on set up either.I guess I must return it because a watch that doesnt show correct time is really no deal.

Love this watch for its lightness and ease of taking it on and off. I'm a bigger fan of analog, but this digital was easy to set. It's comfy and dries quick when wearing it in the pool. I'd even consider getting in other colors.

I have had this watch for a couple of years and I love it!I wear it every day and love the display. It is very easy to use with many functions.The one thing that I don't like but it can't really be fixed is the wrist band. I love the velcro wristband, it is very easy to take on and off..however the end of it after time will start to not stick. Therefore when you take a sweatshirt on and off it may grab and come off. Other than that I think this watch is perfect.
I liked the watch overall and wore it for a couple of weeks before one of the function buttons fell off, essentially making it unusable.  Thankfully, I was able to get a full refund from amazon.

this is a very nice ladies sport watch.  It is sturdy, a bit difficult to set the time, etc... need to go on line to get the directions but figured it out.  good size face for a woman and very easy to take on and off.  also works in water to a specific depth but would not leave it there for too long.

I've had the Freestyle Shark Predator watch for over two months now and use it pretty regularly as an exercise watch. I spent a week and a half vacationing with it constantly on my wrist, and it has worked like a charm. Unlike some other watches (Timex), it really is a water resistant watch when it says it is. It was on me while I swam in pools and beaches, while I did a couple of days of hiking in mountain and forest ranges, and it still works well while I do lengthy runs.Good things about the watch:1. Nylon strap with velcro closure is very secure and can take a beating2. Dual time zone mode was appreciated while vacationing3. Works4. Is not lying when it says it is water resistantThings that suck about the watch:1. There are many screen modes that you'd have to scroll through to get to your desired function. For example, to get to the chronograph mode, you'd have to press the mode button four times from the main clock screen. This can get tedious.2. After reading the two other reviews, I am waiting for the buttons to fall off. So far they've stayed in place, although I notice that the mode button (which I use most frequently) seems slightly more depressed than the other buttons. But hey, it's a nice cheap watch, so you can get another one if it breaks.Update 09/18/07: I've been scuba diving with this watch to a depth of 45 feet without problems.
summary: It's cheap and it does the job

reviewText: The watch came set to California time, and with no instructions for resetting.  The link to instructions on the Web did not yield any useful information, Therefore the watch was useless to me.

I bought this for my daughter somewhere else and she loved it except for the fact after some wear and tear, one of the buttons popped out and she couldnt use it anymore. Overall this has some great functions.

The first time i saw this shoe, i thought to myelf " this is a unique shoe". I decided, i had to have it, but, when i got it, that was another story. I loved the shoe so much i started wearing it immediately. Everywhere i wore it to, people was just staring and saying how much they love it. The shoe is very comfortable, the feeling of soft leather pressing against your foot is never more welcome. I love it, wouldn't trade it for anything else.

I just installed it yesterday but it seems to be working fine and wiring it up was pretty easy. My only complaint is that it does not come with the items needed to properly wire the blinkers. It seems like it would come with it since you have to have it. I just hooked one blinker up and I guess I can fix it later.

I put this on my 79 Kawasaki KZ750 twin (connected to the front wheel).  Works great.  The speedo is accurate, I passed by several radar/speed signs.  My neutral & oil dummy light are not working, I need to double check my wiring again.  I don't have turn signals hooked up yet, but I did wire in some diodes I bought from Radio Shack.  The high beam light works though.  I need to bend the bracket so I can view it better.  I did notice that the odometer & trip-meter are a little off.  When I filled up there was a .2 mile difference after riding only 3 miles.  Not a big deal.

These boots are working out very well for me with a lot of support and comfort.  They seem just as nice as the tech 7 boots I tried on at the store.  Also, I wear a size 13 shoe and the size 13 boot fit perfectly!

I am very pleased with this made in America waterproof clog.  I am a size 71/2 so I ordered the size 8. They were a little large as I expected; so I just added a cheap insole under the removable footbed in the shoe.  Voila! a good fit with a medium thick sock. I bought these clogs so I could have a shoe to slip on when going out in the backyard with my dog.  We have very heavy dews and a lot of rain.  These work great to keep my feet dry on a "business" tour around the yard.  Very happy with these and I expect to buy  the rain boots as well.
5 star because these were exactly what was described and exactly what I expected them to be.  A great buy!
Shoes are very comfortable and I don't need to worry about water and mud.  I especially like the open heel with the slight lip of support.  Great product!

Got my package quick and was very happy with the delivery.  I tried them on, and was really bummed that that they were snug.  I also ordered the Sloggers that have the backs on them in the same size, and they fit great!  I wish they has the clogs in 1/2 sizes, because I'm sure they'd fit like a glove.

I wear size-7.5 in a regular shoe and got size-8 Sloggers. My feet are not super wide, but not narrow either. The Sloggers are a perfect fit.  I have been wearing Sloggers for a couple of weeks now. They are very comfortable, and I have been wearing them not only in the garden or washing the car, but when I have to do quick errands in the rain.  Yesterday, it was pouring and I actually wore them to work, so I was in Sloggers for about 12 hours! I had no problems at all. I was as comfortable in the evening as I was in the morning.  My feet were NOT hot and sweaty despite not taking them off for such a long time.Sloggers are a bit heavier than I expected. They are made of rubberized material top and bottom. No openings anywhere, so they are very good for walking in wet grass. Surprisingly, my feet do not get too hot despite having no ventilation in the shoe. The sole of the shoe is nicely textured.  I am attaching a photo which shows the top and the bottom of the shoe.  Next to the shoe I positioned a ruler so you can see how high the back of the shoe rises.  The back is not totally open, it has a slight rise which help to keep your foot firmly in the shoe.  The bottom of the show has some padding, so it provides nice support for the foot and is responsible for very comfortable feeling.  And of course they are very easy to put on and take off, which is very handy when your hands are covered with dirt from the garden.The second photo I am attaching to this review shows my foot wearing the shoe, hopefully this gives a better idea of the look and fit than just the shoe by itself.  In a close-up you can see a bit of room in the back - the difference between size-7.5 foot and size-8 shoe.The men a work made fun of the shoes, they thought they were ugly (what do they know?), but I think they are cute plus very comfortable and functional.
summary: Great! And not just for gardening

reviewText: I have a couple of goats and some chickens and I used to wear an old pair of sneakers out to the barn every morning to do chores.  There is always dew on the grass and it rains here all the time and the sneakers were always wet, smelly and caked with chicken poop and mud on the bottom.  These shoes are great!  I can slip them on when my hands are full, they are fully waterproof, they hose down when the bottoms are caked with dirt, they have a removable lining and they're pretty comfortable.  They are somewhat loose relative to the length, which is why I only gave them 4 stars.  I wear a size 8 1/2, but the 8 would have been too short.  I ordered a 9, which fits length-wise, but is pretty wide. I have a narrow foot, but I also wear an arch support so I am able to easily fit them under the removable lining to give added comfort and support to my feet.  The soles are sturdy on the stones and uneven ground in the pasture.  They seem like they will hold up well, but they are so low cost that I won't be upset if I have to buy another pair next year.  Plus, they are made in the US.  They claim to have a recycling program for worn out sloggers, but I couldn't see any information about it on their web site.  Overall, a great purchase if you need a pair of inexpensive, easy-on shoes for chores around the yard.
summary: Great slip-on shoe for doing chores

reviewText: Bought for a friend who normally wears size 7, but 7 was too large so returned those and got size 6.  Now she is happy.
summary: 7 is too large but 6 is just right.

reviewText: These clogs are beautiful and just what I was looking for.  They do run a bit small and wish I would have exchanged them for one larger size, but never did.  I would find them a bit uncomfortable if I had to wear them for a good part of the day.
summary: Nice clogs, run a bit small.

reviewText: Purchased as garden clogs but very useful as rain shoes, too.  Sturdily made and comfortable.  Surprisingly supportive.  Not as wide as previous purchases and based on other reviews sized up (I wear a 1/2 size).  For me, they are best worn with socks for better fit.
These clogs are very comfortable and are non-slip when working on wet slippery surfaces like ceramic tile. I highly recommend.

This is my 3rd pair of Sloggers.  I keep one pair by the back door, one by the front and one reserved for working in the chicken coop.  They keep my feet and floors clean since I am not tracking in dirt.  I would not take off my shoes at the door if they were not easy on and off.I love that these are made in the USA.  I love that they last forever.  And I love Amazon's great price on these.  Unlike some of the other reviewers, I would not be caught dead wearing them in public.  They do look a little like clown shoes.
Perfect for the garden. Comfortable for rubber garden shoes. Mark easily so nothing I would wear to town for an errand. Love them for outside.

I had been looking for something a bit more substantial than my Crocs for wearing outside, that would keep me dry in wet conditions.  I had Bogs boots for the winter, so I was looking for some Bogs I could wear in warmer weather.  However, Bogs are so expensive, and I just couldn't bring myself to spend $60 plus on them.I happened across Sloggers shoes on Amazon, and found these garden clogs.  I started reading the reviews, and pretty much all of them were super positive.  Plus, the price was right.  So glad I ordered them, because they are fantastic!  They feel much more substantial than Crocs, so when your feet sweat, you don't slide all over the place in them.  Your feet are supported by a comfy insole that is also removable - I love that!The sole is sturdy with good grip, and the kiwi color is really pretty.  They fit true to size more or less, but if you are between sizes I would size up - especially if you ever want to wear socks with them.  These are perfect for keeping your feet dry in the garden, but they work around town too.  I wore them all day long in town today, and my feet felt great the entire time.  And even though they are slip on shoes, I didn't feel like my feet were about to fall out all the time.  Another plus is that when they get dirty, you can just take the insole out, and hose them off.Last but not least, they are made in the USA!  This is a big deal to me, and I love to be able to support USA made products whenever possible.  These are great quality, affordable clogs.  I only just got them, so I can't say how they will hold up as time goes by, but so far I am a happy camper!

These are the greatest garden/rain shoes.  The fit is true to size, they are comfortable, easy to slip on/off and easy to clean.  Love the color.  I  just wish I had bought them years ago.  The insole adds comfort and makes the shoes feel more natural and not too "rubber-y" or "plastic-y."

I just love these sloggers and from the get go too!  They fit perfect!  Be sure to go up 1/2 size.  They are comfortable and easy to leave at the door when your hands are full!  And I can hose them off cuz of course they are water proof.  I will be spreading the word to all my friends and family and even I will get extras.  Comfortable people ;) Perfect garden shoe, ty sloggers for giving this customer complete satisfaction.  Aloha :)
Very happy with these so far, have been looking for sturdy, comfortable and reasonably priced garden shoes for ages, I think these are the ticket!

Loved these. They fit great, I can take out the insole and just wash or hose down these shoes with ease, plus they are more sturdy than Crocs. I needed something to protect my toes while tending the chickens, (they love to pick at shiny nail polish. lol) These fit the bill perfectly.

I had been looking for a good pair of shoes to wear around outdoors. The first thing I noticed online was the color and then the price. Most crocs and mules are way more expensive. Then I remembered I have had a pair of "Sloggers" for about 15yrs. The only reason I had stopped wearing them was that the insole wore out. If I were to clean them up they would probably look about the same as the day I bought them. This new pair are even better made than my first pair. I have to walk up a gravel road to get mail and these are so comfortable. They have a lining that my old pair don't have so even without the insole I could wear them. I was a little nervous about the size because other reviewers seemed to think they ran small and I wear a ten which was the biggest size. However,they are perfect in fact I could wear thick socks if I wanted to. Love these shoes.

I always wear 6. I ordered these in six and my heel was hanging out hitting the raised edge in the back. But the toe area had ample room on the sides, quite disproportionate.  I could tell that a whole size up would be way too big because of how big they were at the front. They will work for people with wide feet.
I only wish that they were rubber in the inside also so thay can be submerged in muddy waters while gardening... but I love them!! The green ones are pretty too!!

This is one of those few products that you are completely satisfied with, no room for improvement! I got them to replace my worn-out rubber boots, just thought they would be cooler, I never thought I would like them so well. They feel so much like house slippers that it seemed odd at first in the barnyard (I use the for farm and garden work). They are also so convenient to walk out of to go in the house.I normally wear a size 6 1/2, but I bought a size 7, as they did not have my size; and they fit fine.

I just bought these to replace a similar pair I got three years ago. I wear them a lot, and they're very comfortable. This pair feels a bit more snug than the ones they replaced, which is too bad because I often wear them with socks, but overall they're a very good everyday show for me (and yes, I also wear them in the garden).

Some years ago I was shopping in a garden store and came across a rack of shoes called Sloggers and were advertised as great garden shoes. I bought them.I kept them by the door and wore them for out door shoes.I've always had problems with my feet no matter what shoes I wore.I soon realized my feet didn't hurt at all no matter how long I wore my Sloggers.I started wearing them a lot and even out to shop etc.Not to long ago I was looking at shoes on Amazon and spotted Sloggers shoes in some fun colors.I ordered two pair and they are just as wonderful and comfortable as the first pair I had bought many years ago.If you have ever had problems with your feet you will be able to identify with me that no matter what the shoes look like or were made to wear for ,if they are as comfortable as my Sloggers are.....  it makes no difference.....
Fit good and excellent garden clog

I found a pair of these at our local farm/gardening store, thought they were cute so I tried them out. I just had total knee replacements on both knees a few months ago and could not find anything to help relieve the pain from walking...until I wore a pair of these. The difference between now and before i got the Sloggers is like night and day. I now have 8 pairs in various colors and patterns and will NEVER go back to any other shoe!

I get so many compliments when I wear these. I know they are meant for the garden but I wear them everywhere. With socks of course so they don't stink. In rainy weather they're brilliant. Great fit for one expected size. Enjoy.

I really enjoy wearing my sloggers for gardening. They give plenty of support and are very comfortable. This is my second pair, because some animal stole 1 of my shoes off my back deck! Ordered a new pair within a day because I couldn't be with out them!
they are very nice.  I might order another pair for inside the house.  the previous sloggers are for my garden.

This is the most comfortable clog I have ever owned.  I use it in my garden all the time.  And for quick stops at the supermarket.  Great color and the inner sole makes you feel as tho you are walking on air.  A great little shoe.
Very pleased with garden clogs using everyday and quite comfortable walking down to the local garden plot at the complex.

I LOVE these shoes.  The color is great and they are so comfortable.  I got them for working outside (specifically in my chicken coop).  I have hosed them off when they get muddy and they look just as good as they did the day I got them.
Love these .....

If you are thinking Crocs for knocking around in your garden (or as a fashion statement) - try these instead!  They are so much more comfortable than any of the Crocs I've had. The kiwi color is just fun, and they are made here -  that should be reason enough, right?

This clog is a work horse! I spend a lot of time in the garden and these premium clogs are the best garden shoes I've ever used. They're comfortable with or without socks and the removable liner stays in place in the thickest muck or the soggiest watering session (water only gets in when I lose the battle with the hose - it happens!). Clean up is a breeze, either hose them off or knock the dried dirt off of them. They have enough traction to hold steady on wet grass or for mowing. They're light-weight, and the clog style and moisture-wicking liner keep my feet cool on even the hottest days. Plus the easy on/off clog style keeps my hands free.Sloggers also look good enough to wear out on rainy days running errands, etc.The only outdoor task that I don't wear my sloggers for is heavy digging. The clay soil here gets like cement, so when I open up a new garden area I'll switch to work boots. For light digging and everything else outdoors, I live in my Sloggers.I'm on my second pair in as many decades. The original pair never actually wore out; the liner did, and I couldn't find a comfortable replacement so went with a second pair. Well, I went and did it. I bought a pair of the Premium clogs and now I am ruined for the other ones.The original Sloggers clogs have always been my standard shoe all spring, summer and fall for working in the yard, painting, or doing anything that might get messy or wet. They have plenty of support so that you can climb ladders without killing your arches.  The closed PVC toe keeps you from breaking your tootsies if you drop a hammer or something heavy or pointed on them and the bottoms are just thick enough that if you stepped on something sharp and undesirable, you won't impale your foot. (So, I use them for house repairs, mowing, painting, gardening, and decorating as well). The best part if that they can be hosed off, so if you step in dog poo at the dog park, or drop paint or step in mud, no problem. They can be scrubbed and don't have straps to break or stretch. Your sweat makes the original Sloggers vacuum seal onto your feet, so I never wear them with socks.Besides just being pretty, these Premium clogs have a cushion in the bottom that feels great, is removable and washable. It makes them much more comfortable to run around to stores, which is great for wandering all over Home Depot to find that object you forgot to get to finish whatever project you are working on). You can go straight from the yard to the store and back and not have to change shoes. And even wearing them bear, the bottoms of your feet won't turn into callous-mats like flip flops will.Premium Sloggers are head and shoulders better than flip flops or summer sandals for daily wear. Keep your sandals for dates and wear these Sloggers for everything else.

Sloggers 260KW08 Women's Premium Clogs are a fantastic pair of shoes for my feet not only for gardening, but for walking in many conditions.  I usually wear a size 7.5 shoe, wear a 37 medium in Birkenstocks and the size 8 Sloggers are very fine for me.  I likely could also fit into a 7, but because I'd like to wear socks if I desire, I followed the recommendations of others and moved up a size rather than down.  Another consideration I had when ordering was that when I work, particularly in the summertime, my feet swell, so I sized up.  An advantage of these clogs over many others is that their insoles make for a softer, more cushioned feel and they are removable for cleaning or airing out.  I find that wearing these requires no socks in the garden, a huge pro for me since my socks become filthy when I wear Crocs clogs.  The Sloggers put the Crocs to shame even though they are heavier.  I much prefer the feel and appearance of their real sole rather than a self molded one piece shoe.  The black sole is a nice contrast, as is the black interior and the bottom of the sole has a lovely swoosh type design in the Kiwi color.  Walking in dirt or mud is not an issue because these shoes can be hosed off.  The design of the clogs has a rear which is a bit elevated, so your heel is a little more protected than in other clogs.  I've worn Birkenstock shoes for many, many years and now that I've discovered Sloggers, I have an alternate manufacturer to choose from, and these are made in the USA!  These are great gardening shoes which are nice enough to wear all day inside or out.

reviewText: The only shoe you need for gardening and yardwork! My old pair just wore out after three years of almost daily wear, so I went for the lovely blue ones. I generally take a size 7.5 in shoes; the size 7 here fits a little loosely without socks or just about perfect with socks. They have been comfortable to wear for hours at a time, and the sole is thick enough that I can stomp on a shovel without my feet crying for mercy like they were in my sneakers. The low lip on the back had me worried about walking out of them, but it hasn't happened even once yet. If these fell apart tomorrow, I'd still happily buy another pair - but they don't look like they'll fall apart anytime soon!Edited to add: My feet have enlarged here lately (the joys of pregnancy!) and I've taken to wearing these for my evening walk.  I've been walking about 2 miles a night in these for the past month or so, and these are the only pair of shoes I've tried that lets me walk that without my feet hurting for the rest of the night - even my sneakers aren't cutting it. I know this isn't their intended purpose, but hey, whatever works! I've also been using them inside on the hardwood floors for anytime I'll be on my feet for too long - extended cooking sessions, a long load of dishes, etc. They have some scuffs on the toe now but structurally they are still holding up nicely.

There are a lot of options out there for foot wear like these,  but these were constructed well,  and made in the USA. I bought rain boots from sloggers as well.  I will definitely order from this company again!
summary: Love sloggers brand,  and these slip on clogs are just as comfortable!

reviewText: I've been wearing a Timex Ironman of some sort for better than 20 years.  Can't beat the functionality and durability at this price level.

Also the replacement band cost about 50% of the cost for a new watch. For me I just get a new watch.  Kind of a waiste of a working watch.

reviewText: I've worn the watch for a month now and it's just like my old one that I had for many years that worked really well. Hard to go wrong with Timex. good watch and works great but I found it at walmart for the same price. I'm definitely satisfied with the product.

This is a solid watch. It fits comfortably and seems to be durable (I've had my watch for 2 weeks now). The watch has a number of features, several of which I honestly haven't yet set aside the time to figure out. I do like that the watch has the option to chime at the top of every hour, though I wish there was a way to program the chime to discontinue during the night. It has the three features I need most in a watch, which are:1)  Timer2)  Chronometer (stopwatch) and3)  Alarms.When IndiGlo came out for these, my love of them multiplied even further.The ONLY problem I have with them is that the wristbands tend to wear off long before the life of the watch is depleted.  Sometimes I can get up to two years out of them, but rarely more than that.  Often, it's difficult to find a replacement, but some places will do it, however, if it's more than $15, I usually say screw it and buy a new watch.But the time is always accurate, it's easy to set, and there's all sorts of options.  For example:Do you want your alarm to go off only on weekdays?  There's a setting for that.Do you want the chronometer (or maybe the timer) to not appear?  There's a setting for that.Do you want to have more than one timer setting?  Or need to save chronometer info?  YES, this watch will do that.It comes with an exahustive manual, but since the watch has all the settings basically on the screen, all you need to do is push buttons, follow the instructions, and you'll be set.  Give this watch a try.
This watch is awsome. Never fails me i use it during practice when running, during cross country races and even at work. Its definatelty water proof and very durable.

If you don't want to spend the money on a GPS watch, but still want to monitor your time and pace, this is a good watch. I just ran a marathon with this watch and it was nice to have a 30-lap memory for the 26 miles needed.Pros: 30-Lap memory and it stores your lap/mile times so you can look at them all after a run.Cons: You have to manually hit the split button at each mile (easy to forget and you must know where each mile ends if you're training without the benefit of mile markers) and it doesn't display your average pace.
I truly love it. It is my weekend watch when I dont want to wear my fine watches. It does everything they do and more and I dont have to worry about breaking or scratching their crystals.

reviewText: same reliable watch the Timex ironman ha\s been.  Use as my work watch for years. Continue to buy as replacement

I've  used Timex ironman watches for a few years. Every time I break one, I get another to replace it. I like the features, originally buying one for the stopwatch function. I'm pretty hard on watches in my trade as an electrician, and appreciate the non-conductive (as far as I know) exterior. The one thing I do wish they would improve is the attachment point where the band hooks on. I always buy  the one with the buckle strap (maybe I should try the Velcro model) and they break right where the hole for the pin that holds the strap on is. It "pulls out" and won't hold a pin any more. I usually go through at least one strap replacement before that happens. The straps are a pain to change, BTW, due to the "hidden pin" design.

generally satisified with this watch.This is a plain basic watch that works well and is fairly simple to set and operate.I was a little disappointed when I saw that the watch was made in 2005 and I'm afraid the battery may be a little stale.

I have purchased many Timex watches over the years and I am entirely satisfied with this watch.  I always buy the sports watch, as I swim and do triathlons.Things I like about the watch:*Setting the watch is easy and the instructions are clear (although the printed instructions are very small!)* The watch is not too big.  So many watches have too many features and they are large, bulky, and heavy.  This watch is sleek, has a low profile, and has a size that is ideal for average needs.* The numbers are big enough to see easily at a glance.* There are enough useful options, and this watch is not overloaded with too many options.  Too many options are confusing to me.  I like the simplicity of this watch and the ease of use of the options it has.* I like the plastic watch band.  I have tried the velcro strap bands and they wear out after a year or so of use.  The plastic band will eventually break, but is fairly easy to replace.* I like the price.  At less than 35 dollars I have everything I need in a watch.* I like and use frequently the Indiglo feature.  I have even used Indiglo to find my way to the bathroom at night from bed! The light on the dial is bright enough to make your way through the dark for a short trip!Things I don't like:There is not much I don't like about this Timex watch.  I suppose my biggest complaint about this watch and any Timex watch is the difficulty in changing the battery.  The battery will eventually need replacement, and of course one has to take off the back of the watch to replace the battery.  This is tricky and takes a steady hand.  I wish Timex would make the battery more accessible so changing the battery would be as easy as sliding one in or out of a hinged door (like on a hearing aid).Obviously, there is much more to like about this watch than not like.  I do recommend it for a good sport watch.  It will withstand chlorine pools, lake water, rainfall, high and low temperatures, but be careful not to scratch the dial window!  I scratched the main window crystal and ruined my last watch.  Avoid spraying any kind of bug repellant on the window as well, as this can mar (dull) the surface.For me, this watch meets all my needs and I give it a 5-star rating.  My needs are faily simple.  There are certainly other watches that offer more features, but to me, the added features add complexity and are not worth the added bother.The price is good.  The watch is good quality. This is a good buy.Jim "Konedog" Koenig
summary: Lightweight, Options, and Ease of Use Make this a Great Watch

reviewText: This is a good, disposable watch that I expect to last about two years. On the plus side: the watch is smaller and lighter than my previous watch (a G-shock); the display is easy to read, and the buttons seem to work easier. On the minus side: the strap feels a bit brittle compared to straps on previous Timex sports watches, and the loop through which it must be pushed is very thin. The strap loop was a weak point on a previous Timex watch. When it broke, the replacement cost would have been $11 or so -- too high in relation to the cost of replacing the entire watch. In my experience with these watches the strap, strap loop, or battery fail in 18 months to 2 years. But the price of the watch is low enough that I am happy to replace the watch regularly. Because of my experiences with straps and strap loops failing, I plan to wear the watch most of the time (even when showering, so that I am not stressing the strap or strap loop.One final note: the buttons are a darkish blue that makes this watch look more sporty than if the buttons were black. I would have preferred an all black watch, since I often wear it in business meetings.

reviewText: This is the second one of these that I have had.  The first one lasted a little over 2 years before the band finally broke.  The cheap bands are the only thing I have against these kinds of watches, but it seems all watch bands of this type break sooner or later.  I paid $35 for it so I got my money out of the last one. The watch itself has ran perfectly.  I would buy another one, as I'm a runner and it works the way I want it to.
easy to use, but was not crazy about the bent hard shell formed by the first two links of the band on either side of the watch face.

I bought this watch 15 months ago and I've worn it daily and used it for lap swimming weekly. It has worked flawlessly. I frequently use the countdown timer, the 3 alarms, and the chrono (laps) feature. The features are relatively easy to use although sometimes I can't remember which button does what.Another reviewer said the watch buttons shouldn't be pressed underwater, but I do that while lap swimming and the watch has given me no trouble.A few days ago, the rubber retainer clip that notched into the wristband broke off. Yesterday, the wristband broke off at the point where it was buckled. Since the wristband is an integral part of the watch, this renders the watch unwearable. I guess 15 months of daily use out of a watch that cost less than $35 isn't too shabby but I'm a bit frustrated that now I have this otherwise perfectly good watch I can't wear any more.Update, September 09: I bought a replacement for this watch in February 08. The strap just broke in the same place. So this time it lasted 18 months. Someone commented on my review that you can replace the watch strap but I couldn't find any replacement on the timex web site.

I've had this watch for two weeks and everything works well as with the other ironman watches I've had. The only gripe is what others have said - the "resin" strap. It's definitely the weak link in the overall design, but for cost and function, I don't know of a better alternative.
summary: What else is there to say - it's an Ironman

reviewText: I bought this watch thinking it was an exact replacement for my previous Ironman watch. It wasn't - it was smaller and the display has much less contrast (grayish background).  Would have worked, but I didn't like it and so returned it.

This is my third Timex Ironman 100m watch of basically the same design.  I love the watch.  It is durable enough for swimming, jogging, soccer refereeing, and every day wear.  Big, easy to read numerals for the time display make it easy to read on the run.  The buttons are intuitive and easy to use.  The only thing I hate is the tab at the end of the band.  It does it's job of preventing the band from flopping around, but it can be very difficult to undo it to remove the watch.

Over the years I've owned several generations of Timex Ironman watches, along with other competitor's sports watches. This is the best so far and it is a pleasure to see that Timex is constantly refining and improving the Ironman brand in small and very useful ways. Small but extremely useful improvements over the last Ironman watch I owned include:- The Flix feature. This is very useful at night when you only have one hand available. Just activate the night mode, flick your wrist and the watch face illuminates for a few seconds.- When you press the Indiglo button, the face stays lit for a few seconds instead of only as long as you hold the button. Subtle change but big help.- When you press the Set button in any mode, helpful flashing icons appear which let you know which of the five buttons does what function (e.g. "+" to advance a number.) This pretty much eliminates ever needing to refer to the instruction manual.- The wristband curves where it interfaces with the watch for a better fit around your wrist.- The plastic loop which secures the un-notched portion of the band to the other half of the band has a notch which fits into a special hole in the free end of the band. This keeps the loose portion of the band secure around your wrist so that it never snags.The continual evolution in features, rock solid reliability, and excellent value for price will keep me a loyal Ironman user in the future.
This watch was purchased after my other chrono died. I love the size of the face, very easy to read. The buttons are large and easy to use. It has a comfortable fit and nice style. Highly recommend.
My husband is a firefighter and doesn't want an expensive watch but needs one that holds up pretty well in some challenging situations.  This watch does the job perfectly.
summary: Can't beat it for the price

reviewText: I'm not a fan of watches in general. I only wear them when necessary. No more memorizing how many beeps and mashes on a button the size of a flea butt it takes to get back to countdown mode after checking the time. Also, nice backlight that manages to avoid being both too dim and bright enough to spotlight a deer.Extra plus - survived being held hostage for 72 hours by my three-year-old son. It's the only item to ever do so and not come back to me with missing chunks, bite marks or unidentifiable internal injuries.Easily the most useful and appealing watch I've ever used on the field and while doing work around the house.

reviewText: I bought this watch from Target in 1994.  16, yes 16 years later and it still is going strong!  The only thing I've ever done to it is replace batteries when it stops working for a couple of bucks and 10 minutes from Walmart and then for free for some reason over all the years I've had this watch Walmart will replace the thin metal spring loaded pegs that hold the (Mine is silverish metal band but the watch is the same) band to the watch.  They bend out of shape about every 6 months.  You have to be careful not to lose your watch because sometimes it gets caught and bends the pegs and the band pops right off.  Think of them as sacrificial pins.  For a few bucks you can buy a whole pack of them yourself and replace them with some practice and no tools in under 5 minutes.  I got it when I was 16 and it has gone through 14 years of military service so far!  I have pictures of me in basic training wearing it.  Anyway the silver has worn off around the raised bezel areas and along the sides where the crown is, so it looks gold.  The raised bezel has saved the face of the watch from many scratches.  Great watch.  Who knew?

From experience, we recommend a second pair of glove inserts for all gloves.  These are stored within the shells, two inserts in each shell.  They can stay on the back of the hand and not interfere with using your fingers.  Still recommend they be put close to the body when out and about to change when the pair in use gets wet.

If you shop around, a lot of military surplus products really can't be beat for quality and value. Obviously, with usgi surplus, you are not paying for fashion, but function. I needed the warmest mittens available that were still functional as work gloves. These gloves are excellent quality and are perfect for actually USING them! They're not too pretty nor expensive so that you're afraid to dirty them up or scuff them; they are dirt cheap, well-designed and rugged. The leather palms are thick and tough. They are perfect for gathering firewood, shoveling, or snowblowing. Also perfect for staying idle for hours at a time, like when ice fishing. When the dexterity of your index finger is needed, it can slide into the available extra finger. When trigger finger is not needed, it slides nicely alongside the other fingers to capture as much warmth as possible. Comes with ambidextrous wool liners. (Note: A reviewer above erroneously commented that he received 2 right hands- this is wrong. The liners will fit either hand by design.)I bought 2 pairs for this price!Bonus modification information if you are handy with a hot glue gun or needle and thread:I also purchased "3M Thinsulate jacket insulation", available here on Amazon for just a few dollars. After turning the mittens inside-out, I made 3 patterns in the Thinsulate fabric for each mitten, which I then hot-glued to the existing seams around the edges of the mittens. I put 2 layers on the palm side and 1 layer on each back side. Finally, I turned the mittens right-side-out.Now the mittens are so warm that when sliding your hands inside the liners and shells, the captured heat is profoundly evident immediately! Grand total for each pair is still under twenty bucks, and the hobbyist side of me feels gratified for the modification project.I will put the warmth of these modified mittens up against ANY OTHER PAIR now manufactured.They are that good.

Came as expected, but came with dead battery installed.  Was a little worried the strap was defective.  As soon as I got and replaced a new battery, it worked just fine.UPDATE: after 2-3 times use per week on 2-3 hour bike rides for the past couple months since my purchase, I have noticed the heart rate indicating crazy and random heart rates.  I have very in tune with my heart rate at various exertion levels.  When I am doing a light warm up and am in a low heart rate zone- say somewhere in the 130's, I'd glance down to notice the indicator displaying 210.  And what I notice has happened even more often is the heart rate showing extremely low rates- for example, an hour into an intense ride and during a tough part where my heart rate should show the 180's, the strap is sending off 120 readings.  So it's not even close. And I would guess that when I glance down- its probably way off 25% of the time. The 75% of the time that I would consider accurate- its just my guess that it seems like its accurate. Near my max heart rate but not quite there, but lactic acid building, look down and see 170's which sounds right compared to past experience.  But the 25% off is significant. And its made me wonder about the remaining 75% of the time that I think its accurate- maybe its not. I realize that I may have a fluke/dud, as my past strap that came with my watch was always consistent and accurate- very reliable (no random numbers).  I didn't return during this time because I thought the unit would correct itself or I would try various locations and strategies to make it more accurate. But nothing worked. I've owned several heart rate monitors over the years. Especially for middle aged and older athletes, an HRM can inform you with great precision whether you are in your aerobic "zone" or how much under or over it you are. I have abandoned all my fancy bike computers and rely on my excellent Timex watch with HR display to get a good workout without having to track an array of stats.My original Timex strap, even with new battery, became unable to communicate with the watch for longer and longer periods of time until it became useless. This new strap worked fine right away. Follow the tips below to get good results from your HR strap:- Replace the C0232 battery every three months.- Coat the strap's receiver zones with a thin film of Spectra 36O Electrode Gel. This works far better at maintaining a good connection than does spit or hair gel.- Position the strap a little further down your rib cage than seems ideal. For me, having the center of the strap just below my sternum works best. If you start losing the signal during a ride or run, grab the middle of the strap from outside your shirt and position it a little higher or lower.Happy aerobic exercising!
