This watch is perfect for soccer and maybe some other sports too. True story: Last night I refereed a game that had a injury delay late in the second period.  I started the count up timer and then when everything was reset stopped it.  One team broke the 1:1 tie with literally 1 second left in extra time. How did I know?  Because of this nice little watch.  The goal, the beep, the whistle all in bang-bang sequence.  I have never has such an exciting finish and been so sure that I got the extra time right.

i used this watch as football referee , it`s good and simple , easy to use and functioning , the only disadvantage is when you use the ascending way it dose not give the beep sound as descending way at each 15 minutes or at the end of the half time or the end of time , but it`s okay , the light is so weak and useless because i use it in bright places so i don`t care about it , comparing to spintso watch or casio referee watch  this product is recommended due to price and compatibility , overall it`s worth to buy and use , by the way i bought this product twice for me and several times for my colleague referees and we are happy with it.

This is the first and only referee watch I've purchased and used (full disclosure). I have found that it works extremely well as a count-down and as a count-up timer. Since I do mostly youth games, I haven't had much cause to use the stoppage timer, but I've tested it and I like how it works. My only gripe is that there is no way to disable the beep alerts that sound when time is almost out, when time expires, and when stoppage time runs out. I find that everyone else near me (players, coaches, parents) can hear my watch beeping, and they aren't afraid to let me know about it (quite irritating)! I don't understand why there are two backlight buttons with identical functionality; surely someone could have added another cool feature on that extra button? Perhaps a toggle function for the beep?

I purchased this watch last week and used it on an adult game and 2 tournament games.  The watch works well.  I like the single noise beep reminder at 30' and 15'.  The stoppage time clock feature is neat and I'm sure it'll come handy.  Great watch for the price.Two minor annoying things:1. When the countdown reaches 30 seconds, the watch beeps 10 times 4 short beeps.  It feels like it lasts for the full 30 seconds and it's an overkill; one series of 4-5 beeps would probably be enough.  The instructions state that pushing any button will stop the alarm.  I tried pushing the screen light button (right below the screen) but it didn't stop the sound.2. In a puzzling feature, the countdown timer can be set up to 99 minutes.  As most of us referees work games of varying length, the process of resetting the watch from 45' to 30' (like going from a U18 to a U12 game) requires scrolling all the way to 99 then from 1 to 30.  It seems trivial but it's unnecessary as anything longer than 45' in soccer is waste.
summary: Good ref watch - a few annoying features

reviewText: I bought two of these in March of 2011. They both still work, and they are the only two watches I have ever used during this time as a soccer referee. One of the two watch backlights no longer functions, which is odd, because I never actually used the backlights to begin with!The watch (in stopwatch/timer mode) has three lines: the bottom line is the current time of day (which can be set to 12 or 24 hour clock), middle row is the time remaining in the period of play (it counts down, then begins counting up when it hits 00:00:00), top row is an extra timer that counts up (for the purpose of measuring the amount of stoppage time you might wish to add).The only thing i don't like about this watch (and something i would definitely toss these in the trash over, if i could find a watch that remedies this issue), is that, to set the timer, you can only scroll UP through the digits. In other words, if you are reffing back-to-back games, and need to change the watch from 35 minutes down to 30 minutes, you have to press the button 95 times, and watch as the watch scrolls up from 35 to 99, then back to 00, then finally up to 30. Sometimes I just hold the button and start paying attention to something else (who wants to stare at a timer going from 35 to 99?), and accidentally miss the time i was aiming for, meaning i have to scroll through all the numbers again!Please, oh please, tell me there is a decent soccer watch out there that lets you scroll DOWN to the appropriate time?!
summary: Does the job - Wish it would scroll DOWN when setting the stopwatch

reviewText: As with all digital watches, you have to spend a little time reading the manual so that you can learn how to use the 5 buttons on this watch. Once you do that, you can easily use this watch for games of varying length.

Whwn i opened my watch, there was no battery, so i went and had one put in it and the beeping sound was really faint. Within several hours, the watch was dead again. I returned it within the next 2 days.

This is your standard rubberized outdoor watch. It seems to be able to handle some moisture well (ie., sweat from running as well as precipitation during games).It is multi-function, but in practice you're not going to use all the fancy features when you're on the field.The watch claims to have a beeper, but mine never makes any noise (thankfully! I don't want my soccer watch to beep). However, the documentation says it's supposed to beep (maybe with an option to turn the beeping off), so it just casts doubts on the overall quality of the device if the documentation & the product don't match up.The LED isn't very bright, but I haven't ever needed it - I don't use the watch for anything but refereeing and you don't play without lights now do you? However if you wanted the light at other times you'd probably be disappointed with it.It is relatively easy to read the watch when I'm on the field, and the buttons have to be firmly pressed to start & stop the timer, so I haven't yet had a case where the timer has accidentally started or stopped on me.The soccer timer works well - it resets to 45:00 when you hold the timer button down for a second, otherwise the timer button starts the countdown. When it hits 00:00 it starts counting back up so you can see how much added time has been played. The watch comes with a 2nd "added time" timer, that you use whenever there's any play stoppage on the field for which you will add time at the end of the half. The theory is, any time you think you're in a situation that calls for time to be added, you trigger this 2nd timer to count up, then when you get near the end of the half you can look at your watch and see "oh! that's 2:37 of time we've wasted, so I'll add 2 or 3 minutes of added time to the game." Whether or not you use the 2nd timer is up to you, but it's nice to know it's there.This watch is functional but not stellar - surely there has to be a better ref's watch out there? I'm giving this watch 3 stars out of 5 due to the shortcomings I've mentioned above.
summary: A simple digital soccer referee's watch

reviewText: It's okay, but my go-to watch for reffering soccer games is easily the Champion with the big display. Buy that one first before this one.

I purchased this watch for my wife to use while refereeing youth soccer matches. I have not used it myself, but I have worked the touch lines with her in a number of games and she finds it to be a very good tool for her. The particular feature that sold me on this watch, and which has proved most useful, is the implementation of the countdown timer. It gives a thirty second warning before the end of the time, then signals time and starts counting up (similar to many kitchen timers) so that you can do added time or simply be aware of the time that has elapsed since the end of the half (so you don't have to set a separate timer for halftime, for example).I purchased the Casio Men's W756B-1AV Digital Sport Watch for myself and to compare them. The Casio was less expensive at time of purchase and from a brand I was more familiar with (though I hadn't worn a Casio watch myself since a G-Shock I wore for years as a kid), but I find the Ultrak's implementation of referee/soccer specific features to be slightly better and if I were buying for a serious referee or coach, I would strongly consider getting this watch over the Casio, though both will serve well and the Casio has some other features, such as the interval timer, which are useful in other areas.
summary: Solid watch for it's intended purpose. You may also want to consider the Casio W756B-1AV depending on your needs.

reviewText: I received this watch as a gift in 2013.  It came unprogrammed - it was a college sports team watch programmed with the NASCAR schedule for 2008.  Instead of the team's fight song programmed as the "melody", it was the national anthem.  Little did I know there would be a $20 annual charge to update the football and basketball schedules, assuming I only update them once a season (football game times are not known until 10 days before the game in many cases).  Disappointing watch all around.

I thought this was a great idea and I really wanted it so I could show it off.  I received the watch, new, with all necessary items included.  The schedule was easy to load.  However, for some strange reason, it did not play the school's fight song.  I think it had the National Anthem, instead.  I contacted the company and was given an upload to fix this.  Well, the season ended and I was able to show off my watch that cost me a hundred bucks.  Now, I can just go on the website and download the basketball schedule, right?  Except, it costs Money to do that.  And, at the time (a few years ago) I bought this, they did not have the UF basketball schedule available.  Then I learned the saddest part of all when I went to upload the following season's football schedule.  To update the schedule every year for football, it costs extra money.I was very unhappy with that fact.  It was not mentioned anywhere when I first purchased this years ago.  The battery crapped out after a year and a half and I decided it wasn't worth paying the extra money each year for a battery and for the new upload.Also, the USB adapter that connects to the watch isn't very well made.  The piece that grips it to the watch broke after the second upload.  I was able to hold it in place and successfully use it, but just thought I'd let you know to be very careful when using it.Two more things; 1.  It defaults all games to 12 O'clock and will not update when the times change throughout the year.  How lousy is that?  You pay for one upload, you get only one upload.  2.  It does give you the schedule for other SEC teams.  That was pretty cool.

reviewText: I purchased a pair of these to use for cross training (plyometrics, strength training) and will be returning them promptly.  I wore these around the house for an hour, and they are not comfortable with an average to slightly wide foot (mine measures at just under a C width, so hovers between wide and normal).These shoes seemed to want to make the ball of my foot roll outward and off the edge of the shoe.  The heel fit great, but my arch is now aching because of the torsion on the forefoot.  This felt like a design flaw rather than some weird anatomy in my foot (I've never felt like this in a pair of athletic shoes.)I've run in Saucony's before and been very pleased.  This pair does not seem to be up to the usual standard.  Save your money and invest in a quality pair.  When a shoe is listed as being for a budget conscious runner, this is the company giving themselves a license to skimp on quality in the pursuit of being cheap.

I am a nurse and I am on my feet for the biggest part of the day, so my number one priority is comfort. Very happy with purchase.

They held up like a champ and despite record snowfall that year, kept my feel dry and warm the entire trip.From there they carried me through daily 3 mile hikes with my dogs through rain, shine, ice and snow, and never let me down.  Eventually, they did wear out and I gladly purchased another pair.They do take a little time to break in, but once done they are extremely comfortable and durable.  I love this shoe!

reviewText: I purchased these boots a little while back and i have loved them since i put them on. They might not be the best boot for extended hikes but for a good dayhike or just a everyday wearing boot these wear great. They are a little shorter cut boot but still give plenty ankle support, and what i love about them they are very light weight but very durable feeling. I love the vibram soles they are not too agressive and clean out faily easily but still with ample traction in conditions that demand it. reviewText: There is much to like about these boots -- great look, light weight, aggressive tread -- but they do not last! I have worn these boots for about 6 months doing 3 - 5 mile hikes in moderately difficult forest areas. As other reviewers have mentioned, I now have a hole on the outside edge where the leather meets the toecap. The other boot shows signs of doing the same in the near future. This is especially disappointing because I love the boots in every other way. If you like to buy new boots every 6 - 8 months, go ahead and get these, but if you want your boots to last then look elsewhere.
The leather on both boots started separating from the toe in exactly the same outside location after just 10 months of use.  Definitely was a defect.  Otherwise a very comfortable boot.

reviewText: These boots fit very well and required very little breaking in. They're lightweight and great for general hiking and for trekking over everyday snowy ground. After about a year and a half, though, the sole had become very thin and began to delaminate. The good thing is that Garmont has a very good warranty and great customer service. I had the boots sent back to Garmont, and four weeks or so later they had sent me a free replacement pair (of the next boot up in their line, the Sitka, since they were out of Flash III boots for the next few months!).
summary: Lightweight and comfortable but not the most durable

reviewText: I bought this boots about a year ago.It is very well water insulated, but has a big problem:When I walk in a hard surface like asphalt or a hard terrain, the front piece of the shoes bend together with my toes.At the left foot, the leather is bending exactly at the point at the toe junction (my right foot is smaller and it doesn't bend at the same place).When the leather folds, it makes a little bump to the inner side of the shoes and this bump touches my toe.So, when I walk the folding bump touches exactly my toe junction, and after an hour this touch starts to be a big pain.The leather is very very hard, it is not very comfortable.I would not buy it if I know about it.
summary: Hard leather makes it very uncomfortable.

reviewText: I wore out my previous pair of Garmonts and have spent several months trying on other boots to find something that fit as well -- no luck. So I jumped at the chance to buy another pair when I found them and am very pleased I did. The boots fit well, provide just enough support and have great all-round protection. They are very stiff when new and have a long break-in period but do eventually fit like the proverbial glove.

Excellent comfort, stability and support.  Very good traction.  No blisters.  I carried 60 pounds for a few days.  Took lots of day hikes on rocky terrain, some cross-country stuff in rocks.  Decent in snow too.  Prefer low tops to reduce chafing.  Lightest boots that I ever had for backpacking.  Developed a small hole near the toe shield.  These are the most comfortable boots EVER.  Where can I find replacements??

reviewText: These are comfortable boots. The materials inside and out appear to be durable and of high quality. I also purchased the low cut shoe which I found to be more comfortable. I also own shoes from Merrell, Vasque, and Asolo. I would put these boots on a class with my Asolo FSN 95 gore-tex boots, durable and waterproof. Compared to my Merrell MOAB gore-tex XCR, I would say the Garmont's are the much better quality shoe.

I'll agree with others that this brand is very comfortable, but this pair was not very durable.  It's my second pair of this style by them, and I split the sole on the outside of my arch while mowing my lawn.  The boots are about a year old, and I do use them in steep terrain.  This pair did not feel as sturdy as my last, which lasted about 3 years.

On dayhikes and weekend backpack trips in Wyoming's Wind River Range this summer, these boots were comfortable from the first wearing.  They provide superb ankle and arch support which is worth their (light) weight.

reviewText: Used these boots exclusively for a contract job in Iraq.  Once they were broken in, they felt very light weight and very comfortable over rocky, sandy, and sometimes muddy terrain.  My socks always stayed bone-dry, even when I intentionally soaked my feet in a puddle to give them a test.  If someone hadn't stole them in Costa Rica then I probably would be enjoying my third year and third trip to the desert with these boots, but since that did happen, I am here to buy another pair.  Hope this helps.

With 4,000 miles of hiking experience under my Vibrams, this is the best boot I have ever worn. But a word of caution - evaluating footwear is a VERY personal thing. The optimal boot for anyone IS THE ONE THAT FITS BEST! For me the Garmont Flash III GTX was the ticket. Any boot should be tried on inside the store first and tested on both flat surfaces and inclines wearing the socks you will be using on the trail (knowledgeable sales assistants can educate you on the critical aspects of proper fit). I was able to purchase these online without a test drive because they are my second pair. They probably won't have the durability of a pure leather boot but the trade-off in comfort and light weight was well worth it. And, even on my blister-prone feet, they fit like a glove with almost no break-in mileage necessary.

My experience with Garmont boots has been that they are very comfortable but not at all durable.These Flash IIIs were the fourth pair of Garmont boots that fell apart on my feet after just a few months of wear.  The upper leather tends to come away from the outsole along the bend lines and the treads come apart.  I have made some notes on Customer Images.While I understand that I might wear these boots harder than most, for boots to fall apart after three months of wear is not acceptable.  When I tried contacting Garmont customer support after one of these incidents, I got very poor customer service.  I was essentially called a liar by a VP who used bad statistics (I am a statistician) to not own up for his company's lack of quality.I have noticed that these boots tend to last longer in deserts than in the tropics.I only continued to wear these boots because they were extremely comfortable but for the 3rd and 4th pair, I essentially considered them disposable boots.If you intend to wear these boots for only a few months or in dry, arid climates, then they are fine.  Otherwise, they are a waste of money.

I have both this watch and theTraser T4004.357.37.01 Chrono Big Date Pro Blue, Chronograph Watch.  I like the Titanium version better but not because it's that much lighter.  In fact, it's not that much lighter.  This watch is 3.7 oz and the stainless version is 6 oz.  You notice the difference but it's not dramatic (to me).What I prefer is the finish of this watch.  It's a bit darker and a touch less shiny than the picture.  Also, there's nothing to wear away.  The only thing under the titanium is more titanium.Both watches have a couple other features I really like.  The minute hand for the stop watch goes to 30 minutes.  Other "three eye" watches track to an hour and for me it's difficult to see which minute it is.  In this case there is plenty of space between hash marks and the hand steps from one mark to halfway between to the next.  It can also do split times.  For me that's not a big deal but it's nice to have.And of course there's the Tritium.  You can easily read the time in any light, at any time, without having to depend on "charging" the luminescent material.  However, many of the marketing photos I've seen with this and other "tritium" watches do them a disservice.  The markings do not glow as brightly as they are sometimes depicted.  They are not bright enough to read the watch face, read a book, signal for help, or temporarily disorient an attacker.  They glow at a constant level, about as brightly as a "normal" watch somewhere between 10 and 30 minutes after it's been exposed to a bright light.  (Green tritium markings are perceived as glowing a bit brighter than blue ones and it's all in the same ballpark.)  For me, that is exactly what I want.
summary: A great watch but not a feather weight

reviewText: The watch is exactly what I needed. I first saw Traser watches at a watch store, but came to Amazon for pricing. Thanks to the titanium, it's very lightweight. The dial is excellent during the day, white numbers on a black face. Reminds me of precision gauges used in sports cars in the 1950s and 1960s. At night? Incredible. The glowing needles are the reason to buy this watch. Many high-end watches look great during the day, but you can hardly read them at night. Traser should include a couple of extra links for the bracelet, though the existing bracelet fits well. Because of the nighttime clarity, this is now my favorite watch.
Very good looking watch, original, beautiful design. I recommend it with no doubt! Very light (due to its titanium construction.

Well I have to admit that this is the most expensive watch that I've ever owned.  I think my highest priced one was less than a hundred bucks.  Moving up to the $650 range was a big jump for me.  The photo on this webpage doesn't do the watch justice, it's like looking at a fuzzy outline of a beautiful woman compared to seeing her in person!  This watch is simply breathtaking.I love that it has a chronograph but it's not too busy like most and you can easily see what time it is at a quick glance.  For some reason I thought this watch had a screw down crown but it doesn't.  And the bezel doesn't rotate.  The user manual said you can use it for swimming and snorkling but not scuba diving, you need 200 m water resistance for that.  It also says that you shouldn't use it in a hot tub or it can leak from the heat, interesting.  I also thought the tritium would glow a bit brighter than it does, it's rather dim but it is readable in any light if you look close.I had to bring it to the shop to get one link removed and they charged me ten bucks, probably because they saw an expensive watch and figured I could afford it, they were right!  Getting the watch serviced may be tricky depending on where you live.  Here in Colorado there is only one shop that is qualified to work on it.  You can see the shops at the traser.com website.  I really love the gun metal grey band, it's really solid and has a good feel to it.  It looks like it would be extremely scratch resistant and it you did happen to scratch it I bet it wouldn't show very much because of the textured finish which is like a very fine sand blasted finish.By the way, it's not listed on this site but the face is 40mm which is a really nice 'normal' watch size.  The face may be a little thick but I don't think its out of balance with the watch.  Overall I would highly recommend this watch, at least now that I've owned it for half a day.  Hopefully in a few weeks or months my review won't change!~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Update:  I weighed my watch today and it was 112.2 grams with one link missing.  By the way, I tried to find another watch that had tritium tubes, a titanium band, and a sapphire crystal and I can't find one anywhere.  Apparently this watch has no competition if you want those three things!~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Another update:  Well I wore the watch to bed last night and woke up in the middle of the night to see how bright it was and lo and behold it was really really bright!  I guess it just takes some time for your eyes to get used to the darkness and this thing really lights up!

I've had this watch for a few years now.  My dad gave it to me because he complained the face was too thick.This watch has it all.  It is titanium so you know it won't ever weigh down your wrist.  It has a sapphire face, so you won't ever scratch it unless you wear it to hard labor.  It's got the tachymeter, which comes in handy in the manufacturing industry.  The H3 means that it is always illuminated.  And not to mention, the looks are just great.  I love the grey band with the black face.This watch keeps time pretty well, and it is a stunning piece of Swiss work.  I would definitely recommend this product to anyone who wants an amazing watch, but does not want to pay an amazing price.

I really needed a durable watch that I could use both at work and for dinner out. This watch fills the bill perfectly! It has the size and heft for everyday use while the titanium makes the watch lighter and more comfortable for nights out on the town compared to a stainless steel watch. The added bonus of the tritium tubes at ever hour and on the hour, minute, and second hand means that it is easy to see in a dark room or at night. I have had this watch for 2 months now and it has withstood what I put it through on the job (I'm a vineyard manager) while maintaining it's beauty for after work hours.Most people compare this watch with watches from Luminox. I have watches from both brands and I like both equally. Main thing is going to come down to price and style preference.If you are in the market for a watch of high quality that is under $1000 then this is one I would put toward the top of the list!

Very nice watch.  Looks great.  Very light, which is expected for titanium. The band is much nicer then my Luminox or Citizens titanium  watches.  My previous titanium watches have a silver/steel hue, but this a more flat golden color which is more attractive.  Very readable in the dark with the Tritium capsules on the hands and the dial.  Only oddity is that the second hand only moves when the chrono is turned on.  Keeps time accurately.

I've had this watch for 3.5 months now and I can say it is really great.  It's too bad the there have been significant price increases in the Swiss watches over the summer.For the size, this watch is very light weight at less than 98g. The light weight and titanium build make it very comfortable even on hot days.  The watch as a nice band with a push-release and safety catch. I like it better than my other Traser Auto Pro, which does not have a push-release. The watch was supplied with the proper manual, which can be very useful for a chronograph. Obviously the Tritium Illumination is killer... that is why you buy this watch... if you don't need that... then you should spend the money on features you want.If there was one thing I could change it would be the white lettering on the tachymeter; I would really prefer black. Then if I could change one more thing I would rather have the large second hand indicate the seconds when the chronograph is not in use rather than the 3OC subdial, this is easier to read and the hand would not interfere with the large date display at 12OC. These are fairly standard for Chronograph movements though so I accept them.  They are minor really.This watch is Fabulous!
summary: Fabulous!! Titanium and Tritium H3 is the Reason to Buy

I am a watch junkie and have always been a fan of Seiko kinetic watches for their affordability as well as their reliability.  I did not purchase this watch via Amazon because it wasn't available here at the time of my order so I picked it up locally from a Seiko Authorized Reseller to ensure I would have the Seiko Warranty in effect.This is a Kinetic watch which means it collects energy from the motion of your arm throughout the day and stores it.  On a full charge, this watch will run approximately 1 month without movement.  This Velatura also features "Direct Drive" which means that you can hand wind the crown to build up a bit of a charge.  While this feature is cool, it's a little more gimmicky than practical.  Picking it up and giving it a few shakes side to side is enough to build up enough charge to get things rolling.  Trying to hand wind this to any sort of power reserve is going to take FOREVER making it extremely impractical.The face is well organized, the gentle arc on the far left of the face is your power reserve meter.  At the top, the "M" represents a Months charge, in decending order you have "W" for Week, "D" for Day, and then 12 & 0 for hours left on the charge.  At the bottom of the face, in the 6 o'clock position is the date.  On the lower right side between the 3-5 position is the Day of the week display.  This makes for a beautiful design that is also extremely functional to read in my opinion.The face is black vertical lines that add an element of depth to the face with rose gold accents on the hands, power reserve dial, and day of the week dials.  Each of the primary hand positions (5,10,15, 20 etc) are luminescent circles with a ring of rose gold accent.The only flaw this watch has, as I see it anyway, is the band.  The band itself is fine, but being a silicone/rubber type it seems to be a little prone to failure.  I had to replace the first one when the strap guard snapped off for no reason (no damage just snapped off when putting it on one day).  I think the Seiko replacement set me back $60 which seems like an awful lot for what it is, considering it only last a couple years.  This was before Amazon started to carry them, and while they are less, they are still about $40 here.  I do prefer metal bands for their durability, but the rose gold on this watch makes that a little difficult to find a good match.  I've purchased several third party bands that are supposed to fit, even had reviews from people saying they used them on this watch but I couldn't ever get them installed.  Even after taking it to a few local watch-smiths here locally, they couldn't get them on right.I wear this as a daily driver since it dresses up and down so well.  Looks great with a suit or jeans and a t-shirt.  This is a larger watch that may look a little out of place on an extremely skinny wrist.  Be sure to check out the pictures online of people wearing them to get a feel for it or better yet, find one locally so you can try it on.At the end of the day, I love this watch.  I always get complements when I wear it and it's comfortable on the wrist.  It also keeps great time.  If I had one wish, I would love a Seiko replacement metal band in black with a rose gold accent on the safety clasp, but I don't think that will happen.  I'd definitely pick up another one if anything were to happen to this watch.  Couldn't go without it now!
summary: Beautiful & Reliable Watch that Turns Heads

Let me start out by saying that getting to a point with your elderly parent that you realize this type of product is needed...it's very sad. It's hard to think in terms of your once active parent, in my case my mother, needing to be strapped in while in bed for her own safety. But when you do have to make that mental transition, it's good to know there are products like this available.I made the decision to buy this Posey vest after my mother--who does NOT have dementia, Alzheimer's, or any other mental deficiency--refused to obey one simple rule: DO NOT get out of bed unaided. She had fallen a number of times (luckily, without any injuries), and it was just a matter of time before she would've gotten hurt. I had already gotten her an adjustable hospital bed, thinking that its rails would be sufficient to keep her in bed. I was wrong!So I reluctantly ordered the vest.It's very lightweight because of its primarily mesh construction. The mesh is also very breathable and does not make the person hot.Its straps are plenty long enough to tie on each side of the hospital bed, while still allowing the person to move around, like rolling from side to side. You'll have to experiment to find how tight or loose works best for the person you're using this on. You want to allow them some freedom of movement, yet the whole point is to make sure they're safely kept in bed. So too much leeway could lead to problems!The vest can be tossed in the washer and dryer as needed.When I ordered this the only size available was medium. My mother is TINY, like 4'8" and less than 100 pounds. The medium is a bit loose on her, although adjusting its straps helps get around this issue. But if I had it to do over again, and if small had been available, I'd definitely get the smaller size.
summary: Works as expected and is comfortable

I ordered this vest in hopes of using it to keep my elderly mother from falling out of bed.  The information on the website was not at all clear about the fact that the vest was NOT recommended for use as a restraint on a hospital bed.  That information was only made clear in the one-page brochure included with the vest.  Since the vest would not work the way I hoped, I returned it.  Not only did the company charge me a 15% restocking fee, they also charged me $5 for postage, even though I was not charged a shipping charge for the initial order and it only cost me $2.45 postage to return the vest to the company--and that was sending it first class!!!! The company is probably no more than 15-20 miles from my house.  Quite frankly, I wouldn't give this company any stars and I will most definitely NEVER order anything from them again.

My father in law lived with us.  He was a 90 years old, 6ft tall -110 lbs. Holocaust survivor.We loved and respected him very much.  The decision to use restraints was not an easy one. But he was falling down every night when he tried to get up to use a urinal.  No matter how many times I told him to just go in his depends, he was NOT incontinent and would still try to get up - I started to think he may have been a circus acrobat the way he could climb over the bed rails - but this was the one thing that helped us to keep him safe. He actually would put his arms up and ask us to put it on at night, I think he knew it was for his own safety. I got some resistance from health workers as if it was mean, but the truth is, Papa lived with us till the day he passed (just 2 weeks ago) we didn't put him in a home like many others would do, we loved him very much and wanted him to be around family when his time came, and we were able to do this with the help of these restrains. (I didn't think I would be able to take care of him if he had broken his hip) If you are considering this step in the stage of life, I highly recommend this type of restraint, it was comfortable, easy to keep clean, and easy to tie at night, and untie in the morning.I liken this to parents who keep their kids on a leash- I used to criticize other mothers who used this, till I had a VERY active 2 year old boy who ran into the street one to many times. Suddenly it no longer seemed cruel, and seems like the responsible thing to keep the one you love safe!

reviewText: Pants are extremely well made and run true to size(not overly long in the leg). Belt loops really hold the pants up during the endless bending and twisting on a job site. Pants are heavy, not the best for hot humid conditions, but will be just right for the fall in the northeast. Very pleased with Amazon's price point on these pants.

I have had a pair of the Heavy Worker pants for several years, and bought a new pair because mine are starting to look ratty. They haven't worn out, and will probably be around for a long time to come. I have loved them, and will continue to wear them when I don't have to look presentable for clients.The new ones, however, have a radically different cut. The waist/rise is at least and inch higher, and the legs are longer with the kneepads lower for the same listed size. They also feel wider and generally less tailored. I believe they have changed the cut to accommodate 'muhrican's physiques, which, shall we say, are usually somewhat less athletic than the Swedes. For those of us without any extra insulation, however, these new ones just won't work. I had the same luck with the Bantam model, unfortunately.Too bad--now I'll be searching for another work pant brand that hasn't lost its European cut.
summary: The cut has changed a lot in the last few years!

reviewText: I purchased these pants after reading a review in a construction publication. The pants were everything I expected and more.So as such I have since purchased their heavy workers canvas jacket and the Two Fisted fleece.I always look forward to wearing them (one at a time of course).Back to the pants and Blakladers customer service. My pants had a zipper failure. I e-mailed Blaklader and I received a response promptly stating that they would replace the pants or pay to have the pants repaired. My pants were already well used (I built a house in them) so I figured I got my money worth.I still had them repaired at my local dry cleaner as they have plenty of life in them. The owner of the dry cleaner made a statement to the effect that he coveted these pants. Mind you the pants were covered in paint,and had places were I rubbed up against wood truss plates which are very sharp (yet the pants were not cut clear through) .I wear the Blaklader Workwear Bantam Pants as every day use and are my favorite pair of pants for this purpose.I will continue to purchase Blaklader.Steve
They are great quality work pants, my husband loves them. Very durable and heavy duty for what he does. This brand is all he ever wears for work.
I use this pants every day..... Good on my needs..  Make me more productive keeping  tools on the utility pockets..Make sure to buy one small size..

Worth every penny.  the ONLY thing to keep in mind about these is the waist is tighter than it seems go up a size in the waist.11-11-13 I have now had these pants for 2 years and I can whole heartedly tell you these are the best pants I have ever owned. They are still almost brand new looking (there are a few wear marks) even though I wear them 2 times a week or so and I'm not easy on my pants I work as a mason and go through carhartts with the double fronts in 3 to 4 months. I once caught my pant leg on a sharp piece of metal the pants were so Strong they pulled me to the ground and I found my self hanging from my leg, dangling a few feet in the air but they didn't rip at all. there's still two little holes but if I were wearing any other pants I would have been naked. These are great! Spend the little extra and you won't regret it. At least I don't. That being Said,there are a few problems: the knee pads are a little low-not a big deal. And if you're in the tropics working they are a bit heavy and hot.
They are virtually indestructible. Well worth price! I am a tile setter and the knee pads in pants are great.
I love these pants! They get the job done! Sturdy and tough. The only thing I could wish for was a cargo pocket, but still these are great pants.

I am a new convert won over from the Skiller's line of products, and wanted to let you know that I appreciate the quality that you put into your products. They appear to be a more thoroughly thought out design than Skiller's, as well. I really like the divided pouches, quality of construction (triple stitched seams), and quality of material.My introduction to your line was to purchase a pair of heavy worker pants, which arrived Friday (2-25-11). The only thing I would change with this pair of pants is the color of the cordura reinforced areas to brown or another earth tone color that doesn't reveal dirt, cat hair, etc. as much as black does... a worse color for showing dirt cannot be found than black (It has never made sense to me why anyone working with their knees/calves in contact with the floor would want black or navy blue pants). Maybe you should include a lint roller with each pair you sell?  :o) Also, lighter colors absorb considerably less solar heat for those working outdoors in the sunny, temperate climates.I think it would be WONDERFUL if Blaklader could offer a line of work pants made from hemp fabric, as it is 3.5 times more durable than cotton fabrics, and, being a natural fiber, keeps the wearer considerably cooler than the poly cotton fabric. Hemp is also a "greener" product as it requires no pesticides, which would be a drawing point in the ever-increasing consciousness of natural, eco-friendly alternatives to petro-fabrics. It would also be great if you could offer your (hemp) pants in some sort of patterned design that hides inevitable stains, perhaps like a digital camo, rather than solid colors (I don't think I'm ready for tie-dyed work pants, though... :o)The quality of your pants is high, I'd just like to encourage you think a little further outside of the box in the materials, colors and pattern departments.~~~~~~~~~~~~I called the U.S. customer service line for Blaklader just after sending the above note to them, to ask about some features I was unfamiliar with.  When I introduced myself to the rep she recognized my name and said that she was just reading my email (so they actually do read emails!) She was friendly and knowledgeable enough about the pants to answer my questions (pertaining to a steel button and extra loop on the right leg, which is made for fastening and securing a special utility knife used in Sweden, which features have been phased out of the current U.S. versions of these pants... I just happened to get a pair of pants from an earlier lot). I was impressed with their customer service and demeanor.White cat hair from my first assignment in these pants is plastered all over the knees and cuffs of these pants... and is VERY noticeable. I'm sure sheetrock dust would contrast well with the black as well. Just something to be aware of, as everyone else will be, too.UPDATE: July 2013After over two years of use the knee pad pockets finally wore through and there is a minor bit of fabric wear above the knees. Otherwise these pants have held up superbly.
summary: Great Pants, Nevertheless could be improved...

reviewText: Pants are extremely well made.  It's nice to not have to wear a tool belt when wearing these pants.  The pockets are sturdy and well thought out.  The knee pad holders are a great idea -- no more annoying, uncomfortable straps to have to deal with.  Don't really even notice when kneepads are in.  Only complaint -- the kneepads tend to slip out.  I think I will try to get a zipper or snaps sewn in and then they will be perfect.

I like to wait awhile before I review items to see if they live up to my expectations.  I bought a pair of these pants about a year ago and they do...so much so that I bought another pair about a month ago.My work is outside and requires a lot of kneeling on concrete, asphalt, or rocky ground while repairing equipment.  These are the best pants I have ever owned in more than 25 years of this work.Some things I like about these pants:1. A year later and the original pair I bought shows hardly any wear.2. The extra wide/long belt loops don't tear off like thin ones do.3. The knee pads are removeable so I can use one pair for both pairs of pants.4. The knee pad pockets are built-in, so I don't have to mess with straps that are either so loose that they slip down or are so tight thay they chafe the back of my knee and/or cut off the circulation to my leg.5. Each knee pad pocket has a pocket inside on the bottom so the knee pad will not fall out.6. I can put items in the utility pockets and wear the pockets outside my seatbelt when I'm driving so I can easily reach in to get something.7. The fabric is strong and durable (see #1), yet they are breathable enough to not get overheated in hot summer weather.8. There are more than enough pockets for everything I usually carry.Some things I don't like about these pants:A year later and I still really can't think of anything.  Yes, they are a bit pricey, but they are worth every penny.  They last long enough to more than make up for the extra expense.  I will be getting more in the future so I can throw away my "swiss cheese" pants.I have had many people see these pants and ask me where I got them.  I tell them to go to Amazon.com and search for Blaklader (which I have to spell for them).  OK, maybe an easier name would be nice!8/24/13One minor negative and one suggestion for improvement.  The kneepads location is a little low for me, so I have to hike up my pants before I kneel down or else my knees will hit the ground above the pads.  The suggestion is that they make these with shin pads as well!  Ouch!The first pair of pants I bought a few years ago finally developed a hole in one knee and the zipper pull broke off.  They are still very usable, though, and I will.

First I wanted to secure the glitter as it does seem somewhat "unsealed" as though it could come off especially in areas where the shoes bend, or in the toe area.I mistakenly took the advice of one of the reviewers to use gloss "Mod Podge" on the shoe to  secure the glitter.  Although the Mod Podge definitely seems to seal the shoe BE WARNED that it instantly dulls the metallic quality of the glitter!  The shoe with no Mod Podge brilliantly sparkled, while the one with the sealant looked covered with a shiny coat of plastic and lost all it's sparkle.  I ended up giving the shoes a second coat of Mod Podge and immediately dousing them in red glitter (while the spray was still wet) and patting it down with my fingers.  This brought back the sparkle and sealed the glitter beneath.  So far the glitter is holding but shoes only have light wear.  Use Mod Podge/sealant at your own risk - it completely changes the look of the shoes!  It may be a better idea to patch bald spots as needed using this method, than to dull the shoe overall.  If you are not concerned with high sparkle, but more with setting the glitter tightly then use this method.  Your shoe will be more glossy than glittery.

I knew the shaft would be too narrow at the very top and I need an extra inch or so. It's not the boots that are the problem...and for not being a wide shaft boot, I'm kind of surprised I can pull these on. I can wear them with pants, but my husband does a bit of leather work and he is going to make another split on the inside of the boot so I cam get the extra inch or so. I feel it would still be worth it to keep them.I've been wearing these for about a half hour inside and I feel them easily stretching a bit so breaking them in will be easy. reviewText: This is my second pair of MBT Kisumu Sandals.  The price I paid at Amazon is really discounted from what I spent for my first pair years ago. Updated Review:I was a bit hasty in my previous review.  It turns out that due to some confusion between Amazon's ordering system and the seller's system what I received was actually a woman's US size 9.  Shoemania quickly and politely corrected the problem, emailing me a prepaid return label and sent off another in the correct size.  Though they forgot to honor the 2-day shipping agreement they promptly credited me the price difference.  I've had a few weeks to try these sandals now and I like them very much.  I bought them to replace my beloved Mephistos which I had for years and had worn threadbare.  I'm diabetic and have problems wearing most other tighter fitting shoes so sandals tend to be my footwear of choice.These sandals do take some getting use to - they're a lot like walking on cushy rockers.  This makes it more comfortable to walk as the sandals rock forward with you in natural walking motion.  It is possible, however, to accidentally rock backwards far enough to fall backwards, so some care is necessary.  They are comfortable enough to wear all day and on extended walking tours.  One nit is that the strap that goes across the instep tends to push into your foot causing a little discomfort.  This is unavoidable as a result of the walking/rocking motion that is the point of the design.  Another nit is that the clips that secure the straps are a bit small and they're a little difficult to maneuver.  Overall, though, they are an excellent product - well made.  They still don't beat my beloved Mephistos, but they are 2/3 the price and a fine replacement.Previous Review:I wish I could comment on this sandal for its comfort and ergonomic design, but I am unable to squeeze into this very expensive miniature to be able to tell.  When I opened the box I immediately noticed the size problem and checked the markings on the heel strap - European size 40 1/3, US size 9.5.  Puzzled, as the sandals are significantly smaller than my other size 9.5 shoes, I took them to my friend at Nordstrom who measured them with his spiffy meter.  European size 38.5 / US size 8.  That seems more like it.  Why such a significant difference?  Have they no quality control?  For as expensive as these sandals were I expect much better.

I had never before spent anywhere near this kind of money on a shoe.  But I had plantar fasciitis very badly for 3 years- to the point that when we went shopping my husband would drop me off at the door of the store - I would get what I needed and leave, and be almost in tears by the time I left.  At work I never wanted to get up from my desk.  I had tried all the exercises and everything I could to get rid of the pain, but it just persisted.We went to the mall one day, having to go by the shoe store to get to where we were going - and I saw these.  I didn't believe they would really help, but I had heard of them before, so I asked to try them on.  From the first moment I put them on, I could walk without pain.  I never took them off.  I wore them out of the store, and we walked all over the mall that day.  They told me I should break them in slowly, but I personally never noticed any of the problems others have noted.  I have not worn anything else since, and now own 4 pairs.  I will never be without my MBT's.  The days of crying when I got up in the middle of the night are gone.  My plantar fasciitis was gone within a couple of weeks of buying the MBT's, and has never returned.  The only time I get let off at the door anymore is if it's raining hard.  I've started walking for recreation again, and have not had any problems at all -as long as I wear my MBT's.

reviewText: I picked up a pair of these after deciding that I shouldn't wear flip flops while driving. However, these are great for walking. They give an uncanny feeling of being propelled forward with every step, almost as if one is walking downhill. I do feel that I'm using muscles that I normally don't, but I haven't been walking in them for very long. I expect to get used to the feeling. Once they are adjusted, the side snap closure makes them easy to take on and off. They look like they will last for a long time, too.I had never heard of MBT, and came across these by accident while looking for sandals on sale at a large online shoe retailer. I was able to get these for $70, including tax and shipping. I checked other sites, and you shouldn't have to pay more than $100 for them. That's a lot for a sandal, not even counting the $235 price on Amazon, but the fit, comfort, and quality are commensurate with the price. They're definitely worth $70. That figure may have been a mistake, as they were back up to $180 a day later.One reviewer mentioned a seam in the middle of the rear strap. This must be referring to a different model, as mine has a single piece of material with no seam, and nothing on it other than the label. I've owned other sport sandals that made my feet bleed from how the straps cut into them, but these are extremely comfortable, even barefoot. In shoes, I wear a size 11 EEE, so since these sandals come in only one width, I had to go up to size 12. The front strap is elastic and despite the adjustment, if you have wide feet, a smaller size can be too tight.Be aware that this design is intended for walking, not standing. The convex sole works great as long as you're moving; once you come to a stop, there's no flat surface to stand on. You either want to roll back onto your heels or forward onto your toes - the place in the middle where your feet would be level is unstable. The design isn't appropriate for anyone who is on their feet all day, unless they're moving continually. It would work for a mail carrier, but not a cashier.Highly recommended if you can get them for a reasonable price.

My wife got me this watch as a gift for my first father's day. I spent weeks and looked at thousands of watches before deciding on this one. When the watch arrived a day ahead of schedule I was pretty excited. I opened the box and was greeted by a metal tin that was dented on all sides. There was also no sleeve covering the tin like I had seen in all the pictures and videos I saw while researching. I opened the tin and took the watch out. It was a real beauty. However, there were what looked like fingerprints on the crystal. As it turns out the face was pressed up against the top of the tin when the lid was closed, and some of the "Wenger" logo had adhered to the crystal. I wiped that off and noticed what looked like either a scratch or piece of dust under the crystal. I also found it odd that the time and date were set correctly out of the box. My wife bought this directly through Amazon and I'm thinking this watch had previously been returned.  Needless to say I returned it immediately. I'm sure the next person to buy the green src will get the one I returned. My suggestion is to pass on this one.

This watch is branded after the famous 'Swiss Raid Commando' military competition held annually in Switzerland and France since 1986 of which Wenger is a sponsor. The watch features the SRC logo on the obverse in color along with the French language motto "Vouloir, Croire et Oser", which translates in English to "Want, Believe and Dare". This branding may be important to a special ops soldier, military veteran or collector, but it should be understood that such branding comes with a price premium.PROS:Overall the watch has a heft and feeling of quality and refinement, it should prove quite satisfying for those looking for a unique style military piece. The stainless steel case is coated in black via Physical Vapor Deposition, or PVD which bonds to the steel on a molecular level, meaning no chipping or flaking and high resistance to scratching (as are the crown and two activators). The mineral crystal is slightly domed and without flaws. The screw back is non-coated stainless with the SRC color logo inset at center and encapsulated in what appears to be mineral crystal. On the back is also the lightly etched Wenger logo and specs.*The face of this watch is the draw for many; a large clean, crisp dial in "nuclear green" with three sub-dials in the same hue. The watch is quite readable at most angles although the rather large arrow point hour/minute hands can obscure the sub-dials. If you want something strikingly clean and purposeful, this is it.*The luminance of the dial at night is astonishing! Every detail is visible in the dark after just a couple hours of sun. If the watch is exposed to sun (even overcast, winter skies in the Northeast US) it will be visible throughout the darkest, moonless nights. I have never owned a watch with this ability.*The rubber(*) strap is substantial and comfortable.*The 30 minute/12 hour chronograph is intuitive and accurate. The lap time feature is easy to use.CONS:You can easily buy a watch with the same quality and more functions for less money. Without the SRC branding, unique style dial and Swiss caveat this watch would be priced $100 less.*I am a fan of the accuracy of battery-quartz watches, but there is no excuse for selling one at this price point without a solar recharging system similar to Citizen's Eco-Drive. I purchased this Wenger despite the fact that one day in the near future I know it will stop working and I will have to take it to a jeweler for an expensive battery replacement/resealing. The Japanese have figured out how to do this, why haven't the Swiss?*Lacking a screw down crown and only certified to 10atm is a bit lackluster for a $220+ watch branded to a rigorous military competition. I would be highly dubious of jumping into a lake or snorkeling with a watch lacking a screw-down crown. I own two Citizens (one titanium) rated to 20atm with the same features plus solar and screw crowns costing $100 less. Once again, the Swiss need to catch up.*The crystal is neither sapphire nor non-reflective, add to that its slight dome and I wonder how long before an unsightly scratch? A rugged military time piece of this price should have a sapphire crystal.*While the rubber(*) band is comfortable and thick, it's also quite gummy. Time will tell how durable it is but it seems as though if pulled too hard over time it might harden and separate. Once again I feel a military branded piece such as this should have been given a more durable band.SUM UP:While this Wenger is a quality watch and has some collector appeal, its main selling point is appearance, not function or economy. There are dozens of watches which perform the same functions with similar or better quality at a much lower cost. But if you're a sucker for a striking "nuclear green" on black watch which will perform perfectly until the battery runs out, then you'll buy one just as I have and enjoy it in the dark!(*)It is unclear whether the band material on this watch is organic rubber or silicone rubber. The Wenger site states that the band of this watch is "rubber" while using the term "silicon" for bands on other watches. This is an important distinction and one which Wenger should clear up.

This watch is all about quality at a reasonable price. There is a number of specific details about this model that might be good to know in advance:1) The longest hand is a timer hand that indicates seconds; the bottom and the left dial are for the timer as well (indicating hours and minutes respectively).2) The watch shows date, but does not indicate month or day of week. However, in most cases, having your watch show you months, days of week, moon fazes, altitudes, bearings and stock tickers is excessive, IMHO anyway.3) The watch band is not made of rubber - it is actually made of some rather heavy-duty flat-black silicone with anti-slip texture on the inside. This is perfect for the supposedly military application of the watch. Silicone is easy to clean, it lasts longer than any leather (real or otherwise), and it feels much more comfy and soft than any kind of braided nylon.4) Date can be changed separately from time by pulling out the crown one more notch.There are only a few minor cons that I want to mention:1) The crown is not a screw-in type.2) A crystal is not sapphire and it is not a sunken-in kind.

I have owned a few watches but this one keeps drawing me to wear it. The bright "nuclear" style green dial is very cool, and the lumination is good in the dark with only a short exposure to light.Pros:- Attractive, clean dial and face. Easy to read fonts, hands and dials.- Intuitive and accurate chrono operation, like a standard stopwatch.- PVD black coating is durable, and semi-matte finish.- Very avant garde style, especially in the business world. I get compliments on it all the time. Military-types love it.- Interesting heritage and tribute model. The symbol on the case back is a nice touch for collectors.- Date display without too much additional information like day of week or month.- Easy to set and maintain. Crown increments are easy to hit for setting.Cons:- Price. As others have indicated, this is a *bit* much for a quartz movement, mineral crystal and non-screw crown. If you can find one for a good price, its good quality though, and worth it.- Mineral domed crystal. Sapphire would have made much more sense as this is a "ruggid" model. The mineral domed crystal also distorts the view at an angle, and produces pretty bad reflection.- Silicon/rubber band. reviewText: I've had this watch for at least six years, and a few years back, the analog hands stopped working but the digital display still worked. I thought it was junk, and I tossed it in a desk drawer. I pulled it out tonight, and the digital was dead too. I opened it up to see if replacing the battery would get it all running again. After removing the 2025 battery, I noticed that there was something else underneath it. Under a little round padded sticker, there was another battery, a 364 1.55 v. After removing the padded sticker, i found that the straight screw attached to the hold-down bar was too tiny of a slot for any of my screwdrivers, so I just rotated it around clockwise and under the top plate. Dropped the old battery (it was tight), and I replaced the battery with a new 364. the analog hands started moving again. I simply used a sewing needle to get behind the bar to the left of the screw and rotated the bar back around and over the battery, and I replaced the padded sticker. Installed a new 2025 battery over top of the other battery and replaced that hold-down bar, then the sticker over it. Replaced the cover with the four Phillips screws, and it was good to go once again. It's a good heavy watch that works very well, but you need to know that it's not junk just because the analog hands stop moving.

Two weeks after receiving this watch the analog hands stopped working. Before buying this watch check out the many unfavorable reviews at the 5.11 web site. If you really want a tactical analog-digital, check out the G-shocks. Much better made.

The main attraction of this watch is that it provides ballistic calculations for precision shooting with a rifle.I've found it to be quite useful for making bullet drop and windage corrections.  The software seems to be comparable to other ballistics software I've used, as the resulting corrections appear consistent with results from other ballistics software programs.I have two complaints:  One is that the analog watch hands tend to obscure the digital read out.  When inputting and reading ballistic data, the hands often get in the way.  I solve this problem by simply putting the hands in "set" mode, shutting down the hand movement, and leaving them at 3 and 9 o-clock positions, so they are out of the way.  When I'm done shooting, I reset the hands using the digital time read out (the 2nd time zone reading.)  Only problem with this is that the watch is not waterproof when in set mode (because the crown is unscrewed.)The other complaint is smaller, and that is that the input options for the balistics data is not as precise as it could be.  Temperatures are entered in 10 degree increments, altitude in 100 foot increments, etc.  It probably doesn't make that much of a difference, as my inability to shoot straight introduces a greater level of error into the system than does the rounding effect of the input data, but still, it would be nice to have more precise increments of data.Haven't had the watch long enough to comment on long term durability, but it's held up fine so far.

I don't log a lot of miles running so they suit me just fine.  I own a Cleaning Service and wear them the remainder of the time...So yes, I practically live in these most of the year.Comfort:Like I said, I spend most of my time in them.Durability:No more or no less than any other athletic shoe - average.  Like all sneakers, I tend to step into them without untying the laces, often crushing the back heel.  This results in the internal structure breaking in short order,  creating "sharp" plastic poking into your ankle.  If your like me and can't be bother untying the laces, take time to use your fingers as a "shoe-horn" to avoid crushing the back of the shoe.  If you do this, they'll last until the tread falls off.Value:As good as it gets.  Sure I've owned eighty plus dollar athletic shoes, some being more durable with possibly slightly more comfortable and greater support, but....It reminds me of a story.  I was talking to a wine connoisseur about his experience drinking that $100 plus dollar bottle of wine, "Yes it was fantastic, but it wasn't eighty dollars better than the twenty dollar variety.

reviewText: I bought this band for my Citizen dive watch. At work I need to write and type on a computer - who doesn't? So the bulky rubber strap that came with the Citizen had to go.I have not yet had The Band on for an hour and already I can tell this was a good purchase. Some initial observations:1. "The Band" is thin enough to write and type with comfortably. Good for us Jacques Cousteau IT types.2. Unlike some Velcro watch band designs, "The Band" does not use a ring to pull the band back towards you. You simply wrap "The Band" twice around your wrist.3. As others have said, learning how to wrap "The Band" on is a little tricky. If you have ever wrapped an Ace bandage around your wrist, the procedure is very similar to that. You know how hard it can be to get that initial snug wrap? Same thing with "The Band". I can see how the process will be frustrating in the morning when I am in a hurry. Oh well...score one for the ring style bands that go on very quickly.4. The instructions say to slide your watch to the end of the narrow strap until your watch is up against the wide part of the band. I found this put a lot of stress on the watch spring bar and was uncomfortable to wear. Sliding the watch back so there was about a 1/2" of narrow band between my watch and the wide part of the band fixed the problem. The above will not really make sense until you wrap "The Band" on with your watch and see how it feels. Expect to do some adjusting until everything is comfortable based upon your wrist and watch style.5. For a large dive or tachy-whatever watch, the wide band makes a nice stable "platform."6. As others have mentioned, this is a casual watch band. Depending upon your line of work, it may not be suitable. This is not a criticism just an observation. A Patek Phillippe would not be suitable on the beach where "The Band" would be.Overall I am pleased with the purchase. It will just take some time to learning how to put "The Band" on my wrist.
summary: Wear a dive watch, need to type and write? This band works.

Now to put it on you just put the end of the band (the one you cut) right up to the end of the other side and its a perfect fit every time.

These rash guards DO run small, and are a bit short as far as arm and torso length (I'm 5'4", and about 128 pounds and the arm length isn't long enough for me) but the snug fit IS great if you are a competitive swimmer who needs a rash guard with NO drag and doesn't chafe in the process. These particular rash guards are really designed to be form-fitting to create less drag in the water for swimmers and athletes. They DO make rash guards with a lot more "room", and the way to tell is by looking at the product picture. If it hugs the torso in the product picture, it's designed to be skin tight like a bathing suit, not like a shirt. I hope that makes sense.I get a size SMALL in these (usually wear an 8-12 in clothes) and it fits just about right for me. It's comfortable, but tight enough that it creates very little drag when I swim. I swim in the hot Florida sun, two miles a day, 365 days a year, so I desperately needed something to help keep the sun off my skin.Because of the short arms and the fact that the rash guard will sometimes not cover the small of my back, I tried other brands (Dakine was the latest) to get a little more coverage. It was a mistake- I got horrible burns and irritations at the seams. Body Glove's products are built really well in that regard- even though I wear my rash guard skin tight, the seams NEVER irritate my skin.I'm not a total believer that the rash guard presents as much UV protection as it claims- I still get a pretty good tan when I wear mine every single day. But I think anything is a help.It's also nice and light, very easy to wash/rinse by hand and drip dry, and easy to tote around and pack. It's a nice soft material.It's not the best rash guard I've ever worn (I had one from Rip Curl that was a better fit, better at UV, but I can't find that particular model anymore :() but it's very high up there. I recommend it for swimmers needing some extra UV protection without chafing and drag.

Finally got a chance to try this poncho a couple weekends ago on a day hike.  It started raining, and I pulled this poncho out quick and slipped it on over myself and my pack.  Plenty of room! I was covered from head to just above my knees, and the expanded backside hangs just a bit lower but not in my way where I would trip on it.One recommendation though... before you take this poncho into the field, open it at home first and "prepare" it.  The plastic material may not be fully "cured" yet, so it tends to stick to itself from the factory.  Extra drying time before balling it up and putting it in its compression sack would probably cure that, but we as consumers can't control it.  So, take this poncho out at home and go through it carefully to fully separate it apart where it has stuck together.  It won't tear (don't be rough with it, of course) but still take your time.  I guarantee you don't want to break this out in the field without doing this step first, or you'll spend 2 minutes trying to get it on right.  Once it's prepped, it will slip on in seconds and not re-stick to itself.Folds up and then rolls up to easily fit back in the included compression sack.  Best piece of lightweight rain gear I own, and if there's even a chance of rain on a backpack trip, this comes with me.Not recommended to leave in a car or hot environment during the summer.  The material is relatively thin and I would expect that it would age after a couple years of heat exposure.  Keep it in a climate controlled environment when not needed, and get years of use out of this poncho.  A tad bit pricey for just a poncho, but the design is worth it to me.

I was very pleased with the results I got from this chronograph. I took it out into the woods and set it up. It was a moderately sunny day, and there were tree limbs overhead, but using the provided sunshades it gave me consistent results for loads out of my Marlin 1894 in .357 Magnum from about 15 feet away. They were also pretty much in-line with what my reloading manual said they should be, so I am pretty confident in the accuracy of the readings as well.I then switched to the same loads out of my 2-inch snubby revolver, and got errors from the first two shots...not too surprising to me considering the muzzle blast out of the snubby is pretty ridiculous. I backed up a few feet and it began registering the shots successfully. Then I let one of my rounds stray a bit to the left and hit one of the rods for the sunshade support. The sunshade went flying, but was unbroken. The rod was bent into a "u", but I straightened it out in my vise when I got home, and it's (almost) as good as new. I know there have been some complaints on here about the flimsiness of the sunshade, but you will be happy for that if you hit it...it keeps stuff from getting broken.Overall, I'm very pleased with this product. I did a significant amount of research before purchasing, because I'd read a lot of frustrated comments regarding chronographs in general. I didn't want to go cheap and get junk, but I didn't want to spend a bunch of money for something that didn't work any better than the cheaper option, either. I was very pleased with the results that I got from the chrony, especially considering that is is pretty much the cheapest option out there. When I did my part and put the rounds where they were supposed to go, it delivered accurate, consistent results. Great product...just don't expect it to be bulletproof :-).

I have used this product for 4 years now and love it.  If you reload then you really need to have a chronograph, their are so many variables involved including things like chamber dimensions that vary from gun to gun so the load manuals aren't always accurate.  The F-1 has proven to be accurate and durable (I clipped it with a 223 bullet once that peeled back the metal housing a bit and it still works perfectly) especially for the price.  I would recommend setting it up on a cheap tripod so you can easily adjust it to the best height and this will make it very easy to level it on rocky or unlevel terrain.  One thing I will mention to the folks who get a lot of errors with this unit, make sure to read the manual, sometimes you want the shade screens up, sometimes you dont.  Also you will sometimes get errors when shooting subsonic bullets up close to the unit as the muzzle blast will get to the unit sooner or soon after the bullet does.  Also take your time setting it up at the distance recommended in the directions and shoot thru it level and 4 inches above the sensor.  Keep in mind at close range to account for the sight being X inches above the barrel!

reviewText: :EDIT: I've owned the chrony for about three months now and decided to come back and upgrade my rating.The chrony still has issues that should be worked out, but I've learned how to operate it more reliably, which obviously makes it more enjoyable to use.I use it almost exclusively indoors and refused to buy a $60+ light kit for it. I've found that any normal table lamp, with a 100w incandescent bulb will work fine, as long as you place it next to the Chrony, between the two diffusers. Take the lamp's shade off, too. After I figured that out, almost every single shot is recorded.Also, using a rifle rest is almost necessary. The chrony requires such an exact window for your shot, that taking the time to pause and aim is a pain in the butt. Set it in a rest, aim once and pull the trigger.I have also masking taped the rods together from their 8 individual pieces to the 4 connected pieces to hold the diffusers. I've also taped the diffusers together (just at the edges, though). Now that there are less parts falling all over the place, it's easier to handle, albeit it takes up a slightly larger footprint.My other gripes, listed below, are still issues for me and should be considered as such.The last line of my original review states $90 ($95) is too much for this. That is still very true. This should be a $40 device, especially with its flaws.:END EDIT:I've wanted a chrony for quite a while and finally bit the bullet, no pun intended.At its current cost, I am very disappointed.My gripes. Which is all they are.... YMMV:The device is way too finicky to casual use. It seems like you need a very exact environment for this to reliably register your shots. I shoot pellet guns, primarily pump or spring rifles. Having your shots wasted because of not-quite-perfect lighting or missing the edge of the electric eye by an inch is frustrating. A wider window of operation would be nice. By that, I mean instead of an approximate 4" x 4" area where the chrony will register your shot, something like 10" x 10" would be more suitable. I don't want to have to set up lab conditions just to use this.Lighting conditions need to be perfect, apparently, for this to work. Inside, I shouldn't have to buy a separate light kit to use it. Outside, I shouldn't have to fiddle with the plastic diffuser. Which is a gripe in itself.The metal dowel rods and the three piece (x2 for a total of six pieces) diffuser kit is a total pain in the butt. It breaks down for tight storage, but they don't stay together when you want them to. With that, if you're going to have the pieces break down into smaller pieces, have them fit inside the chrony for storage. They don't, so I have to have a larger box just to store all the pieces in.When closing the unit, one of the wires is always in the way of getting pinched. From the factory, this should be at least taped down.An automatic shutoff after x minutes would be very, very nice. No more wasted batteries.The owner's manual leaves much to be desired. Especially what the ERR1 and ERR2 actually mean.For $90+, I want the above gripes fixed. For $40, I could maybe settle with these gripes.

reviewText: Shooting Chrony's are some of the most accurate and best chronographs you can buy.  And they're reasonably priced too.  You need to have a good view of the sky, or use the diffusers with plenty of light, but if you're shooting outside or in a well lit room that should be pretty easy to do.  I use this one primarily for paintball use, and like it better than the yellow handheld model available, and the radar model too.  The best feature for paintball is that you can just shoot, wait a second, and shoot again.  The F-1 remembers how many shots you've taken and displays the velocity from the last shot.  No need to physically reset the chrony for each shot.

This has worked great for helping me adjust my loads for .38 special, 9mm and 7mm-08. The readings are very reproducible and easy to read at 10' off the display. The only issue I have had so far is with plated ammo on a sunny day. Even with the diffusers, the lead was fine but the Berry's needs a Sharpie line to pick up.

I have tried this in lots of variable lighting, with and without the white pieces.  When the sun was angled or there are windy branches overhead I tried shading with cardboard, led lighting, etc.  Sometimes it reads where it seems like it should (2400-2600) and is very consistent shot to shot but then I'll get readings in the 900's, then 4000, etc.  All over the place.  This weekend it would give what looked like half velocities, 1100s nonstop then suddenly a 2300.  Lots of different ERR displays.  Also if anyone is shooting a rifle nearby it picks up their blast (more than 10-15' in front and 8+ feet to the side) and errors out every time so I'm always trying to get the shot off before them or I have to go forward of the line to power cycle.  Lots of wasted time and I have very little data, maybe 20% of my shots have numbers I might trust but how can I know?  I actually put it under the target at 100 yds, clear blue sky with no covers and read it with a spotting scope, that worked better than anything else but you have to shoot at the target that's directly over it then move it every time you shoot somewhere else on the paper.
