So far, I have used this for my Airguns, and have yet to use it for any of my other firearms.  For Airguns, I have used it for .177, .20 and .22 calibers - from rifles to pistols.  I have used it for my Weihrauch HW80 & HW95L, Gamo Sporter rifles, and for my Baikal IZH46m, Webley Alecto .177, Beeman P1 .177, Crosman 2240, Crosman 2300t, Smith and Wesson .357 Replica Airgun - and in all cases, this registered consistently and accurately.All of the measurements I logged for each gun, then took the guns to my local Airgun dealer, and they allowed me to do a verification test on their Chronograph.  In all cases, the readings I got on average on this unit were with plus or minus 5 ft per second by comparison - which is well within the margin one could expect due to all the variables.There are some things about this unit they could improve - for example the "face plate" with the Chrony name is a foil like substance stuck on the front of the unit with poor adhesive, and you could peel it off if you  wanted.  I keep catching the corner and it will probably start to peel.  Would have been nicer if they painted it or used better adhesive.  This is not a big deal, and by itself would NOT warrant knocking off any stars on the rating.Second, the white diffuser panels that you attach to the rods are cheaply manufactured, and assembling / mounting them is a little dicey as a result.  They are supposed to "snap" together in two spots, but due to the poor tolerances the snaps don't hold and the fall apart.  When you get tension on them and bend them onto the rods, the tension / bend holds them together, but I still find myself using a little masking tape when I snap them together to hold them.  Another problem is around the snap posts, I can already see cracks forming in the cheap plastic resultant from the tension needed to repeatedly bend them.  Simply put, these plastic diffuser panels will not last long term without becoming brittle and / or cracking over time.  In my opinion!Bottom line - The diffuser panels could use some re-engineering to make them out of better plastic, and so they snap together better - other than that, the unit works!  Four stars, one star knocked off for the panels and sticker.  I will probably feel a little less satisfied if I am sitting here in two years with broken or unusable panels - but lets see how they hold up.  I may do an update at a later time.

I bought this watch to replace a 16-year old ironman triathlon which kept time very precisely, had a remarkably long battery life, and survived thick and thin.  I dropped it countless times, and even put it through the laundry once when I forgot it in my pocket.  It kept working, even though one of the screws securing the back plate was missing!  The last time I dropped it the battery was dislodged.  Once I slid the battery back it started working again, but I seemed to have erred in the reassembly because the two front buttons don't work now, which means I can't *set* the watch without disassembling it.  It probably would have lasted another 16 years if I hadn't been more careful while trying to service it.I am hoping the new watch will last at least as long as the old one.== PROS ==1. One difference between this and the old watch that I really like is that setting the watch is much easier, as noted by other reviewers.  When setting the watch, additional display elements appear which literally guide you through the process.  Also the ability to go backwards is especially nice, although I recall my older one let me set the tens digit and the ones digit of the minutes separately, which IMO is at least as good.2. You can set two different times on this watch and switch between them.  The maker calls this a 'second time zone,' although in truth you can set a completely different date as well, which in my case turns out to be very useful.3. The display is very legible.  The LCD contrast is noticeably higher than on my old watch.== INTERESTING ==1. The indiglo feature, when viewed in low-light conditions, is light-on-black.  It may be slightly more legible in the dark than the old watch, but in normal lighting it makes the display more difficult to read.2. The indiglo lights up automatically when the alarm sounds, making it possible to read the display in the dark without even pushing a button (apparently timex engineers think people use the watch as an alarm clock, see more below), but as already noted more difficult to read in normal light.3. There are weekday only/weekend only alarm options.4. You can choose between MM-DD and DD.MM displays5. The loose end of the strap clicks in very securely to the sliding loop.  It's very snug and getting it in is a little more work than I'm used to, but it's nice to know that it won't be slipping around, which is a problem I've had with other watch bands.  (I replaced the band for a different reason, noted below.)== CONS ==1. Size.  This watch is a monster compared to my old one, and I hesitated before ordering it on account of the size.  It is at least 30% wider, almost twice as thick, and quite a bit heavier!  I don't understand why anyone would want a watch so large and heavy.2. The band is molded into a form which curves down around the top of the wrist, so it isn't possible to take the watch off and lay it down flat on a table.  That's a common use case for me.  Fortunately, I was able to have a different band put on it.3. Start/stop are two different buttons.  This makes using the timer and chronograph features more awkward with this watch than the old one, and I end up fumbling to find the right button to stop it.  Not useful at all for timing very short intervals.4. Automatic 'snooze' alarm.  If you don't push a button to stop the alarm *while it is beeping*, it will beep again after five minutes.  If you let the watch beep for the full 20 seconds, then the only way to prevent it from beeping again is to turn off the alarm.  I consider this an annoyance.  I don't always have a hand free to push a button on the watch, and I don't appreciate the fact that it's going to beep again.  Snooze might make sense on an alarm clock, but IMO not on a wrist watch.5. It's difficult to turn the 'chime' feature on/off.  Apparently this can only be done while going through the sequence of actually setting the time.  On the old watch, turning the chime and the alarm off and on was done with a single button while in 'alarm' mode.6. The old watch would show the current time in the top half of the display while setting the alarm.  This was a particularly handy feature which always impressed me.  The new watch doesn't do that.7. When setting the time, timer, and alarm, there is a noticeable delay during which the next, done, +, - indicators flash but it is not possible to actually do anything.  I find this somewhat annoying.To sum, I'm glad the ironman triathalon watches are still around.  I'm happy with this watch.  Nonetheless, I liked the older model better.  IMO this is another example of the adage 'newer is not necessarily better.'
summary: Nice watch but my old ironman was better

reviewText: This is the third running watch I've had and it's my first Timex.  I've owned to Casio's before (one being a g-shock), but after finding my g-shock to bulky and cluttered, and loosing my other Casio I picked up from Walmart, I decided to look around to find a new durable running watch.I run cross country and track so going from a generic stopwatch to a 30-lap chrono watch has been sweet.  The lap timer is easy to use and the display is big enough to take a glance and see my split and total time side by side.  The recall feature works perfectly and you even have some room to adjust the settings to configure your lap display how you like it.My favorite thing about this Timex, is its ease of use.  The only time I've had to look at a manual is when I first got the watch.  The display updates as you go through the various modes to show you what the new buttons mean so there is never a question on how to set the time or recall your laps.This watch is extremely  durable.  It has already taken a few shots and I've swam with it on several times.  The screen and body have held up nicely and I don't foresee any problems with them in the future.  The strap is great also.  I really like the notch that keeps the excess strap in place.The countdown timer and the alarm both work as expected.  The timer has some different settings and is easy to set up.  My only disappointment with the timer was that you can't set different intervals.  Like if you want to run for five minutes and walk for two your going to have to invest a little more for a watch that allows different intervals.  The alarm works well too, and the beeping successfully wakes me up in the morning, but I'm not a heavy sleeper so some may find it too quiet.Overall this watch is durable, easy to use, and can track splits really well.  The watch is a little bulky if you are used to a more minimalist watch but for me the weight was perfect, and for the price you can't go wrong with this watch.

I've been a G-Shock fan for a while, but after buying this watch, I am seriously rethinking my loyalties. For the same price or cheaper than an entry-level G-Shock, the Ironman Shock gets you the same basic functionality (stopwatch, countdown timer, light, alarms, 200m WR) and then some (30-lap memory, improved band design, superior legibility, user-friendly guided settings).Let's break those improvements down a bit:-The Ironman Shock has a 30-lap memory with its stopwatch, so you can time and review your laps or intervals rather than just your whole run/swim/bike. Want to know if you took that hill faster than you usually do? The Ironman Shock will tell you, a standard G-Shock will not.-The band includes a notch for the keeper to rest in, so the keeper will not slide around but will do its job and hold the extra strap in place.-Unlike G-Shocks, there is no excess visual flair (like redundant seconds counters) taking up space on the dial. The digits are large and legible, easy to read at a glance or from an angle.-With a G-Shock, you either have to constantly refer to the user manual, use trial and error, or simply memorize the correct buttons to push in order to change the settings. The Ironman Shock guides you through any settings changes with blinking "next," "done," "+" and "-" markers to indicate which buttons you should push to do what. No more guesswork!In addition, the Ironman Shock is a more convenient size than most G-Shocks. It's comparable in size to the DW5600 and significantly smaller than most of the other G-Shock models so you can actually wear it with long sleeves or a coat in winter.No, the watch isn't solar-powered. It won't do your homework for you, either, even if you ask it very politely. But it's the best bang-for-your-buck sport watch out there. Casio would do well to learn from the user-friendly features that this watch packs, or the G-Shock may soon find itself dethroned.P.S. I got my Ironman Shock for $35 from Wally World. Good luck finding a G-Shock that cheap.

It keeps accurate time, is equipped with a dual-time feature, has a chronograph, countdown timer, and an alarm function. My everyday watch had been a Luminox, but the timing features this watch offers,  coupled with its "big, but not too big" size have moved this watch to the top of the rotation. The EL function at night is nice as well, lighting the numbers on the watch face rather than the entire background. It doesn't have the additional unnecessary  timing features that some Casio watches have (my opinion), so if you want a comfortable watch that has all the essential timing features in a sturdy package, at a fraction of the cost of its competitors, look no further.

reviewText: This watch replaced my previous Timex Ironman, which had lasted me *almost 20 years*. This "classic" model is almost identical to the one I had, except now (most excellently) comes in a blacked-out styling. (The only thing wrong with my old watch was the Indiglo nightlight feature finally died.)This is my everyday watch. It's resilient. The new shock resistance feature is something I had been looking at in more expensive watches, but is frankly a pure bonus in this instance.Be aware this watch is not: a dive watch, a fancy chronograph, even that pretty compared to other options. If you need that stuff, your price point lies upwards.For the money, this watch is very, very good.

First, a bit of background info.About 5 years ago, I went through a major watch phase, trying everything from Seiko 5's to Omega Seamasters.  I was 100% focused in on automatics.  Then, I happened across a photo of a Citizen Eco-Drive diver (Citizen Men's BN0000-04H Eco-Drive Professional Diver Black Rubber Strap Watch) on a Hirsch Carbon strap that I really liked.  It was a bit odd getting used to the idea of a quartz watch, even though it was solar powered, but I decided to buy the watch, and that cured my watch lust.  It has been my only watch for 5 years now (and I HIGHLY recommend it if you are looking for an accurate, mid-sized analog diver).Fast forward to now.  I find myself regularly traveling outside the US to places without cell service or electricity.  This has made me want a watch with two time zones and need one with an alarm.  Of course, this meant a digital watch.  After I got over my initial revulsion (remember, a quartz watch was a big step for me!), I started looking at digital watches, primarily G-Shocks.The problem I found was that they were generally quite large, to the point of just being rediculous looking on my smaller wrist.  They had overly busy dials and they often times didn't have the functions I wanted, especially on the low end of the price scale.Again, I happened across a photo of this Timex Shock watch on a forum, and promptly went to Wal-Mart to check it out.  I was immediately blown away by the incredibly legible dial, ease of setting ability and how easy it was to switch between timezones. Then I noticed how low the price was!Timex seems to have succeeded in taking most of the best G-Shock qualities, at least the ones I wanted, and tweaking the things that I found to be lacking.  They did this while keeping it under the price point of the lowest priced G I found (the iconic 5600Casio Men's DW5600E-1V G-Shock Classic Digital Watch).So in summary, here are the pros and cons as I see them:Pros:1) Incredibly legible display - Large digits, good contrast and great viewing angles.2) Indiglo -  The reverse indiglo feature, where just the digits are lit, is brilliant.  Helps preserve night vision.3) Night mode - Helpful when adjusting settings in the dark. I like that it turns off after 8 hours.4) Ease of Setting - With the "Next," "Done," "+," and "-" prompts when setting, there is no need for a manual.5) Band - The resin used feels of a higher quality than most Timex's, similar to a G in my opinion.  The strap keeper desing is very well thought out, and so far seems to work as designed.  The buckle seems of a higher quality than the similarly proced G-Shocks.6) Size - While bigger than your averaged size watch, I don't feel like I'm wearing a hockey puckon my wrist with this (but see cons below).7) Ease of Use - The buttons are big and easy to press.  They are still shrouded, though, so they are protected from knocks and accidental presses.8) Alarm - Seems loud enough (but see cons below).  I like the "snooze" feature.  If you don't press a button during the 20 seconds it is going off, it will automatically go off again in 5 minutes.Cons:1) Size - While the diameter is quite nice, especially when compared with a G-Shock, it is still a pretty tall watch.  Its not a deal-breaker for me, but something to be aware of.2) Alarm - It wakes me up, but may be too quite for some. I have little experience with digital watches, other than playing with them in a store, so I have little to compare to.  It may be normal, or even louder than others.3) Ruggedness - I think any quartz watch is an order of magnitude more shock resistant thatn any mechanical, and likely far more tough than anyone would need (unless you are a soldier, perhaps), so I think this watch is even more than tough enough for rough duty.  That being said, I think the G-Shocks are a little more robust feeling. This really isn't a con, but thought it may be helpful for someone.4) Fake Hex Bolts - Now, this is just being nit-picky, but I just don't care for the fake plastic hex-bolt styling.  Either make them real bolts, or make it smooth to get rid of some visual clutter (I am a big fan of visual simplicity, especially in a watch).I think Timex has really nailed this in terms of value.  The feature vs. price ratio this watch provides is hard to beat, IMO. You really can't go wrong!Update: 5/30/13.Well, one year later and the watch is still going strong.  It seems to lose about 2-3 seconds a month, which isn't bad.  It has also held up to daily wear, including some abuse, with only one small issue.  Last week, I noticed that the lower right fake hex bolt had broken off.  I must've hit the watch on something, but don't remember specifically what would have caused it.  I have hit the watch against many things for the year I've been wearing it, so it takes awhile to break one off.  It doesn't seem to affect the watch, it is still seems water resistant, and nothing is loose.  As I suspected it is just a stylistic choice.I still recommend this watch, as it is still one of the best, easiest to read digital displays available in this price category. Other than this issue, it is still ticking along just fine.  I will however lower my review to 4 stars to reflect the hex bolt durability concern.

After about two years, the watch still looks good. This watch is tough! I don't know what kind of plastic is used on the face, but it doesn't have a scratch on it. But it is much more legible then a g, and I can count my laps with it in the pool.  I got it from Wally World for $35. I've always been a fan of Timex's user-friendly interface, durability, functionality and ease of use. This product adds great looks to these already awesome traits that I love about Timex watches. I already tried a G-Shock watch but I have to say that you really need to read the manuals for you to use it and the buttons are a bit hard to press. This watch on the other hand is so intuitive to use. I'm very happy with this purchase that I made :)
summary: Great looks, awesome functionalities and user-friendly interface combined!

reviewText: Love this watch, despite it being relatively cheap. It doesn't feel cheap and works as I need it. Has both 12 and 24 hour settings and a good alarm if you're into that.

The good:This is not as big of a watch as you might think from looking at the picture. I like that.The LCD is clear with excellent contrast, and has a wide viewing angle. The viewing angle is the reason I was looking to replace my Armitron, which had a narrow viewing angle LCD that required aligning the wrist each time.The display prompts you when you are in the settings mode. This is my first Ironman but I had no trouble setting everything without looking at the instructions. Another bonus is you can set up / down if you miss your mark. Intuitive and well designed!The band is comfortable. In fact the whole watch is comfortable. An improvement over my G-Shock where I really feel that I'm wearing it the whole time.The illumination is superb. You can set a mode by holding illumination for 4 seconds where you can illuminate it with a push of any button, for example the Start/Split on the top. Very convenient.The buttons are easily pushed on purpose and hard to push on accident due to the guards around them and the stiffness.The locking band keeper is an excellent feature that I didn't have any trouble working with as some people have reported here.Stronger mineral glass lens vs acrylic for almost all the other Ironman series.200M water resist vs 100M for almost all the other Ironman series.The beeper is loud enough without being annoying.The bad: Viewing angle! Woe is me, I have purchased yet another watch with a viewing angle problem... the main reason I was shopping for a replacement for my Armitron. While the display is legible at all angles, it can't be seen without turning the wrist due to the high wall where the Start/Split button is and the deep recessing of the display within the face. This is not readily apparent looking at the marketing photos. So disappointing. But its such a stellar watch in every other respect, and the Armitron is really showing its age, so I will keep this. If this watch ever dies, I will try another Ironman but from the models with an acrylic lens that have a lower height. Maybe you will prefer the deep set aesthetic, I don't. Its probably due to the 200M depth and the mineral lens. I really don't need a watch with that level of protection; I would trade it for a wider viewing angle.To summarize the watch is remarkably comfortable and just exudes quality. Almost perfect.
Good watch, its held up to alot of abuse, still works well, looks ok. I would buy the watch again.
My husband has been trying to replace his old Ironman and finally found one that suits him.  He loves this one!
I wore the watch in a 6 foot deep swimming pool and it fogged up under the crystal.I like the style & functions but it is worthless to me if I'm not able to wear it in the water.

This is a great watch and it looks BOSS! I have had it for a little over two months, wear it all the time, and and there have been no problems. I decided on this one because the face of the watch is all one color, except for the grey buttons. On a lot of the other models the face would have two colors and the band would match one of those colors, but I thought those looked kind of awkward so I got this all black one.

When I ordered this watch I was worried that it was going to look like a wall clock on my arm(BIG!!!). I was pleasantly surprised when I tried it on for the first time, it was a perfect fit. With my new watch on I feel like IronMan! Awesome watch and great value
This watch is a great product for a child - adult G-Shock replacement for a fraction of the price. Great Watch

reviewText: Bought this watch as the price looks attractive. It was almost half the price of a normal Casio G-shock watch. I got a big wraist so when I wear it, it kind of look small to me. But is ok. I use it to run and swim. So far still working good!!!! How will last long.

reviewText: I love it.  The only thing I would change is the strap retainer piece holds the strap a little too well (but it's a heavier duty watch, so it's just doing what it's supposed to).  I would definitely buy it again!  I've worn Ironman watches for about 15 years and probably won't ever change. I am 52 and I can read it without my glasses, also it is very easy to set and it lights up at night.
summary: Big and I can read it without glasses

reviewText: I purchased one Timex Ironman every year since the batteries go dead within 18 months. Although watch repair stores charge something around $9 dollars to change the battery, it costs additional $35 dollars to do air pressure test if the watch has been in water. It is not worth the $44 dollars so I buy a new one. With Timex warranty, you have to pay for shipping to get it to Timex then an and additional $10 for replacement which is truly worthless since I have even done that and it takes eight weeks to get the watch back, an absolute joke, eight weeks. I use digital chronograph not analog for mountain biking, surfing, hiking, etc. which needs to be simple, small and digital not analog, with all needed functions and this Timex certainly offers all without any further mambo jumbo, unwanted dials, distractions and colors. With this Timex T5K196 Ironman, I only get the dials that is required, in a bold shape without the round features and excessive visual flairs. If not all but certainly most chronographs are bulky, heavy, big, with too many colors, and worst of all with the start and stop dial on the side of the watch instead of the face of the watch which makes it difficult to use especially when mountain biking and need to start and stop the chronograph continuously. Face diameter of 43 mil is perfect. Walmart was selling for the same price without added shipping and delivered to a local FedEx Store at no extra charge with great return policy as well as $5 for two year full insurance policy.

The product itself is fine.  A throwback to the mid 1990's look for the Ironman.  I like the color of the various "buttons"-- it is more of a matte gray rather than blue.  Amazon service lately has been quite poor have been having a lot of issues with delivery.  This was no exception.  Would not ship to a PO Box with no explanation as to why.  I have much larger items (including books from Amazon) sent without problem.

Now that I've had this watch for about 4 years I appreciate it even more, because it is practically like new.What makes this so much better than many other comparable watches is that the face, buttons, and lettering are all recessed slightly.  This reduces scratches on the face, prevents the buttons from breaking off, and stops the lettering from rubbing off (which makes a watch look old).  The wristband has held up well (no cloth or velcro to fray or wear out).  Has been swimming dozens of times (including in the ocean) with no problems.  The original battery is still going strong.  I hope they leave this model on the market indefinitely so I can get the same one when the time comes.5/31/2013 Edit:Ha, must have jinxed it with my review, as the battery is going dead (acceptable) and it got steamed up inside last time I swam with it (not good!)  Still it has been a pretty good run.  Maybe I'll try a new battery with some silicone grease on the main seal and see if I can get a few more years out of it :)
The watch is great, I use it for lap swimming, and no complaints so far!Easy to set, easy to use, and looks better and smaller than the ugly G Shock.

I really liked this watch. It's no where near as bulky as a g-shock and doesn't have the pointless LCD displays. The watch itself is shock resistant. The case: not so much. The four screw looking fasteners on the face plate are just plastic push pins, and it doesn't take much to dislodge them.  Once all 4 are gone, so is the trim cover. I'm not sure its worth the hassle to return the watch to Timex for a new cover and pins.  I may buy another one or look at a Casio 5600 variant.  I've had it approximately 3 years and would have given it 5 stars if it held together (the first pin fell out and was lost 3 months after I purchased the watch).
I have been using Timex Ironman since many many years, definitely is an excellent watch.It is light, and easy to use.I recommend it.

Wore a Timex Ironman Triathlon Solar (which also included hands) for years. Hands stopped working, but all digital functions still working on the Solar. Decided to give the Ironman Triathlon (T5K196) a chance. Thus far am quite pleased with the T5K196. Easy transition because the digital functions remain unchanged, so no learning curve. Background is lighter and easier to read. Numbers are slightly larger and easier to read. Don't accidentally bump the "Start/Split" button as easily as on the Solar model. Slight modification to the end of the strap/retaining loop makes the retaining loop more effective and easier to adjust and stay in place. Because the T5K196 does not have the "hands" of the Solar model, the overall size of the T5K196 is smaller and more comfortable to wear. Very comfortable to wear while exercising.
Easy to read,accurate,comfortable and durable. I wear this watch on the job,working out and for just about anything else. It's tough to go wrong with this one.
I was very surprised when this watch just died after 1 year.  It appears the battery life was very short!

This is my second such watch.  I don't use it for diving and generally don't expose it to other "extreme" environments.  I just like the fact that it is fairly rugged.  The numbers are easy to read, but I'd be happy if they were just a bit bigger.The band on these watches seems to be fairly durable.  I wear the watch almost 24/7, and the band seemed to show no perceptible wear after a year.I can't really comment on the watch's waterproof credentials since it isn't normally exposed to moisture other than rain.The watch sits a bit higher off the wrist than some watches, but it's not really an issue to me.The buttons and functions are all very intuitive so directions are really unnecessary.Unless/until something better comes along (in the same price range), I'd replace this watch with another identical one if this one broke.
I have always worn timex time pieces, they can be relide upon. This model is my favorite I need a watch that can handle the rough evironments I work in.
Bought this for my husband to wear on vacation.  He loves it and wears it to work out as well.  Great value.

I prefer the design over G-Shock watches. Unfortunately, one of the face plate screws fell out/broke off with light use. Had to send it back to Timex for replacement (cost me shipping and the hassle). This happened to a previous Ironman several years ago as well.

I am an avid outdoorsman/triathlete and this watch is the ideal tool for my lifestyle. I have a rather small wrist at about six inches and this watch fits comfortably and securely weather I am interval training at the gym or hiking out in the woods. The illumination is a bit unique in that it primarily lights up the numbers as opposed to the background. The watch is very legible in all light conditions. Currently this watch is the best "daily beater" I have come across, especially at this price range.

Bought this watch two weeks ago, too early for "five year" review!!  That said, I've owned a lot of sports watches and this one may well have incorporated most of the features used by most of us some of the time!!!  Dual time, easily reviewed with one touch of "start" button in time mode!!!  Easy and very convenient, I keep second "zone" on UTC.  The clarity of the watch face is beyond expectations re: any digital watch I've ever seen.  Large digits, unbelievable contrast, have to see to believe, and programmable format to some extent.  Chronograph, with lap counter and review easy to function and access.  Timer easily activated and set with a touch of the "start" button in that mode.  Alarm functions CAN BE HEARD and the back light has to be seen to be appreciated!!!!  Also, it beeps and BLINKS at you when the alarm activates, if you fail to hit a button on the watch it will reactivate five minutes later .... pretty dern good and it works!!!!  I can't see the band on this one breaking any time soon .... it's comfortable but very substantial .... can be replaced!!!!!I don't get excited by much but this watch has been thought about by someone(s) who know something about what is going on technically and have obviously "been there" when it comes to using a "data watch" in the real world.24 hour format available, intuitive setting all modes, beeps on/off, daily, weekly, weekend alarms available, hourly alarms available (never used that myself)................... A LOT OF WATCH, FUNCTION AND USABILITY TO BE IN THE $40 DOLLAR RANGE!!!!!Now, will it endure ......... "time" will tell???????  If the submersion rating (200 meters) is even marginally correct if should last for years!!!!  One last thing, a friend of mine has one of these, has used it constantly for months and has yet to exhaust the battery ... he found out Super Wally World will replace the battery for $7.00 .... I checked with our Walmart and it's true!!!!!!!!I DO NOT WORK FOR AMAZON OR TIMEX!!!!! Or, for Walmart, thank Goodness!!!!  lol

I needed a new everyday/work watch.  My last watch was a regular Timex Ironman (slightly smaller than this one, but same basic features).  I was looking at switching over to a G-Shock, but I really enjoy having the larger digits on the Timex.  The menu and settings are straightforward (and the same as my last watch), but the Shock version adds that extra heft that makes this a great all-around everyday watch.

reviewText: I LOVE TIMEX WATCHS ,ALWAYS HAVE FOR A LONG TIME. THEY WORK WELL AND LAST A LONG TIME ,SO I ALWAYS GO BACK TO TIMEX.GREAT WATCH FOR WOMEN OR KIDS.

I was a timex man then i tried casio now i am back. For the money you cant beat this watch i use it as work watch holds up too.

Loud Alarms, great digital display, not super bulky (and I have small wrists). Love the countdown timer. I have tried other watches and none can compare all around to this watch.

I like this watch so much, I am currently wearing my third one. I bought my first Ironman Classic when I was in the military because of its stealthy look and Indiglo feature. Over time, this watch has proven to be a great choice. When I travel, I always use the dual time zones and the alarm function. It is also a great watch because it is compact, light, rugged, waterproof and has a resin wrist strap - so you can wash it clean with warm soapy water and keep it sanitary. (Never buy a sport watch with a fabric/Velcro strap.) It looks good with a suit or jeans and a T-shirt. Setting it is very quick and easy, and it is low-profile and doesn't snag on anything. I bought my most recent one via walmart.com on 1/10/13 for $36 and free shipping. I like how Timex updated the watch with some new features, but kept the design and basic functions the same.
summary: One of the Best Digital Watches Around

reviewText: I am delighted with these boots.Icebug Women's Speed BUGrip Hiking BootIn the middle of an unusually bad NYC winter with ice all over the place for weeks, I now can walk with confidence that I'll stay upright.  I wore them for the first time today in a Nor'Easter storm, through slush, ankle-deep puddles and snow with no problem.  I even walked on some icy patches just for the heck of it because I could - and got silly and took a photo of my feet in an icy puddle, because these boots are waterproof.  All of this shows these boots make trudging through winter weather virtually carefree. "Virtually" because it does state in the package insert that there's no guarantee against slipping.  You also need to take care when walking on smooth surfaces elsewhere, e.g, indoors.  That said, for me these boots go a big way in removing the "fear factor" in trying to get from point A to point B in hazardous winter conditions. I believe the odds are that I'll get there.  They're warm and roomy too, with enough space for all your toes AND thick socks. I also own a different brand of winter boot which has fancy Vibram soles but they're not good on ice.  I'll wear these any time there's ice in the forecast.
summary: Wish I knew about these sooner!

reviewText: I bought these boots while preparing to move from FL to AK in Jan.  They were a godsend as we got off the ferry to ice-covered streets.  They are warm, comfy and work wonders on slick surfaces.  They sound a little funny when walking indoors, but it's well worth it for the security of walking sure-footed on ice.  Sizing seems accurate, but I would go up rather than down if undecided between two sizes.  I love them!

I bought these shoes for a hiking trip. I loved them, even though I did not keep them. The Icebug is made for heavy-duty ice and snow, and has metal studs on the bottom, which would have scratched our hardwood floors. Thus, they are pretty much outdoor wear only. Given that we don't have much winter in our area, they were just overkill for my needs.Otherwise, I found them to be well-constructed, a comfortable fit, light weight for their size, and extremely well-insulated. Kind of hated to give them up! If you live in a harsh winter climate, I'd highly recommend these shoes. The style was also fairly cute for this sort of active footwear.

I had never heard of Icebug brand before googling "ice boots" in order to stay upright this past icey winter in Boston. I really wanted the commuter boots, but could not find in my size. The main difference being that the commuter boots slip on and off, while these boots lace. The studs in these boots do not retract, so although they provide excellent support on ice and snow, they are a little slippery on marble floors and brick/cobblestone sidewalks. I got used to carrying around slip on shoes for indoor use. These boots are water-proof, but don't have much insulation, so an extra pair of warm socks are needed for cold days. I was so impressed with the comfort and soles of these boots, that I'm considering buying a pair of running shoes for the winter
summary: excellent stability on ice and comfortable!

reviewText: Living in Norway I always use my Icebugs to protect myself during the winter. They keep me safe and people often ask me about what shoes I use. It is nice to be able to help people that way.

I walk about  15km a day... so I really needed something that would grip well and work on all kinds of surfaces.... Today was my first day with these boots and they performed great....they are light ,  my feet were dry and they worked on 90% of the surfaces i came in contact with...I would recommend adding a better insole if u walk as much as I do and be careful on ceramic tile.... other then that i had no problems with them at all.

I live in MN and have battled slippery conditions for a lifetime.  I bought these with the hopes of eliminating the insecurity of slips and falls when doing anything outside...even just walking across a parking lot!  I love these boots!  They are comfortable, warm, and the traction is just what I've been waiting for.  It is so nice to feel secure on ice!  I wear an 8 1/2 and purchased an 8 1/2 and they fit perfectly.  I can even get a thicker sock on if I need to.  They are also stylish.  I would definitely recommend these to anyone looking for a great outdoor boot.

Possibly the best watch ever made. Has strap, several buttons, dial with numbers on it you can change or just watch (so to speak). End of velcro strap sticks out and can get caught on things. Otherwise I would of given this one 6 out of 5.

So far, enjoy the watch plenty. My last timex broke after a bout of whitewater rafting, but so far, but I've always been an ironman customer so it was hard to break tradition. The strap is nice and easily adjustable and doesn't get too dirty or smelly even with intense exercise. Happy so far.

reviewText: I like it enough that this is the second one I've bought.  I like:  1) that you cannot not accidentally push one of the buttons (with another model of Timex Ironman I found settings and modes being changed accidentally).  2) The attachment for the band is wide enough to accommodate a 3rd party replacement band (some other models of Ironman have a very narrow band attachment that forces you to buy the expensive Timex replacement band should it break).I give it a 4 star because it could be a bit smaller.It's a $35 watch -- so don't expect it to last a lifetime!

For thirty four bux, I got myself a 200 meter waterproof, shock-proof ironman triathlon watch.  Nowhere else can you get this build quality for such a low price.  I considered getting a heart rate monitor, but decided that to use it the way you want to use it, you've got to wear the chest-strap which seems really cumbersome to me.  GPS would have been nice, but widely available internet mapping sites can help with a lot of that info if you just bother looking at it.  Overall, highly recommended.

reviewText: I enjoy the basic lap counting functionality of this watch and I use it to swim laps. Unfortunately, the initial battery that comes in the watch only lasted about 3 months of light use. This seems a little short to me. I am going to get it changed and hopefully it lasts a little longer this time.

reviewText: Feels nice and durable, have yet to really test it in a steam room or ocean, but i am sure it will stay tough

I've owned several Ironman watches over the years, in a variety of styles. Others had an alarm that was loud enough to wake me up, but the alarm on this is too soft. So I can't use this as a backup for the alarm on my cell phone.Also, the velcro strap is so long that it gets caught in various things. It should be shorter.
i bought this for my grandson who is very hard on watches.  He loves it and says that it meets his standards for being durable, reliable and fun!  I think that Timex does make a quality watch.
Given as gift since it was closest to old one he had and liked.  Haven't heard any complaints.
This was a birthday gift for my husband.  He has been very pleased with the durability, quality and performance.  I was pleased with the price!

Very nice design, i wear it almost everydays. Very good for running in my case.  Easy buttons. The only thing bad is that not works for swimming but for the price and quality is awesome. For me is very nice. Highly recommended for runners

My husband has been very partial to the Timex brand.  He really has nothing but good things to say about this particular model.  It was my Christmas gift to him.  For once, I found something for him that is practical and that he enjoys.
Timex makes a very durable watch.  I wear when working out and when working in the yard, on the house, etc.  They last for years.  Great purchase for the price!
it was easy to set and small enough to fit my nephews wrist which is good. the lining was more blue than the purple it was suppose to be but that was ok for me.
Great gift...this is a replacement of the same..........love the velcro band. It's so adjustable and exactly what the runner wants.
Still getting used to the velcro, but all is good.  Has been one of the better Timex watches I've owned.

This is the third Timex Ironman watch I've purchased from Amazon.com. The previous two models lasted about two-and-a-half years each. The first one's wristband broke and the second one just fell apart. This one's dial is much bigger than the previous two models and much easier to read. The only feature I don't use on this, or previous models, is the lap feature. The buttons, especially the "start" button on the bottom of the dial, could be a tad bigger. If this one lasts three years, at $30, it's not a bad purchase.
summary: It will probably last about three years...

reviewText: I have set the time, date and time zone numerous times.  The watch does notretain settings for more than 1 day if that long. Now it does not work and I amreluctant to replacing battery because the watch has never worked properly.I do not recommend this watch!

How can you make the Ironman better? Double the water resistance from 100M to 200M and add shock resistance.I chose this model over the other four or five shock resistant models for the wrap around velcro strap which is very comfortable and makes the unit a bit lighter than the ones with plastic straps. Best of all it was only a little more than than a regular 100M model.

Great for using as a stop-watch as well as lap watch. Durable construction and good looking.  The velcro band is comfortable and the fact that the display glass is in-set makes it hard to scratch.All around great watch for the price.
the watch has everything my husband was looking for and i got a better deal than in the local stores
summary: my husband loves it and it made it by christmas!

reviewText: I bought the watch for my son who is joining a track team.  I figured he could keep track of his splits and use it for all his running needs.  Well he actually loves it and wears it every day instead of just running.  I have owned many ironman watches myself and love them.  They are tough and dependable.

This particular model has been around for about 15 years or so, and is just as good as ever it was. The delivery was fast and accurate. Looked for this watch in brick and mortar stores and none of them had it, so the prompt delivery was great!

So far so good but don't believe the picture as posted on Amazon --- the date is reversed with this true sequence Day of Week, Date, followed by the month - somewhat like a military date except the year does not appear.  As for functionality so far so good with a great size display.  If only they had written the instruction in the same manner, otherwise break out your magnifying glass.  Like most others who have offered reviews here I do not believe you will be disappointed with this watch unless you are highly critical and in that case you probably should not buy this $39.00 watch if you expect $100.00 features. If you can afford something better go for it!
This Timex Watch is great with a great price. I love the Vel-Cro band. I run a lot so the timing function is important to me.  You will not be sorry if you purchase the Timex Ironman.

I picked this up as a replacement for my $10 WalMart chronograph that I was using to track my swimming lap times until the buttons fell off. Definitely worth the extra $30. I have a small wrist and the bezel size looks perfect on mine and the face is very readable. The case is a little thicker than my other Chronograph, but still very comfortable. The only quirk I found was the velcro strap would catch on my golf shirts. Easy fix with a small flat head screwdriver to pry the spring pin inward on both straps and swap them so the velcro now claps on the outside of my wrist.

It's rugged and dependable, I'm replacing one I wore for 2 1/2 years but misplaced while travelling. The last one I wore pretty much every day and wore it snorkelling, hiking, rapelling, in the shower, you name it and although I scratched the glass on it somewhat it still functioned perfectly.
summary: Can't beat it for the price

reviewText: I own too many Ironman watches, but you can't beat them for features, ease of operation, good looks (in my opinion) and general all-around quality. If you don't own one get one! You won't be disappointed.
summary: Typical Ironman, but with shock protection

reviewText: This is a very durable, low end watch that has worked without any problems for the past yr.  I especially like the watchband which is comforable and easily attached to your wrist.

This watch is just what I was looking for in an every day watch. I can wear it to work and then to the gym for my workout. I use it for interval training and recently kept it on when I went for a swim! Outstanding utility and value for the price. Can't go wrong with this purchase!

Bought this to replace my 10+ yr. old Timex Ironman Triathlon when the strap on the old one broke.  Like the older one, this watch is accurate, accurate, accurate.  Add the easy to use timer & stop watch features, and what can I say?  Highly recommended.

I purchased this product three times, this last being a gift.  The first one lasted ten years with only one battery replacement after six years.  I finally discarded the watch because the Velcro in the wrist band had failed.  The replacement for my originally purchased watch is still working without a hitch after about five years.  I initially bought this Timex product because I like the chronograph feature, being an avid runner and cyclist.  I keep buying this model as needed because of my experiences with Timex reliability, even after getting the watches wet occasionally in the rain or while swimming.

I used this watch for training, traveling and working. Could count laps, have an alarm on my travels and its waterproof. its an amazing watch but the only down side is its velcro strap. great watch at a good price. One of my favorite watches. I'm a watch fanatic. I would get it again.

Keeps great time, love the indiglo light, easy to read at night. The date and day are always ther, no need to press a button to find out the date. Very water resistant, I never take mine off, not even to shower, it is my constant companion.
I have been using tis style watch for several years.  I like the Velcro strap, the watch is durable, easy to use and relatively inexpensive. I received good service from Amazon.

This watch is GREAT! The velcro strap was comfortable. Picks up odor easily however (reason for 4 stars) but I liked the musk.The face is easy to read and simple. You can't beat the price. I've had it for a few weeks now and it's been working like a charm. I'm a little old school and prefer velcro straps, which seem to be harder and harder to find on good digital watches these days, so this was a great find for me.

I bought this watch to replace the one i bought for my husband years ago which is still working but was getting worn as he uses it every day. This purchase was a good replacement, it looked just like it did in the picture and my husband seem to love it.

I enjoy using this for travel and running. I wanted an inxpensive watch when I dont use my garmin watch. This fits the need and price point I was after. I have owned Timex's in the past and have had good results.
just what I ordered Lost my other watch in the atlantic ocean. Same watch as I had before. Work in the construction field (Finish Carpenter) It takes a beating and still always works.

If I had it to do again, I would spend the extra $5 and get the plastic strap.  This watch has a velcro strap.  I have a great disdain for any of that metal pinching watchband. reviewText: Perfect every day watch. Comfortable band, easy to set/use, and durable. Can't go wrong with this watch if you want something that says guy's watch.

I've owned several Timex Ironman watches over the years. I find them to be reliable and easy to use. I ordered this one with the Velcro band for running. I've owned other Ironman watches with bracelet and buckle bands. They're all good, but the Velcro band is the best for sport and activities. In my experience if you try to change the battery yourself on these watches, the buttons tend not to work afterward. I've learned that when the batteries go it's best to throw them away and buy another one. I've had them last up to eight years on the original battery though.
My son loved his new watch, he even had to get it wet to see if it was really waterproof. Great watch!

ok a little about me: i am an IT guy, not an athlete/ gymrat/ runner. But i still love this watch. i ove being on time and i am OCD about knowing the exact minutes with seconds so i can time myself. it even has a stop watch function, timer and alarm. It can save upto two different times. love the indiglo and the Velcro strap . Worth every penny cause its so freaking durable.

I bought this watch for my tall, thin teenage son and he loves it.  He is tall but has very slim arms and one of the larger, heavier men's watches would be too bulky and uncomfortable on him.  He likes all the functions and it's easy to use, even after you lose the folded instructions that come with it like you always do.  He wears it all day at school as well as for running, swimming and cycling and says the velcro strap is extremely comfortable.  He keeps thanking me for buying it for him. Priceless!

reviewText: Great watch for the value.  Meets all my requirements w/ the features I want and is very stylish.I've had the Timex Ironman style watch in the past, but they had the metal bezel.I was concerned if I would like the lightweight plastic design, but it's fine.One of the reasons I picked this particular watch is it came w/ the Velcro band.Looks great w/ the navy blue trim on the band.You won't go wrong w/ this watch as it looks and feels great.
GREAT PRODUCT FITS ALL MY NEEDS AND IS A VERY GOOD SPORTS WATCH WHICH IS VERY HELPFUL IN MY TRAINING
This is my third Ironman.  They all very accurate, durable, and inexpensive.  I have replace them because the case gets worn after 5 or more uses of hard use.
This watch is great, it works perfectly. As a Timex I would recommend it as a "all kinds of uses" watch
This is my second watch like this, its rugged,looks good water proof and the band lasts along time. Keeps good time, and numbers are big with the lighting for night makes it a Kool blue.

I first bought one of these, with the Velcro band, about 15 years ago because it was what all the other soccer refs were wearing. My last was bought about 11 years ago. The band is tattered and ratty, nothing you'd like to take in public. But the watch, itself, is STILL running and absolutely accurate. I have the latest version on my wrist as I write. It is an improvement design-wise. Its quality longevitywise requires quite a few years of use to determine.But I am impressed enough with it that I have ordered another to give to my Warrior son who is soon going to Afghanistan. He expressed an interest when I showed it to him. He surprised me as he has never worn the watch I gave him for graduation. He said he needed a good watch for where he is going. OKfine. Poor quality, I would not recommend this. I have had ironman watches before and it is obvious the quality has diminished.

Based on a coach's recommendation, I ordered this for my son who needed it for cross country training. Well worth the money and arrived quickly. He really likes the velcro band on it, and I liked the price--cheaper than buying it in a store! Does everything he needs it to do!

I had the Timex Expedition watch with a velcro strap for years that looked good and held up to all kinds of conditions before I lost it and wanted another, but they don't sell that particular model anymore so I ordered this one.  Out of the box it's anther great Timex watch for a great price.  I specifically wanted a velcro-style strap because you can always get a perfect fit with it on your wrist and it's very comfortable.  You also don't have to worry about a band loop working loose, partially undoing the band and having it annoyingly stick out.  As with my previous Timex watch, I'm not worried about the fabric band getting "funky" as it should stay pretty clean with a wash in the shower or regular soap and water once in a while.  The display is easy to read and the features are straightforward and simple to use.

I purchased this watch through Amazon and went surfing with it the next day. After catching a small wave, I felt it dangling from my arm. I strapped it on tightly and proceeded to catch a wave to the beach to take the watch off. When I caught the next wave the watch had come off my arm and I could not find it. reviewText: Great bargain for this watch. I paid less than a major discount chain was selling it for. I wear it to work and it holds up well.
summary: Great watch for the money. Very functional.

reviewText: Timex Ironman are the best watches for the price. I am glad that Timex continues to provide quality products at reasonable prices. It has all of the features that I need. I was mainly looking for a watch with a countdown timer to use while running, and this watch is exactly what I needed. It is a little bulky, but it is made to reduce shock while in a sporting event. The numbers are also easy to read while running, so I am very pleased.Also, Amazon has so many great products to choose from, it is always my first choice when shopping online, primarily because they are the least expensive.

I have not has this watch for long, but it is very easy to use and has not lost a second over these first 2 weeks.  I have not had occasion to test the "shock proof" feature or "200m" depth, but having used Timex products forever, I trust them.I especially like the velcro feature.  It does not look like a kid's watch, but the easy on-off and adjustment make it an excellent fit.

I bought this to replace an older Timex, and this has been a great purchase, especially for the price.  I'm not an active runner, but I am a coach, and I need a sports watch, and a watch to wear when just out doing stuff.  The larger numbers on the face make it very easy to read, but the dial is not oversized by any means.  It's also easier to set up than my previous Timex.  One thing to note, that is not shown in the picture, is that there is a navy blue edging around the band and face, it's not that noticeable, but it's definitely there.  I am very happy with this watch.

This watch is simple and looks good on the wrist.  One thing I didn't realize from the pictures, was there is a thin blue stripe along the edge of both sides of the band, it actually looks quite nice.  Setup is easy and its very comfortable.  This will be getting worked over in the future with military training and I will update with any issues I may come across.
I loved how fast and exceptional their service was in getting the product to me. Extremely attentive to my needs and a great product. I will definitely order from them again.

So, this watch does everything I want an inexpensive watch to do. It keeps perfect time, has a stopwatch, alarm, etc. But the most useful feature (for my uses anyway), is the repeating timer. You'd be surprised at how many smartphone timers can't do that (I'm looking at you, iOS). In addition to all the other features, I appreciate the velcro band. It's durable, easy to remove, and, most importantly, it's comfortable. I've had no problems with getting it wet or cleaning it. My last watch, (which lasted me YEARS) was very similar to this one in construction and design. The velcro lasted quite some time. (I actually bought this one because I lost my last one, not because it broke or was unwearable) Keep it clean and you shouldn't have any problems. Great product. Shipping was one day late, but I attribute that to the shipper, not amazon. 5 stars.
It is very easy to use and works perfectly. The Velcro strap is very useful and makes it easier to wear in any condition. Great quality.
Works great for everyday and occasion I need a watch for. The price could not have been better anywhere. I Highly recommend this watch to anyone.

Sometimes the velcro band will snag on things but so far that is the only drawback.  The light on it though not bright enough to do anything with other than read the watch is very effective at that.  It has been banged around for a month or so and I have had no issues with it.  I would buy another one.
Not the best band for my use, but I thought I'd try it.  Being one who never takes his watch off, the band stays wet too long.  Otherwise the best watch value year after year after year.
summary: Love the watch, should have stayed with original band

They seem to break very easily and finding replacement bands can be very difficult.  I've also found that replacement bands are almost as expensive as the watch itself.  I hope that the velcro band will prove to be more resilient, and if not then perhaps it can be replaced with a standard watch band.As with my previous timex watches, this one is working very well.  It remains to be seen how much I like the velcro strap, but so far I am quite pleased with this purchase.

I have had these watches for about 30 years. I replace them every three or four years as they age. No metal to make contact, very shock resestant, water proof and survives chemicals  as well. reviewText: Over the past 25 years I have owned three Timex Ironman watches. They have been in salt water, mud, and just about anything you can throw at them and they keep running. All of them still run. It's the bands that wear out and then I buy another one. I use the ones with broken bands as kitchen timers. Pop in a battery every few years and you're good to go for literally decades. Another plus is that the buttons work the same for all of them, so I don't have to re-learn setting the time, timer, stopwatch, etc.

Love this watch, which is a replacement for several Ironman watches that preceded it (lost my last one). The more robust waterproof rating is nice (200M), as I have used previous generations scuba diving.  For me, this is the one watch that I can use for timing virtually everything- working out, cooking in the kitchen, grilling, as an alarm clock, and even for setting alarms for siestas or time outs for my little ones. Highly recommend this watch and its feature set.  I'm also a big fan of the fast wrap bands. This model already comes with one vs. adding one as a substitute.

This is a great watch. It is a bit larger than I thought it would be but not by much. The velcro band is very comfortable and I barely notice that I am even wearing the watch. Its a simple watch without any bells and whistles. But it is very easy to program and use all of the functions. It looks classier than most Iron Man watches that I have seen or had in the past.  The Indiglo night watch is great.  The one thing I would change if I could would be the length of time that the indiglo stays lit once you press the button.  When I look at my watch in the night I can read the time in a fraction of a second, but the light stays on for a couple of seconds after the button is depressed. I dont believe there is a way to modify that.  It would be nice to have the option to have the light just come on as long as the button is pressed.  But that is a minor quibble.  Its a fantastic watch at a good price.
summary: Just what I was looking for

reviewText: Just in case you're wondering, the watch definitely doesn't float! :) Had this watch for a total of 4 days before it was stripped off my wrist while wake boarding. I'm a novice boarder, was not going fast, and didn't hit the water hard when i lost it. I was actually in the water, preparing to take off and it somehow slipped off my wrist. I thought the velcro was fastened tightly enough but guess not! I Love the watch design, size, price, functionality and even the velcro strap (despite it's vulnerability to lake water), enough so that i plan to purchase another one. Unless you can see/dive to the bottom of the body of water you're in, take it off!
summary: Great Watch but... NOT for Water Sports

reviewText: Absolutely everything I need in a watch to track time. I am a runner and needed a watch to keep splits so I could pace myself during long runs. It does everything that it says it will do. The night light function is great. Thanks for a good watch. Once again, well done Timex on the Ironman series.

Highly recommend it.

reviewText: So far (1 month) it works fine.  I'm not going to trust the "waterproof" claim since my previous Timex died after being submerged.

You can rotate the outer dial to get the other directions. It stays on for a few seconds and then goes back to your set face. (date/time) The buttons are a little too easy to accidentally press, but for the price this watch is great. Has a black silicone rubber type band which is soft and comfortable.

Other than that the INDIGLO could be a little brighter.  Resin strap is great for outdoor activities and then straight to the shower - no worries.  So far I like it and would buy it again.

It's a time-teller not a bloody status symbol.Of course the crystal has become scratched (duh!) but otherwise it takes abuse. things I like: rubber strap - comfortable, flexible, doesn't pinch. Lightweight so I forget I have it on. Has a stainless metal clasp not velcro or something that will wear out. I like Indiglo. I like the "timer" function - it will count down a number of minutes that you set between 1 and 99. Great for not forgetting to flip burgers or check on the kids. Alarms are handy too. I don't use the compass much but you never know...

I still love having a watch to check time (it's a pain to pull out your phone to look), and Timex is still my fav. Their website is poor, but they still make solid watches (the bands usually die before the watches!) I had a very solid seller, too!

Watch is a decent watch but the digital compass never works like it should, very untrustworthy.  Other than that it pretty decent. Don't like the face however that is why the lower star rating scratched too easy I though.  Should of been better for $50.  I have had mine for 3 years and the NSEW and the degree marks have warn off and the color of the plastic turn ring is gone, now just milky white.  All functions still work properly and still on original battery too!Overall a good work/outdoor watch though!

I got this watch last Christmas and, after wearing it for almost 365 day, I don't have any major complaints. The indiglo works great. The alarm is acceptable (would be nice to be able to program multiple alarms, but that's not a deal breaker for me).Overall, I would recommend this watch.UPDATE: It's been four years with this watch now. I've had to replace the band twice, which was no big deal. Other than that, it's still going strong after being worn literally every day during my very active life. I'd still recommend it for sure!

I'm a plump, classically hourglass-figured lady. I am just at the border between normal and overweight on the charts, so not radically large, but also not a skinny, athletic person.I tell you this to help explain the fit of Icebreakers products. I am a petite (short) 12/14 with full bust, small waist, full hips, and I really require an XL size in this brand. The sleeves are too long, even though they are intended to reach your hands to use the fantastic thumb-hole feature to keep the wrists warm. My Icebreaker Women's Tech Bodyfit 260 Top comes pretty low on my hips because I am short through the torso. This is fine for warmth, but not as flattering as an item of clothing could be.My kids are willing to wear their Icebreakers over bare skin, but I always try to keep an under-layer between my skin and my wool. I am very, VERY sensitive to this sort of thing. Normal people will likely find this wool smooth enough to wear as any layer--base-, mid- or top-layer. A very fine silk undershirt is enough to protect me from itch, which is certainly not true of all woollens.My top is hot pink. (It was on sale.) The fit and look is pretty sporty. When I'm cold, I really don't care, but this isn't my preferred style. Sometimes I even layer this top under a thicker wool sweater more to my sartorial tastes, and it works great as a thick turtleneck that way with the zipper pulled up.If you like wool, this is worth the splurge. If you are trying wool, try to get a piece of Icebreaker or Smartwool on sale first, to see how you feel wearing it. Personally, in spite of the itchies, I've switched over almost all of my socks to wool and am now working on mid-layer upper clothing. It really is amazing how comfortable you can be if you can avoid the itch.

reviewText: I have had this shirt in black for about 4 or 5 years now and can't say enough good things about it.It's soft and comfy, doesn't itch even when worn next to skin, is really nice and warm and it's great to have the option to unzip the neck if it's not super cold.I also really like the thumb loops which make putting layers on top of this shirt quicker and easier.
