This Tech Top turtleneck with the half-zip in black is my favorite top in the world!  Five or six years ago, I bought one in black (which was the only color option that I remember having), then I got two more in the same color when it was on sale about a year afterwards, in case they stopped making it.  They are still in good condition after a crazy number of wearings/washings.  Those tops are 5 stars, no question!I bought a new one of these tops last week (Dec 2012), expecting it to fit the same as my earlier ones, but it did not.  I ended up returning it.Firstly, the neck was way too high - it pressed up on the underside of my chin uncomfortably, it wouldn't "scrunch" casually around the neck because the material was too stiff, and it just looked silly, thick and awkward (on me, anyway) with the top half folded down on the bottom half.  I don't mind tall turtlenecks - but this was just too high.  A couple of weeks ago, I saw somewhere another recent review of this that mentioned how surprisingly tall the turtleneck part was - now that I have tried the 2012 version of this top, I know what she meant.Secondly, the sleeves were too long.  These sleeves do have thumb holes, but even so, they were lots longer than my thumbs.Thirdly, the material seemed a bit less nice than before.  This might be because I ordered a grey one this time and was comparing it to my old black ones.I would give the particular top I returned a 2-star rating, but in honor of my older Tech tops and my general appreciation of Icebreaker, I have put 3 stars here.-------Some general info on Icebreaker:Because some of Amazon's listing descriptions for Icebreaker items have very few details about the products, making it difficult for the customer to make an informed purchasing decision if he/she is unfamiliar with this brand of clothing, below I'll type some information and personal impressions about Icebreaker clothing.Note that my review is quite long and usually only the first half of it is shown on this page. If this happens on your screen and you wish to read the second half, all you have to do is press the "read more" button at the bottom of the review and Amazon will show you the rest of it.  :-)----------------------OVERALL IMPRESSIONIcebreaker's marino wool items are generally made well, last a long time, are easy to care for, feel fantastic on the skin, are "natural", don't get smelly easily like polarfleece does, let the skin breathe, etc.Many of my Icebreaker items have been worn and washed several hundred times and are still holding up much better than would be expected.I am a BIG fan of this company's products.  For my overall experience of them from around 2000-2010, I would give them a solid "5 stars"!However, I regret to say that my opinion of the items I have bought from Icebreaker in 2012 is not as high.  In the last 2 weeks (late 2012), I have bought 7 items from them and I decided to return all of them because they aren't as well-cut as the very "same" items that I bought in the 2000s (which I still have and wear, so I can make like-for-like comparisons easily).Based solely on my 2012 experience of Icebreaker products, I would give them 3 stars, "it's ok".  For me, this is not good enough to command prices of $50 - $100+ for quite simple items, even if the basic wool material itself is outstanding and long-lasting.---------------------MY EXPERIENCE WITH ICEBREAKERI bought my first Icebreaker clothing about 13 years ago when I needed some long underwear for skiing.Up until about 6 years ago, I had been buying Icebreaker items very sparingly, due to the eye-watering prices at London UK sporting goods shops .  Then, I discovered that Sierratradingpost sells various Icebreaker styles (usually discontinued items from years past) on their site for a discount. Fortunately, for a couple of years after I discovered this, they had a large selection of women's Icebreaker stuff, so I bought quite a few things for great prices. (These days, Sierra's Icebreaker selection for women appears to be smaller, and the prices comparatively higher, than before.  I expect that there are more discounters they have to compete with now, to get that kind of stock.)In addition to bricks-and-mortar sports shops and Sierratradingpost, I have also bought Icebreaker items from several sporting goods online retailers, Amazon, and the Icebreaker website.I still have almost every Icebreaker item I've bought.  Even the discounted items have been somewhat pricey, but the quality and longevity were worth the initial investment.In the last two weeks, I have tried to replace a few of my key Icebreaker items but found the fit and cut of the current versions of the same items to be sub-par.  I will keep using my old items for another year, and hope that next year's fit and cut will be better-suited to my body shape.----------------------CAVEATWhat I have written below is based on my current knowledge about their products, but it is possible that I have misunderstood some aspects of the brand.If you wish to better understand their product offerings, I would absolutely recommend that you have a look at the Icebreaker official site to view their entire range and gain more clarity about what items are for what purposes, what the wool weights are about, what the quality levels of the different clothing collections are, etc.(Unfortunately, their website, while snazzy, does not fully explain these things, leaving it up to the customer to piece some of the puzzle together.)----------------------ICEBREAKER WOOL WEIGHTS:Icebreaker's marino wool items generally come in four weights of fabric: 150, 200, 260, or 320. This is "grams per square meter".150 is quite thin.It provides light warmth.The material is generally see-through.  (I wouldn't wear items of this weight out and about in public without anything over them, but some reviewers have said that they do.)It's good for a first base layer, for strenuous exercise, or for sleeping in.Their items of this weight, especially in the ranges intended for athletic use, tend to be really form-fitting in one's typical size.All Icebreaker material seems VERY resilient and long-lasting to me, but because the 150 wool weight is pretty thin, it is the likeliest to be torn, develop holes, get "runs" (like pantyhose).  I don't think this happens too much with it, but I've seen some reviewers mention it (most often talking about how they accidentally poked holes in it with long fingernails), and three of my 150-weight leggings have developed runs in them after several years of heavy use.200 is slightly thicker, but still on the thin side.It's pretty warm.The lighter colors are definitely see-through, such as grey and cream. My older black and brown items made out of 200 weight wool don't seem to be see-through, but some of the newer dark-colored ones might be.It's good for a base layer or mid-weight layer, for exercise, and sleeping in.Especially in the ranges intended for athletic situations, their items of this weight tend to be form-fitting in one's typical size.260 is on the thicker side.It's definitely warm, a cozy weight.None of my 260 items are see-through. I can wear tops made out of this weight on their own (without anything over them) and not worry that my underwear or too many lumps&bumps; will show through.It's good for a mid-layer or top-layer, and sleeping in (if you get cold at night, like I do).Items of this weight tend to fit looser than items of the same size in the 150/200 weights do. This may have something to do with how much naturally-stretchier the thicker fabric is, but it also seems that they cut these 260-weight items bigger because this weight is often worn as a top-layer or middle-layer, instead of as a base-layer.I like this weight the best.  I think that the company says that this is their most popular weight across the board.320 is thickest, of course.It is quite warm, very toasty and sturdy.This weight is generally a top-layer, so items made out of this material are relatively loosely-cut.--------------------------ICEBREAKER LINES / RANGES / "COLLECTIONS" OF CLOTHING:Icebreaker makes different ranges - some intended for wearing as normal underwear (like panties and sports bras and tank tops), some intended for wearing as thermal/long underwear, some intended for wearing as everyday clothing, and some intended for wearing as athletic wear.Even though at first glance most of their items appear VERY similar to each other, there are different feelings to the fabrics (even in fabrics of the same wool weight), different quality levels, different cuts, and different design details amongst these different lines, so it is good to check their website about the particular Icebreaker item you are thinking of buying to make sure that it is intended for the activity you want it for.Two of the popular ranges at the lower end of the Icebreaker price scale are:BodyfitThe Bodyfit range seems to be for athletic situations, but also casual-wear and sleeping-in. The knit of this range's wool is usually flatter and less stretchy than the knit of the ranges that are for underwear or purely casual wear. Items in this range are usually cut to fit relatively snugly.EverydayThis range is made of a looser, thicker, stretchier knit than the Bodyfit, and is more for general sleeping-in and casual long-underwear needs, not so much for athletic situations. (However, I'm sure that they would be okay in many athletic situations, and I have worn them skiing and hiking.) Everyday items tend to be made of a stretchier knit and cut to fit more loosely than the Bodyfit items. I wear a size below my ordinary size in this range.Other rangesTheir other ranges appear to include: Black Sheep Collection, RealFleece Collection, Pure Plus Collection, Journeys Travel Collection, Premium Underwear Collection, GT Technical Sports Collection, GT Bike Collection, Technical Base Layers Collection, and Technical Mid Layers Collection. Please see the Icebreaker site for more information on their ranges.Frankly, I feel that they've made this aspect of their brand over-complicated and too confusing for the average customer, and I have not been able to locate any overview of the various collections on their site or on their product packaging materials.-----------------------ICEBREAKER COLORS:Icebreaker tends to make most items in black, as their basic universal color.Many items are offered in about 2 to 8 other colors, as well.  There is often some version of blue, red, grey, and green - sometimes a pink, sometimes a brown or purple, etc. Often the colors are skewed towards the cool end of the spectrum (which I notice because my coloring is on the warm end of the spectrum and cool tones look awful on me).The different weights of wool and/or different ranges (e.g., Bodyfit, Everyday, Journeys Travel Collection, etc.) will tend to have their own mini-set of color options.  (For example, the current grey color in the 200 Bodyfit is a medium-grey and is called "blizzard" and the current grey color in the 260 Bodyfit is a dark-grey and called "metro", and they don't offer those particular colors in other weights of wool or other ranges, as far as I know.)They change their colors every year or so (I think), and some colors tend to sell out mid-way through a season and are not restocked, so if you see an item in a color that you love, or there is a matching set (of long underwear or something) and you want both pieces in the same color, you probably should get it at the time, because it's not guaranteed that it will be available in the future.---------------------EXTRA DESIGN FLOURISHES:A couple of their ranges, mainly the more athletic lines, feature "pops" of contrasting color in a certain part of the garment, such as a stripe running down the sleeves or down the sides, or a triangle of bright material at the ankle. Most internet retailers' photographs of the garments do show these features because the areas of differing colors are pretty obvious, but it pays to read the item descriptions (and check out the manufacturer's site for confirmation) if this kind of thing is not what you are looking for.In a couple of their clothing ranges, mainly the underwear, 150-weight, and casual-wear lines, some of the tops and bottoms have printed patterns (like floral motifs or abstract swirls - sometimes in contrasting colors) on the sleeves or in the hip-region. This *can* escape your notice when the only images of the item you have available to you are the tiny product photographs that most internet retailers provide, so do double-check the customer reviews of the item, and maybe the Icebreaker site's own full description of the item, if you want to know for sure if the item comes with a printed pattern on a section of it.---------------------ICEBREAKER SIZING:Sizing and fit are so variable from person to person and from brand to brand, but in case it may help, I'll talk about my experiences with Icebreaker clothing.For reference, generally I am usually a women's size 4 or 6 in US sizing, a women's size 8 or 10 in UK sizing, and a small when it comes to small/medium/large sizing.  This goes for both tops and bottoms.---Sizing of TopsAlmost all of my Icebreaker tops from the last 13 years -- crew tops, long-underwear tops, turtlenecks, and zip-up jackets -- are women's size small.The only tops I have in size extra-small are from the Skin range (which they phased out in 2006, but the sizing and type of material used for the Skin range appear to be very similar to those of the current range called Everyday).Generally, I know that an Icebreaker small top is probably going to fit me.The main issue that I've had with their tops is sleeve length (too long).  This is not uncommon for me, because I do have arms that are on the petite side:  most suit jackets I buy have to be shortened a little in the sleeves, and I often have to turn up sweaters one turn at the cuff.  And one feature of some Icebreaker tops is a thumb loop which necessitates that the sleeves are meant to be about three inches longer than the wrist - I understand this, and just roll those tops up a turn or two.  However, I've read quite a few reviewers' comments that mention that Icebreaker sleeves tend to be long, and I do think that their sleeves are longer than normal.  ["Normal" being subjective, of course!  ...the only women I've met from New Zealand actually did happen to be tall, lithe, and willowy, so maybe that's normal there.  :-) ]  Last week, I bought a 2012-made Icebreaker "Oasis" top in a size small, and while it was too tight in the chest area (which is normally NOT a problem for me with Icebreaker), the sleeves were a crazy four or five inches past my wrist, even though they didn't have thumb holes and therefore were meant to end at the wrist. I had to return it.---Sizing of Leggings:I have run into inconsistency in Icebreaker legging sizes. I have some in extra-small, some in small, and some in medium.  (And in one 2012 collection, the extra-smalls are a little too big for me but there isn't a smaller size to go to.)I have not found Icebreaker's official sizing chart (available on their site) to be terribly accurate for leggings.For the leggings, it seems to me that one must experiment in each Icebreaker clothing range and wool weight to discover the best size and fit for oneself.I will spell out below the ones that I have tried.  Because the sizing of the "same" leggings sometimes has varied across the years, I will mention what year I got them.1.  BODYFIT range1a. Bodyfit 150 leggings2006 or 2007 Bodyfit 150 leggingsSize medium. The label says "slim fit" (possibly back then they had different "fits" within the Bodyfit range, but they don't seem to now).Fit me snugly, but well.Waistband comes up to the belly button, feels secure.2008 Bodyfit 150 leggingsSize small.Are a bit too small for me this winter - they fit me when I'm about 5-to-8 pounds less than I am at the moment.Waistband hits 1 inch below the belly button, feels okay.2012 Bodyfit 150 leggingsI decided not to buy new 150-weight leggings in 2012 because after a few years of heavy use, my old Bodyfit 150 leggings developed some un-mendable "runs"/"ladders". I still wear them and love them, but they are slowly self-destructing. It is comparatively easy to snag them on a rough surface or to poke a fingernail through them when pulling them on or off.Actually, I've just looked on the Icebreaker site (December 2012) and they don't list ANY Bodyfit 150 leggings.  The only 150 weight leggings they list are the "Sprite" leggings from the Premium Underwear Collection.  Also, I think that the "Nature" leggings (which are a discontinued style) were of 150 weight, and I have seen these still on sale on a few websites.1b. Bodyfit 200 leggingsCurrent suggested retail price of around eighty (discounted price of around sixty).2008 Bodyfit 200 leggingsSize medium.Fit me, and there is extra room in them - I probably could go up 5 to 8 pounds and they would still fit. When I purchased those mediums, I tried on the small size and found it to be way too small, especially along the tight and narrow waistband that these leggings were made with at the time.  (I think it was a reaction to the consumer response to that waistband that they made the newer waistbands really wide and soft.)Waistband comes up to the belly button, feels secure.2012 Bodyfit 200 leggingsAt first, based on the Icebreaker official size chart, I ordered a medium in these.  They were too big, so I exchanged them for a size small.The small fit relatively well - snug, but acceptably so.Waistband came up to 2 or even 3 inches below the belly button. This is a more "modern" position for a waistband, of course, compared to coming up to the true waist, but I prefer "athletic" base layers to cover my entire body - neck to ankle, to enable the base layer shirts to be securely tucked inside the base layer pants, and to feel really secure when I'm moving around -- but this waistband was so low on me, and so wide and stretchy that it felt like it was about to slide down to my hips at any moment because the elastic wasn't very tight.Not only from the practical side was this low waistband a problem, but MAN, the whole cut of the upper part of these leggings seemed to be designed to make my tummy area look as flabby and unattractive as possible!  I tried my old leggings on when I took these off -- just to check that it wasn't bad lighting or post-Thanksgiving excess weight that was to blame for how these made me look, but my older Icebreaker Bodyfit 200 leggings looked a lot better on me than these leggings did.I had to return them.  I have decided to wait until next year's production, to see if they alter the cut of the waist area.1c. Bodyfit 260 leggingsCurrent suggested retail price of around ninety (discounted price around seventy-five).2012 Bodyfit 260 leggingsSize small.Fit relatively well - snug, but acceptably so.Waistband came up to 2 inches below the belly button. They had the same issues as the 2012 Bodyfit 200 leggings did - waistband too low, too loose, too wide, and quite unattractive in the belly region!I also had to return these.  I hope next year's will be cut higher on the waist.2.  EVERYDAY range2a. Skin 200 leggings (discontinued 2006) - the Skin range was probably similar to Everyday.2005 Skin 200 leggingsSize extra-small, yet are the largest I own - I could gain 15 pounds and they would still feel okay. But they fit me nicely when I'm at any weight - 10 pounds less or more than my present size - they are simply the coziest and softest that I own.Waistband comes to about 1 inch higher than belly button, feels secure.2b. Everyday 200 leggingsCurrent suggested retail price of around sixty (discounted price of around forty-five).2012 Everyday 200 leggingsTwo weeks ago, I bought them in size small which were too big, so I exchanged them for an extra-small.  Even the extra-smalls had extra material in places on the legs, which is unusual because my legs are not toothpicks (this kind of legging is not supposed to be baggy, so the cut of these must have been off).Worse, the upper part of the extra-small leggings was cut strangely - the waistband was in a deep V, so that the middle was 3 inches below my belly-button (which is way too low for me), but the sides rose up 3 inches higher than that (it wasn't a curve, it was a visible V).  Yet the waistband elastic wasn't tight enough, so the tall sides wanted to sag down and bunch up around my hips -- strange.  (And that was not the way the smalls I tried on the week before had fit my waist area!  In fact, I think the smalls of last week fit me better generally than the extra-smalls of this week.)  I don't have the energy to go through the rigamarole of ordering a different pair of extra-smalls, but maybe I just got a bad apple.I had to return the extra-smalls.I was very disappointed because they were the 7th Icebreaker product I've tried in the last 2 weeks.  This Icebreaker shopping quest has taken up a fair bit of my time lately, but I have nothing new to show for it.  I've given up trying to get anything now and will wait a year and see how their 2013 production fits me.3.  OTHER rangesTheir other legging types are more expensive than the Everyday and Bodyfit, and seem to be geared towards high-tech athletic use, or constructed to be worn on their own as pants/trousers. Some have Lycra in them. Check out Icebreaker's site for more info.--------------------------------OTHER TIPSThe other main retailers of this kind of product sometimes offer free shipping on their Amazon listings of an item but don't offer free shipping on the exact same item when sold through their own site (even when the price of the item itself is the same on both sites), so it can save you money if you pay attention to that.The best selection BY FAR is available from the manufacturer's site, but the prices there are generally higher. However, they have discounts from time to time, such as their "Black Friday" sale when they offer 30% all items that are black in color.Amazon sometimes calls the Icebreaker Bodyfit range "BF" and sometimes "Bodyfit", so if you are searching here for Icebreaker's Bodyfit range, do a separate search under each of the two search terms to get the most accurate results.In terms of merino wool socks, I prefer Smartwool socks over Icebreaker's. Sierratradingpost is one retailer which often carries a large selection of them at good prices. Those socks last a really long time. I wear them almost year-round because the lightweight ones breathe really well even when it's warm out.The Smartwool women's small size is the only sock I can find that truly fits my feet (which aren't even that small, all things considered!) without bunching up inside my shoes.If you have a smaller foot (size 7 or less) and are female, note that the Smartwool unisex socks in the small size are bigger than the smalls made just for women, even though that company's size guide says that they both are meant to fit the same range of women's shoe sizes.

The description on Amazon is very sparse and does not (as of this writing) explain the sizing method of this item.  The item boasts a removable insole and a somewhat stretchable heel loop.  By including the insole, you can reduce 1/2 size, or by stretching the heel strap, you can increase the size.  Thus it is supposed to be adjustable.Sounds great.  Problem is, the insole (if you need it, like I do, in order to get the fit right) immediately starts slipping out of the back of the shoe with every step you take. Notice that there is just open space at the lowest part of the heel, and that's where the insole starts to protrude -- by several inches after taking 30 or 40 steps.So I have the following choices: (a) constantly shove the insoles back in or (b) remove them permanently and tolerate a looser fit or (c) glue the insoles in permanentlyNonetheless for the price, the comfort, and being able to take out the trash in the rain, etc. you can't complain.  But you have to get lucky on the fit, as the adjustable feature really just doesn't work.I am updating this review after a few months with a somewhat higher rating.  Despite them being a loose fit, because the price is so low and because it is a unique product, I decided to keep them.  It is a great convenience being able to slip them on without stooping over, and still have it not flop like a flip-flop sandal.  I only wish the maker would bite the bullet and start producing half-sizes, so that all of us can have the size we were meant to have.

WARNING:  MBT has informed me that while Amazon, LLC is an authorized reseller of genuine MBT shoes, Amazon Marketplace has authorized and UNauthorized sellers.  Some of the MBTs being offered on Amazon.com by Marketplace sellers are COUNTERFEITS.  Everyone has known for some time that most of the MBT shoes being sold on eBay are counterfeits (cheap knock-offs) and now apparently they have snuck in here.  There is no check done by Amazon to make sure their Marketplace sellers are selling genuine MBTs and not counterfeit MBTs; they rely upon customers to tell them after they have received them that they are fakes.  This can be difficult as while some counterfeits are obvious, others are very clever and the average MBT customer may not be able to tell that the workmanship or materials are substandard until after the Amazon return window has closed!  If you like counterfeit shoes that is fine, but you can usually find them for about $30 which is why crooks like to try to pass them off as genuine selling them for the full MSRP and pocket the difference.I think I have owned the entire line of MBT shoes for women that fit me for some time. This MBT Women's Lami Casual Sport Mary Jane and the MBT Kaya Mary Jane are my first choices for when I am going to be out all day. They are the most comfortable through the top of my foot and still has all the shock absorption and rocking benefits of the MBT line. I think this shoe is correctly classified as a casual shoe rather than a walking shoe and I would agree with that - it is my favorite casual shoe but not my choice as a walking shoe.I will now compare the Lami with the Kaya. Both of these Mary Janes have more give or squish when rocking than the rest of the MBT line thus the classification as a casual shoe instead of a walking shoe. The Kaya is much lighter than the Lami. The Lami feels much more substantial all over than the Kaya. The Kaya has a squarer cut out and shows more of your upper foot - the toe knuckles are exposed but not my toes. Lami comes up much higher against the Achilles tendon and if that is something that is going to bother you as it did some other reviewers, then the Kaya would be a much better choice. The Kaya strap goes across the upper foot just once with the securing strap doubling on the side of the shoe whereas the Lami doubles over the top of the foot for more warmth and less foot exposure. The Lami actually runs in 1/3 sizes but to me eventhough my Lami is 2/3 size smaller than my Kaya, the fit seems the same to me both in width and length as well as arch support. The Lami looks sportier than the Kaya. I own them both and wear them both often. Both are excellent shoes.The Tunisha Mary Jane is similar to the MBT Lami and Kaya Mary Janes but New MBT Tunisha Womens Fitness Shoes - Cork - SIZE US 7 has no arch support - it is for people with flat feet.MBT technology and superior materials allow many people to walk pain-free that wouldn't otherwise due to a variety of medical conditions. Just read all the testimonies about how people love being able to walk pain-free because of this shoe. The MBT shoes were originally designed as medical devices and then marketed to the general public; they help people with pain in many places including feet, knees, hips, spine, back, and neck by changing your posture, absorbing shock, stretching and strengthening various muscles and the neurolomuscular effects of rocking. If you are just wanting the rocking technology, there are lots of copycats out there such as Skecher and Aspire but the quality of material used does not compare to MBT. Someone told me that I had spent $200 unnecessarily because their shoe was the same and I went and tried on the Skecher and Aspire and let me tell you that yes they rock but the quality of materials used is not the same at all. The MBT absorbs shock 1000 times better than Skecher or Aspire for one thing which is crucial to my shoe selection for me.MBT technology also "raises your bottom line" and if you aren't used to them, you will be needing to stretch out and you will be sore let me warn you. A neighbor told me they read a newspaper article that said toning shoes don't work and all i can say is they must not have worn MBT! Anyone switching to MBT from other non-toning shoes will wake up the next morning SORE like you overdid it at the gym. Muscles would not get sore like that if they were not getting more exercise than they are used to. Also when one gets to be over 30 or 40 years old, your balance muscles start deteriorating which is why you hear of senior losing their balance and falling down; the tone-up shoes target these balance muscles.Here is my summary on the MBT shoes for Women I worn or tried on:MBT SHOES:best walking - Casual Blackmost comfortable lightweight shoe - Kaya Mary Janemost comfortable with high achilles tendon support - Lami Mary Janebest for long narrow feet - Forabest for narrow feet - Wingubest for small ankles - Patent Namabest for large/swollen ankles or diabetics - Sport (this is a unisex shoe)best for flat feet - Tunisha Mary Janeif you like it real tight across the lacing area - Zurimost annoying/high maintenance - Chapa TrailMBT SANDALS:prettiest - Stakabest walking - Kisumu2most comfortable - Kisumu (original, not Kisumu2)best standing - Pandabest for long narrow feet - Habaridressiest if the buckle rubbing your ankle doesn't bother you too much - SalamaFor those on a budget, I get just as much toning benefit and pain-free walking with Rebook SimplyTone. The SimplyTone also works your inner and outer thigh and gives more of a leg workout than a bottom-line workout. It offers just as much shock absorption and pain-free walking as the MBT and both are better than the Mephisto line for shock absorption which is what I wore previously. However, you might really miss the rocking of the MBT line which I believe has a very relaxing effect neuromuscularly as well as neurologically.MBTs run small compared to other shoes. In MBT, I wear a full-size (not half-size) larger than in most other shoes.FAQsQuestions about usage1. Q: Do they reduce cellulite?A: MBT shoes were developed as a medical device. In the past few years we have learned about the toning effects. MBT shoes help to tone and firm the muscles of the abdomen, buttocks, thighs and calves and increase circulation. We have lots of positive customer feedback regarding cellulite reduction. Wearing MBT shoes activates the stretch reflex thereby helping tone the postural muscles, improving posture and lengthening the body (which will reduce the appearance of cellulite).2. Q: Can they help me to lose weight?A: MBT shoes will help you become more active using more energy during the course of your normal activities of daily living. Wearing the MBT shoes during aerobic exercise will help you burn more calories, thus helping to lose weight and gain a more sculpted appearance.3. Q: Can I do the following in my MBT shoes: squash, badminton, tennis and football?A: MBT is designed as an instability shoe to stimulate the muscles responsible for posture and balance. It replicates walking on an uneven surface: so imagine playing squash etc on uneven ground. Therefore it's not suitable to wear MBT shoes for agility sports in general (such as racquet sports, football or dancing).MBT shoes can be used when exercising with free-weights, step and aerobics. These activities should only be taken up once you are used to walking correctly in the MBTs and have reached a good fitness level (approximately 12 weeks).4. Q: How long should I wear my MBT shoes for at first?A: MBT usage should be between 1 to 2 hours per day for the first week, and then gradually building up the time, until the MBT can be comfortably worn for over 2 hours, by which time muscle activation and proprioceptive feedback are sufficiently attuned to wear the MBT all day, every day. If applied as a medical or therapeutic tool, make sure you refer to a health specialist. The amount of time you are able to tolerate wearing the shoes will depend upon your initial level of fitness and health. Basically, there's just one simple rule: listen to your body!5. Q: Does body weight have an influence on wearing MBT shoes?A: MBT shoes can be worn both by light and heavy people. In the case of very high body weight, it is possible that the soft part of the sole may wear out and require replacement sooner.6. Q: I love my MBT shoes and want to wear them all of the time, but I'm getting blisters on my heels, what can I do?A: Do you have the right size?MBT shoes should be snug on the instep, tight on the heel and comfortable on the toe. If there is any slipping at the heel it is possible that they are too large for you, or if your foot feels as though it is struggling to move but can't, it may be that they are too small. In either case you need to return to the dealer where you bought them so that they can check the fitting.Are your laces tight enough?It might seem obvious that you'd need to do up your shoes tightly but this does really make a difference. Pull the laces firmly from the very front of the foot to ensure that the foot is held snugly and does not slip. You will usually gain about an inch of lace by doing this and, for most people, this will be enough to make sure they stay snug.What socks are you wearing?The type of socks you wear is really important as the wrong ones will increase heat and friction which may cause blisters. We recommend that you wear good quality sports socks made from a breathable material that cover the ankle completely (i.e. not 'rainer socks'? Do not wear tights, pop socks, or socks made from polyester or nylon; and do not wear any style other than the Kisumu sandal with bare feet. It might also be a good idea to try anti-blister socks which have a double layer of fabric so that the outer layer moves with the shoe but the layer next to the skin does not, therefore reducing friction.Extra measuresIf the above things do not have any affect you might need to try gel pads as some people find that the shape of their ankle might not be compatible with the shape of the MBT inner heel, for example their heel or ankle may be thin or bony.7. Q: My MBT shoes are dirty. What can I do?A: The sole construction and Masai Sensor of MBT shoes should not be exposed to aggressive liquids (acids or disinfectants), salt, oil, manure, blood, protein, grease, fertilisers or mud. If they are exposed to these substances they must be cleaned as soon as possible.To wash MBT shoes thoroughly inside and out, use a soft brush (old tooth brush/nail brush) and clear mild liquid hand soap with water up to 30c. Remember to dry them upside down so that the water drains away from the sole.It is best to clean your soiled MBT shoes immediately so that dirt does not become ingrained8. Q: Can I just put them in the washing machine?A: No. Due to the complex nature of the technology in the Masai Sensor, MBT shoes will disintegrate if put in the washing machine, and they cannot be repaired.9. Q: Can I get them wet?A: No. Due to the complex nature of the technology in the Masai Sensor, MBT shoes will disintegrate if put in the washing machine, and they cannot be repaired.MBT shoes should not be put in an oven, microwave, or under a grill! Believe it or not people have tried, and it has never ended well!My personal two cents:one cent: USA medical studies continually state that 70% of foot surgeries in USA would be avoided if people simply wore properly fitting good quality shoes - MBT is the best quality shoe in my opinion but please make sure they fit you properly. reviewText: I owned a pair of Shape-Ups and was considering buying another pair to match more of my workout clothes when I came across these. It turns out this brand and its concept predates Shape-Ups considerably, and I believe they are better shoes, too.This works well as a toning shoe, as does the similar Skechers Shape-Up. However, MBT shoes were not created to give people more of a workout as they do their everyday walking around; they were created for comfort and for less stress on key joints.My primary interest in these shoes was that they were comparable to Shape-Ups but were a better brand, but I have to say I have really come to respect this brand, its mission, and its products. Unlike Shape-Ups, MBT makes shoes for a variety of occasions, even work and dress shoes, to serve those who really need the joint relief this style of shoe provides. I don't have joint pain, but I do have muscle pain in my back and a once-shattered tailbone that is still not perfectly healed. Standing - not just walking - in these shoes forced me to engage my core rather than slump back onto my hips and spine. While that itself wore on me after awhile, I did notice improved posture and less pressure on my lower back and tailbone.I have to say that I haven't worn these in quite awhile, as I began to have fewer and fewer opportunities to wear sneakers or casual dress of any kind. The relief for me personally was not so great that I sought out times to switch to these shoes, and while dress shoes are made by MBT, my need was not great enough for me to invest in a wardrobe full of these. However, that is not the fault of the product and thus I give it a 5-star rating for quality of brand, selection of styles, and effectiveness of the product.Price would be a sticking point. These are expensive. To that I say, if you need them, you need them and they're worth it. If you're looking into the toning shoe fad and aren't sure how you feel about it, pick up a $65 pair of Skechers Shape-Ups and then upgrade if you really love the concept.UPDATE: I've been wearing my MBTs for about four days now, and today I had to wear heels all day, then I slipped on boat shoes when I got home. Lying down for a little bit, my spine felt like it had been hammered on both ends. My back muscles felt cramped and my tailbone felt like it had been smacked with a frying pan. I'm going to have to say that yeah, these are extremely comfortable and they must do wonders for your posture.
summary: Do your spine and joints a favor! (Better than Shape-Ups!)

reviewText: I've used this for a few months now and so far the metal kick flap on the side fell off.  Plan on installing this by screwing it into a large piece of wood so you hold it down with one foot while you brush the other.

Bought this unit for down at the barn.  We threw it outside the barn door, it poured down rain that night, the next day everyone had a chance to use it on their very muddy boots!  It has a side panel that folds down so you can hold the unit in place with one foot on the side panel while scrapping off mud on the other.  We were all so impressed with how good this got all the mud out of even the little channels in the soles of the boots.
summary: Great unit - cleans very muddy boots!

reviewText: We purchased product for use of cleaning dirt/hay off shoes after working in the garden.  Product did not meet our expectiation.  Poorly made, there were not 2 fold down magnetic sides as described, no hardware included and was difficult to use as free standing.
Works well, especially after I mounted in on a 1x6" board for more stability. Gets into the deep crevasses of my boot soles very well.
My husband generally always approaches the back door with mud, etc. on his boots.  this works great for that problem.
This is a nice way to get wet grass and dirt off your shoes.  It is small and convenient to leave by the patio door.

First, this was exactly the product I was looking for - along the lines of what they have at golf courses.  So when I go out with the dog I don't drag half the yard in with me.Second, I had planned on needing and/or wanting to permanently attach it to the deck so it didn't move etc...  Trouble free scraping.  BUT the wings on this thing are great, allowing you to step with the other foot and scrape the other one.  Allows me to drag it around to different spots, and easily clean it out every now and then somewhere other than in-place.  The magnetic part is nice for flipping up to move, storage, or on the day you do decide to mount it somewhere.I was hoping to find something cheaper, but this was well worth the money, its got a good weight to it, and solid construction.
summary: Perfect - just what I was looking for

reviewText: I bought one of these a few years ago, and it worked pretty well.  But due to rotting wood in the scrubber, one of the bristle sections came off and I bought a new one.I thought the new one would be good, because Amazon still lists the product as having "Magnetic folding plates on both ends".But Bosmere seems to have decided to completely cheap out, and now absurdly ONLY HAS A PLATE ON ONE SIDE.  That means you can only clean one shoe unless you are going to flip the scrubber around every single time.  I don't think so.  (Yes if you have it on a wood deck you could screw it in, if you don't mind putting holes in your deck, but mine is for my front door with a concrete porch, and I'm not going to put screws into the concrete.  There is no logic to only having the plate on one side, other than for Bosmere to save a tiny amount of money... but they are just hurting themselves in the end since they will lose customers.)I guess I'll probably get a piece of wood to mount the whole thing to since I've already used it and don't feel right returning it, but that is not nearly as nice looking at my front door, and it is inexcusable for Bosmere to make such an anti-consumer change.  (In Bosmere's slight defense, their packaging (and web site - http://www.bosmereusa.com/Product.asp?_pcode=N472US) does indicate that the plate is only on one side.  So at least they are not lying, but they don't seem interested in telling Amazon to change their current erroneous description.)
summary: Bosmere has nerfed this product; now only has a folding plate on one side!

reviewText: This is probably the best boot scraper I've ever used.  The only recommendation I would make is that it should be mounted on a something fixed. It comes with the ability to be mounted (we used some heavy lumber pieces) so it will stay in place while being used.
I really advise anyone who walks their dog(s) in parks or on or off trail to buy this item. Well made and works well with my size 12 cleat sole boots.

The brushes work great and the overall product is study.  The photo shows a fold-down plate on each side, but there's only one.  It definitely worked better after attaching it to a wood base to stand on while scraping boots.  Overall, it does the job.

It would appear that the boot scrapper needs to be secured to a solid surface inorder to work effectively.  Unfortunately, drilling four holes in my deck is not an option and I have brick in the front of my house.  The hinged step plate helps but the unit still moves when being used.  A suggestion was to secure the unit to larger board where your weight will keep it from slidding.  All in all, it does the job and I am satisfied.

I love how it can be mounted permanently or you can flip down a ledge to hold it steady with one foot while you're scraping the other. I also love that it gets the sides, not just the bottoms, of the shoes.
This is a Great product. Gets my boots clean every time no matter if it is mud, clay, or dirt.
summary: Great for cleaning your boots before you go inside

reviewText: Mounted with screws on a wooden porch at the cabin and used it today for the first time.  It works perfectly and will really cut down on dirt, snow, etc. being tracked into the cabin.  Very pleased with the quality and function.

I got this as a gift for my husband and he loves it.  With his occupation he comes home with mud covered boots regularly and was always tracking it in and so I saw this and got it and we don't have that problem anymore.  It takes the mud off the bottom and the sides.  It is well-built.
The boot scraper is a very good value for the dollars.  It is quite light weight so it needed to be attached to the step to work properly
It is a good product however it is very flimsy. Could be made stronger as when you push your foot through it twists
Works great, easy to install and does the job.... Essential for anyone who works outside and needs to come in often to clean their boots.

This is a pretty sturdy brush that can be screwed right to your deck. It comes with two kind of wings that fold out on the base with a slip resistant surface that you step on with the non-brushing boot. The bristles are large and quite stiff and quality seems above average.

The first two that I purchased on a single order came with folding sides on each side and seemed very sturdy.  Somewhere between my first order and my second order of a single boot scraper this was changed and it only has one fold down side.  Pretty annoying to kick it around with your feet or turn around the other way to scrape different boots.  Newer one also seemed pretty flimsy.  Why would they change this?

I had a boot scraper I really liked that disappeared and couldn't find a replacement. After much looking around I found this one that is very functional -- the large side brushes are great. I was afraid it might be a bit awkward to have to stand on the stabilizer to scrape the boot, but got used to that quickly. Only thing I'm not thrilled with is the green color. It is right at my front door and beautiful would have earned it some bonus points.

Got this as xmas present for my husband (ok, kinda sorta for me...tired of what he tracked in).  I love that it can be moved around and used anywhere -- doesn't need to be anchored down in any one spot -- because it has the side metal flap that you step on while using it.  Bristles seem to be holding up reasonably well (I've read posts about that not being the case with some).  We've been using it for about 6months and it still has alot of wear left, I think.  Glad I made this purchase.

I bought two of these, on for the front door way and one for the back, but one of the brushes did not come the the mounting hardware. It is not a big deal if you do not plan to mount it to anything, but buyer beware.

This boot scraper works great.  I carefully considered buying one that you screw down, but ultimately decided on this one.  Good choice, as it can easily be taken off the porch to rinse off and can easily be moved to sweep up underit.  "Flaps" on either side allow you to hold down the scraper with the foot not being cleaned.  This product works great for us!
I'm ordering my third one of these.  One for the front door, one for the back, and one for a gift.  It works.  I ordered them all from Amazon and got them quickly.

DONT BUY THIS BASED ON THE GOOD  REVIEWS HERE1) advertised as having two fold down magnetic plates to stablize when using.Mine has only one.. and the other is secured with tiny rivets to two small hinges ..2) for the price paid, I expected something much more substantial.. This wont last.reading other reviews, I see some people received different units , some with two plates and some with none..I agree with other negative reviews, that for the price, this is junk.Ive seen problems like this from Amazon in the past where they change suppliers ,. so prior reviews are not applicable....Returning this junk....responsibility for this is shared with Amazon and the manufacturer
summary: DONT BUY THIS BASED ON THE GOOD  REVIEWS HERE

reviewText: We have a 50 x 80 ft back yard. My wife is an avid gardener and she's planted an amazing variety of trees, veggies and flowers in it. In the winter and spring she's out there mulching,fertilizing and planting almost every day in her "gum boots". The Bosmere Boot Scraper/Brush does a great job of cleaning those boots when she's ready to come indoors.  She particularly likes the fold out metal tabs which allow holding it down with one boot while cleaning the other.

I bought this less than three years ago and have used it infrequently.  I'd guess maybe 20x per year.  Today when I went to brush the grass off my sneakers the top half of the right brush broke off.  It's wooden and must have weakened from being exposed to the weather. It wouldn't be so bad if one could buy replacement brushes somewhere, but I contacted the vendor and they don't make them. This product line fit great on my foots,so why to change ?the only little issue is, durability ,for the cost I think this shoes are great.

They are lightweight, extremely comfortable, and look great.  I really dont have any complaints except for the little sticker with the logon on the heal is starting to come off, but after 2 years that is acceptable.  I usually dont keep a pair of shoes for this long but i have no reason to buy something else.  None of the material has torn as did with my Pumas, my laces have not frayed or become damaged in any way.  Im defiantly buying a pair of sauconys again.

reviewText: These shoes were too narrow for me.  It's not a problem I usually have, and I've had good experiences with saucony.

My first pair I had to ship back because there was a slight bubble near my toes on the right foot.  The second pair wasn't that much better.  There is something that is not right with both the left and the right in different places that hurt my foot over time.  I would not purchase these shoes again.
LOVE THEM!!!! Best shoe to run in by far. And for the money...Forget about it! Getting ready to buy my second pair. Not because I need them but because they are so comfortable. I need more colors.
I love this shoes. They are very light and well made. Perfect for me. I would recomend it to a friend.
This shoe fits like a glove...feels great...holds my feet steady...have stopped looking at any other brands period!!
Best Running Shoe I've owned. I have two pair of the Blue and two pair of the Red. Can't wait to see what the Triumph 7's are like!! Good Job Saucony!!
Very good shoe if you have a high arch and like more of a cushioned sole.

This shoe provided much needed support and cushioning that I need for my plantar fasciitis.  I have had these shoes for a while and they are ready for replacement which I will do with the current version of this style.

reviewText: My fourth pair of Saucony Triumph's...and it won't be the last. Great quality, great running shoe.
In general, excellent shoes. As they are a little on the hard side, they are fast.  I'm going to use them on races.
This is my second pair of the Triump 6. One of the best cushioned and comfortable running shoes I have ever worn.

I thought i was on the Canadian site and all purchases were in Can $, it was not .It was in US funds ......not happy .2.The shipping costs were nearly 50% of the running shoes ......way to much.The next time i will be sure of my purchase and either refuse to pay the big difference in price or cancel the order .

These shoes are the  B E S T  running shoes on earth. When U wear them you're just PROUD of them.... That's what I like most of all. If these shoes are back in stock, I'd buy them at least 5 pairs. I'M LOVIN' IT !!!

reviewText: I have the Triumph 4 as well (350 miles on them) and really liked it which is why I decided to purchase the 6.  This is an excellent shoe with great support and excellent cushioning. It is a bit stiff at first but loosens up nicely after about 30 miles.
The seller was excellent. The shoes are ok. The Triumph 5s seem to offer better cushioning.

These shoes take some break in time to get used to if you had the triumph 5 before these. They are a little stiffer than triumph 5 in the heal and forefoot. That may have been the aim of saucony, but I was not a fan. Some runners like this but I wish I knew this before I bought them.
summary: Not as soft out of box as triumph 5

reviewText: I am training for my first marathon and needed a shoe with excellent cushion due to my size (195 lbs).  I have always heard and read great things about the Saucony brand.  As a lifelong Nike and Adidas running shoe wearer, I decided to make the switch because of the Progrid's high review in Runners World and my wife's praise of her first pair.I ordered the shoes and it arrived a couple days latter.  I took advantage of Amazon's $40 off the price with the use of their card and got the shoes for under $40.  My local shoe store had the same shoe for $119.Great ProductExcellent PriceFast Delivery
I bought these for my husband to replace an older pair of the same model.  He loves them.  Fast shipping, too.
Saucony is the only shoe I will run with. I have suffered from planter fasciitis in the past with other brands. These shoes long out wear the recommend 500 miles.

Saucony has regained the magic of the old Triumph 4 with the Triumph 6. The Triumph 5 sucked. I tried the 5s, returned them and then bought a batch of the 4s that I hoarded like gold. Thank goodness Saucony brought the Triumph 6s out when they did....I was down to my last pair of the Triumph 4s.

These are my first cycle shoes and attempt at clip in's. I think they're attractive because they match my bike! Isn't that vain. I wish these shoes were more comfortable and I may add some padding inside. My feet aren't use to hard shoes, being a runner.

I work in concrete everyday and these are better the the yellow boots.  These boots stretch when you pull them on and they come off easy by kicking your heel on a hard edge. I spray a little polish on the inside of boot so my shoe slides better when putting them on.

The overboots themselves are great. Pull all you want, they will stretch right over most of the boots you are wearing. Snug, secure, comfortable, and will last as long as several pairs of the cheap PVC boots. That's time saved going back to the supply warehouse. That is unless you have some oversized work boots to go into them.With most of my standard sized boots (Wolverine, Bass, etc) in 13W (approx 13 to 13-1/4" sole length), these slip on and off just fine.The problem is with my Thorogood 13W steel Moc toe wedge boot, which is a copy of a Red Wing 1907. I think Thorogood simply used their sz 14 lasts to make these, as the sole measures 13-7/8" from end to end (rolling the ruler along the sole). The steel Moc toes simply add to the bulk.The day I decided to get a pair of these (based on recommendations), I was wearing my smaller-soled Wolverines boots. I placed my boot on the measuring display on the side of the box, as well as the Treds measuring decal on the floor at the building supply store, and the measurement showed my boots were well under the max measuring line to use the L/XL sized overboots (odd choice for a boot size, since they also have an XL and XXL). The store didn't carry the XL or XXL, and I knew of only one other store in the county that carried this brand of overboots. Thought they would fit the same on all of my boots. After a couple of uses, though, I realize they just aren't going to work with the larger-soled Thorogood boots, as I discovered when I tried the overboots on them later.I love the Thorogood work boots; it's just that they're too big to fit into these overboots without a ton of effort to get them on and are nearly impossible to get off once forced on. I went back to the supply store and compared the Thorogood boots to the measuring display on the floor and box, and they came up just a hair width below the max measuring line for the L/XL size.I will look for the XL, one size up, for use with these boots or other Moc toe / steel toe boots, on the off chance they too are oversized. Wasn't really planning on getting two pairs, but thats what I am going to have to do. Fortunately, I will get plenty of use out of these pouring concrete, whichever workboots I'm wearing.At the Treds.com website (I discovered after the fact), they have a sizing chart (not available at the retailer I went to; they only had the put-your-shoe-on-the-line sticker on the floor, plus the measuring marks on the product box). The chart shows that a sole length of 13 1/4 - 13 3/4" should use the L/XL, 13 3/4 - 14 1/2" should use XL, and 14 1/2 - 15 1/2" should use XXL. Wish I had that info before I purchased the smaller pair. Now I will end up with two pairs.Finding the XL version here at Amazon takes a bit of work, though. A standard "Treds over shoe / boot" search doesn't show the XL model in the results. The seller who markets most of the other sizes here doesn't advertise the XL, and it is instead listed at Amazon under another title... "Treds XL Over the Shoe 17" Slush Boot", part number 17853, ASIN B001I014I8.If you wear longer 13's or 14's workboots, or larger, definitely try these on for size if possible, because they may not fit well.Note: These are not lined. I didn't find that a problem. Just thick, solid stretchy rubber.Update: Received the XL sized overboots, and they work perfectly with the larger workboots. Just FYI.
summary: Sizing Issues - Know your Workboot size...

reviewText: I do concrete for a living and these boots are the best over boot I've ever used! They go and off easy but they don't just fall off if you get in the deep mud or sticky clay on a jobsite
Very nice high quality bands bought 2 . Went to the mall and had it put on when got it looks great. I would definitely recommend if you're looking for a rubber band!
Used this to replace the stock band on an Invicta Russian Diver.  The fit is perfect and I haven't had any issues yet.  Exactly what I was looking for.

The Modena Italian Rubber watch band is a replacement for a one year old rubber original equipment band on a 45 mm watch. The original failed by spitting at the buckle. The Modena is much more substantially built and should last much longer.
Bulky and extremely non ergonomic.  The strap is way too large and bulky.  Only suggest this item for anyone who has wrists the size of the hulk.

Received this strap today and am generally pleased overall.  I bought it to go on my Invicta Grand Lupah.  It makes a great looking combination.  It is also extremely soft and flexible, which makes it very comfortable on the wrist.  The only drawback is that this strap attracts lint and dust like a magnet!  It is virtually impossible to keep clean.  I'd love any suggestions on how to keep this strap from looking like a lint brush!

The garter belt works fine for holding up my hockey socks, but the plastic pieces don't secure to the metal loops very well. reviewText: Product came missing parts.  Contacted vendor & was told by email they would mail missing parts.  Nearly 2 weeks later no parts.  Have emailed vendor & asked if coming or do they want the item back.

I am a 79 year old female wanting a garter belt for my support hose.  I did not want a fancy belt as I wear jeans all of the time and work in yard a lot.I received the belt in a timely manner but the plastic clips were not attachaed to the straps. reviewText: It gets the job. For some reason one always pops off while playing. I am still happy with my purchase of it.
just like you would think it would, nothing fancy or complicated, all parts function fine hold the socks where you have it set.

This belt was what it was advertized as but I didn't know there was not a backing to the garters.  I was useing this with compression stockings.  I wore hhe belt one day and had large and painful blisters thad had burst .  I was at a meeting and couldnot remove belt.  buyer beware.

I love these water shoes but the sizing is all over the place. reviewText: Great A++

I ordered these shoes for a last-minute beach vacation. They were pretty comfortable when walking around from the city street to the beach. Sand tends to get in them as you walk along the beach but I assume that is pretty standard across all beach shoes.The size: I am an 8 so I ordered the 8-8.5 and they were too large to feel comfortable, so I reordered this time the size 6-7 which fit snug but not constricting by any means. It stinks because I sent the previous shoes back but was penalized (by Amazon) since the return was not their fault so my cheap purchase added up.Wear: I walked a fair bit in them from hiking (on paved paths) to the beach. There's not much shock absorption but it is to be expected. I was afraid I was going to tear them putting them on, I had rips starting along the inside of each ankle trying to get them but they held up all-in-all for the 9-day trip.Swimming in them: they were pretty comfy swimming in. I never got a huge pocket of water that weighed me down and the material is pretty light-weight and dries pretty quick as well.I would probably reconsider and seek another brand when I'm in the market again for water/beach shoes.

Simply stated, these do not, it feels like being barefoot while you are swimming...It is a different experience altogether on land or poolside. I did slip on more than one occasion during my vacation.I bought one size lower than my shoe size and these stretched nicely.These are great in the water, just beware outside of it!

I was somewhat confused about what the "ion-mask" shoe really was.  Is it water proof?  The answer is no.  It is highly water repellent.  Most of the time your feet stay dry because these shoes repel water.  The advantage of this technology is the shoe is way more breathable than something like GoreTex, because there is no membrane just breathable mesh.  The disadvantage is that if you really get the shoe wet - as in crossing a stream where part of the shoe is actually under water - your feet will get wet.  These shoes are great if you want a very breathable shoe for damp conditions, they are not great if  you are counting on them to be waterproof.I need a wide toe box and found these shoes fit very well and were very comfortable.  They might run a little big.  The sole is not as stiff as a hiking shoe, more like a trail shoe, so may not be the best choice on rough terrain, but is very comfortable.  My big problem with this shoe (other than the confusing claims made about how waterproof it is) is its durability.  Mine lasted less than six months until the sole separated from the shoe.  The shoes also looked pretty worn by that point.  The fabric on the inside of the heels was badly frayed and some of the fabric on the outside had ripped.  I could understand this if I wore them in rugged conditions, but I mostly wore them around town.  Anyway, I replaced them with a pair of GoreTex shoes.  My feet are hotter but I need a shoe that will stay dry in all conditions.
summary: Comfortable, water repellent shoes that did not last long

[UPDATE]At the time I wrote this review, I had only worn the rainpants for a short time in a moderate rain.  Last week I wore them in a downpour for an hour on the freeway.  They do leak in the middle, not a lot - my jeans were damp rather than soaked.  But it they were distinctly uncomfortable for that part of the ride.  Rainpants costing over $100 shouldn't leak at all.  I suspect that you could treat them with seam sealer and plug the leak - but seam sealer wears out after a while & you'll only notice when you get that cold trickle "down there."[ORIGINAL REVIEW]Here in Seattle, you've only got two choices: either you ride in the rain or you ride in August.  Rainsuits are more popular than sunglasses.  Not sure how it happened, but my old pair of neoprene rain pants shrunk over the summer.  Needed a new pair, did my homework & decided on the Icon Pdx's.The ads are right: these don't suck.  They're very well made, lots of adjustment straps, etc.  The zippers are all the nearly-waterproof type, well protected by flies.  All the snaps, straps, zippers, toggles, etc are big enough to use while wearing gloves.  Overall construction leads me to believe they'd take a lot of abuse (AKA "real life") without a problem.The stirrups are removable, I like that - stirrups are a bit of a pain, and the Pdx's legs have drawstrings on the bottom which keep the pants from riding up in the wind anyway.The legs are long enough for a tall guy with his legs stretched out.  The pants are fully lined with a breathable mesh that should keep them (and me) from sweating.  The outer pockets are as close to waterproof as you can get while still allowing easy access, a little on the narrow side though.  I can't get my paws into 'em even without my gloves on.Two nits keeps this from being a five-star review:They're a little tight in the waist for 2X's - oh, they go around my ample middle with a little slack, and they've got room for my chaps - however they're not big enough to go over my leather jacket. I prefer bibs that are sized to go over my jacket, but they work well enough with a waterproof over-jacket on top.Nit Number two is the supposed reflective graphics.  There are only a couple, they're small, and both of them are Icons.  errr, I mean "graphical representations of the company name" (which just happens to be 'Icon.')  One of them is basically in my lap & if a car's headlights can actually hit it I'm probably no longer shiny side up.I'd prefer some reflective stripes instead, and I really don't like having a lot of logos pasted all over my body.  If they want me to endorse their product, they can talk to my agent, same as anybody else.  ::cough::
