reviewText: Very durable shoe with more than adequate protection. Have used them on several 1000 kilometres of riding from Whistler Bike Park to cross country epics in Rossland. They can handle mud and water quite well, though they're not waterproof obviously. On occasions when I have completely submersed them, I've hosed them off, pulled outside the foot liners and left them to dry naturally in my laundry room. Generally dry within 24 hours and ready to go. I will be buying FiveTen's again for sure.

Looking to try platform pedals (I normally used clipless), I picked the Freerider Scribble model because they were under $100/pair, and appearance-wise they matched my other casual shoes (a pair of DC skate shoes- I used to skate a long time ago!) so if I decided to pull the plug on the whole platform pedal experiment, I could still use the FiveTen's for daily casual. Walking around in the FiveTens when I'm out and about will look normal, compared to if I were to try to go casual with my mountain biking, SPD-equipped shoes.When they arrived at my door, I tried them on for fitment. The FiveTen shoe sizing is about the same as with my Shimano shoes, but if I had to be critical the FiveTen's seem to be a tad tighter on the sides; this is most likely due to the fact that my Shimano SH-MT32L Mountain Bike Shoes have thinner sidewalls, where the FiveTen's have padded sides. It didn't make it uncomfortable though, just a little more snug. The toe area is just as roomy. Since the FiveTen's are a more "casual" shoe with a thick, padded tongue, you don't lace these up as tight as other shoes, but they will stay on just as well.Trying them on the soles are not as stiff as the MT-32L's, but not as flexible as my regular DC skate shoes. The centers feel stiff - good when it's time to pedal, since if it's too soft it would absorb some pedaling power when it's time to hammer down. As for the sole compound, the color combo I chose came with the stickier S1 compound (depending on the shoe color, some come with S1 and some come with a less-sticky "PH" compound) and it was immediately evident walking around in my garage - I could literally hear the soles stick to the bare concrete!Sitting on my bike for a quick test "feel", the first thought through my mind was, "wow - these are sticky!" Once I had my weight on the pedals, the S1 compound stuck like flypaper. I couldn't even slide the shoe around on the pedal, nor could I twist the shoe to change my foot angle. I had to actually lift my foot of the pedal to reposition - and when taking a look at how the shoe touched the pedals, I learned why. The pattern of the sole combined with the sticky rubber compound let the pedal pins lock into the sole; either a pin would sit in one of the many recesses in the sole, or it would sink into the raised portions of the sole. For reference, I was using a pair ofBlackspire Sub4 pedal, 9/16" - blackpedals.With the traction there, the first thing I did notice was that my pedaling was cut in half; because I could no longer use the upstroke when climbing (like you can with clipless pedals), I had to rely on just the downstroke. The second thing that I noticed was that in the beginning I was always stepping on the pedals in different fore/aft position; I got spoiled by the clipless pedal and how it automatically positioned my foot in the right place. However, the next ride afterward I didn't notice those first two complaints anymore. I simply adapted to pedaling with downstroke only, and positioning my foot centered on the pedal quickly became second nature within one ride.I have now converted to platform pedals exclusively because of these shoes. It might be difficult to grasp for long-time clipless users (I was one) but if I had to pick the best "plus" for using the FiveTen's with platform pedals: Freedom. My FiveTen shoe may feel "locked on" with its awesome traction, but the split second I have to move my foot, I don't have to subconsciously remember to unclip first - I just move my foot, and it will move. This actually saved me from a crash recently; I was heading downhill on some rough terrain at speed, and when I got to the bottom the surface turned into loose round rocks - a fast change from the packed dirt at the top and middle of the hill. My front tire got loose at speed, but I lifted my left foot and stuck it out to regain my balance, saving myself from a crash. To be honest, I'm not sure if I could have unclipped in time to do the same, as it was a matter of split seconds between surviving (which I did) and crashing (which, thankfully, I didn't).Everyone who's said that the FiveTen shoes stick like glue are not making it up, these have amazing traction and you would have to feel it to believe it!

reviewText: Bought these after the soles on my Five Ten Impact Highs delaminated. I like these better for pump track and dirt jump type riding. The soles aren't quite as stiff as the Impacts so I can "feel" the bike better. The narrower foot bed and lack of side "grips" (on the Impacts the soles wrap up on each side of the instep) allows me to set my feet more quickly and accurately in the pedals. I ride Wellgo B-103 platform pedals and with the Five Tens I might as well be clipped in. Five Tens are just as good as their hype!Sizing: For me, Five Tens run about 1/2 to a full size small compared to my other shoes. I have size 10 in both Impact and Freerider, but I wear a 9 1/2D in Lucchese boots, a 9 1/2D in Ariat boots, a 9D in Allen-Edmonds oxfords, 9D in Bally loafers, 9M in Bruno Magli loafers, 9 1/2D in Cole-Haan loafers (made in Italy), 9D in Cole-Haan oxfords (made in USA), 9D in Johnston & Murphy (made in Italy), and a 43 (Euro) in Scarpa. ( I didn't list all these to advertise the brand of shoes I have, but for comparison sake in hopes that it might help someone else choose their correct size the first time around).Looks/Style: When my 15 year old son first noticed my new Freeriders he said, "Whoa, those are cool!". Doesn't get much better than that! They look great with jeans, and are comfortable enough to wear all day.Company: An additional note on Five Ten the company, after 6-8 months of very light use the sole on the right shoe of my Impact Highs completely delaminated. I called Five Ten, a person answered the phone almost immediately, listened to the situation and emailed me a return authorization number. I sent the shoes back at my expense, they received the shoes in about 4 days, and 3 days later a brand new pair of Five Ten Impact Highs showed up at my door. AMAZING! (LOL, if I'd known this was going to happen I probably wouldn't have purchased the Freeriders in the first place, but now I'm glad I did regardless.)FIVE TEN IS AWESOME! I doubt I'll ever buy another brand of shoe for biking, or hiking, or climbing. Don't hesitate to purchase Five Ten shoes - you won't be disappointed. ( I have no affiliation with Five Ten whatsoever.)I checked every other source for these Freeriders and Amazon had the best price - and they shipped for free and arrived in two days with Amazon Prime.

These boots may seem like overkill for most people, because they are HEAVY and expensive - but let me tell you from personal experience that they are worth it.  They lasted me for years with heavy use.  I wore them for basic day hikes, for long backpacking hauls, for 45-mile speed hikes, for traveling thru Australia, as work boots for construction, around horses to protect my feet, around rattlesnakes to protect my feet, and even as winter boots in the snow in Boston.  They have been EVERYWHERE with me, and they lasted for a very long time.  (Compare this with GTX boots which often crack, don't stay waterproof for very long, and usually wear out in about a year with heavy use.)An important thing to note: although they are billed as "dry climate" boots, they work just as well as GTX if you waterproof them.  The beauty of leather is that it holds up so much better than synthetic fabrics, is more comfortable, more durable, less stinky, etc.  BUT - you have to maintain them.  This is very easy to do - just rub some mink oil into them if they have been getting wet a lot and are no longer shedding water.  I usually didn't do this very frequently, maybe every month, or at max every week if I was hiking quite a bit.  Once they are well-oiled, they shed water no problem, and will keep your feet very very comfy and dry.  They never gave me blisters, which is a beautiful thing.  I think these boots are very unique because hardly anyone makes full leather shoes anymore. This isn't because they aren't as good, but because they are much more expensive compared to GtX and other synthetic fabrics and we are turning into a disposable culture!Also - two downsides:1. like many GTX shoes, they do not breathe.  This means that your feet will get sweaty in the shoes from time to time on a hot hike.  Don't worry - when you rest for the day, just unlace your boots for a second and air your feet out.  No problem!  If you are really having a problem, change your socks.2. They do NOT pack well for travel - they are super heavy (built for anything, any adventure you may come across!) and will weigh you down if you aren't wearing them on your feet.  So take this into consideration.But, all of this being said, if you want a shoe you know will support you no matter what, that will always do the job when you need to be sure of your footwear on a backpacking trip or a big trip, you should buy this shoe.  It won't let you down.  I will keep buying this shoe as it wears about every 5-7 years or so, because I have never had a more comfortable and reliable boot.  Go for the real leather experience - you won't regret it!

reviewText: I am sad to report that this product isn't for me. There were puckers (as the instructions indicated there might be, as well as that these puckers are "normal"). Then the pain came...Although my breasts LOOKED fabulous, within minutes they didn't feel so fabulous, because the skin on my breasts is thin and delicate and it was pulling. I tried to work through the pain by ignoring it, donning a tank top and going outside to play with my girls for a bit, but it wasn't long before I had to run inside to take them off. Then come the REAL pain...removing them :( Even following the removal instructions, my poor boobies suffered skin removal in 3 spots that hurt for over a week while they healed :(  So, ladies, if your boobies are anything like mine, then try to keep my experience in mind, so you don't have this happen to you.

I purchased these breast lifts to wear in my wedding dress. They lift quite nicely and I prefer them to the lifts that are applied from underneath. They don't provide cleavage at all, but can be used in conjunction with other Hollywood products like the Shantina Lite Adhesive Bra. The biggest drawback is that the adhesive might show with a scoop, sweetheart or square neckline.
The product was easy to use. They were affordable., Shipped fast, and the results were fantastic. I would recommend this product to anyone wanting to wear a strapless dress or top.

I decided to try these for my casual summer dresses and for a formal strapless dress I wore to a wedding. The instructions are easy to follow, and the lift they provide is excellent if you want a natural, bra-less look as opposed to a push-up look (I'm a C cup, about 36). They do look a little funny in the nude, as they cause a pucker or fold in the skin, but once you're dressed, no one would ever guess your little trick. ;) And they stayed on in sweaty conditions, dancing, etc. I decided to REALLY test them by keeping them on overnight and then wearing them in a rugby game the next day, under two sports bras. They actually stayed almost totally in place through the 80-minute game.There may be issues with some low-cut dresses where the adhesive might show -- I solved this problem by using fashion tape to secure my dress just above where the adhesive was. I have a casual knit dress with a plunging V that I've worn these with, and they didn't show, but again I secured the dress with fashion tape to avoid any potential accidental exposure. :)I didn't experience pain from the lifting or the adhesive like some other commenters have. My only note of caution (echoing the instructions that come with the product) is to take them off VERY slowly because I made the mistake of removing them in a hurry the first time, and I did suffer some blistering and raw skin, and maybe a bit of skin torn off. The next time, I removed them VERY slowly and it was fine. (I had been sweating so the moisture probably helped.) There was a bit of blotchy reddening in some spots, but it faded quickly.On a side note, I've been thrilled with all of the Hollywood Fashion Tape products I've tried -- the tape strips and multi-pack of different size tapes for clothing. I've ordered all of them through Amazon and they've all arrived quickly. Highly recommend!

The watch design style and functions are the best for the money. It runs on a high end Swiss ETA movement and is highly accurate when compared to an atomic clock or watch. This watch has not gain or loss a second in 2 weeks when compared to atomic clock time. Unlike expensive 100% mechanical chronographs, winding or self-winding (automatic), this electromechanical watch with its stepping motors can provide stop watch accuracy to 1/10th second or 100 msec. One draw back is that as a stopwatch, it cannot keep track of elapsed time beyond 30 minutes. There just isn't enough space on the dial to add another one hour or 12 hours subdial. Two features that make this chronograph stand out against comparable ones. One is the cockpit instrument design which allow easy reading in low light conditions and legibility of the hands and numbers (both very large). The other feature is the chronograph function buttons which do not protrude from the watch case but yet can be pushed in with ease with your finger tips and not so small like other chronographs that you need to use your fingernails.

Above 100 mph they were useless. BUT in all fairness I go out to ride with different intentions. If I'm jumping on the busa to tear it up, then I put my helmet on. If I'm going out to enjoy a nice leisurely ride to enjoy the weather or to the store or to a friends place, not intending on riding fast at all then these fit the bill perfectly! 5 stars from me anyway and I will buy another pair in case these happen to break or I lose them, I will want another pair :).

Dear Amazon Shopper,This wallet is a tankish monstrosity, the greatest strength of which is simultaneously its only real weakness.  Before I get into the shortcoming of this wallet, however, let me just cover the basics.You're probably looking at this wallet because you want something durable that holds stuff.  Well friend, if that's the case, you've come to the right page.  The nylon is over-strength, the seams are overstitched, and the construction is generally overengineered; unless you're using this wallet to play tug-of-war with your German Shepherd, I suspect it will last a very long time.  In terms of capacity, this wallet will hold your cash, cards, and change, and has interior and exterior transparent sleeves for ID's.  If your current wallet holds it, this wallet will hold it, and then some.However, there's no guarantee that your pocket will hold this wallet.  One of the persons to whom I gifted this behemoth ultimately opted not to use it, after discovering that the wallet would not fit into his back pocket (neither when empty nor when full).  As such, I recommend this wallet for persons who opt to carry it on a belt, as carrying it in a back pocket is only viable if your pockets are very large.The bottom line: a cavernous wallet layered in nylon armor at the expense of form-factor.Thank you

Probably due to lighting when they took the pic. The Jr showed that it was lighter looking (ACU pattern as well), which is the colour I wanted. But that too was the same as the original. So, the colour will vary from the picture. Just be warn!Original: Pros:*Large room for cash/receipts. Has a hidden zipper area to hide cash/receipts in as well. When I say large, I mean big enough to fit your work check in without folding it.*8 card slots which you could double to 16 cards to hold. Inside clear window can hold cards as well, more than 2. 16 plus cards it can hold, by my account.*Zipper pocket to hold change or similar size objects.*Able to hold passport. You can put another passport in there i assume,or what you want, but I don't know if it'll fall out since it's upside down. Didn't test it. Part of the Shark-bite closure acts like a fall out protector. So the cards can't fall to the ground. With that said, I didn't test this. I say this only by observing it. You will see what I mean when you get it.*Stitching looks good & solid. The material feels durable. I've been a leather wallet person. Never would go over to the Velcro closing type wallet that's made out of plastic type material. This wallet feels stronger than that.*Life time warranty!!!Original: Cons:*It is a bit bigger than I would of wanted. The only pants that I have try to put it in was my work pants. Which was a tight fit & only slid down half way. But I no longer wear those pants (due to other reasons not related to the wallet) since I got new pants for work that they fit in.*I know it's military thoughts of design & they may have needed the change holder. But I think it doesn't need it & that would of made this a bit smaller in size that could of been better.Jr: Pros:*Small size, about the size of a bi-fold wallet, maybe a just a tad bigger. But still small enough to fit into any pocket.*About 5 slots to hold cards, double it up to hold 10.*2 clear windows, one inside & one outside. Could hold more cards to make the count 10 plus of holding.*Has a deeper area, like the original for the passport, but not as deep. To hold a bit bigger items. I didn't test it out.*Has a hidden zipper like the original to hide your money/receipts in. Still plenty of room for your money on the Jr. That would be 2 areas to put money in, just like the original.*Change holder on this for all your change or small object holding needs.*Stitching on this looks stronger as well as the material it's made out of.*Life time warranty!!!Jr: Cons:*Was about the same size or just a bit smaller in bulge as my leather wallet.*The inside clear window area has a bit of trouble getting cards in & out of due to the zipper for the change pocket. Bad location for the zipper. Should of just left the change holder out.*The very top card slot also has a bit of trouble due to the seam angle in. You can get a card in there, just a tighter fit.*Outside clear window doesn't have part of the shark-bite closure system above it to help protect cards from falling out like the original. I did not test this window out to see how well it will hold. So it may hold just fine without trouble.All in all, it depends on what you need. I wanted a wallet with more room & cut down on the bulge. The Original was the one I went with. And I debated between both of them for a while. Was going to go with Jr, just cause it was smaller. But it being about the same bulge as my old wallet. That just denied it for me.Get both of them to see which one you want. Best way to do it! If you have a army/navy store near you that sale these wallets, go test them there. You can always return one or both of them to Amazon.
The best wallet I have ever used. You can fit anything I mean any number of cards in it with a option for passport. It will be yrs before I buy another wallet but will go back and get the same one!!!
Fits all my cards nicely.  The wideness makes the wallet slimmer.  Although it is large it fits all my pockets just fine.
summary: Larger wallet makes a slimmer wallet

reviewText: The picture on the website doesnt do it justice.  I am one of those guys that carries the kitchen sink in their back pocket.  I go through wallets all the time. This one has the best design and holds all my stuff where I need it and is easy to get to.  Plus it doesnt feel like I am sitting on a kitchen sink.  It is well made the way it secures itself is neat and easy to use.  I dont see a thing wrong with it.  I dont see myself wearing it out.  If I do I will be happy to get another one.

If you are looking for a larger wallet as I was, then perhaps look no further than the Spec-Ops Brand T.H.E. Wallet.  I was not necessarily looking for a wallet that would hold more, but instead looking for a wallet that would let me somewhat spread my different cards etc, around a bit therefore making the wallet thinner in profile.  This wallet does that well which makes carrying a wallet in your back pocket much more comfortable, and as an added benefit should not throw your hips out of alignment when seated on it.  I will review this again in a year to let you know how it holds up.  From first appearances though, I would say that it was made to last a very long while.
Best damn wallet ever! The construction and stitching is super durable it will last forever! But if it doesn't, it has a lifetime warranty!

I had been looking for this type of wallet for a long time to replace the one I had but could not find one big enough to hold hold all my stuff.The Spec-Ops fits the bill perfect,it won't fit the pocket in some of my Wal-Mart Chinese jeans but I don't  do anything with these other than work in the yard.I'm retired Navy so to get on a base I must show my ID and the ID window makes this very easy unless I have to take it out.Overall it is a great wallet and I am well pleased with it.Oh, one other thing,I showed it to my barber and he said he will order one.
this wallet is a little too much for every day carry. but i bought it for travel edc--hanging from my neck, right in front of my neck knife. as usual, spec ops does the quality right.
This wallet is top of the line. Well made, very large and full of compartments to hold everything. Best fit is in your side cargo pocket but fits in most rear pockets. Made in USA.
Perfect - room for everything but doesn't take up too much room.  Wish I knew about this years ago!  Definitely worth it!

My leather Savvy Caddy wallet is still in nice shape after 4 years of heavy use but since I am expected to work in all types of weather condition I needed something to stand up to the weather better, this is where the Spec Ops wallet comes in, I love the wallet except that it does not carry all my cards that my Savvy Caddy did (24) which I knew going in, it is a little wider than I expected but still do not have a problem slipping it into my rear pocket. If they come out with a model that does not have the zippered pouch for change or Misc they could add a few more pockets for cards. Do I have any regrets...NOPE!
summary: Nice and I love the ACU pattern

reviewText: First the positive, and the reason I gave it 3 stars. The quality of craftmanship is second to none, and for some, well.. It might be perfect. The negative's I see are this.. It's big, I mean really big! But oddly enough it holds the same amount of cards and stuff as my old wallet did??? Everytime I open it, the bill side ends up instinctively on the bottom (did I buy a left handed wallet, lol). And last you cannot close it with one hand, I found this out when I took the family for ice cream tonight and struggled until I finally had someone hold my ice cream just so I could close my wallet. I really wanted to like this, they do make other sizes that one probably should be considered first IMO.

I had a tough time deciding between this and the junior model but chose this as I felt I needed a little more capacity. This certainly has enough capacity as it's a big wallet - as is clearly called out in the measurements.Pros:This is a well constructed wallet - it just feels durable and looks well made. I believe this will last for many years.I love the two clear windows - especially the one on the outside. Makes showing my ID so much easier.Even big it's very light.Cons:Size - I'm a big man (6'3 350lb) and it's a snug fit in the rear pocket of my jeans and slacks. Might be a problem for people of normal stature with normal sized clothes. However, if you're typically wearing fatigue or cargo type clothes I don't think you'd have any issues.Overall I'm impressed with the quality of this wallet. If I had to do over again I'd have gone with the junior based on what I typically wear. However, I'm still keeping it for casual use and have bought a junior version to use with my normal business attire.
Great size for everything I need. Plus having two ID windows is preiceless... no more digging for my secondary ID.

This is a great wallet for the price. It holds everything I need it to, without killing my butt while its in my back pocket. The only reason I didnt give this 5 stars is that it is hard to get in and out of the back pocket of several of my pants. Jeans are ok, but slacks or work uniform pants I have to fight with it.

I always had problems with bulky wallets in my back pocket, they are uncomfortable and will occasionally even bruise my behind, but NO MORE!!  This wallet is amazingly comfortable, folds down almost flat and fits EVERYTHING!!! I occasionally have problems with a few pairs of my dress pants in getting the wallet out quickly but most are no issue and never a problem with any of the jeans I own.  When this one wears out, I will definitely buy another.

I bought it for travel to foreign countries. It has two holes for lanyards that I string to my belt for pick pockets. I got pick pocketed before and I didn't want to go through that again. It's good for airport travel. But the size is not practical for out in the town. I can only fit it my cargo pockets or back pockets of certain jeans.

Didn't really think about this when I bought it but there actually a lot of bulk just in the wallet itself maybe should have ordered the smaller version. However is very well built and holds every thing I wanted plus some just as advertised.

I absolutely love this wallet, it has all the room you could possibly need for cards passport and the two clear i.d. holders make life much easier. I've only had this wallet for a week but if it holds up as well as my last military wallet (30 years) which judging from first inspection seems possible if the shark bite can hold up as well as Velcro. This could very well be the last wallet I willever need, I might get the Jr, size as well since the full size will rise above blue jeans pockets. Would not hesitate to buy again.

It's very well put together and fits fine in most of my pants. There are a few that it is snug in, but because it's wider than my old one, when it's folded it's not as thick. It has plenty of room in it. I have all my cards in it, and 3 spare keys. I would definitely recommend this to friends and family.
summary: T.H.E. last wallet I will probably ever own

reviewText: This wallet is the best I have ever owned!  Very durable construction, flat layout of credit cards avoids  bulging, and it fits nicely in pocket.  I purchased this after my chiropractor informed me that part of my back problem was caused by sitting on a fat wallet.  He approved of this one.

My only wish is that it came in more colors.I bought this for my husband, who is in the Air Force. He doesn't like it because it is camo. I knew that he'd hate it being camo BEFORE I purchased it. However, at the time of purchase I did not realize that you could select the color by clicking different pictures. I still bought it because his wallets take a beating in his flight suit. I was sort of hoping it would be about an inch smaller? But, it still fits in the leg pockets on his flight suit.Regardless of his dislike for the size and the color, he still took it with him on deployment - mostly because I threw his old wallet away on trash day and forced him to take it. I imagine that he will grow to like it.Why am I so insistent on this? Because he destroys his wallets. He needed a new one and this one had amazing reviews on how strongly made it is. Plus - the biggest thing was the image had a picture of the coin on it, with a pocket that is PERFECT for it. Every time I opened my husbands old wallet that damn coin fell out and most often slammed my toe. Yeah, it may sound petty but those things are heavy and can hurt!Anyhow, when it got here I tested it. I did not hold back out of fear it would rip. If it ripped by me tugging it all over then it was a worthless product and he'd ruin it within a few months. I tugged at the pockets, at each bill fold area the mesh pockets. None of them even felt like they'd rip. More than enough room for receipts, credit cards, ID's, money, and this and that. I love that he can readily show both his military ID and his drivers license, since there is two clear pockets on it. He no longer has to double and triple his credit cards and other work related cards. This thing, to me, is awesome. Perhaps it is because I am a chick who LOVES a lot of pockets when I buy a purse. But I love this thing for its room, and strength.If my husband still hates this wallet after he gets back (due to the size) I will buy him a new one (Solid color this time!) and give this to a friend. If he doesn't mind the size I will just dye it black.
awesome wallet will purchase more in the future. It is huge but not as bad as I thought it might be.

My husband loved this wallet.  A friend of mine has used this wallet for about 6 years and I hope my husband will get that much use out of his. It has ample room and folds nicely.  The only drawback is the size, it is a little larger than most wallets and while it will go in all his pockets, even his dress pants, it is a little harder to get in and out of some pockets.

This wallet has everything.  The only drawback is the bill compartment opens opposite of how you normally hold the wallet and it could be made just a tad smaller overall so that its not such a tight fit in dress pants back pocket.
summary: Tight squeeze in the dress pants back pocket

reviewText: Wow, this wasn't a wallet, it was a purse.  I couldn't even fit it in my pockets, back or front!  Returned it and going to try the mini version.
summary: This isnt a wallet, its a man purse!

reviewText: Wallet arrived quickly and is high quality. Best feature is zippered cash section, allowing for separation of two currencies or cash and receipts. WIll fIt In pockets as advertIzed. Would go for Jr version of same wallet if u don't need to store passport.
While it is large it does hold all the things that would be unable to fit in a standard wallet.  Build quality is excellent.
No complaints about this item if you like keeping your things organized...this is my second one in 3 years...only wallet you will ever need.

This wallet is rugged, closes securely, opens quietly, and has seemingly limitless space for the items I carry every day. It holds my plastic cards, passes, license, and cash with room to spare. The mesh pocket fits a Fenix LD01 light and a Victorinox Cadet knife. In the long zippered pocked there's room for a small pen, some first aid items, a book of matches, breath strips and a condom. Then I ran a few feet of paracord through the loops with my keys attached, which can also fit inside the wallet when necessary.Because the wallet is longer than usual, it can hold all this and still stay relatively flat. It fits inside my front pant pockets snugly, but getting it in and out is not too difficult. I also like the coyote tan color of it. I've tried a number of wallets in the past, and this one finally lives up to my expectations.

im not gunna lie this is a big wallet and i did end up buying the JR also just cuz its smaller and fit better in jeans and shorts. i use this wallet when wearing cargo pants or putting it in my backpack. still a great product and very well made.

This Spec-Ops Brand wallet is solidly constructed, well designed, and made in the U.S.A. (As a Scot with relatives living on the faraway continent, I believe in supporting American manufacturing whenever possible.) Spec-Ops Brand has developed a unique fastening system called the "Shark-Bite", which makes opening and closing the wallet simple and reliable; and it dispenses with hook and loop closures, making it quiet, effective and novel. My wife, a tough dame who spends the greater part of her days out-of-doors in wellies and tactical gilet, simply loves her Spec-Ops wallet, which can be attached to a belt for ease of carry.
Best wallet I've ever had and probably the last.  Function galore.  Will fit it a suit pant, jacket or blue jeans.  A little tight for shorts but still works.
summary: don't let the size fool you

reviewText: Firstly, know this up front: this wallet is kind of huge. It fits fine in the back pocket of a pair of blue jeans, but if you like to carry your wallet in your front pocket, forget it. Not with this one.The wallet lives up to its sales pitch. It's tough, it's full of pockets and nooks and crannies. If you actually loaded this wallet up, you'd end up like George Castanza on Seinfeld (yadda yadda).My only real nit? Opening and closing the wallet is sometimes a bit of a pain in the butt. I've had the wallet long term now, and if it was going to soften up it would have. That's the only reason I dinged it one star. Otherwise, buy with confidence. This is a nice product.

Looking at this product now, I can see that the dimensions are, indeed, mentioned. I didn't look at the dimensions when I bought this; I thought I would be getting a standard tri-fold wallet that would easily fit in my pants pocket. If that's what you were also looking for, look elsewhere: this wallet is huge. I mean, it's approximately the size of a standard CD-ROM jewel case. It is awkward and difficult to fit in my pants pockets (any of them). I guess this wallet might work well for you if you use a purse, or if you have extremely large pockets.On the plus side, It has lots of compartments and stuff, and is made in a way that should last for years and years. I'll be selling mine.
Lots of room. It was a little bigger than I expected it to be but it was exactly as advertised. It seems to be well constructed and I'm looking forward to seeing how this holds up this year.
I've found that I often forget I'm carrying a wallet, as it is so flat.Exceeded by expectations for a wallet

The wallet is a bit larger than most, but it's perfect. It fits everything I own.  I'm hard on everything I own and this stands up to my abuse as an outdoors person.  You can literally fit about 35 cards in this wallet, coins, and much more.  Love the license or ID card display on the front.  I would recommend this to anyone.  You will love it.
summary: Best Wallet I Have Ever Owned

reviewText: I'd still be using wallet #1 but the plastic windows - especially on the outside of the billfold cracked, scratched and yellowed. This is what I call my 'airport wallet' - as my Military ID comes out of my wallet ready for TSA inspection. My drivers license easily fits inside utilizing the other pouch and plastic window.In over 10 years of use - not a single tear of fabric, loss of stiching, or failure of the sharkbite clasp to stay closed. The wallet has been crammed full of receipts, cards, both credit and business - creating a bulge large enough for multiple warnings from my chiropractor.Since back surgery - I've tried to thin the wallet - but working as a defense contractor in South Korea necessitates carrying both Dollars for on base purchases AND Won, as Korea remains a largely cash economy-and THE wallet takes it all in stride. Add to that a Korean PX/Commissary ration card, retired military ID card, 3 credit cards and a weeks worth of receipts for tax and banking purposes - and you still have room left over for challenge coins, a COSTCO card (yes there's one in Daegu) as well as pictures of the family.It's not a fashion statement - but is the most useful resource for carrying things of importance-kept at your fingertips. Never had a second of regret for the purchase.

But now I love it..  It was a bit awkward to use at first. It's bigger than my traditional trifold and when fully opened it's 12" long. I have always used a trifold wallet but they were just to thick for the back pocket. I would have to visit the Chiropractor every so often because the wallet would tilt my pelvis.. Anyway  Lots of pockets and easily accessible. I get by the 12" size by folding it in half to access the pockets.
summary: At first I wasn't sure about this wallet.

reviewText: Has pockets for all the stuff, slots for frequently used cards, could use a few more. Place for passport, folding money, airline tickets, et.al. Very nice, durable, should have had this 5 years ago. I recommend this highly.

This wallet is HUGE and I love it. Fits way more than I would ever need it to and is a great size for my pockets. If you're a smaller person and don't particularly have big pants it might be too big for your pocket however, so you'l have to carry it around some other way, which might be more of a nuisance. Built really well, I couldn't see anything damaging this wallet unless you were specifically intending to damage the thing.

The title says it all.  Bought one in Qatar in 2003, took it to Baghdad in 2004, and have used it every day since.  The most durable wallet I have ever seen or used.  Normally, I'd state that I would buy one again, but I'm not sure I'll ever need to, as tough as this one is.
summary: 9 years of daily use and still going

reviewText: tuff fits lots of things fits in most back pockets but it bothers your ass a bit wen u sitting on it for a long time like wen ur driving...O n one more thing to keep n eye on, as big as it is it can sometimes slip out of your back pocket with out u noticing.
will hold up to about any thing I can think up a lot of room to carry a bunch of stuff then some fits into my blue jeans and will use it alot

I have had this wallet for about four years and not once have I been disappointed with it. I am a truck driver and it holds all of my oversize documents. Passport medical card, and all three of my ID's. One of the best things about it is that I don't feel like a five year old with a velcro wallet. When this one finally wears out I will be looking at the checkbook version.

In a nut-shell, this wallet can hold a lot, and is very durable.  I've owned this for about 6 months now, and haven't made a scratch on it.  It will fit in any normal back pocket, too.  Other wallets I've had, holding what I hold in this wallet literally make holes in my back pockets.  That's what made me search for a wallet that was more durable, and wouldn't let my "good luck" military coin I keep in my wallet make holes in my pants...I was very fortunate, and found this. This wallet is of the same quality and has sold me on buying this until the day I die..hopefully spec-ops continues making it, it is simply the best wallet there is for the money.

reviewText: I bout one of these in the field in Iraq in 2004 it lasted damn near a decade before I had to replace it because of the plastic dried out cracked and broke other then that it didn't wear out It was still functional.
Best wallet I've ever had!I highly recommend this wallet to any man who carries more than just a driver's license and debit card.paul

had this wallet for a few weeks now, easily fits a passport several credit cards, and displays my ID nicely.pros: fits almost everything you could need. the change pocket is nice, and for how much it holds, it isn't too bigcons: can only fit one passport in there easily, if I try and fit two, its a bit too tight. this could be a downside for someone with dual citizenship, or a tourist and business passport.overall, I'd probably get it again if I had to. would reccomend, but not a full 5 star for me.

reviewText: Big enough to carry just about anything you need.  My only issue is that it doesn't fit in a couple of my jeans pockets but that is on Wrangler LOL!  Just a large wallet.  It does fit in a majority of my jeans and business suit pockets.  Great window pockets for ID and other items.

When this wallet arrived I was not impressed. It was big. Compared to my old leather bi-fold it was ugly. There was a dent in my pocket to the tune of $30.00, so it was rather pricey. I started to load it up with my credit/debit cards, I.D.s and cash and it started to look a little better to me. I had room for more cards and more cash plenty of room. Even though this Spec Ops wallet was large it fit nicely in the front pocket of my Maxpedition Remora. It actually fit well in my back pants pocket as well. I used the wallet for a couple of days and though unusual (shark bite closure) it really worked well and I enjoyed using it. The materials the T.H.E. wallet is made of seem very durable and the construction of the wallet seemed very good. I'm a little concerned about the plastic window on the outside of the wallet but several reviewers who have owned this wallet for many years said they had no problem other than yellowing so it's not much of an issue. So I am satisfied with this Spec Ops product and am relatively certain it will last a long time. But it's still ugly. :-)Update: 26June14This wallet is still serving me well. It has broken in well and the credit card pockets can easily hold four cards. As a matter of fact if I have two cards in the pocket they are too loose and can easily slide out.  The sharkbite closure is also breaking in and has become easier to use. I'm expecting many years of service. I highly recommend this product.

reviewText: I needed a new wallet and I like pockets and secret hidey places so I got this one.It's bigger than what I thought it would be.Too big for my back pocket.  I should've gotten the smaller one instead.So I keep all my stuff in it and keep it hidden in my car.

Tactical Holds Everything is what T.H.E. stands for. You know I could probably smuggle small pets in this thing.I was pretty shocked by how big this wallet really is. The Shark Bite closure takes a little getting used to when you're used to flipping a bifold wallet out like Captain Kirk flips out his communicator. Once you get used to the Shark Bite it really does not slow you down. The wallet is not as fat as my little bifold. I think that's because the cards and money you put in it are spaced out a bit more.Good wallet. Seems like it will last a while too.

reviewText: I had a leather bifold before this thing. It looked like George Costanza's wallet.I put all my stuff in here and it looked like there was nothing inside at all. Great wallet. Well made. It is a little on the large side, taking me a little time to get use to how large it is. I would definitely recommend it

This item is without a doubt a high quality wallet. As noted in other reviews, this wallet is slightly larger than normal.  It may not fit in your "skinny jeans" or other smallerpockets - but aside from that one complaint, this is a MAN'S WALLET designed to be carried for years in the worst of conditions.

This thing is amazing. It really does hold everything and if you wear cargo pants like i do it is no problem to have in your pocket. I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a wallet that holds everything.

HAVE USED THIS FOR WEEK AND STILL CANT FIGURE OUT WHY I BOUGHT IT, ITS HUGE DOSENT DO ANYTHING MY OLD WALLET COULDNT DO,ITS VERY HARD TO CLOSE AND ITS BIG!! KINDA WAS HOPING MY FIRST PURCHASE FROM SPEC OPS WOULDA WORKED OUT BETTER.PRETTY BUMMED. actually it sucks, its uselessly big and does nothing a 5 velcro wallt would do, except this ones sucks to open and close, wish i never bought it.
This is probably bigger than you realize. I often times need to put it in my leg cargo pocket because of the size. Having said that, I am glad I got it because I make use of all the slots!

First off, love the wallet.  It's literally twice as big as my old tri-fold, but it's sturdy, rugged, and definitely doesn't blend in.  It also fits my passport which is a great feature in a wallet.  I've got an insane amount of space, and even carry a little bill of rights card, some business cards, and a flash drive in it.  And some condoms, which can be hidden quite well but easily reachable.There's really only one bothersome flaw with the wallet.  On the front, with the window for my ID, in which case I use for my college ID and I keep my driver's license in the inner window--I've found that I cannot remove my ID without opening the wallet, because the closing slot is in the way of my fingers and the card.  If you could find a solution for this, perhaps having the card slide into the side, that would be excellent.Definitely a rock solid wallet.  I can understand some business men not liking a wallet like this, but for men under 30 it is superb.  Not to mention I can wear it around my neck, where people can see my ID.  :)
Everything fits inside, lots of pockets....but a bit too big for pants pockets.  Probably need sth a bit smaller for my style

I had one of the JR wallets years ago and when the I'd window finally faded so much that I couldn't use it for work anymore I had to get a new wallet. I opted for the $20 Walmart brand leather wallet that lasted about 2 years before disintegrating, a problem that I never had with these spec ops brand wallets. I did some looking around and came upon this model. Im a guy that likes to carry a small flashlight in my back pocket along side my wallet. I was able to do this no problem with the spec ops the wallet jr. I have not had the same success with the wallet, however I prefer this one. Because everything is more spread out and it fills my back pocket it's much more comfortable to sit on for long periods of time. The mesh pocket on the interior is much more durable than I expected and a great place to keep a challenge coin or spare house key without it causing any discomfort while sitting on it. International travelers can also just as comfortably store their passport in this wallet as well. Great construction and I will never buy a different wallet again.

Yes, it's big...why are you leaving low ratings? Can't you read dimensions?Anyways, this wallet is awesome. Everything you need fits inside, and then some.

This is a great wallet.  It is big, probably too big for many people (if you want a standard sized wallet, get the T.H.E. Jr.) to keep in their back pocket, but it works great in a cargo pocket.  It is crazy durable, and has the added plus of being made in the US.  I would absolutely recommend it.
I have used the wallet daily for seven years now and it still is going strong. Had no issues and shows very little wear.

This wallet is big and I can stuff a lot into it and still keep it organized. It had held up for a while now too with no serious signs of wear. It fits in most all my jeans pockets easily.
