This is my second  Spec-ops T.H.E. wallet. The first one I carried for over 10 years and it was still in great shape with exception of the zipper which finally wore out. I have probably used the zipper a million times!! That's no exaggeration as you can only imagine with 10+ years of use. I will buy another when this one wears out. Thanks Spec-ops!.
so far so good let's see how long this product last but so far I really like how I can fit almost everything inside this wallet. well worth the money thus far

This wallet sits large and flat in your pocket.  Not for people who like thicker, smaller wallets.  It does fit in my jeans and slacks.  Sticks out slightly tall in my jeans, but just barely.  It has deep money pocket and lots of slots for credit cards.  Zippered pockets are functional, but the zipper slider and pull tab form a lump in your pocket.  Velcro would have been better I think instead of zippers, or maybe a low-profile slider?  Construction quality is excellent and I expect this to last me a long time.  It says "spec-ops" with an American flag on the inside tag.

Wallet exactly as described, seems very rugged. Been using several weeks with no signs of wear; love the clasp, so simple it just works.Wallet is a little large, I have had to get a few new pairs of pants with larger pockets, but I needed the large wallet for all the stuff I carry. You might consider the Jr. if you don't want to buy new pants. I can carry it in the side cargo pockets, back pockets, or it has holes to run some para-cord through and wear it around your neck. I would buy again if needed.
Best wallet around. Holds all my stuff and then some. Is rather large. I tend to not carry my wallet on hip so size doesn't bother me

I work outside all the time in all weather needed something that closed better and this fit the bill.  Velcro always gets messed up with as dirty as I tend to get. It is larger than I expected but that isn't a bad thing it fits in the back pocket fine but it takes up the entire pocket.  I had a bit of trouble sliding it in and out at first but none now.  I kept on catching the flap  on the edge of the back pocket, but u just flip it so the flap faces you and it slides in fine.Will see how long it lasts it seems pretty sturdy, but I tend  to be hard on most anything I wear.

I got tired of my old, ragged leather wallet after several years of use and sitting-on in my fat rear pocket, so I decided to try this one out since everyone was raving about how great it is.Let me tell you... this thing is big. I'll post two pictures, so y'all can get a sense of the size difference lol.Big it may be, but it really can hold a lot. It's still thin, comparable to that of a "normal" wallet. It's more wide than anything, but it's tough, built to last, and comes with a lifetime guarantee. I'd recommend you stop waiting and go for it!
summary: Large, but beats my old leather wallet!

reviewText: i would recommend this wallet for sure.  it has room to hold more than i need to carry.  the only con is it is a bit big if you carry your wallet in your front pocket.  otherwise perfect

I can now carry everything I own in this wallet, it's kind of like that blue box on DR. Who when you open it people are like CRAP that's one BIG Wallet, I like to pretend I'm and FBI agent and I flash my ATM Card at them, LOL I love it.

This is a great wallet! If you're going to buy it just make sure to get the right size. I first got T.H.E Wallet and it was just to big to carry in a pocket. I returned it and got T.H.E Wallet Jr. and it is a much better fit. It's got plenty of room for cash, receipts, credit cards, ID's and so on.The duel windows are cool because you can put your driver's license in one and another form of I.D (Military, school, etc) in the other. I don't carry change in my wallet but if you do its got a spot for it. I'm very happy with the purchase.

I can fit a passport, vaccination record, bills (also in the nice zipper compartment for high dollar value bills), and a few cards.  Once I loaded it up though, folding it and getting it closed was a bear.  the special enclosure is great for being quit and secure, but does not lend itself well to a moderately full wallet.  plastic window arrived with black permanent marker marks on it but I just ignored them.  I can wear this around my neck with thin climbing cord, but the knots have to be outside the folded are to allow it to close.  when the change zipper is in the closed position it hits the fattest part of the rest of the wallet next to the other bill zipper location, so hopefully in future designs the reverse the zipper direction.  For belt wearing, there's no external belt band.  You have to tuck the top of the wallet up behind your belt, between two belt loops if your pants have them spread out far enough, and then fold the bottom & close the top.  When you open it to get to your bills, you may prefer to take it off your belt to work with it or you have about 10" of wallet hanging down below your belt line while you try to get things out of it.  Design could use a little work for ease of use.  Too large for normal back-pocket storage in pants.  Too large for Carhart cargo jeans side-pockets too ... so I'm restricted to neck, belt, or large cargo pockets ... or a waist pack.
summary: great workmanship .. doesn't hold as much as I'd hoped

reviewText: Sadly, I had to return it, don't listen to the others that say it fits in a standard pocket, did not fit in my pockets on my dress pants for work.  I'm out of the miltiary now but loved the "tactical" products still and the strength associated, I'm lookign at the Jr version now, but just remember for size thinking - it will fit a Passport in it without bending, And then it has about 1/4 of an inch over that size on all corners...  Rating it as a 3 because the product was great, but the size and other reviews lead me to belive it would fit fine, and it didn't.  Wallet is HUGE!
summary: Despite the other reviews, it was HUGE and did not fit in work slacks back pockets.

reviewText: What fits in this wallet is everthing you would put in a wallet and more. It will be just the thing for when I travel. But I have ordered the Jr. wallet for every day use.

Solid quality build and good design wallet, if you can call it that.  More like a card catalog that holds more than just cards. It fits into the back pocket of jeans, snugly, but is better in side cargo pant pockets.  Holds a lot of cards, cash and even coins. And the "shark-bite" clasp is very good, but it, along with the bulk of the whole, makes it all a rather large item altogether.  So full props for design and manufacture, the LxW dimensions were just more than I wanted to keep dealing with.
summary: Built like a tank, and takes the space of one

reviewText: If you need to carry a lot of cards, paper work, recipts and cards,ect., this is for you. Very well made to say the least. I mention it in my weekly planner review since it holds a small planner. Has a great closure system called the "shark bite", easy to open but stays closed.
Great wallet. Pretty much everything said positive in the other reviews is correct. Very durable, plenty of space, comfortable, zipper compartment is great.

It is hard to find a wallet that is so well built and well designed that I can't find any complaints.  This would be it.  It is built very well, holds EVERYTHING you could ever want to carry.  Most importantly, when folded and latched shut....it is flat enough to sit on comfortably.  IT DOES fit in Levi pockets just fine.  There is NO size issue with pockets.  Yes it is big but it fits in your pockets perfect.  No need for the smaller option from Spec-Ops...this one is not too big in any way. Good stuff.

Does the job. I wear 511 pants to and from work and it fits rear pocket perfectly, however it's definitely to big for casual use. Will purchase a micro-wallet for dress clothes and such. But this holds everything I need in a far superior fashion. Organization of necessities is great.
While it does fit in most of my pockets, do not trust the closure when wearing on a belt or neck strap.Extremely disappointed.

My old wallet was falling apart.  I wanted something that could hold credit cards and cash without become overly bulky. This did the trick.  It is a little larger than a standard wallet which allows me to carry a spare key, a passport, some blank checks, paper cash.  I carry it in my front pocket with the tab up and I am able to reach in, open it, and retrieve a key card without ever taking it out of my pocket.  The closure which consists of a rigid tab with a loop of webbing fits into a pocket when closed.  I stays secure. I have yet to have the wallet open.  With my old wallet, I was always have stuff fall out.  This wallet is exactly what I needed.
Got this from my brother for work we thought it where going to break easily but it's still going yheay

I wear a size 10-D sneaker and shoe. At the advice of the manufacturer, I ordered size medium overboot, which is supposed to fit shoe sizes 9 and 10. Unfortunately, I can barely get my shoes into them, mainly because the oveshoe is not wide enough inside. It's a frustrating struggle to get them on and off. The length is perfect, but I hesitate to order the next larger size because it might be too long and interfere with my operation of the brake and gas pedals of my car. I'll probably wind up giving them away to a friend or family member with a smaller shoe size. I'm afraid I am very disappointed with this purchase.
summary: A struggle to get on and off my shoes

reviewText: These Honeywell shoes fit well...nice quality overboot. I have used them a few times and am very happy with this transaction and would recommend to any ofmy friends. Great price...

I bought these shoes for my husband.  He works in a resturant and his feet would get wet but he needed non-slip also.  These work great!  He wears them everytime he goes to work over his gym shoes and comes home with dry feet.  After a while the non-slip wears off but he just tosses the old ones and puts on a new pair and off he goes.  He loves them and others at work have asked where to get them.  Very good value.  I reccomend these highly.
I ordered these to replace the pair I have had for around eight years. The picture shows Ranger made in USA. The pair I received were Servis made in China. Sent back.
summary: Another great product sent to China to be made.

reviewText: I bought my Freestyle Shark 2.0 in Florida in 2009. I work in the Baseball industry so I use it a lot. This is a great watch that looks sporty and classic at the same time. My only concern is the P/U band. After several years wearing it, one day it just broke and it is understandable. My problem is not the fact that it broke, is that when I went online it is almost impossible to find the exact replacement and also, the price of the band replacements is almost 20% of the total value of the watch.I have a Technomarine which is a way more expensive watch and the band replacements are easy to be found plus the price is not as high as Freestyle. I recommend this watch but keep in mind that fun with it might come to an end two or three years down the road.
A great watch. Good value for money. Rugged and accute. Simple to set and looks good. Was delievered fast and well packaged. Very happy and highly recommend.
I absolutely love these shoes.  They give me great foot support and are light weight.  Plus, they just look cool.  I may order a second pair for when my current pair wear out.

Good overall shoe for the money, does run about 1/4 size small in my experience. I found it to be light weight and durable, I hate that show companies just change or create new shoes each year, so long as it a notable improvement of the last years model.

I have owned a Dynamic chainless bike for about three years and I decided to try Sonoma's chainless women's bike for my girlfriend.  On the plus side it is about two-hundred dollars less than Dynamic's and it rides nice enough.  On the negative side, it is a little heavier than Dynamic's and Sonoma uses poor quality parts.  Like the brake handles and cables are very cheap and of poor quality.  The large bearing at the top of the fork is rough and it was originally so tight that it was difficult to turn the wheel.  I had to re-adjust it.  The gear shift cable needed to be adjusted in order to get the gears to shift smoothly and there wasn't any grease on the drive gear at the back wheel.  The tube in the front tire was pinched between the wheel and the tire, putting a big hole in it.  Had to replace the tube.  I don't know yet how well the bike will hold up, since I just got it all together today.  I really like the chainless drive system, but the rest of the bike is nothing special and in fact looks and feels rather cheap.  For the price I would expect better quality control and better quality parts.  So I think that the most I can give it is 3 stars.  It is chainless and rides nice, but it is of poor quality and may not hold up.

Be careful how you use the FiveTen Savant!  This boot was suppose to be a companion to the 5.10 Canyoneer boot.  That is definitely NOT the case!  After only a half dozen Class III slot canyons, the stitching securing the rubber toe piece, on both boots, blew out.  It didn't just give way...the stitching actually disappeared, leaving the toe piece unsecured on both sides of the boot.  The Savant would probably make an OK trail boot, but it definitely does not belong in technical slot canyons.

I bought these for their stability, durability, and traction during parkour/freerunning.  Wall runs, tic-tacs, etc rip shoes apart!  I destroyed one regular pair of running shoes & decided I'd needed something better.Traction: The soles on these have been amazing...after nearly 2 years of abuse, they still have tread.  The rubber is quite sticky, especially after being wet.  It picks up dust quickly and loses some of it's grip, but most grippy rubber soles do the same thing.  Painted metal surfaces are hit or miss in regard to traction too.  My biggest concern with these is that they leave black marks on some surfaces.  This limited where I, with a clear conscience, could practice parkour.Stability:  They've felt stable everywhere I've taken them...all the odd angles your feet can be in as a traceur.  And, on a mega-hiking trip over varied terrain.Durability:  The light gray material is very thin (breathable, but weak).  The dark gray material provides consistent fit & performance, but I've worn holes in the light gray material.  It isn't a real complaint considering all that I've put these things through.  Besides frequent freerunning, I used them for a 26hr hiking trip to the summit of the Mount of the Holy Cross in Colorado, then around Halo Ridge & back down to camp with full packs ... dirt trails, stream crossings, boulder fields, scree fields, snow fields.  They performed well, but show signs of being an 'approach shoe', and not a full-scale 'hiking shoe'.

Alright, I had the version prior to this.  Nonetheless, I'm just now buying another pair after 3 years of intense wear.  I'm an avid freerunner and cave spelunker so these things see everything under the sun.  I did a 5K mud run in them after 3 years on top of everything else... and they survived!  They are literally starting to fall apart so it's time for a new pair.  $100 shoe that last for over 3 years... you make the call.

I am really happy with the five ten savant, the fit is great, it laces up nice without any stress points in the laces and it breathes well, keeping my feet comfortable through the day.  I bought the shoe for the gym, and for exercising in general, especially walking and it has been very comfortable.  The sole has lots of grip, trailrunners would do well in this shoe, however my only complaint is that the sole does mark surfaces, any wet areas on a tile floor, or wood floor will get black marks from the shoe.  This however is the compromise for the high grip factor the sole gives on any surface.  I have purchased other shoes from five ten and they all fit and hold up very well, definately recommend them to anyone needing a good all round shoe for the gym or the trail.

Great fit and support for most hikes, scrambles, and canyoneering. The tread sticks like glue to surfaces. So much so that if you are used to anticipating a slide or giving way with your shoes you have to adjust your step because this shoe grabs, especially on slick rock like we have here on the Colorado Plateau. Wore them once and immediately ordered a second pair.
summary: Simply put, this shoe Kicks A**!

reviewText: I ordered a half size larger because that's all that was available, thinking I could wear thicker socks to make up for the larger size.  I'm glad I got the larger size because they fit like a glove.  They actually fit too snugly across the ball of my foot where I have a small bunion.  I hope they stretch out a little.  I recommend ordering a larger size, and if you have bunion issues, don't buy this boot.  The quality and workmanship are excellent.  They'll keep my feet warm and dry.

Pajar are the perfect winter boots for real Montreal winters! Superior warmth, quality, workmanship. Great fit. The red version is really fun. And above all, you can't beat this price: less than 70$ for Pajar boot is simply unheard of!

While searching for a holder for my hair dryer, I had to be mindful of the size of the opening. This model holds my salon sized FHI nano hair-dryer perfectly. The dryer does not try to fall out and the nozzle fits through the opening with room to spare. It was easy to install and came with all the hardward necessary including the wall-drill type wall anchors. You can arrange the holder to lean left or right before tightening the screw. Note: you will need an "eye-glasses" sized flat screw-driver to tighten the screw completely.  Overall, I'm very pleased with this holder and highly recommend it.

The holder looks great. However, the anchors that were sent to hang the older are to big to be placed side by side. The bad part is that I knew better then to use the anchors, but I wanted to hang it so I went ahead and tried. Well guess what now I have to fix a nice hole in the wall. Furthermore, the screws that were sent did not have a deep enough hole to place my screwdriver in them (this is a first for me). So I ended up going and buying smaller anchors and screws to go with them, Once I did this everything else was fine. I just don't like fixing holes in the wall.
summary: gave improper tools to hang holder

reviewText: The workmanship on the hair dryer holder is a bit rough in places. In particular the casting of the hooks on the back of the unit that secure over the mounting cleat aren't quite straight, so it wants to swivel on the wall.An improvement would be a rubber ring over the top, because being steel it scratches the hair dryer.

This a really nice, heavy-duty piece but unfortunately it was too small for the barrel of my hairdryer. I had to return it but I would recommend it to others as long as you measure the diameter of your hairdryer barrel first.

All you need to do is make sure to measure the hair dryer you plan on using to make sure it will fit properly.I did and ordered this since I wanted the stainless steel/brushed nickel look.  It is very secure with two hidden mounting screws concealed with the standard set screw feature used on other bathroom fixtures.May cost more than others, but looks as good as I thought it would in our bathroom.
summary: Works like a charm and my wife loves it!

reviewText: I was trying to find a good hair dryer holder so I could keep it handy, but off of the counter.  This product exceeded my expectations!  Wish I had found it earlier.  It's compact and fits in a small spot and my hair dryer fit perfectly.  A great organizer.
It does the job, what can you say, it's a holder. Easy to install, very handy. Wife's hair dryer fits

If you are like us and your bath room is designed to be functional but a with a slimmer of elegance then this is for you. My wife and I have a small master bath and every morning having to wrap and unwrap and putting away the hair dryer was a pain. So you dont do it and end up layng the dryer plugged in on the sink or on the toilet tank (not very safe either). This holder solves our problem allowing us to mount the dryer in the corner, plugged in and tucked away like it was meant to be.Great Product!
summary: Great piece for the working bathroom

reviewText: Doesn't quite fit flush to the wall but appears sturdy enough to hold up just fine.  I only found one small blemish/scratch in the materials.  I use it by placing the handle of the hairdryer into the holder which is working out great.

The holder came with 2 sinkers and easily installed into the wall.  It is very sturdy, and the hair dryer can be inserted in either of two positions (with the handle slid into the unit or the top slid into the unit).  It works very well and has reduced the clutter on our counter top.  I definitely recommend it.

Great design.  Modern Look.  Holds my wives hair dryer and keeps it out of the way.  Great for a small bathroom.  One small criticism would be the mounting screws.  The plastic things you stick in the wall and then screw in the screw into are cheap.  Had to use a different type which worked much better.

This is the perfect solution to putting your hair dryer in the closet. It was simple to install and the unit can fit in the holder either handle first or as shown in the picture. The only thing missing with this item is a training manual to get my wife to use it.
I Love it!  My hair dryer is no longer on the counter, or under the sink with the cord all over.  The sleek design looks like it is part of the bathroom with a purpose! .Stylish and sleek!

This hair dryer holder just isn't made very well.  The welding that secures the C-shape to the wall bracket failed after a year of use.  And, as another reviewer mentioned, the metal edges of the holder are rough, so over time they've badly scratched the finish of my hair dryer.Bottom line: unless you like shoddy workmanship and want to give your hair dryer that "lived-in" look, avoid this product...
summary: Poorly made, broke after a year

reviewText: I wanted something that could hold my hot hair dryer to save counter space, and this does the job. It was super easy to install, and works like a charm. I think my hair dryer is a pretty standard size, so unless your dryer is abnormally shaped or sized it will probably be fine. I even tilted it on the was so its more like a holster, and I can even put my hair dryer in it when its still running if I need 2 hands for a moment. No more worrying about getting electrocuted by dropping my dryer in the sink! :)

I purchased this item recently to reduce some of the clutter on my bathroom countertop.  It works very well.  The hairdryer fits in it very securely and the opening allows it to be used in different ways.  It fastens to the wall easily and securely.

Because of the cord and size of my hair dryer, it is always in the way. I can leave it on the counter or, to save space, stick it in a cabinet where it will take up too much space and be inconvenient.This hair dryer holder solves the problem. In my case, it fits between the counter and toilet. Either the handle or the nozzle goes into the holder and the dryer is out of the way, but handy when I need it. The cord can stay plugged into the wall. Also, the stainless steel finish matches the nickel color on my faucets.There are two reasons this didn't get the fifth star: First, the edges are hard--not really sharp, but if I'm not careful, I can scratch the hair dryer putting it in (big deal--it's a hair dryer). Second, and more important, the screw holes in the holder are too close together. The anchors that hold it in are too close and it doesn't feel real secure yet. I will probably end up having to put different anchors in or relocate it to screw it to a stud.Overall, this is definitely an item that I am glad that I got. I just am not sure why I didn't do it years ago.
worked just as I needed.  kinda wish I had a place to hang the brush next to it.  I like it very well.
Good product. Easy to install. 4/5 because it will scuff up the hair dryer pretty bad. If that's something you care about buy something else.
All was as promised and on time. Unit looks good, of quality and fits my hairdryer perfectly ... finally, it's out of the way :)  I would definitely recommend this friend and family.
I've looked at a lot of different kinds and decided on this one. GLAD I did. It's perfect. It's so handy and simply stylish. Choose this one!
Easy setup. Works great, but edges are a bit sharp, Could use a clear plastic liner along the rim and vertical edges.

This would definitely work with just about ANY hair dryer. The opening is BIG and it will hold either the nozzle OR the handle, whichever way you want to place it. I like that I could have mounted it at a 45 degree angle so it wouldn't be straight up and down, makes it easier to use. But upon receiving it and visually trying to place it on the wall, still in the packaging, it's not what I want in our bath so am returning. Will keep looking for something that works and will look good when it's empty on the wall (hairdryer in cabinet) when guests use the bathroom during visits. This one looks like a brushed steel soda can with both ends removed and a big area of it missing on the side.
summary: Nice, but not exactly what I was looking for

reviewText: I have been looking for a solution to hold my hair dryer and keep it out of the way.  This holder is built solid and looks great.  It anchors to the wall very strongly.  It also keeps the hairdryer from making contact with the wall.  This is important because if you use the normal hooks that you would hang the handle loop on, the dryer tends to scrape and drag against the wall and mark it up.  With this holder, the dryer quickly slips into it and keeps off the wall.
Great product, great price. This does a great job of keeping the hair dryer accessible, but not on the bathroom sink counter. Several option on how you choose to hang your dryer in it.
Beware, this holder is not designed for all hair dryers. This holder has unfinished edges which causes damage to the hair dryer plastic casing for types that get bigger near the handle.
summary: Not made for all hair dryers

reviewText: The welds on this item failed as soon as I mounted it on the wall. I didn't even have a chance to insert my hair dryer before the tube fell off the wall connection!

The cuffs of these booties are very oddly sized. My daughter wears a size 3 1/2 shoe and the cuffs on both the size Large and Extra Large are too narrow for her to get her feet into. Quality looks very nice but I would only recommend them for kids with very narrow feet.
summary: Only for kids with narrow feet!

reviewText: Hi All, this watch is amazing, good quality in materials, nice design and resistance, I recommend 100 %, I'm using it during my swimming practice

This watch looks great (the yellow/black one, at least), and it is built well.  I bought it because I needed a watch that would hold up to outdoor activities including in bad weather, and it works fine for that.  Plus, the large (analog) watch arms make it easy to see the time at a glance.But in other ways, the watch is disappointing.The digital display is very hard to read, plus it is partially covered by the watch arms.  So, any functions that rely on the digital display - stopwatch, alarm clock, timer - are less useful.On the plus side, it's fairly easy to read the digital display in the dark when you push a button that turns on the backlight for a few moments.  (The digital display is still partly covered by the watch arms, though.)Setting the various functions is not at all intuitive and requires reading the manual, which of course is tiny with many folds and comes in about 12 different languages.  On a bicycling trip in Alaska last week, somehow I accidentally activated the alarm, which by default is set to midnight.  At midnight, the watch started beeping, waking me and my roommate from a much needed sleep.  I got it to stop beeping, but the next day I couldn't figure out how to turn off the alarm, because I didn't have the manual with me.  After a few minutes of trying different combinations of the four buttons, I turned off the alarm.I might return it for these reasons, or I might keep it.  I don't really need any of advanced functions, the time is easy to read even at a glance, it seems very weatherproof, and (revealing how superficial I am) I like the way it looks.But for you, it would probably be worth looking for a different watch, unless all you want to do is tell time and look good while exercising/hiking/cycling.
Watch appeared to be almost new in the box. Was advertised as 'New' but had obviously been slightly used. Still, for about 1/5 the retail price it's an absolute steal.
I switch the metal strap due to the strap is hard on my wrist. I ended up spending more money.
But it was very light and low quality metal.  I didn't really wear it all that much.  It was very loose and felt like I would break it super easily.

I had steel toe boots (texas steer) I've been wearing to work for about 4 years and still going strong. The soles were worn and I decided I needed some new ones to keep my feet from getting sore from daily use. I bought these Trex footbed and the change was like night and day. The soles fit perfectly (my shoes were a bit bigger than my feet) into the boots and it's so comfortable. It feels like walking on air. I can tell from the construction that these will last unlike the gel ones.
summary: Feels like walking on a cloud.

reviewText: Looks really cheap for $100.00 price tag.  Got for a gift and was completely embarrassed.  Some parts appears, looks and feels like plastic.  Pretty sure gold around dial is.  That's what I mean by cheap looking for the money.  Never buy this product!!!!!
summary: cheap looking for so much money

reviewText: it meet my expesctioonsit is very georgeous watch an i would by it againi would recamend it to my friends

reviewerName: B. WILLIAMS "B WILLIAMS LOOKING FOR LIGHT"
reviewText: ...GREAT PRODUCT...  These fit well and are very well made. I have a backyard that floods when we have extra heavy downpours, so these are perfect for making the rounds. Thanks for the Great price Amazon and Baffin, for a very nice product.
Was just what my husband wanted for working. in the mud and chasing those duck and goose decoys.  He likes that he does not need to wear shoes in them.
Arrived quickly, fit correctly and seem to be of excellent quality.  Only time will tell how they hold up.  I live on 12 acres and use boots a lot.

Bought these for outside gardening work and metal detecting.  Fit is slightly loose but heavy socks fix that fine.  Extremely well made and durable.  The price is very reasonable.  I have compared these to more expensive boots from other makers and these are every bit as good.
summary: Great Boot at a Fair Price

reviewText: Great boot.  The heel should definitely last longer than the comparables.  Metal toe is a plus.  Order a size larger for a wider foot.
I bought these boots for my son and he loved them.  My husband has a pair also.  They work great for working outdoors or even walking the dog on a wet morning.  Slip them on and off you go.
Top quality. These are genuine work boots, heavy duty and roomy. I gave them as a gift to my nephew, whose feet are huge. He likes them!

Excellent quality boots. Unfortunately, people who have to wear these boots are hard working stiffs and we usually have wider feet just like we have bigger hands and banana fingers!I spoke to Baffin in Canada and was told this is what the US market demands like their US customers Amazon.com and affiliate Endless.com and they don't make them wider. I checked out many sites for other brands. Nothing comes close to the quality or price. Most other brands are also regular "M" width!LaCross boots are generally wider, but the quality is so bad that every pair I ever owned has split open after a few months of use.Be careful ordering Baffins as they come in B series "M" wide which is even narrower than the D series "M" wide. I love them though!I discovered my right big toe was always wet and found out the right-foot boot leaks at the toe, but having had them for several months, can't return them.
summary: Top quality rubber and build- too narrow for the working man's feet

reviewText: Great boot. Great fit. Made in Canada. Quite a few of these rubber boot manufacturers sent operations over to China. Nope, I am not buying their junk. Baffin has a Great product and rubber boot product line. I'd say middle of the road as far as pricing.
great boot mine came with steel toes but was not in the description built well they should last a while
Not all rubber boots are alike. These are well made and comfortable. I own a pair of Baffin snow boots and love them, don't know why I didn't buy these sooner.

I love Baffin boots.  They are made in Canada, and the ones I have had before fit well and wear like iron.  I bought these boots for barn use, thinking the steel toe would protect me from cattle stepping on my foot and the steel shanks would protect from errant nails. reviewText: So far I've used this on just one winter backpacking trip, and a few times around the apartment.Pros:- Very warm. Lots of insulation, and the cord locks seal in even more heat if you need to, and keep out snow etc. The fact that no snow melted or froze on these shows how well it kept the heat in.- Fabric seems fairly durable (but not the stitching), and water resistant. I walked around in the snow a lot around my campsite, and these were fine. The 'Polar Proven' writing on the sole wears off immediately, but that has no effect on the usability of the product- lightweight- Vegan (most booties are made with down)Cons:- Stitching came loose after a few days! at the front of the toes, right wear the front of the sole meets the bottom of the black reinforcing nylon. Haven't noticed seam tears elsewhere yet, but have seen a few loose threads.- Not compressible. I packed these in a compression sack for a day, but the soles are stiff and so these don't compress much.- Writing on the sole comes off and can get on your stuff- after a few hours in an expensive sil-nylon stuff sack, that sack now has the 'Polar Proven' writing permanently marked all over it, kinda like an iron-on pattern. It doesn't bother me that much, just adds character to my gear, but that writing is just silly and they should get rid of it or make it last longer. I don't think it had any effect on traction when it was there anyway.Note on sizing: I wear a men's 11 - 11.5, and got a large, and found these slightly short. Definitely wearable, but tight in the toes. So I'd recommend a larger size.Bottom line, if these would hold up better, they'd be great. Eventually I will get around to having the damaged sole repaired, or do it myself, but it might be tricky to sew because of the location of the tear. Currently, they are still usable despite the damage, but I haven't used them much. If you get these, realize that repairing these will be necessary and inevitable, and soon after you start using them. As it is, there are few vegan booty options out there, and these are inexpensive, so as long as you're okay with the inevitable repairs, you'll probably like them.
summary: Very Warm & Cozy but Not Durable at all!

reviewText: These are OK but cheaply manufactured.  Their quality control in basically non-existent  as mine arrived and were missing the squeeze clips to tighten the ankle and the top snow cuff..... on BOTH booties.  I would have returned them except that I save clips, straps and accessories from old gear and used old clips to make my booties workableThe sole is very thin compared to other brands and it is my guess that cold will find it's way in thru the sole.These will make an adequate pair of slippers/booties around the house but for camping I will go with higher end products.

Someone else said that  XXL fits size 10.  My feet are 12EEE and the XXXXL fit just right.  A pair of the regular booties in XXXL were too tight until I broke them in.
I am using them in my dry cabin and I LOVE them! Warm but not to the point your feet are sweating, comfortable, and holding to your ankles/feet. Perfect!

I own the Baffin Cush slippers for over a year now and it no longer warms my feet. I ordered these boots as an upgrade and hoping for high marks. Unfortunately this is not the case.I agree with other reviewer's comments about the soles. The grip they designed for the soles are the words Polar Proven written in a grey rubber. The picture shows a portion of it. These rubbed off the moment I started walking around on our hard wood floors. I have the laminate type floors if it makes a difference but just after a few days of use, 80% of all the grip was gone and I can make out a pattern of my foot. Not fun cleaning up the tiny rubber specs.After the grip wears off in 3 days the sole becomes very slippery, I wish I had a bigger kitchen, I can use these to act like I'm skating. Once the grip is gone, these are excellent for practicing your moonwalks. I've got pretty good at it.After a week of use, I was putting on the left one by holding the cuff with one hand like normal, I put in my foot in and rip! the top nylon cuff that holds the drawstring rips off halfway as if it wasn't sewn good. The cuff on right boot was solid.The bootie does get high marks for warmth as expected for a full insulated bootie. But with the large rip defect and no grip, back they go.Thanks to Amazon's fantastic return policy, I packed it up, UPS picked it up and I'm on Amazon looking at other brands now. Moonwalking skill increased take note.

They aren't the most stylish looking things in the world, but who cares when it's -40 out?  I'm not a fashionista anyway!This product is lightweight and I have taken them out camping. reviewText: Dunno why they play so coy with the sizing on amazon, but here's what the label on the product says:MENS;L - 7/8XL - 9/10XXL - 11/123XL - 13/11 (I'm guessing they probably meant 13/14 but that's what it says...)WOMENS;S - 5/6M - 7/8L - 9/10XL - 11YOUTHS;YS - 10/11YM - 12/13YL - 1/2S - 3/4M - 5/6I have 9.5 so I got the XL.  There's the physical SENSATION of having no room, but if I actually push my heel back into it, I have a normal amount of wiggle room for a 9.5 shoe.  By virtue of the materials and how it is built, your foot, unlike with a laced-up rigid shoe, migrates to the center of the boot and the cushy material expands to fill all gaps - probably not a bad thing if you want something that will be form-fitting to your foot anyway but if you think that sensation of being in contact with the boot on all sides of your foot might bug you, you might go a size larger.  I imagine if you just sit with your feet up on a coffee table or something reading a book for awhile it will compress the insulation in the back of the heel enough to give the toes a little more wiggle room.  In fairness to the manufacturer, the lower of the two drawstrings appears to be an attempt at a solution to the problem as well - tightening it will pull your foot back towards the heel and give your toes a little more room.  I'd say that all by itself is about a 50% solution for people who dislike the encased feeling on their toes.As far as the rubber stuff on the bottom goes - looks real attractive in its brand new state.  From the other reviews, sounds like it is going to wear off pretty quickly.  One word of advice here folks - SHOE GOO IS YOUR FRIEND.  You ought to have a tube in your junk drawer.  If not, go get some.  Now!  Are you the type that also has no duct tape or wd40 in the house?  What were you thinking!?!?  Rectify the situation ASAP...  Or order it with these booties.  I have some old running shoes that literally fell apart that I glued back together and while they're now just shoes I quickly pull on to grab the paper, go to the mailbox, etc they are definitely not coming apart again in my lifetime.  If you start to see fraying on these booties - shoe goo the stitching areas.  If you start to lose traction, you could shoe goo the entire sole - which would also waterproof it.  If you plan to go this route, lay up a supply of tongue depressors and toothpicks for application before you start - you'll see what I mean.So shoe goo is going to be my future traction solution - either that or maybe the stick-on stuff they sell at the hardware store for ladder rungs, icy steps and the like.  Or maybe the stick-on stuff used to provide traction in bathtubs.  Basically it should not be hard for those of us with hardwood floors to find ways & means of not cracking our skulls.I could see how the sole could compress down over time and you'd end up wanting to replace these... and at around $35 per pair why not, but one other way to go would be to add an insulated insole.  If you want to go really crazy, hilariously enough, I ran across a product here on amazon - heated insoles with a remote controller keychain fob.  I'm not ready for that level of awesomeness yet - but maybe later...I spend a lot of time working in front of a computer in my basement which has tile flooring, so these boots are great for the winter if you like to keep your thermostat down.  I haven't had a chance to take them camping yet, but keeping feet warm in a mummy bag always was a problem for me - I came up with a solution, which was: polypro sock liner, wool sock, huge wool sock, but I could see these booties being an even better solution.  For anyone who gets cold in their mummy bag - you may also want to look into expedition-weight long underwear.  I found some thick polypropylene uppers and lowers awhile back that are super toasty.  Personally I prefer a subpar sleeping bag while wearing warm clothing to an awesome sleeping bag - if you have to get up in the middle of the night or when you get up in the morning, you're still wearing half your insulation.  So in my opinion it's better to upgrade your clothing layers before upgrading your sleeping bag.  Just my two cents.  It's pretty cool these booties have a reasonably tough sole so I won't have to screw around with hunting around in the dark for my boots, pulling off socks, stuffing my feet into a cold pair of boots, and lacing up if nature calls in the middle of the night.  Clearly, too onerous of a task when out there roughing it!  Camping is all about maintaining the highest possible level of comfort, am I right?...but anyway, supercool product.  Dunno why anyone uses normal house slippers when these moonboot thingys are available.  4 instead of 5 stars due to the issue with the manufacturer's rubber material on the soles.  However a little time and a few dollars (a tube of shoe goo is maybe $3) you can soup it up into an even nicer product without too much trouble.  Considering there are other booties out there for $75 or more, doing the extra touches yourself isn't too awful a prospect, so I chose this product over the more expensive (possibly slightly better engineered?) products.
summary: A slightly flawed easily upgraded supercool product

reviewText: I LOVE these booties (and theBaffin Unisex Cush Insulated Slippers).  I got the Cush slippers last year in November and just ordered these as the soles to the Cush slippers are just starting to wear thin (although there's still a few months of life left for sure, the new ones are more to augment the old ones).They are similar to the Cush but are a taller, more adjustable, warmer and with a much thicker sole (this is good and bad.  Not quite as comfy in the house but much better insulation from the cold ground). Both are ubber comfy and very warm.  If you're going to be using them in a house that is fully/mostly carpeted I would recommend the Cush slippers, if you're going to want light use outside or for camping, or on all hardwood or other hard and colder flooring surface I would recommend the base camp booties.By the time the Cush are completely worn out they would have given me a over a year of use in a house with a mix of (some) hard wood and (mostly) carpet plus many trips out to the car and around the corner to the mailbox.  The exterior sole material on the base camp booties is the same as the cush from what I can tell, but there's an additional layer of firmer insulation in the sole of the base camp booties.  I expect these booties to last a good 18-24 months.  That may not seem like a long time but it's worth it - less toughness, more comfort.I usedKiwi Camp Dry, Heavy Duty Water Repellenton the Cush slippers and that did a great job of waterproofing them.  Not to the point where you can walk in puddles but but when I had to run outside in the snow it kept my feet dry (although the Cush slippers were, um, very slippery in the snow.  Almost ate it a few times).  I'm going to waterproof these base camp booties and I'm thinking they'll even be suitable for treading through small puddles due to the much thicker soles. I'll post back on this one.  It is summer and I don't think I'll have a lot of opportunity to use these just yet.  I bought them now because they're about $8 less than they were in the winter time.  We're going camping in a couple weeks so I report back on how they performed in the field.Like the Cush slippers, these booties run a little small (although not as much as the Cush slippers). I've had my Suunto Core Regular Black for over six months, having purchased it used from an eBay auction in June 2013.  I am a watch fanatic, and I was impressed by the Core's large digital display, so, when I found a good deal, I snatched it up.  Although the Core is a fantastic watch for all its functions, as I work in law enforcement, on patrol, I need a watch that does some things that the Core does not.  Here is my critique of the Suunto Core, positive and otherwise, with respect to its use as a duty watch, after my having worn it exclusively for the last six months.The Suunto Core is a large watch, with a 50mm diameter, and it has a very uncluttered display, with a lot of empty space.  It is appealing to look at and definitely exudes a tough, cool character.  After six months of wearing it, I have yet to scratch the crystal or rub off more than a few tiny dots on the outside edges of the bezel.  This is a rugged watch.  It looks like a cop watch and probably draws the same kind of attention that my cargo pants do when I wear either off-duty.All watch bands should be as nice as the Suunto Core's.  The silicone band blends with the watch nicely, and the five serrations on both sides of the band have a gentle curve that compliments the curvature of the bezel.  The buckle is excellent, with rounded edges and a tongue that is 1 cm wide and snuggles into the frame effortlessly.  The holes in the band are perfectly spaced, and the retention band for the strap has a small tooth that snaps into place, securely preventing the strap from coming loose, something that I have yet to see on any other watch band.  The band is quite soft, especially in comparison to Casio bands, and it hugs my wrist snugly without being uncomfortable, restraining the watch from twisting out of position on my wrist.In daylight and indoors, the Core's digital display is the easiest to read of any digital watch I own, and that includes Casio G-Shocks and Pathfinders.  The time display numerals at 1 cm are nearly twice as big as those on my Casio Pathfinder (6mm).  Even at an extreme angle, where the LCD turns from its light grey background to the purple-green haze, it's very easy to read the time.  At night, as long as there is just a little bit of ambient light, such as vehicle headlights, overhead street light, or a full moon, the display can be read a lot more easily than my Casio's.That being said, it makes me wonder why Suunto could not develop a decent electroluminescent (EL) display, as it is a pale, dim green, which makes it difficult to read quickly.  Casio backlights are far superior to Suunto's in terms of brightness and color.  Even in a well-lit indoor room, I can see the Casio's green glow and read the display still; on the Suunto, I will not see the EL at all, and the digital numerals will be washed out, which is odd.  The Suunto Core also lacks an automated electroluminescent function, so I have to push a button in order to light up the face, rather than have it automatically activate as I roll my wrist over in the natural motion of viewing a wristwatch.Although I have yet to replace the battery, I know the Core is energy hungry, which may be why the time needs to be corrected regularly, once a month.  I don't think a digital watch should be off by an entire minute after sixty days, but my Suunto is.  I was spoiled by my Casios that received an atomic clock signal from Fort Collins, Colorado, but even my Casio Pathfinder that does not have this function is only off by mere seconds every year.  Luckily, replacing a CR2032 on the Suunto is an easy task.The Suunto will display time in hours and minutes, but does not allow for a 24-hour time readout.  Also, if I want seconds displayed as numerals, then the date will not be displayed, as these functions use the same line on the LCD.  There is a digital second hand, but it turns off after a few minutes and needs to be reactivated by pushing the light button, which is irritating.  Since I often need to get time in hours, minutes, and seconds at a moment's glance on duty, this is a dealbreaker for me.I like the myriad functions Suunto has programmed into the Core, such as the sunrise-sunset predictor, the superbly accurate altimeter and barometer, and the large compass display, but I rarely use them.  Suunto wasn't trying to make a military or law enforcement watch with the Core.  While I can recommend the Suunto Core in general as an excellent, rugged digital watch, I would not use it on-duty because of the shortcomings I've listed.
summary: Superb Watch But Not the Best Choice for Law Enforcement Use

I've owned many fine watches, including names such as Breitling, Raymond Weil, Longines Valjoux and others. I've also owned many "sports" watches. All things considered, the Suunto Core is at the top of my list!  Talk about bang for the buck!  It's not the fanciest and certainly not the most expensive, but there's just something about it that screams cool!The first thing I noticed when taking it out of the box was its size.  The overall diameter of the watch is around 2 inches. The display area (face) is just over 1  inches.  Although this seems large, it doesn't feel that way on my wrist.  In fact, it's one of the most comfortable watches I've owned. The case back is rounded at the edges so it doesn't bite into your wrist.  It's also very lightweight. You hardly know you're wearing it.The next thing that struck me was how clean and well laid out the display looked. The characters are sharp and easy to read.  Unlike some other similar watches, there's no clutter or unnecessary foolishness.  The designers made excellent use of the available screen real estate.The watch provides many auxiliary functions, including various timers and alarms, barometric and altitude displays, time and date, plus sunrise - sunset information and a compass function.  You can change the units of display, language, backlight function and a host of other options. One of the things that really set this watch apart from it competitors is how easy it is to program.  It's menu driven and so intuitive that you hardly have read the instructions, which by the way, are relatively easy to understand.  Not perfect, but better than most.  As a bonus, You Tube contains a wealth of instructional videos for the Suunto Core watches, so if you learn better by demonstration, then this is a great option.I just purchased this watch, so I can't speak to its long-term reliability, but I have found all of the functions seem to work as advertised.  Considering its relatively modest cost, I'm actually amazed how well this watch performs!Looking through various reviews on this site and others, the main complaint seems to be that the altitude / barometer functions drift and require frequent recalibration.  This has not been my experience and in many cases, I think points to a basic misunderstanding of how barometric altimeters work. In fact, because Suunto allows you to lock the barometer or altitude settings, this watch is way ahead of the competition if dead on MSL pressure or altitude readings are important to you.  (It's actually my opinion that trends are more important, but that's beyond the scope of this review.)The only complaint I have so far, and it's minor, it that the compass function would be a lot more accurate if the watch included some form of level.  Timex for example, includes a small bubble level on their Expedition series compass watches. Keeping the surface of the watch level is important to obtaining the most accurate readings.The bottom line, this is a great watch and well worth the money.  I would definitely recommend it to any of my friends looking for an all around sports watch.

I gave the Suunto Core a try but I ended up having to return it.  This made me sad; it's a good looking instrument that seemed to fit my needs.  But here's the main problem: the altimeter is not accurate enough for my purposes, which is navigating while climbing or hiking off trail.I contacted Suunto and told them I was having accuracy issues even when I carefully set the reference elevation before each use.  I asked them to provide an accuracy spec so I could determine whether or not I had a defective unit.  The response they gave (after a delay of several days) was their standard admonition to "recalibrate".  Here's an excerpt:"The watch will need to be recalibrated from time to time, especially after large changes in the weather of if you have been in a pressurized environment (eg. an airplane).You can calibrate your watch by entering the sea level pressure or the reference altitude, normally it is easier to use the reference altitude as this can be found fairly easily for any location (visit google earth) and always remains constant.Even small changes in the weather will result in a small change in displayed altitude."To which I say a great big "duh".  Of course you have to set the elevation every time you intend to use the altimeter for navigation.  I had been careful to let them know that I knew this so I was somewhat irritated with their response.  Clearly they didn't bother to read what I wrote.  This was just the first of several gaffs by Suunto.  Let me cut to the point of this part of my review: Suunto customer service is terrible and their website is a train wreck that will have you pulling your hair out.  That's all I'll say there.But back to the Core.  I was consistently seeing errors on the order of 4 to 5 percent of the difference between my starting elevation and my destination.  For example I'd start at a known trailhead elevation of 4000 feet, set the reference to ~4000 feet, climb to a known peak of 8000 feet and observe the Core to read ~7800 feet.  In a white out in the mountains two hundred feet is plenty to get you lost, friend.  And it wasn't a single instance, where the sea level air pressure might have been rapidly climbing, it was consistently off.  I started carrying an older Suunto altimeter (X3) along for comparison and that did fine.  So I'm convinced it was the Core that was the problem.  I'd have gotten a replacement Core but Suunto customer service could not give me any reassurance that it wasn't a problem with all Cores.  That performance problem alone is enough to render this instrument inadequate but there's one other detail that's troubling.  When setting the reference elevation you can't set it very precisely.  On my X3 for example, I can set the reference to within one foot, even though that instrument measures only to the meter so the displayed elevation changes in three foot increments.  The X3 will then show you your elevation to the nearest three foot increment as measured from your starting reference.  That works well.  With the Core you can try to set the reference to within three feet (it won't let you enter in one foot increments) but as soon as you leave the setting routine it rounds your starting elevation to the nearest millibar, which translates to about 30 feet.  Which is really annoying.  In short this is unacceptable to me.Other aspects of the Core are nice.  The watch and various timer functions work well and are easy to learn.  The compass works surprisingly well, better than other electronic compasses I've tried.  As other reviewers have noted, the thermometer is useless when it's on your wrist.  Gee, it's always 85F.  I didn't test the thermometer off wrist.  And as I said at the beginning, I think it's a good looking piece.  I had the "regular black" and even that one was acceptable to my wife.  I wouldn't wear it out to a formal occasion but it doesn't scream "geek" as loud as some of these other wrist instruments.As usual, Amazon was stellar in their customer service and ease in returns.  Thank you Amazon.
summary: Not as good as I'd hoped

I used to use the Vector, which was their previous entry-level ABC (Altimeter-Barometer-Compass) watch.  I just got the Core after waiting for Suunto to shake out the kinks, and I like what they have done.  The Core is an attractive watch that is easier to read than the Vector, with what appears to be a user-friendlier interface.Suunto offers five buttons on the watch, and they are used reasonably well.  The click-throughs to get to functions have not changed all that much, but they seem a bit more logical and easy to learn.  The amount of information that is readily displayed has not changed all that much, but it is easier for me to spot.  Moreover, they've added some helpful add-on's that I do not remember from the Vector (sunrise/sunset, e.g.).Where I am headed with this watch, the ambient temperature is going to be way above whatever my body will put out, so that is not an issue for me.  However, like all watches, strap it to your backpack if you want a true reading at all times.One thing I have noticed is that the Core takes a much different take on how the altimeter should function than the Vector.  Therefore, setting the watch to beep every X-feet of gain/loss no longer seems to be an option (at least if it is there, it is so deeply buried that it is practically gone).  In its place. the Core takes a more holistic approach to AB functions, and offers what they call the "Storm Alarm."  It recognizes that altimeters are affected by barometric conditions, and vice versa.  Therefore, while the watch offers a very useful altimeter, the baseline assumption is that it must be set at the beginning of a day, or reset according to known waypoints as weather fluctuates.  This appears to be a much more realistic approach.  Meanwhile, if you know that you are on a flat plain and the Storm Alarm comes on, then some system is coming your way.The compass is fine--just set the declination when you get there.The backlight is more than serviceable for use in darkness.Two notes on appearance.1.  The watch is not ostentatious to my eyes.  Rather, it appears very functional and much "cleaner" in look than the Vector.  However, know that it has a very large surface, so it will be noticed.  I am using it for everyday use, as well as for my adventures.  However, if you are looking for whimsy, this might not fit the bill.2.  My elderly mother loved my Vector because the numbers where large.  I suspect she would like the Core even more.Primary uses: everyday use (i do a lot of public speaking, so legibility is a plus); travel; cycling; skiing.

This is a good watch, when it it working.  The problem is that is keeps failing.  The time-keeping function is great.  The altimeter is also very good.  Like all altimeters, you must periodically adjust the height to account for changes in barometric pressure.  The compass is very hit and miss.  I have learned that this is generally the case on all watch compasses.  The compass is usually good enough to use, but not good enough to rely upon if you are out in the woods.  The reason for the two stars, is that I have had two identical fails of the lower button on the right side of the watch.  The watch stops processing any input from this button rendering the watch useless.  The first fail happened under warranty, and Suunto quickly replaced the watch with a new watch.  This is great customer service.  However, the replacement watch has now failed in the same way.  This makes it very hard to recommend this watch.

fast delivery, arrived with no scratches or scuffs. Looks everything like it does in the picture and better. I have already received plenty of compliments on the buckle.
bought this rash guard in 2011. I rotate this out with my other rash guards so it gets about 1 grappling class a week worth of wear and it has held up well so far.
The glove gets wet easily so you can't use it in rain or snow. I am not sure it keeps your hands warm below zero either... living in Minnesota it did not work for my husband anyway...
i'm very happy with this product and the vendor. I will do business with him again. it is impossible to find xlt in my area.thanks again tom smith

these boots seem good. a bit heavy and quite loose around the ankle.i would recommend buying at least a half size smaller. the boot has an inner liner that is removable but boots cant be worn without it. i brought them for working around the property and general kick around boots but they`re a bit to heavy. they will be good in winter though, keeping the water out and feet warm, so only good for wet days for me. probably should have brought some gum boots. they would be good in the snow.

These boots arrived sooner than expected and the fit is great!It has a liner in it so I guess this should help for summer months.It also has the drawstring around calf area that can be adjusted, so if you have big calf It possibly will work for you.To me it seemed to big of an opening but I thought about calf  or thick pants. Living in Colorado on a ranch that is located above 7000ft, where the winters can be wicked, these boots are great!  They are easy on/off, adjustable at the ankle, well insulated, completely waterproof, and true to size. They are also much lighter than I expected them to be, which is a plus since slogging through snow drifts is tiring enough without boots that feel like they are made of concrete.  They also keep my feet comfortable without making my feet sweat and the liners don't bunch and are washable.  All in all, I am very happy with my pair of OilrRigs and have already recommended them to several friends that are also farmers/ranchers.Its a great pair of boots at a great price--what more could you ask for?

9/9/2012  Review Update:  I've been wearing the watch for 12 days and am even more satisfied with the Wenger Aquagraph than I stated earlier.  However, I'm not changing my "4" rating to a "5" for the following two reasons:  First is the short band which came with the watch (see review below).  The second reason happened earlier this week.I called Wenger to inquire if replacement bezels were sold separately (like Seiko and other popular watch brands do.)  I wanted to buy a red bezel and a green one.  The lady from customer service was very polite, but told me Wenger does not sell bezels separately and there is no chance that they will anytime soon.  Period.......______Received my new Wenger AquaGraph 72235 at the office today (8/28/2012) and have been wearing it for the past six hours.  I bought it to replace a Victorinox Maverick GS which IMHO has too much clutter on the dial.  I find the AquaGraph is easier to read and the simplicity of design more pleasing to my eye. The 3-6-9 add a nice touch.  I like the white rectangle around the date window which makes it easier to find and the lume is much better than the Victorinox.In reading other reviews about this watch, I've found mine to be no different.  The "triangle" on the bezel doesn't line up perfectly at the "noon" position and the second hand doesn't always pause on the mark (like my $27 Timex has done for several years.)  How hard can it be to exercise a little extra quality control?  Also, the rubber strap is almost too short for my wrist (I had to use the second to last hole.)  I've since retired the Wenger strap to the box and have replaced it with a plain rubber strap with a deployant type clasp.  Again, I like the simplicity.At first I thought this watch was too heavy, but after a few hours I don't even notice the difference.  I'm pleased with my purchase and feel I've gotten good value for my money.12/30/2012 Update:  Still enjoying the watch!  Despite the crystal being "mineral" rather than sapphire, it's holding up very well even thought I've subjected it to numerous impacts both at home and the office.  As far as I can tell, the watch is losing about six or seven seconds a month which I find acceptable. Here's a link to a YouTube time lapse video of my watch.  [...]

Great sport watch with rubber/silicon band. Bold green color bezel looks great (copy of the Rolex style from a few years back) but they do a good job making it their own. Best thing is that the dial is simple, bold and easy to read! It's not cluttered like most watches I see these days. It's pretty big on the wrist, but that is the current style of these kind of watches, and why I purchased it (it's not "rapper" big). I own a blue Rolex Submariner two-tone and a Tag Heuer F1 diver style watch too, larger than those. Diver bezel is great for timing while you are cooking or waiting for a table at a restaurant.Immediately took off the band because I can't deal with the strap buckle type; I put on a rubber "quick deployment" strap I found on Amazon. Very happy with it.

The 1000m is more of a showoff thing than actually useful, but there's no way I'm taking an automatic near water.The Superluminova illumination is poor, well applied lume makes a huge difference.The hands are unaligned from the markers on the face, common in quartz watches, but still irksome.It has a screwdown crown, screwdown case back, and the screw in lugs have rubber gaskets.

As far as the watch itself is concerned, a very beautiful precise instrument. I love the form factor. The watch band however is too small to fit around my wrist. I have to put the pin on the last hole. I plan on getting an aftermarket band to replace the Wenger one since they do not make a larger size. That's the only reason why it only gets 4 out of 5 stars.

I was eying this watching for a long time, and found it on Amazon for just under $200, which is a great steal. If you read some of the other reviews you'll notice a common complaint about the strap being too short. I have to agree with the other reviewers. I not a large man by any means, but I also found that the strap is too short. Fitted snugly, I am on the 3rd to last hole, loose I am on the 2nd to last. And while it fits, you aren't left with much strap left to facilitate ease placing the watch on or taking it off. I had to measure to my wrist and it's only 7 inches in circumference. Any bigger than that, and I think you would have to be looking at other watches or getting an extra strap to go along with this one.The watch itself is exactly what I wanted. The second hand doesn't perfectly align with each of the tick marks, but that doesn't bother me. I am definitely shopping around for a new strap that accommodates my wrist better.
summary: Quality watch with a few short comings.

reviewText: I was looking for a true deep sea watch (for scuba diving) without the hefty price and the Wenger Aquagraph hit the mark. Easy to read, great luminescence, clean design, and a rugged case. The bezel moves easily and has large numbers for quick reference.The rubber strap is substantial and good for everyday use but if you plan on wearing it over a wet ot dry dive suit, I would recommend purchasing the Wenger Deep Diver Kit (also through Amazon)which includes a strap extension which you will need to use to wear the watch over the bulk of a suit. The kit also includes replacement straps, and a screwdriver (for the strap pins) all in a compact case.My only suggestion to Wenger to make this watch perfect would to make the primary watch band longer so that you don't need the strap extension because it is bulky.

I purchased this watch as an everyday watch that I could also use as a diving watch. The watch itself is sort of OK but the band is awful. It is so small I think it was intended to be for a child. I do not have a very big wrist but I have a very hard time getting it on and it's uncomfortable. A diving watch usually has a longer band so it can be worn over a wetsuit. This watch would never go over any underwater garment. The watch is at risk of loss because the sliding bands that are supposed to hold the loose end of the watchband are so close to the end and also move that it would be easy to have the watchband open and the watch fall off. Victorinox sells a band on it"s website for $65.00, I guess that's the gimmick.

I got this watch on the rubber strap and immediately put it on a watchadoo bracelet. It is now my go to watch for all activities that require a worry free watch. This watch is built to be worn in all conditions and hasn't let me down. Great size and feel and if you don't like them heavy keep it on the rubber strap. A true "tool watch" that won't disappoint.
The watch is excellent with zero defects of any kind.  The band is so, so.  Bought a green canvas strap from Crown and Buckle and now it's one of my most comfortable watches, I forget I have it on.

The watch has a screw-down crown for diving purposes. Surprisingly my new watch worked only with crown completely released/unscrewed. I guess it is a factory defect. How can I trust the manufacturer and dive with this kind of quality product?

I have had this watch for two weeks now and am happy with it so far.  The buying experience with Amazon was smooth as usual.  The rubber band that came with it was too small (had to go to last two holes) so I put a 22mm steel bracelet from my old watch on it.  Much nicer with the stainless band.  If you want to go that route, then purchase the watch with the rubber strap and buy an aftermarket stainless steel bracelet (you can find them for around $50.00  then you have two bands and don't pay the extra 100 Wenger charges for the stainless bracelet.  The second hand doesn't line up exactly with the numerals on the dial, but it's a hair off and if you aren't anal about it, you probably won't notice.  It has kept time well (only lost 2 seconds in two weeks).  The warranty requires you have Wenger service it for the three year warranty period.  That means you must send it off to Wenger for battery replacement if it runs down before the time is up. My only other complaint is that it has a mineral crystal instead of a sapphire one, but only time will tell how resistant it is to scratching.  So, with a $450 retail value bought through Amazon for $230....I'm very happy with this watch and would recommend it to anyone.

Aquagraph is a great watch - simple, very robust and stylish (if you like this kind of watches). My only complaint goes to the length of the armband. It's roughly 7.5cm + 11.5cm and for me that was too short. I could reach the penultimate hole of the armband, but the remaining part was so short that it was hard to handle. To my surprise, I was unable to get a longer replacement band, so I had to replace it with a generic one.

Received the watch and was very impressed with the look and feel.  I will say that the watch itself if very large and has some decent weight to it.  The only issue with the watch was that it stopped working within the first week I owned it.  I am assuming that it was just a faulty battery.  Amazon and the seller were EXCELLENT in making a return and full refund very easy.  I will purchase another Wenger, but maybe a slightly smaller watch.
summary: Great looking watch, if it worked

reviewText: I ordered these slippers and was excited when they arrived, only to find out that one has a defect in the rubber side of the sole, making it impossible to use since it rubs against the side of the foot and hurts me, also the rubber soles are black and not pink as in the photo, and overall it is cheap looking.Another thing is that I ordered a size 8 and these are HUGE, my feet are absolutely drowning in them, they are wide and thus making it very uncomfortable to wear.

I have tiled floors in my entire downstairs and standing in the kitchen for any stretch of time is back breaking. So I got these slippers and they are okay but Walmart had a great clearance sale on the men's Dearfoams and they are made much better and you can go outside in them for shorts spells like getting the mail.
