reviewText: Good quality and great customer support. I would definitely recommend it. Customer support helped to make an exchange and get it on time.

I bought this for my 9 year old son to use for year-round swim team during the winter months here in GA.  The jacket itself is very nicely made and seems to work well when worn right out of the pool as well as over sweats.  The zipper on this jacket has very fine teeth and getting the zipper started is difficult for smaller hands.  I recommend buying this or any swim jacket in a darker color.  There's a reason they are the most popular.  We bought the red so we could see him more clearly at meets, but plenty of other kids buy the same colors making it still a challenge to find them sometimes.  The bonus of the dark color is stain resistance.  These coats will be worn when then eat snacks or post-race meals and they will get stained.  Washing them doesn't seem to take out the stains entirely and I have seen this on dozens of jackets at meets, so I know it's not just us.  Great jacket, but buy a dark color.
This is not the warmest parka but works to go from the pool to the car. We live in the south, so it never gets too cold.
summary: Fits fine, but not super warm.

reviewText: doesn't fix me
This Nike shoe makes a great coaching shoe or just everyday walking or exercise shoe. It cleans up very easily and lasts longer than your average running shoe.

I love these things but this brand is almost impossible to find anymore.  Perfect for those of us who either don't want to or don't have to wear a bra.  They are clear so can be worn under anything and not show.  They stay in place and can be used for a long time until they stop sticking.  I use them for much longer than the box says they will work for.  You can rinse them off in water and they don't lose their stickiness.  They are pricey, but considering they are reusable, it's worth it.
Got this one for my daughter for Christmas.  It's small but it's a key chain so you should expect that.  The figure is pretty cool and the colors are very good.

Really nice watch. I'm using it more than a year, and it still looks almost as new (all you need is to clean rubber belt time to time). During that year I used this watch in expeditions to Africa, New Guinea, New Zealand, Siberia and Mongolia. Works perfect, but you need to calibrate barometer after flights.It is VERY attractive, and few friends of mine who own Rolex for few thousands dollars thought that my Timex WS4 is better than their. It is - if you are traveling:)Delivery is fast - they shipped watch to me from US to Europe in 3 or 4 days.

One of the most amazing watches you will own!People will constantly ask you about it and give you compliments.It has a good array of functions not really needed by most but good to have just in case.My only sad note was it couldn't keep up with the altitude I was reaching while riding an airplane, it probably clocks out somewhere around the highest mountain a person can climb or something.

I have been using the balck version of this WS4 watch in Denver, Colorado for a week now and have found the altimeter to be very accurate.  I calibrated it at the mile high stairs on the capitol steps elevation marker for 5,280 feet, and drove to Estes Park. At the 2 mile high marker it was only off by 5 feet (should have read 10,560 feet but read 10,565 feet), drove to the gift shop close to 8,000 feet (can not remember the exact elevation) and it was only off by one foot at their elevation sign, and then drove back to the capitol steps in Denver where it was exactly where it should have been at 5,280 feet.  Calibrate it on the day of your adventure like you are suppose to and it is very accurate and a pleasure to use.

I was shopping for a good outdoors watch for hiking.  For the money - the WS4 has it all!  I love the layout (call me a geek) and I am wearing it every day.  In fact, a lot of people stare at the watch - lord knows what they're thinking. LOL.  Anyway, when the WS4 arrived, I read the instructions but couldn't get it to recognize my altitude.  I set the home location - but that didn't seem to work. I double checked the weather setting and that had no effect.  I read some blogs and finally decided to have it replaced.  Amazon immediately shipped a new one but after it arrived, it had the same problem.  What were the odds of receiving two defective watches?  I decided to dig a little deeper online - until I found an obscure blog about "hard setting" the watch.  I had no idea that after I set my home location or the weather that it needed to be hard set.  After setting a feature - simply hold the Stop/Reset button until it beeps - and you're hard set.My only complaint is the instruction booklet.  It's not in-depth enough for this advanced model - and if you're over 40 (like me) - pull out your magnifying glass - because you're going to need it.  The booklet was written for ants or 20 years olds:-)I've used the watch on a few hikes I know really well - and I'm astounded by how accurate it is.  Activate the chronograph while hiking and it keeps a fantastic record of your hike (time and elevation / differential).
summary: "Hard Set" - to make it work - otherwise I'm blow away.

reviewText: It is a very good watch, just need to rd the instructions on how to set it up but it isnt very hard to do. It is alo very nice to look at :D
summary: Very good watch, i love it

reviewText: I got this watch a few months back, and its been great! All the features work perfect, and the orange color is really cool! Worth the money it costs by a lot! Love it!

Use it for all my triathlon/running trainings & any sport activities.Travel with it around the world because of the dual-timeBracelet replacement of my first yellow WS4 watch was completely inadequateAltimeter is not very preciseCompass is not easy very precise & easy to read
summary: Like the watch by itself, but not all the functions. This is my second Timex WS4

reviewText: This is a good watch but the screen could be a little smaller and yet still qualify as big. The temperature reading is always off unless you remove the watch for a few mins.

This thing is huge! It gets caught on everything and makes my wrist sweat. The temperature reading is only accurate when you are not wearing it and the slightest change in weather dramatically changes the altitude reading. The compass works really well and the watch it's self is very user friendly. Also this thing will take a beating as I have found out over the past year that I've owned it.

Occasionally this watch does show the correct barometer reading BUT the dot matrix display NEVER shows or can it show the correct reading at 5,280feet. For that you have to set the correct reading as the "home value". Still the dot matrix displays what the SEA LEVEL reading would be at this altitude and will always do so regardless. Once the "home value " is set the barometer is fairly accurate; the weather icon fairly accurate. Setting the altitude depends on where you are. There is no "automatic" function reading from see level as "0" and moving upward. It too must be set as a "home value". Both barometer and altitude are measured by the same sensor. That can cause one or the other readings to be off often significantly. The temp should have been adustable but isn't. Everything else about the watches other functions are great, the display is great. Having atitude and barometer measured for 36 HOURS is very good. I own two Casio ABC watches too. The Casio Protek PRW2500 is NEVER wrong! I suspect that's due to increased techology. However all this sounds, I do like the watch. Impressive in this day and age of enormous watches on the wrist. Hey, we have wide screen TV's now, might as well have a wide screen watch!
summary: 2013 review of the Timex WS4 ABC watch

reviewText: This is the best watch I have ever own. It can tell you all the different things that one can use in everyday life from the weather aspects.
summary: Timex with  everything a person needs in a watch.

reviewText: I was sold by what was supposed to be an extra long strap so you could strap it outside a jacket;  it's not so long.  And the whole watch feels cheap.  I'm much happier with my Casio watches.

The watch in all is a good watch.  It lives up to expectations but the compass failed within 1 month of purchase.  I sent the watch back in for repairs and have not received it back yet but customer service was really decent.  I think personally that it is as accurate as some of the several suunto's that I own.  Except for the compass issue it seems to be a great deal.

Let me say the good things that I love from this watch.1) The weather report is very accurate2) The size is the same of a suunto, the only difference is that one is square and the other is circular.3) The temperature feature is very accurate, and when you remove it from your hand, in a matter of 3 minutes shows the real temperature.4) The barometer works great.5) The altimeter is very very accurate! The only bad thing is that it update very slowly.The only bad thing is that the watch screen can get scratched very easy.
Despite it's form it's been my daily watch and I'm totally satisfied with it, first you have to check how to program it, I use google to perform this task because the manual don't specify it

First off my last 4 watches have been a timex.  The last two were expeditions of another type.  I still have all the others and they all have taken a licking and are still ticking.  This watch is bigger on wrist but you get used to it after wearing it for about a day or so.  Its surprisingly comfortable and display is easy to read.  Functions are cool and work if you actually read the instructions to learn how to properly use them. I was in the market for a suunto but didn't want to drop 500 on a daily wearer. This is much more affordable and it does all the same stuff.  It has understated style and I can't seem to stop looking at it.  Face seems like it may scratch easily due to it being so large, and I am a little worried it may break over time but if I get two years out of it I will feel it was worth the price.  It's a dope timepiece overall though.
summary: I like mine so...I guess I recommend it.  just don't get a black one because then you'll be like me.

reviewText: I find this watch to do everything it claims, at least for me. (I restrict my pursuit of the 7 Summits to reading and documentaries). Though a little bulky, it is fairly light. The only negative I can think of is that the elastic band's adjustablility is limited for thin wrists.All of the functions work well, and the compass, barometer and altimeter are quite consistent in their readings. So far my peak altitude has been 1148 feet...very depressing!I highly recommend it!

I like the watch.  For my profession it serves its functions well.  The barometer and altimeter come in handy when dealing with mountain terrains, and same with the compass.  It looks cool and is pretty light for its size; I get a lot of trash-talking from people on its size....  But I think they're slightly jealous of its good looks.I'm sure there are better watches out there, but for the money and my personal lifestyle, it's great!

It's more the interface that attracted me to this watch ... the predictions are pretty accurate , yes the temperature is higher when the watch is worn ... however that's understandable just as if a thermometer was placed near a heat source ... just minus a few degrees and you have the right degree... the compass is a nice function to have and is accurate.. as for the weather prediction icon don't forget it's predicting the temperature in advance so the next 6 - 8 hrs not the current .. and it's always going to be a prediction.. so nothing is set in stone... Overall very pleased with this watch and it's just a fun one as well....Enjoy~

very large watch. fairly easy to navigate once you practice. temp gauge not so accurate and in the instruction booklet  it says to wear it over a jacket or on your pack (well then what's the point of a wrist watch) but the body raises the temperature...so that's not so accurate. i'm not sure how to read this compass so i'm not sure if i calibrated it correctly. i was able to use the chrono and review easily. i love the orange color. it has two clocks analog and digital and you can choose what other info you want to display. baro, elevation or date/day. so i guess this watch can predict weather patterns....that is if you set it correctly and back to the temp issue not sure how that affects it's forecasting ability. overall, i like it....and i'm a gurl!

I was really drawn to the design of this watch and I wanted it to work.  Notwithstanding the other reviews, I realized that I could only get an accurate temperature reading with the watch off my wrist.  No big deal...all the other watches that measure temperature are like that too.  I liked the elastic type strap furnished with this particular model.  It looked good, was comfortable and worked well with a metal clasp for both direct wrist use and over outer clothing.About 10 days into wearing it the watch went blank?  No hard use just everyday normal wear.  The rear battery compartment was a twist off and was easy to get into but was not loose?  The battery measured full juice...OK!?  I reinserted the battery and tightened the cap and voila' the display came back on and I reset all functions.  The watch appeared to be functioning normally and I wore it for a few more days but the barometer would not budge from its 10.-- inHG reading?I decided not to fool with it anymore and returned the watch to Amazon for a refund.  I was disappointed but decided to pay a little more for a new Casio PAW2000-1.  We'll see how that goes?
summary: I really wanted it to work!

reviewText: overall i like the watch very much.  the altimeter is accurate and the compass works great.  the thermometer works well when you take it off (normal since the body temp affects the sensor).  i like a big watch so this is perfect (initially i thought it might be too big even for my likes but i got used to it).  my only complaint is that the excess watch band comes out of the plastic holder constantly.  still would recommend it though for the price.

After wearing the watch for about 3 weeks, i came up with these remarks:- Complaints on the design: A horizontal dividing LINE and a CIRCLE that's enclosing the analog display was engraved on the screen cover instead of on the LCD which made one feel like wearing a kiddy kiddy watch.- The time display was supposed to be a BIG BOLD font, but why o why the designer opted for a thin tiny winy dotted font, not minding time reading as the main focus of the wearer.-The thermometer is there for a reason of having a thermometer. It could not be calibrated and doesn't respond to ambient temperature fast, but respond to body heat fast and the changes in reading is abrupt - not gradual.- Altimeter seems ok, the margin of error i recorded is (-)5 meter at same reference point at random, so far.
summary: More of bulk, less of substance..

reviewText: Its a bit hard to read sometime, numbers are made of dots.  Night light only helps in very dark conditions.  Easy to set. Thermometer is all but useless since you have to take it off to get an accurate reading.  Comfortable to wear even though large.  Update: after owning the watch for a while, I find it hard to read most of the time as it's a pixeled display.  Hard to remember how to set with all the options.  Cool looking though.

Not as good as I thought it would be, alt and temp doesn't work. Could have been a great product if those two items actually worked, but they didn't. You have to reset Alt, direction, and leave the watch off of your wrist for at least an hour to get within 4 degrees of the actual temp. Now after trying Casio and Timex I realize they are all like that and Rolex doesn't even have the options, back to the 60's I go, that works.
summary: Not as good as I thought it would be, alt and temp doesn't work

reviewText: All the hype about the size of this guy had me interested but it's not big enough!  I've got really bad near sightedness and need reading glasses over my contacts to see close-up.  A big display would help but this one crams too much at once when what I could use would be a really BIG display of one function at a time.  This of course is my problem and won't affect everyone else.  It works well and functions well, tho the instructions ain't much help.  I have a hard time believing that guy made it up Everest with this - the clasp pops open on its own with little encouragement.  I've got a Casio Riseman and it's good but I'm still looking for a bigger view - Suunto anyone?
summary: Big Display? Not big enough for me

reviewText: First the Pros : It's a Timex, so quality is good. The watch is well built. I like the widescreen, as it makes it easier to read. The alarm and hourly chime are very loud, which is a bonus. Like some of it's more expensive companions (like the Suunto) it has an easy to change battery. I like that the time display page shows the time, temp, and a 'weather icon". The Cons: The ABC features of the watch. I have several ABC type watches including the Garmin Fenix, the Suunto Core, the G-shock Mudman, the Casio Pathfinder, and the Casio Riseman. of all these watches, it seems that the Timex is the least accurate, even after calibration.

Having viewed many many pages of watches on the Amazon web site I finally decided that this could be the watch I was looking for. Once ordered it arrived within a very short time. To my surprise and initial consternation it was much bigger than I had expected but once I got used to it it is quite comfortable and fairly easy to use. Functionality wise it has all the functions an outdoors adventurer could want (except for GPS functionality). It is easy to read anjd jumping between functions is simple. All in all a very nice watch.

First of all I love Timex  --  this watch keeps time well, it's alarm works fine, all the usual time piece type stuff work fine. However those things are not the reason you would buy this watch, you buy it for the altimeter,barometer,thermometer, weather condition and compass right ? Well the altimeter was off -- the barometer was off-  I was unable to adjust them -- the compass went haywire on me only once , thank god I was not in the back country and really needed it --the temperature ( the manuel says" it will be off by 10 degrees") mine was off by 12 - 15 degrees , it recommends  it be worn on your belt- if you want an accurate reading- ON YOUR BELT-- IT'S A WRISTWATCH. The weather conditions well if the other settings don't work that feature didn't have a chance .  I gave it time, I played with it, I wanted it to work but will listen to reviews more carefully next time.
summary: should have listened to ALL the reviews re. this watch

reviewText: I bought this watch while overseas for a mountain hike and it was great!!!! Would buy another in a second. I'm a barber now and the only problem was the nylon stretch band catching hair in it other than that I would still be wearing it!!!! Got lotsa great comments on it too!!!!!

This watch is great for any pilot. The barometer, altitude, temp, and compass may be off but its just a guestemate. It gives you an idea of where you are at in these areas. Overall a great watch for the price.
summary: Great watch for the common aviator

reviewText: Bought this for my husband for Christmas. It's was $40 cheaper on Amazon. He thought this watch was so cool, but when he wore it...it hurt his wrist due to the size of the watch. Unfortunately, we had to send it back for a refund. Too bad it didn't work out.

this will be a rough review of pros and con of the watch, features that are included and what makes it great compared to other abc watches.When I first got in to these type of ABC watches, there were so many choices. I didn't know which one to get. There are known brands such as suunto, garmin, casio, etc. but Timex is reputable definitely.However I chose the WS4 based on how clean looking it is, compared to other watches. Everything you need at the moment is on the screen.Functionality, compared to other ABC watches, they do what they do. Thermometer, altimeter, barometer, compass, time keeping, dual time, timer, stop watch, activity log recording.One thing I noticed is that there are features included in this watch that are not included in other watches, and other features from other watches are not included in this.Ex. storm alarm is not in this, separate log keeping is not, sun rise sun set. - well to me these are not the most deal breaker of all.What WS4 have that is not on other watches includes a big 36 hour graph from altimeter to barometer to temperature, big analog clock on screen all the time in any menu. The weather forecast indicator, thermometer, ease of access in switching readings on barometer, altimeter. separate dual time including 24 hr format for each. Repeating timer to the seconds.  Altittude alarm, chronograph for above certain altitude. interchangeable separate view for chonograph - overall time and the time splits. compass calibration is good with declination level to get you where you wanted.final awesome setting is the multiple altitude reference point setting. the altimeter may drift like every other abc, but you can easily readjusted from known location with specific altitude reading.I notice this watch has an anti- fog, grease coating on the glass. oily and sweat smudges dont easily stick to the screen compared to the suunto watches. on the suunto i had to constantly wipe smudges off from finger prints.No wonder timex nailed it with these function making it one of the most ease of access abc watches I've ever come to try.Switching between menu is clean - altitude menu, barometer menu, chronograph, repeating timer, alarm, log recording (just hit up the stopwatch) keep track of every detail from altitude height, difference,max, min, barometer, high-low, temp high-low, to averagesHowever what I found that was most important was reading visibility and readily function, even in the roughest situation such as a heavy rain storm, dusty, night time. I can still read the screen and operate with ease. I've tried other ABC, but this one has the smoothest transition while operating the buttons. Not to mention one of the brightest looking illumination when the metal indiglo button is pressed. you can hold it until it beeps and then every button pressed will activate the lighting- very useful in darker places.The time keeping is superb, I'ved test the time keeping and accurate to the seconds is on par with very very very little split second time drift. Over the course or 2-3 month, the second only drifted off by 1/4 of a second. the quartz mineral is high quality. forget the radio-sync actomic time solar power time keeping shenanigan from casio. One single cell battery for 2.99 on the ws4 will last for more than a year. It does not justify the extra 100 dollar for a constant needed to charge solar power watch.Compare to Suunto watches, believed me I used both, although they are lighter and cool looking, their durability lacks in terms of watchband and scratches. I've used ws4 for nearly half a year, no scratches and marks on the screen or the metal casing. I had more trouble with the suunto in reading the small font and operating the flimsy buttons. I know for sure the heavy duty resin band on the ws4 will outlast the band on the suunto.in terms of water resistance, rated at 50m this is better than suunto- consumer price range watches which is only 30m. I've read about condensation problem in suunto watches. But with the ws4, I've not had any problem, I let it get splashed in the rain, wash it in the showers,put in tub of water to clean, the sensor were still working 100%. Although I know for sure Casio has the better water resistance in term of 100m rating.Overall, this watch is tough as a brick, I can accidentally bang it in hard surface and it is left unscathed. I would say the ws4 is for people with bigger arms, stature, or else you will stand out. But people complimented me and was curious about what type of watch I wore. I notice it's a bit bigger and tat heavier than other ABC watches I've test.only some minor problem I had was the thermometer reading when worn, but like all other abc watches, requires you to take off watch and wait a while to get accurate reading.the weather forecast is accurate 95% of the time after getting it calibrated from very high barometer reading ( meaning super sunny and clear weather) but it is set to go after that.But the choice to invest in abc watch is up to you, the timex ws4 is well reputable and quality to me. just make sure the guy next to you dont wear the same watch.
summary: One of the most solid ABC watches I ever used.

reviewText: I love this watch!!!  The build quality and precision you come to expect in a Swiss watch is all here.  The bezel is all stainless and the glass face is clear and big (not too big though, like those "other" outdoor watches).  It's a heavy watch and it's ready to do battle in the outdoors.  The band is exceptionally nice with matching red stitching, a stainless buckle, and sturdy, bendy water proof silicon construction.  The compass portion of the watch is dead on when properly calibrated (easy to do).  The instructions are easy to follow and guide you through all the settings for the watch.  As nice as this watch is, two things to keep in mind for the future would be: battery replacement and band replacement.  The battery is not user serviceable and will need to be replaced by a shop that has the special tool to remove the back (typical with all fine watches).  The band itself, if ever needing replacement, looks expensive and may be difficult to obtain (probably only through Wenger). But overall, if you are looking at this watch because you want a digital compass watch (the reason I bought it)  with a little more sophistication, metal construction and Swiss reliability, than this is the only watch of it's kind out there for the price.  A great value!

These socks are thin. Another reviewer urges you not to buy these because they'll develop holes very quickly. I was wary when purchasing this watch because I don't have the smallest wrists and I often find watches very uncomfortable. Speaking as an RN for most of my adult life, I think the NAME of this watch is very very misleading.  In order to "scrub" for surgery or any sterile procedure, whether in the Operating Room or elsewhere, the RN, LPN or tech MUST remove all rings and watches.  They are not  considered able to to be cleaned by the usual scrub techniques. (Hands and arms are NOT sterilized in a proper scrub, merely cleaned very well. Sterile gloves are then applied in a special way, to keep the hand clean, and the outer gloves sterile.)This watch which is called a "Nurse/Nursing Cyber Scrub Gel Watch" could lead some people, looking for a gift for a student or new RN or scrub technician, to think the person could wear this while "scrubbed in" as the phrase goes.I never found my own regular Timex watch to be a problem with normal hand WASHING in between patients or in between task.  But it would be removed, along with my ring, if I had to actually use sterile technique and "scrub" in surgery or elsewhere.I just wanted to clear up any misconception.
summary: NOT for a Scrub nurse or tech.....

reviewText: This is a great watch.  I had never heard of Sartego watches when I bought this watch so it was a bit of a leap of faith; but everything else about it said buy it and now I'm glad I did.Firstly, the watch was just what I was looking for: simple, elegant, sleek.  Even dress watches these days tend to be chunky, covered in bezels and chronograph dials. This must be great for mountain climbers and divers but for me it just gets in the way of reading the actual time. This one is simple and uncluttered which makes it easy to see the time.  The one feature it does have on the dial is the day/date calendar, which was a mandatory requirement for me as I find myself using the date feature quite often.Second, it is made of stern stuff.  It has a titanium case and band which combined with its sleekness makes it a really light and comfortable watch to wear.  It also has a sapphire crystal face, which is superior for resisting scratches to the mineral crystal normally used on watches in this price range.Finally, it has one trick up its sleeve which I didn't expect.  The adjustment knob on the side has a thread so you have to unscrew it before pulling it out to change the time. I would never have known how useful this feature was except that my last watch was rendered useless because the adjustment knob kept slipping out by itself, which stops the watch.  A tiny but very clever feature.The only negative is that this watch comes without a battery, so you'll need to buy one as your first order of business. But you'll probably have to take it to the watch guy anyway to fit the band, so it's not so much an inconvenience as a small extra expense.UPDATE: (January 2014) Three years on and unfortunately I had to replace my watch, but I like it so much I bought another exactly the same. It's ultimate demise was due to me somehow smacking it on the edge of my bedside table in a very uncoordinated attempt to catch something falling off the table. This separated the band from the watch body. I could have gotten it repaired but there was another issue that it had developed, which appeared to be a problem with the battery connection. The watch stopped dead for a week, I assumed the battery was flat but when the guy at the shop tested the battery it was fine, and when he reinserted it the watch started ticking fine. Six months go by and the same problem happens again, with the same fix. So when I totalled it a few months later I decided a new one was in order. Hopefully it was a one off problem. Given the price of the watch I was not unhappy with three years but hopefully the next one lasts for much longer.Also I originally said it doesn't come with a battery. My new watch did, so I guess on my first one it had just died before I got the watch.

I started running with minimal shoes about three years ago.  My old shoe was the NB Minimus trail and while a great shoe it just didnt have the protection over rocks.  I ordered the Inov 8 Rocklite 315 hoping for that extra protection from rocks, expecting the shoe to weigh a ton.  To my surprise, while heavier than the NB the 315 is a shoe you that is surprisingly light and definitely gave me the protection I needed.  I've ordered a second pair as a back up but unless they are wet probably wont need it for years.  Look at reviews of this shoe if you still have any doubt and you will see how/why Inov has taken a decisive lead in the running shoe market.

This a light good traction trail shoe-Inov-8 Roclite 315 Trail Running shoe.These shoes feel pretty comfortable; but I put in the Sof Sole cushion inserts which have more cushion in the heel as well as in the entire foot bed compared with the inserts that come with the shoe which were evenly thin.The traction is excellent on dirt, gravel and asphalt. The uppers sit low on the back of my heel; but the heel was securely in place. I had plenty of toe space. I ordered a half size up from my normal shoe size and they fit great. They lace up easy. The toe guard is helpful and protects the toes well.With the inserts in these shoes the walk was comfortable on asphalt as well as off road. I like them so far. My feet did not get too hot; but breathed well even while wearing extra cushioned socks by Defeet (Cush.)I wore thinner socks today Defeet's Aireator and the shoes were even more comfortable. I was surprised that I did not miss the cushioning of the thicker sock. The shoes are easier to get on and off than my previous Glycerin 8 by Brooks which has a higher heel that you step into. So these shoes come off easier than I am used to which is nice. They also are easier to put on as a result of the low uppers where you put your foot inside. The mesh is fine enough that my dog has not bit into it like happened with the looser mesh of the Glycerin 8 uppers. The toe has reflective stripes on each shoe. These shoes are comfortable with the Sof Sol inserts.
summary: Light good traction shoe-Inov-8 Roclite 315 Trail Running shoe.

reviewText: I like the design of these shoes (minimalist with good traction) but two of the lugs on the heel broke off. This is a significant failing.

I am completely impressed by how durable this shoe is. I have had it for about a year, and it has been my daily driver. Usually my shoes are worn out after a year- this one has taken my abuse like a brute. It still looks pretty good, and it still functions perfectly.I worked construction this summer in this shoe. That included roofing. If you have ever put on a roof, you know it is really hard on shoes. It puts a constant sideways strain on the shoe because of the pitch of the roof. These shoes handled it like a champ.I like the mesh on top. It is tough- unlike any other mesh I have come across. It feels almost like a window screen to the touch.The shoes also feel good on my feet. They are both free and supportive. They are light, too.

What a shame they aren't going to make these anymore!I now have 2 pair--one for winter & my winter socks and another to get me thru this summer.  We've has some horrible muddy trail running conditions all fall long and these were champs. I'm no stranger to mud, and have lost a few shoes to it. But these never felt like they were going to get sucked off, and the traction was incredible.  Since I often run barefoot as well, the minimal structure of theses shoes were just perfect for me (and my weak right ankle too) too.

for their intended application - light trails and fire roads - these are fantastic shoes. yes, they fit very close to the foot. i would not call then 'small' since i wear the same size in these as in other shoes. but they are intended to be minimalistic, close fitting, thinner than typical midsoles, no removable insoles. i have not had any of the durability problems mentioned by others, and have been wearing mine for almost a year. i like them so much i bought another pair when i saw them on sale, just in case mine wore out prematurely and/or vasque discontinued them in the future. those are still sitting in my closet, waiting for their day. meanwhile my first pair keeps putting on the miles. 5 stars.

I have purchased the VASQUE brand in the past and have been satisfied with them.  I have some mild foot problems, and normally buying Merrell exclusively.  That being said i was looking at these and decided to take a chance.  I read many good reviews, and many bad reviews so it was hard to make a decision.  These are the facts about this shoe:  #1.  It fits small.  Maybe not a half size small, but small.  It is more narrow than other shoes of medium width.  #2.  It is very nice looking.  I was pleased with how it looked and the quality of the materials used.  #3.  It does NOT have a removable insole.  What it has is a hard "air cushioned" space between your foot and the sole.  Well i didn't feel any air cushioning in these shoes.  I tried them on for a few minutes and they already hurt my feet.  I am really surprised that a company of Vasque's stature would sell a product like this.  Terrible footbed.  As i wanted a red accent running shoe and didn't find any Merrell's to my liking i'm going to give the North Face Double Track a try.
summary: Not sure what VASQUE was thinking...

reviewText: I was torn between getting this or the Suunto D4. Being a previous D3 owner, i was looking to try something new. With the ability to replace batteries myself, and the gazilion different alarms i can set this was a clear winner.edit: after owning this for over a year, i have to admit that i have a love hate relationship with the watch.the manual is almost jiberish, and there are wayyyyyyy too many alarms. I love how customizable it is, however,it is not as simple as the D3.Price: not exactly the cheapest, but will give you the most bang for buck when compared to any freedive computer out there.Verdict, my Suunto D3 still works so till i do my FII or PFI courses this just might sit collecting dust in my room.

Overall this watch offers good value for money. It's about $200 cheaper than the Suunto and offers all the requisites of a good freediving computer. No thought necessary once you have set it up. Just dive and it will record your depth, bottom time and surface interval. Make sure you set the activation depth below 2 feet though as you may end up recording more than one dive per dive profile. I'm a pretty good freediver but I'm fairly certain that I don't have a 5 minute bottom time on a working dive! The one thing that I would criticize is the volume of the alarms. It would have been nice if they were just a bit louder.I am happy with the purchase.

I have a Casio HD watch I picked up about seven years ago or thereabouts. The watch face reads "TEN YEAR BATTERY" in small but earnest "bank it" type, so it's still ticking along just fine. However, the watch band had disintegrated a year or two into wearing it, I expect because I was wearing it in Houston heat, and coating it with my Houston sweat. (You'll never guess where I was living when I wore this watch.)Anyway, very recently I realized I still had this watch sitting around, and it was still ticking, so I figured I'd check Amazon to see if I could find a replacement band. It was ridiculously easy to find, particularly since the model number for the band is embossed on both pieces. While unnecessary, the watch repair kit I'd purchased about the same time came in handy for replacing the broken bits of the old wristband with this new one. I could've just as easily used a pocketknife to release the spring-loaded wristband pegs, but I rather like using the right tool for the job. (Make of that what you will.)Of course, being brand new, the band has a tendency to lie flat; I'm wearing the watch even now, in an effort to "train" the band to be more curled. Hardly a deal-breaker; just a personal preference.

The watchband is a Casio branded band and was the exact one that came on the watch. The only issue was that there were no pins in the pack as there should have been. Email to Amazon resulted in a credit. Since I still had the old pins, this more of am aggravation than anything else. Remember to keep the old until you install the new.
summary: perfect replacement but.......hang on to the old pieces

Fit well, easy to slip on. Work well for walking the dog in the rain.  I have had lots of compliments on them.

reviewText: Great look and fit.
I bought these for my mom to use while gardening. She loves them and they are so comfy and cute she has forgotten to take off and has worn them out and about!

I loved everything about this shoe except for the label that is sewn in on the top edge on the binding. It scratches with every step. I carefully cut it out and found that it covered the raw edge where the binding starts and stops so now I have that showing but at least it's comfortable now. I bought this for walking the dog in the dirt and mud, since I don't do gardening and it works great for that. I can easily clean them, not like sneakers that take a long time to dry, these wipe down and are ready to go again.
I use this for light gardening jobs ; its pretty, durable and comfortable. The quality is great! Overall, its all that I expected it to be!

i walk into work somedays quite a hike not an issue with wet feet now, have used them several times received alot of compliments.  Fit true to size, cushiony inside likem emory foam. could wear all day.

I want sure how to order, so I ordered them a little large.  I don't mind. It makes them easy to take off. I have had trouble for years with my arches hurting after I shovel.  Not in these shoes.  They are so sound and strong.  I love them!

I will be ordering more!  Very comfortable fit!  I can wear them all day in the yard.  I even wore them whitewater rafting and they kept my feet comfy and easy to walk over the rocks.  I never have to worry about walking around when it's raining.  Love these!!
Love these Sloggers so much I ordered a pair for my husband.  He loves them too!  So comfortable I can wear them all day!
Many people have said that they are longer than another shoe would for the same sizing. I don't think so.  I actually but my size thinking they would do fine but they are a bit small.

reviewText: Nice and comfortable wear a 61/2 order a 6, shoes fit with out socks and with thin socks.Bought for working outside in a garden center.

Purchased these to run out and open/close the chickens or bring things outside but find they are my go to shoes. I run around the house barefoot and find that when I need to run a quick trip somewhere I put these on. Since they are plastic they get hot with bare feet, but hay, for a 10 minute trek it works.

So far I love them.  Great for working in the garden and walking through wet grass.  Always keep them by the back door to slip on.  Very well made.  Fit is great.  I normally wear an 8 1/2 and I ordered a size 9 and they fit fine.  The back doesn't come up all the way so they are easy to just slip on.
These are easy to slip on and off and work perfectly for quick trips out to garage or just walking the dog.
These are so pretty and water proof. I never expected them to be as comfortable as they are, perfect. Love them
These are the best shoes, waterproof, cute washable and very comfortable to walk in.  I have 2 pairs now, one for garden work and one for wearing out and about.
These shoes are so well made and very comfortable.  They are the perfect garden shoe.  Easy to keep clean, Highly recommended!
These were exactly what I wanted. The perfect shoe to slip on and run out the door to feed the horses real quick.
The shoes were comfortable and waterproof. I did not get blisters when wearing with no socks. Great to wear when watering plants or just working out in the yard.

This is the second pair of Sloggers that I've purchased.  I use them when working in the yard & garden, especially when it's damp outside.  No more soggy socks.  They are easy to slip on when the dog needs to go outside.

reviewText: This shoe is comfortable enough to walk in.  Great for rain-country. Comes in plain, or fun colors so there's one for everyone.
summary: Colorful and comfortable rainy day shoes.

reviewText: Very easy to put on when gardening or taking the dog for a quick walk.  I love the colorful design.
Could easily wear these all day, and they keep my feet toasty and dry. Also, they are actually easy to step into, without bending. Great product!

I love these shoes. They are pretty and so comfy! And they can take a beating...I slip them on to putter around in the garden or do more serious yard work. I don't see any reason why one needs to compromise and wear those "other" outdoor slip-on rubber monstrosities. :) Unlike those, these Sloggers don't scream out "I give up!" These are fun and different and, above all, they are workhorses that do their job second to none! Highly recommended.
summary: Friends don't let friends wear Crocs...

reviewText: I wear these shoes all of the time. I keep them by the door for yardwork, taking out the trash, checking mail, etc. Easy slip on and they fit just right so they stay on!

Live in Florida so I didn't want anything to heavy or hot.  These are just the ticket to walk the dog and work in the yard and not get your feet wet.  They are so comfortable, I forget to change shoes when I come inside.  As far as the fit goes, I have wide feet and these shoes are roomy so for me it is a good fit.  I'm going to order anothe pair.
summary: Great shoe for walking the dog in the wet AM grass

reviewText: These fit very, very loosely, so I doubt a special 1/2 size insole would help. However, the size is not that much of a problem because I wear these Sloggers to clomp around my garden paths after a rain. The size would be a problem if I were planning to walk a distance. Also, I ordered the design shown in the illustration but received the green colour with animal pawprints. It would've been a waste of my time and money to return them for exchange, so I've resigned myself to odd green colour and safari-style pawprints.
I love Sloggers.  These garden shoes are so comfortable and so stylish.  I've gotten many compliments.  Ordered a second pair.  Love, love them and USA made!!!!

I live in Alaska where it is muddy or rainy often. The description of working in a "garden" matched  what I experience going to the grocery store or movies here. I was tired of ugly rubber boots and wanted something pretty to slosh around in and easy to slip in and out of.  I was a HIT at the last party... everyone wanted to know where i got my pretty, comfortable, and Waterproof shoes.  (ONLY in Alaska are you considered stylish wearing garden shoes!)  But hey they work and look really cute! They are true to size. I wear a 10 women's and have wide feet, and they are OK..even with thin wool socks.  When I wear them  is it usually 40 - 50 degrees F and so my feet do not sweat at those temps. The backs of them do slip a little bit when i walk - but i don't mind that. If i had to run from a bear they would fall off. The traction is GREAT - does not slip on hard wet surfaces! I am very happy with my Pretty waterproof shoes that i wear for everything but the garden! ( we wear tall mud boots for that)
summary: Perfect fun shoe for wet muddy places

reviewText: The fit is perfect with regular socks. Thicker, cold weather socks might be uncomfortable.  I typically wear a size 8 and that's what I ordered.

This is a great shoe for many other chores besides gardening.  I have chickens so this is the perfect shoe for gathering eggs and cleaning the hen house.  They are very comfortable besides being attractive enough to go to the grocery store.  I ordered a size larger than I usually wear so I could wear socks with them in cold weather.  They have replaced my clogs.

I bought these to wear to lacrosse games. We are always playing in the rain in the spring. They fit well. They look cute. And my feet were totally dry!  I was flooded with compliments and truly enjoyed wearing them. Great buy!!

Very comfortable shoe with good arch support, true to size. I have very narrow heels and was worried about the heels slipping,they do not slip off my feet, even going up and down hills ! Great for the garden, the mud and the compost pile. At the end of the day you can wash them off, so easy ! Love them.
Mom had back surgery but missed her gardening. I got these for her so she wouldn't slip trying to stand up. She loves them.

I ordered these shoes to wear at the horse barn when I'm rinsing or washing my horses. I was tired of getting my leather paddock boots wet and ruining them.For the price, these shoes are good. They are indeed waterproof. But they are cut a little low so I still get a little bit of water splashing into them, but its not too bad. And they are really big around the ankle so they don't stay on very well when walking (& its not that they are too big, my toe is very close to the end when standing). I am used to clogs and slides so I don't mind them flopping, but it did take a little getting used to.But they save my leather boots and they keep my feet dry in the wash rack so I will gladly keep using them.  I wish that they came in some solid colors instead of the loud prints, but I only wear them to the barn so its not the end of the world.
I bought these to wear while gardening and tending to my chickens.  I have wide feet and these fit great.
I love these shoes.  I wear them around the house, to the mailbox, to the grocery stoes and sometimes to the garden.  They are confortable and washable and the perfect shoe to just slip on and go.
summary: Sloggers are more than just garden shoes

reviewText: Great footwear for walking around at the dog park, which can get a little muddy! They seem to run small.

i love love love these sloggers.  they are my first pair and i cannot wait for it to rain so i can jump in puddles with these Great fitting shoes. i am usually a wide and was scared to order online, but they fit absolutely fantastic! i mean, perfect.  the only drawback is that they are a little low in the back heel area and a foot slips out occasionally, while wearing barefoot.  so cute, cannot wait to wear them, thank you sloggers!!

reviewText: I love these Sloggers.  They are true-to-size (I wear an 8, and these fit perfectly).  The sole is much more comfortable than I expected. I love the pattern, and the fact that it won't wear off.  I also love that there is no place for the shoe to leak.  Recommended...wish I'd purchased them at the very beginning of the gardening season!
Great shoe to wear anytime
Good!!!!!
love them,easy to slip on, durable in the wet grass and for gardening removable inserts...purchased the boots for someone and liked them so much picked some for me too!
I am glad I purchased these, will probaby purchase another pair. Made in the USA so wonderful. Comfortable and the design looks like the picture.
Love them!  I work at a Coal Mine in the office and these are perfect for wearing.  They are comfortable and they clean up easily!  I received my shoes before the estimated date.

They are comfortable, however your feet get very hot in the shoe. I live in Florida and the Summer rainy days are already very steamy. Show would be great in a colder climate. reviewText: They run large. I wear an 8.5 and per the instructions ordered up to the 9. It was way way too big even with the half sizer insert they sell. The 8 fit well. I love these shoes - waterproof, great for running out to the garden in the mornings through the dew.  I've slipped them on to clean the car and run errands.  These are great for gardeners or anyone who is out working in the yard.  Easy to slip on and off, make for quick runs outside to grab things from the garden.  I'm usually around a 9.5 but they only had size 9, fit great - very slightly snug, but that helps them stay on.  Would highly recommend and love the fact that they are made in the USA.
Love these shoes! They keep my feet warm and dry in rain, mud, and even snow. Rather stylish too! Very cute.

i expected them to be higher to the ankle but they turned out to be no that high. i needed some new shoes for the car wash and the have a good grip at the bottom but since theyre short my socks still end up getting wet.Its a good shoe, just not for what i needed them for.
summary: not what i expected but still good.

reviewText: Comfortable and cute!……I wore them to work all day, then came home and walked the dog in them…..love them…...great buy.

reviewText: The color and pattern was what I expected. The right shoe does squeak when walking without socks. Guess this should be expected. Even so, I like the shoe very much.
summary: The shoe is perfect for wet yard wear.

reviewText: These Sloggers do the trick - they keep my feet dry when I walk my dogs through wet grass and mud.  They are roomy enough for me to wear a pair of cotton socks, which is fine with me, as I didn't particularly look forward to bare feet in non-breathable shoes.  They are exactly what I was hoping for - something for the warm weather walks when I didn't need my snow boots.
These shoes are Made in the U.S.A. and that was my first criterion.  They are well-made, waterproof and comfortable.  I can just slip my feet into them, hands free and go.  Well-worth $35.00.

Really like these for early morning forays into the backyard (dewy grass) or working in the garden when muddy. Easily washed off. They're pretty, as well! Only criticism I have is the width & tend to be a little loose.

These are great, especially since we had so many wet days this spring.  The backs of the shoes are lower and I feel more comfortable with a higher back, and that's why I didn't give them 5 stars.  However,  I'm sure they would be perfect for most people.  They are very comfortable and made in USA.
I have a pair of these shoes and absolutely love them. I got these a gift for my daughter because she keeps looking at mine!
summary: Great shoes for gardening or just running out to the mailbox

reviewText: Bought these as a gift for my mom. She loves them. Wears them on rainy days when she has to work outside.  Claims they are extremely comfortable :)
summary: Sloggers Women's Rain and Garden Shoe

reviewText: I don't write reviews, but I just took the dogs out for a walk on the soggy grass, and I fell in love with these shoes right then. They are really cute. No wet feet during walk. I have some never damage in my ankles so I have trouble finding shoes that don't aggravate that problem. These did not. I wear a 61/2, but some reviews said to get a size down. I got a 6 and they were perfect. They seemed snug but when you have them on a few minutes, they fit perfectly. I'm going to order a pair for my sister and another pair for me.
Love the way they look and feel!  Easy to slip on and off.  Waterproof so my feet don't get wet when walking in the dewy grass.
I love my Sloggers for gardening.  Comfortable and waterproof, they are easys to walk around in and I forget that I have them on.

It's so easy to slip on and off, so I can run in and out of the house as needed. The shoe hoses off easily and thoroughly too. To top things off, it couldn't be more comfortable. The sizing guidelines were accurate. I love the shoe (besides, it's pretty!) and even bought a pair of the men's for my husband.
Very comfortable, easy to clean, cute, and water proof. The only reason I couldn't give them 5 stars is that they squeak when you walk.
Cute rain shoes. True to size. Comfortable enough to walk around a bunch of stores. Made in the USA - .
summary: Comfy and look great for quick trips to the store in the rain.

reviewText: For the price, these have far exceeded my expectations.  I was looking for a casual, water repellant, easy care, nubuck style shoe to slip on for wearing around the yard and casual errands in wet weather.  I also have found them to be good in snow, ice and slush as well, keeping my feet from getting cold or wet (so long as you keep snow from getting in them from top opening, it doesn't permeate the shoe).  I imagine they will be equally good at keeping the feets temp regulated and dry in the warmer months as well.  I wear them constantly and, even though they don't have super arch support, they are comfortable and don't aggravate my lower back at all.  I also like that they are easy to clean (the removable/washable insert is a nice touch) and that they come in an array of cool styles.  I will probably invest in the 1/2" sizer to get a more snug fit and can't speak to their longevity, but so far, can't beat em at the price.
summary: Where have these been all my life?!

reviewText: I bought these to use at school during  my car duty assignment on rainy days. They fit like shoes and are very comfortable, They take less storage space than my other rubber boots. The design is  wonderful as well.

These are fabulous!!!!!  I love the colors, they're true to the pictures, they're comfortable and fun outside to work in and definitely eye catching when I'll wear them any where I want to go in the summer!

Just got these, so don't know how well they will wear, but they are pretty, comfortable, and have a great tread on the bottom.  They look like the picture, just a bit darker aqua.  I was very pleased the way the design laid out on the shoe, as in the photo.  The colors are so pretty!Usually wear an 8-1/2.  Ordered the 9, as reviewed suggested, and they fit great.  The photo looks like they will rise higher on the foot but they are a little lower than expected.  Not a problem, however.Looking forward to comfortably sloshing around in my garden from now on in these!P.S.  I've had these for 1-1/2 years now.  Wore them all winter too.  They are my everyday shoes.  Very comfortable!  The toes are looking a little dull now but I don't really clean shoes very often.  That might have made a difference.  They still look good, imo, though.

They fit well and are so comfortable that I can wear them all day. They also do what they're supposed to, that is, they keep your feet dry and protected when you are out in the garden. Best of all, they are attractive! My only wish is that that it came in 1/2 sizes.

I wore a pair of Birkenstock Prof clogs as my 'porch' shoes for years. They were literally starting to disintegrate, and I just couldn't get myself to spend $65 on muckers (the Birkis were originally my surgery shoes, and retired into mucker duty). For under $30, I decided to give these a try, and they are actually more comfortable. I usually slip then on barefoot to do barn chores, but they work with or without socks. If heel slip bothers you, these aren't for you, but for me they are like a clog that hugs my foot like a shoe. The only downside is that while the clogs were roomy enough for long wear in hot weather, in Florida 95% humidity, if I wear these all day in the garden, my feet do tend to pickle just a little. Still, I am about to order a second pair. I have a wide foot, and these are fine. The 8 worked for my 7 - 8 feet.
I have always been a big fan of Sloggers Rain & Garden shoes, so I wasn't disappointed at all ... living in FL with high humidity, they fit just about any weather ....
These shoes are very water-proof and easy to clean. They were sized a little wide for me but otherwise very comfortable to walk around all day at school or work.

We bought these for a week of camping in the North Woods, as a girl alternative to the very expensive muck shoes the guys have. They fit true to size, were extraordinarily comfortable (and super cute), and worked perfectly for the campsite and for fishing on the boat.  We wore them pretty much the whole time with no discomfort or other issues. Highly recommend. Now that we are back home, they'll be our slip ons for rainy days until the next trip! Great value for the price!

I live in a rainy climate (sometimes 3 weeks straight of it) and saw these shoes on a friend and had to have them. I don't know why people would spend hundreds of dollars wearing bulky boots when these will do. The pattern is so cute too!

reviewText: I fell in love with these when I opened the box. The bright and colorful design is just perfect for inspiring the wearer to garden outdoors. They are very comfortable to walk in, with one tiny flaw (maybe related to the shape of my foot?). The right shoe somehow traps a bit of air so that as I take a step, you hear a funny squeaky sound. The left shoe doesn't do that. By wearing foot socks, that sound becomes nonexistent. I'm impressed that even though the bottom of the shoe has grooves in it (to prevent slipping?), and it may hold mud there, once dry, the mud pops off on its own like ice cubes from a rubber tray. Nice feature. A fun, happy shoe to wear!

I was using Crocs to walk the dogs, but hated them when it was wet outside. These are a really nice, good looking alternative. They are easy to slip on, they are comfortable, and keep your feet nice and dry. The downside is that they aren't warm other than the fact that they don't breathe and if you wear them too long your feet can become a bit damp. Overall though I wear them lots to walk the dogs and go the the market.
Perfect for working in the garden. Very comfortable! I found them true to size. However, I do have wide, flat feet.

reviewText: I needed shoes to wear in wet weather and these certainly fit the bill perfectly.  The insole is surprisingly comfortable, so much so that I wore these shoes all day at the office - and I use a stand-up desk - forgetting entirely to change into my dress flats. I couldn't be happier with this purchase.
Love them!! Delivered fast. I wear them to work and im always getting my feet wet, but they keep them dry!
These polka-dot sloggers are super-cute, and great for slopping around in the garden.  They look terrific, and are easy to slip into.
This is the best garden shoes I ever had.  It keeps my feet dry and warm, and best of all it is sooooo comfortable.
These are just lovely and I get a lot of complements when I ware them out in the rain. Run true to size as well.
I've had lots of garden shoes over the years, but this is the best for summer!  It's light weight, durable, true to size, and cute, cute, cute!
These are a little heavy, but very comfortable.  I wear them everywhere. I love them.  So easy to keep clean.

Dear Sloggers,Please make your excellent shoes in smaller sizes and in half sizes. These garden shoes are cute and seem to be made solidly (and in the USA). I normally wear 5.5 in dress shoes and 6 to 6.5 in tennis shoes. So I ordered the smallest size offered (6) and was hopeful that they would fit. However, when I tried them on they felt really loose. I took a few steps and the shoes fell off! So I tried putting on thick socks. The garden shoes still slipped off. I bought these hoping to tromp through my muddy yard while doing gardening and landscaping work. I can just imagine the shoes getting stuck in the mud and my feet coming right out as I try to walk! But now the hunt for good garden shoes continues...
Got these to take the dog out and get the mail, especially if it snows and I love them. Just might get another pair. My Husband is now looking to purchase a pair for himself. Very comfortable.

I chose a 5 star rating because they deserve a 5 star rating!I have 4 pair now, they are the most comfortable shoe I haveever put on my feet!  I have bought 5 other people some also and theyfeel the same way!!!

I purchased these Sloggers (rubber clogs) to have something to quickly slip into if I was going out in the rain or light snow.  They are perfect. Secondly, they keep my feet warm and dry.  I love them.  Perfect for my needs!

reviewText: I actually bought a pair of these super-cheap from Amazon warehouse, which rated the condition as "Very Good." Before I made the purchase I called Amazon to ask if I could return them if I wasn't satisfied, and Amazon said yes. Well, in fact, these were actually brand new, and I love them. It's hard to believe that rubber shoes can be so comfortable and permit your feet to breathe.

I received this shoe today. Colors are great but there is barely any cushioning on the sole( as it is claimed). I really wanted to like it, but the fit isn't right. It keeps on slipping out of the back. I typically wear size 7.5 wide so I got 8. I am afraid to exchange it with 7 because it may hurt my toes then.Here is one thing I want to mention (this may apply to some individuals)-- when I walk on these, it makes farting sound non-stop. LOL.

These are exactly what I was looking for when I'm gardening.  The bottom of the soles have deep treads that keep thorns from coming up through and also keep me from slipping.  They can be hosed off without damage and the insoles are also removable.  They are very comfortable even with socks and don't hurt my feet.

Bought these to replace an old pair of "throw on" shoes and so far so good! Bought a half size up and the Slogger "half-sizers" insoles to put in the shoes. The shoes themselves are great, the insoles - not so much. Had to get heel grips to add to the backs for the shoes to fit right. But I am not disappointed at all in the shoe itself. Just the right thing to go out in the rain with the dogs!
Love the shoes I have had lots of compliments on them already. May purchase another pair for my kids and myself.
Shoes fit well with good padding, quality construction. Easy to slip on. Colorful style. Would buy again. Fun to wear.
My feet were wet all of April, so this came at just the right time.  I look forward to enjoying these on man rainy days.

reviewText: They are comfortable, fit well (order up a half size) and keep your feet dry.  All for a great price!

I love these.  Really cute and so easy to slip on and off.  My gardening friends are eager to order similar ones.
I use ths shoe in the garden daily. I am an avid gardener. A quick spritz with the hose and all of the mud and dirt is washed away. Liner is also washable. Great find. I would order again.
