Option to display hunting vs fishing data at the touch of a button.Not so much: remote (outdoor) sensor frequently becomes un-synced from base station, esp. during colder weather despite fresh batteries. Have to unscrew the back of the remote sensor to change batteries and push the reset button and this is fussy. Remote sensor sometimes seems to report inaccurate temps but maybe that's because it's close to the house. A little tricky to set the tide station and other settings; for the love of god don't lose the instruction sheet as this is not intuitive. The # of tide stations available is a bit limited; serious fishermen may need a more expensive unit. Labels for the display numbers are tiny but not much of a problem once you get to know where each number is.Its not a watch as the title says, its a weather station. Have not yet checked the tide diagram accuracy against actual conditions or tried any of the alarm functions.

This bag is well made ang large enough to fit a few items. It is long enough to fit a gown. The hole where the hangers fit is reinforced.

I ordered this gown garment bag as well as dress bag and a suit bag.  I was so well pleased that I reordered another dress garment bag and two suit bags.  These garment bags are well made and each as a place for a cedar plank that can be replaced next year.JR

Bag is really nice. I purchased a few for my longer length dresses and evening gowns, unfortunately, I only got to keep one for my self. Got this for my doctoral robe and it's great.  It fully protects the garment and allows it to breathe as well.  It's really long so for someone who has a long gown as well.
just as described-nice construction.  Was able to store 4 long dresses (2 of them with full skirts).  The window is just a half window but was not a factor for me.

A very good bag.  It held up real well on my cruise and is still in great shape for me to use on the next one.  Definitely recommend fro the price.  I put 5 dresses in it and it could probably hold 2 more.

Just ordered this garment bag a few days and just received it.  Shipping was very fast, it was expected to arrive on the 28th but instead arrived on the 23rd.  The Garment bag is sturdy and really is great for several gowns.  It's great that it also has a window so that you can view what dresses you have inside.  Great Garment bag!

reviewText: This jacket fits true to size, but is a very european fit.  If you have a large chest/trunk, I would recommend going up a size.  The material does not stretch whatsoever, but I have fairly long arms and sleeve length is adequate.  Fabric, zippers, embroidery are all top notch.  The jecket hides better than most white jackets I've seen, only letting extremely dark shirts underneath show through a bit.  Very nice jacket overall.  Material could be a bit softer/stretchier, but that may change with wear.
Great boots in the perfect size for my son to feet over his big feet. and cheaper than i could have gotten locally

I grew up in a farm town. These are the boots I remember seeing farmers wearing at the feed store, in the hog lot, at the livestock auction.  They are heavy duty .. and be warned, after wearing these while chasing a wounded deer through a swampy area I really felt the weight.  Also-- and this is my own fault -- I am a big guy and my calves (on my legs, not from cows) are so large that I can't buckle the top two buckles.

The boots are sized properly to fit over shoes such as sneakers.  The tread provides good footing without being so deep that small stones lodge in the tread.  Since our driveways to the barn and other storage sheds are gravel, this has been an issue in the past.Since the flap inside is continuous the boots can be hosed down carefully without getting water inside the boots.We only had one problem.  Check your boots carefully when they arrive.  The first pair had a clasp missing.  However, return and replacement was very easy and the replacements were shipped the same day I printed out the return label.  They didn't wait for the package to return.All in all, a good product and good return procedure.
These boots split in the back and I ended up with wet feet.  I used them maybe 15 to 20 times before this happened.

I ordered these boots for my husband and son and they loved them!  My husband had been looking for the 5-buckle boots as he calls them, and when they arrived he was thrilled and so was my son.  I got them two sizes larger because you keep your shoes on with them and the fit(s) were perfect!  Great reproduction of an old-time item!

I bought these boots and we've had the warmest winter that I can remember. I never fired up my snow blower this winter. So, my review is based on the observed quality of these boots. They are easy to put on over shoes (I bought them one size larger than my shoe size to ensure easy use). They are very heavy rubber and it looks as if they'll be long lasting. These might be a bit too heavy if you walk a mail route but for the average snow shoveler or snow blower user I'm sure they'll work just fine. I really like the obvious quality of these boots. But I'd be happy not to use them next year, though. See? Global warming is never bad for everyone.
summary: These Boots Were Made For (snow) Walking

reviewText: Boots heal ripped after 4 times wearing.  Very dissatisfied. Do not buy this product. Very unhappy with quality of boot.

the boots are great and have had for a little over a year the steel toes are great but i cant stand when your walking or moving and u kick the back of your foot and it hurts but thats what you get for ordering steel toed rubber boots but other than that it is the best and cheapest rubber boot ive ever had in my life

reviewText: After several occasions of dealing with soaking wet shoes and socks, I decided to buy some rain boots for those awesome brew days. I figured 20 bucks why not? Great boots and the steel toe is a nice added touch when dealing with heavy stainless steel keggles. They do run a bit bigger than size but using thick socks does the trick.

The rain boots themselves are amazing and are of good quality, but I have never dealt with a pair of size 11 shoes/boots that were this huge. I had to return them and order a whole size down to a 10. Originally I thought I may have ordered an "over the shoe" by mistake, but after returning to my Amazon account, the description surely says "over the sock". Great quality, needs better sizing.

I chose these boots to ride quads in wet weather. They are steel toed and have worked great for this use. I had to wear 2 pairs of socks to keep my feet warm but I almost fully submerged the boots and didnt get a drop of water on my feet. Im very happy with these boots.

I bought these boots for my 12 years old son's camping trip. They are not fashionable but my son was very happy that those boots were so good during the camping trip as it rained a lot but his feet didn't get wet a bit.

I am a regular size 13 and after reading the comments indicating these boots run a little big, I thought I would be safe ordering size 13 as I like a little extra space in my shoes.  Well, I received them and they are narrow and two tight on my feet.  Definitely not a true 13 particually noticable when you try wearing them with a pair of thick socks.  I will return them for a size 15.

I was a little hesitant because my father-in-law wears size 9 and these pair is 9. Usually when buying boot they need to be a size bigger, specially if guys wear cotton socks. But he told me that they fit great and the steel toe was nice. They fit him right with socks on!
Bought these for working with cattle on muddy days.  Its a good solid farm muck boot.  Size was good. I am not gentle on these and they get tossed in the truck but have held up so far.
these boots are extremely durable,and seem very sturdy. they seem to be a bit roomy,but not enough to go a size larger. Steel reinforced to is excellent. Awesome find at a great price.
My boyfriend loved the hat.. but the shipping rate is ridiculous for a friggin foam hat. I could buy a better quality hat for the same price elsewhere.

I was looking for a new messenger bag for daily use for school, but after 3 days of use one of the straps starting to tear off, so i stop using it and i haven't been able to get it fix. I liked the bag, but i dont recommend it for daily use if you care more that a laptop and a notebook.

I bought this bag to use as my "personal item" on a trip to England—the idea was to carry an ipad, a few personal things, a notebook, etc. on an airliner. It fit nicely under the seat and handily carried the stuff I wanted to access during the flight. But after 3 days on the trip, the metal clasp that keeps the bag closed came apart. My handy spouse tried a fix, but the metal was so soft that the clasp wouldn't hold. In addition, the bag is heavier than it needs to be. Did that contribute to the clasp failure? Might have done.

I purchased this to carry a 13 inch laptop.  Once thing you'll definitely need in that case is a laptop sleeve, since this one lacks a padded pocket.  I bought a laptop sleeve and it actually fits perfectly in the "document pocket" on the back side, so that's where my laptop lives.Overall I really like it.  Utilitarian, plenty of pockets but not too big.  Here's the drawbacks:1. Stitching can be a little dodgy.  one of the strap loops gave out on me after about two weeks2. The water bottle pocket isn't nearly big enough for a normal water bottle3. The clasp to open the flap can be a little bit finicky.  I was initially concerned with wear, though it's holding up just fine, it's just a pain to get in some times.4. Stock strap is uncomfortable (I bought a new one and though it doesn't match the rest of the bag, it's a lot more comfortable)Now here's the things that really stand out as great:1. Quite versatile: lots of pockets and spaces that allow you to use it how you need to2. Large-ish amount of storage for a small bag like this3. The canvas is sturdy (except the stitching issue mentioned above)4. Is unobtrusive so it's not screaming "Steal me, I have an expensive laptop!" nor does it look like you just stole it off a hoboOverall, I'd recommend it.  The biggest issue was the stitching, which I feel like I might've got a bad one, and the strap, which is easily replaceable.
summary: Decent bag for a 13 inch laptop with plenty of extra space, but a little cheap in its construction

reviewText: I was really excited to get this bag. It has tons of pockets and lots of storage space. It's so heavy that the seams are coming undone even though I don't have much in it. Also, It can only be surface washed because of the board in it.
summary: I try to avoid using this bag

reviewText: I guess I was looking for some army surplus kind of stuff, and this bag looks really cool and pictures of it on Amazon make it look rugged and versatile.  In reality it isn't as versatile as it looks, you can't put much in it or it won't close right, and the handle is connected to the top flap so it doesn't carry right. As for rugged you can forget it. From day one it started losing thread, the seams started unraveling and the snap fell apart. Another total waste of my money.

I bought this bag to carry my research field gear (15-20 lbs). Everything fits in the bag comfortably and most items even have their own pocket, which is a plus. Unfortunately, during my first serious trip into the forest, the shoulder strap broke. The shoulder strap clips onto a small D-ring which is sewn into a loop on top of the bag. The sewing on the loop failed within the first mile of my hike. I had high hopes for this bag, but now I'm back to my old trusty backpack.

This has become my perfect traveling/take to work bag. It has enough pockets to keep all my gadgets and cords in, and has enough compartments that i can cary my lunch in as well. Perfect size for the ipad. Also I tried it out but haven't really used too much, but you can shove an ipad in the clear map pocket and be able to use it while its in there... great if your using in in a place where you want to protect it. Also small and comfortable enough to wear while on a motorcycle, so am very pleased.

It's a little over a month old, but it starts to fall apart. If you intend to use it, use it once a month as a purse - DON'T rely on it as your primary bag!1) It looks sloppy because there aren't enough hard parts to keep its shape.2) It is not meant for laptops. Even a small Dell D430 made the handle rip off. Don't even think about putting anything heavier than a book there.3) Velcros on the back flap clearly aren't meant for everyday use. They just screw up the fabric and make it look ugly.As someone who needs a reliable bag every day, I am very disappointed. Bad, predictably bad design.
This bag looks really cool, but the strap broke twice.  We exchanged it the first time, but the second time we just returned it.

That's right. I said it has cool compartments. I wish the water bottle holder was a tad larger. The canvas material seems durable enough, the zippers have me worried a little bit. It's comfortable to wear and holds more than I thought.

I love the capacity of the bag! Fits my books, laptop, notebooks and a whole bunch more! Its so big that for a short person like me (5'1'') it's a bit of an annoyance. It hangs down to my knees so I have to also carry it by the handle. If it wasn't for that I would have given it 5 stars! It seems sturdy and like it will last. Perfect bag if you live in the city and need to carry EVERYTHING in it while your out and about!
summary: Fits everything! but not the greatest for short people : (

reviewText: I like it -- plenty of pockets, though some may not be very useful (the map pocket in side the flap, for instance). It's bigger than it looks in the picture (check the dimensions) -- easily holds my 12 inch laptop; but get a neoprene sleeve for a laptop (no padding in the bag). I can't comment on durability, yet, but I like the soft, casual feel of the cotton canvas. And I wouldn't call it weatherproof, though I haven't gotten caught in the rain with it. It should be fine in light weather, but maybe not heavy rains? At any rate, I'm keeping mine.

I am very rough on bags and I can tell you this bag can take the bangs. It is a bit heavy once filled, but that isn't a problem for me because when you place journals, pens, keys, etc., in the bag, any bag will become heavy but not all bags can take the punishment.  This one does. I am tempted to order another, but I will wait and see how long this one lasts.  I have had it for about 5 weeks and love it!  I have no problems recommending it.  I especially like the top handle when the bag becomes a bit heavy for the shoulder you can switich to the top handle.  It serves me well and I'm sure it will serve you well if you need a rugged bag that looks well and wears well!  I live in NH and we have had a rough winter, but this bag has done well.  And, no I'm not part of the company, I just think when someone makes a good product they deserve the credit.  So far the bag works well for me.  Bill
summary: This is a MAN BAG that takes the BANGS!

reviewText: I liked that this bag has so many pockets and places for things.  I HATE digging through a purse or bag. I knew it was a large bag, cuz I did read the size description.  I just had high hopes that it wouldn't be too big for what I needed it for. It was. A great bag for anyone who needs a big, cool bag!  :o)
summary: Great bag! Too big for what I wanted it for...

reviewText: My 16 year old son wanted a shoulder bag for school this year.  He told me he likes it a lot.  He carries it to school daily.  I am happy with the construction of the bag.  It seems to be very durable.  After a month of being in school, the bag still looks brand new.  I am happy I purchased this bag for him.

I bought this bag to carry my laptop and some paper work to take on the airplane for a trip.  I had a pretty light load in it.  While at the airport, the stitching came loose around the strap and the strap came off.  The weight of the bag ought to have been easily handled.  I had to carry the bag for the rest of the trip.I am really unsatisfied with the quality of this bag.  It looked so promising.

So, being the guy I am, I like a good, manly bag.  None of this purse crap, right?  So I did some research, and this is the bag that won.  I've owned a couple messenger bags in the past, but felt like nothing really fit correctly in them.  My laptop bag is the same style as this bag - instead of  the "landscape" orientation that you get with messenger bags, this is a "portrait" orientation.  I've owned this bag for a little over nine months now, and it's more durable than any bag I've ever had before.  When I bring it to work, I can fit any tools I need, a coffee cup, an ipod, and headphones in it, along with various pens, my phone, and a charger.  When I'm out and about, I can carry a sweater, my tablet, a notebook, and anything that I might come across in my journeys.  The bag holds just about as much as I can comfortably carry around in a day without being overly uncomfortable or heavy.  It seems to be the perfect size, and due to its slimmer, longer profile, doesn't seem to get caught on anything or anyone while on an airplane or public transportation. I do have few complaints, though.  One of which is the strap.  It's attached to the bag via the top - and many other reviewers complained about this.  The strap on mine has come off twice.  I took this bag to a tailor, and they fixed it for about $22.00 dollars the first time, and after the strap came off again, they repaired it for free.  My other complaint - the large pocket on the outside of the main compartment, inside the flap has a sharp edge that I have cut my finger on a few times.  There's a learning curve to this bag.Update:  Two years later and the bag is still ticking.  It fits everything. I love it and when fails (not in foreseeable future) I intend on rebuying.Update 2:  This bag finally failed.  The clasp on the bag gave out, and I tried to replace it myself but was unsuccessful. I purchased a new one immediately and received it today.  I believe the first one I received was a knock off - the build quality of the new bag is top-notch and it has Rothco labels sewn onto the inside. Also, the clasp is a different build - similar in function but not cheap looking.  Neither of which applied to the original, might I add.  I haven't had a chance to test the new one out, but I'll post a review of it.  I'm demoting a star from this because of how the new one looks and feels and because the original just didn't cut it.

You may notice some of the reviews for this bag which claim that the strap broke shortly after purchase like I did.  I'm writing this review in order to tell everyone out there not to ignore those reviews like I did.I purchased this bag for my big weekend at Dragon*Con.  I was initially pleased with the bag as it's many pockets and pouches held everything I wanted them to with room to spare. Two Nintendo DSs, 3 decks of Magic:tG cards, one netbook, a plethora of pens and pencils, a journal, sketch pad, and notebook.The bag performed admirably the first day.  By day two the stitching near the handle strap connection started to fray and by Sunday both sides of the strap had ripped off and I'd clipped it to the handle just to get by but even that ripped by the end of the day.This is not a military surplus bag, it's not the bag the military uses, it's not even a replica of the bag the military uses, and it is certainly not an engineer's bag.  Unless of course you're an engineer who's supplies consist of feathers, tissue paper and bubble wrap.Don't ignore the negative reviews and don't buy this bag.

He was carrying around a back pack & now he has a sturdy bag with compartments and the option to carry it on his shoulder.  He keeps commenting that it is sturdier than his back pack and really likes it, plus has a more professional look.

The design of this bag is very useful, however the quality of the shoulder strap/carry handle webbing attachment is very weak. My first M-51 lasted a few months before the webbing attachment failed. I ordered a new one and it only lasted two weeks before failing in the same place.  Made in INDIA.

This is a great bag - holds everything I need it to for the daily to and from the office trek. Lots of places to put things and keep them handy. The clear plastic sleeve on the inside of the flap is genius - I can put files in it and even notes to self that stay visible. It's very durable, and is well made. I'm happy with this purchase.

Like other reviews said I can't believe someone thought it was agood idea to have the straps attached to the top, on the part that opens, instead of the sides!? Mine is working ok so far sometimes I fill it full of heavy college books, it is sooo heavy but it hasn't broken... yet. I can tell It will sooner or later though. I think the most that should prob. be put in it is one big book and binder, if you don't want it to wear out fast. The metal closure in the front is going to give out before the straps ever will, but it's because the straps are attached to the flap instead of the sides, cause all that weight is putting stress on that little metal peice that turns to close. Lots of places to put stuff but I don't recommend it if you want to carry heavy stuff. I've been using it for almost 6 weeks now and I like it but it's too heavy to carry 2 books & 2 binders, I'm starting to carry half in it and the other half in my hands. I still like it though and soon I won't have so much heavy stuff to carry.

After reading the reviews on here I decided to go ahead and order one. I recently ordered one of those Rotopunch tools they have commercials for on tv, and plan to modify the bag a little to fix the issues mentioned in the lesser reviews. Hopefully moving the anchors for the strap will help with weight redistribution, and a few heavy duty brass snaps will secure troublesome pockets.
summary: Looking forward to getting this M-51

reviewText: I bought this bag for a few hand tools and note books.I loved all the little pockets.Then the strap broke.I was sad.

I love the overall design of this bag. However, I did have to immediately replace the clips for the shoulder strap. The clips which came with the bag were very lightweight, and because they had no capacity to swivel, were very insecure. If the strap was twisted, they would pop right off. Fortunately, new clasps are cheap.Another slight problem is the location of the handle/attachment points for the shoulder strap.  The handle is inexplicably offset from the load bearing structure of the bag. To lift the bag by the handle or shoulder strap is to lift it by the flap that covers the compartment. This actually wouldn't be a problem, if the front flap were longer, but as it is it puts a lot of stress on the front clasp. I added a couple of D rings an inch or so back, attached to the main body of the bag, to take the stress off the front clasp.The only other small complaint is that both side compartments could be bigger.  The larger one is barely large enough for a small water bottle. It would be nice to be able to carry even a 20 oz soda bottle, but that is more than this side compartment can handle. It is a fairly good fit  for for an iphone in an otterbox though. I have yet to find a use for the smaller one.
Great item

I got this bag for my husband who is an Architect,  he is really happy with the quality of the product and very impressed with the amount of compartments that it has.You have room for everything you need out on the field.

The strap is made of low-quality canvas material that is too narrow and cuts into my shoulder with only an iPad mini, a book, and a bottle of water. The "pad" on the strap is nothing more than the same material attached by a few loops. It is fairly uncomfortable even with a light load. The hooks are attached to the "handle" on the top flap and are already showing signs of strain. The "reinforced" pockets appear to be nothing more substantial than cardboard sewn between two layers of the canvass. The two side pockets are too small for water bottles, and I certainly would not put anything of value in those pockets because the flaps are held in place with inexpensive eye and hook fasteners. The rear pocket side zipper opens if the items in this pocket are too heavy.  The large center pocket is great, but it is covered by a flap of canvas that is not water-resistant despite the plastic lining on the inside of the flap. I would never use this bag in a light mist and definitely not in the rain or snow.  I gave this bag three stars because I need the pockets and the dimensions are perfect,  but I only use it when I am carrying just my iPad mini, a book, and a bottle of water, and the weather is assuredly dry.  For another $20 or so you can find a better made bag on Amazon as good as if not better than this one and for the extra money, a better made bag is a better return on your investment.

The handle frayed, and one of the seams attaching the handle to the bag ripped off within a year of purchase. If you're planning on putting more in this bag than a legal pad a paperback or two, buy something sturdier.

I am enjoying the bag quite a bit.  It was larger that I was expecting, but not too large. (Review the dimensions again, trust me) It is quite sturdy and will stand up on its own--which is handy.  I've had other bags in the past that look great but aren't very sturdy and that becomes inconvenient.  The bag has been a hit with my guy friends as well and 2 of them have ordered it for themselves.  It has lots of space for pens, pencils, keys, cell phone, files, etc.  I don't see myself changing from it soon.

This bag only rates a single star as it is minimally useful, and I can't give it a lesser review.  I've ordered this bag twice and returned it both times for quality issues.  While well laid out with useful pockets and organization features, it is shoddily made- both examples I received had stitching that was unraveling on key seams, and musty, funky smells. The single stitching used to attach the shoulder strap to the top of the bag will give way under strain. My second bag had rust stains around the clasp and blue dye stains on the back.  The panels that give the bag its shape appear to be cardboard. The untreated canvas is going to absorb moisture and stain rather easily.Excellent size and layout, and I really like the look- if only it had been made by workers who cared about it, and spec'd with quality materials.My advice- look elsewhere, especially if you intend to carry anything weightier than a small paperback in this bag. I am soured on this manufacturer's products now.

This bag is made of heavy-duty canvas that will take abuse.  It's got plenty of places for keys, pencils, business cards, etc., plus external zip pockets for stowing things without stopping -- like receipts, tickets, flyers, and things you're handed while traveling.  It's large enough to hold notebooks and magazines, as well as most laptop computers. And it always amazes me that when you set it down, this bag stands up on its own. The canvas makes it a little heavy, but the extra weight gives you durability.

I purchased this bag about 3 months ago to carry a tablet computer and school items. The stitching that held the shoulder strap tore, I attempted to fix it and now all of the stitching that holds the handle and strap is torn. I don't have the tools to repair thick fabric, so I'm either going to try some other strap or get it repaired.I've read a few other reviews that talked about the stitching, they're right. If you're looking for this type of bag, I recommend you look at something else.
bagprosgood priceresistantmany bagsconsits heavyslightly wrong sewnif the bag is placed horizontally, something small can escape

putting the handle on the main flap puts a lot of stress on the teeny weenie black clasp' and throws the balance of the whole bag off.more unforgivably, they also put the STRAP on the main flap, instead of along the sides! I might actually try sewing for the first time in my life to remedy this.i'm using it for a few papers and various odds-and-ends (not books or a laptop -- more like my ipod charger, a multitool, mini flashlight, a few crayons for the kids, that sort of not-heavy stuff) so the weight i'm putting in it shouldnt put too much stress on this bag's weak spots, but if you're looking for something to regularly carry more than one heavy textbook or a fat old laptop, look elsewhere! (iPads would be okay, tho.)other points:Nice soft fabric feels nice. Lots of pockets, but only one iphone-sized pocket on the outside that i trust enough to put an iphone into. Lots of pen-sized pockets. Nice rear flap that opens up to reveal another dozen pouches.TLDR: For light use only! Not a laptop bag or backpack!
summary: same problem as every other cheap-but-cool bag!

reviewText: I have had briefcases, bakcpacks, messenger bags and sling bags.  This bag kicks the crap out of all of them.  It has sewn in pockets for more than 10 pens/pencils.  Pockets on the side for tape measure (I keep my iPod charger and cord there) and cell phone and pockets in the back flap for more tools and pens.  I can carry a couple of notebooks, magazines, a book and it will still fit a full-sized laptop. Recently, I took a trip and all of my gadgets and travel documents were very easy to reach and put away. I would not trade this for anything else!
This is my daily working bag and i love it.  This great bag is sturdy has all necessary pockets.  It is confortable and arrived on time.

It looks a lot nicer in the photos than it does in reality. Sort of like a hamburger on a McDonald's commercial or coupon versus the real thing. It frayed easily with a little bit of use in the field. The bottle holder on the side might - keyword "might" - hold a juice box for a small child. Or maybe some pens. Don't waste your money on this one.

This is what I was looking for for long time purchased bags that look good and nice but when I received I was unhappy, I'm in the IT service and this bag can hold my laptop and all my tools plus pickup rollers for printers and plotters. on a compact bag.  :-)
summary: ... looking for for long time purchased bags that look good and nice but when I received I was unhappy

reviewerName: James D. Lellman "jack of all trades"
reviewText: After only a few weeks of infrequent use, the strap broke completely off. Don't buy this.

I bought this bag because I needed something to carry my medical supplies in...what I got, was a HUGE surprise as to just how much this bag actually holds.Before buying this bag, I would carry 2 - 3 separate bags; 1 for medical supplies, 1 for personal items, & sometimes 1 for clothing items.Having bought this bag, I now carry only one bag for everything.This is a very well made 100%  22 oz cotton canvas bag.The flap that covers the front of the bag has a large pocket on both the inside AND the outside; when you open the flap, there are pockets for a small note pad & pens/pencils; a pocket for cell phone/keys/ what have you; there is a LARGE inside pocket that can hold a pair of blue jeans, a T-Shirt, underwear, socks & an extra pair of shoes.On the back side of the bag there is a zipper that goes from the left side all around to the right side; inside this is a medium sized pocket; across from that(also on the backside of the bag) is a medium sized pocket along with some small pockets for various goodies you may wish to carry.I know that some women use this for a purse & now that I own one, I can understand why. There is very little that this bag can not hold, including but not limited to, a 17 inch lap top computer.I highly recommend this bag, you will not be disappointed.
The quality of the bag is okay. Can't take much weight because the stitching is coming out after one month of minimal usage. Should be used mainly for carrying work folders, iPads & laptops

I was looking for a smaller bag to ferry things back and forth to work. Didn't need or want a laptop bag. It will carry my netbook with ease if I need it to. Very impressed with the number and variety of pockets everywhere. Very tough...well made. I do have some trouble with the clasp on the bottom sometimes...but overall, not really an issue. I like how it looks and functionally, its the best I've ever seen while keeping the overall size down. I'd recommend it to anyone. You may want to cushion the shoulder strap.
It's exactly what I was hoping for!It carries everything, and there is no cheap lining in the pockets to fray and rip!Very sturdy!

I purchased this bag to carry my school books and papers, as well as a laptop for class.  I must say I was pleasantly surprised when it arrived and everything fit.  The main pocket has plenty of space for 2 large textbooks and a notebook.  Also, the back pocket is perfect for a small laptop and you can fit the charger in easily too.  Their are plenty of pockets for pens, calculator, phone, and any other accessories you want to carry.  The strap is heavy duty and doesn't even seem to be straining with all of the weight in it.  I am very happy with it so far and I am glad I made the purchase.

I love the bag.  It looks great.  It's the perfect size for me.  But yesterday the shoulder strap broke, specifically where the shoulder strap attaches to the bag itself.  I've been carrying a lot of junk around in it, but the load was relatively light when the strap broke.  I'm disappointed that it only lasted 6 months.

Definatly a little "light" in the durability department.  I would have gladly paid an extra $5 to be put into the main strap clips, and the closing mechanism (mine broke clean off).A good-looking bag, but really should have been a little better made.

Excellent field bag.  Although a bit large it will replace my two camera bags when going out for the day.  Plenty of room for specimens (if you tend to come home with your pants pockets full of stuff), laptop, mouse, power supply, phone, ipad/pod/pick, etc.Not Mil-spec, but close.  Canvas is soft and doesn't have the military oil-like smell (that's a plus).  The back opens up book-style and was a pleasant surprise.  Looks like a person could take notes if you put a note pad back there.  The side pockets can hold small items and the large one can hold a water bottle, but not very well.  If you absolutely need to take a water bottle on your field excursion you can fit several of them in the main compartment or in the front flap. I prefer a camel back to toting around water bottles, anyway.****UPDATE****After using this bag on a trip with a moderate amount of stuff in it the bag ripped loose where the carrying strap attaches to the bag, making me unable to carry the bag except with the handle.  I am very disappointed.  I may get the bag repaired at a canvas shop.  3 stars since the rest of the bag still works.
I originally found this in a review in Make Magazine. Everyone said it was amazing. It is amazing. Enough said.

The bag is nice, heavy fabric, lots of pockets, nice strap, I'd have given it 5 stars, IF the twist closure hadn't pulled off the first time my son used it! The twist part is held onto the bag by two VERY flimsy metal prongs that go through the fabric and a reinforcement piece below, and are then bent over. But I could bend these prongs with my fingers! I'm looking for some way to fix this, as otherwise, the bag is great.

I wanted something a little more rugged for my computer, and was astounded at the prices of designer messenger bags (basically Man Purses)This thing is heavy duty. If you review a 22oz canvas bag as being too heavy, you should look into your materials more prior to purchase.Build quality is about on par with made in India product. Slightly off centered clasp a couple uncut threads. All in all though its definitely got the storage you need and even a bit of padding for the computer itself. loads of various compartments.

I have had this bag for a couple of weeks now. It has more compartments than I know what to do with. After reading reviews about the weak plastic clip thing that holds the flap, I have been careful with it; hasn't broke yet. As for the side compartments, one holds my keys and the other my sunglasses.All around great bag for the price.***I am an environmental engineer and I use it everyday going to the office and out in the field.
It was completely different from its picture online. I did not like this product at all and I advice people not to buy it. If I could I would have given it a 0.

This bag is the perfect size for me.  Smaller than a messenger bag yet large enough to hold all items I need for a day outing.  I have also purchased the Rothco Map Case in the past which I also like but this M-51 bag is what I will be using most often.  It is well structured and has many useful compartments.  I purchased this from Direct Premium Buys who shipped me a genuine Rothco bag which I have found not all sellers do.

Yeah, this pack is a bit off.  The licking mechanism is finicky, and not very strong looking.  The shoulder strap I had to re sew with nylon string as it was unwinding, and the strap itself keeps crunching up on the shoulder, making it uncomfortable.  Some of the pockets in this bag I just don't understand.  For example, one of the big pockets on the side has a Velcro seal, but there is a zipper under it that goes to the same pocket.  If you accidentally unzip it, or it gets caught, or even after time the zipper kept creeping, you just lost everything in that pocket.  Horrible design that I can't understand why they put it in.
summary: Not that good looking, and some poor designs

reviewText: I read reviews about the poor design on the strap buckles BUT sadly did not heed the warnings.  This is a very poor design and the strap buckle broke on my second trip!  If you intend to use this bag over the shoulder, then DO NOT BUY, you WILL be disappointed!

I'm a case manager and have been looking for a bag with wide openings so things wouldn't get stuck on the narrow corners as I pull papers, binders, and a laptop out many times/day.  I also wanted a tall bag, not wide. I went as far as to measure the dimensions I needed to fit all of my items into one bag (I hate carrying around multiple bags).  This was the only one I found that lived up to all my needs.  It can hold a great deal of items and has many compartments.  It's not really fashionable, and if you're small like me it looks like it's bigger than you!  But it holds everything I use (laptop + mouse+2 power cords+2 other items, clip board, multiple pens/pencils/markers, large hand sanitize, papers, keys, 2 cell phones, 3 note pads, a few file folders and some other small stuff).  Having the shoulder strap is great, but being short like me, it's not very comfortable at times because the plastic threading thing sits on the top of your shoulder and the comfort strap does not cover it... but I try to not carry it for too long as it is heavy with the amount of items I have.  Alone, this bag is really light (so if you don't have the office in your bag like I do, it won't be a problem).I would recommend this bag if you're looking for functionality, lots of space, multiple compartments, and being tall not wide! (And for the price... I couldn't find anything more reasonable!)

So I like this bag, Seems like something made purposely imperfect. It's the cheapest messenger type bag I could find that was just black and simple in design. Make sure your laptop will fit, my Dell XPS 15.3' does not. It has a lot of useful pockets, made of some very strong and durable material. This will not rip or tear easily.
summary: Great bag - feels like something made purposely imperfect

reviewText: This bag is ideal if taking a journey and want to keep all accessories with you and strap across to be hands free.
The bag is heavy duty.  I was able to carry a computer, lots of paperwork and a few clothes. It had plenty of pockets for everything else.  It was perfect for airplane travel.

As a Texas Master Naturalist in East Texas, I'm often tramping through forests and woodlands and this bag is perfect for carrying books, small binocs, camera, etc. I use it a lot and it gets thrown in the back of my truck or on the ground but it's held up well.  The ONLY negative I have is that the two side pockets on the outside of the bag are pretty usesless.  They aren't large enough for a bottle of water and anything you may put in them could easily fall out.  That said, I love this bag; it's exactly what I needed.

Recommended. Good product and fast shipping. Reliable services with quick response. Love this product and was satisfied to get what was actually advertised. I love this bag. It fits my iPad along with the rest of my crap just perfectly.

So I got this bag because when doing surveys, punch list or construction observation I always have to carry STUFF.  Online, it seemed like it would work and it does.  It has an outside pocket that fits perfectly my 25' measuring tape, another one for my cell phone, a pen/pencil organizer which is a must and main pockets for writing pads and sketches.  I use the bottom horizontal pocket for things like  tissue, chapstick, a small bottle of hand sanitizer, ear plugs and hand wipes.  The space is realistic and generous, made out of canvas with good stitching gives you a sense of confidence that it will not quit on you in the middle of a survey.  The smaller pocket next to the pen/pencil organizer fits my point and shoot camera when it would be too risky to take the SLR.  The only things that would make this bag perfect would be a non collapsible pocket for a couple of dust masks, a pocket for some safety glasses, some kind of clipping accessory so hang a hard hat on the outside, and also the strap used to grab the bag from the top (not the shoulder strap) that it could be reversed to loop around a roll of plans.  I carry this bag across my body with the pocket for the measuring tape facing the front and the easiness of reaching and putting away the tape to write something down is my favorite feature.  It is made to fulfill it's intent, to be a field bag.
summary: Out in the field; what to do with all this junk!

reviewText: Bought this for my husband to carry his iPad and a couple other items.  Fell apart after a month.  Buckle broke, tried fixing it and then strap broke.

This is a great bag, but...I really thought it was smaller and it's as big as any messenger bag out there. Beware if you are shopping for this to be used as a mid-size or satchel bag.When I made additional research and found out the reality I was unable to cancel the purchase and being over seas its a hazel to return the package that less then US$100.00 purchase. So I decided to keep it and use it as a regular messenger back instead of a small shoulder bag that was my original intention of purchase.Nice pockets and compartments, but I give it 3 starts because of the misleading description.

I bought this bag as a mobile professional, I wanted something that was both large in capacity not in size as well as very compartmentalized.  The bag's layout is nearly perfect, with only a few strange design decisions marring its utility.  For the price it was good but inside 2 weeks of use several components broke already.  That being said of products on the market this one is pretty unique, especially with the fold out back.  The key flaw that bothers me is the placement of all lift on the top of the flap.  I plan to correct at least the strap placement myself with the handle being of less concern.  I'll get into why its a major set back in cons below.The Good:Great material and general build quality, the layout of pouches etc is perfect and this bag is just extremely functional for any mobile professional weather a journeymen or a businessman.  The inside of the flap has a clear plastic sleeve great for placing a map or something else you would like to be able to view at leisure without handling it.  The back folds open to expose a great series of pouches for storing anything from small camera components to art supplies to tools.  The back aslo still functions with a separate flap as a quick access Velcro pouch for things you'll regularly need to get your hands on. The front, interior and sides are pretty typical bag layout with pouches and pen holders and a pocket perfectly sized for a note/address book.  You can fit up to a 16.5" laptop in this bag and still have room for a DSLR and some other toys/tools.The Bad:Cheap parts, the zipper pulls(the little string extensions not the zipper itself) are horrible, first thing I pulled one off with a gentle tug when opening a compartment.  Then the snap for the flap broke by the end of the week, note I only take my bag to work and back with me no back packing or anything intense it just broke when I was walking down some steps.  The shoulder strap is not of the same quality as the rest of the bag, while its made of the same material the stitching is not as neat, the clips don't swivel and the shoulder pad adds no comfort.  I would immediately replace this if I were going to travel with the bag.The snap breaking wouldn't be an issue if it wasn't so necessary.  The flap needs the snap because the strap and handle are secured to the flap.  This means that when you lift your bag you open it up to an extent.  The simple act of putting the shoulder strap so it lifts from the side would have alleviated many issues, as is you can't flip open the top and easily access the guts of the main reservoir with the bag hanging from your shoulder.  This is a HUGE mistake, and it seems like a rather stupid one with only 5 minutes of demoing the bag you'd have realized this limitation.  Shoulder bags are becoming more popular with fellas as they add function you can carry and access them more easily than a back pack etc, that is not the case here.Conclusion:This product is a series of trade offs.  To get a bag of this size with a similarly functional layout would typically be 4 times as much if you could even find its unique combination of features.  Sadly silly oversights are extremely damaging to this bags function.  A better strap attachment point would have simply removed the need for a flap fastener in the first place, lol.  Zipper pulls always tear away over time so that doesn't bother me too much.  However my brother was looking at getting the same bag different color as he loves the size/utility of it but I warned him away sighting my concerns and he agreed.  I'm a pretty pro-active consumer and will simply get strap clips stitched onto the side of the bag to resolve that major issue and keep on using it.  Being that it will hold the laptop I'm going to get and the camera I have plus attachments I'm a pretty happy guy at 35 dollars, still I don't understand why these cost free revisions weren't embraced as they would take this from a C product in need of light costumer modding to a AAA bargain.
Its a great field bag for investigators, engineers and surveyors. It holds everything I need and its tough enough for field work. The best part is that it is actually washable. I love it.

This bag was a purchase for school books and drafting tools.  When it arrived I noticed many more pockets than those visible in the dark pictures.  Under the main flap are located enough pockets to fit six pens, a calculator, pocket dictionary, hand sanitizer bottle, flash drive in a pocket, and a pocket for miscelaneous drafting tools.  The back pocket unzips out to become a horizontal flap exposing two more rows of approximately two finger pockets and a note pad pocket.  I was surprised at the space of the main pocket which will fit a large laptop, however I doubt textbooks will fit at the same time.  The material was of a heavier canvas than I was expecting.  The strap seems of a quality to stand up to carrying books for one class at a time; possibly two books if not of the medical field. I look foreward to field testing this bag.
Very practical. Lots of pockets .I just like it and it met my expectations .Good quality materials and solid crafmanshift.

I was surprisingly ok with the size. I love love love all the pockets but most of them are open.  If the pockets were secure in some way I'd be more inclined to keep it.  This is my carry-my-crap-to-work bag and I have way too many little bits & pieces for them not to be secure.  I like them organized so putting them in a big zipper pocket isn't an option.  The water bottle pocket is, as usual, too small for much of anything, I kept my keys in it.  It came with a grease smudge on the flap. That and the pocket problem is what made me send it back.

I bought this bag for my school books and absolutely loved it until the buckle popped off after only two days of using it.  The carrying straps are attached to the top cover that buckles down and not to the sides of the bag.  This causes the weight of the bag to be put on the buckle and not the bag itself.  Don't expect this bag to hold the weight of three paperback college textbooks (two small and one regular sized) and a pad of paper without having problems with the buckle.  If it didn't have this problem then I would still be in love with all the pockets and places to organize my things.

I bought this bag in May of 2011 and wore it for a year as a student until April of 2012 when the fastener broke.  I admit I put a lot of books in it and the weight of what you put in the bag bears on that one little turn buckle at the bottom.  I'm disappointed because I really love the bag.  The material and everything else is in great shape.  So I bought 2 alternative clasps I'm going to try and sew on and see if that works.  If not, I'll probably buy a different bag but I really wish I could resurrect this one.
summary: Great bag but the turn buckle broke

reviewText: Bought this bag and i must say i liked it very much for the first three weeks.  It felt sturdy, lots of pockets.  My disappointment came when one day i reached into the backseat for the bag and the strap got caught between the seat and the door, not in the door but between the seat and the door.i pulled, ok i tugged, and the strap gave way!! WTH!!! Just like that???!!!  i mean it says a "engineer" and "field" in the name.  Don't engineers and people out in the field, tug at their bags??? Ok maybe i am read too much into the name. In looking at where the strap gave way it appears the stitching was done too close to the edge.Needless to say I was truly disappointed in the quality of the stitching.  Not to be outdone i got it sewed back and the bag feels really sturdy now, i can tug the strap!!.  had the other side also sewn up also.Overall the bag is nice just be aware it does not like to be tugged at, and if you do you might have to effect your own repair.

This is my favorite bag for fitting all of my crap in that I need when working on site.  It's got all of the right pockets in all of the right places, something that I can't find in any other bag.  I overpack this thing to the limit - lots of stuff fits in all of the various pockets.  I really like the clear document pocket in the flap for storing certain papers that I need to access easily.However, the strap pulls out within about 8 to 10 months of once-a-week or so use.  Since the bag shoulder strap is supported from the flap and not from the sides of the bag like most other bags, it pulls out within about 8 to 10 months of use.  If I do indeed buy another one of these bags (looking for alternatives as I just broke my second one of these bags), I will sew alternative strap attachment points on to the sides of the bag since I usually use the shoulder strap and not the handle for carrying the bag.Another issue that I had recently, also due to the bag being supported from the top of the flap, was that the flap closure pulled out.  Again, this could easily be alleviated by attaching the strap to the sides of the bag.  That one change would make this bag just about perfect.
summary: Great, but I have to get a new one every year.

reviewText: I bought this as opposed to the others around Amazon for a couple reasons:1. Smaller size is more suited as I'm not a laptop user and big messenger/laptop bags get annoying.2. The canvas material has an awesome texture/color.I was not dissapointed on either of these points and was pleasantly surprised on a couple more;3. The locking mechanism is pretty nice. No annoying velcrow RRRRIIIPPPP yet still nothing too complicated.4. It could actually fit a laptop vertically.. (not a netbook either, a full size laptop)I highly reccomend it!

Not just for men--I'm a woman in my mid-twenties and I LOVE THIS BAG! It was given to me as a gift and the first thing I noticed was the nice, simple style. The heavy-duty canvas exterior is lovely left plain, but is also a great canvas for personalization. The next thing I noticed was the quality of construction--it's quite well-made. I love the reinforced back zipper pouch--it's actually the perfect size for my 13" Macbook Pro in its sleeve, and the solid construction of the bag makes me feel secure about carrying my laptop in it. The third thing I noticed is all the different pouches and pockets--some I haven't even used yet! It makes my little geeky heart very happy knowing that there is a place for all my stuff in this bag. The strap is well-constructed and solid, highly adjustable, and comfortable to wear. This is the perfect bag for classes, everyday use, and travel. I absolutely love it.

I purchased this item for my husband and he loves it. I did not think that the quality of the cloth would be sturdy, but it actually is. Its a good size, and can fit a textbook in there (textbook as in something akin to the heavy science textbooks. You can fit a lot of items in the bag itself. However it did not come with a strap, and I am not sure if it does? If yours does not come with a strap then you can always buy one from target or any other store near the luggage section. The product itself is made in India.

The bag is really good for the price. However, the quality of sewing is not the highest. I also found this bag to be somewhat heavier than I expected.This bag is roomy and has several compartments that can help to keep everything organised. The rear compartment is similar to map compartments in military bags: it can be unzipped and unfolded.

I got what I paid for but... they could have spent a little more time on the stitching and the buckles are pretty cheap. The fastener that holds the main flap pulled out of the canvas after 2 weeks of daily use. I only carry a tablet and a portfolio, not a heavy load.
summary: Looks nice but it lacks alot.

reviewText: This bag is cool looking and useful.  I took this bag on a 6 month trip through Asia.  It lasted 4 months, which was pretty good considering the wear and tear I gave it and the fact it costs 35 bucks.  Ultimately, it frayed where the shoulder strap buckles attach to the body, as another review also mentions.  I liked it and would buy another for a similar trip.  The major upside to the bag is that it is usefully designed with a lot of pockets (some outside, some inside, some hidden) for pens, phone, computer, books, passport, cash, etc., and it is nice looking without being expensive looking.  I liked that aspect of it when traveling in poorer places such as the Philippines where carrying a fancy bag on the street would have been out of place and would have marked me as a wealthy target for crime.  Finally, the fact that it only cost 35 bucks meant I could throw it away without regrets when it frayed and at the same time I was headed for Singapore, where my expensive leather briefcase was more appropriate.  It would also be a good bag for a student on a budget, with the proviso that you might have to replace it or repair it after a year or so if you stuffed it with heavy books.  One last thing: the dye (at least on the black model) rubs off on your pants if you do a lot of walking with the bag rubbing against them.  The pants come clean in the wash, though.
summary: good bag worth more than the price

reviewText: I really like my bag. I found several areas to make improvements, I put a thin metal sheet in the clear slip cover in the main flap that way I can fill altoid tins (with small magnets in the bottoms) with my small items and keep them handily displayed for easy access. I would like to see a better clasp on the front flap but I will see to that soon myself. My only problem so far is the tendency to over pack it and make it to heavy, because of the many pockets and room it has available. I will also improve the strap to compensate for the heaviness of my bag (my problem). I would suggest this bag to anyone who likes a bag with many pockets and likes to find a place for all their little stuff they like to carry around. It seemed like I was discovering pockets for the first several weeks I carried the bag.

Very well made bag . Like the how easy it is to organize my things in it. This is the second one of these I've bought. The first being for my teenage son. He has had his for at least two years and it is holding up nicely through all of his adventures. Not sure about the negative. Not sure about the nature of the negative comments, about the durability of the bag. Those comments almost made me not buy it. I am glad I did.

The bag is wonderful, if you are going to carry tools or things for school or work I would recommend it completely. The thing s that the size is considerably larger than you expect... the measurements given seem like an understatement. Love the bag, though. The build is amazing and will probably last for quite a while.
summary: You just don't expect the size.

reviewText: This bag holds everything but the kitchen sink.  I have to take a lot of stuff with me when I go to work, I was having to carry more than one bag to take it all.  Now I don't.  Easy access to things you need a lot, I am simply in love with this bag.

The clasp that holds the opening flap down broke within a day of use. Using superglue does not fix it, since the weight of the bag stupidly pulls on the clasp when over the shoulder. I suppose I can still use the bag without fully closing it, but it looks a bit disheveled. I hope the strap doesn't break soon too like other reviewers said :/. I like the design of the bag, but it is built like garbage. For 35 bucks you should really be getting at least a year out of it, not a day. Regret the purchase.

I like the bag but it super heavy. I picked it because I thought the canvas would be light.  I didn't anticipate that it would be so heavy.  I was looking for a light weight bag.  I am going to take it apart and remove the plastic that is causing the weight.
I traded my old briefcase for this engineers bag.It's a little heavy with all my work items, may need to find a better shoulder strap for this bag.

When I received this bag, I was ecstatic. It was everything I had hoped for, and that's saying something. It was small enough that I wouldn't be able to make it twenty pounds overweight as things accumulated, but it was large enough that it had room for everything I would need.It is also an organizational dream. It has a wide variety of pockets, pouches, compartments, and pencil holders which gives you a place to put literally everything. When I used it, I carried a textbook or two, two notebooks, pens, pencils, replacement lead, my kindle, my water bottle, a multitool, a small flashlight, my kindle charger, my ipod, my ipod charger, my phone, and a few granola bars.Sadly, about a month and a half into using it, it broke on me. The D-ring where the strap clips to the top of the bag frayed off, followed by more fraying in other areas.I'm sure I could fix it if I really wanted to, but I'd really rather not have to reinforce it myself.If they built this exact bag from more durable materials, I'd be all over it. It really is perfect for what I needed, and had an excellent layout for organization.Edit: This review has apparently sparked enough interest to warrant a discussion on how much this bag is designed to carry. While I appreciate that it is possible to overload a bag to the point of breaking it, I'd like to note that my bag typically held just under ten pounds of items -- I weighed it before classes started.I don't think 10 pounds is unreasonable. A bag featuring this pocket/compartment design, and of this size, should be able to support at least ten pounds. I will admit that I was hard on the bag in the sense that I used it a lot. It went with me everywhere, as I walked to and from campus (a mile and a half each way), as I went to work, as I went on miscellaneous errands. But, again, for a product advertising itself as a "field" or "journey" bag, I would expect it to be built to withstand such conditions.For the final time, I loved this bag while it worked. I dearly wish I could have it in full-grain leather, or even heavier canvas. Or better yet, in ballistic nylon. If such a product is ever designed, I will buy it gladly. Over all this is a great bag and I may even consider ordering one in the olive color as well just to mix it up.

This is a Chinese $5 watch masquerading as a $50 watch. Even though it looked impressive and kept time well when I first started wearing it, I just tossed mine into the trash after attempting to replace the SR626SW battery for the first time, because its general condition after little more than a year of light use was so bad that I didn't want to spend $3 to $5 for a new watch cell.Here's a list of things I found to be objectionable or unacceptable:* The body is made of painted pot metal.  It is bulky and heavy, and the finish is easily damaged.* The stainless steel back is difficult to remove, as the notch for prying it off is obstructed by part of the watch case.  Damage to the case finish is unavoidable and to the o-ring is likely.  Due to the pot metal body, which corrodes fairly easily, water resistance after reassembly is unlikely to be achieved.* The spring pin tips are made of soft, annealed steel that deformed easily even while I attempted to disengage them to remove the strap and gain access to the watch back.  From perspiration and occasional washing of the strap, the innards of the spring pins on my watch had rusted to the point of no longer functioning.  Even a drop of Kroil penetrating oil was unable to bring them back to life.* The adjusting stem is nickel-plated brass, and on mine the plating was completely gone.* The "crystal" appears to be soft soda-lime glass, easily scratched.* For the size of the watch body, the Japanese movement inside is tiny, and the watch battery is puny, giving it short service life.  A larger movement could have accommodated a larger battery with longer life.About the only thing worth salvaging was the nylon webbing/Velcro watch band.  Perhaps I can pair it with a nice digital watch instead.  The band alone would probably sell for at least $5 as a replacement item.Even though the watch looked good when new, I would try to get it on a 60% or greater discount and expect it to be a disposable item.  I bought mine at Big 5 Sporting Goods when it was on sale for just under $20.

reviewText: I will be brief....buy this pocket watch if you are looking for an awesome product that is beautiful and functional.  I can't stop looking at it.  Worth every penny and then some. This is my first pocket watch. After extensive review I decided on this one (I love the two-tone). The watch has a solid feel to it. It looks nice and gets plenty of compliments. Mechanically the watch is sound. For mechanicals/price you cannot beat the movement on this watch. The old railroad watches were required to keep time within 30 seconds per week; this does not meet that standard, never-the-less, it does keep good time; on the order of 5 to 8 seconds per day. If you think that is bad, please note that that equates to a 99.98% accuracy (rounded to the hundredths). I am a stickler on watch accuracy, but owning a mechanical that keeps time to within +/- 1 minute PER WEEK has a sense of pride to it that a typical quartz cannot produce.I highly recommend this watch to anyone with a pallet for both character, and personal nostalgia.

I purchased two of these watches after extensively reviewing the different types of pocket watches and customers' experience with them. I wanted a nice time piece with the option of putting a photograph of my father inside for myself and one with a photograph of me as a present for my father. I also remember being given a mechanical watch that was a prop from a high school play. That watch eventually fell to pieces, as I did not have the means to maintain it. The novelty of the watch remained, and I am pleased with its replacement almost 15 years later.The Charles Hubert 3846 is indeed a fine piece of craftsmanship despite being a modern watch. The two-tone accent is quite tasteful; even the bezel for the picture frame is not gaudy. As other reviews have mentioned, the watch does come with a silver chain which, in my opinion, looks better than a gold one since it allows the focus created by the watch's dual tone to remain on the watch; that being said, I am sure it would look fine with a gold chain and may try that option one day. I will add that I am very glad the watch came with a chain; I was promptly able to use it without having to wait to order one. I was a bit hesitant while looking at the size of the watch, but after purchasing it and examining it, I find that I thoroughly enjoy the heft and weight of the watch. Since I am an early riser and am in the habit of laying out my pocket items the night before, I rather enjoy winding this watch as part of my regimen. I would agree with the caution that one should wind the watch gingerly and stop winding when the crown no longer turns. For the technical eye, it is pleasant to see the machinations of the watch as it tells time and listen to it ticking. As for keeping time, the 3846 watch keeps pace with the quartz wristwatch I wear regularly. I must say that I am tempted to make the 3846 my regular time piece except that I live in Philadelphia; pulling a watch in and out of one's pocket is not the wisest way to tell time. If I continue to fancy doing so I may need to purchase a more subtle or plain time piece. That being said, those who have seen the watch say that it is beautiful, so I both concur and add to those who have gotten similar comments about their watch.I will offer a few cons to the pros, as nothing is perfect. To begin with, having instructions for removing the bezel and inserting and securing the photograph would have been useful. I assumed that there was a way to do it (i.e. it unscrewed or had clips) but doing so incorrectly could have resulted in unnecessary damage to the watch (e.g. stripping the bezel or losing the wire that holds the photograph). Secondly, since the watch goes the modern route of using glowing hands to enable time-keeping in the dark, it might have been useful to include glowing points where the numbers are-perhaps four marks at 12, 3, 6, and 9 to keep the subtlety of the watch. I can, however, appreciate the conservative nature of not including them and having a general idea of where the numbers are based on which way the hands are pointing. Thirdly, a brief schematic of the watch and some information about the watch (e.g. construction, location of features) would also have been useful, again for the purpose of either instructing the newcomer or reminding the novice. Finally, it would be nice if the crystal were glass instead of plastic, further adding to the watch's beauty and minimizing the possibility of scratches should the watch be in a pocket having other objects it it.Summarily, the Charles Hubert 3846 Two-Tone is a beautiful watch with pleasant design, observable time-keeping ability, and mechanical interest, which is why I rate it a 5-star watch. As an added bonus, I noticed that there was a silver version, and the magpie in me may consider adding that one to my collection. I am looking forward to presenting this watch to my father and wholeheartedly recommend it to any others looking at it for personal use or gift-giving.I. Dugan

It feels heavy and high quality, and he shows it off to everyone. He wears it with the included chain 2 - 3 times a week, and so far it has held up to this gentle use beautifully. reviewText: Wonderful craftsmanship, this was a beautiful wedding gift for my husband. He loved it, and there was room on the back to have it engraved. We loved the option of the stand in the back (which isn't too thick) because it will get more use as a desk piece because he won't have the opportunity to actually wear it very much (except for formal events.) Overall a great pocket watch!

Bought this for my dad and he loves it. It's a super neat design that I feel looks cool regardless of age. The silver/gold coloring gives a unique feel to it and you can use either gold or silver chains with it and neither look odd.

This watch comes with a chain, which is something not depicted in the photos or mentioned in the description.  It is the same chain shown with the Charles-Hubert Paris Mechanical Pocket Watch, and silver in color.The watch itself is beautiful and has some serious weight to it.  It arrived in a black cardboard box within a box, so the packaging has a nice presentation if you are buying this as a gift. The watch was in a black cloth cinched bag inside the inner box. It also comes with rudimentary instructions and a lens cleaning cloth.  The watch itself displays upright very nicely on a desk with its swiveling leg stand.One reviewer said one of the "pins" on the leg stand came out of their watch.  I examined mine and the "pins" actually appear to be tiny phillips head screws.  I can't imagine how they would work themselves out of the watch except through frequent manipulation of the stand or a poor borehole for the screw.  The screws on mine appear to be very secure.The second hand on my watch was at the 30 second mark when it arrived and as soon as I began winding the watch, it began moving.  There is no way to stop the second hand with the stem once it gets moving if you want to set the time precisely to UTC.  So before you begin winding it, if you want to match it to UTC, don't starting winding it until the UTC seconds count is where your second hand is.The front glass cover is large enough to see the entire face of the clock.  The only reason you would ever need to open it to read the time is if you put a photo in the cover.  The glass cover does screw off for ease of placing a photo in it, and the bezel is studded so you can grip it easily enough to unscrew it.The back of the watch presents a very sensual, buttery look with the brass casing and inner works visible through the rear glass.  All of the crystals are glass on this piece, not plastic.Make sure you read the instructions before winding the watch or fiddling with the stem to open and close the cover.  It takes all of one minute to fully understand the instructions, but they are important to read and understand.This watch is definitely worth the price.  (Edited to add: This watch was $90.00 when I bought it.)

reviewText: I have so far resisted jumping on the GPS bandwagon where my running is concerned, and this watch will probably help me stay a Luddite. It's been many years since I owned a digital watch, and Timex has gotten this one right. Details that the casual observer might not notice: The buttons are beefy (though they occasionally do make a squeaking noise), and I don't worry that the spring will wear out. The display is shifted toward the top of the screen so that, when viewed from your arm, it appears in the center. The features for runners are excellent. I especially like the target time beeps during chronograph mode and the Interval Timer function. The other reviewers are correct: the "Tap" feature is more of a "slap" feature (although the force required can be changed, I just left it at "medium"). This is obviously intentional on Timex's part -- you wouldn't wan to get false taps during a run, and I certainly haven't!
summary: The features for runners are excellent. I especially like the target time beeps during ...

reviewText: I have bought several of these for my daughters over the years.  They are inexpensive, work great and they like them for exercising and timing their runs.  This is an upgrade from one that finally quit.  They get broken from activity that is no fault of the watch, just active people.

Pros:- For a waterproof athletic watch, very attractive/slim/sleek.- I have had no problems with the waterproofing.- The loop that the watch strap goes through snaps into place, to keep the watch secure while racing.  Nice design feature, not visible in Amazon photos.- You can set multiple time zones, and select which one you want to be the primary one in use.Cons:- Indiglo is practically nonexistent (only visible at night/in the dark), as compared to other Indiglo watches I have owned.- The "tap" feature doesn't respond no matter how hard I whack the watch.  However, it seems to work when my wrist hits the water's surface.  As a result, I often finish my swimming only to find out that it thinks I have done hundreds more laps than I actually have.- If you start the stopwatch (a/k/a "chrono" mode), it counts it as a workout.  The only way to reset a workout (e.g., if you accidentally start the stopwatch), it automatically saves the workout.  You cannot delete a saved workout.  Every saved workout is averaged into your time.  Given that the "tap" feature seems to have a mind of its own, you will have numerous unintentionally "workouts" recorded because you accidentally hit your wrist on something.  As a result, all the progress tracking, average times, and other special features are practically useless.- Alarm is subtly quiet / discrete, not loud enough to wake me up, and it stops after only a few seconds.  Not functional as a wake up for people who tend to snooze.  OK as a daily reminder (I use mind to make myself leave work and go to the gym).Overall: Great for a waterproof, daily-wear, travel watch.  Not so great as a way to keep track of your triathlon training, or as a way to wake you up.  I am glad I did not pay the MSRP for the watch.

I bought the Timex Ironman T5K416, which may be a perfectly fine watch except that it doesn't meet the stated "alarms settable for daily, weekday, weekend and weekly". The WEEKLY feature was critical for me - i.e. being able to set the alarm to ring each week at a specific day/time (e.g. Thurs, 11:30 AM). The T5K416 doesn't have this capability, so I returned it with no problems (thanks Amazon). This was no fault of Amazon, since the Timex website also mis-advertises this watch: In the description, it says "daily, weekday, weekend and weekly" but the downloaded PDF says "daily, weekday, weekend" (no "weekly"). Many watches on the Timex website are similarly incorrectly described. The only Timex I knew about with the "weekly" feature was another Ironman model T54281. I had owned this once before, but vowed not to buy it again because the "sleek" band breaks within a short period and is not replaceable; this problem is noted in the many critical reviews on both the Timex and Amazon websites. So, how to find a Timex with the "weekly" alarm and a reasonably durable band? The Timex website was useless, as was a phone call to Timex customer service who said "daily" is the feature I want, but I informed this rep that "daily" means the alarm goes every day at the indicated time, not just on one specific designated day. I was getting discouraged, until somehow, after more web browsing, I found theTimex Ironman Sleek 50-Lap Full-size Digital Men's watch #T5K335, which does have the "weekly" feature (confirmed when I downloaded the PDF from the Timex website), and a band that looks reasonably durable. So I ordered it from Amazon, wore it today for the first time, and Voila! The alarm went off exactly as set: Thurs 11:30 AM. Just in time to buy lunch before my meeting.Bottom Line - Probably the T5K416 is fine if you like these Timex styles, but the following sums up my experience:The right Timex I wanted to seekBut my chances were seeming quite bleakTrue, they all take a lickingAnd keep right on tickingBut few alarms chime once a week
summary: Timex mis-advertises this watch - no fault of Amazon

I'm a  Casio watch fan. My mom is in her early 60s, and she likes small round analog watches, with full arabic numerals. But the problem with those is battery life. They last one year, max. Then, they charge her $7 each time to change them.Finally, I told her to stop that, let me change them. (watch batteries are three bucks for ten through amazon...)There is always the option of solar watches, which theoretically never need a battery, but they are still expensive for a decent one.Meanwhile, I bought her this watch. Casio digital watches have no moving parts, and the batteries tend to last FOREVER. This one, I'm sure will go at LEAST 3 years before needing a battery.Now, even for a person who generally prefers analog watches, one has to admit that the features on this are wonderful:- Easy-to-use countdown timer. They're all presets, so no having to set them! Also, they can be activated from the home screen. Very easy to use, even for those of us who are not technically minded.- There is of course a stopwatch and alarm too. If you care to learn how to use them, they can be well worth the time.The watch is also light, accurate, and has just a bit of flash. Gold watches aren't popular now, especially not digital ones. But silver doesn't match with everything, right?  It matches a gold wedding band splendidly.The bracelet is gold plated on the outside only. The inside and sides are brushed stainless steel. I wish they had plated the sides, but it is a thin bracelet, so not noticeable, once on the wrist. The bracelet is folded steel links, which can occasionally pull an arm hair, if you have many on your wrist. In this case, I can recommend a nice brown leather strap; they are ALWAYS more comfortable than a bracelet, because they breathe.In the end, I think my mom will stick with her quartz analog watches most of the time, and my hope is that she will wear this one around the house, and maybe use the timer to help her remember things, like steeping tea, cooking a dish, changing laundry, etc.Or maybe she will wear it for a nice change of pace sometimes? That would be great.
