I purchase wallets frequently. Budget wallets, designer wallets, even leather specialty store wallets if they catch my interest. I find them interesting. I like to break them in, wear them out, switch them up. I'm a dork. Granted. However, I have NEVER owned a wallet with chain, or even just a plain old wallet chain rigged up with an existing wallet. So, I took the very affordable plunge that is this Carroll Tri-Fold wallet.The wallet is a tri-fold, as you will undoubtedly learn from the description above. And it is leather: Split leather, to be exact. So I cannot yet attest to the durability of this wallet over a long period of time. Split leather usually gives up quicker than a full on genuine leather, but the material they have mated this one with seems extremely thick and durable. So we will see (and for the price, how choosy can you be?). Anyway, to continue the features: there is a single, quite large, money pocket and two primary slots for cards and whatnot and a picture holder. A third, if you use together or remove the pictures insert. So if you are a heavy card user, this probably will not work for you. There is no "window" slot, for IDs or anything, so you will need to physically remove it when you are carded for anything that the young folks can't purchase. Also, there are two snaps on the inside of the wallet to hold it closed. Unfortunately, they are exposed on the inside of one of the card slots and I'm pretty sure they will bend whatever card is placed in that slot over time and with your weight. The stitching seems pretty good.Finally, there is a little rivet/metal lined eyelet that attaches to the chain, so that is good. The chain is not heavy, nor is it light. I have given it a good twist or two and a couple yanks and it seems sturdy. At approximately 12 inches in length, the chain is just right for most of us. The split leather snap for your front belt loop seems to be constructed of the same materials as the wallet body. Also, there is an extra little snap near the belt loop attachment for whatever you want, I suppose.Oh right, as with most tri-fold wallets this one is a bit fat. But... maybe a little fatter than your average tri-fold. So, consider that when you decide how much wallet bulge you want in life.For the price, it is a decent little set that I think will last a while. But watch out for the fatness, the snaps, and the lack of card slots, which may set you back.

The frames are a great disappointment.  The hinge on the right eyepiece on the frames I received flops open when I look down which is very irritating. As my vision deteriorates, I've been forced into progressive lenses and that present a problem using my camera's view finder, especially in bright sunlight. My routine is to whip off my sunglasses, jam them in my mouth, then frame the image thru the VF. Sweaty sunglasses with sunscreen on the bows are pretty disgusting (yuk!). And flip-up clip-on sunglasses over my prescription clear glasses leave my face spaced too far away from the view finder: my camera's EVF senses sunlight and assume I'm not using the EVF (annoying!).The Hoodman PhotoFrames, with a few whines, pretty much solves my problem. I bought lenses at LensCrafter (their prices have exploded!) and had them mount the lenses in my Hoodman frames. The end product functions very well: I can walk around with corrected sun glasses, then when I see a shot it just takes a quick lift of my right lens using the corner of the camera as I bring it to my eye and I'm in business.As I said, I have a few whines:- the lens retainers (the metal loop that surrounds the prescription lens to hold it in place) are shaped for clear vision or far sighted corrective lenses. Post-cataract surgery, my vision is near sighted. So my lenses don't fit the frame very well because they have more curvature. The fit is close enough to retain the lenses, but it sure looks precarious.- as another poster says, the hinge doesn't have much friction; if your prescription lenses are heavy (maybe polarized lenses which are laminated), the lens can flop away from your face when you lower your head. There is no adjustment to pre-set friction and no detent stop.- I love the loops that fit over the ears because they keep the glasses on my face when my hands are occupied; others may not feel the same way.- the typical range of frame sizing (pupil spacing, bow length, and lens-holder curvature) is not available- the one-size-fits-all approach is unfortunate. In my case the bows are a few millimeters too long, but not too long to make the frames unusable.On the plus side,- the frames are light weight and comfortable;- the loops retain the glasses when active;- my EVF doesn't see enough light to cause it to shut off the EVF display; and most important- they do the job! I can flip the lens out of the way easily without losing the setup I'm trying to frame.I gave a 4-star rating because of the one-size-fits-all limitation and the lack of friction adjustment (or alternately a detent).With respect to doing their intended job, however, they are an excellent (and apparently the *only*) choice for eye glass-wearers. (You who wear contacts are to be envied as there are less expensive solutions.)
summary: Finally I can use the view finder easily!

reviewText: This lens frame can be useful especially when your hands are occupied with a heavy camera and other items while shooting. You don't have to take your glasses off- just flip the lens up.  I prefer to press my eye up against the camera viewing port so that I can see the entire frame of the shoot (thru the lens).  Wearing glasses prevents me from seeing the entire field.  I adjusted the camera's diopter adjustment so that the view would be in focus (w/o glasses). I did have to buy a special (-3) diopter lens adaptor for the camera so the camera's (onboard) diopter would be in range for a good focus (w/o glasses). The problem I have with this frame is that the lens will not stay down in the closed (down) position on gusty winding days. Also the lenses/frame will not stay in the down position when I bend my head down. This was a real nuisance since I wear these glasses full time.  The lenses are mounted on small hinges which I tried to tighten up (i.e., tiny screws) but they tend to work loose.  I gave up trying to keep them tight.  To keep the lenses from moving up (when not viewing the camera) I've attach two small ringlet gasket (purchase at a hardware store) through the temple bars and snap (stretch) them to the screwed-lens mounting (titanium) frames that holds the lenses in frame.  I had to experiment with different sizes of gaskets to get the one that was not too tight nor too loose.  It doesn't  look pretty but it works.

I LOVE these glasses, I wear them every day. They work great, they make photograpthy easier, as I can focus better. These pants are high quality and are a really nice product.  The overall construction is well thought out and the quality of materials is superb.  They add a level of protection while the wearer forgets that they have them on.The fabric used in the waist and leg bands are the best for the job.  They are cotton, about 3/4 inches wide, and feel very comfortable against the skin.  The elastic is also well engineered.  It has enough memory in it to provide a near water tight seal around the legs and waist without becoming too tight so as to become uncomfortable to the wearer.  The elastic bands never roll over.The material used in the body of the garment is a plastic coated nylon taffeta of the same type used for babies.  It is soft and pliable, quiet, and adds almost no additional volume or bulkiness beneath regular clothing.  Heat is able to transfer through it efficiently leaving the wearer comfortable.  Because of its nylon properties, it is somewhat slippery on the outside.  Less so on the inside.  This allows the wearer to move around in bed or to easily pull other clothing on over this pant while it stays securely in place.The overall shape of the garment fits just right over underwear, pads, or more.  They look good on the wearer because the nylon fabric is of such high quality.  These pants will not leak if they are used with the right diaper or pad.  The key to preventing leakage is in selecting an inner diaper/pad with enough absorbency to keep liquid locked away.  These pants do a good job of providing that final level of protection in the form of a water proof barrier.They will last a long time if you wash them in cold water and hang them to dry.  Heat, like for all synthetic fabrics, is not recommended.  Use of these Pull-On-Pants should be considered for day or night use.  The wearer will even forget they have them on.  I have compared them to every competitor on the market and these are clearly the best.  They are comfortable and have certainly helped me solve one of life's little problems...

reviewText: BON usually makes a great product.  These spiked shoes, leave much to be desired.I am a general contractor, and recently bought two sets of these for a nasty floor we were stripping of black tar mastic.  These spiked shoes arrived, and we realized they take about 20 minutes to assemble.  The spikes on the shoes are bolts that come in a baggy.After we fumbled around with the tiny parts for what seemed like forever, we strapped them on.  That is when we discovered two more fatal flaws with this inferior product.  The straps are very poorly designed and are a cheap, elastic (much like what you would have on a pair of underwear, believe it or not!) and don't tighten on your boot enough to feel secure slopping over wet tar.  The next problem is the size.  Come on, these are designed for contractors, not little boys!  They are TINY!  I wear a size 12 (the recommend using a steal toe boot, which I do anyways - Red Wing Pecos) and about 25% of my foot was hanging over the toe of these shoes.If those things were not bad enough, here comes the most annoying part... Remember the bolts I mentioned earlier?  Yeah, the 'spikes'.  Well, no matter how tight you make them the nuts work there way off, then you lose your nuts in your mastic or resin.  No fun digging them out, and even less fun fumbling with the tiny nuts when they are covered in construction grime.  One of my employees was over the boots in about 5 minutes, I fumbled and tripped on them for a few hours before I finally tossed them in the dumpster with a cuss.  Keep looking guys, and when you find some that work please shoot me a message!
summary: Keep looking, these are a waste

reviewText: I decided to epoxy my garage and didn't think I would need these spiked shoes.  I was wrong.  YOU NEED THE SHOES!  So, just go ahead and get them when you get all of your other supplies.  I paid about $25 for these on line including shipping.  I could not find them at any stores in town, so, you will have to plan ahead to have them arrive before you begin your project.I wear a woman's size 8 or 9 shoe and the straps were too big to tighten properly.  So, I put on a pair of my husband's size 8 work boots.  The straps fit very well and held tight throughout the job.  The straps did not drag in the epoxy at all.  The spikes did not leave marks in the epoxy.  I could go wherever I needed to go without worrying about walking in the epoxy, even after I had applied the flakes.The shoes are flexible enough to walk around comfortably so I don't think you need to spend the extra money to get flexible shoes.  I don't think I would like the slip on shoes either.  It was good to know they were securely fastened to my boots throughout the job.The extra money you would have to spend to get longer poles to spread and roll the epoxy without walking in it, makes these shoes worth the money.  You will relax and not have to worry about how you will reach the epoxy without stepping in it.  It is worth the money for peace of mind.

Maybe I'll pin a red silk tulip, a yellow daffodil or a daisy chain to the brim... I agree the fit could be snugger but I don't think the issue is size or diameter. This watch is amazing. It predicts the future! The watch can predict if my joints are going to hurt while looking nice on my wrist. Before I got this watch I did not know what low and high atmospheric pressure meant. Yes I heard it thousand of times on TV but I had no idea that the atmospheric pressure was so important and that is had to do so much with the weather patterns. The only thing I knew is that when the weather was bad my joints would hurt. Now I know why.The compass feature works. It will show me the right way and works perfectly. The altimeter feature is awesome, it will tell me when I will run out air and will get very tired easily. Watch carefully where the tiny cylindrical spacer goes and how it works.Solar watches are the way to go. My oldest solar watch is twelve years old and still works. This watch is much lighter than you would think on viewing the photos.  It is striking in its appearance, though quite large so perhaps best suited to those with larger wrists.  The titanium band has a nice feature in that the back of the watch is stiff at the initial links so as to prevent slippage around the wrist.  It will likely be necessary to have the strap adjusted and you'll probably need to visit a jeweler or watch repair shop to have it done because it's next to impossible without the specialized tools needed.The watch itself is feature-rich, but the instructions take time to decipher. The solar powered battery works as advertised, but don't expect a full charge unless you leave it in a window in the sun or under a lamp for a few hours.  It will maintain current charge levels simply based on available light when worn in regular daytime conditions.My only complaint (aside from the inadequacy of the instruction manual) is that the volume of the tones used is quite low and doesn't appear to be adjustable, e.g., alarm, timer, hourly chime, etc.... The same watch with this feature costs about $50 or so more at the time I purchased and, unless you travel frequently, may not be worth the extra cost.Overall, it's an excellent watch that represents great value when you consider style and features relative to cost. I read a lot of reviews about this watch prior to buying it. Most of those reviews were good but some of them were bad so after having this for a few weeks now I'd like to mention a few things that may explain the bad reviews that I read. Most people did not seem to be using their heads or just I'll informed.First I should start off by saying that this watch takes a reasonable amount of intelligence for you to get the most out of it. I have yet to find anything negative about it but you need to keep these things in mind.Be careful when you size the band or ask someone to size it for you. This band does not use the typical link pins like most watches.  You know, the kind that are split and spread out to hold the link pin in place.  When you push the pins out of this band, each pin is held captive by a small split barrel that goes into the middle of the inside smallest part of the link. If you push any of the link pins out and you are not careful, that small barrel is going to fall on the floor or roll off of the table never to be found again. That small barrel is split because when the link pin grows through it, it spreads out a little and causes the proper tension to hold the link pin in place inside of the band. If you lose this small barrel the link pin is going to slide through the one side of the band and go right out the other side. If the small barrel falls out just remember it can only go into one side of the smallest part of each link. It won't go into either side, just one side where you can see that the hole has been made larger for this barrel to fit in.After you get your band adjusted you will need to calibrate the barometer. It will be kind of close right out of the box but not right on. Once you calibrate it, it should stay within a couple of hundredths of your local barometric pressure reading. There are a few places that you can find highly accurate barometric pressure reading in your area. In my area there is a local county airport and on the (NOAA) National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration web page I can find the current barometric pressure reading for this airport. Barometric pressure readings seem to stay fairly accurate within 25 miles or so ofnwhere you live.  Barometric pressure is listed on the NOAA website as "altimeter". Why would it be listed as altimeter when we are looking for barometric pressure and not altimeter?  Well, that's because when airplanes calibrate their altimeters, it's actually controlled by barometric pressure so when you read altimeter on the NOAA site they are telling pilots to dial that value into their altimeter while they are sitting in the runway. Keep in mind that on the NOAA site, these values usually get updated once every hour. Sometimes when they are updated the reading is delayed by 15 minutes or so. As soon as that value updates on your web page, calibrate your barometer and it should be pretty much right on every time you check it from that point on.Now for the altimeter. The altimeter on this watch just like in an airplane's altimeter is affected by changes in barometric pressure. Barometric pressure changes constantly. From time to time an hour will go by and barometric pressure will not vary that much. Other times it will rise quickly or fall quickly. If you calibrate your altimeter on this watch and the barometric pressure does not change much then your altitude reading will stay pretty much spot on. If you calibrate it and the barometric really changes drastically then the accuracy of your barometer on this watch will drop in accuracy. In order to properly calibrate the altimeter on your watch you need to have a good reference altitude. What I've done is made notes of the actual altitude of my house, where I work and other locations that I frequent. Now the easiest way to find these reference altitudes is to use Google Earth. Not Google Earth on your iPhone or iPad because that program will not show the actual elevation.  On those devices it will only show you how high you are viewing any specific area from. You need to use Google Earth on your computer. That will show you the actual altitude of any place you rest your mouse on. Once you find these reference points you'll need to be at one of them and calibrate your altimeter. You should find that if you set it at your home and drive to where you work the altitude should be correct as long as it's not a day that the barometric pressure is changing rapidly. The altimeter can only be calibrated in increments of 20' so you'll have to pickthe increment that is closest to what Google Earth showed.  Also, don't expect to calibrate this on the ground and then fly in a commercial airplane and watch the altitude change. Remember that they pressurize the cabin so your barometric pressure that you will read will be based on cabin pressure and I've already noted that the altimeter is affected by changes in barometric pressure. The altimeter on this watch is mainly meant for hiking and biking, not flying. In a small Cessna it would probably work fine but I wouldn't want to rely on this for landing the plane.Lets talk about the temperature reading. This temperature sensor is really meant to tell temperature when the watch is off of your wrist. Keep in mind that when you wear the watch and press the barometer button to see the temperature, it's probably going to read around 83 degrees f. That's because the heat from your body has raised the temperature of the watch and the sensor is located inside of the watch. If you take the watch off I have found that it takes about 30 minutes for the watch to read actual air or room temperature. There are some people out there that have attempted to calibrate the sensor so that it takes into consideration their body temperature so they calibrate it to read room temperature while the watch is on their wrist. This is kind of a boneheaded thing to do because your body temperature is going to be affected by a number of factors. Also, if you wear a watch fairly loosly like I do it's not always going to be tight against your wrist so the watch temperature will always be changing.In order to get the sunrise and sunset feature to be accurate you'll want to read the manual on how to adjust it and again, find your house or city on Google Earth to get the latitude and longitude and put that offset in the watch and you'll read within a few minutes of any of the sunrise and sunset times that you will find on the web for your area.I'll be honest and say that I haven't adjusted the calibration of the compass. From what I can see it's close enough to my GPS, the compass on my car's mirror and a little handheld compass. I would expect that if I were lost in the woods or anywhere else for that matter I could get headed in the right direction. There are some adjustments that you can make to the compass off of maps but I haven't seen any reasons to calibrate it.So with all of that said, this is a great watch. The automatic backlight feature works great although I bumped the default time up from one second to two seconds. The power saver feature also works as advertised.If you are on the fence about buying this watch and bad reviews are what have you on the fence, hopefully I've shed some light on these issues that are really non-issues as long as you are using the watch properly.

reviewText: The Casio Pathfinder is a great watch.  The titanium band/case is very durable and even though titanium tends to scratch easy, I havent noticed any scratches on the band yet and its been through hell.  I found out while traveling that I had to calibrate the altimeter a lot, which can be a problem if you dont know what altitude you are at to begin with cause then you cant calibrate it.  The compass tends to be accurate and that can be a useful feature to the outdoors type.  Im currently deployed in afghanistan and I hope I never need to rely on my watch to get me back t base but its good to have back-ups.  As far as the temp/barometer go Im not so sure.  The temperature gets thrown off by your body heat, but if you take it off and let it acclimatized then you can get a more accurate reading.  I dont know how to read barometric pressure, but Im sure once I figure that out it could become useful.  The worldtime feature helps a lot esp when Im traveling around the world but still need to know the times back home and my destination.  Atomic time keeping keeps your watch accurate so you never need to worry about setting it yourself.  Over all its a great watch, very light weight (it will surprise you), and will last you a long time.  I realized the solar power feature charges pretty fast and there a battery meter that will let you know well before hand that it needs recharging.  Im outside a lot so it tends to stay fully charged. This watch if definitely worth the cost.

I tried to contact casio asking if they made titanium replacement for this part of the watch but they did not respond to my email. reviewText: First of all this watch is much lighter than it looks. 3-15-2014. Success!  I received the new (actually was new and never opened before) Casio Men's PAG240T-7CR "Pathfinder" Triple-Sensor Multi-Function Titanium Watch in two days and scheduled a call from CASIO Customer support for resolution of the "Sunrise-Sunset" reversal issue for Friday evening between 5-7 PM, but they never called. Today(Sat),I further examined the Casio Instructions for this watch and determined that I failed to understand how the functions worked correctly.  At manufacture the Latitude and Longitude are set for Tokyo which is configured EAST of GMT (UTC) Greenwich, England. My time zone is NYC which is WEST of GMT.  The watch Latitude and Longitude must be changed to match NYC, not TOKYO.  The instructions do not clarify that change is required and lead the user to believe that by changing the WTC location to NYC the correct Latitude and Longitude will be entered into the watch memory. By entering the correct Lat-Long combination and making sure that it's WEST(in my case), the Sunrise-Sunset time now correctly display on the watch.  The original watch was NOT defective; just the instructions confusing. I have now fully tested all the many features of this watch and they work as promised by Casio.Features:  All the features are useful, but you have to read the instructions that generally explain any restrictions (see my explanation above). For example: The temperature reads the temperature of the watch case, so if it on your wrist it will show body temperature. You need to take it off your body and let it sit in the environment you want to measure for about 30 minutes to get a reading of that environment. That's logical, when you think about it. The instructions are lengthy and I recommend reading them on a computer from Casio.com if you want to understand the features before investing in this watch.Amazon.com has once again proven to be a great supplier of products and excellent customer service.3-9-2014.  Sadly (see correction above), I returned the watch (postage paid by Amazon) due to a suspected malfunction of the sunrise-sunset display. This unit had previously been opened and returned to Amazon. Amazon promptly refunded my money.  I reordered another Casio Men's PAG240T-7CR "Pathfinder" Triple-Sensor Multi-Function Titanium Watch. The price had reduce to $159. This is a 2011 model from Casio, but a great tool.3-8-2014. I don't collect watches but have four working ones (two are Casio). I chose the Casio Men's PAG240T-7CR "Pathfinder" Triple-Sensor Multi-Function Titanium... as my everyday watch for several reasons.1. My Casio AE2000W-1AV model ($25) has performed well for numerous years and withstood well my moderately rough treatment.2. I have friends in the jungles of the Amazonas (Venezuela)with Casio G-Shock models and they find them very sturdy and perform well.3. The basic features of most Casio digital models are easy to read and similar, while the extra features are often very small and difficult to view without a magnifier, but can still be useful and functional.4. The metal bands have held up well (I do not use the resin or leather bands - personal preference) but are only available on a few Casio models similar to the Casio Men's PAG240T-7CR "Pathfinder" Triple-Sensor Multi-Function Titanium.5. The weight of the Casio is fairly light compared to others I have: 1) Elgin analog 5.4 oz; 2) Armatron digital 4.5 oz; 3)Casio AE2000W-1AV  3.7 oz; and 4) Casio Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR is 3.9 oz.6. Case and display module dimensions of the Casio models are similar. The Casio Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR  case is 5 mm larger but the display module is almost identical in size. The added case size is occupied by the compass dial and sensor buttons.7. The Casio Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR digital display numerals are easier to read as they are 3 mm wide vs. 2 mm wide on the Casio AE2000W-1AV  and Armatron units, with the Elgin being analog.8. The extra features on the Casio Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR  are something I wanted but had not been previously willing to purchase out of concern that they would fail easily. The durability of the Casio modules has changed my mind.9. The Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR has an 8.5 inch wrist size capability metal band with adjustment to 8.0 inches without removing links. My wrist is 8.0 inches.10. The User Manual of instruction for the Casio Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR is available on-line.  The printed manual that comes with the unit is in three languages (English, Spanish, French) and exceptionally small (1 mm) print.  Viewing the manual on a computer display where it can be enlarged is very beneficial as the instructions, while correct, are complex. If you want to read the printed manual I recommend a 3x or 5x magnifier, unless you have Eagle eyes and can read 1 mm printed characters (I can but with difficulty).11. The printing on the Casio Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR display dial ring around the display are less than 1 mm and really need a magnifier to read easily.  However, once you know what they represent you can easily reference them without much problem.Enjoy the watch.Caveats:1. If your wrist is larger than 8.5 inches in circumference, then DO NOT buy the Casio Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR as it will not fit you without purchasing extra links from Casio. The maximum adjustment on the bracelet is 10 mm. If you need to remove a link, the links are 10 mm wide. A total of six links can be removed.2. The band uses 0.7 mm pins to hold it together and that requires special pin remover tools. You can buy the tools from esslinger.com, which I did because of the higher quality of steel pin punch, or get less expensive ones on amazon.com.3. The sensor features (compass, barometer, altimeter, temperature) increase the cost of the watch ($175 for Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR  vs. $25 for Casio AE2000W-1AV).  However, if you want those functions, they don't come cheap, but can be very useful.4. This is not a Rolex, so don't expect to impress the local jeweler or your friends.  Although Casio units do keep more accurate time then my Rolex that I gave to my son after 30 years of use (I had it rebuilt and was like new).
summary: Casio Pathfinder PAG240T-7CR is a great watch with some caveats

reviewText: "Casio Men's PAG40-3COS Pathfinder Triple Sensor Watch"The Swiss Army tool of watches. Every watch should have the features this watch has. Even with a large 50 mm case this is a light weight watch. It is so light weight, I barely know it's on my wrist. All the sensors have their own large dedicated buttons. I find the barometer/thermometer feature very convenient. I never have to wonder or check the weather, I always know what temperature it is at the simple push of a button. And it can predict what the weather will be! The other feature that, I also find convenient to have is the compass. At the simple touch of a button you know which direction your going. This watch at first may make some seem a little timid. A few minutes with the instruction booklet (if you need it) and you will have all your sensors calibrated or to your liking. I prefer Fahrenheit when it comes to temperature settings and not Celsius. This watch will come with the Celsius setting from the factory. I haven't been hiking with it but the altimeter is nice to have so you can track your altitude, cumulative ascent and decent in route to your destination.  A feature that some may not consider is the clasp. The clasp is a fold over clasp and secures quite nicely. No worries of it coming lose and losing the watch. The mineral crystal is very thought, I have owned it for weeks now and not a single blemish. This is a watch that you can where to work or play. The watch is more than just watch it's like a computer on your wrist. Finally, and maybe the ultimate feature is that it's solar powered. Never have to worry about battery's again! Amazon.com has the best price on the internet. There may be an unfamiliar website that may have it for a few dollars less but it's not worth the risk. For the piece of mind and price you can't go wrong. If you have any second thoughts about this watch remember this an easy watch to use and has an easy to read instruction booklet. The booklet is a bit thick but most of the information you will not need. The box that it comes in appears to a be "green" box (recycled or Eco-friendly). Which, I find very appeasing that it's environmentally friendly. The Casio engineers did an awesome job on this watch. If you want to be in the know. You will want this watch. I would highly recommend this watch to all military service members.Note: I have received many questions about getting an accurate temperature reading. You will have to take off the watch and let sit to read the ambient temperature for several minutes to get a precise temperature.
summary: "Casio Men's PAG240T-7CR Pathfinder Triple Sensor Watch"

reviewText: Very good price, amazing features combined all in one ,very usefull and also good looking in the titanium color and last but not least all that solar powered and with four battery level indications.

I have had this watch for almost three years now and I love it! It's stylish, really light weight and totally maintenance free. In fact, it's so light that I sometimes forget I am wearing it. It has a lot of other features which you may or may not have to use; for instance, I have never used the altimeter or barometer but I have used its dual time display feature very often and found it immensely useful.Also, solar charged batteries - no hassles having to replace batteries at all. The functions of this watch are great.  Compass works well, barometer works well, Altimeter works well, Solar charger works well and time is correct.  Anyone who claims that Barometer reads incorrectly probably has not taken it off their wrist.  Think about it, how can the barometer get an accurate reading while directly placed on your body heated wrist.  Take it off and allow some time for it to get actual reading.  Read the instructions and follow them, I have had great readings from all functions of this watch.  I take it hiking, hunting, camping, fishing and outdoors mostly and love it.  I have one complaint and look forward to fixing that with an easy watchband switch.  I am not a big fan of the titanium watchband, it easily comes unsnapped and almost caused me to lose this watch on a couple separate accounts.  I finally learned to use a small piece of duck tape when I go on my hikes to strap around the latch (works well).  I will be soon replacing band with a nylon or leather band that is more secure.  Other than the titanium band, I love this watch.  Main thing: If you want correct readings, follow instructions!Update 10-10-12:  I used my pliers to carefully crimp the band connector (or whatever it is called) and it now locks perfectly.  I actually love the band now and have not had a single problem with it.  Another cool factor:  I found a setting that initiates the night light when you flick your wrist......! Totally cool and useful!  I love this watch!  Expensive, but you get what you pay for.

I'm a graphics artist and of course, my hands are sliding up and down between keyboard to trackball to digital table the whole day...more than your average user. However, against a smooth wooden surface it can get scratched? I never thought that would happen!Its a pity though, as I really find the Titanium colour and look to be truly beautiful for a watch. But if you use this watch like its intended to be used, be aware that the surface scratches easily.I took the watch hunting with me the other day, and it worked really well for predicting sunrise/sunset times, which are critical for hunters. The temperature feature was also really helpful..at least in confirming why it was so cold up knee-deep in snow! I did find it worked pretty good in the hot tub as well, as it gave a pretty good indication of the underwater temps of the tub. The barometer was equally good at predicting bad weather. I wasn't too sure about the Altimeter though it showed I was 860m up a mountain at one point.All-in, I would've given this watch 4 stars or even 5 if not for the pain I feel now looking at the strap. For what its worth, if you're not staring at the watch close up, you would probably not notice the scratches on the strap. Under bright light though, they do show up, as shiny streaks against the matt surface of the strap.

(Please note that I did not buy this through Amazon.com or from the current seller, so this is not a reflection on them.) This "pattern" is a single sheet of paper that someone just started writing general directions on.  There clearly was no editor, nor did they take the simple step of having someone actually try to use this "pattern" with no previous experience.  The primary factor in writing up the instructions seems to be that everything had to fit on a single 8.5x11-inch piece of paper.  In fact, the first sentence is "Use the leftover material from your Bow n Go Bag..."  At the top of the page in extremely faint, teensy, tiny print it says, "Companion Pattern to the Bow n Go Bag (sold separately)."There are alternative instructions for making a piece of quilted fabric to glue onto the flip-flop instead, but if you want to make the pretty pictured flip-flops that match the bag, you are simply out of luck.  I paid a staggering $12 for this when it was new, and felt that it was frankly a case of theft when I received it in the mail.  I bought some of the required items, but calculated that after buying the pattern, fabric, the Craft-tex Plus, the heavy-duty fusible foam batting, the Shoe Goo Glue, and a nice pair of flip-flops (it is too much work and expense to apply to a pair of old, worn-out flip-flops), I would have been out nearly $100, when you take into account five different shipping & handling charges. reviewText: I gave it 4 stars because I do really like the purse, but I have some dislikes about it. Important to read the upate about the strap at the bottom of my review. The front and backside of the purse is soft flexible leather with enough support to hold the shape of the purse without slouching while it sits on a table. The sides are not leather, but I'm guessing it's a thick nylon fabric.  Since the velcro is pretty strong, the double sided zipper makes it easier to position and angle the holster to your needs (even though it's for both left and right handed). If you still have trouble putting the holster in, then cover the Velcro with a long enough strip of paper that I can slide out... Sorta hard to explain, but there is a video review for that somewhere.The purse is divided into 2 large sections for your junk. The divider part of it is very thin and is nothing more then 2 layers of lining. The side of the purse oppose to the firearm has the 2 small open pockets on the inside. I use one for my cell phone and the other for keys. Each open pocket is a different size. The smaller one fits my iPhone w a thin bumper/case just fine. Anything bigger, you could use the bigger pocket. The firearm side area has a typical size zippered pouch inside. Here's my dislike... The firearm I carry sort of bulges out making that pocket a little tighter, so you have to carefully pick what you put in there. Then it also makes it a little hard to reach your hand all the way down into the bottom of the purse on that side.As seen in photos, there is an outer zippered pouch (same side as the firearm). Here's my other dislike, because of the buldge from the firearm, that pouch is rather tight and because the leather is so soft, you will see the silhouette of any items in there and likely to rub into the leather.. That makes the pocket is rather useless other then putting receipts or a grocery list.The firearm area is padded w a thin layer of dense foam to help hide the shape of the firearm. It also helps hold the shape of the purse. The holster that comes with it seems a bit cheap but it does the job. If you have a very small firearm then it might slide out a bit. Maybe you could use a safeypin or Sew a tiny section together with a strong needle to help?(updated) I forgot to add info about the shoulder strap. One side of the strap is leather and you can see where the slash proof wire is in the middle. The other side, to support the soft leather, is a heavy duty nylon webbing (sort of like a dog collar). Pros: the clips are nicer looking then I thought they would be.  When eating out and depending on they're of chair, I can unhook it and loop it thru the arm rest or the back do the chair. I refuse to put my purse on the floor eeeww! From the GTM's site you can buy a longer strap and wear the purse across your body for extra security. CONS: the nylon webbing was very rough especially on the edges. It kept catching on some and delicate fabrics like super rough man-hands loaded with dry cuticles (yuck). I ended up taking a nail file and carefully wear it down some (fine sandpaper should work too, but just be careful). I've noticed it's worn down more after a couple months of use.  It is still somewhat rough and I still catches on delicate fabrics. I tend to flip the strap around so the leather side touches my shoulder.
summary: It's a nice purse and serves its purpose.

However, 6 months after the purchase, the stitching in the bottom broke loose and needed repair. She contacted them and they took her information saying that they would get right back to her regarding how to get the purse repaired.  Now six weeks later, they have not so much as sent us a post card, much less tell us about their return policy for obvious manufacturer defects.  We have two gripes to share in this review:  1. Gun Tote'n Mamas should not sell crap that will fall apart in six months for nearly $100.00.  At that price it should last for years without issues. 2. If Gun Tote'n Mamas wants to stay in business, they better stop lying to to customers and provide far better customer service.  Shame on them for the shabby construction and the shabby customer service.  A company is no better than the customer service they provide.  That being the case, we have given this product one star and would gladly give them a lower rating if it were possible.To Amazon.com I only have one suggestion.  Get rid of products and companies, such as Gun Tote'n Mamas, that produce and sell garbage at significant prices that warrant high quality products and great customer service.  We suggest that Amazon.com look into the practices of the company that produces this product.

reviewText: My wife loves the design of this purse, not just for the concealed carry pouch. The length of the shoulder strap is just right, all the pockets are sized correctly. The zippers work very well and don't hang up or skip. The black leather is wearing very well with minimal care, it doesn't show every scuff and scrape like other leather purses will. I owned one that I purchased almost two years ago and it was starting to look worn and I decided I needed another purse as I like them to look nice.  I really love this purse, people (who do not know it is a concealed carry purse) have complimented me on it several times and a woman who usually carries a Coach bag even asked where I bought it.  It is roomy, has an outer zipper compartment for a cell phone and car keys.  The concealed carry area is good for my Ruger SR22.  I like that you can move the holster and it has Velcro so it can sit exactly right and you can move it for left handed (me) or right handed quick action.  If you are alone in a parking lot at night heading towards you car, it is a comfort to just unzip that compartment rest my hand in there while I walk to the car.  There was a car jacking in the mall near us and one in the supermarket parking lot where I shop in the last couple of years.  You just never know.  I like to carry when I am at the bank as well, as there truly are bank robberies, though the ones in my area have all ended peacefully with no shootings.I like the feeling of having my firearm concealed with me.  I wish the purse wasn't quite so heavy, but that is mainly what I keep in it instead of the purse itself.I now own my 2nd one, in the exact same color and style.  I hope they continue to make this one as I'll probably need another in a few years.  The color is a good one, neither too light or too dark, so I don't feel I need a summer vs. winter purse.  I am donating my old purse to the NRA trainer who taught me how to shoot and worked with my family on personal safety.  I had this purse with me when he trained us and he trained with me how to use this while the boys in the family worked with holsters and other concealed carry methods.  His eyes lit up when he saw this and he was delighted with it too and said he was going to have to tell his female clients about this purse.  Now, he will have a demo one to use for training.This works well for me and I hope I never have to use my Ruger on anyone, anywhere, but I am prepared and thankful for this purse that is always over my shoulder.  I would take someone completely by surprise, I'd say, as no one would ever suspect this purse to have my firearm inside.  I have confidence that I wouldn't be the unarmed victim in a mass shooting, I would be able to at least have a chance to save myself, loved ones or children.  There are crazy people out there and those of us who have CC permits might be the only thing between a lunatic and everyone else's lives.  I highly recommend this.

reviewText: Aug 20,2013 I lost the watch on an overseas trip, and promptly re-ordered the same watch when I returned.=======July 8, 2013 Editing my original review below from Nov 2012. The watch has been working just fine. I have no problem with "hair trigger" buttons. And so far the band has held up well. So - I strongly recommend this watch, particularly if you need the "weekly" alarm feature.=========================================I've had Timex digital watches for years now, because I like the styling and I need the Countdown Timer and Alarm features. This time I was particularly looking for a version that has the "Weekly" alarm feature, i.e. can be set for a specific day/time (e.g. every Wed at 11:30); this is in addition to the more standard "Daily, Weekdays, Weekends" alarm options. Many watches on the Timex website mistakenly indicate Weekly when you first look at the descriptions, but on the downloaded PDFs, they says only "Daily, Weekdays, Weekends", and not "Weekly". Some of these watches are similarly incorrectly advertised on Amazon, but I attribute the fault to Timex, not to Amazon.  I actually bought one from Amazon and immediately returned it when I realized the Weekly alarm didn't exist (no probem; thanks Amazon). The only Timex I knew about with the "weekly" feature was another Ironman model T54281. I had owned this once before, but vowed not to buy it again because the band breaks within a short period and is not replaceable; this problem is noted in the many critical reviews on both the Timex and Amazon websites. I was getting discouraged, until somehow, after more web browsing, I found the T5K335, which does have the "weekly" feature (confirmed when I downloaded the PDF from the Timex website), as well as a band that appeared reasonably durable. So I ordered it from Amazon. After a few weeks, so far so good; but still hoping about the strap - seems better than the T5K335, but maybe not as durable as some other Timex watches. The band is "integrated", i.e. it goes all around the watch and is not replaceable. Why does Timex have to chose a seemingly less durable band for its "Weekly" alarm watches. For this reason I deduct 1 star.The following sums up my experience:The right Timex I wanted to seekBut my chances were seeming quite bleakTrue, they all take a lickingAnd keep right on tickingBut few alarms chime once a week
summary: A "Weekly" alarm, with a decent band

reviewText: I bought the previous version of this watch in 2008, that one lasted for 3 years, through vigorous use.This version only lasted 15 months for me. Could timex have changed one of their suppliers for the rubber in the wristband?Pros: every feature I want in a watch is great.  Timers, chronos, alarms, button placement, all are exactly as desired.Cons: the watchband is an integral part of the watch, and cannot be replaced. And this one cracked after 15 months of real use. Warranty is 12 months.Caveats: I swim in pools, lakes, and sometimes oceans. I wear this in the kitchen, on the bike, on sunny hikes, while working in the yard or washing the car. I put it to hard use. It gets all sorts of stuff on it. I always wash it separately in the shower, as I did the previous watch, but it has touched all sorts of oils (from Canola to two-stroke) , alcohols (from Purell to Bourbon), and soaps (from fels-naptha to borax), so maybe that's reduced the longevity for me.But the old one held up to that abuse longer than this one did.Overall, I love it, but I wish I could replace the band!

PROS: Rugged, retro styling, current time shown in every mode, accurate barometer, great feature set for the priceCONS: Digital display has modest viewing angles, resin band is thin, altimeter is pressure-basedOverall, this SGW300 series represents a terrific bang for the buck.  I was debating between this watch and the G-Shock Riseman (which I may still end up getting one day).  At 1/3 the price, this SGW300 possesses an accurate barometer with trend arrow, a world clock (more cities than the Riseman!), and good toughness (100M water resistance, works in both temperature extremes).  Since purchasing the SGW300, I haven't been disappointed.Three styles are available for the SGW300: black resin band, green cloth band, and stainless steel (folded link) bracelet.  I chose the black resin for aesthetics and functionality.  The black looked stylish and uniform on the case (the green one has light gray buttons and a dark gray sensor on the left, which I didn't like) and the green window on top reminded me of some old-school Casio's.  Plus I didn't want to deal with odor/sweat issues with the cloth band.  On the negative side, the resin band does get thin and the buckle is plastic.  The SGW300 does have 18mm lugs, however, suggesting that the band can be replaced should the original wear out.  The buttons on the side of the case are easy and pleasant to press.It's a sizeable watch, but on my 6.5" wrist, the SGW300 looks and wears fine. [EDIT 11/2011- I ended up trimming 0.25" off the end of the band because it protruded a bit too much.  I smoothed it down with an emery board.  The overall look is much improved.)I love how time is displayed on EVERY mode.  And the alarm tones are reasonably loud.  The display, on the other hand, is merely decent.  At some angles, the uncluttered display shows thick, dark digits quite clearly.  Yet many other angles cause the LCD digits to fade quickly -- I've seen better (the Casio Fishing Watch comes to mind).  Illumination of the display is produced by two amber LEDs, which work well.  One can customize the duration of the illumination, a feature that more expensive models often lack.Like other Casio's, this altimeter is pressure based and can be unreliable if the weather changes.  There is no trend guide for the altimeter, nor is there any memory mode.  The thermometer, as mentioned in other reviews, needs to be off the wrist for at least 15+ minutes before correctly registering ambient temperature.The SGW300 is a hidden gem in the Casio world.  It shares and sometimes surpasses the features of more expensive models.  It lacks the frills of atomic clock synchronization and solar battery power (the SGW300 battery is rated to last at least 3 yrs).  In the process, the SGW300 emerges as an affordable watch for its extensive feature set, handsome retro looks, and good durability.  Highly recommended.

reviewText: I read hundreds of wristwatch altimeter reviews before settling on this watch.  Other reviewers (both amateur and industry product testers) noted that this watch provides a quality altimeter for a fraction of the cost of similar, high-functioning products.  I am happy to report that this well-crafted piece of equipment lives up the hype.  In the course of my research I learned that most watch altimeters read altitude based on barometric pressure, and that this can change not just in response to height, but also weather changes.  One must always be prepared to re-calibrate these watches at a known altitude at the starting point of each trip.  That said, I found that every time I checked it was accurate to within 50 feet--even when rapidly ascending and descending in my car--even when ascending during fast-moving storms and highly variable weather (something I had not expected).  It never quit on me, even in below-zero wind-chill on Mt. Hood. The temperature gauge is only accurate when the watch has been off your body for at least 15 minutes, but it still works.  The more expensive version of this watch includes a digital compass, which may be dangerously inaccurate and not necessary.  I am in awe of the performance capacity of this amazing piece of equipment.

The model numbers are confusing.  Amazon's product page and Casio's website both call this SGW300H-1AV.  Once you put it in your shopping cart on Amazon, it is referred to as SGW300H-1AVCF.  I did receive the desired product with desired band (resin), and the packaging confirms that it is SGW-300H-1AVCF.I had been considering spending $150 for a barometer watch, and am so glad I discovered this instead.  For about 2-3x the price of a bottom-of-the-line wristwatch, you get a barometer.  But note that unless you live in a complete flatland, you will see pressure changes as you travel up/down even over very small hills.  So, you learn to ignore the pressure changes as you commute, for example.  However, this watch adds value in a few ways.  First, you get actual local pressure -- not that of a city 30 miles away.  Second, having it on your wrist gives you something to think about in idle moments (it's fun to watch the pressure change, watch the direction clouds are moving overhead, and imagine where the highs and lows might be).  Third, it's kind of cool to see how much pressure changes with altitude.  Actually, there's a down-side to this.  Where I live, the pressure has been around 24.8 inches.  Since all the weather reports and books use sea-level pressure, I have no intuitive feeling for whether 24.8 inches is high or low.  I guess I will develop that with time, but for now I'm just watching how the numbers change over time.  Actually, there is a pressure trend section of the watch which shows an arrow near the middle for small changes, and farther to the left or right for larger changes.  It does seem to work in general, but I am not sure how reliable this feature is, since it sometimes seems to show a change that doesn't match my interpretation based on the numbers displayed.  But perhaps it is referencing the original data at higher resolution, while I am displaying the numbers in mmHg, which is rounded to the nearest 0.05.The altimeter reading is merely calculated from the barometer reading, and I will probably place more trust in the GPS-based altitude on my Android device, since that doesn't require accounting for weather changes.  However, it is convenient to be able to glance down at my wrist for approximate altitude while driving.The thermometer, which shows a compromise between your wrist temperature and air temperature, has but one practical use:  To measure the temperature in places where you habitually take the watch off for long periods (e.g. bedroom or perhaps office).  Even when you take it off, it takes a long, long time to adjust to ambient temperature.  I made the mistake of recalibrating the thermometer, because I couldn't believe it was showing 80 degrees in my house half an hour after I took it off!  There is no way to go back to factory calibration (although you can obviously re-calibrate using another thermometer).  My advice is to be patient, and trust the factory calibration.The other aspects of the watch are just what you would imagine if you were to pay $15 for a non-barometer Casio watch.  The displays are perfectly visible from all typical angles.  The screen does not scratch from normal wiping with finger/shirt but I'm sure it will when it hits a rock.  The watch is about 1-7/8 inches across (perpendicular to the band), not insanely bulky.The main design criticism I have is that, when you are in barometer mode, if you want to see the altitude, you have to press the Mode button five times to get into Time mode and then press the Alti button.  Since other than the barometer/altimeter it's just a cheap watch, it seems silly not to allow the user to conveniently toggle between barometer and altimeter mode (e.g., just let the user press Alti while in barometer mode -- currently, this has no effect!).  Also it would be nice to have the date displayed all the time without having to go into Time mode.  Also, I would have gladly paid a little more if they could have added moon phase, tides, and sunrise/sunset times!  Surprisingly, there seem to be no affordable watches that combine all these features.  Since the pressure-trend display is blank in most of the watch's modes (or useless in Time mode, where it just shows graphic display of seconds), it would have been easy to put moon phase or tide height there, for example.I was going to buy the version with analog hands added (SGW400H), but was concerned the hands might block the barometer reading, which was the main feature of interest for me, so that didn't seem worth the risk.  I would have bought that if it had a feature to automatically fold the hands down (which some expensive models offer).  Another feature I thought would be cool is a graph-like display of the pressure over time, which some watches offer, but if you are commuting up/down hills that would not be meaningful most of the time anyway.All in all, it's a decent watch and well worth adding just $20-30 to have the barometer.

When reviewing a merchandise from Amazon, buyers often resort to criticizing the service (usually provided by market place merchants, not Amazon itself) and are frequently and promptly reminded by other reviewers to concentrate on the product, not circumstances under which they obtained it.With this review, I again want to emphasize that the check-out process, communication and promptness of delivery of this watch by Amazon has been stellar as always. The company's performance in this regard worked like a 'swiss clock'. Its attention to what was being sold and how, on the other hand, didn't.Once I held this 'timepiece' in my hand, I first and foremost realized that its crystal was NOT made of synthetic sapphire. As a test, albeit not the most reliable, one can knock the crystal with a nail: if the sound produced is like what one would expect to emanate from a solid rock, it's most likely sapphire. If the sound is more like quiet clinging from glass, the crystal's most likely made of mineral glass - a much cheaper and not desirable substitute. Those who know their watches also know all too well that sapphire is the most expensive part of a stainless steel Swiss quartz watch, once all the markup and pretentious hype is taken out. It's important to the product's reliability and integrity. Further, no one has to pay an exorbitant sum to own such a watch. Many, including some Wenger, Victorinox, Zodiac, and some Tissot watches can easily be found priced under $300.Researching the web, including Wenger's own site, revealed that the crystal of this watch is only 'sapphire-coated'. I shouldn't have to explain the difference.My second close examination found the watch bracelet made out of thin stamped stainless steel sheets, thus making the links hollow and taking away that subjective but wanted 'substantiality', or heft, in good watches. When handled, the 70489 Alpine - especially its bracelet - feels and sounds made of tin.Why then did I ever purchase it, one might ask? Look at the Amazon's page for this product, read through Product Specifications, and see for yourself what's stated there. Listed fifth from the top, it says 'Dial window material type: synthetic-sapphire'. So, it's only $119 with free s/h for a Swiss made, sapphire-crystalled watch with solid stainless steel body and bracelet - after all, the Amazon's description never explicitly stated otherwise, and no one could have thought genuine Swiss-made watches are made of cheap, stamped sheet metal - thus an excellent deal, and good looking too! How can one go wrong!It's currently on it's way back to Amazon, of course...So, with this very review, I give Amazon (Wenger should be ashamed as it is for giving this 'timepiece' - well, it's a piece of something for sure - a MSRP of $200) ZERO stars for such a beguiling description. Who looses here? Amazon, for I sent the product back for a full refund, and I'd hope anyone with self-respect and common sense did as well.On a side note, somewhat irrelevant to the purpose of this review, Wenger seems to have forgotten what the Swiss watch industry stands for in this day and age. No, their watches are NOT more reliable than Japanese- or even Chinese-made ones. Those frequently keep accurate time better. The construction, the materials, the aesthetics of a Swiss timepiece matter the most. Such watch must have some jewel-like properties to its quality, and that quality must be very good overall. It's having the back held by screws (the more, the merrier) and not of the push-in type, screw-in crown for better water resistance. The bracelet can be made of rubber and still be a very good one; however, if stainless steel's involved, it has to be nicely finished, 316L steel used throughout, including on the solid links. Or the watch could be made of ceramics, tungsten, and other high-quality, high-tech materials. And it's always welcome to have a synthetic sapphire crystal, even if that does push up the price.Wenger, if you forgo all the above, where does that leave you and your products that's so different a place in the minds of consumers from where all that Chinese-made garbage is?
summary: Amazon should correct the description or face more returns!

reviewText: For a $225.00 list price watch, the rubber wrist band is a piece of crap! In about a month's time I had to buy a new leather strap because the one that came with the watch completely broke down. Even more disappointing, when I wrote the company, they didn't even bother to respond. I won't buy another Wenger watch, period!

reviewText: I really like this watch.  I had gotten away from wearing watches but a situation came up where I needed to start wearing one again.  I am a fan of most anything Wenger, my briefcase, some of my pocket knives, and now my watch.  The quality is fantastic.  The time stays completely accurate and the band is very comfortable.  I rather like the size of it, even if it is a little beefy.  If I had to replace it, I would replace it with the same item.

Overall the watch is nice.  It isn't too large, has a good clean look and the construction seems solid.  However, the strap is bad.  I returned my first watch because one of the strap fasteners broke after a few days.  Now I'm on my second watch and after a couple months, the strap is starting to crack and fall apart.  I don't take it on/off frequently and I keep it clean.  But it just seems the strap is of poor quality.  The watch description says rubber, but when you look at the 'band material' in the specs, it says calfskin.  Either way, its not holding up well under regular use.  I may try to get a leather repair kit to fix the crack before it gets too big, but might be better to buy a whole new strap.  One of the fasteners is coming apart as well because its not stitched, it just uses crappy glue.I like this watch because it isn't too flashy and a reasonable price, but they need to use a better strap.
summary: Watch is decent but the strap needs help.

reviewText: This watch is perfect for a casual/classy look. I havent worn a watch in over 10 years, but my wife bought this watch for me for my birthday and I love it. It looks great and keeps accurate time without costing hundreds of dollars. Some people will over spend on an unattractive watch just to show it off, like some sort of status symbol. reviewText: I got this watch as more of a dressy/stylish type watch. The quality of this Wenger watch is even better than I was expecting. It comes with a nice leather strap. The face and details all add up to an attractive Swiss Made watch. I would not really consider it "rugged" or a watch the I would "swim, bike" with as the other reviewer mentions. That would ruin the leather strap and the shiny silver surfaces would scratch easily under any type of rugged conditions. This is a very nice casual/dress watch for about $100.My one major complaint about this watch, why it did not get 5 stars, is the glow paint used. I also wear Luminox watches which are real sport watches that are made to stand up to rugged use. Luminox uses a glow material that is made to last and will glow bright under any circumstance, like night sights on a gun, making it easy to read at night. This watch uses a thin layer of light activated glow paint that needs to be exposed to light before it will glow and does not even last long enough to make it through one evening. This is the one major drawback. It can make it very difficult to read at night. You can hold the watch right under a bright lamp and it will glow brightly but only 10 minutes later it dims to a point that is unreadable if you are in a dark bar/club. The Luminox watches, you do not have to worry about this, they will always glow bright. This is more of a stylish watch and is very attractive but -1 star for using cheap/thin glow in the dark paint that does not retain light long enough to last through the evening.Other than that, I would definitely recommend this watch if you are looking for something nice to wear, made by a quality Swiss company, but don't want to spend much money. If you are looking for a rugged sport watch, I would recommendLuminox Men's 3001 Original Navy SEAL Dive Watch

I used to have a very expensive Marmot Exum Gore-tex shell Marmot Exum Jacket - Men's which I absolutely loved. Unfortunately I lost it and had to find a replacement. Although the Columbia Hot Shot II is not quite at the same level as the Marmot shell, it is a really nice waterproof shell and in different ways from the Marmot, has its own strengths.What I really like about the Columbia Hot Shot II is its extremely light weight. For camping or hiking it is fantastic since it packs so small. And the amazing thing is that once you ball it all up and stuff it into your pack, when you need it all you have to do is shake it out once and its essentially wrinkle-free and looks great. The sleeve length is good and the velcro straps at the wrist help you close things up in nasty weather.I also like that the jackets seams are all fully taped which assists in making it truly waterproof. There are also pulls for the hood and waste that aid in keeping the elements out.What I don't care for is at quick glance it seems like there are two inside mesh pockets. In fact they are the lining for the outside side pockets. Although you could theoretically use them as inside pockets, that's not their purpose. They also act as a means to provide additional ventilation to the shell... you un-zip the side pockets which then serve the purpose of vents in the jacket.The reflective stripes on the jacket could have  been more effective than they are but still they offer a minimal amout of night-time visibility and add a nice styling touch to the shell.There are no pit-zips in this shell.  I'm not knocking the shell for the lack of pit-zips, I only mention it. Under extremely strenuous hiking for instance, you can get a little warm in this and pit-zips would have been nice to assist in cooling/ventilation. But it's not a deal-breaker since you know beforehand that the shell lacks pit-zips so if you want them, just don't get this shell but choose another.My biggest gripe with the shell is that the attached, non-detachable hood does not have a stiffened visor. In hard rain, this is an extreme oversight since water literally streams down your face because the hood has no structure to prevent that from happening. Other Columbia products have a stiffened visor on their hood so this is an area that disappoints. A workaround for me is to wear a visored cap before pulling up the hood over the cap.Overall I'm quite happy with this shell for inclement weather. It is a good lightweight shell that is very packable and remains wrinkle-free. I like the Burnt Orange color for its great visibility and I'm happy with my purchase. I'm 6'2" and bought the XL size which provides good arm length and ample room for layering underneath.UPDATE: 12/1/2010 - I've been wearing this in some really rainy weather lately and I must say that the lack of stiffened visor is a real pain in the butt. I also feel that the jacket would benefit by being a bit longer in the body. I still like it for it's light weight and packability but it does have a few cons which I've mentioned.UPDATE: 12/13/2010 - I wore this as a shell the other day for some good hard XC Skiing. I had two layers underneath, a base layer of wool and a fleece vest. I was working up a pretty good sweat and this did not breathe very well at all. In fact, when I completed my ski and took off the shell, it was completely frosted inside. So I would not recommend this for hard exertion usage in cold weather.
summary: Extremely light weight and easily packable waterproof shell

Keeps great time,  very rugged construction, would be a 5-star rating but for:(1)  Although I was amply warned through others' ratings about the barely audible level of the alarm, I got it anyway, and sure enough, it is one faint-sounding sonuvagun.  Somehow, though, the simple act of setting it seems to keep whatever event you wish to be reminded of more front-and-center in your mind.  Maybe that's just me - and I don't use it to wake up with.(2)  I carry the watch not on the supplied carabiner, but on a chain in my front pocket or watch pocket, and the alarm set button atop the case is easily accidentally pushed and set.  That button should be set not by a simple push, but perhaps with a push and twist, to avoid unintentional activation.

This product is advertised as an alarm pocket watch. As one other buyer noted, the alarm function is completely useless. The alarm cannot be heard.In addition, the time cannot be set accurately as there are no minute markers. It follows that time cannot be read accurately. This seems strange from a company that supposedly makes watches and knives for the Swiss military.I have another Wenger watch and was expecting something of the same quality. Clearly, this was a mistaken assumption.

First, I really love the look of this so called Wenger 73015 "Traveler Alarm" Black Dial Pocket Watch.The black face is very good looking, it has a black rubber bumper like guard built around it to absorb shocks/drops etc, water resistant to 99 Feet,beautiful stainless-steel case, it has the date function as well as a small well built leg that can pull out from the back to enable it to securely stand on a flat surface/table etc.It's built like a rock and feels like it, plus I always wanted a real "Swiss made" watch, so I bought this to hang on my waist pack/back pack/any shoulder bag.So what is the problem?The problem for me is the watch is called a "Traveler Alarm" and I bought it because it is supposed to have an "alarm".HOWEVER.... what Wenger calls an "alarm".... on this  "Traveler Alarm" can not even be called a joke at $156.94. (which is what it cost me inc. shipping)Sitting in my quiet bedroom... I have to hold the  so called "Traveler Alarm" 2 to 3 inches from my ear TO HEAR THE SOUND OF THE ALARM!I was in shock after it arrived, I set the alarm to hear it, and when it went off I thought it wasn't working.... until I held it 2-3 inches from my ear!The sound of the so called "alarm" is the tiniest "chirping" sound imaginable! I don't even think a dog could hear it! (and we know good a dogs hearing is)It's really a shame about the alarm, as I really like the watch.But if I am in an airport restaurant or bar and I need this to go off to let me know my flight is coming up... FORGET IT.At a bus or train station... FORGET IT.In the street.... FORGET IT.If I have to hold it 2-3 inches from my ear in my quiet bedroom... then what is the point of spending $156.94 for a Swiss Made "Traveler Alarm" Pocket Watch!!??Fortunately the seller SwissOutpost has a return policy.... but keeps the shipping charge and charges a "re-stocking" fee!So I'll get back my money... LESS $6.95 shipping to me... LESS $5.50 to send it back... and LESS a $10.00 "re-stocking" fee.Which obviously means I get refunded $128.49 of my original  $156.94 spent for this watch.... better than nothing.If you don't care about having a "real alarm" that is "AUDIBLE", it's a nice watch.If having an alarm that FUNCTIONS and is easily "AUDIBLE".... DON'T BUY THIS WATCH.**Update as of Sept 5th.:As a Labor day special, I just bought a Black Casio Men's AW80V-1BV World Time Ana-Digi Data Bank for $19.56 .. free two day shipping.With "3 different Daily Alarms (1 with snooze)"  YEA!!Later for Wenger Swiss "Travelers Alarm" watch.***Update as of Sept 9th. :SwissOutpost the seller/shipper has told me they no longer charge a "$10.00 re-stocking fee" on returns, I have received a complete "full refund" of $156.94 including shipping.To be fair to SwissOutpost... they shipped lightening fast, have a very courteous Cust. serv.. It's really Wenger who makes/designs the watch is where the problem comes from.
summary: If you need a "REAL" alarm function.. DON'T BUY THIS WATCH.

BEAUITFUL CRAFTED POCKET WATCH, BUT APPOND ARRIVAL THERE WAS NO MOVEMENT OF TIME.HAD TO SENT TO WENGER N.A. FOR REPAIR. HAVE NOT RECEIVED BACK YET!SO I HOPE TO SEE IT SOON.

reviewText: First, the watch I received from the seller had obviously been returned by another dissatisfied customer.  When I received it the protective film on the face was askew, the watch was loose in the presentation box and the manual in the box wasn't even for this watch.  Clearly the seller just reshipped a defective watch.  Not happy at all about that as it is being sold as "new."  At least open your returns to see if everything is there before shipping the product to the next customer.As for the watch itself, "swiss made" means nothing these days.  Truly nothing.  I've seen more garbage "swiss made" watches than I can count lately but this one is the top of the worst.  The only feature that actually worked was the time keeping.  The dual time hand doesn't keep up with the main hour hand so it's useless.  The date doesn't change (and I'm certain I have the right am/pm setting).  The alarm, when it sounded at all, is 5 to 7 minutes late from where I set it and I tried over and over again to be precise and each time it was late.  When setting the alarm the date wheel would move which doesn't seem right to me.  The second hand doesn't match up the the tick marks on 1/2 of the dial, this is a pet peeve of mine.  I just think if you're going to the trouble to make second hand marks then the second hand should line up with them.  It's "swiss made" after all.Don't buy this watch.

Keeps accurate quartz time and like the extra time zone in a quality Swiss watch. Do not use the rubber, hook, or alarm and therefore my rating does not reflect those features, which would lower the rating.

I purchased this watch for the alarm function and the fact that Wenger makes quality products. The watch is well made and quite hefty but I returned it since the alarm is inaudible at either bedside or in a pocket. Moreover, it can't be heard more than a foot away from my ear. According to the Wegner service rep I contacted, the alarm level is typical for this type of product. This was very puzzling to me since the appearance and objective of the watch (with the protruding buttons) makes it clearly an alarm model, rather than merely a pocket watch with an added function. If you're looking for a new pocket watch that has a sturdy, quality appearance and don't care about the alarm, get this one. But if you need a pocket watch with an audible alarm for wake-ups or reminders, look elsewhere.

I am an avid league bowler with 200pin average.  Shoes should fit and should feel comfortable.  I don't feel that you absolutely need to invest over a $100+ for a pair of bowling shoes.  Honestly, any pair of shoes that have a sliding surface and doesn't have a marring heel can be made into bowling shoes.  If you are looking to get your own shoes and away from the the rentals at the lanes, you practically owe it to yourself to invest in your own shoes.  Chances are, if your are renting shoes every week, you can pay for these in less than two months of rental costs.These Dexter shoes started very stiff.  Took about 9 games or so to break them in for the leather to soften.  They do slide naturally, and aren't too slick.  I've heard that some Dexter products are so slippery out of the box that it's uncomfortable.  I believe that these shoes should last several league seasons.  Shoes run true to size.  These don't have that tennis shoe feel, and you may require insoles if you have large arches in your feet.
summary: Decent bowling shoes for the price

I purchased the Kangaroo Keeper at a local office supply store. I was excited because I have a hard time finding stuff in my purse and I wanted a keeper to put an end to that 'hurried digging to find my cellphone before it stops ringing' thing.When I first removed the keeper from the box I immediately noticed the smell.  It smelled horribly of a mixture of fuel and mothballs.  I thought I would never be able to use it and was instantly disappointed.  However, I decided to open the keeper and set it out to air.  That did help dissipate the smell a lot.  About six hours later I was able to put stuff in it and put it in my purse, though I have left my purse unzipped, just to let the keeper continue to air.One thing I especially like about the keeper, is that it is a good contrast to the inside of my purse.  My purse is dark colored and it is hard to see items in my purse because there is no contrast.  With the keeper, my objects contrast against the light (tan) color of the keeper.  It makes it easier for me to locate what I need.The pockets of this item are okay. However, I think they should make two pockets that are wider than the widest pocket they currently have.  I can slide my Samsung Mesmorize phone into the largest ones, but it is a snug fit.  It's not hard to remove, but I'd like a bit more room.  I also think that all the pockets should have the elasticized tops.  The straight tops are okay, but the elasticized pockets are nice and flexible and you can put stuff into them and remove things much easier in those pockets.  I also like the key keeper, and the fact that the pack I purchased included to different sizes.Things I am not so impressed with are the smell (although that has dissipated), and the type of material chosen to make the keeper.  I am waiting to see if it is durable.  If it is, it will be fine.  I thought it might be better if it was made in suede, but it's possible that this vinyl-type material is the easiest to keep clean.  I am also unsure if one could fit a water bottle into the pockets.  If you reversed the large keeper, putting the pockets on the outside, it might work with a small bottle of water.Overall I'm pleased, thus far, with my purchase, although I probably should have tried Walmart or Bed, Bath & Beyond and saved $5.00 on the price.
summary: Kangaroo Keeper:  Once You Get Past The Smell...
