reviewText: I bought the Kangaroo Keeper for my wife because she gets frustrated when searching for things in her purse. When I finally received the items I noticed a smell not unlike diesel fuel or insecticide (it's made from polyethelyn). I tried everything from vinegar, clothes detergent and simply airing it out. Nothing works and now the Kangaroo Keepers are hanging in my garage competing with the exhaust fumes from my car; and my wife still continues to struggle with finding things in her purse. Don't buy this, it's toxic!

I was using several smaller cosmetic-type zipper bags to move my things from purse to purse, so when I saw this product, it looked as though it would do the job a little more easily. I don't know if I'll ever be able to find that out, however, because the inserts have such a strong chemical odor that I do not want to put them into any of my purses. I've tried spraying them with Febreeze and setting them outside to air out, and I have also sent them through a machine wash with extra detergent, but the odor persists.Perhaps over time, the smell will finally dissipate, but until then, I can't review the performance of the product. It's too bad, because the insert looks as though it would be quite useful... if only it didn't smell like a vat of dry-cleaning fluid.
summary: Has a strong odor of dry-cleaning fluid that won't go away

It doesn't let out water or leak, so fill it up with ice.  The only problem I have found with this cooler is that it zips at one end, so it can be difficult to get to your drinks without spilling a lot of ice. Even more important for an uptight course that has a stringent no alcohol policy this bag is concealed perfectly, and allows you to easily get your drinks out onto the course, without being seen, where they can be enjoyed in peace.Depending on how often you take drinks onto the golf course this cooler bag may be worth it for you.

This band looks great on my wife's Gucci watch. It replaced a nice band with a quality band.

I've searched high and low for a small narrow suede watchband to replace the one on my first childhood watch - it's an old windey-watch, not valuable at all, but I love it and wanted to be able to wear it - the old suede band had fallen apart and this replacement is perfect.  It arrived quickly, seems to be good quality and I'm pleased.

Received the watch bands in perfect condition.  Shipped securely.  Nice well padded watchband.  Fun color.  Looks great with my vintage watches.  Only question, when did watch bands start coming without the pins?

It looks sharp on an old Tissot Seastar with a blue face. I was dissappointed to see it was made in China but what isn't these days. On installation it seems I must have nicked it because it has a small cut where it attaches to the watch. This makes me nervous as to the durability of the band since I was not using any tools to put it on. Also it was 18mm but the buckle half is closer to 17mm. I am not sure if this is a quaity control issue or natural variation in the material.
summary: Overall it does what I want but there are some issues

reviewText: Good quality leather and very nicely made though a bit stiff and a tad shorter than I would have liked.
summary: Nice for a summer switch up

reviewText: Excellent boots, warm, and comfortable while driving. Every steel toe made for construction has steel shanks that don't bend, so all of my boots would leek after a few weeks. These are more flexable, no leeks. Just don't leave them in a damp place over night  they obsorbe moisture like a sponge.

This just arrived today.  I was looking for a well made pair of boots to replace my aging Robert Stevens felt lined rubber boots which have begun to crack.  These Wolf Pac boots are exactly what I needed.  They have a very thick felt lining.  I wear a size 9 -9 1/2 shoe, so I ordered these size 10's as I usually need a larger size boot, especially with heavier socks.  The 10 is a snug fit, but I found it easier to slip these on than my old boots which have a thinner lining.  It is 5 F out right now, but these boots kept my feet (also wearing heavy wool boot socks) warm on my brief test walk outside in the snow.  The soles are flexible but have a steel shank and a really thick cleated tread. Added bonus is these are quality made in the USA.  Hopefully these last as long as my old boots which I have had for ten years, but the price is extremely reasonable.  This is an excellent value from what I see so far.Pros: Well made all rubber outer construction.Thick felt lining keeps feet warm.Steel shank sole, thick cleated tread and steel toe.Made in USA.Easy to slip on.Need to wear them a bit to see if I can find any problems.  With the weather as miserable as it is this year that shouldn't be an issue needing to wear them.
Functional, great for yard work & using a chain saw... Slips on/easily. Great value for the price. The material/ make suggest they will last a long time.

I work at a turkey processing plant, so the floors are always wet, have animal fat/meat scraps on the floor. I bought these originally in August, 2013 and come the end of the December 2013, into January 2014, the boots have fallen apart. At first I enjoyed these boots, they kept my feet dry, were fairly comfortable, and seemed to be slip resistant.After a few months, the 'slip resistant' nature of these started to fade out. Then within the last month-month and a half, they started to crack on the inside and outside of the foot near the middle of the boot. I've owned numerous PVC/Nitrile/Rubber boots within the last two years, but these were the only ones that were basically splitting in half.I personally wouldn't buy ONGUARD brand boots again. While they are a decent price, you do get what you pay for.I've uploaded some pictures of my boots. Don't mind the meat on the bottom :)

The hat itself is 'ok' however the product color (coyote) and the product photo are NOT even close to what arrived to me via UPS.Not 'coyote' in color and definitely it was not black.I ended up with a DARK brown cap in color.  What's up with that?Product description has two color choices (only) so where did this color come from.Not even close.
summary: Coyote in color ?  It is not.

reviewText: longer bill then i was expecting. but functional. material seems standard for the price.not amazing not bad. velcro is sown down properly. no corners sticking out and doesnt rip off with changing or taking off patches. the back strap is an adjustable velcro, dont know what the keeper string is suppose to do. (its also velcro but inserted through a small hole in the lining material on the back side.) i dont know any one high speed enough to need that who isnt already adjusting the strap for a snug fit. maybe if your a crew chief around choppers all day if your allowed a hat, but thats what ear pro does. what ever. good hat for the money.

This is a hat! I have a condor and a rothco velco...they suck! This is durable, it is what a hat shout be, nice thick bill that retains the shape you give it. This is coming from someone who owns over 40 hats...this one is the best made hat I own...it is great! Highly recommend hazard4 hats, I'm curious to see what else they make thats amazing.What I'm trying to say is, yes this hat is more expensive at $24, but the others are 12 and this one is ten times the quality.
Ok got the hat the other day. Have bought similar hats in the past this one was exceptional. All stitching is good velcro is centered and clip function works good.

When I ordered the hat, I was excited, as it fills a need for one hat, a billboard, per se, that can be changed as the job description changes...When I got it and opened the box, the coyote tan hat greeted me.  I ordered black.  I contacted the company, and received uber assistance in exchanging the hat.  One interesting thing though...I wore the tan hat for a couple of days, and it fit incredibly well (my head is a little large, with a high crown) When I returned it and got the black one, it is made differently.  While still fitting, it seems to be slightly smaller in circumference above the adjustable band in the back.I still love it, and will wear it often, but I wonder about the difference in the hat.  Perhaps a different person sewed the black one?Also, the shipping was incredible.  I got the hat within two days of ordering, and got the replacement within 5 days of shipping the incorrect one back.Overall, 10 stars, if this is indicative of their entire product line, I will be getting more!

Was initially pleased when I opened the package.  The cap seemed sturdy enough, and the multiple patches of velcro for mounting morale patches was the whole reason I bought it.  But when I tried it on, I discovered that it was not the cap for me.  As someone who can't stylishly or comfortably wear strap-backed caps due to them having to be fully extended to even fit on my head, I can safely say that these hats seem to be made for smaller heads than mine.  Even with the strap in back fully extended, it would not fit my head comfortably.  Sold it to my brother, whom it fits reasonably well, and he seems to like it just fine.  If the company ever makes a larger version, I will be very interested.  The only complaint I have other than the size is the retention strap and clip. If you want it fully retracted, there is nowhere to conceal the clip.  This is a minor issue, though, and I suspect the strap could be easily removed if it became inconvenient.

I tend to read a lot of reviews before I buy something from amazon and I was cautious of buying this cap because I found that another buyer had trouble with the size...I have a big dome, almost a 9 in cap size, and this hat fits me very well and there is room for more. Its simple construction is comfortable and it is adjustable from the velcro back strap. It has places to put patches, one on the fastening strap, the sides, the main patch in the front, and has velcro at the apex of the hat.Even the chicks dig it, I am serious, I was complemented my many for the look of this hat. lol The look of the cap looks like you mean business.Recommended for those who like to swap out Morale patches and going to the range. Haven't tested it in the field.
summary: Nice simple tactical hat, fits big heads!

reviewText: Nothing that special about this hat.  The bells and whistles written in the specs are a bit overrated in my opinion.  It's a hat but it doesn't really shout quality when you get it, it shouts, "hey I'm a hat with velcro on it..."

A lot of types of these hats online now, but this one is stitched better, and is made with better materials. It is made in Taiwan which is much better craftsmanship then china. Nice because it has the ability to add other patches or Velcro accessories to the hat, like a flashlight holder, or more patches. The hat is adjustable and fits like any other adjustable baseball cap. The hat also comes with a cord and clip to hang on your collar or clothes instead of needing to use the Velcro, or just lose the hat in wind or during moderate movement and activity.

Incredible construction, built like a tank, the lanyard to connect to your collar is brilliant. I was going to look for one, but here it was already. Definitely worth the money. Much better than other caps on the market for work in the field.I used these hats on an outdoor two week photo shoot, and they're worth every penny. For me the nicest thing is that the strap in the back is closed with Velcro, not a buckle. When I go to shoot photos and turn the hat around, there's no metal buckle pressing into my forehead. The back strap also has Velcro loops along it, so you can put on a horizontal morale patch if you like.The built-in lanyard was fantastic on windy days, saved the hat from going over a cliff when the wind gusted. Have one in black, one in tan.

I had ordered the black version of this hat and was extremely pleased. The black hat was a very pliable material, and had a deep gusset for the depth of the head. The coyote hat was a more rigid material, and had a shallower pocket for the head. I could not believe how different the two products were.

I live in Alaska. I am lacking in the full head of hair department . I bought 5 of the original beanies produced by helly Hansen . These new are lighter than the original. Single layer vs double. The fabric is not meshed like the original. This is the exact reason it is hard to order via Internet
Not rocket science.  It fits on your head and is thin for under a helmet.  If you noggin is small or medium size though this isn't for you.

When I bought this only the small size was listed. I checked HH's own web site and found nothing.This is a good product but the small size is a little too small for me. Other than that it is a good product and works as described.

I also think the size should be a bit smaller to qualify as a beanie - I don't have a tiny head but this still has a lot of slack. It shifts a bit - I like the material and construction however, quality.
Description and the photo of the beanie looked solid and think... I open up my amazon box always geeked and I find a du rag in there.. I said wtf put it aside on table... I take it as lossShazam
These are just the best- cool looks, great performance, these are the only shades I've worn for years, and will continue to do so as long as they are around!
These sunglasses arrived broken. I didn't bother ordering a replacement pair since they appeared pretty cheaply made. I figure they would just chip or break again. I don't recommend them.

These sunglasses have wonderful lenses but the frame is very fragile and cracked after I had worn them only a couple of times.  I have tried to use Superglue to hold them together, but it has not worked.  I wouldn't recommend this product because of the fragile frames.
Great sunglasses. My only complaint is that they are very stiff and tight. Also moisture fogs up the inside when they press so tightly against my face.
It's a good value for polarized, and I like the shape. Note that it's the wrap style (rests on your eyebrow and cheek). I'm not a big fan of that style regularly, but I'll keep it for sports.
Very pleased with product, love the polarized lenses.  Looked like a much more expensive pair.  I am very happy with these.

I've gone through countless pairs of similarly priced sunglasses and all of them seem to get damaged or scratched very quickly. I bought these last year and they still perform like new. Super scratch resistant, and I put my glasses through very tough conditions. I frequently drop them and I store them in my laptop bag with a myriad of other items which would normally ruin other glasses. These still show no signs of wear. I also bought a few other models and frame colors of this brand, but still have not had to use any of them yet. I figured I'd run through them like my previous sets. Nope...these are still going strong. I do use the amber on cloudy days though, great for fishing and driving.

I purchased these polarized glasses in hope of finding a pair flattering for a woman and for fishing.  I also am very hard on glasses so I didn't want to invest a lot of money.  These are great.  I am able to see through the water well and my husband tried them on and they look good on him too (except he isn't into tortoise shell).  We are ordering another pair for him.

I have had these for about a month now and used them to replace a pair of Maui Jims which I kept breaking.  I figured that if I was going to break sunglasses all the time, I should do it with cheap ones.  I have yet to break this pair.  The frame is very stiff, but the lenses themselves are just as good as my old sunglasses.  I would definately recommend them and plan to buy another pair when I inevitably break these.
summary: Very nice, especially for the price

I have bought these several times and this order has been the best quality of all!!! best fitted socks I have perchased

Whoever created this sock is a true genius!

Awesome socks.  If you can't figure out how to not have the toe seem bother you like some reviewers, your clearly too dumb for a pair of socks.  They are nice, price is great and they go great in my minimalist shoes.  Buy again I will.

Seems to be a recurring theme with these socks.They fit great - breath well but fell apart fast.Throwing out my first sock out of two 6-packs today due to wearing on the ball and a hole in the toe. Had them for less than six months.My old UA socks - some 30+ pairs - I threw out 6 socks in 8 years. Not a good sign of their QC department.
summary: Great Breathability - fell apart in a hurry.

reviewText: My husband loved these socks. The extra large size fit his size 14 feet perfectly and they are smooth around the toes without that noticeable toe seam that most socks have. They are his new favorites. i will be ordering more soon. I would definitely recommend these socks.
These socks are very nice for xlg mens socks.  They hold their shape and fit nicely.  It is not easy to find xlg socks in the stores.
awesome, should have got them at the beginning, now I have increased my treadmill time by up to 12 miles, fantastic workout gear
Toe seem is huge and extremely uncomfortable.  This is my one and only complaint. But it is a huge factor to me. I can't stand to wear them.
This is the second time I have purchased these for my son.  Assuming they are the same quality as the first, they should wear well.  My son likes how they fit.

I am diabetic and my feet are a major concern for me. These socks give them a degree of extra comfort and have improved my over all foot health. I recommend them to any and all people who have problems with their feet or just have a bad tiome with sweaty smelly feet. :)
These socks wear wonderfully and don't bunch or slide around anywhere. They have great support and don't make your feet too hot during the day.
I have these ones and the white ones . They are very comfortable and durable socks . and worth the price.
They feel really good! I don't think I could have asked for better socks. I recommend getting them. UnderArmours for the win!!!

I was looking for socks that were a bit thinner for some running shoes that thicker socks don't work as well as I would like. These are quality and fit well, (which with the big feet I have is no small feat). Would not hesitate in buying more.

Not worth the extra price.  Already wearing out on the bottom after 3-4 uses.  Had similar socks to these a few years back and they lasted 10x longer.  Not sure why these are so bad, but I won't be purchasing more.
These are the most comfortable and durable socks I've ever owned.  They don't make my feet sweat, plus they look very nice with any type of shoe.  I'm actually going to order more right now!
I have been very pleased with my purchase. These socks are very comfortable and ware well. I will be buying them again.

i don't ask a lot from a pair of socks.  i do however expect that i can get more than a couple months wear out of them before they start getting holes in the toes.  these socks don't pass muster, they will need replaced by a better product soon.

I love these socks. They're extremely comfortable and my feet don't seem to sweat (and therefore smell) when I wear them. I run in the freezing cold (for which I have long UA socks) and in sweltering heat (for which I have these). Great pick for trail running or just wearing with casual shoes.

Was looking for a black ankle sock and decided to give these a try.  Was very please to see sizing avaiable.  I take a US 13 and most socks are one size fits all, basically ending @ 12-13ish.  These fit nicely with my foot not pushing for space.  The sock is comfortable and almost doesn't feel like its there.  Both the toe and heal are reinforced for added durability.  The sock's seams(transitions between foot and heal and foot and toe) are more subtle which will likely reduce chafing in activities and I also think will add to durability as I have seen some socks where the sock splits apart at the seems.  The region above the forefoot has a nice breathable mesh which in some athletic socks I have had in the past was too much of a mesh to the point that in socked feet you looked funny.  Haven't done any activity with them nor have I worn them for any duration just out of the shipping box, on and "hmm these are NICE!".  Now I just want to see how they hold up over time(wearing/washing) and if the damn washer/dryer steals em like some of my other socks!
Was so happy to find these in the larger size. I didn't realize that my husband was buying average size socks for his large feet. He's amazed at how much more comfortable his feet are.

I've been wearing UA socks for roughly 5 years.  I don't own any other brands.  I do change styles a little bit, but these are the most "airy" and extremely comfortable.These will be a repeat purchase
My son states he loves the way the son feel and is very happy with these socks. Will order more

Seems to me as if this sock trapped the moisture inside of the sock, therefore making it seem a little damp when I take it off.  No bad odors though, which is the upside.  Unfortunately, it picks up all kinds of dust and particles on the bottom even after only 1 wear.  Nice design and fit, and it look good, when new and clean.
very comfortable, I bought two more pack of these, When it is warm outside these are the only socks I wear.
I love these socks, they are great for being active. They keep my feet dry and cool when i ride my bike, or working out at the gym. I cant wait to buy some more of these socks.
3 pairs already have holes which surprises me considering the quality I typically receive from UnderArmor products. Usually 5 star quality.
I love a distinctive logo on the sock.  This separates mine from my two sons.  These are soft and very comfortable
great sock, great price. i ordered these because they came in a larger size than average socks. it's hard to find lo-cut socks for size 14 feet.
Horrible quality. The socks fall apart within three uses and I don't even use them to workout. I use them to walk around during the day and I've never seen a crappier product from UA.
summary: I've never seen a crappier product from UA.

reviewText: You will love these socks, they are very comfortable. Great way to care for your feet. Highly recommend these for the committed  runner.
These are great socks - they have moisture absorption and shock absorption. We ended up returning for the no show, but they are great socks and I would recommend them to anyone.

Phenomenal socks.  Fit well, handle moisture well.  I've used mine a lot, and washed them a lot, and haven't experienced the falling apart that other reviewers have mentioned.  And I crammed size 15-Wides into them.
My son needed extra large, these are perfect.  He was very happy with this "sock" stuffer as a gift item.
Fit well, as I wear a 13 shoe, these socks had a little room at the toe and a perfect fit at the ankle.  A good thing.  Price was right also.

The socks were great the first use, but after the first wash they shrunk drastically. Now they are snug fit, still great sock for gym/cycling/walking ect. They will shrink a lot though, one pair ripped as I tried to stretch it around my heel. I would try another style of socks next time. Had a pair of under armor socks before that didn't shrink as bad as these n they lasted a lot of use n washes.

I bought two 6 packs of these socks. I rotated them in with my other 30 plus pairs of socks. I have none of these Under Armour socks left. I got one to two uses out of each pair. Every single sock developed holes in them. There was no consistency to where the holes developed. It was definitely an overall weak sock. I had the heels open up, the ball of the foot, the toes, the top of the sock, the outside edge, and even had a couple rip completely in half as I put them on. I washed them with all my other socks that I am still wearing so it is not a matter of bleach or anything like that.
summary: Lowest quality socks I have ever owned.

reviewText: Even though they were the wrong size for my husband, they fit my grandson.  This prevented me sending them back.  The quality is really nice.

Locally I can only find these in size L.  I have size 13 feet - so I needed XL.  I ONLY use these types of socks ad I love them.  They are durable, comfy, breathe, and last.  I love these socks.By the way - if you have size 14 or 15 feet - these run a little large on me - so I think you should be fine too.
Great Socks that fit perfect.  XL fits a size 14 foot very well.  Nice breathable top of the sock with padding on the bottom.

I ordered these socks and they were delivered on February 20th.  Today is March 4th and the socks already have holes in them.  I am very disappointed and hope to get my money back!  I can't imagine anything from Under Armour falling apart this quickly, which makes me think they might be fake, although the packaging looked real.  Sooo disappointed!
Form fitting, elastic is great so the neck of the sock doesn't ever stretch out. Only socks I ever buy now.
These are nice socks. I wear a size 14 shoe and they fit perfectly. They've been thru the laundry a couple times with no shrinkage. They work!

I've got size 15 feet - the XL fit perfectly. Great ventilation and cushioning. I'll be ordering another 6-pack - they're definitely worth the small extra cost.Update 12/03/2012:While these socks started out fantastically, within 2 months I've lost 3 pairs to holes under the ball of the foot - and I'm about to lose a 4th.  I'm not hard on socks - I got almost 5 years out of 6 pairs of socks from Sam's club.  In fact I don't even use these for athletics - I have several double-layer socks I use exclusively for exercise and sports.  I only wear these around the house and for taking the dog for walks.  Having a full dozen pairs of these, it's not like I'm wearing the same pair every week - maybe twice a month, max.  For the additional cost and the Under Armour brand, I expected more from these socks.Update 1/25/2013:After a short 4 months, half of which were full-on winter when I wore wool socks instead, I'm down to 3 pairs - and those already have small holes starting.  In the last few months I've only worn these with slippers around the house.  Total fail on Under Armour's part.

Extremely comfortable. Love the design and fabric. Only reason I gave it 4 stars rather than 5 is because on a few of the socks, the grey thread is starting to loosen where it meets with the black. I have no holes yet, but in time I think they will develop some. I think these are probably the best socks without spending a ton of money.

I'm excited to actually have found some socks that fit my size 14 feet -- can never find them in the store, but these do the trick. Hopefully, they'll last a little longer without wearing a hole through the toe than my other shoes.
So just make sure that you buy a size up, because otherwise they're super comfortable, very durable, and pretty damn stylish too.
summary: Under Armour Socks are too small.

reviewText: Calling these thigns "Extra Large" is just crazy.  I wear a 13 shoe and they will fit the first time I wear them, but they are tight.  After a single wash, they are very tight and the material does not give at all...Pehaps would be better if the sizing was more accurate.

Having big feet, it is often hard to find socks that fit. These socks do fit and are very comfortable. Not sure yet how long they will last as they are thinner than other socks, but for now I am pleased with the fit and style of these socks.
I love the arch support in the socks...keeps them in place when working out.  Good moisture dissipation as well.  Couldn't beat the price!

I have had these socks in the past but bought them at a store for a lot more then they are selling for here on Amazon. They are very comfortable socks that go just slightly above my gym shoes which go up to my ankle. I swear by these socks and I recommend that you buy them too if your looking for a comfortable gym sock that does not allow your feat to get to hot or sweaty.
very thin, rip very easily and too tight around ankles for extra large socks.  too cheaply made for the money I paid.

I bought these to wear to work and whenever I'm out of clean white socks, and they've been great. They're comfortable and breathe well, and they've held up great. The only downside I've seen is that my girlfriend stole a few pairs because she likes them too, so I have to order more.I've had a few where the top of the sock "uncuffed" a bit, as if the stitching wasn't solid enough. It's only a few socks though, and it doesn't affect them other than cosmetically, so whatever.EDIT: So six months or so in, nearly every single sock was wearing very, very thin in the heel. A year in, holes were developing in the heel, and by a year and a few months they're all in the garbage. I kind of expected more for almost $2/sock. I've since switched to theNike DriFit socksand they're far and away better. They're more comfortable, they look better, they're holding up MUCH better, and they seem to be more consistent.The downside is that the Nikes are usually more expensive. If you watch the deal sites you can find them on big discount, which brings them down to a comparable (or even better) price. Even at more expensive though, would you rather buy something cheap that wears out in six months or something expensive that lasts years?
summary: Great socks all around, or so I thought

reviewText: The socks arrived on time, and looked just like the picture. But they are thinner than the socks I have gotten from UnderArmor in the past.

I really like the socks so far...I've read that some are falling apart after a couple of washes...They are in there now...One major grip...I ordered 3 packs and they shipped two with thestamp label on the back of the sock...and one pack they tried to sneak in with "Under Armour"written in...I figure the logo is bad enough but to put your name in a place where everyone cansee is unacceptable...Unless you are paying me to advertise your socks...yes I know its no bigdeal...Unless you find out someone gets free sock, gear and monthly paycheck...Just to showoff their stuff...
summary: You get what you pay for and maybe you don't

As always, Under Armour has good quality products. I have had these socks for quite awhile and I like them very much.
The XL socks are 13-16 I ware a size 12 shoe. These are the biggest sock I ever had. I don't have to struggle to put them on  anymore! These are Perfect! Soft as well!

These socks are really comfy, bought them for my son but my daughter keeps taking them.  They fitted exactly as we'd hoped and the colour is great, white socks always end up looking grey.  Would purchase again for sure.
under armour continues to build tough durable workout were love um  .these socks are comfortable and very durable and thick best workout sock around

reviewText: Socks fit and wash well. No surprises. Under Armour makes a good product. I would have liked a smaller package as I only needed three pairs.

I'm wearing these socks right now. They fit well, and feel good on my feet.  I really like the color combination as well, I think i've had enough of solid white Hanes socks.These have a slightly different feel, soft in a different kind of way; i wish I could explain it.I'm very happy with the purchase. I was hesitant spending 20 dollars in 6 pairs of socks, but after seeing them and wearing them; im glad I bought them.
The specifications on the amazon.com listing read these socks are seamless. That is important to runners. The socks are not seamless and is not on the packaging anywhere.

I bought a bunch of these and at first I thought they were really good but that did not last. They stretch out of sizes after some washings and they would not stay on my feet. I did not know under armour made these, so when I found them, I bought them. Glad I did. They fit well, and look good too.

So far these socks are an excellent investment.  The X-Large tag on the socks sort of scared me because I have large, wide feet, and usually XL really doesn't work for me, but these were great.  Let's hope they hold their worth for the long haul.
if you need comfortable socks, these are what you buy.  Under Armour basically outfits my athletic collection.  They're a little on the pricey side, but I am so happy with the quality.

reviewText: So my commute is a little over 12 miles and in the rain, needless to say, I'm out long enough to just get completely soaked. So, I tried these.The material is truly waterproof. HOWEVER, the top, were they close around your leg, (a) doesn't stay up, but continuously falls down your leg, forcing you to reach down and pull it up, and (b) lets a ton of water in as it drips down your leg. A ton of water, as in not even five minutes into my ride I could tell that my shoe was literally sitting in a pool of water inside this thing.I don't know why I thought it would work to keep the water out; I guess I thought, "hey, they make these things for a living, so they must know something I don't." But no, the makers of this product clearly haven't contemplated the fact that gravity makes water...drip...downwards. BAM. Truth bomb.Avoid this product; it doesn't perform as intended.

reviewText: My situation is a little unusual, I was trying to find something to cover my son's special orthopedic high-top shoes that are like sandals (open-toed).  I needed something to keep his feet warm and dry in the winter; he can't wear boots because he just kicks them off against the footplates of his wheelchair.  These shoe covers are easy to get on and off because of the rear zipper and fit well over his special shoes, although the XS size is a bit narrow and might not accomodate wider soles like athletic/running shoes.  The material is lightweight but it is wind- and water-proof.  And they actually stay on his feet!  The price was very reasonable and I am happy with this purchase.

Here are my two-cents on durability:  I'm ready to retire my first pair (several small holes and tears) after more than a year of service.  I am a year-round bike commuter (using standard pedals with toe clips) and wear these not only when it is raining/wet, but also when the temp. is below 30f (I live in Chicago, so that's most days in the winter.)  I'm guessing I got about 120-140 one-way, eight-mile trips out of them... and could have gotten more had I not walked around in them so much. The booties are thin enough not to be hot in the summer, and the fact that they are wind-proof helps a surprising amount in keeping the feet warm in the winter.  Like any other piece of cycling gear, I didn't expect them to last forever... but they kept my feet comfortable and dry for about 25 cents per one-way trip.  I think that's pretty reasonable.

I bought this jacket because I am allergic to down but need to stay warm during Boston winters. Overall, I am happy with this jacket although the sizing is weird. The body is a typical width for a medium and will easily accommodate a thick sweater, but the sleeves are tight, even on my skinny arms. The sleeves have been a good fit with my thinner sweaters, but are snug when I wear my oversize sweatshirts. Not tight enough for me to want to return the jacket, but noticeably tighter. The sleeve length is longer than most other women's jacket brands, although I have yet to find a company that makes women's jackets with sleeves long enough to keep my wrists covered when I am brushing snow from my car. The neck and wrist cuffs start off very snug, but loosen up pretty quickly with use -- mine were comfortable after a day or so of wear. The cuffs are great features for keeping out drafts. I like that it has the type of zipper that lets you zip from the bottom up if you will be sitting for extended periods of time, and the insulated hood is a nice feature as well. Side- and top-entry front pockets are good for keeping hands warm without having to worry about knocking your keys or phone out of your pocket. I am very happy with the flattering fit and its ability to keep me warm and dry so far this season, although I haven't had a chance to wear it in temps below 30 degrees yet.

reviewText: After a week of use, I'm happy with my SportBand. I was looking for something to give me distance and pace while running, and this does a nice job. Out of the box, it was very close on both a walk and a run on the track (2 laps each). Using the software, I can set it to scroll through distance, pace, and duration only. While the display is small, the readout itself uses the entire display so it is very readable. Only negative is the website (costs a star). It is slow to load, and it tends to oversimplify the data presentation. For example, instead of showing actual pace on the vertical axis of a run with a grid line, the vertical is dimensionless and effort is put into 3D effects with shadowing. Edward Tufte - HELP!

This band does all the essential functions I need to track my runs.  Fairly accurate right out of the box, but easy to improve accuracy with a simple calibration.  If you spend the extra money on a Nike+ heart rate monitor it'll sync with the band and give you pulse as well.Love keeping up with my runs on this device and being able to compare and compete with myself and my friends.

I have a very small wrist for an adult female and this band fits great.  The mileage was off a bit, but once I calibrated it it seems to be spot on up to about 5 miles.  It is very user friendly and a great value.

I like this watch a lot. It has its flaws, but for the price, its pretty great. Originally I used my phone to track distances with one of the many available apps, but I don't like carrying my phone around and it also drains my battery pretty badly. This is a pretty great option for those of us who don't want to spend 150+ for a GPS watch.The good parts:It tracks mileage pretty accurately AFTER calibration. I ran 2.5 miles on a track the first night I had this watch to calibrate it. The initial reading (before going in to calibrate) had me at 2.93 miles. Clearly it was pretty far off. However, the next weekend I ran an organized 5k race and wore the watch. It tracked me at 3.13 miles, which is probably pretty spot on when you figure in a little bit weaving on the race course.Its cheap. Like I said, if you want a GPS enabled watch, you'll be spending AT LEAST 150 bucks, probably far more if you go for one of the more advanced Garmin models. They're great watches, I'm just not a place where I can afford that.The Nike+ website is awesome. All of your data is easily imported to the Nike+ site and you can see your entire run in detail. Its awesome, I get detailed feedback and it keeps a history of my runs for no extra charge.The bad:There's no backlight. I assume this was done to converse battery life (which I can't attest to due to not running more than 5 or so miles with it), but it sucks for night runners. If you don't run in a relatively well lit area, you'll be doing a fair amount of squinting.The face orientation is kind of awkward. The watch is very slim, which looks nice, but also puts the face at a perpendicular angle to the average person. It makes it much harder to see what your current distance or time is while running. You can't just do a quick glance.All in all, I think its worth the price. However, if you want to spend more, there are better options out there.
summary: For the price, its really hard to beat.

Beyond that, I had two gripes: the band itself is not comfortable. The attachment of the band through the holes spent the greater part of my run trying to eat through my epidermis. Needless to say, it was not pleasant. Also, the USB connector is designed extremely poorly. Because of the connectivity, I had to lift my computer off the table anytime that I wanted to plug the USB in due to the overhang that would force the USB to disconnect.All in all- save you money. This is a very poorly conceived, inaccurate, and superfluous piece of technology. I would recommend getting a GPS watch from Garmin if you are interested in keeping track of your runs with any precision.
This product is amazing. Now I like going for a run. I can search my exercise on the web. It is highly recommended.
very nice and easy to adjust the sizing as well as sync the band. i used it a lot and enjoy it

I loved the Sportband at first, even though I experienced some of the frustrations of other reviewers, I reset the band and sensor and had no difficulties.  However, I only used it for about a month and a half.  It was very hot and humid in my area, and I noticed the screen was going blank during runs.  I couldn't tell if it was still recording.  Finally, the screen went blank permanently.  Tried resetting.  Tried charging.  Got nothing.  I have since bought a new watch from another company, and it is 1000 times better.  I wish I would have picked the second watch for all the miles I ran this summer.
In two month no work.No got more battery and then i can't charged the batterry again, that is the reason a give two star

My daughter bought me this for my birthday. We're both avid runners and have been for years.  I spent hours finally getting it to record the distance "close" to an accurate reading.  I finally figured out that over-adjusting the calibration values would allow me to manipulate the result enough to "tweak" it to an accuracy level I could live with which was always at least .10 off a mile lower than it should be.  I prefered under recoding to over recording the run.  I also learned to live with knowing every 10 miles meant I ran at least 11 ;-(Then the software for loading the results stopped working.  I tried every suggestion but nothing worked.  I'm a computer professional so I'm sure the issue is either with the firmware or the USB connectors.  You can't update the firmware without the software working.  This is after only 2 months.Called Nike support for a refund and all they would offer me is another one.  I explained that I'm so unhappy that I just want a refund so I can buy a GPS watch instead but they don't offer refunds.  I called the store where it was bought and they have a no refund policy after 30 days.  I'm so dissatisfied that I'd rather not even bother with another even though it would be free.  Bought my daughter Garmin Forerunner 110 GPS-Enabled Unisex Sport Watch and she loves it.  Wish I could get a refund so I could buy one.
summary: Save yourself the trouble, aggravation, time and money

reviewText: I'm a casual jogger/runner: 5-20mi a week. I'm also a tech nerd, so I thought seeing my run data would help motivate me to run more often. This is the first run tracking device I've owned.The sportband itself is ok though possibly a little overpriced. You have to download and install a small software utility to allow the sportband to sync with the Nike website. I had some difficulty getting the software to work correctly the first 2-3 times I synced a run. Now it seems to be working ok. I simply plug the usb portion of the band into my laptop and it syncs: no problem.The Nike+ website is a little disappointing. I was hoping for more reporting features other than just length of run. I'd like to compare runs to other runs in graph form and put custom tags on runs based on the route I chose that day. The visualization of data is pretty week for anything other than total length/time of your run. Who knows, maybe Nike will improve the website in the future.The site will also post your runs to FB if that's your thing.Based on comments I've seen on various sites, there are probably cheaper, better, and more accurate solutions out there for tracking your run stats. That said, this is probably a decent starter solution for a casual runner like myself.

This product was never able to measure the distance of my run correctly. I calibrated it per manufacturer's instructions. It was consistently off by as much as 20 to 30% on the actual distance. Seem to be confused by change of incline in runs. Very disappointed in its performance.
I love this. I love that it keeps track of my run. Only downside is that not every Nike shoe is equipped to hold the sensor. Lucky that I love the pair that fits it!
I love this Sportsband! It tracks my miles! Does just what it said it would. Just plug in to USB on computer to download runs and charge Sportsband. Love it!

I love my Nike Sportband.  It is very comfortable which is extremely important for me.  My daughter encouraged me to make this purchase and I am truly enjoying tracking my running and walking.  It is a wonderful fitness tool.
It's a great watch wear it nearly everyday. I run with it all the time. We own 3 of them

This little unit works great and can be used as wrist watch if you want a cool looking Nike watch.  You basically just tell it to start when you're ready and to end at the end of your trip and when you're able to put it in your computer, just install it and see the info.  You can see your pace from start to finish and how long it took you.  A very cool little device, but I'm sure it has more things that I haven't figured out yet!

The Nike SportBand is a great companion for running.  I am a pretty small person; therefore, wearing a huge GPS watch tends to get in the way and looks pretty ridiculous.  This is a great option for when I want to go on a run and don't want something bulky on my wrist.  It does a fairly descent job of getting a correct accuracy on your runs once you calibrate it.  I found that I had to calibrate it every few months depending on how conditioned I was during that month since my stride seem to change.I have had this product for over a year and it has been great to take on trips with me instead of my GPS watch.  However, you have to understand that you will not get an exactly accurate measure of distance (at least I don't).  However, you should come pretty close.My only gripe about it is that sometimes it has software/hardware failure in which it does not upload your last run to the website.  There are some ways to fix this, but whenever I fixed it, it ended up deleting all of my runs on the watch and I was not able to upload them onto the website.  I was pretty frustrated because I had gotten back into training for a marathon and I lost several of my runs.  I came across this issue once but other people have commented that it has happened several times.I really enjoy the Nike+ website because it is very user friendly and has a lot of training options.  I wish it would be more customizable though but I will take it for now.
summary: Easy to use with some flaws

reviewText: I am a beginner runner and I wanted something that could track my time, pace and distance as I started running 5K's. I looked into the GPS watches and found them to be more money than I wanted to invest. While looking for watches in one of the stores I stumbled across this. For $60 it has all of the features that I wanted, and also the option to add on a heart rate monitor, which I plan to do in the near future. Once you calibrate it, it is pretty accurate - I ran a 4 mile race and it had me at 4.05 at the end. For my purposes, that is close enough! The watch and the website are easy and fun to use. I don't have Nike shoes but for a few dollars several companies make a pocket for the sensor that you can attach to your shoelaces. I couldn't be happier with this product.

i had to buy a new one of these because the clip it has is not too reliable. My first one got stuck at the bottom of a lake while i was swimming! But i liked it enoguh to buy another one. Another down side is that it has no light. The only thing i use it for is to tell time on runs or anywhere else.

I bought this product after getting frustrated with the iPod nike+ product. With the iPod nike+, my workouts would often disappear between the end of my workout and me loading it onto my computer. However, I have never had that problem with this SportBand! I also love that its much more convenient than the iPod feature, as I can simply strap it onto my wrist rather than wearing an arm band!
I have the Polarlink heart rate monitor and use it with the Nike+ sport band. It is great for monitoring your heart rate during a workout and it looks great too! Cleans easily as well.

I'm so glad I bought this.  It keeps me motivated to get out and run.  I especially like how Nike+ website reviews my past performance and gives me averages.  It also lets me set goals, which keep me from being too lazy.  Love it!
Please, I want to know why you have not yet shipped the item to me. I was hoping to get this stuff today.
simple runners watch.  calculates distance based of nike+.  upgraded to an iphone an my nike+ stopped working.  (needs the ipod)  this allowed me to keep using nike+

My Dad loves to run and his birthday was coming up, so I decided to buy this for him because he always asks me how long he was out running or tries to approximate his mileage. I figured this would be the perfect gift for him since I already bought him some Nike+ running shoes. I bought this and the Nike+ sensor because I didn't know that the Nike+ sensor was included with this purchase. Initially I felt like I wasted money but once I realized that you have to replace the sensor after it dies out I was put at ease because now he has an extra sensor just in case something happens to the current one. I also gifted him the Nike+ App from the App Store for about $1.99. Let me say that he LOVES this. He just went out running and he told me that now he feels good about his runs because he knows how long he's been out and how many miles he ran. He also loves the fact that he can upload his times and miles to the server. I would highly recommend this to anyone who loves to track their mileage and time while running or doing any type of distance work out. If my Dad loves it then you or whoever youre giving this to will love it too. Just remember that the Nike+ sensor is already included with this.
This product is a piece of garbage...  I mean that literally!  you can find mine in a landfill somewhere.  Get the fitbit one and leave this alone.

I purchase 2 of these. the 1st lasted a year. when that died, I purchased a 2nd one that lasted around 4 months. I loved the simplicity of the watch & found it very easy to use...but it's not worth the money if it doesn't last. I returned the 2nd one & receive a partial refund from Amazon. To me, it was not worth spending $118 over 16 months for the use of this watch.
summary: save your money, this is practically disposable

reviewText: This is a great device for estimating miles on the fly. I use the map my run app on my phone for more accurate mileage but it can be kind of a pain to pull out my phone to check how far i have run. Would have given it a five star if i didn't need require me to buy a pouch to use it without nike + shoes.Up dateThe device will not upload my workouts to my computer. I have tried to do a factory reset and i have tried re-downloading the software from nike.com. i am currently trying to contact nike to fix the problem but the hold time is to long and their call back feature which claims some one will call you back in about 5 minuets is now pushing 45 minuets.

I bought this because it is so easy to use, however the accuracy is terrible. When you go to the wesite it has a place to input actual miles run but does not fix the watch. I have ran 3 half marathons and 2 12k's and the mileage recorded has been short every time. Really messes up your training when you are trying to run a specific number of miles. Looks good though, and I just wear it as a watch, not a training tool.
I am unable to download the data from the watch as I have Windows 7 and it doesn't work!  Had some techie people try other options, but no luck.  So much for that!

I got this for my wife and it took a few times of calibration to get it to be fairly accurate.  We went on a 4-mile run - I wore my Garmin Forerunner and she wore her NikePlus watch and as soon as we finished the run, we both stopped our watches.  We used this to calibrate the watch and ever since then, her watch has been pretty accurate.  I like Nike's software too.  Easy to install, easy to find your way around but why can't I minimize the application window when the unit is plugged into my computer?  How annoying!  So if you're charging the unit, you'll see the Nike utility on your desktop the entire time with no way of getting rid of it until you disconnect the unit from the PC.  Just a small gripe.  I also bought her a shoe pouch for the foot pod since she wears ASICS.  Seems to work fine.
summary: Nice tool for running for a decent price

reviewText: GPS pace watches, move over!  I researched for a few weeks and was looking to by a big, bulky GPS/pace watch.  I'm really happy that I found this one.  Its light, fashionable and pretty darn accurate!  FYI when you get the watch it cycles through the different categories (time, pace, chrono, calories) but you CAN leave it set on any one of those while you run.  Which is great because I can look down and see how fast (or slow) I'm running in just a few seconds.  It lacks a light, but that can be remedied with a headlamp if you're running in low light conditions (which you should anyway for visibilities sake).  I'm very happy with this purchase.
went through two units.  both with display problems.  didn't last over two weeks.

I sent this item as a birthday gift to a good friend.  It arrived without any instructions and it did not work.  The birthday girl got online and looked up the instructions, but never could make it work.  Don't waste your time, spend the extra bucks and get Fitbit.
The sportband did not work when I received it in the mail. The band would not connect to my computer.

Nowhere in the description did it mention that this was a "Livestrong" branded item. They also only showed one pic of it, not the side that says it.  I'm sure this had everything to do with the Lance Armstrong scandal. Had I known, I wouldn't have purchased.

This sport band does exactly what it is supposed to do.  I love being able to track my minutes, miles, pace, etc.  As a beginning runner, it keeps me motivated.  You don't have to buy Nike shoes in order for this to work.  I put the shoe sensor in my sock at first.  I then ordered a little pocket by iArmbands to put the sensor in; it connects to a shoelace.  -This is a good product at a fair price.  I highly recommend it and never run without it now.
I love this Sportsband! It tracks my miles! Does just what it said it would. Just plug in to USB on computer to download runs and charge Sportsband. Love it!

I was very excited when I bought the sportband three months ago. Now, well, I'll put it in the garbage as it is too late to get my money back.The band is fine when you are a beginner. It is easy to use and very intuitive. However, it is not enough for more experienced runners and totally useless if you run at night, since there is no backlight.Also, the software that uploads the runs to the Nike+ website is also very poor. I cannot sync the runs and that was the dead end of this product to me. I don't know why, but Nike seems to hide its customer support numbers and emails. I tried to contact them via facebook, but have never got an answer back. But, if you don't bother with the Nike+ website, you should be fine with this.Pros:Easy to use, especially for beginners.Cons:The sync software doesn't work;You need to spend extra money to buy a special nike+ polar heart monitor, if you wish to check your heart rateNo backlight makes it totally useless for night runnersLack of customer supportBottom line: Spend a little bit more money and buy a decent monitor. Nike is great for sports shoes and clothes. Monitors, watches and other electronic gears are not their specialty, so, don't expect much out this type of Nike products.
summary: Not as good as I thought

reviewText: This isn't the most accurate running watch, but it's the best you can get without paying for a GPS watch. Calibrating helps, but you need a long run you know the exact length of.
I like this band a lot. It's comfy and doesn't dig into my wrist. The usb  port is really good too. For the money, this band is worth it. Oh, and yellow is my favorite color.

Bought this for my husband for Christmas, since he was just starting to run. I thought this would motivate him and make him more excited about it especially because he loves technology. I saw that you can link this up to your computer and create your own page on Nikeplus.com and track your progress. Well, now he is training for a full marathon!!! He absolutely loves this. The only initial issue is that I didn't know that you should have a Nike Plus shoe, so he had to go out and buy one, but now he is claiming that it's the best investment he has ever made. The only thing that he complains about is that the Nikeplus website is really out of date and seems to not function correctly all of the time. So if Nike could make sure that the website is always working properly, he would be much happier.Overall, I am really happy I bought this for him!

THIS IS THE COOLEST WATCH EVER!! i love that it counts calories, distance, and the time, it's everything that I need!this was a really good price too, and it shipped when it said it would. great quality, great satisfaction.

upon purchase, the interface with the software and website are terrible and utterly counter-intuitive. it will not connect with the mac software, allow me to sync my profile, and the sportsband won't sync with my iPhone - a major reason I bought it.

I bought it recently and so far I have been saying "where have you been all my life?"  It is light as a feather.  Easy to use and upload data.  You can calibrate your runs/walking.  It keeps me on track with my run distance/time.  You can scan for time/distance/calories/chrono/pace.  On the Nike+ website where you can keep track of all your progress, they have virtual coaches so when you upload ur runs/walks. There you can see your progress towards your goals, take on challenges, post to FB/Twitter, .  The overall experience is engaging, keeps one intersted, and most of all makes working out and achieving new heights fun.

Great product and second Nike+ SportBand I've owned, but this one for some reason won't maintain a charge and conveniently happened 14 days after the last day for a return/refund.  I'm starting to wonder if if might be better to buy again directly from Nike because a friend ordered the same product and ran into the same exact problem (won't maintain a charge).  Lesson learned for me and sharing so you can make your decision knowing some concerns others have.

I hated carrying my phone or bulky gps items with me while running.  With this watch I can throw it on and start running and I know exactly how far I've gone, how much time has passed, and how many calories burned.  It's so light and easy to throw in a gym bag.
summary: Quick easy way to see how far I've run!

reviewText: The initial setup of this device was quite cumbersome, but after you get through it, the product is very easy to use. Nike+ also seems to have quite a few quirks to get used to. Hopefully they will revamp the site soon.
summary: Works like you expect, hard initial setup

reviewText: I really love this little pedometer.  It keeps me on track, of a daily 6 miles. You can setup goals on the Nike running web page that your pc or mac will go to, when it is plugged into the USB. Part of it fits right into my Nike fittnes running shoes, but you can get a strap to use it with any shoe.
Didn't calibrate at any point when uploading onto the laptop and then broke after 3 days. (pixels malfunctioned)Was very disappointed to have to send it back faster than it took to deliver it...

Not as accurate as I'd like even after carefully calibrating it, but good enough for beginners. (It's often off by .01 per mile, which is fine at short distances but adds up on long runs.) Website is slow but again, good enough for someone looking for basic goals/recording. Watch is sensitive to humidity so I'm very careful to keep it out of the rain/sweat. Comfortable band, easy to read text, works just fine in a pocket on top of the laces rather than inside a special shoe. Instructions are easy to follow. Shows time, pace, miles, elapsed time, and calories burned. My favorite feature is being able to see my current pace.

I bought this to help me track my running. I was a brand new runner when I bought this. The calibration was terrible. It had be running 2.5miles when I was really only doing 1.6 (on a treadmill).After the second week of using this it stopped working. The band itself still turns on but it will not link to my computer anymore. Total waste of money!!!So, just to write about how crappy they are. I bought a new one from the store. Returned the broken one. That one is now broken too. My wife's is also broken. This is a chronic issue with these, read the reviews and DO NOT BUY!!!

I actually bought this sports ban for my sister. She just started running. So far it's been a great tool for her not only to disply mileage, time and colries burned, but the online community is great motivator too. My preference is Garmin, however for a beginner that doesn't want to spend a lot cash, this is a great option.
This sportband is fabulous. Comes in colors to match the shoes, doubles as a watch, very comfortable, easy to use... love the Nike + program! I hightly recommend this item!

I liked this watch at first.  It read my distance, I could easily link it to my nike+ sensor and upload it to the nike+ website.  Well a year later and it just stopped working.  Maybe that's why it was only $60.
summary: Stopped working in about a year

reviewText: Got this a month ago and I took two days at my local HS track to calibrate it.  I did two 2 mile runs and 2 1 mile walks.  I then tested it the next run at the track again-DEAD ON Accurate.  I was impressed.  I like its simplicity.  Some of these bands are getting too complicated.  Just hold the button down and run.  I also use it at Title Boxing with just the heart rate strap to count calories.  Works fine there too.  My only complaint is that is has no backlight, but I can live with out it.  The Nike web upload of your runs is really cool.  There is so much you can learn about your runs after uploading.  You have to buy the heart rate monitor separate but I liked this band so much I didn't mind getting it.  Just make sure you get the right one because Polar makes several different monitors for different bands.

Being in the military does not allow me to carry Ipods on runs so this is an amazing alternative that I am very happy about.  after calibrating it 3-4 times, it is incredibly accurate.  A must have for anyone who is unable to run with headphones.

Pros:- comfortable wrist band- small and lightweight- USB connector idea is pretty neatCons:- display is very hard to read: no backlight, digits are small, watch face is oriented 90 degrees from viewing angle- mileage tracking is grossly inaccurate (up to 30% off), even after calibration; appears to make the absurd assumption that you always run using the same length stride- if you want the watch to display elapsed time once you push the start button without having to push any other buttons, you will not be able to see the distance run until your run is over- cannot be used as a basic stopwatch because it must communicate with sensor on shoes- does not display seconds for runs lasting over an hour- recalibrated runs are not updated on web site to reflect actual distance- web site is so slow as to be unusable- clearly costs only a few dollars to manufacture = overpriced at $59- by the time you discover all of these cons, you will have used the watch so that it cannot be returned

Is it super accurate in calculating distance ran?  Could anything that works like this ever be?  It's accurate enough.  But that is not the most useful feature anyway. YOU CAN INSTANTLY SEE IF YOUR PACE IS DROPPING!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Are you a serious runner?  Do you want to hit your mark on a long distance run, especially an unmarked run? This is your coach riding next to you telling you to pick it up! When I head out on a run I already know how far I'm going and know what pace I want to run.  I use this device to keep me me on pace. I also like the auto-logging of my runs using the online features.  Finish your run plug it into your computer and get some instant gratification from it showing you how you hit your marks.  I use to write down what I did on a calendar. Now, WOW, look at a whole year of running on your computer screen!  Look at several years.  From a guy who's been a serious runner for over 40 years, it is wonderful.  Get a little pouch to hold the sensor in non-Nike+ shoes.  I usually wear a regular running watch to show my overall time and splits (if i'm on a marked course) and the sports band on my other wrist with the pace feature selected.  Con: It is hard or impossible to see at night (no back light) so depends on how many street lights on your route.

I left it in my laptop for about 6 hours and it quit working. i couldnt do a thing, even tried to reset it on my computer. VERY FRUSTRATING. it looked like a bunch of mumbo jumbo alien letters on my watch. I never got it wet, never dropped it, or anything. Just over charged it. After about 3.5 months the battery died and i was able to use it again. It lost all my stats and hard earned miles (which was the whole point of the dang thing). Now it appears to be working fine but you never know if it will malfunction again. I would recommend saving up for the GPS watch or something, i heard those are good.

My wife has tried two of these sport bands from Nike.  They don't work.  The site is always down and their facebook page is FULL of complaints from others with he same problem.  Great idea, lousy execution.
I bought 2 one for me and 1 for my wife It works great and it looks awsome, perfect for what I need and it is a good price!!!

I purchased this watch about two years ago and I loved using it. After calibration, the watch was very accurate and it was a great addition to my training. Nike recommends that you wear the watch with the face on the inside of your wrist so it is easy to check while running. I tried this and it was more convenient. However, this was a HUGE MISTAKE! The USB part of the watch is held on by a single snap, and a single flick of the wrist can cause the watch to come loose and fly off. This happened to me three times. The last time, it flew off somewhere on a trail and I was unable to find it. I contacted Nike and they told me they would not do anything, but recommended the $170 Nike SportWatch with GPS.I'm upset about this huge design flaw that doomed this awesome watch. Although it is a LOT cheaper than the other watches, it's probably worth the extra security. I'm out $60 and lost 3 weeks of training data. Overall, I'm disappointed in this watch.

This product has a lot of potential, but there are just sooo many flaws.  Do a google search, and you will realize that there are all sorts of bugs with the Nike+Connect/Nikerunning app AND website.  Not intuitive at all, and you are not able to easily customize, calibrate, and the instructions are awful.  Granted, a lot of this products flaws have to do with the Nike+Connect software, that I didnt realize until after I purchased it (you cannot enter a run manually?!?!?!)  I joined RunKeeper.com, and rather just use my phone which has a GPS.  Bulkier, not as comfy, but more accurate and the website and software dont make you want to pull your hair out.  Returned!
summary: Awful.  Amazed Nike would put out such a lousy product.

reviewText: For runners this is a great option to buying a GPS watch.  Accurate, hardly noticeable on the wrist and easy to manage and maintain.

I had to buy this product for a gym class. I wouldn't have bought it if I hadn't been required to, and now that the class is over I won't use it again.On the good side - it was accurate as far as distance goesOn the negative side - it is annoying to use, it is no more helpful than a $5 step counter, it doesn't count seconds after you reach an hour, if the button gets bumped at all it turns off in the middle of the workout (AND MESSES UP YOUR CLASS GRADE!!)

This Sportband is awesome!  I was a little afraid after reading all of the reviews stating that it was inaccurate at tracking distance, but I thought that it was worth a shot seeing that it was only $50 compared to the much more expensive GPS watches that are big and bulky.  I was pleasantly surprised!  It is small, cute, and stylish.  I bought the red plum/crimson.  Very girly and pretty.  The battery lasts a really long time, and because it is so cute, I find that I'm wearing it more often than not on a daily basis.  I have a definite mile loop that I do every day and it is always well within range of the actual distance.  only downfall, and the reason I gave it 4 stars, is because I found that the tracking works well when you're doing a steady pace; however, sprints is it's downfall.  It gets very off course and inaccurate when doing intervals or sprints.  But overall, very stylish, girly, useful as a daily sport watch, and accurate when doing laps or distance training.
summary: Great for paced runs/not so much sprints

reviewText: This watch worked OK for maybe 16-20 runs over a one-month period. Then when I pressed the button to start the timer, the timer didn't start. It would tease me by acting like it was going to engage, but it didn't. No/unreliable GPS function = why did I waste my money? In fairness to Nike, my problem may be from user error. If anyone has overcome this issue, I would appreciate it if you tell me how you did it.I am petite and my wrists are small. The Nike band didn't fit very well. You secure it by pressing two knobs into holes. It's a little tricky to do one-handed.The Nike screen is small and to see time, pace, etc. you need to press a button on the bottom to scroll through. I found this awkward to do while running. Its distance accuracy was consistently off by about a 1/2-mile despite calibrating it. I know this because I used it on a marked course. I also found Nike's free site to which you can upload workouts frustrating. Knowing the distance was wrong, I wanted to correct it online, but as far as I could tell, there is no way to adjust errors there.
Perfect watch for running, lightweight, easy to use and it seems to fit any size wrist! (I have small ones and it's perfect =) Great buy
Love it!!! It was acurate and the Nike site was easy to use. I look forward to continued use of the sportband and even bought my sister one.

Unfortunately I cannot give high praise YET on my new Nike+ SportBand.  It arrived dead as a door nail ... and would not charge in any USB port I tried.  Thanks to Amazon being so great, I used the Return feature and a new one will be shipped out a.s.a.p!So this is NOT a bad review on the product, but only this particular unit.  I will re-post once I try out a working model.

I have had my Nike + Sport Band for about 4 months now.  Until today it worked excellent.  I was no longer able to connect the device t my computer.  (Did not detect USB device).  I contacted Nike customer service.  They helped me try to trouble shoot the problem over the phone but with no success.  Since the product is still under warranty, Nike is shipping me a new sport band at no cost and I will be mailing them back the old one upon receipt.I have enjoyed running with this sport band.  The accuracy is only as good as your calibration.  As long as your pace is consistent with the pace you calibrated it at.  If you run faster than the pace you calibrated it will record a slightly shorter distance whereas if you run slower than your calibrated pace it will record a slightly longer distance that what you actually ran.  It will get you in the ballpark though.The biggest draw backs are the absence of a light to help with night runs and the fact that it is not water proof although it is water resistant.Good Job Nike and thank you for the wonderful customer support I received over the phone this morning.
summary: Good training tool and excellent customer support

reviewText: I've been running for 3 years and this is my second nike sportband.  I tried three other watches and they are toocomplicated.  This one is great for tracking your runs and watching your pace.

After struggling a little to get the software to connect (I tried it on 2 computers - one will not take it at all).... I finally got the SportsBand to upload information.  Then after 2 uses ... yes, 2 uses ... it no longer detects the product.  I have tried everything.  The same thing happened with the GPS Watch Nike sells.  Just skip Nike with these products.  Stick with Garmin.  This is a big waste of money.  More frustrating than it's worth.  UPDATE:  The Sportsband no longer charges.  This thing is awful.  I have probably used it half a dozen times.  It's garbage.

I love the watch in itself, the color, feel and display, but the GPS unit only worked the first time I used it and now the watch doesn't even register it at all! I don't live in an extremely remote location, so I expect the GPS signal to be picked up just fine... I was apprehensive about buying the SportBand after reading all the negative reviews, but in the end I went for it, figuring that the potential benefits of having a really useful and relatively inexpensive instrument outweighed the inconvenience of returning it should it prove to be a lemon or a dud. I've only had this for a day so I can't speak about its durability or longevity, but since I went through my own period of frustration in getting the watch to work, I thought I might share a few tips and save someone else a lot of hair pulling. After combing the interwebs to troubleshoot this thing, it's actually proven to be an amazing little device. What I really fault Nike for is not including and displaying this info in a conspicuous manner - say, in the instruction booklet or in the online FAQ, where people might actually see it and use it to solve the issue, rather than dreading the inevitable call to an ignoramus in customer service that will end up boosting your blood pressure and heart rate in all the wrong ways.So anyways, if your watch won't link up to the sensor here's what you can try:1. Wake up or restart the sensor. I understand many if not most of these units will be shipped with the sensor in sleep/standby mode. Push on the button once with a pen until it clicks to wake it up. To reset, hold the button for 3 seconds until it goes to sleep. Then push on the button again to wake it up.2. Reset the watch. Push and hold both the top & side buttons for 10 seconds until the screen reads "Nike." You'll have to plug it into your computer and use the Nike+ software to re-input your settings for weight, time, etc.3. Push and hold the SIDE button for 5 seconds. That makes the watch find the nearest sensor and link to it.I had to do all these things to resuscitate my SportBand which I thought was DOA but was in fact just a little groggy from prolonged hibernation. The other problem people - and by people I mean myself included - seem to be having is that the calibration is waaaay off. I went for a 1-mile run at a track to test its accuracy and the watch said 0.3 miles, and wouldn't even let me set the calibration in the software - WTF!? Well, turns out Nike has an expanded user manual in a PDF buried in their site somewhere, from which I culled this useful tidbit:1. THE SENSOR NEEDS TO BE ORIENTED WITH THE LOGO SIDE UP, SWOOSH POINTING TOWARDS THE HEEL. This seemed to do the trick, with the accuracy jumping from an execrable 30% to a whopping 90% - and it finally even let me fine-tune the calibration! Since I use a pouch that threads through the laces and wraps around a few times, this actually took some careful visualization.2. Apparently the sensor should be oriented as flat as possible on the shoe. I changed the location of my pouch from up by the tongue where it was nearly vertical, to down near the toe where it's more horizontal.3. This is probably just voodoo, but it may help the wireless transmission to have the sensor on the same side as the hand you're wearing the watch on. Left wrist, left shoe, and vice versa.Hope all this helps!

reviewText: I bought the Nike+ Sportband after I lost my old Nike+ sensor.  You can buy a sensor separate, but I wanted to try this product because I skip around a lot on my iPod and it can interfere with the Nike +.The display is a USB that plugs into the waterproof sportband and into your computer.  It displays as a watch until the sensor is activated and then it will display distance.  A button on the bottom can be pressed to switch to time or calories burned.  I find it difficult to detach the USB from the wristband, but this just means it won't come undone while I am running.  The band is also difficult to snap, especially if you have small wrists.The first thing you should do is to plug the USB into your computer.  You can log-in or create a Nike account and make sure it has your correct weight.  Then you will need to do a run to calibrate the sensor.  It should be at least a half mile.  I made the mistake of calibrating on a treadmill.  My next run's distance was way off what I knew it was.  If you read about calibration online, it will tell you that for accurate results, you should run outdoors in normal conditions at your regular pace.  The sensor detects your stride distance and this will ensure accuracy.The display can be difficult to read in the dark, but otherwise I really like running with the sportband.  I no longer have to run a route with set distances.  It's convenient to look down and see how far I have gone.  It can double as a sporty watch, the band is pretty cool and comfortable.

I had a difficult time finding one, either in store or on-line.  The price on Amazon was a little higher then I had seen other places, but Amazon was the only place I could find one in stock.
