I got this a few years ago with the hopes to log my miles. I am a college runner at the D1 level, so I log lots of miles. I purchased this in high school, where we would run 5-6 miles a day. This watch, after some frustration getting it synced, would stay on for only 2-3 miles, then turn off. When the battery dies, you lose any data that was logged. If you run 1 mile or less in perfect weather, buy it. If you run a more than 3-4 miles, in varying weather (i.e. extreme cold, extreme hot), avoid this like the plague and go buy yourself another pair of trainers or a nice pair of spikes instead. Don't expect to use this watch everyday running 9+ miles runs like I am now. My alternative-- use a stopwatch and take splits at places on loops where the mile splits are. Much easier than this piece of junk. Way for Nike to have such a short warranty. I will never buy anything other than shoes or apparel from them again.

I am satisfied with my product and would order another if the one I currently own were to get damaged or lost.I only have minor things that dissatisfy me and those are simply that the white band very quickly and easily becomes dirty and henceforth, unwashable. Secondly, if you are a morning runner like I am, this watch may not be useful to you because it contains no light to be able to read the numbers, and is not visible unless there is some sort of direct light. Lastly, I thought it would be easily accesible to read while running, but due to the fact that it is not readable unless your arm is bent in a weird position, since the face is sideways, it's arbitrary to read quickly and easily while working out. Overall though, I really like the fatures of this watch including the pull out USB detachable, the fashionable look (which I've gotten many compliments on) and the features of being able to check Pace, chronological time, calories, and distance. It has been very helpful and useful to me, and I enjoy wearing and using this product daily.

I loved my SportBand...until it inexplicably quit working just 6 months past warranty. I guess that's ok, since the item only cost me $59. I'm debating replacing it with another, since I really did enjoy the device. It's simple, lightweight, easy to pack, etc. It's a disappointment now that the display no longer works. I wrote Nike about it, and I will update the review if they opt to replace it for me or at least provide a discount.

Like most of these Nike+ et al products, this one is long on commecialization and short on actual usefulness. My Fitbit performs much better and has a more serious integration with health and fitness programs on the web. The Nike site seems more geared to Facebook and getting "likes" than fitness. It's a little annoying to set up and if I were to do this all over again, I would just buy the Fitbit device over this device for the same price.
summary: A little difficult to set up, but....

reviewText: I love my Nike sportband. I find it very accurate and a great motivator to keep exercising consistently - by tracking mileage and pace it keeps one pushing harder and going a little bit further. The feedback keeps me from skipping days as you get addicted to the progress charts on the Nike+ website. This is a great tool

I run about 40 miles a week and was looking for a less bulky item on my wrist than my 7 year old Garmin 201. I figured it would be nice to not worry about charging or leaving the Garmin turned on. I was hoping to simply walk out the front door and run without syncing with satellites. It was going to be back to low-tech running with the benefit of pretty sharp looking web site and details stats. The first two runs went fine but then I began to notice some real issues. You can't manually add runs with the Sportband. I know you can with the assistance of free app for the ipod but not the Sportband. Also you can calibrate runs but they don't update your stats they just prepare the device for the next run. As most runners, I like accurate stats not "kind of close" or completely missing runs. That was the final straw... when I ran a 14 miler and it didn't record. I also experienced the device simply stopping in the middle of a run and restarting near the end.So needless to say I'm back to my old Garmin happy again. I just wish I would accidentally step on it so I could move up to a 305 or 405. :)

I was not happy with this product at all. It worked fine when I ran on the street, but anytime that I tried it on a treadmill it was totally inaccurate. The first time I tried, I ran for about 45 minutes and when I checked the Nike plus at the end of the run it said I'd run less than half a mile! I couldn't pull that off if I had been crawling. I gave it a few more chances and had roughly the same outcome. I would not recommend this product.

Over-priced and doesn't correctly measure distance. I compared it to the runkeeper app I downloaded for free on my phone and was much more satisfied with that app. Save your money, get a wristband or armband for your phone and use that to measure distance for runs. Not worth the almost 60.00 I paid for it.

I purchased the Nike Plus SportBand (Black/Cool Grey/Silver) and received it today. I charged it up, installed the sensor in my shoelace pouch and went for a walk.(I had previously downloaded the software on Monday and installed it.)My first walk was a mile but only registered .32 mile. My next walk was 2 miles and only registered .67 mile. I can't walk far enough to get to the calibration screen.I have done the factory reset between walks, and re-registered with a different screen name.Between all the walks and screen names, I have been over 4 miles with the longest only registering .67 mile.Bluntly, if I can't get Nike to replace this unit, its going back. I don't trust this particular SportBand, but I'm willing to give another one a chance.How-ever, I am not going to wait 6 months to see what happens. As it stands now, recommending the Nike SportBand is out of the question.Update: I just got off the phone with Nike. They seem to be nice people, so I am willing to give them another chance. Tomorrow, I am going to take a 2 mile walk and see if we can calibrate this sucker.I'll let everyone know how it goes.I just got off the phone with Nike again. THIS particular guy seemed to think that all I had to do was to move the sensor forward towards my toes and everything would be fine.To be completely blunt, Nike's warranty is worthless. Nike's customer service is worthless. I will be returning this ASAP.
summary: Very Pretty but highly inaccurate product and worthless customer service.

reviewText: I love this product & how it links all run information to [...]  I am a beginning runner & it records all of the information that I need.  It is easy to use and set up. I was not too upset, because I had worn it for at least 2 years about 5 days a week, in rain, snow everything!  I am a regular runner but not a techie.  This has been perfect for me. I will try to be more careful to pull this one apart and let it dry out when wet, etc.  Not sure if that will make a difference but it might make it last a little longer.

Two years ago when I was training for Chicago's Half Marathon, I brought a Nike+ Sportband to help keep me motivate and it worked!Back then, I didn't run to music, but loved the idea of being able to track my miles, pace, times and calories simply and easily.  Plus, the Nike+ website with my "mini" cheering me on the more I ran was too cute!The sportband works perfectly. It's easy to sync both to the sensor and to the website. ORIGINAL ORDER DATE: November 8, 2011This is a beautifully made watch.  The Picture doesn't do it justice.  The sub dials are bright silver with concentric rings that contrast much more than the picture shows.May have been an earlier prototype picture?It is a Japanese quartz chronograph , which is different from a swiss layout.The main sweep hand is watch seconds  and the small subdial is chrono secounds.There is no 1/10th of a second dial, instead a 24hr indicator dial, which is an equivilent of AM/PM.The Chrono indicates just seconds and minutes up to 30 min. and then stops.  It does NOT run contiuously.It is a large watch at 50 mm, but not grossly oversize.The band is a very nicely finished custom band, designed specifically for this watch.It is adjustable with a very nice Gold deployment clasp.  But: CAUTION! you have to cut it to fit it. And you only get one shot at it,  if you cut too small (SHORT) the story is over.  You'll have to get a new band to try again. a real pain.  The clasp alone is worth $35.A real bargin at $150.  If you think you might like it, give it a look.  You have 30 days to say No w/Amazon, no questions asked.  I always buy from Amazon if I can.BTW:  Very nice gift box too!  I have had great luck C-H Paris, I'm glad they are branching out into watches, instead of just Pocket Watches.  I think they'll do well, esp. at this $/value ratio.EDIT:  After almost two months this watch is still in lock step with an atomic clock.  It's a Japanese Movement of unknown caliber, but whatever it is, it's a good one.  1/7/2012Edit 2:  Just updateded to DST and this watch just won't quit! 3/13/2012

This is my first pair of Native sunglasses and I think they are well made and worth the price. I want to first comment on the weight of the frame. They are very light, although not the lightest I have worn.  I am not sure why that is considered negative by other reviewers as these sunglasses were designed for physical activity, where you want a very light frame.  Additionally, that is why the lens are made from a carbonate rather than heavier glass. However, I do agree these are designed for smaller faces. They fit perfectly on me and I definitely do not have a medium to large face.  The build quality was great. They are flexible but spring right back into place for me.  To the reviewer who had an issue with the frame being crooked, it seems like a defect in your glasses. I would guess that would be covered by the warranty though.One of the biggest strengths of the sunglasses is the little details they have thought through. The nose piece is flexible enough that the sunglasses fit comfortably and stay on (I have a weird nose and usually this is an issue for me), the sunglasses venting works well, and the rubber on the earpiece helps the sunglasses stay on without being an uncomfortable tight fit.My one complaint about these sunglasses is that they do not sell a photochromatic interchangeable lens on their website, which for trial runs or hikes can really come in handy going through more shady to bright areas without taking off the sunglasses.Summary: For getting several polarized lens, good optical quality, and a light, sturdy frame, similar sunglasses would cost and extra 30-60 bucks easily. Buyers looking for a good pair of sport sunglasses should definitely consider these.

reviewText: These are my first Natives, and I had seen the brand sold in REI for some time, so thought I'd give them a try. Plus, the price I paid here on Amazon was fantastic, too hard to resist really. Anyway, I love the polarized lens, very clear vision and protect my eyes very well. I love the fact that another pair of lens and a hardcase came w/glasses.My take on these is that they are a solid pair of sunglasses, overall. Construction is rather light, feels somewhat "cheap", but maybe b/c they weigh so little. Also, the frame has a tendency to lay crooked on my face, probably due to the interchangable lens design. I fix that by simply bending down on one side, but it is annoying to do everytime I put them on. I've studied the construction and it looks well made, but have to wonder how long these will hold up over time.....I really like the silicon on the nose bridge and earlobes, never worry about them falling off my face, even when sweating! I would agree w/the other reviewer who says these are made for smaller faces, they are. I have smaller facial features and always buy glasses that are more proportionate, so found these to fit me very nicely. I could see how a person w/a med. or large face would not like these, but smaller faces a very nice fit.To conclude, I'd gave these 4 stars b/c of price and design. Because of the frame, I cannot give 5 stars, maybe these will prove me wrong over time, but the bending does have me wondering. I'd be willing to buy more Native eyewear in the future, but will probably stay away from this particular "interchangable" design.

I waited almost one year to write this review since I feel it is necessary to really get to know a product before I give an opinion. Out of the box this watch was just OK. Yes it is plastic and to me that is not a problem but it has a black rubber wrist strap and that was the first thing I replaced. I recommend the Luminox Evo velcro strap as it fits perfect on this watch and is way more comfortable for everyday wear. I found the rubber strap to be hot and sweaty especially when I was out on the boat in the sun.For daily wear you will almost forget you are wearing it because it is so light. At least if you follow my advice and loose the rubber strap. The illuminated dial and hands are great for night time viewing. The watch also keeps excellent time. In almost one year it has failed to loose one minute! I can not say the same thing for my 3K cost Tag Heuer. The only issue I ever had with it was that I dropped it from the kitchen counter on the hardwood floor and the second hand jumped one second requiring the watch to be taken apart and the hand reset. I also have to say the crystal has held up very well to daily use. I have one very small scratch near the outside of the crystal that you have to look very hard to see.I would not hesitate to recommend this watch to anyone looking for a durable accurate inexpensive timepiece.
summary: Been a good watch for the money

ORIGINAL REVIEW: I've ordered this and am waiting for shipment to arrive.  But just FYI -- This CORSAIR MODEL NUMBER SHOWN is for "DUAL CHANNEL" MEMORY - not QUAD CHANNEL memory. TheCorsair Model Number for the dual channel memory is as shown in the title - it has a letter A in the model # . . CMZ-16GX3M4"A"1600C9.  The Corsair Model Number for the "quad channel" memory has an X (not an A) in the model number. The title of this listing sounds like they're advertising "quad channel" memory. This model # isn't quad channel.  It's FOUR RAM DIMMS of DUAL CHANNEL MEMORY -- not the same as single vs dual vs quad channel memory -- which is totally different. I've requested Amazon review and change the title if appropriate to their needs for accuracy.UPDATE Jan 2012Well -- I see that Amazon did change the title of this listing. Good. DUAL CHANNEL MEMORY - FOUR DIMMS - 4GB ea!  Now, to report on the use of this memory now that it's been installed for 1.5 months. NO space interference at all.The height of the heat spreaders on this Vengeance series RAM are NOT a problem at all with my CPU Cooler.  Zero overlap on the RAM with plenty of room to spare to help keep DIMMS and board cool. In a HAF X, plenty of good air flow. I've read, however, that the spreaders on the RAM can be a problem with other larger types of aftermarket CPU heat sink fans. So, give consideration to this if you're also choosing one of the larger heat sinks that overlaps the RAM slots.  Just FYI -- with the H80 my CPU is still on 13 degrees C in a 67F room and Motherboard is staying around 20C.  So NO complaints here.  Very pleased with how this RAM works with all components of the board, CPU, cooler, etc.ABOUT BIOS: When you install this 1600 RAM on the Asus Z68 boards, it will install at 1300 speed.  This is a function of Intel Chipset, but you can set your RAM to 1600 if you want in the Asus BIOS or using the ASUS utilities.  Also if you want to use the XMP profile, remember to enable the XMP setting to enabled as well in BIOS. Ability to change settings in BIOS will depend on which board & CPU you buy.

I've had my Casio G-shock G7900MS-1B black watch with blue trim for about a week now, and I'm absolutely delighted with it.  It keeps great time, it's comfortable on my wrist, the rich blue trim against the black surfaces is appealing yet masculine, and there are so many fun features on the thing that it's more like a wrist toy than simply a wristwatch.One of the coolest and most useful features is called "auto-electro-luminescence" or "Auto-E.L." for short.  With this feature, you can set the watch so that the back-lighting lights up whenever you raise your wrist up toward your eye to check the time.  The screen stays lit up for 5 seconds.  This feature is extremely useful if, say, you've got one hand on your telephone and want to check the time of the phone call, without putting the phone down to push the little back-light "on" button with your other hand.  You turn the auto-EL on or off with the push of one button.  Furthermore, the auto-EL turns off automatically after six hours, to conserve battery life.  This is really useful if, say, you turn the auto-EL on at bedtime, because it will automatically turn off approximately when day breaks the next morning.  As you can see from reading my review, I'm delighted with this feature.There are lots of other cool features as well: you can set the watch to beep each hour, or not.  With the "timer" function, you can count off a period of time (say, 15 minutes of break time from a conference), and the watch will beep when the 15 minutes have elapsed.  You can also set the timer function to automatically repeat over and over again - say, when you want your child to begin her homework after a 10 minute break, and she begs for another 10 minutes and you give in, over and over again.The phases of the moon function is pure, meaningless folly, but fun.  Yes, I have found that it accurately displays the correct phase of the moon, but who really needs this information??? If you're in a profession that really needs this information, say -- an astronaut on a flight to the moon --- I suspect that you're going to have other, more sophisticated sources of determining the phase of the moon and it won't be left up to you and your Casio.  But, it's fun nonetheless.  And the tides?  who really cares?  What are you going to do - walk into a room and announce, "it's 8:30 am, and by the way, it's Neap Tide in the Chesapeake Bay ..."  But again, harmless fun.The watch has an easy toggle between 12/24 hour time display, a feature I find useful as an emergency services worker.  Date and day of the week are also prominently displayed in the main display.  The face of the watch is quite legible -- I find many watch faces annoying these days because all the secondary features tend to get in the way of simply telling the time, but this Casio model avoids that annoying pitfall.The buttons are easy to use and watch appears very well-made.  And it's inexpensive enough so I don't have to fret over getting it scratched, worn, or roughed-up.  I've worn it in business settings and while exercising with equal comfort and confidence.  I'm not a computer expert, but with the help of the manual and about 30 minutes of studying it in a quiet place away from children and other distractions, I was able to master all of its many features (stopwatches, timer, alarms, auto-EL, "world time", etc.).I have to sit through a lot of meetings, conferences, etc., and they are somtimes overlong and boring and I have a bit of ADHD, so my Casio is a lovely little, innocuous distraction during these eternal meetings. My children think the watch is cool, too.If there is any negative at all, it is simply that the watch is rather large.  Even though it's very light-weight, you will still notice it at times on your wrist due to the size, and it will catch on things when, for example, reaching into the back of a crowded regrigerator to get something at the back.I would heartily recommend this fun, attractive, quality, multi-function watch to anyone and everyone.
summary: A really cool, useful, attractive, huge wristwatch.

I'd like to start by saying I absolutely love 51 - 30's I own 3 myself and I plan to soon buy another. Although I have to say that this 51-30 design in particular is seriously flawed and it’s no coincidence this model cost much less than the others.The problem is the outer bezel and casing, you see in order for the watch to have that rough rock’ish texture they apply a thin layer of a sand’ish metal compound to the watch and then just polish over it. Kind of like a sticker, over time as the watch bumps and nicks things this layer will start to peel off leaving behind streaks of smooth stainless steel. If the stainless steel and the polished compound was the same color this issue would be hardly noticeable but since the stainless steel is slightly darker, as the compound starts to peel it leaves the watch looking seriously damaged and discolored. Over time the peeling becomes more frequent and rapid as bigger sections of the stainless steel are exposed.As a result of these issues I believe Nixon stopped producing this model. When I owned this model I attempted to get the bezel and case replaced under factory warranty and they told me they were unable to replace the parts but were willing to allow me to exchange the watch for a new model. Just something to keep in mind before purchasing.And in case you’re doubting my review due to the other 5 star reviews. I will say the peeling issue didn’t start until I had owned the watch for around 8months.
summary: After 8 months, the bezel and casing finish starts to peel leaving the watch discolored

reviewText: Arrived on time and as expected. It was easy to set up, did not even have to look at the instructions. The band is very soft, I am happy, because some bands tend to be scratchy. Large numbers, easy to see.Thank you Amazon!

This watch claims to be water-resistant, however it performs poorly even when it is near water or in a high-humidity environment.  I have had non water-resistant watches that have lasted longer exposed to water than this one did.  After only 3 weeks of use, it completely died.  Every time I gave my children a bath, washed my hands, or walked on the beach (not even submerging the watch in water) the numbers would fade away and would eventually come back after about 24 hours.  However, after several times of this occuring the watch finally gave out and will no longer work.  I contacted Timex about repairing it under warranty and I have to send them the watch and pay $8 for shipping and handling.  I think this is poor customer service on Timex's part and will not be purchasing another "water-resistant" Timex watch in the future.  It is a beautiful watch and I was very happy with it's appearance, just extremely disappointed in it's performance.
summary: Not recommended if you will use the watch anywhere near water

reviewText: I love this watch. The face is easy to read with large numbers but in a nice size oval that is not overlarge. It is sleek and attractive. The silicone strap is marvelous. I was afraid a white band would pick up dirt but mine has remained white as snow throughout all my work in nursing (I do wear it in the shower each night). It keeps time wonderfully and the ring that keeps the band in place actually holds it in place unlike most of my other watches that I constantly have to tuck in all the time because the end slips out. I'm putting in an order for another one! I do wish it came in some other colors.

Classic Timex with a Sleek and Sporty Look . . . Easy to read face with time, day of week, month and day. Also seconds. Indiglo light. Comfortable band. Reasonable size for a sports watch - not too big or too small for a women's wrist. Sporty but stylish enough to be worn with casual wear and can get away with wearing for office or dinner. Not bad looking for a digital watch. Since it has a white band, may be suitable for those in the healthcare profession. Overall a very good value. I may end up purchasing the version with the black band as well.

reviewText: I used to buy a new Timex Ironman RESIN-strap watch every year, not because the clock mechanism stopped working, but because the resin strap would stain, crack and/or break, and the "metallic" finish on the face of the watch would wear off and I'd end up with a sadly worn, ugly but still functional watch.  So I tried the black version of this SILICONE strap watch, and LOVED IT!  The silicone band is soft and comfortable, and did not stain.  Also, the face is rimmed with real metal, not just a painted metallic finish.  Unfortunately, after six months, some of the buttons stopped working and the watch was no longer functional.  So I took a chance and bought the same watch again, this time with the white silicone strap.  I love the white strap - it looks sharp & crisp, it's super-comfortable, and it DOES NOT STAIN.  Unfortunately, four months later, the start/split button is starting to malfunction.  I have to press very hard to get it to work.  What happened to Timex quality?  Maybe I got lemons both times but it's discouraging.
summary: Great-looking watch, but Timex quality is going downhill.

reviewText: Definitely the watch for me - 1 week of ocean, pool, and bath/showers - I didn't take it off the whole time I was on vacation and it worked perfectly!!  I now wear it every time I'm going into the pool and it has never failed.  It's definitely a Timex . . . takes a licking and keep on ticking! Love the interval and alarm features for my running time, too!
This watch is stylish and functional.  It's been put through it's paces and has withstood water, sweat, and lotion without ant issues.
Looks great, functions well, but water resistance is terrible.  First time wearing in a pool and it got condensation inside.  A few more dips and simply stopped working.

I bought this not having seen it in the shops but having seen similar.  It was a great price so I ordered it from Sydney Australia on a Monday and had it delivered to my door from the US by Thursday of the same week!The watch itself is very easy to use and stylish.I would highly recommend it.
I wanted a watch that I could wear at work, when coaching, and for tracking my own runs. This fits the bill perfectly. No complaints.

My husband got sick of seeing me around with my old Timex Ironman, so I got this one as a replacement. The old one was 4 years old and indestructible, but it looked a bit ratty.The new watch is missing the "hide" function, which is a shame. I really liked the ability to hide menus I don't need/want, which is really all of the menus except the timer... Now I'm obligated to click through all the options to get to timer. Sad.The watch is pretty. I must admit it is a good looking watch. The metal layer looks good, but it's definitely some kind of metallic paint on top of plastic. I am not a decent watch protector, so I've had my watch for... eh... 3 months? and the metal rim is already starting to wear off. I've also already managed to scrap the poor watch in multiple places.The white silicone strap, however, is amazing. I envisioned a slightly see-through watch band, so I felt some disappointment when I first saw this watch, but now I'm completely over the watchband disappointment. This white watchband stays white even though you probably guessed I am clumsy and I am not careful with my watches. I've accidentally swiped it with pens already and it somehow is staying white. I'm tempted to test some clothing dye on it as I dye yarn/fiber, but I'm afraid to find out in a dye vs watchband battle, dye will win.In any case, so far, so good.
quick ship and excellent product!  so excited! packaged in it's own box with instructions...brand new and LOVE the style!  thank you!  highly recommended!

I have had various Timex watches over the years, so I've stuck with the brand (although I had a poor experience with one of their cheaper watches).  This watch is a really nice looking watch.  I even wear it to work when I'm in casual dress.  I purchased the While Silicone strap watch.  The only thing that I don't like about the watch is the band where you try to tuck the remaining band through the clip.  The little clip (don't know the right word to use) has a notch to help grip, but, the band seems to come out frequently.  I wear my watch to bed, and often I have awaken and the watch has come off during my sleep.  A couple of times, it has nearly come off during the day as well, but usually it will "loosen" before it just falls off completely - so I haven't lost it.  I did not take off a star for the band - its a little bothersome, but, I just deal with it.  Due to my limited activity lately, I have not really used all of the functionality such as a timer.  Its a nice watch - I would recommend it or even give it as a gift.
summary: Nice looking, has held up, the band is "ok"

I keep my ID there for use at bars or anywhere else my ID gets checked.The only drawback is that it is what it is; you're not going to look like a high-roller with a nylon and velcro wallet.  I removed the velcro to keep from drawing attention to myself when I open the wallet but it still looks like the wallet I owned when I was eight years old.Ultimately, this is one of the most practical things I own and if you're looking for a really simple wallet that is durable and well-made, buy this now.

The band is also comfortable and flexible (I found the Suunto band uncomfortable). I recommend this watch.

I bought this watch on sale at a department store and thought I got a deal...until I searched Amazon and found it cheaper here by about $5. Anyway, the altimeter is within 100 feet out of the box. In Michigan, it reads 600 ft to 800 ft on my one hour commute from home to work. I looked up the elevation of the two cities and this is within 100 ft.I am at the beach in Florida as I write this and it reads - 40 feet at actual sea level. This is accurate enough for me. Through the mountains on the way here, it varied from 200 feet to 1800 feet. I bought it to take with me on my trip to Machu Picchu.The barometer is also accurate, once calibrated, and changes in pressure can be used to predict changes in weather. In the US, in range of a network, you can get ten day forecasts hour to hour on your smart phone, but out in the "bush" it may help. I like having the world tie function and the stopwatch and countdown timers. I have used the alarm mode also and find it loud enough to wake me up, barely.The thermometer is a bit of a disappointment as you have to take the watch off and let it sit for quite a while to get the temp. This will let me know the temp when I wake up camping, if I took it off at night, but on the move, it reads your skin temp. I wonder why they don't put the temp sensor on the top of the watch far from your skin? It does tell me the water temp when I swim and has fairly good accuracy in water. I was in a hot tub and it read 106 degrees.Overall, for about $50, this is a great watch. I did not buy the Pathfinder types starting at about $140 here as they are too big. This watch is plenty big, but it is very light and does not bother me on my wrist. Those Pathfinder models look huge in the customer pictures and seem better for men with really big arms/wrists. I am 6'4" and weigh about 190, so I am on the thin side. Being a triathlete and swimmer, I need a watch I can wear in the pool, while running, and on my bike, so it can't be some big clunky thing.

I accept the fact that an inexpensive watch can't be expected to provide accurate barometric pressure or altimeter readings and I know accurate temp readings must be off the wrist for a few minutes. But the lack of quality control is immediately obvious because of the misaligned analog hands and the alignment is not resolved by following the instruction manual.Such is the nature of mass-produced consumer level products made in third world countries. I got what I paid for. I still plan to buy a higher quality Casio multifunction watch (near $200) that doesn't have analog hands that won't detract from it's beauty and functionality. reviewText: This is my first Casio watch in 20 years. I've had this watch for a month now. I fly airplanes for a living and got this watch for all my hiking and cycling that I do when on the ground. I've found it to be extremely accurate. I am able to calibrate the barometer, thermometer, and altimeter each time before a flight according to airport ATIS. Alternatively, I've used readings from Weather Underground to calibrate it as well. I use a GPS unit to calibrate the altitude or use airfield elevation as a reference.Once calibrated, the readings are nothing short of phenomenal. When in the cockpit, the altimeter reads exactly what the cabin altitude is to an accuracy of +/-100 feet. (Cabin alt readings are in 100ft scale anyway on flight deck displays). Temperature readings are accurate if you leave it off your wrist for a few minutes (as the manual suggests). The altimeter reads accurately outdoors to within 10ft (cross-checked with a GPS unit) and the barometer is accurate as well - reading 1030hPa when the ATIS reported 1031. Quite remarkable.All this accuracy boils down to one thing - proper calibration.Build-wise, the watch is super light. It's easy to forget you're wearing a watch. It's constructed of resin and plastic and so should not take knocks and bumps as well as a tough solar. But hey, for the price, it can't be beat. And yes, it tells the time and displays two timezones, has multiple alarms and tells you the date and day. (Whew) I'm a happy guy.

reviewText: This is a fun watch.  I've owned lots of Casio watches and they are all incredibly durable. The altimeter was a bit off (10m / 30ft) however I've recalibrated it recently at sea level and now the reading is very accurate. The barometer seems to work very well and it shows if the weather is getting better or worse - very handy info when hiking. The alarm function is great with a total of 5 different alarms. I've also use it under water (7m / 20ft) and it worked very well - you just need to remember to rinse it in fresh water after diving in the ocean or pool. All in all a very nice sports watch at a very good price.

My main complain I have is that the thermometer is easily affected by your body heat, which always read 90.f when I wear it on my skin. Of course that's different if you are wearing it on your jacket, you'll get an objective temperature reading.

The watch time, when set to the official U.S. time clock (for me, its [...]) loses around five seconds per month  The altimeter, when calibrated on a day I want to use it, is within 20 Meters of another standard when I travel, and subsequently head to the hills, or head down to sea level. reviewText: Got my safety cat today. It's a tad smaller than I expected it to be, but fits nicely in the hand--any bigger and it would probably be too unwieldly. What's more, it's heavy for its size; this is a sturdy little gadget. I don't think it will ever break.I'm honestly not sure how effective this would be in a fight. It likely depends on the person using it. The main advantage of the safety cat, I think (other than discretion--who would ever guess this is a weapon?) is that you won't forget you have it on you. If, say, I carried a knife in my bag/pocket (I don't), I don't think I would have the presence of mind to dig it out in the event that I needed it. The safety cat goes on your keyring, and you carry your keys, so you constantly see it and it's constantly ready for action. All you have to do is get your fingers through the holes and PUNCH!There is no doubt in my mind that it would hurt like hell to get hit with this thing. The points on the ears aren't sharp (so you won't accidentally nick yourself) but they *might* be able to break skin with enough force behind them. Also, the description says that the ears have been strategically distanced so that they can effectively hit the eyes. I'm not sure I would have the heart to purposely get somebody in the eyes with this, even a mugger. Plus, I'm afraid I might get sued if I permanently blind somebody. (Although they won't have gotten a very good look at me, amirite?) I'm not sure of the legal status of this thing in my area, but who cares? Like I said, no one would ever guess this is a weapon. I guess I'll just have to wait to find out what the law says until after I nail somebody with it.All in all, I didn't buy this because I was looking for a serious defense weapon. I just saw it and thought, "Wow, that's really cool! Wow, only five dollars! *BUY*" So, shame on me. It's a great conversation piece at the very least; all my friends LOVED it and want one now. But who knows? One day it might end up saving my life. If I were a sensible girl, I might say something along the lines of, "Gee, I hope I don't ever get the chance to test this!" But in complete honesty... I do. I do, indeed. I look forward to it.

I ordered three of them. And it makes it less noisy. I prefer it that way, but it's an easy and cheap fix.Picture here:[...]Really sturdy without being beefy, so not a big deal to pack in a pocket and pretty stealthy in a purse. You're not pulling a gun out, it doesn't look like a huge weapon that will intimidate people and make you look like a freak on a killing spree.The holes: you can fit your fingers deep in them and get full control over the cat's head, good grip with the jaws relying on the back of your palm.The ears: as I said in the title, it looks REALLY effective. I haven't had the "chance" (fine by me though) to use it, but when you'll unpack it, you'll feel that you have the power to cause huge damages at the tip of your fist so be sure of what you do and just use it to get out of a bad situation. THIS IS NOT A TOY.Really, take time to gauge the situation if you feel the will to use it: the ears are spiky, solid. Just a quick blow to the belly would already be enough to cause pain to the ribs or chest, so watch out if you aim for the face or the skull.You don't need to be a professional fighter: any hit landed will be successful and should help neutralize the threat.It is lightweight, but the construction in a metal bridge structure fashion makes it really solid, rigid: impossible to twist it or whatever. I guess you could break one of the ears by hitting the pavement really hard if it's not straight perpendicular. But your knuckles would die in the meantime.The finish: good, soft, no burrs, nice anodisation, nice keyring, large enough to have like 5 keys on it, but not too big so your keys don't need to have abnormal dimensioned holes.This teal is really light, it makes the thing look funny. I offered it to a friend tonight. Some people were around but no one realized that it could be used to fight, so I guess that's just perfect.Looking for a low profile weapon not to attack anyone but just to feel better knowing you have a backup plan for the subway at night, walking to your home alone, something really stealthy and realiable? reviewText: I have owned this watch for just under a year now.  Within the first two weeks of wearing it, the crystal face started accumulating scratches, which is something I have never had a problem with on any other watch--Casio, Timex, Fossil, and Tag Heuer.  In addition, the band, which is black stainless steel, has also faded and is riddled with scratched.  At $380, I certainly wasn't expecting the quality of a Tag, but with all of the advertising hype around this watch being a "Navy Seal" watch, I expected a reasonable amount of ruggedness which this watch completely lacks.  Recently, on a day when I was indoors and not doing anything Seal-like, the face cracked.  I called the authorized Luminox repair center in Rhode Island, explained my dissatisfaction and was told that the problem wouldn't be covered by warranty and that I would have to pay approximately $70 to have a new face put on.  The repair center is a third party repair center, so there was no point in arguing or getting mad at the lady who told me that it was a corporate policy of Luminox not to cover cracked glass--convenient way for Luminox to hide from dissatisfied customers.  I now have to fork over the $70 to salvage my $380 investment, but once I get it back, it will be used strictly as a dress watch.  Also, when I called the repair center and inquired about upgrading to a sapphire crystal instead of the mineral crystal (which Luminox acknowleges in the manual is soft and subject to marring) I was told that one was not available for my style of watch.  The fact that they even put a scratch-prone face on their watches when they have another option available for what appears to be approxinately $25 more speaks volumes about the company and their products.  Long story short, I am very disappointed in this watch.  Luminox makes a cheap product and, not suprisingly, doesn't stand behind it.  This will be the last Luminox watch I ever own.  If you are in the market for a rugged watch--beware.  Spring for a Tag Heuer if it won't break the budget, or if it does, Casio G-Shock's are a much better option--I have had one since 1990 and it is still running on the same battery!!

reviewText: I just received my new Luminox 3152 BO. I wanted to write an in depth review because I was not able to find such anywhere on the Internet.  Please keep in mind I have only owned this watch for a few hours. So actual reliability is something I will not touch on.This is my first Luminox watch.  But the watch had several features that intrigued me.First the watch is called a "Black Out" watch. The face of the watch is black. The Arabic numbers on the watch are also black.  This makes it hard to see the numbers under normal light conditions.  However they do have what Luminox calls "Night Vision Tubes" at each 5 minute increment. The "Night Vision Tubes" are also on the hour, minute and second hand.  During normal lighting situations, these "Night Vision Tubes appear to be white in color. In low light situations, the hour, minute, second hand and numbers 1 - 11 appear to be blue in color. The 12:00 position appears orange in color. (This helps orientate the watch in low light situations)These night vision tubes are not very bright and appear no brighter than a typical watch with illuminating hands. (The type you stick under a lamp to charge) But apparently you do not need to stick the Luminox under a light. Luminox states these Night Vision Tubes are supposed to be good for 25 years.The day calendar is at the 3:00 position and numerals are also in white.The case is made of stainless steel as well as the band. Both are black and the watch feels substantial in weight.  I am a fairly large guy and was worried that the watch band may not fit.  The watch came with all the links set at the longest position and it did just fit.The bezel rotates in one direction only. This is so if you bump the bezel,....it will show that you have less time left on your dive VS bumping and  thinking you have plenty of time left. (Seems pointless as I do not know anyone whom does not use a dive computer anymore.)The crown was the area of my concern. Once unscrewed it just did not feel well built. It felt like a decent pull and it would fall apart.  However, once the time and date are set, and the crown was screwed back down, the crown did feel secure.Setting the date and time was very basic. However my watch seemed to have a hiccup. I pulled the stem to the first stop and set the date to the day before actual date. I then pulled the stem out all the way. I had to pass the 12:00 position three times to get the date to change to the current date. (Should only have had to go past 12:00 two times at most.) I have purchased Citizen watches for the past 3 decades. The overall mechanics of this watch do not seem to have the quality of a similar Citizen watch.I suspect that the back of the watch may be the reason that this watch sells well.On the back of the watch case is engraved the navy seal trident.  This might give the "cool" mind set to the watch. And the watch might have been given away at some ceremony to some Seals. Or it might make a decent duty watch. But with no bezel cover and the "night vision tubes" glowing, (Though not much of a glow) I would expect this watch would not be used in the field.Overall this might be a cool watch. But  I paid almost $400.00 for this watch. With the mechanics of this watch feeling rather like a $100.00 watch, I would not purchase again.  I have a few days to decide whether I am going to return this watch.So I will take a few more days, before making that decision.  I will update this review if anything else come to light.UPDATE: After setting the watch precisely to my time clock at work and to my Citizen AT4007-54E on 5/18/12, I found that the watch had lost 14 seconds within 24 hours.This is a nice looking, "cool factor" watch. But for a nearly $400.00 watch, it should keep better time and the build quality should feel better. The watch has been boxed back up and will be returned to Amazon.com tomorrow.
summary: Ok, but better watches available for less.

Let me start by saying I like the look of the watch.  It is clean and simple, which I like.  I wish they had a metal band for this watch as the rubber strap is a little thicker than I like.  My dislike comes from the service.  Five weeks after receiving this watch, the time was way off one morning.  I thought maybe the stem had come out and caused the time to get off, so I reset the watch.  The next morning the same problem, the movement was sticking.  I went onto my Amazon account to request a return, but it was past the 4 week period that Amazon will take a return, so I had to go through the Manufactures’ warranty.  I went on the Wenger Web site and that site points you to a very simple .pdf page with instructions on how to get the watch serviced.  They do not have an on-line request for a return authorization, nor do they have anything in place on-line to track the status of your repair.  So, I called the toll-free number and the person on the phone said something like “Manually fill out the paperwork and just mail it to us we will process the repair, no need for a return authorization.  Be sure to insure it if it gets lost”.  That was the return process, just mail it to a black hole in New York.  The .pdf document says it takes 3-5 weeks for repair.  After six weeks, I called the warranty people “Precision Time” and asked about the status of my watch.  A friendly lady found my order in their system and told me they had been moving facilities and were backed up on repairs.  They couldn’t tell me how much longer it would be, but she hoped for 2 weeks.  She said I would know when they got to it, because they would call me and tell me how much the shipping would be to get the watch back.  I expressed my displeasure on the time and having to pay again for shipping.  She said it was out of her hands, they only do the repairs for Wenger.  She then gave me the Wenger Customer Service number.  I then talked with Wenger Customer Service and she was helpful, but it was out of her hands as Precision Time is a separate company.  She said she would call and ask for expedited service and a waiver of the return shipping fees.  I asked for a new watch and not a repaired watch as it was only 5 weeks old.  She then asked why I didn’t take it back to the place I bought it and I told her that Amazon would not take it back after 4 weeks.  This is when I found out that  Amazon is not an authorized retailer, so she could not replace the watch as it might not be an actual Wenger watch.  I was left to the mercy of Precision Time.  I did receive my watch three weeks later with no shipping charge.  Point of the lesson of this sad tale:  Be sure who you buy from is an authorized retailer if you are making a significant purchase.
summary: Watch is OK, but watch out for the service!

First off - I hike fairly often, and have had MANY ABC watches. For the money, this watch doesn't come close to the Casio Pathfinder series watches. I'm staying with the Casio.Pros: Looks nice, has many of the features you would look for in an ABC watch.Cons: Cheaply made bezel. The silicon or rubber band has given my wrist major "indian burn" / burned red marks on my wrist. This watch needs it's battery replaced, whereas the pathfinder is solar. This watch has already lost a couple of minutes of time, in the month I've had it, the pathfinder is atomic. It never ONE time has detected a change in barometric pressure - enough for the little weather trend arrow to bend. Yet, it is clear outside - then major rainstorm, despite having the exact altitude set on it. It is somewhat difficult to use, perhaps it just takes more getting used to.This watch is pretty cool looking and all, but, for that much money, it needs to be more useful and keep the time correctly. My wrist rash I have each time I wear it, may just be different from person to person. Who knows. Maybe I'll give the watch to someone as a gift. Too bad, it looked pretty sweet online.

An awesome watch. From looks to function, this watch is a must for you outdoorsy people. Got mine from the seller OUTSIDE24, who shipped and packaged the watch excellently. I was a bit skeptical buying it at first due to some of the reviews I've read, so let me go over some problems that I've heard that other people have had.The compass: From many reviews, I've heard that it's not dead on accurate, but for me that's ok. I'm not in the military or anything where accuracy is needed. After testing it, that assessment is correct, it's off by a few degrees, so for those of you who NEED accuracy, the compass on this might not be for you. Easy to calibrate, but not clearly told on the instructions. Go to Suunto's YouTube channel where they show you how to calibrate it.Altimiter/Barometer: Also not dead on accurate. Always a bit off, but considering this is a watch, the fact that thsi function is even on there is nice.The bezel: Many people have said it scratches up easily and that it's the most fragile area. Due to it being made from plastic, it is the most fragile. I wouldn't agree with the fact that it scratches up easily, just be careful with it. I've banged it up already a few times (got this watch 2/7/2014, ordered 2/5/2014), and no scratches. The overall build of this watch is exceptional and as long as you're not careless, this should last a while.Rubber strap: Looking at the build of it, it seems that with time, the rubber will start to age and crack. Many reviews say that you have to replace it after 1-2 years, and looking at it, that looks like it's the case.Visuals: A lot of people have been saying that it's hard to see the time on the watch sometimes, and that they need to shine it under a flashlight to see it in the dark. In the sun or even low light, it's honestly not that hard to see the time, you just have to angle the watch right. The light is also bright enough to see the time in complete darkness, I know there has been complaints about how the light is not bright enough. The light, however, is a bit glitchy. When I'm on compass mode with the light on, the light blinks on and off. Might be a battery issue.Overall, this watch is great and looks sick as hell. Although it's not dead accurate, it's a great watch to have.

The main drawback for me is that the alarm and timer signals are so quiet that I often cannot hear them, especially if there is a sleeve covering the watch, or a small amount of noise in the room.  I doubt very much that I would hear the alarm if I was sleeping (I mostly use the alarm for reminding me of appointments).  Other negatives for me: I found it very difficult to use the multiple alarms, and eventually kept myself to using just one of them, which works easily; I have no experience with chronographs, and was unable to figure out from the instructions how it works; Recently (around 3 months since I got it) I discovered that the Indiglo feature which allows you to see the time in the dark, is no longer working.  I'll be sending it for warranty service.Update 4/27/14:  I got the watch back awhile ago from warranty service, and I believe it is a new replacement.  It looks identical to the original one I had, but the buttons are easy to press, the light works, and the alarm is much easier to hear (though I still doubt I would hear it in a noisy room or if I am sleeping).  I'm very happy with it.  (FYI, for warranty service you need to send an $8 check to cover postage).

reviewText: I've had the watch for a few weeks now and it's holding up well. I use it for running and rarely take it off. It holds up even in and out of water, doing dishes. The band is perfect for a woman's wrist size. The functions are easy to use and It seems pretty durable.

I've had this watch for almost 2 years now. It's comfortable, easy to use, and easy to program. I'm on my second one of these. The first one still works well, but the band broke while I was in the process of moving. I probably could have just replaced the band, but it was easier to just replace the whole thing. I had it out of the box, set to the correct date and time, and on my wrist in under 5 minutes. The only downside to this watch (I had to think to find one) is that it does look a little funny with my dressy clothes, but I'm someone who never takes their watch off for any reason and I figure the tan lines look even more funny than the casual watch. Bottom line is after my new watch breaks, I'll probably replace it with this one again as long as it's still available.
Great watch.  My daughter loves it.  She is a college softball player and needed a watch to keep up with how fast her time was.  So far she loves it.
Relatively easy to use and intuitive procedures for settings. I was able to set it up without consulting instruction booklet . Excellent value for money.
Exactly what it says.

Been wearing Timex running/ironman watches for years since they first came out as I was a cross country runner in HS and college then switched to marathons and road racing then triathlons. I no longer run but still have the mindset of a runner. When I hike, its how many minutes we climbed that mountain, etc. That said, I had misplaced my regular Timex ironman watch and after 3 days or feeling naked, and running late, without my watch (I'm not in the habit of checking my phone for the time as my watch less husband is), I went to Amazon. Wanted a "cheap watch" as the best way to find my old watch is to by a new one. This fit the bill. I REALLY like the thin band and the familiar watch face is comforting. Of course, I found my old watch I day after getting this in the mail but I am wearing this one exclusively now.
summary: Great every day watch for runners and not. Cheap and a GREAT value.

reviewText: Perfect watch for a smaller wrist. Very easy to program. I especially like the large display. It's a great value for the price.
My 10 year old daughter loves this watch.  She likes the style as well as the functions.  Great choice for young ladies.

I love the style of the watch but the first number does not show so even when it's 11 o'clock AM or PM you can only see one of the 1s and 10 o'clock it says 0 at 12 o'clock it says 2 ...I would like to get a replacement and I need to know how to go about that please send me a message
I am not sure of all the functions yet but I like it so far. Its a nice looking watch.

I wanted a watch for my job at the hospital and this works perfect. I love the fact that the strap is thin and the main controls is just big enough. The color purple is as depicted. A royal purple, which is classic. The black straps are matted with a sheen outer portion, which makes it professional, but sleek. Perfect combo.One awesome feature is that the little piece that holds the strap in place (not the metal portion, but the resin loop portion) has more material in it. This means that if I snag the watch whilst running or walking, it won't let the strap come out of place. This helps avoid the annoyance of having to slip the strap back into place.I noticed some people said that the start/stop that was on the top of the face of the watch was annoying, but I don't find it that way at all. I think it's neat and I don't have to push super hard to get it going.All in all, if you're looking for a sleek, but stylish running watch that can also function in a professional setting, look no further!
This is a very simple timer watch, but works great for timing runs! I recommend it to anyone interested in buying this.

I don't like watches so when looking for the perfect running watch it had to be small and not very noticeable. This fit the bill in every way. It has such a small wrist band and I hardly notice it while running. Some reviews said it's not waterproof under water, but I think that is expected and if you read the instructions it says not to press buttons under water. But for running this is great with laps (more than the 10-lap it says. I did at least 30 splits on one run). It kept all my splits for review and has a great timer that you can have it stop or repeat after it goes off. Love the black color with the hint of purple.
summary: Perfect minimalist watch, sleek, and comfortable for petite wrists

reviewText: Good watch. Very nice looking. Easy to use features. I bought this for my daughter who runs cross country and it comes in very handy . The watch has a big display but the watch is perfect for smaller wrists and slender/ athletic built ladies.
I've been wearing this watch daily for a little over a month and love it. The thinner band is very comfortable and it feels less clunky than some digital watches I've had in the past.
Great watch. This is my second one. I like the alarm its great. Timex make great watches. This is my work watch.
This works great for my child. It has been put to good use and has taken a beating with all the sporting activities being done with it.

I love ironman watches but don't buy a new watch when the cheesy thin slider that holds the top band down breaks as it always does. Go to Home Depot or Lowes or any plumbing supply place. Look for a 10 pack of O-Rings hanging on the wall in the plumbing aisle. At Home Depot they are called #208 O-Ring with a 9/16 outer diameter x 3/8 inner diameter x 3/32. One will slip over the buckle of your women's ironman watchband and you can easily with one hand slide it on and off the loose top band to hold it down. It is black, it looks nice, and it is comfortable to wear. Save the other 9 for when your watch actually dies and the band of your new ones break too.
summary: Great watch but here is how to replace a broken strap holder

reviewText: I have quite skinny arms and this watch is a nice size. Not too big but not too small easier. Has the usual range of functions and the digits are easy to see. I really like it.

As a nurse, I am washing my hands all the time ... I need a watch that can stand up to the possibility of getting wet throughout the day and this watch can do that.  Did not need all the 'bells and whistles' that go along with this watch but, it is difficult to find one that only tells time. If I ever get back into running, the other features will be a big plus. Also, the indiglo light on this item is greatly appreciated as I work at night.
This sporty watch was so nice to give it to my sister & I like the combination of violet & black color.

I was looking for a watch to wear while running. I have a great analog/digital Casio G-Shock which I use for outdoor activities but it's bulky and the chrono display is small and hard to read.It was hard to tell from the picture but the Timex is large enough to look great on a man's wrist but is still thin and lite enough to be perfect for running.Big digits and a good indiglo (light) display are exactly what I needed.I just got it today so can't comment on reliability and durability but out of the box- it's perfect for my needs.
summary: Lite, slender, great colors, big display for the chrono

reviewText: This watch is durable and is easy to operate. Met expectations for the price. I use the face with date, time and day of week the most.
Great watch.  Used in the pool and the ocean without any problems.  Seems scratch resistant.  A lot of extra functions.  Easy controls.

I have had a problem setting the day and date from DAY 1. It keeps good time, but the chip inside was not checked as it left the factory. To return it, is a big problem. The cost of sending it back is really not worth it.I paid under 40 dollars for it, so if it just keeps time and nothing else, so be it. I have found that Timex is NOT the Timex of a few years ago. I use this watch as a sport wear watch, but also to time soccer games for my 6 and 4 year olds.  It's easy to see and easy to use.  Lots of features and you can turn all but the watch on or off.  I like the big start/stop button and the easy to use big function buttons.  The indiglo works well and I like having multiple alarms.  The countdown feature probably gets used more than anything else
summary: Great fun watch, use it to referee

reviewText: This is exactly as expected, and serves its purpose. It looks classy but bright, and the picture is true to color. It isn't too big, but very easy to see the face. Would recommend to athletic types or those looking to clock a workout.

I have been a Track and Field and Cross Country Official for over thirty years and have had a Timex on my wrist for most of them.  It is an excellent timing device, is quick to respond with lap and finish times and reliable. My last watch haas been in use for more than 10 years and is still functional in every aspect except size.  The new watch is larger and is better for these old eyes.  5 stars and more.

reviewText: i am a big guy and i love timex watches..this is one of the extra large ones that looks better when i wear it. being a little older i love the display on the timex watches ...it is larger and easier to read.. and it remains accurate all the time.

reviewText: I do love the watch, but the wristband did not last very long. I have had to replace quite a few of these resin wristbands now. They do not last!

reviewText: I am very happy with my new watch, both in the speed with which it was received and the quality of the product itself. I bought this watch because my eyes are getting so bad and my last Ironman sucked as for as the indigo light - everything about this one is great so far. I wear the snot out of this thing and it looks exactly the same as when I got it and I can still see the time at night!!
This watch is really cool. It has a lot of instructions though. Its a little confusing at first. I use it for cross country.

reviewText: This one is fairly easy to use, and I was actually able to set it up and do what I need to do, without the manual. An ironman watch should be able to take the punishment.  After all, it is supposed to work out there.  Barely a bit over a month, and I already have two major scratches on it.  And I must say, I really do not abuse my watches.
My son works outdoor all year round, this has turned out to be great for him in all seasons thank you

I really like the watch and would have given it 5 stars but being a large person could have used a longer band this is a problem watch makers seem to ignore. I usually by divers watches to get the longer band but I like Timex watches because of the cost and reliability.
Great size, fits on wrist well and is easy to swim and workout with. Very durable and able to handle roughness.

It is not as nice as the older versions but it is still the best. Very good everyday watch. Im a lifeguard and i run track, so my watch gets a good beating. These times watches have always held up to the sun and water.

Bought it cuz I needed and like large watches,not large buy the term,but also the numbers on the watch, this watch is not what I expected by size or size of numbers, advertisment of picture,And Word,Oversize,Is misleading.

This is my second T5K529 in Orange and I absolutely love this watch. I've had Ironman Watches for years and they've never failed me. It performs just as well as my $400 Luminox. In fact, better. Definitely recommend this watch.
I love this watch.  I love the size and how easy it is to read and work. I use it to teach aerobics and bootcamp.  The options on this watch are perfect for instructors.

Attractive and fits my teenage sons narrow wrist, easy to record lap times around track, bright light for nightime viewing, water resistant . . can swim with it no problem, misc other useful features, and relatively inexpensive.
I really like this Timex.It fits great & it's so lightweight.It was well woth the price I paid for it.

I have a few fancy watches, but I recently left a desk job to cook in a restaurant and didn't want to mess them up in a kitchen. But this is pretty minor and I still really like the watch.

in my watch, but not ostentatious. I feel fashionable wearing this watch, but it's by no means gaudy or flashy. It just makes me feel a little out there, a little noticeable, a little different. Puts a smile on my face whenever I turn my wrist to look at the time. I highly recommend this watch.
He is an Ironman fan and the snap of orange looks great - a nice change from the traditional black.
If you wanna watch that does the basics.  Perfect for runners, refs.  You also get a reliable timepiece from Timex.

This was overall a good watch.  Fits comfortably.  Easy to read.  Nice illumination.  Kept time well.  Buttons intuitive.  Everything you expect from a Timex.  I docked it a star because the orange is fading way earlier than it should.  I'm happy with the purchase.  Does what it's supposed to.
Does everything advertised. Been diving with this watch numerous times to 120 + feet with no issues. The light worked well at depth and I really like how easy it is to read the face.

the watch is great, lightweight, looks very cool, postage was very quick, i wear it to work and water sports swimming surfing excellent easy to read

I was looking for a digital watch to use for track, and I decided to pick this up at the reasonable price of roughly $33. As any Timex Ironman you get the time, day of the week, day of the month, the month, a chronograph (timer), and 3 alarms. Also like any Timex Ironman it is very reliable, well working, and lightweight, which you probably already knew. But out of them all you should definitely opt for this specific model, mainly for its exclusivity among other digital watches you may say being worn during any kind of sport. It is roughly 43 mm going from left to right, which is a good size for a dress watch and quite large for a sports digital watch such as this. The orange case is also unique and a very bright, colorful, and nice touch. FYI if you are worrying about the extra size causing the watch to weigh more, don't bother, it is still practically inconceivable on your wrist as of weight. Overall this is a strong and tough watch to wear during whatever sport you do, and has a pleasant and unique touch that will stand it out from the crowd. 10/10.

I expect more to be released in the future.The other iPod watch bands which are made out of cheap nylon / poly material. They're lightweight, and probably great for sweating to the oldies. But they look cheap and durability is a real concern. The leather bands end up rotting with sweat and grime, and eventually need replaced.The Hex band is super-durable. It's relatively light, and the links and clasps use jewelry-standard construction - which is to say, it won't fall apart or come undone, but you'll need to take it to a watch store or jeweler to remove or add links to size it to your wrist. $5.I've been wearing it for about 3 months, daily. So far, the matte silver coating that matches my iPod has yet to wear away or scuff significantly. Just spots where it rubs my desktop. I imagine eventually it will show signs of wear that warrant a replacement, but not any time soon. The mounting plate for the ipod is metal, and perfectly designed to lock in the iPod securely (without wiggle), but super-easy to unclip and remove the ipod.I get a lot of compliments. I've always liked Nixon watches, and this band with the iPod has a similar aesthetic, just cleaner. I'm sure there are folks out there thinking, "What a dork. Guy has an iPod on his wrist." So be it. Eventually, there will only be 2 kinds of watches. The Rolex, Seiko, Breitling kind... and the iPod kind.One last thing: The open dock port and earphone hole are a exposed to moisture and grime. I'm looking for silver or light gray rubber or plastic plugs for these since most of the time, I'm not using them and would prefer to seal them. I waited a while so I could use this product in a couple of different applications before I rated it.  I'm glad I did.  For starters, Schampa is a known maker of quality balaclavas. It can go a full day under a helmet without stretching.  The neck protecting wind panel is of a durable material that is soft against the body but keeps the wind and dust out.  It's split to lay evenly and comfortably both front and back.  Easy to breathe through.For the down side:  The open area around the eyes is small. The bottom part is cut almost straight across so if you pull it up over your nose, it's almost resting against the bottom of your eyes.  OK, I have a big nose, but I doubt that's the issue in this case.  You can see what I mean by looking at the picture illustration.  The other part I didn't care for is that you can't comfortably pull down the face and nose cover below your chin.  That's one of the tradeoffs with it being made out of a material that won't stretch... you can't pull it down to keep from fogging up glasses at a stop, take a drink of a beverage, talking, or whatever other reason you'd want to pull it down.For use under a motorcycle or snow machine helmet, it's great. Much better than many other products on the market.  To use by itself without a helmet, I think I'd look for something else.

I can barely tell the time in a pitch dark room with the lights off.  Further, the glow in the dark markings on the watch is a bit disappointing, but to me that didn't matter much.  Lastly, to turn off the LCD display you have to hold down one of the buttons for 5 sec.  This my friend is a design flaw.  I like to keep the LCD display off because i just don't want clutter of information every time i glace over the watch. What would have been better is to reduce that time to 1 or 2 seconds.  I guess the designers felt that by hyperextending the wrist one may unintentionally turn off the display by pressing the button, but if you wear the watch you'll see how that is very unlikely scenario.I would still wear this watch and i think i would still buy it again, but those are my complaints.

It's hard to decide where to begin with this watch --- I own a number of watches, three of them Breitlings, with a couple of Luminox's thrown in. So being "fair" really isn't the easiest thing to do ...So --- all in all, I really like this watch.First: it's hard to find a titanium watch with all of the features present, at this price:Dual display12/24 timeUTC offsetDSTSelectable date format$Button-press beep on/offHourly chimeWorld Time (with a LOT of listings)6 Alarms --- 1 repeat schedule, 5 daily)Chronograph, with 10 splitsCountdown timer (beep on last minute, every remaining ten seconds, then continuous at end)Heavily-grooved bezel edge (read: functional), approx. two clicks per minute... and ... TITANIUM.This watch may look a bit "clunky" in the photos --- it is not. It weighs under 2-1/2 ounces, and is sized the way you'd expect (or should expect) a functional chronograph to be.The perforated leather strap is very nicely made. It is thick and well-made, but not my personal preference (I prefer metal bracelets or nylon NATO (tight fit under those spring bars!!!) or velcro one-piece (perfect!!!). The titanium bracelet costs half again as much as the watch, which defeats the purpose, here.A neat trick: the LCD displays can be turned manually (making the watch look "cleaner" and less cluttered, and saving battery capacity. The displays come back on as soon as you push a button. This feature can also be set on a schedule (say, LDS's off at 0200, back on at 0700). So, some interesting thought behind it. (That, or it will be a battery hog!)It strikes me that Momentum has taken the time to listen and observe, and come up with some items that are functional, nice-looking, and priced to a bearable level.So --- what's bearable? My Breitling Aerospace is one-third as thick, has half the functions, has a titanium bracelet, weighs slightly more, costs ten times as much. Fair comparison? Of course not. But --- the faces of the two watches (except for the LCD windows) are almost identical. The Momentum's bezel has blackened minute hashes, the Aero's is "stylishly" engraved only. Functionally, the Breitling operates through the stem only (no push-pieces), which is elegant, but fiddly. Do the two watches swim in the same tank? No.Where this watch falls only a bit short is luminescence. It is not tritiu.m or Superluminova. Dark-adapted, you should have no trouble, but it isn't wildly bright; certainly OK, though. The internally-illuminated digital displays are an advantage, but they tend to reflect a bit off the inside of the crystal, hazing the view slightly.UPDATE: I am used to HUGE lume, and have been informed by the manufacturer that they do use a form of superluminova ... and that they may alter the application technique. As I'd said, they really do seem to listen.!The crystal is NOT two-side ant-reflective sapphire. What are you expecting at this price range?Don't even think about stuffing a heavy Zulu strap in under the spring bars, unless you want to pop the bars. (What is it about these clearances that manufacturers (including Breitling) do not get?) I ordered and use the plain velcro one-piece (it has a nice skinny mounting panel, and a light velcroed nylon bottom patch. It offers infinite adjustment and un-lose-ability.The push-pieces (buttons) are styled into a teardrop shape. Why? Who knows. When you push them, do not push on the tapered ends --- they will tend to wedge a bit into the case and bind. (They don't stick, but they won't push smoothly, either.) Push them in their centers, or at the fat ends.I have no idea how "indestructible" this watch will turn out to be. Typically, I wear a watch 24/7, in the shower, in the garden, in the shop. If the watch can't take it, the watch goes away. I bought this watch as a "beater," something that can get whacked on more than usual without worrying too much about it. Everything's relative --- I know a lot of folks who think $100 is a lot for a watch.If you have a "wristwatch-related-illness" then this one probably belongs in the collection. It's so usable that I've been wearing it since it came.(Other watches currently owned and worn: Breitling Aerospace; Breitling Blackbird (original Arabic numerals); Breitling titanium Chrono Avenger; Luminox titanium F-117 chronograph.)Beep-beep. 3 o'clock. Done.PSI tried the Hadley-Roma steel bracelet on this (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B001EYVBOK/ref=oh_details_o02_s00_i00) and it's pretty good (if you have the tools to wrench the links apart.
