Was looking for a spring, summer windbreaker type jacket with lots of pockets (gotten used to my winter coat with ample pockets for scarf, beanie, keys) - wanted something to keep in the car or pack to throw on during the cooler Spring/Summer nights, and could double as a mini-backpack (because of the ample pockets). Also wanted something I could wear downtown and was somewhat stylish - Well, can't get everything you want. I had difficulty finding any casual, stylish jacket that fit the bill in the pockets department so I went looking where I knew pockets were a plenty - winter sports jackets. This jacket might pull off the so-called "outdoor chic" but that's about it, it's not bad though for an outdoor jacket.Quick notes about Marmot: I own a couple of Marmot jackets, a softshell and a hardshell. The jackets fit somewhat differently - Both jackets are sized small, however the softshell is near skin tight and the hardshell is loose. A hardshell should be loose in my opinion, but whether a softshell should be loose or tight I think is preference, so let it be known that Marmot tends to go tight on softshells.I am about 5'8" 170 lbs. I compared both the small and medium Tempo Hoody -The small is somewhat tight, it bites into the armpits always and your elbows in certain positions. Zipped up, it feels somewhat like wearing a compression/rash guard type shirt. Definitely no room for layering anything other then a base layer, tshirt, or button up underneath comfortably. It looked good but I couldn't get comfortable in it.The medium fits comfortably, no tightness in the armpits or elbows. I went with the medium. I guess I am between sized because it is a tad baggier than I'd like for aesthetically reasons, but doable. You can fit a fleece underneath, up to a 200 I think but it would get tight. The torso is also a tad longer than I'd like (an inch or two longer than the small). The long torso is nice for actual snow adventuring, for keeping the cold out when you raise your arms, and keeping your jacket nicely tucked underneath your backpack hip belt.Marmot categorized their softshells into three types, M1 thru M3, M1 being warmest and driest, M3 being the lightest and most breathable. The Tempo is an M3 and it makes sense: no liner, no fleece, very thin, moderately light weight. All warmth is from the thin layer of softshell material only, so it's not very warm at all. With just a shirt and this jacket on, comfort range for me would be 60 F+ for just standing around. Might be good to 40 or 50 F being continuously active, running, skiing. This is exactly what I wanted for my uses, Spring/Summer night windbreaker for walks around town.The material is very stretchy - the small feels like a compression/rash guard type shirt, though tighter because it is thicker than a compression shirt. Since the material is stretchy, all the stuff you pile into your pockets will sort of show through to the outside as a 3D imprint. I haven't tested this out, but I would imagine if you are running in this jacket, bulky items would make the jacket start to bounce and swing - I hate that, so if I were running I'd wear a light backpack to stow keys, phone, camera, or get a stiffer jacket if that exists. For snow sports and walking around, it's fine.Durability: In my opinion, would probably do OK with moderate travel through bush and rock climbing, but I'm not a climber so who knows.There are four pockets: two side pockets, one outside chest pocket and one inside chest pocket, all zipped. Nice high "collar" for keeping elements out when you are zipped up. The hood's brim has a slight stiffness to it. Drawcord for shrinking the hood around your face and also a drawcord for shrinking the hood to the back of your head. Drawcord for the hip hem. Hook and loop straps for the two wrists.I can fold it down to about the size of a thick, thick notebook.It's not marketed for use in a real downpour but I ran a full stream of water over a sleeve for a minute and the water slid off no problem. No doubt this is attributed to out-of-the-box brand new water repellent but still pretty cool.Summary: Aesthetically, wish the the jacket were a little shorter and tighter for the size medium. Looks aside, for pure outdoor use, I really like this jacket, will be my new choice jacket for most outdoor activities.These type jackets can get very expensive - I think this one is pretty reasonably priced for what you get.

reviewText: My wife and I both have pairs of Beech Quatro yoga sandals that we wear only inside the house on weekends, when we're on our feet all day in the kitchen for ethnic cooking marathons. They really seem to be effective in reducing leg and back pain after long hours of standing. They're "inside shoes" only. We've never worn them out of the house, because we don't want to soil or scratch our tile floors with sand or stones picked up from outside. We had been meaning to get extra pairs for outside use for quite a while, but never got around to it. Then I found out about the new (as of Spring 2011) Beech Fusions, and decided to give them a try.The Fusions are quite a bit different from the Quatros, in appearance, construction, materials and fit. The soles of the two types are exactly the same size and profile, although the Fusions have a little more arch support (it's barely noticeable, though). The Fusions have a hard, textured rubber bottom rather than the softer, smoother material of the Quatros. The strap of the Quatros extends along the side of the foot like a conventional thong, while the Fusions have a wider crosswise vinyl strap like that on an athletic slide. This strap is softly padded on its inside surface and fits very snugly, unlike the Quatros strap, which is quite loose on the top and sides. The toe separators are the biggest difference. The Quatros' separators are made of elastic cords sheathed in black plastic tubing, which provide more separation than the Fusions' much thinner rolled-and-stitched vinyl thongs. They still provide the benefits of toe separation, but not as much. On the other hand, the Fusions are easier to walk in without the slight awkwardness of the Quatros.Bottom line: we're very happy with both the original Beech Quatro yoga sandals and the new Fusions. The Quatros remain for indoor use only, since our cooking marathons do not involve that much walking, which is less comfortable than in the Fusions because of the greater toe separation. The Fusions are easier to don and doff and easier to walk in, which makes them our sandals of choice for shopping, running errands and other trips away from the house. Regardless of which one you choose, you will realize at least some benefits in terms of posture, stamina and relief from leg and back pain. I didn't believe it at first (see my review of the original Beech Yoga Sandals), but now I do. They really work.
summary: Toe Separation in a Slide Sandal

reviewText: :Wink Shapewear is amazing! During my pregnancy I read a lot about how belly binding and girdle wearing can help with supporting the abdomen and also help with the mushy "mommy belly" post birth. Sounded like a good idea so I looked all over the Internet for the best girdle... And I was pretty picky. First, I'm now a single mom so it had to fit my budget of under $80. Second, I knew I was having a C-Section so it would have to be comfortable over my incision. Third, I read about the post pregnancy discharge (eww. I know) so something that I had to pull up like underwear didn't seem logical to me. I also wanted something with super strength as I had to fit back into my work uniform ASAP and I gained 80lbs during my pregnancy. So many options out there... I waited until 2 weeks before my section date and prayed it would show up in time... Wink's ultimate belly and hip shaper met every qualification I had set... It's budget friendly, I didn't have to pull it up like underwear, it has super sucking and tucking capabilities, and it looked like I could possibly roll it up if it irritated my incision. I was sold! I was a bigger girl (fit and fabulous but larger than life at 5'9 and pre-birth 275lbs) when I ordered it and my measurements were an inch bigger than what the fit guide suggested for the XL/XXL size but figuring I'd lose weight, I ordered it anyway. When it arrived I was shocked... First, it seemed so small that I double checked the size (that was probably due to my belly being huge and not accounting for its stretchy potential). Second, the material felt really soft for being something that's supposed to suck and tuck. I packed it in my hospital bag thinking I'd be able to squeeze into it, I was wrong. About 2 weeks after the birth of my son I was able to squeeze into it. The most beautiful thing about this garment is the 6 different levels of hooks! I was on the sixth level when I started to wear it and as I lost more and more weight I'd move to the next level of hooks... Making its value even higher because I didn't have to keep buying a different size as I shrunk! My son is now 3 months old and I'm on the first layer of hooks (its actually getting a little loose but I love the support it gives!). Because of this garment I was able to fit back into my work uniform 8 weeks after having him (even after gaining 80 pounds!) and everyone at work was amazed that I even had a baby because this garment made my stomach soooo flat. It is easy to use and doesn't bunch under clothes and it really helped to support my back and stomach. It was so comfortable that I often wore it to bed as well. It didn't irritate my incision... Being something that wraps around the belly, I could control if/how it touched the incision area. The only thing I had an issue with was the fact that I have super huge and wide hips and if I attempted to wear this over my hips it would roll up. So I just pulled it up a little higher to the bottom of my ribs to prevent the bottom part of the garment from rolling up. I'm now 20lbs away from my pre-pregnancy weight and the XL/XXL size is now too big or I'd continue to wear it under my work uniform because it definitely helps to support the entire abdomen area while giving it a beautifully taunt shape!

The girdle is seamless under clothing, so it shows so noticeable signs or lining that I am wearing one. It has 3 layers of hook and eye that allows for adjustments and easy bathroom break. It helps to keep me in shape, making my body look slim and trim. I normally wear it under my dresses but it can be worn under pants also.

reviewText: I’m a production engineer in Venezuela and travel across time zones every month.  For years, I’ve been searching for a quartz analog-digital watch that included world time with a user defined time zone, plus a countdown timer longer than one hour for long flights or production runs, and of course, also the usual day, date, stop watch and alarms, chime and beep on or off, digital displays and luminous hands.  Format 4 has all that plus a screw in crown (as in my 45 year old, fine working Rolex) for 10 atmospheres water resistance, screw in back plate, second hand,  rotating bezel, not too big a case diameter, and is also solidly made and reasonably priced.Momentum read my mind! Format 4's case is made of Titanium, thus lighter compared to steel watches.  The print work on the face is sober (unlike cheap or toy watches.) The olive green digits on black display are highly readable (the more light the better) and good enough in the dark. I was also pleasantly surprised to find a user defined long term alarm, which I set and labeled for my next year’s wedding anniversary, a date I always forget.Format 4 allows for Daylight Savings Time adjustment for each time zone, important because countries differ in policy. Curios about DST, I wrote a question on Momentum’s website.  I received a phone call in less than 24 hours, plus a follow up email.  With this level of fast and motivated customer attention, and their renewable 2 year warranty for up to six years, I’ll wear Format 4 long term.Momentum does not make their movements.  But neither do almost all brands except for Rolex and a handful more! Most watchmakers, including the well know high priced brands, buy movements from mostly four specialized makers in Switzerland and Japan.  Format 4 has two movements from two manufacturers.I added to the black rubber strap a Hadley-Roma 20mm butterfly push button deployment clasp.  It upscales the Format 4’s appearance and comfort, and adds safety putting the watch on and taking it off.  The clasp, part BKL150W, available in Amazon, is brushed stainless steel, indistinguishable from the case’s slightly darker titanium metal.Momentum got it perfect with Format 4!
summary: Momentum got it perfect with Format 4!

reviewText: I have several rubber watches and was attracted to the appearance and the functions of this particular watch.  I have a Brietling Aerospace Chronometer and the Momentum has the same functions at 1/10th the cost.I have had it about 2 weeks now and took it on a hiking trip to Glacier National Park.  It works fine, although navigating through the functions is not easily done as with a Timex or Casio with similar functions.  You have to read the manual to figure out how to set and work it.  The pros as i see it are: appearance, functions including multiple alarms, chromo, timer, world time and both digital and analog format.  Additionally synchronizing the analog and digital functions is easily done once you figure out how it works.  The cons (the reasons I gave this 4 stars instead of 5) are: difficulty/confusion in setting the watch and an unreadable night light function.  The night light backlights the led and makes it hard to read.  It would be a much better function if they just turned on the led lights without the backlight.  Otherwise it seems to be ok but that is with only two weeks experience with the watch.  It does have an energy saving capability where you can turn off the digital led and have it come back on automatically which seems to work well but I don't have any idea how long the battery will last with and without this capability.  All in all not a bad watch for the price.

The watch was extremely NOT waterproof.  I'm talking you wash your hands once and you've literally got water droplets in the watch face.  This is not normal!!!  The watch was never even submerged or even showered with, but it soaks up water like the freakin titanic!!!2.  The band tended to smell pretty bad now and again.  I'm a very clean person, but the band would smell like sweat after 3-4 days.  I would take it off and clean the band with a q-tip and hand sanitizer and it would be ok for a few more days but this was an endless cycle...  The smell was bad enough where I would have to take the watch off because I was embarrassed, it smelled like rotting leather.  (It probably was.)3.  Well last  but not least I had the watch for less than 30 days before the band just randomly broke while I was walking to class.  Literally less than a month!!!4.  My god I almost forgot, the last 2 weeks I had this watch, the damn thing kept HORRIBLE time... It literally lost 3-5 minutes PER DAY!!  Seriously, like can any watch have this many problems???  It blows my mind!!!  I could probably buy a $5 watch off e-bay and have better quality than this.  Really sad since I liked the design so much.  Hopefully soon some other company will remake this watch and do it correctly, because the design is awesome, but the watch is total junk!So in overview like I said, even with all the messed up things with this watch, I still really enjoyed it and was fine dealing with even having to clean it constantly and making sure to be extreamly careful when washing my hands not to get too much water on it...  and then re-setting the time EVERY MORNING...even after all that, then the dang band breaks after less than 30 days of use!!!  This just sends up red flags to me that it's total junk.  I think I paid like $29 or something for this watch on amazon, and I thought I was getting a deal with all the extra features this watch had (rotating face...).  The fact was, I basically rented a piece of junk watch for more than a dollar a day until it broke...  Do yourself a favor and go for quality, not looks.  This watch looks cool, I have to admit it, but trust me... IT IS NOT!

It has a large face (the watch is about 2.5 inches across) and is easy to read in most any conditions even without my glasses. To start off, I ordered this on a saturday evening, and received it via UPS on Tuesday around 7:00PM, and that was one-day shipping.Anyways, the watch has some really cool functions, and looks amazing. I've owned $20 watches at Walmart/Meijer stores, Rolex, Omega, and I've recently been using an iPod Nano 6 with a white Nanotch(tm) watchband. The G-Shock has a white matte finish, and if you're a student, or someone working at a cubicle and writes a lot, then it is a possibility that you could smear graphite (from the pencil or ink from pen) onto the watch, but you could wash it off with soap and water.This watch is based off timezones to calculate the time, and it comes with a manual (timezones are at the last pages). The manual is in English, Spanish, and French I think b:The hands move around based on what the digital display reads; you can turn on and off daylight saving time too. (Watch arrives in EST, NYC.) We all know that the watch is waterproof, shock-proof, anti-magnetic, so I don't really need to say anything an those topics. You can change the backlight duration from 1.5sec - 3 sec, and it is pretty cool. There's military time (24HR digital display) and the normal time (12HR) with a little PM that is in the top left corner of the left display, when it's the afternoon. It has a really accurate stopwatch, with laps and a split. (Great for running and you don't have to be worried when it rains, unless you have your phone) There's a timer, which for some reason, only goes up to 24 minutes... you can adjust the duration. (You can set it to one time run/alarm, or a constant loop until you turn it off).There are 26 world times; I have mine to London, and it works GREAT. (Takes like 2 seconds to calculate but I'm fine with that) It has 4 alarms; you press reverse or forward to stop them, a snooze (Like a wake-up alarm) and you press either reverse or forward to snooze it. Will come back on in like 3 mins, but you have to turn it off and on again to stop it.)There's an option to turn on hourly chime which beeps twice at every hour. You press reverse to turn on the backlight, and hold it down for 3 seconds to enable the auto-light when you tilt the watch 45.  The left circle on the upper half of the watch displays whether snooze, alarm, auto-light, or hourly chime is on. The middle has something to do with the stopwatch, you can see some accuracy in the timing (I guess xD) and the right circle... This I'm clueless on, but I think it also has to do with the stopwatch and stuff :).The hour nobs are "glow-in-the-dark", and, unfortunately, the hands don't have an illuminating tab on them. The lower left display shows the time in digital form, press forward and it shows the date. The bottom right screen shows the day (eg: Mon as in Monday) and below it is the seconds. (Btw the hands are SUPER precise when they point at the little lines like for example, it is 1:00 or 13:00. The hands point exactly where they should be, and when the seconds reach around 30 seconds, the minute hand moves a tiny notch! Then, when it's 1:01 or 13:01, it points normally.) The contrast on this watch is really nice; I've gotten tons of compliments... some of my friends are even jealous! This is my first G-Shock and I'm not disappointed! I LOVE the double-clasp band, doesn't seem like it will come loose, the buttons have a nice texture, and I learned how to operate this watch in about 5 minutes (I was CLUELESS when I first got it, lol) The manual helps, and I HOPE my review helped you too! Relatively fast shipping, great watch, beast looks, best $100 I spent! This watch is part of the Japan Movement, and is housed/cased in China (I don't care where it was manufactured :D) and I'm simply just impressed... the dial is pretty big, and it it looks beautiful. If you have any questions please ask! I will hopefully respond quickly :)UPDATE NOVEMBER 2013: After using this watch for more than a year (Sept 29, 2012) I can say it's still working fine! Battery life is (supposedly) 2 years... I don't have any battery problems with mine! However, the paint is starting a chip slightly. I've gone snorkeling/scuba diving, dropped it many times off high places, FROZE MY WATCH, and many more rigorous tests... this thing is a tank! Some dirt and grime is starting to build up around the strap; it has a slight brown tint from my use. I don't use auto-light at all really, and the snooze is somewhat quiet... so don't use this as a primary alarm clock!I love the stopwatch. It's so freaking usefull and goes to the thousandths of a second! (ex: 12.345 seconds) Hopefully I will post a picture on this page to show what it looks like after all this time!

As a previous owner of at least 3 Casio G Shock watches, this one is my favorite. There are numerous reviews on the amazing features of the G shock watches,so I will not be commenting on any technical specifications-you can read about those details on Casio's website.Now on to my review...first, the size of the watch itself is large but not huge. I don't have a large wrist and this watch fits very nicely on my wrist. When I compare it to my Casio PAG-240 watch, I would say that it actually wears a little better than the latter watch. The case itself is 51mm. The weight of the watch is surprisingly light, after a few minutes on your wrist you may forget it's there.The color of the watch is one of my favorite designs. The band is a resin, matte, white finish. I was a little skeptical of the color at first...because of color fading, discoloration and how a white watch would look on a man. I can tell you that after wearing the watch for 2 weeks, I love how the watch looks! Trust me when I say people will notice your watch! The combination of the white case and band contrasting with the dark face really pops on your wrist.People will be looking at your watch before they make eye contact with you. White Casio G Shock watches are hard to find in stores where I live. You will be the proud owner of a watch that looks very unique and expensive.The face of the watch is my next favorite feature. The actual color is more gun metal than black imho. The dials on the face display different items. The alarm,hourly signal,snooze and auto light is on one dial. The other 2 dials display stop watch seconds and speed information. This is a way to input a known distance and then in conjunction with the stopwatch use the display to calculate speed!The digital-analog box displays the time in either 12/24hour formats. The other box displays the day of the week and seconds. My least favorite feature is with Casio's choice of color for the displayed numerals-they are a very faint, light silver color. In bright daylight, of low light situations you will have a very difficult time seeing the display. I work in an office environment everyday,so the fact that the display is very hard to read doesn't apply for most of my daily use. I can read either the analog or digital display quickly. The hour and minute hands are nice and large-so you can tell the time quickly during the day.At night or in low light conditions you will need to use the led light. The led light is bright and although it does not actually illuminate the hands or the display boxes,it does a sufficient job of creating ample light in which to read the hour/minute hands. You will not be able to read the digital parts but the rest of the watch is illuminated enough to see the hour markers. On a side note,the hour markers are glow in the dark reflective so that helps.The watch case itself has a nice look and feel to it. It appears rugged in design and has several screws in place to help hold it together. The watch of course is waterproof,anti-magnetic and shockproof. Again, if not familiar with the G Shock family you can read all about the design/features on Casio's website. Casio has been making G Shock watches for over 25 years and they keep improving their product each time.In conclusion, I own 3 G Shock watches now, and have never had a minutes worth of trouble out of any of them. They are built to last, and they do. The combination of the white matte band and gun-metal face add a very attractive time piece to your wrist. The only negative would be the previously mentioned faint color digital display. I would not let that discourage you from purchasing this watch. The  watch has been worn under long sleeve shirts, winter jackets and has been in my wrist for 2 weeks and it appears to remain in perfect condition, the band and case has remained in its pristine white color.Lastly, the only thing that would make this an absolutely perfect watch would be the inclusion of a solar battery.I would highly recommend this watch from Amazon and Casio...in fact the longer you wait the more it costs. The watch is in high demand,limited quantities(even on Amazon) and rises in price daily. I paid $98 for mine 2 weeks ago.This watch will not only help you tell the time, it will help those around you tell time because they will be STARING at it!

The watch was broken when we got it and there was no paperwork in the delivery package to detail how to return the item to the vendor.The watch did not tell the correct time, would not sync to the proper city or sync the analog hands to the digital time and within a day just stopped working all together.  We certainly did not expect to have these extreme problems with a supposedly brand new, name brand watch from Amazon.  Ultimately, we had to return the watch to Casio, at our own additional expense, because the watch we were sold was defective and we had no way to contact the Amazon sub-vendor.The watch was purchased over a month ago and it has been at Casio repair for over three weeks of that time. We are still waiting to get the watch back.I am very disappointed and angry. I bought the watch as a gift and it has been nothing but a headache since it arrived.  I was skeptical about buying this item from Amazon and now realize we would have been better off buying it anywhere else.  I doubt we would have had these issues had we purchased the watch at a traditional retail outlet near our home.  We would have had the watch sooner and been able to see and test it out in the store before purchasing.  Also, if it were defective, we could have brought it back to the store rather than incur additional expenses by having to ship the watch and repair the brand new watch through the manufacturer.  Buyer beware unless you are looking for hassle, inconvenience, aggravation and to spend a lot of money.

Hold down the Adjust button for 15 seconds until you hear a beep and see the display that usually reads the day and seconds begins to blink. From here click the "forward" and "reverse" buttons to select your city code. My wife saw a woman wearing a hat similar to this one night and thought it was cute. After looking online it seems the name brand version sells for over $100. Due to the nature of "Fads" I just couldn't see spending lots of money on something that most likely will be out of fashion in a year (if not already). This is obviously a knock-off and I certainly didn't expect to get a top quality product for under $20 but truthfully, this really isn't bad at all.What your getting is a decently made inexpensive version of what you could buy for well over $100 by going brand name. Visually it doesn't look obviously cheap and unless your comparing it side by side with the original, or have friends that are fashion snobs most people will be oblivious that its not the real thing. Honestly, I thought the real things were "Cheap" and was kind of shocked at how much they sell for.Appearance:The colors are accurate to the picture. The lining is black and the paw prints are in the correct places. The ears don't always stand up perfect but are even in height and in the right places. It looks like what it is supposed to look like, which is a cute, spirit hood hat thingy.Quality:Seems to be decently made. Although inexpensive it doesn't feel terribly cheap or fragile. That being said, I wouldn't think it would last a lifetime either. If I were getting this for a young girl and she wore it every day of winter I would think she would get at least 1 season out of it before needing repairs. Treated with care would probably last a couple years.Use:Ok, based on some reviews for this product let me make this clear. The main purpose for this hat is to look cute. The secondary purpose is to add a little warmth from the elements when its cold outside. The hat absolutely satisfies the cute factor without a doubt. Because of the material and combined thickness of the lining and outer "fur" it also provides a good amount of warmth, certainly on your head. I wouldn't wear this for any prolong exposure to the elements, but for quick trips from the house to car to mall or from school to the bus this should work fine and in all cases better then not wearing anything on your head.The "glove" parts are a great way to briefly keep your hands from the elements but are in no way a substitute for real gloves.  Again, This is made to be cute and with your hands in the sleeve/pockets it is very cute indeed.Rain, Snow etc - No, this is not appropriate for wet weather. It is in no way water proof or resistant and would be no different then putting a stuffed animal on your head and going out in the rain. If your wearing it and it starts snowing you should be fine, again, better then nothing but I wouldn't put it on to go out in a snow storm, it may keep you warm enough but I fear it may ruin the fur.Overall:I like it and feel it is worth the money. It appears well made (only time will tell), adds some warmth to your head and doesn't look overtly cheap. Also it is very cute and I smile every time my wife puts it on.

I wear all kinds of compression almost every day when exercising and have several top brands.I cycle 3 times a week, cross fit 3 times a week, and yoga 3 times a week. Each time I am wearing some variation of compression skin whether its a top, bottom, sleeve, warmer, recovery etc. Every single other compression item from every other brand works perfectly and fits perfectly. These 110 tights however have 1 major flaw in their design which make them absolutely useless for my purposes.First off, they look great, fit great and the material is very nice looking and feeling. The compression is also substantial and seems to work well. Certainly a high quality product so there is no problem there. Where they dropped the ball is, there is a large continuous stitching that starts at one knee, comes up the thigh slightly inward, continues across the pelvic region, then back down the other side to the other knee. It also has an identical one on the backside. This appears to bring the inner thigh panels, and crotch panels, and bind them to the front and rear leg panels. Herein lies the problem.The location of the stitch and the fact that it is continuous rather than stopping and starting again at the leg/pelvic crease, renders these useless for any type of fitness where you would require to squat or lunge in any fashion.Every other pair of compression tights I have has the legs, and crotch, butt and inner thigh, all independent from each other to allow maximum movement and functionality, with no restriction point.These 110 tights are basically for sitting and recovering only.  If I were to squat down rapidly, they would explode and I would be naked. :)I was under the impression that these were able to be used as fitness tights, then you can immediately insert the ice packs and begin recovering right away. That is how its pitched and presented. They even come with a thermal bag for the ice packs to be taken with you to use right after whatever you do. That is not entire true.Bottom line. I am returning them due to their limited application. I can't see spending $200+ on them. If you are only looking to walk, light jog etc... and or just use them to sit around in then they are great. If you want to do anything vigorous in them, make sure you wear underwear in case you blow em out in public.

reviewText: I will first say that I haven't been able to find another automatic wrist-watch that is less than $70-$80, let alone less than $15. (Wal-Mart has a very pretty one for $125, but they also have one or two more-average-looking ones for around $80)This watch feels fine on my wrist (though after the band had adjusted from use, it started wanting to slide down an inch or so), the watch face is also an okay size (I suppose it's about a medium size - perhaps a little larger than some, and smaller than the super-large-faced watches). It has a nice, thick... um... watch case area. Thicker than most watches I've seen. The second hand is constant, while I would rather have an incrementing/ticking second hand, but I think it depends on the person. The watch is quiet. I have to put it up to my ear to hear it ticking (it ticks maybe around 20 times a second? I could never keep up to accurately time it). I can also sometimes hear the pendulum quietly 'woosh' if I move my wrist right next to my ear.I didn't get the same watch as pictured. It's very similar, with the same shape and the same patterns, but it's not the exact same. The back view of the watch is almost completely different, other than the basic shape. The back does not say a thing about it being stainless steel or about being water resistant, the pendulum is shaped differently, the screws inside are blue instead of silver (but that does add more color to it), and etc. I didn't get a box or directions with it. I'm not sure if I would have if I'd asked or not.I've asked someone at Dakota Watch Company about the watch, and the person I spoke with said they thought the metal could have been made of a blend of stainless steel and other metals (but they didn't examine the watch, just glanced at it when I held up my wrist).There was a thin scratch through the metal on the back of the watch when I got it (from the edge of the watch to the start of the back window), but I haven't noticed any scratches since. I wore the watch for one week straight (not including when asleep - I laid it face up when going to bed) to see how it did, and I kept track of how it kept time. There were two or three times I had tried winding the watch, but I could never tell when it was finished (I've also found that it's a lot easier to wind if you use an adjustable wrench. The groves on the knob are a bit too deep for me). When setting the time, pulling out the knob won't freeze the second hand (it will make a quiet clicking noise when pulling it out, by the way). I found out later that if you wait until the watch stops, you can set the time backwards and the second hand won't start. It takes about five seconds to shake the watch enough to get it moving after this, so I'll set it five seconds fast. Also be sure to set it as close to an even 5 minute mark as possible (for both the second and minute hands), since this is one of the types of watches that only mark every five minutes. I also have a quartz watch like that. During the first week, I'd noticed the watch losing about two and a half seconds per hour on average (but it varied overnight, from seeming to keep time almost perfectly to losing as much as it does during the day). This 2.5-2.7 second loss of time will really add up. I found some sites online that say this kind of watch can be adjusted, but I don't know of any place close to where I live that will do it for me (Jared's said they do that type of thing, but they have to send a watch off to have it adjusted). I had bought the watch knowing that other reviewers have said the band is terrible, thinking I would replace it with a silver chain (or even a black rope), but I haven't yet found something acceptable to change it out with. The band has stayed together for me so far, though, and it does look kind of nice. When I put the watch on, the buckle may slice a thin sliver off the edge of the band, and the belt-loop beside the buckle had come unglued at one point (I tried sewing it back together. My bad stitching has held so far).I've decided to only wear the watch occasionally, but it loses more time when I do this (wearing it constantly keeps it wound better - and you'll need to wear it constantly to know how much time it's gaining or losing - but the time may need to be reset frequently if you decide to always wear it, unless taken somewhere to adjust).I asked YouYouPifa about the watch and they said to wind it 30-40 times and not to wind it backwards because the movement can get stuck, as well as it being normal for the watch to loose a lot of time. They also said the watch should work well for about 12 hours after taking it off, if it's wound up.

The weight is very comfortable... not too heavy, but with just enough heft to hang nicely.The accompanying chain, with a lobster-claw clasp, and at 30", is the perfect length to provide for a good balanced-look. I recommend an initial cleaning (of the chain ONLY) --with a quick dip in a jewelry cleaner -or- washing w/mild dish soap and warm water & pat dry--  prior to wearing though, to avoid any discolouration transferring to one's neck.Setting the time is easily achieved by pulling the crown ring up, then turning the crown to the proper time.  Pressing the crown down causes the pendant face to pop-open so that the time  may be read.I am very impressed and satisfied with this item.  The price point makes it a very affordable gift as well.This is one rare example of getting more than what one paid for. Very Nice, indeed!-C.C. [Amazon Prime Member-Reviewer]

Laurens watch, in opposite, requires manual switch to dive mode but gives you ability to control your session start-end(excluding surface time-above 1.5 meters) and provides depth reading to whatever below 1 ft, - to me more fun..

As I am a cheapo who doesn't do enough diving to justify an expensive watch, I thought this watch could be useful as a basic rough depth and time indicator. As a watch it's fine, however if I wanted something that was just a watch I'd have bought just a watch, or if I wanted a watch that spewed out random numbers I'd just have bought a calculator watch and periodically mush buttons randomly .The first day I got the watch I decide to test it in my 1.7m deep pool. Bam, turns out my pool magically grew to 2.9m! And then shrank again on the second dive down 1.6. After that they were within .2m. I could live with that. Easily.The next inaccuracy was the day afterwards. Let's go for a freedive I said, it'll be fun I said, we can know roughly how deep we go I said.As soon as I entered the water and was making my way towards the site, the dive mode kicked in. The mode that's only supposed to turn on when you are below 1.5m of water. I was barely below the surface, in all seriousness the watch would have been, at a maximum, 30cm (1 foot for you imperialies) below the surface.So how do I know how far down I went I hear you ask? Literally no idea is my reply.On the next day of christmas, my dive watch gave to me a stuck-in button that was faulty. (Read to the tune of 12 days of christmas).As I'm not a complete cretin, and I like to get my moneys worth out of things, I always rinse off my gear in freshwater after going for a splash in the sea. This watch was no exception, I dunked it in a bowl of freshwater and pressed the buttons. Later that night, as I was dozing off, I checked my watch for the time. And it was blank. Turns out if you hold a button in for a while the screen turns off. This isn't super fantastic if the buttons are prone to sticking when accidentally pressed. Which they are on this watch.On the plus side I ordered if with Amazons express shipping and it came so much earlier than I was expecting. That's where the extra star comes from!So in conclusion. If you want an oversized time telling piece that also has the date, a stopwatch and a countdown timer that all work fine unless a button sticks, this is the watch for you. If you want to accurately measure how deep you've been and how long you've been under for, it is probably worth spending a bit more money. I've been trying to learn for so long that usually buying cheap means buying twice, but I love a bargin.ThanksAndrew MortimerEDIT!Wow, so I've now had this for 2 months, and, apparently, for the last 24 hours I've been under 3.3metres of water. Honestly, what the s***? Watch is clearly buggered and I'm about to begin the long, arduous and, most likely, unsatisfactory process of getting my money back. Damn you Pyle!

reviewText: I buy everything I review. To receive FIVE stars, a product must meet >90% of the manufacturer's claims. I don’t subtract because I don’ t like the color or appearance (too subjective and personal). I review form, function, ease of use, and construction quality. Please forgive typos: I’m an evidence-based scientist, NOT a typist. If you find my review helpful, please click "YES". This helps me improve future evaluations (which I do for free to help people make more informed decisions).Their Claim:  Bottom timer with watch functions and depth gaugeMy Verdict (details below):  True but with some major flawsIt's a watch, stopwatch, thermometer, countdown timer, and has dual time zones. All #'s are large enough to find and works very well. It's even stylish to wear as an everyday watch. I like the looks and these features work exactly as designed.Next, the dive component. When you go into water, it automatically changes to DIVE mode (which you can also go to by pushing the MODE button, generally to review your dives). When underwater, them mode button won't switch to any other function. It has a water sensor, and when submerged, the watch believes you are diving, and locks it into that mode. Come out of the water, and you can toggle between modes again. That is a bit troublesome as you can't tell what time it is underwater, or view the stopwatch (so, if you want to spend six minutes at a ship wreck then do something else, or you know you have to be back at the boat in 30 minutes or they're leaving without you, you can't time yourself that way; plus, you can't toggle to the time of day under water). That shouldn't be the case. But it's not a deal breaker, more of an annoyance.When you are in the water and go to about three feet, the BOTTOM TIMER (BT) starts up. That's pretty great at this price point. It works exactly as it should. But here's the problem. If you're diving, then come up to snorkel on the surface to a different dive spot 100 yards down the coast, or come up for ANY reason, the BT stops. When you go back down, it starts again from 0:00. So, on one 2 hour dive at 30-feet, during which I came up a few times to speak to my dive buddy, each time we went back down this unit THINKS it's a new dive. By the end of the two hours single session dive, it had seven recorded dives. They're numbered and easy to scroll through.The problem is that to use a dive table to calculate RNT, you need to know how LONG you've been underwater (total) and the maximum depth you achieved. To figure out your BT with this unit, I had to add up each BT from all seven dives it thought I took. Again, not a big deal, but it SHOULD have an ON/OFF button for the diving function, and simply record one dive as, get this, ONE DIVE. That is, if you come up after 7:35 to get something from the boat, when you go back down, it should start at 7:36, not 0:00. It would be SO simple to do that. In fact, when in DIVE MODE, none of the buttons do anything. So, why not assign this function to one? I guess they don't want you pushing buttons underwater as that can compromise water tightness, but it should be doable. That's my major issue. One dive is one dive; not seven or seventeen.The depth is a bit off. In a 17 foot pool, when placed on the bottom, it recorded 13.4 feet each time I brought it down (very consistent, not very accurate). That's not quite accurate enough for diving IMO.The temperature gauge seems pretty close, but I didn't know the exact temp of the lake or pool, so I can't speak to it's veracity.For the price point, this is an AMAZING deal. I'm only going on dives when on vacation, so it suits me perfectly. But if I were a regular diver, this would not suit me at all due to the BT issue, and the depth gauge being inaccurate.In reality, when I go on Caribbean dives, I usually submerge and ascend just once, so the BT issue won't be arise. Even if I made multiple ascents, I can add the dive times together at my leisure later when I get home. But if I need to know under WATER how long I've been there, which is important when you're approaching decompression time limits, this simply doesn't cut it.For the casual diver like me, this works. For a regular diver, you're going to have to spend $200+ for a real dive watch.One other thing. Having a rotating bezel on a digital watch (bezels are designed for analog watches only) is like having a tampon dispenser in a men's locker room: I mean, what's that all about? They're trying to be cute, and it doesn't work. It has NO purpose on a digital watch. None.

reviewText: I bought the silver band watch for my granddaughter who is a great Justin "Beaver" (her pronounciation) fan.  The watch did not work but since it was on sale and the store was going out of business, I figured it was simply a dead battery.  BUT - TRY GETTING TO THE BATTERY. There was nothing in the package to show you how to replace the battery.  Now, I've had enough watches to know that usually you have to remove the back.  But, you have to first, GET to the back.  I managed to remove the pin from one side and then came the fun part; getting the back off.  I tried twisting it off - many of my previous watches opened this way - but not this one.  Finally I found a tiny little "lip" on an area of the back piece. So, I used a jeweler's screwdriver and lifted the top right off.  If only there had been diagram it would have saved me a lot of time and a lot of scratches on the back of the watch. Luckily,  you can't see them with the band on it.  Assuming that the battery is the issue - this should be a nice watch. It's cute and my g.daughter will love it just for the image of Justin.  She has a learning disability and being able to use an LCD watch will make it easier for her to tell time.  By the way, I bought this watch at K-Mart and their RETAIL value is only $9.99 - I got it for 40% off during a sale.  There's no way it retails for nearly $30.00 and it certainly isn't worth that much.
summary: HARD to open and replace battery

reviewText: Excellent fit. Could be warmer. Hood works well with helmet. Good for lots of snow. Pockets need more lining for electronics safety

I ordered a medium and am 5'6, 155 lbs. Naturally, when I removed the removable fleece liner, the jacket was baggy and noticeably baggy visually. The fleece liner fit perfectly. In most cases, if you're wearing such a heavy, weather-proof coat it is expected you will wear lining that will end up filling up the empty-space that has been built into the coat. With that being said, the size I ordered fit great for me.Recently went snowboarding for 8 hrs in 25-32 degree weather, and felt warm from beginning to end, from sitting idle to boarding (which tested its warmth during windy conditions). I wore a UA long-sleeved compression base layer (not cold gear) and t-shirt.I fell quite a few times, jerking my body every which way, and sweat quite a bit. After it was all said and done, I hung up my coat and  it looked the same as when I got it in the mail. There were no scratches, rips, unraveling threads, and after letting it air out, it didn't smell (from sweating), although that isn't an excuse to at least launder the fleece liner.The luxury of having several pockets on both the outside and inside of the jacket for different purposes with waterproof zippers is fantastic.The best part is I don't expect to purchase another coat for a long, long time, which makes the price ($243 for black medium) of the coat justified. reviewText: A very sleek and low profile watch that looks good with formal wear too.I use mine for circuit training, jogging, swimming and daily wear.Its very simple to operate and has essential functions like;- dual time- snooze alarm- timer with repeating option- stopwatch with lap recall- night mode*I wonder why casio does not make watches with night mode, night mode is a basic feature in every digital timex watch which allows the user to operate the watch in darkness easily. Any button pressed will illuminate the screen and dim after xx seconds.Pros- very affordable- sleek and low profile- easy to operate- lightweightCons- an all black version ie black panels and buttons would have been perfect- can't find any yet....SummaryBuy this watch if you are looking for a sleek workout watch which is affordable and easy to operate.**Update on 5 Nov 2012Ahhh...the indiglo doesn't work anymore!Whether its "button activated" or "night-mode activated"...it's gone....I will not be not sending this back for warranty because I live half the world away from US.This is my 4th Timex, but I guess I will  still buy Timex because the operation is very user oriented.

This is probably my fifth or sixth version of this watch. They have lasted from two years to about four or five years and are generally quite reliable.I wouldn't have needed a new one except when I removed the last battery, I couldn't get the buttons to work when I put the thing together!Each time I buy this watch, it tends to get a bit better. The exception is that the previous version had small buttons that looked like they would fail (they did) and required you to push fairly hard (they were undersized).Anyway, this version has nice improvements. The buttons are bigger (too big, IMHO) and easier to push. I haven't had any issues with them being overly sensitive as other reviewers have. I wear the watch on my left wrist a little below my actual wrist. The buttons that could prove troublesome are on the left edge of the watch and wouldn't be an issue unless you wore it on your right wrist (and had big hands). I have had to adjust to light pressure on the buttons, though.The alarm is louder than the last version and the indigo light works on the numbers rather than illuminating the entire screen. I have only used the alarm and chronograph (with split times) and both work just fine. I took previous versions diving (they are not diving watches) and they survived. No reason to believe this version would be different.All in all, I am quite pleased with this version!

reviewText: I thoroughly enjoyed my watch at first. However, I work in a profession where I wash my hands often, and my watch has gotten moisture under the face of the watch and it's now foggy. Very disappointed for a waterproof watch.

The last three (all purchased through Amazon) have gone from shoddy to worthless. I give up. I will never buy another one. I set up the day, date, timers, alarm, etc. I then headed out for a run. reviewText: This is a nice watch. Has all of the functions that I wanted, looks nice and pretty light weight. It is fairly sleek and I haven't had any trouble snagging it on things. Two minor, unexpected observations: The orange is darker (less bright) than I expected and it seems to get dirty easily because of the color. Not a big deal to me, but was not expected.

The Timex Men's T5K608 is an absolutely excellent watch in most regards and at just under $30 a great bargain, but overly sensitive buttons were a deal killer for me.On the positive side- This is an incredibly comfortable watch to wear. Not only is it super light, but Timex has done a simply brilliant job with the band.- The numbers are big and easy to read- The backlighting works well- The watch looks good- Having an extra time zone available at the push of a button is a major convenienceHowever... The buttons are very sensitive and not recessed so if you are active, or wear the watch while sleeping, you may find it switched to a different mode. I've awoken to find the watch showing Japan time and looked down while doing an obstacle course to see the watch had switched itself to a countdown mode.I wanted to love the Ironman but ended up returning it and getting aCasio Men's DW5600E-1V G-Shock Classic Digital Watch, a roughly comparable watch. The G-Shock is $10 more, lacks the two time zones, has smaller (though perfectly legible numbers) and wasn't as immediately comfortable as the Timex. However, its buttons are recessed and stiff so there is little chance it will put itself into the wrong mode, and I get the sense that it is a generally more solid, shock and wear resistant watch. Much as I liked aspects of the Timex, the Casio is a better watch for me.
summary: Excellent Watch Marred By Overly Sensitive Buttons

reviewText: I am a bit of a watch "junkie" and the Timex Ironman has always been a favorite. This is a nice, sleek watch that works just fine for daily activity as well as timing my workouts and training.

I've had it for two days and compared it to my Casio Men's DW5600E G-Shock repeatedly. I just like this one better and I'm shocked - no pun intended. Durability is the biggest question in my mind - so time will tell - but at least I can read the numbers on this easily and user interface is awesome - better than expected on a watch at this price.Here's what I really love about this watch:- 50% lighter than the g-shock- Sightly thinner - it's close though- I can actually read the numbers - my eyes aren't what they used to be and the Timex numbers are a good 50% larger than my g-shock.- Fantastic contrast of numbers against background: much better than my g-shocks - the background is whiter - so easier to read.- Smoother, sleeker design and a few mm thinner makes all the difference with my dress shirts - I think it's the sleekness more than just being thinner. It doesn't 'catch' on my shirt sleeves - which I find very annoying about my two g-shocks unfortunately.Additional Pros- Buttons are easier to work with than the G-shock. (could be a con though - we'll see)- User interface feels more modern and intuitive.- Dual time zone and easy, intuitive switching is really nice- Band is thinner and seems a better fit for my thinner wrists- Band lock: I was annoyed at first like some else said. But, now I really like it. It locks in the band strap nicely so there's no movement at all. If you're someone who removes your watch a lot, you may be annoyed. If you don't, you'll probably love this.- Indiglo 8-hour night mode is pretty cool - jury is still out on this one - but I think I like it.- Very inexpensive - disposable in fact.Cons- Buttons are easy to press. It's more of a 'pro' for me right now but I just bought this a few days ago and can see how it may become a 'con' like some other reviewers mentioned. Time will tell and I will definitely edit my review if this becomes an issue. At the moment I like how much easier they are to deal with compared to my G-shocks.- Durability: potential con - I couldn't find any reviews addressing how long these last. This feels less substantial than your average g-shock watch. But, they're super cheap so even a couple of years would be nice. But, the g-shocks last forever and even if you beat on them, they still look great. This one - I don't know - I hope it proves to be indestructible like the g-shocks but it doesn't feel as industrial strength. Time will tell. It's so light, maybe it just feels less rugged comparatively but it will be just as good.It's a keeper for now - but if the watch face (acrylic?) ends up being anywhere near as rugged as the G-shocks - I'll be a very happy camper.

I have owned three Timex Expedition watches over the last 5 or 6 years and I really like them.  When the display on the latest one decided to let go, I decided to try the Ironman instead.  After a couple of weeks, I have decided I like the Expedition better.A definite "pro" on this watch is the display has excellent contrast and is very easy to read, especially when using the Indiglo backlight. The top button will change T1/T2 when held down, and this will happen even for innocuous actions like putting your hand in your pocket for a few seconds.  On the Expedition, the top button turned on the Indiglo, so it wasn't as big a deal.On the other hand, if you actually use the lap timers, split times, etc. quite often, you might say this is a "pro" as they are very easy to activate while wearing the watch.Switching between the two models can be confusing due to the different button layouts.This is a good watch, but if you are already used to an Expedition model, you might want to stick with that model instead. reviewText: I admit my fascination for watches is a weakness. I just need one - but I have several. If it were only about telling the time I should have been satisfied  long ago. But as I said, I have a weakness.Up to now I have aspired to Swiss luxury. Pressing my nose on the jewellers window along with other noses beside mine - contemplating what might be - with a small mortgage.But then came the Timex Ironman. Inexpensive, practical and with all the functions anyone other than an Astronaut / Pilot or Deep Sea Diver would need - it caught my eye, my curiosity and my wallet.The idea was to buy a watch that would serve for outdoor knockabout stuff free from the fear of scratch, bang or bust. That was the idea.The reality is a timepiece that works - at work or play. It is light, it is functional and it is accurate. Some reviewers here have complained about the side buttons which they say are easy to set off by mistake. To be honest I haven't found this a problem. The timer is useful for eggs and the alarm is helpful for life. It's waterproof and the beep is good too - if you like that sort of thing, (which you can switch on or off), like an electronic cuckoo chirping on the hour through the day. (It doesn't do it at night so as not to disturb). So far, it has proved to be robust and easy to wear - which is why it's become a easy companion. It isn't too large and it isn't too tacky. In fact it has a smooth and smart black finish - with a clear and visible screen - which works well for the city and the park.All in all, it's an easy recommendation. Tick tick. Tick.
summary: Light, durable and accurate. An ideal companion

reviewText: I wanted this product to solve my problems - and it does serve to hold up your strapless garments - with auxiliary damages that I alluded to in review title. Product design of bra strap + pin fasteners is a much needed, compact way to fasten garments without the bulk of separate safety pins. Tried this product for the first time on a new dress ($150) and new bra ($30), for 6 hours of wedding festivities. Unfortunately, when removing my dress at the end, I noticed that the brooch pin had caught and dragged on the silk interior of my dress.  Also some pin damage to bra.  Of course, fabric tears and ladders would have been created by safety pins. This remains an issue to be resolved and, obviously, it's terrible to ruin expensive, new garments.I'll be specific in hopes that the product might be improved... hoping so, because I'd be first in line to buy!ATTACHMENT PROCESS = 3/5The metal hooks that attach to the bra tend to be wider than some bra strap loops are made, so it took careful stretching and slow application.  After attaching the metal hooks, the bra goes on and dress over that.  To pin yourself (rather, your bra) into the dress, it's easy to get the front but requires some contortion (or some help) to get the back fastened and length of strap adjusted.FUNCTIONALITY = 4.5/5Keeps the bra from slipping and showing out of the dress.  Keeps both bra and dress in position.COMFORT = 4.5/5Minor issue of rhinestone straps creating imprints on your skin, if you choose to shift your strap at all.AESTHETICS = 5/5Definitely dresses up your look.OTHER = 2/5Brooch fastener can drag on silk fabric, similar to the wear of a safety pin.
summary: Meets needs, but tears up silky fabrics

reviewText: These boots appear to be well made and tough, while at the same time they fit perfectly and are very comfortable with a nice big toe box. I have an off-label purpose for them: I live in the California foothills and take my dogs for long walks every day in rough terrain that includes a reservoir, lots of hills, rocky slopes, dust in summer and mud in winter, foxtails and Velcro burrs at least half the year, and rattlesnakes. Ordinary hiking shoes and boots get penetrated by the rouge-fine dust and the foxtails, attract the burrs like magnets, and provide little-to-no protection against the rattlesnakes. These high-topped rubber boots, though never intended for hiking, give me exactly the walking gear I need for my daily excursions through tall dry grass and into the shallows with my dogs. I can't say yet how long the boots will put up with the kind of flexing associated with walking up hills and around steep slopes, but I can say that they aren't pinching or causing blisters. They aren't made to breathe so my feet get pretty hot but--with hiking socks over thin socks--they don't rub anywhere, and hot is better than all my alternatives. I fold my jeans around my ankles and pull the outer sock over the fold to keep the socks from walking down my heel and that works fine with these boots. They have a comfortable sole insert, though I will probably replace that with some orthotic cushioning. Good product, good price!

Most boots do not have enough support for me and before I've walked to the barn my back is killing me. The top of the boots is just about mid-calf for me.At first I thought I was never going to get my shoes pushed inside them, but they did indeed finally slip in.  I would hate to have to pull the boots on and off shoes all the time though.  I just put an old pair of shoes inside the boots and leave them there.Pros:* Thicker than most overshoes, like the kind usually just pulled over dress shoes.* Good traction.Cons:* Hard to pull over shoes if you are going to do it on a regular basis, though other people might have more strength than I do and not find it so difficult.* The fasteners are elastic loops that fit over "buttons" on the shoes... the first time I pulled on one to fasten it, the loop went flying off and under an entertainment center!  Just be careful when fastening the boots so you don't lose the loops!  For myself, I'll confess I don't bother fastening the boots.  They work just fine without doing so.Overall, I would recommend these boots, especially for someone who would like more support than most boots have.  Just find an old pair of shoes... the soles were coming off the walking shoes I put in mine, but it doesn't matter since the boots are waterproof and hold them in place.  When these wear out... and I expect it will take a long time before that happens... I'll be looking to buy another pair!

reviewText: A few months ago, I bought the Heritage Extreme Winter Gloves and was very disappointed in them. They were stiff, took a while before they warmed my hands up, and they were too bulky. Last month, I discovered these DuPont ComforMax gloves, and fell in love instantly. These are without a doubt the best winter gloves I've ever worn. They're extremely soft, durable and warmed my hands up within minutes, keeping them toasty the whole time I kept them on. I don't care if these are made for skiing or anything else- if you need gloves for the winter months, these what you need!According to the tag, ComforMax Classic gloves have 4-5 times more fiberfill layers than other insulation. Each layer is just 5-10g/sqm. Seriously, it feels like you're wearing a blanket on your hands when you feel the inside of these things. I've let a few other people try them on and some of them gasped, remarking how soft they are. It might sound dumb to be praising gloves so much, I know. But these things are just too good! The leather exterior is smooth as heck and moving your fingers around is simple. With the Heritage gloves, I felt like my hand was doing more work than it should just to do simple things like reaching in my pocket. Here, I can pick things up easily and even zip up my jacket. For gloves this big, that's impressive. The outside of each glove is very well-padded too. I tried punching a hard wall with them on and it felt just like my old sparring gloves by Everlast. Trust me, your hands are safe with these puppies on.So they're super warm, super soft and flexible...so how come I'm not giving them a full 5 stars? Well, I was actually on the fence with this, and if Amazon let you give half stars, I'd totally give these 4.5 out of 5. There are two small things keeping them back from a perfect score for me. One being the high price and the other being something that's kind of my 'fault'. First, you get what you pay for with these, though I wish Amazon was selling them for a bit less like they do with most other things. When I found these in a store last month, they were 2/3 what they cost here. Chalk that up as another missed opportunity in my life. As for the thing that's my fault, it's the fact that I have, as others have put it, 'piano player hands'. My fingers are thin, and even with the small size of gloves, there's a tiny bit of room inside. I don't know if this is a result of that or not, but there's also some excess fabric around the tips that makes it hard to pick up small things. If you have regular hands though, this should be a problem, and neither of these should prevent you from buying these.I can't say enough about the ComforMax Classics- they're amazing! I can't wait to give them a shot this winter if it snows.
summary: Nearly flawless gloves for cold days.

Since I stuffed far too much change in my Hatsune Miku wallet of the same style, it tore. The wallet was still functional and after almost two years of use, I decided to buy a new wallet. I learned from my previous hinged wallet that I shouldn't throw a bunch of change into it. If you're like me and really don't bother to use change, I'd advise getting a separate coin purse. I'd hate to see this wallet share the same fate as my previous one. There are plenty of pockets for credit cards and whatever other cards you may have. reviewText: I tried this at the Penny Arcade Expo today in Seattle, WA and they were quite fun. The demo lady was an expert at them. My lucky self got to use the new Necomimi ears while I was volunteering at Comic Con Chicago 2012. Since then I have been a little obsessed with them.In case you have not heard of these http://www.neurosky.com/necomimi/Default.aspx is the website. These are, for the most part, mood ears. They move in tune with your emotions.They are hysterical. Oh. And they really work.They don't work when you move your forehead muscles. (I tried.)They don't work on a timer. (I timed it.)They don't work by your temperature. (I'm always hot.) At least it seems that way to me.When I wore them a year ago people would ask me questions, when I did not know the answer the ears gave me away. When I got excited about something - you just had to look at those ears wiggle. I couldn't even get sad wearing them. I tried - people asked me to. I couldn't! I was too happy wearing these ears! I couldn't even really tell they were on my head except for the whirrrring of the ears when I was excited. The ear clip and forehead node I didn't even feel. I wore them for pretty much for four days straight. I only didn't wear them on the train home because that's all Chicago needs, more train crazies.A couple days ago for my birthday, my family finally got me my own pair. Playing with them again, I can tell still hear the 'whiring' of them on my head. That seem to be the only downside to these. They are so fun to wear. Oh - another one is I would not suggest getting them wet, as they are mechanical.Of course I checked out what www.Pawstar.com had in terms of covers. Black, pink, leopard, fox, perfect - now I can get rid of these white removable ones that come with the headgear. And of course I'll make my own ear covers. ;) I'm the kind of girl that will wear these to the grocery store, clothing shopping, and showing them off to all my nerdiest friends. All the while telling everyone what a great product they are, as long as the ears match my outfit of course.

This is definitely the perfect gift for any girl.I regret that I did not order at once two pieces (second item will be delivered soon).High quality and good looking thing. reviewText: Followed the advice of other reviewers and ordered one size smaller than my normal 10.5-11.  The 43's were pushing against my toes and had to be returned. The pedals and cleats are very well made, including a tight fit when you get them locked in.  The value is especially surprising, with the pedals almost like a free bonus.  I would even recommend them to Cycle/Spinning Class students (these are the SPD clips needed for most Indoor Cycle classes) as they are less expensive than any separate shoe/cleat combinations I have found.  Keep the pedals, so when you are ready to take your cycling to the street (or dirt), you can put the pedals and and use your shoes for both.If you're still reading - SPD style clips/cleats/pedals are generally considered for "mountain" bikes, not for serious "road" bikes.  While they can be used for either, I like the "mountain bike" style shoes because they are more comfortable if you spend any time walking in them.

I saw this watch advertised in a sporting magazine and immediately fell in love with it. As other raters have commented, the watch looks great, and has usefull bells and whistles, albit perhaps not the most accurate, according to some of the reviews posted here. One GLARING erroneous marking that I noticed right off has me rather puzzled, and I'm thinking that there is perhaps an explanation for it that I'm not aware of. The watch has a non rotating, fixed bezel, which has the usual 360 degree compass markings, ie: 00 indicating North, is at the top 12:00 position, 180 indicating South, is at the bottom, 6:00 position. So far so good. Where it goes weird is all the other markings are on the wrong side of the bezel! Just to the RIGHT of 00 (North), are the markings 330, 300, and 270...indicating North-NW, West-NW, and West, at what should be 90 for East. To the LEFT of 00, are the markings 30, 60 90, indicating North-NE, East-NE, and 90 for East. It's easier to see if you just click on the picture of the watch for the enlarged view. See the 270 at 3:00? Should'nt that be 90? And so on. It's the same in the magazine pic. I never noticed it in the pics, only when I had the watch in my hand did it jump out at me. I apolgise in advance if I'm missing something here regarding electronic compasses...I tend to beleive that this has to be the case as something this glaring would have been addressed by now. Otherwise, appears to be a solid watch, and I would have given it at least 1 additional star had it not been for this quirk.UPDATE: 1/4/2013...I'm giving the watch an add'l star (to 4 from 3)as the issue with the compass markings has been resolved. See post from Victor Diaz in the comments section for the explanation. As to the accuracy of the compass readings, in my experiences I've found them to be spot on(save for the inital confusion with the bezel markings). Same with the barometer/temperature readings...although in the temp mode it's best to remove the watch from your wrist for a minute or two, then take the reading, otherwise your body temperture will affect it by 5-10 degres. If left in the temperture mode, the watch will continue taking multiple readings, eventually displaying the actual air temperture after a few minutes. In South Fla the terrain is pretty much at sea level, with the watch consistently displaying readings of 100-125' below sea level, which would be erroneous, but then again for my purposes, I don't need it to be more precise than that.
summary: Puzzled By Compass Markings AND UPDATE

reviewText: I searched a lot for an analog/digital watch and settled on this one for three main reasons:1.  It has a second hand, which I need for my job.2.  It has a large digital display, which is easier on my aging eyes.3.  It has a solar powered battery, so I don't have to take the back off every year to change a battery.I wasn't too sure about not having a crown to manually set the time, but the automatic adjustment feature worked very well, you just choose a hometown near you that is listed around the watch face and it automatically sets itself.  I did notice it was about two minutes off, so I used the manual adjustment feature and it has been right on for a month now.  Both the analog and digital times match exactly.  The solar power feature works well too.  With normal wear, it gets enough light to keep itself charged to the H level.  Hopefully the solar battery will last for many years.The altitude/baro/temperature/compass features are cool, but I really have little use for them.  The altitude sensor works off of pressure, so you have to calibrate it to get an accurate reading.  I would think it would only be accurate for a few hours after you calibrate it or until the weather changes.  The temperature feature is nice, but you have to take it off your arm for a few minutes or the sensor just reads your arm temperature.  The compass feature works well, I've used that a few times now.  The second hand spins around to point to magnetic north (or true north if you change that setting) and the digital display gives you your bearing from north.I like that the crystal is recessed a bit into the bezel.  It should help protect the face.  I have no scratches at all so far, and I'm tough on watches.I found the manual to be very well done.  The print is very small, but I downloaded a PDF to read it better.  The explanations and examples are very well written (not like it was translated from some other language).  It only took me about 10 minutes to get it completely setup when I got it (set the time and date and the various pressure/altitude units and all that).  The watch has so many functions, but navigating them makes sense once you figure out the button sequences and use it for a while (all the functions except Comp/Baro/Alti are accessed via the Mode and Adjust buttons).The light lights up the analog face very well at night (the 5 minute increments and the hour/minute/second hands glow in the dark, but not for very long).  But the light doesn't light up the LCD display at all, so that part is useless at night, if that matters to you.  The watch is also a bit thick, so it stands up off my wrist a good bit, so I can get a normal shirt sleeve over it.  Probably just as well, since a shirt sleeve would block the solar charging (although it is supposed to last 6 months on a full charge).  I'm not too sure about the band either.  It's plastic and feels thick enough to last, but I take it off at night, so time will tell how well it holds up.  The band also has a raised part at the end of it to hold it in the keeper.  This is good if you wear it all the time so the end of the band doesn't pop out, but it makes it a pain to take the watch off.  I may just take a knife and shave that raised part off.Overall, I really like this watch.  I've had it for a month now and have had no problems with it.  I give it 4 stars instead of 5 mainly because the LCD is useless at night.  It would have been nice if both parts lit up.  I'm also not crazy about the plastic band, but I suppose I can change it if I need to.

*** Update 5/2/13*** It is a pleasure to report that it has been almost 4.5 years and this product is still working flawlessly. I used it on a 5.5 mile run and it is as good as the day I got it. See comments to this review -- others have made good tips that I agree with. The bottom line -- if you are still using it after this amount of time, you are either ready for an upgrade or at least won't mind having to buy another unit!Original Review:I'd hoped that getting this new running gadget would encourage me to exercise more often. So far so good. I asked for this for Christmas and, well, it has accomplished it's primary function for me... I've been running almost every day since I got it. I was turned off by the gigantic size of some HRMs, and did not need something to keep track of splits as I run on my treadmill at home and the gym.As a heart rate monitor, the functionality is pleasantly simple. It tracks your heart rate for the whole workout. You hit the big button to start, and it goes to work tracking the length of time, the average heartbeat, and the peak. While you are running, it displays your current heartbeat. That's it -- but sometimes it's better to keep it simple.I should point out that, as a watch, the watch piece tells the time and date only. If you want/need splits and a stopwatch, you should look elsewhere.Here's some other thoughts: I was worried that the strap would break but realized after a couple workouts that I was probably wearing it a little too tight. Since adjusting, it is much more comfortable, has not fallen off, and, as a guy, you *almost* forget that you have it on. My wife cracked up when I took my shirt off after a recent workout. She said that, from the back, it looked like I was wearing a bra (or Manzierre, or Bro, if you prefer).I had no original intention of wearing it while NOT working out, but I've found it addictive, and have enjoyed observing how drinking a cup of coffee while sitting at my desk does raise my heart rate about 10-15 beats per minute on average. Also, as I've started to get in a little better shape over the last 3 weeks, I see that I have to run either farther or faster to get my heart rate up to certain thresholds. And, now my heart rate does not go up as high from merely climing the stairs at home. I believe that these insights, among others, are very encouraging for someone who is just getting back in shape. The encouragement aspect combined with the simplicity makes this a great starter heart rate monitor for anyone considering.
