reviewText: My daughter loves this coat.  It is very light, I'm not sure it will stand up to the Midwest winter, but so far so good!

I live in New England, and when I took the jacket out of its packaging the first time, I thought "there is no way that this is going to be warm enough" - it is the lightest winter coat I've ever purchased. However, it works great, as the jacket is not only warm enough, it is really good at regulating your body temperature.  It takes about two minutes to warm up once I step outside, and I don't overheat as quickly once I get my blood moving.  I also like the thumb hooks for the sleeves to prevent drafts and snow from getting in, as well as the lined pockets.  It also cuts the wind well and keeps you dry.  The outside fabric has a very subtle pattern to it, so it is not just basic boring black (up close anyway).  Altogether, I think the omniheat lining explains both the light weight and the temperature control, which is great because the lack of bulk keeps you from looking like the Michelin Man, and contrary to another review, the omniheat lining does go down the sleeves, nearly to the wrists.  That said, I would have preferred a hood that was a) removable, and b) that had some kind of string or toggles to tighten it.Size-wise, I am a 14, and an extra large fits fine with a sweater on underneath.My one concern about this coat is that the outside fabric is so thin and seems like it may be a bit snag-prone, so I have to wonder about durability.  We'll see how it holds up to wearing a cross-body bag daily, and to the washing machine, but I'm hopeful that this coat will be as durable as my other Columbia gear.
summary: Amazing technology with a few design flaws

This watch simply does not have bright enough lights to beat sunny outdoor conditions.  This is a major limitation.Buttons feel a little iffy, but not too bad.No instructions included.  Ok, it's a digital watch and doesn't take a lot of figuring out.  Still, I expect at least a barebones starter guide with something like this.Unique choice of display functions.  You can cycle through the time, the date, and the seconds on the minute.  I would frankly prefer an actual stopwatch feature over that last viewing option.Update September 2013: I decided to tear this watch down to see what was in it.  It does in fact use LEDs, the effect I described previously is caused by a red film which helps diffuse the pinpricks of LED bulbs into more readable lines.<del>Finally, I have a lingering suspicion that this is not actually "LED."  The style of the time being displayed reminds me much more of a traditional bedside clock.  Still, I don't have anything to really bases this against so that could just as easily be my own ignorance.</del>

Setup was simple, the book was easy to follow, the watch is comfortable and the chest strap stays in place throughout my runs/jogs.  Some people say that it takes a while to start registering a heartbeat, but I just run my fingers under the tap for a second and then place the water collected on each of the chest contact points....simple as that.  I don't use gels for that....a drop of water on each point does the same thing.  All considered, I am very happy with this setup and have ZERO complaints about it.  I'm not an athlete, just someone who is interested in focusing my cardio a little bit better to enhance weight loss efforts....not training for marathons here. Once I decided to get a HRM I decided on three main criteria:  I wanted a large display so it would be easy to read; I wanted it to have a decent interval-training option; I wanted it to be reasonably reliable.I couldn't find any good master comparisons of all the current watches, so I decided to start with the large display.  I figured it would be easiest to get large numerals on a vertical display, so I did an image search and tracked down all the HRMs with vertical displays.  I read reviews and manuals on these, and checked the reviews at various sites.  I also did searches for reviews which mentioned interval timing just to try to ensure I hadn't missed something.  A different (more recent?) version of this watch, the T5K545, came out on top.  The proportion of dissatisfaction in the reviews is at the lowest end of the range for this price bracket, and it had the best interval setup I could find with a large display as well.I didn't notice the difference and bought this version of the watch (the main difference seems to be in the type of chest strap it comes with).  I have had the watch for a month and am very happy with it.  The HRM works exactly as described.  The watch is easy to read and has good flexibility in terms of setting up what is shown on the display.  The interval timer includes 2 programmable workouts, each can be set for up to 8 intervals with beeps at the change, and the workout sequence can be set to repeat if you like.  These intervals can be set for specific HR zones, and if the HR alarm is on, the watch will give distinctive beeps for being above or below your target for a given interval.  I have found the HR recovery timer to be very useful as well.  At some point I will probably program my own HR zones rather than use the watch's built in zones which are set up according to the standard percentage of max HR.I found the watch easy to set up but I read instructions and don't usually have problems.  I can think of people who wouldn't want to mess with it, so factor that in if you're not comfortable playing with gizmos with a lot of options.When I first got it the tap feature did not seem to be working, but after setting it to the highest sensitivity and learning to touch it with 2 fingers and a quick tap it's working fine--it almost seemed to need to loosen up a bit.The watch is huge.  If you don't care what it looks like it works fine even on very small men's wrists.  Due to the fixed angle of the band coming off the case it's not going to look fully at home on even the largest wrists but that's something few will notice on the large wrists.A note about heart rate zones.  Although the idea of training according to zones is very appealing, finding out your real maximum heart rate in order to set those zones is problematic.  The common age-based formulas give you an average which may be as much as 20 beats off your actual MHR.  Timex has a 'Tools for Success' brochure with an exercise-based process for figuring out your MHR which offers a nicely different approach.  Ultimately, unless one wants to use a doctor or try one of the radical strategies found on the web, one has to watch for things like how your workouts affect you, how well you recover, etc., and adjust accordingly.

reviewText: This is a solid Timex heart rate monitor (HRM).PROS...Lots of functions and very easy to use, especially if you are familiar with Timex watches. A button on my previous Polar RS300X broke into.  I have had excellent luck with other Timex watches and am expecting the same for this one.CONS...The TIMEX HRMs use a different transmit frequency than other HRMs.  I have used two others (Polar and Omron) and they used the same frequency, so I could interchange the strap/transmitter or watch and it would work.  Also, the spin bikes at the gym were set to the same frequency as the Polar HRMs, probably because they are more prevalent. One minor complaint is that the transmitter and the watch take different batteries.  Both are common, but it would be nice if they were the same.  Finally, do not get this HRM if you want something petite. This is a big HRM, but I like it that way.

I used Polar HR monitors for years. They worked fine but they were expensive and battery replacement required mailing both the strap and the watch to an authorized repair place, paying money, and being without them for two weeks or so. The last time my Polar battery failed I bought an IsoKinetics HR monitor. That just didn't work. I ended up returning it with the help of Amazon (IsoKinetics didn't want it back until Amazon "encouraged" them.) With my fingers crossed I bought this Timex one. The first time or two the chest strap didn't make good enough skin contact but after it got some sweat on it it started working. (Polar is the same in this regard.) The display is big and clear enough to read at a glance while running. The buttons work fine. The wrist unit is convenient enough to put on and take off. It's fairly nice looking but big. The reading seems accurate. You can replace the chest strap battery yourself. The wrist unit battery can be replaced by a local watch repair store (you don't have to mail it somewhere). Two shortcomings compared to Polar: the reading isn't detected by some exercise machines that will detect Polar readings, and it has no extra features (no average HR, max HR, zone, etc.). You can display the duration of the current workout or the time of day by pushing a button, but that's the extent of its "features". Overall I'm very happy to give up the features in return for the substantially lower price. When I started with Polar years ago I used all the features just to entertain myself during the boring job of working out but after I got used to the features I stopped using them. What I really need is just to know my heart rate during exercise and this Timex model does that job very well.

reviewText: It shows your heart rate and the length of time you have been working out during the workout. After you turn it off, you can see the length of time, the average and the highest heart rate of your last session.It is simple to use and gives you just the basics, which is all I wanted.

This is a farce of a Heart Rate Monitor this does not count calories burned or Duration or anything other than give you your hrear rate. The Best Buy goes to the Timex Personal Trainer T 5g971This will cover target heart rate recovery heart rate Calories burned and Average heart rate. For the same price! And the strap is better smaller etc.
This is a useful tool to use when exercising, especially for cardiac patients who are doing rehab programs as required by their doctors.
All I wanted was an HRM that was economical and worked.  Great for basic training.  I love the simple operation.

It is a piece of junk. The chest piece is very difficult to put on and when it is on it apparently is doing it's job but the wrist piece does not seem to get "the Message". When I get on a piece of cardio equipment in the gym, that has a built in heart rate monitor, it picks up "the message" from the chest piece immediately and reads my heart rate---and then after 30-60 seconds the wrist  unit finally begins to read my heart rate also. I would not recommend this product to anyone.
My husband likes the many tracking items: heart rate avg, high and low.  More options than his previous Bowflex monitor.
I wear this Heart rate monitor for , biking, running, also at the gym. Purchased it about  5 weeks ago Great so far.

Maybe it's my age or my stroke but I can not even get the time, day, and date to set to the correct numbers.  I've been trying on and off for a few days but the watch just will not do what the instructions say it's suppose to do.  I'll keep trying of course but boy,  it's exceedingly frustrating.  This watch is suppose to do amazing things.........a digital heart rate monitor, an interval timer, a chronograph, alarms, and of course, a large digital read out of time with second hand, day, and date.  I don't like the feel of the heart rate monitor strap because it is very tight on my large frame.  The watch is also water resistent to 100 meters and has a terrific indiglo night light.  At this point, this watch is useless to me until I can figure out how to get the watch to do the primary set up.  And one more problem is that the wrist strap is very small.  It's really meant for a tinier woman.  I will probably end up giving this lovely watch to a little niece of mine who will probably figure it out quickly and who is small enough for the wrist strap.  I honestly think this watch is fabulous but it's not made for everyone....me in particular.... so if you are tiny and have lots of patience give this gem of a watch a try.  Of course, I am not positive it's all my fault for not being able to set it up properly so if it's a malfunction of the watch, that is an entirely different story.
summary: It's beautiful but oh soooo complicated!

reviewText: My wife has been using this watch for about a month now.  Its face is easy to read, and it has the usual features one expects to find in a digital watch (alarm, stopwatch, etc.).  This one also will monitor heart rate.  It seems accurate.The watch seems fairly solidly constructed and should withstand the rigors of a basic exercise regime.  It has an adjustable fit strap and is comfortable to wear.In all, it's a good basic watch for someone interested in being able to monitor heart rate while exercising.

Sporty and stylish, this is perfect for the gym or while out jogging. The watch is not heavy and made of a durable resin material in the band. While it works as a full featured watch the main reason to get this is for the heart rate monitor and calories burned readout. While many training machines like the treadmill have bars you can grip that will then give you a readout for heart rate results can vary from machine to machine. The watch allows you to get consistent readings from whatever type of exercise you are doing. Looks-wise this has a fun sporty style. The color on this is closer to a magenta whereas in the picture is looks a tad more purple. Overall a good item for those who regularly exercise and go to the gym.

A disclaimer here. I'm a writer and I have very little patience with poorly written instructions. And if ever there was product--handy, attractive, not too expensive--that deserves decent instructions, it's this one.I have but 28 days to review this product. . . and I may just figure it all out in that time. But it shouldn't be that hard. Instructions need to be arranged first things first.  So, first how to set it to measure heart rate, then information on setting time. And it needs to be step-by-step.Mind you, I love digital watches. I have had at least two dozen in the last two years--one in practically every color of the rainbow and many different manufacturers, including Timex. So I'm not unfamiliar with how to set these guys. But this one has more features so it is naturally a more intricate process. And that takes me back to my original statement: A product this good needs either better instructions or better design.I may end up just using it as a watch and ignore the trainer features altogether.  I mean, I do love the color!
Great hrm for the money. Just very confusing if you just want to know your calories you burned with a normal workout.
summary: Good for the money, just a little confusing

reviewText: This heart rate monitor/watch has lots of features:  monitoring of time in your HR zone (beeping if you go under or over), lap count, calories burned, recovery timer, etc. All that is great, EXCEPT when you have to figure out how to use all the features. The thick instruction booklet made me dread figuring it out, and the instructions were complicated---even to set the watch.  That, along with having to wear wet and wear the chest strap, seemed a bit too much trouble.  I kept asking myself, "Is all this really worth it? Don't I already know if I'm working hard enough based on how I feel?"  Well, the truth is that knowing I am not in my target zone does give me the incentive to push myself a little harder.  Even so, I'm not sure it's worth going to the trouble of strapping on the chest strap for every workout.  On the plus side, the watch is lightweight and a cute pink (so maybe not so great for men :).
summary: Does the job, but the instructions are too complicated

reviewText: This watch is nicely sized for women.  The belt is not too big and the watch is not too clunky, in fact it is pretty stylish looking.  This is not a completely bare bones monitor but it is simple enough so that anyone can use it for tracking their workouts.  But it does more than that and it's not all that hard to figure out how.  The instructions are clear and useful and I found it easy to set the watch up for me.  The review feature is nice. You can also download more information from the website including a very useful manual called Heart Zones Tools for Success that is very helpful in estimating your maximum heart rate and helping you to increase your fitness and reduce your weight.  [...]  I find the monitor complementary to using RunKeeper ap or MapMyFitness ap on my iphone and keep a log on a spread sheet that includes data from the monitor and data from RunKeeper.  My log keeps me motivated.  I would recommend this monitor to any woman who wants to improve her fitness.
summary: This heart rate monitor/watch is just the ticket

reviewText: As other reviewers have mentioned, this can be a bit of a bear to set up....the instruction manual is massive, the print is tiny, and it takes forever to get through all of the steps, but once you have everything set and calibrated and ready to go, this is quite a nice little device. I especially like the indiglo feature.If you have the time and the patience to work your way through the instructions, then go for it. If you're easily frustrated, you might be better off looking elsewhere.
summary: Frustrating Instructions, But A Worthwile Product.

reviewText: Is a great product, and it's beautiful as well so you can use it for everyday not just the gym

Got this via Prime, and it is perfect for me-- helpful in my exercise program ensuring everything is In proper limits.It is a little complicated to program, but whenyou get into it, it goes quickly.Helpful info as you run or whatever you do!Pretty in pink, you can be fit and in fashion!An excellent product! Well worth the price!Ellen George

It seems it doesn't sense well under the water. I have seen 30 bpm and I know that I cannot reach that level because I have a pacemaker implanted which is programmed to stimulate my heart if it drops below 52. The strap is comfortable and the watch cute but I think the software is not well designed. The bottom at the upper left corner doesn't have too much to offer, neither the lower at the right. I haven't had patience yet to set my heart zones. It doesn't have gps but I knew this when I bought it and I don't like too much the way to reset the chronometer. You have to press for a couple of seconds and when swimming that disturbs your rhythm. Despite all, I like the watch and somehow it accomplishes my needs. I will try soleus or garmin.

The chest strap is comfortable and the monitoring device rests on top of the strap, rather than being a hard piece of plastic against your skin.  Readings appear to be accurate, in comparison to the gym equipment I use that have a heart monitoring feature.  Watch is easy to set and program, AFTER reading the instructions.  The watch has many features besides monitoring, and it can get a little confusing hitting "this button" two times for the chronograph or hitting just once for another feature, or holding "this button" until "this happens."  If you refer to the included instructions and cycle through the features a few times, you'll be just fine.  The watch portion is durable.  I like that you can still have the time showing as well as your heart rate.  My last monitor was one or the other.  The watch is not too bulky and comes in a cute pink color.  My only complaint is the plastic fastener that holds the watch strap in place.  It feels a little flimsy.  I feel that if I pull the band too hard to take the watch off, the plastic fastener will snap right off.

This is my first heart rate monitor training watch and I love it.Chest StrapI had concerns about the strap on whether or not it would be uncomfortable. I found out this is not the case. I can barely tell I'm even wearing it and it is easy to clean and remove. It doesnt rub my skin and fits well underneath a normal sports bar. (You dont need to purchase those special sports bars with the insert for this..in my opinion)WatchI read several reviews about the functionality of the watch to be confusing and annoying. I didnt find this to be true at all. It was very easy to set up my stats, clock my workouts, get my average heart rate, determine zones for maximum performance, etc and i didnt even read the entire manual. Just read the manual if you get confused. They have it all layed out.Negatives:I do wish I was able to track my workouts each week. There isn't a way to save the workout one day and compare to the next or to total the week and give stats. This is on the less expensive side of heart rate watches so I am happy with the way it is. This is by no means a negative to the product. Just my end user preference.Overall, great purchase. Very happy with my selection.

I work out 4 days a week for at least an hour. I'm very pleased with this watch. I have had other HRM (heart rate monitor's) before and this is by far the best especially for the price! I am not very techno savvy but once this was set up, it's pretty easy to use. I love that it has an alarm, timer, lights up, etc. Just a great product all around. And for the chest strap, I was a little worried about it. My other HRM didn't have a chest strap. But, I wanted one that did have one so it would be more accurate. You don't even notice you're wearing it. It is comfortable and moves/stretches with your body. And all this at a reasonable price. I've never been disappointed with Timex products and this watch is no exception.

This watch and chest strap provides much information about your workout.  It is a stopwatch, interval timer,alarm clock, and heart rate monitor all in one.  The user's manual is detailed and easy to follow, which makes setting up your heart rate monitor to your specific preferences is simple.  You can also indicate your gender and weight and it will tell you the amount of calories you burned during your workout along with you minimum/maximum/average heart rate.  (I do not believe it is 100% accurate, but I appreciate having an estimate at least).  There is an option to have the watch chime whenever you are above or below your specified heart rate preferences, but I shut off this option.  Also, the heart rate monitor does not work unless you use the the chrono mode.  I almost always time my workouts, so this is not a problem for me.  Once you remove the chest strap (or it is 3 feet away from the watch), and leave the chrono mode, the data from your workout is erased so you might want to record it elsewhere if you are keeping track of this information.  The color, a bright pink, would not be my first choice, but it has definitely grown on me!  I have some concerns about keeping the chest strap smelling fresh as well, but that concern does not take away the value of this product.  I highly recommend it!

I might be naive, but I expected this watch to actually have a heart rate monitor somehow within the watch to catch your heart rate from your wrist (you know, like the doctors and nurses do!). But no, instead, you have to use this bulky/inconvenient and terribly uncomfortable strap thing around your chest, with this plastic device that snaps on, and then work the controls on the watch with that somehow relaying info back & forth. It's not even worth it to me! So, leaving that aside, how about the watch itself? Well, it's huge and looks like a kid watch on my wrist. Plus it's super thick. And then the rubbery watch band loop has a bump on it inside where you slide the slack through, so it's a total aggravation to take it off because it catches on that thing and does not want to come through.The watch itself, functioning just as a watch, is fantastic. I love the color of the LCD (to me, it appears to have a dark purple hue to it). I also love the Indiglo which looks awesome. I love the features this watch has (general stuff like alarms, and the stopwatch that goes to 99 hours!!!)Also, being that it's Ironman, my lifelong favorite watch brand, it's durable and feels like it will last many years.I am just kind of torn on whether this is really a worthwhile watch to have because the heart rate monitor aspect is useless to me, and that being said, it would make more sense to just simply buy a watch by itself.I guess it just comes down to a person's personal preference on this, perhaps.Also, I am including two pictures (above) so you can see just how big this really is on me!

I'm a runner and triathlete and was curious to see what kind of uses the Timex Ironman Road Trainer watch could be used for. I currently use a Garmin 610 (with HRM- heart rate monitor) for running and biking and a lesser version Timex watch for swimming. I was hopeful this would combine the information for all 3 sports while I'm saving for the Garmin 910.To start with the watch comes with a HRM and a strap and a very thick instruction booklet. Since I already owned/used a Timex watch for swimming, I was familiar with the settings. Even so, it took a bit of trial and error to set the time/date. The directions were not helpful in how to set the watch, especially since you have to use a button they don't refer to, to actually save the settings. It's not too hard to figure out but annoying that it's not intuitive or easy to follow the directions.Right away the wristband is stiff and difficult to manipulate. The watch face is also bigger than my other Timex but smaller than my current Garmin 610, to give some comparison. It makes a nice in between face size. The Timex works by storing "lap" data and displays the current lap number and time. Click the "mode" button and you are in the "chrono" setting - which is where the time and lap number is displayed.The stop/start and split buttons are pretty easy to find - the split button is the big pink one on the face. Sometimes while swimming I find the split button to be tricky though. I'm not sure how hard I have to push to record the lap but push too hard and it records more than one lap. So I usually waste several seconds (wait 8 seconds after pushing the split button and the time resumes while showing the lap number) to ensure I only pressed hard enough for one lap to be recorded.The pink Timex offers more options than my other one - namely interval timer and a heart rate monitor. The strap and monitor are built similar to my current Garmin one. The interval timer is meant to remind you of when to run intervals - or can remind you to eat/drink or any other alert you'd like. I find this a bit difficult to set but once I did it was a nice reminder if you want one. I found the Garmin settings easier and more intuitive but once I figured out the Timex ones they worked just fine.Now to the meat of the watch - the HRM. To use the strap you have to wet the plastic probes and place them on your diaphragm. This isn't a monitor of a wrist pulse. I found the Timex strap to be stiff and it chafed me badly. To be fair, I chafe easily but the Timex strap was so stiff I was almost bleeding. To see my HR I had to set it up on the watch and tell it what was a resting HR and recovery one. I already knew what my HR zones should be but the booklet offers no help there nor were the instructions that easy to follow when trying to do this. After a bit of messing up and wanting to throw the watch, I eventually figured it out.To see the HR while running or biking you have to push the HR button. It's not that big of a deal. The watch is also set up to beep at you when you're above or below your designated HR, which is nice. As a HRM it works decently and accurately, if a bit painfully due to chafing. However as a run or bike watch, I found it nearly worthless. It's not GPS based so it doesn't count laps while running or biking. You have to already know when you hit each mile and without a gps, how would you know that? It's just a timer, which is helpful when swimming but not helpful when running or biking if you're going for a certain distance. If you want to run or bike for a set time (say 30 minutes) then the timer may be more useful.Overall this watch's effectiveness and usefulness depends what you want it for. For serious runners/athletes I can't imagine it'll do much for them without the added GPS function. It's limited in the data it offers - timing mostly - so it limits the usefulness of the watch. I find it only useful for swimming. If a casual gym goer wants a HR monitor as the primary use, this could work but other than that it's a more expensive swim watch that offers interval alarms. At best it's a backup swim watch for me.
summary: Depends what you want to use it for...

reviewText: Perfect for keeping time intervals and monitoring my heart rate. Exactly what I was looking for and works each time.

Timex is known for affordability and quality so I was looking forward to trying the Ironman Road Trainer. But as much as I wanted to love the Timex T5K722F5 heart rate monitor I feel it has a lot of drawbacks.As noted in the product description this is a strap on heart rate monitor. It includes a black strap, pink watch and thick instructional booklet. The first issue I found was with the strap. Other resin Timex watches have a soft feel to them but this one is stiff making it harder to strap on and to unstrap.The booklet it comes with tells you how to workout within your optimal heart rate, however, it does not tell you what that heart rate should be. Instead it tells you to refer to another online digital booklet to get this information. It shares this at the beginning of the book under resources and that section was easy to miss. In fact, I did miss it and had to thru the book several times to figure out where to find this information. This should have been included in the booklet.Next the Ironman does not share calories burned. It simply gives your heart rate and beeps if you go over or under. This would be fine if the unit was simple to operate but it is not.  I also did not feel the light up "indiglo" feature worked well. Sometimes it lit up when pressed, other times it did not. And when it did light up the face was hard to read. The buttons to set the watch were hard to press.As a watch, the Ironman's face (when not lit) is very clear and easy to read so it does get a big plus for that. And though I prefer black others will love the hot pink Ironman strap.Overall, I feel there are better choices for a heart rate monitor with more features at this price point.

I had a timex ironman in the past and loved it.  I use this watch to see what my heart rate is doing my workouts.  When starting the watch, the heart rate display is immediate.  It amazes me how fast the chest strap transmit to the watch.  I have tested my heart rate with the machines at the gym while wearing the monitor and they are no exact but very close (usually off by 1 or 2).The one thing that I'm not thrilled about is the heart rate monitor strap.  It seems thin.  When wearing it during exercise, you can hardly tell it is there.  The strap got curled when I first wore it and now the wrinkles seem to be permanent.It is awesome at telling me how many calories I just burned!
summary: This is an awesome watch for what I wanted.

reviewText: I do a lot of running, but I also love weightlifting, so I find it's hard to get a watch that calculates heart rate and calories burned for both of these activities. However, I absolutely love the Timex Ironman Road Trainer.First off, the watch is great to wear all day.  It even offers an indiglo night-light which makes it easier to see when dark.  But when you use it for training, it's super easy to use. It does have a lot of features, but if you read the manual, it's very easy to figure out. The chest strap is easy to put on and after pushing one button on the watch, it is synced up.  In Chrono mode, the watch times your activity, tracks your heart rate, and when your activity is complete, simply hit review and all the stats are there for you.  It shows you your average heart rate, time in Zone, and calories burned.I previously used a Polar t40 heart rate monitor and never thought I'd find something similar, but Timex has really stepped into the heart rate monitor market with this one.
summary: A great timer and heartrate monitor

reviewText: Absolutely love this watch and monitor...skipped the strap and used it with my  heart rate bra. Works like a charm. Definitely recommend.
I teach Spinning and Tabata and love it for these classes.  I also use it for my own Cardio workouts.Wish the light was brighter when trying to read it in very low lighting in the Spin Room.

This watch worked perfectly for approximately 2.5 months.  Thereafter the buttons....one-by-one......stopped working:-(.  Really liked it, but have to purchase another (different) one.  Feel lost without my HRM.

I have the same watch in men's, and got this one for my wife. The watch itself is a great item, I have used a Timex Ironman for years and the quality never ceases to amaze me. I do like the heart rate monitor on my watch (it's an older version) better than the one on this watch, but it still works well. Does what it promises.

First of all I'm not a major fitness buff.  I work out moderately because of age and aches and pains.  This band was sweaty on my wrist.  It would be better if it had some sort of cloth material.  It also came with a thick book of instructions which made me cringe so I'm still not sure how you use it.  I never seemed to get my heart rate up high enough for anything to register. I love a good workout but due to knee problems I have to keep it moderately light.  So this wasn't of much use for me.

My wife field-tested this for my review and found it as good as the Polar she uses. It is well-designed and well-made with careful attention to all the details that can become irritants when she's yoga-ing, dancing or lifting weights. It does its job without involving overkill features and too many controls. She is very pleased and rates it just a little below her Polar but well worth buying. As an outside observer and not a user. I like the balance between form and function. It is clearly designed for function -- monitoring, displaying and calculating -- without looking ugly and attractive without being a glorified fashion accessory.A nice product.
summary: Good value, well made and reliable

reviewText: Very simple to use, good information, big enough numbers and buttons that you can use it while working hard without risking an accidental deletion of your data.

I have been using my Nike Fuel band which has no HRM (Heart Rate monitor) for quite a few months while shopping for a HRM. So when I saw the availability to review this watch I was excited, plus they had the watch in pink wow. I couldn't wait to get this item.The packaging was fantastic, the corrugated box along with its packaging protected the watch from hurt harm and danger...LOLEach component was wrapped separately, the sensor, watch and band. The manual was tucked neatly on the side of the box and when I pulled it out I thought OM to goodness do we need this much instruction. I opened the little book and it has 200 pages, luckily only 43 of the 200 pages are for US/Canada residents. Still excited because now I only have 43 pages to read before I can get started playing with my new toy.Two weeks week later, I am still reading and fiddling with this watch, why you ask? Well the instructions are so complicated that its annoying, and confusing. Umm let me rephrase that, its not complicated the watch has so many functions Digital HRM, Time of Day, Chrono modes, Interval timer, Recovery, Review, Alarm, HRM Setup, and User Info which is way too confusing for this non-tech savvy user.So what do I do I had it over to my wife who is tech savvy and has the mental capacity and the stick to it stuff to set this up for me in no time. Well my Amazon consumers it has been a week and she still don't have a clue how to get this thing to do what it needs, so for me its just a watch with a back up light, several other functions that are no good to me boo-hoo!Today I took the watch out again because I had to write this review, not wanting to be beaten by a PINK HRM watch I tried again as of today all I can say is I LOST, the PINK HRM watch beat me.

When I opened the box, the first thing I noticed was the bright pink color. I love pink and my running shoes are neon pink so this was perfect for me but if you're looking for a watch you could wear both for exercise and everyday wear this might not be the best choice.Setting up the time was a bit confusing and the included manual was necessary. The reason I was excited about this watch was it would be easy to track my heart rate while I ran. Once set up it is easy to determine your heart rate but the heart rate monitor is uncomfortable. You have to wear it on your upper chest and it didn't really fit well over my bra. Once it was on there were various ways to track my heart rate but I was so distracted by the sensor I couldn't concentrate on my run. I may get used to it over time but it is a bit annoying. Other than that, I like the watch.I've worn it to work at a retail store and it hasn't gotten in my way at work. I would not recommend it if you're looking at it for a heart rate monitor since it is uncomfortable but as a watch with a timer it's great.

Received this watch from Amazon Vine today, and have been enjoying the learning process immensely. I have to admit that it did take me a while to figure out how to set it up and I don't think I quite understand how the chromo business works entirely, and it took me way to long to figure out how to get the annoying too-low/too-high beep to quit.  I am not entirely sure I understand all I need to, and that will take some time, so this review is far from finished. However, this amazing gadget monitored my heart rate on my afternoon bicycle ride, warning me to slow down when I was going at it too hard to be smart and, ah c'mon,  it let me know beyond a shadow of a doubt that I was way too lazy on that one hill. This gizmo has more bells and whistles than my first car, and for a serious workout person, it will become invaluable. For me, not so much. I am of an age where I need to pay attention to such things, as my heart rate, but I can only use it some of the time. I swim and do aqua aerobics and discovered in the fine print of the instruction manual  that, while it is waterproof to some 60 PSI of water pressure, I cannot use it as a heart rate monitor when swimming laps or exercising in the pool. Evidently the heart rate reader and the watch don't communicate well through a viscous medium like water. But for my bike ride and aerobics classes it will be perfect, and certainly far more accurate than counting my carotid beats for 15 seconds and multiplying by 4.  Like every Ironman watch I have ever had from Timex, however, I had best keep the instruction manual handy when it comes to to switch off Daylight Savings Time. The last Ironman watch I had came to a bad end.  I smacked it with a hammer in frustration and tossed it in the trash after several days of trying to change the time. I hope this one will be easier to reset. Will continue to experiment with this Ironman Road Trainer and will report my findings.Timex T5K722F5 Women's Ironman Road Trainer Heart Rate Monitor with Resin Strap Watch, Pink/Silver Tone, Mid-Size

This monitor is fantastic!!! It's a little complicated to set everything up - there are LOTS of screens - but it just takes a little patience. But after that, it's easy to use, the dial is big enough to be read easily, the chest strap is comfortable and I hardly notice I'm wearing it. No need to buy anything more expensive or more complicated. This definitely does the trick AND makes working out more fun and more productive!

You can store just about everything in this watch. The problem is, it takes a long time how to and where. The instructions don't give you a thorough step by step walk through. Mentions alot of interval setups but doesn't explain the purpose of it and why it's important. It just explains you can store calories and such on it but doesn't show you how. Very confusing and frustrating to make all the features work. I'd like to use it during my workouts but I take a long time figuring out how it works.

I have used heart rate monitors for my exercise for a long time. This has the great features of a timex watch as well as a good HR monitor. the chest strap is comfortable and picks up the signla very clearly. It is easy to setup and the HR is available at all times when you are wearing the chest strap. It's fun colored sports watch to wear alone and a great HR monitor during your workouts. Price is right too!

reviewText: After my old heart rate monitor watch finally bit the big one (the strap cracked) I shopped around looking for a new HRM watch.  I use  an app to track my GPS location/speed, etc so was able to not require that feature as well which would have bumped up the price.  I have been using this watch now for almost a year and love it.  I use it when running to track Heart rate and when swimming to time and track my laps.  No issues with using it in water as it's an "ironman" watch whereas my older HRM watch that was supposedly water proof to 30m had to spend several days in rice after my first attempt to use it to track my laps when swimming.  Easy to input your personal data, change settings, and use.  The ONLY complaint I have is that it doesn't have the memory to store more than one recorded workout at a time, so if you don't write down your data after every workout you lose it.

reviewText: From my wife Sarah: I wanted to have an accurate heart monitor to use while exercising. I thought this looked great, but I'm disappointed in it. Here's why:- It comes with a chest band that you must wet and wear around your chest to get your heart rate. This is not mentioned on the product page. I thought this product would take my pulse at my wrist, and work through the watch only, but it doesn't. I don't want to have to use a chest band. That's just way too much complexity and effort for me.- The band had a problem. It stuck, and it was really hard to get the watch to unlatch and come off. I was close to having to break it to get it off, but finally got free of it.- The directions are super complex, and it's way more work than I thought I was getting into. I exercise very moderately, and thought I was getting something simple and easy to use, but perhaps someone who's into more intense exercise would like it as it is.Personally I won't be using this.

I picked up this watch for my wife to use while running. She wasn't sure about it at first, but after we set it up for time/date and she tried it on, it grew on her. reviewText: I truly had high hopes for this watch, even after reading quite a few bad reviews. I figured I would give it a try, but to give you a bit more of an insight this is my background experience:- Web Developer (so yes I code and a lot) it's been more than 8 years doing so.- UX and Interactive experience- Tech and Gadget junky- Watch collectorThose four are my most relevant skills and hobbies to what follows:The watch itself if good looking but the build quality for the price tag is like any cheap plastic watch you can get for a lot less, still the good looks kinda let that slide. Functionality seems decent while it's working, but it seems to be a common issue for this watch to disconnect from the phone and that's when hell goes loose. After it disconnects (which you wont notice until you hear/feel your phone and not the watch) trying to reconnected in some cases (happened to me and to a lot more people for what I found online looking for a solution) is almost impossible unless you open the watch take the battery out and short the watch to hard reset it, not without having to also go through all this (copying and pasting from the seller support).1) If your watch doesn't immediately reconnect with your phone - DO NOT*  Press and HOLD the CONNECT button for >6s to put your watch into pairing mode.*  Forget the device from the app.*  Forget the device from IOS.INSTEAD:*  Press and release the MODE button (colored button on the top right side of the watch) to wake the watch.*  Tap the "LINK" icon in the app corresponding to the device in question..This should trigger a device reconnect.  If the reconnection does not succeed after several attempts, then:*  Power off/on the Bluetooth of the phone and tap the "LINK" icon again.*  Kill the app and re-launch it, then tap the "LINK" icon again.Only if all of the above fail, should you initiate the pairing process .2) If your watch is in pairing mode (e.g. all of the icons blinking) and that your phone can't find it - DO NOT*  Perform a "Hard Reset" (e.g. removing the battery) unless all other options have been attempted.*  "Reset all settings" on your phone unless all other options (including a "Hard Reset") have been attempted.INSTEAD:*  Forget all devices from the COOKOO app.*  Kill the COOKOO app.*  Forget all devices from the Bluetooth settings of the phone.*  Power off/on the Bluetooth of the phone.*  Restart the app.If the device does not appear in the list of devices:*  Check with an app such as "LightBlue" that the device is "discoverable"*  If it is not, then perform the "Hard Reset" procedure.If the device does appear in the list of devices, then proceed with pairing.3) If your watch is in pairing mode (e.g. all icons blinking) and that you see the "Pair/Cancel" pop-up appear then disappear immediately - DO NOT*  Keep trying to "catch" the "Pair/Cancel" pop-up before it disappears - you'll just frustrate yourself.*  Perform a "Hard Reset" (e.g. removing the battery) unless all other options have been attempted.*  "Reset all settings" on your phone unless all other options (including a "Hard Reset") have been attempted.INSTEAD:*  Forget all devices from the COOKOO app.*  Kill the COOKOO app.*  Forget all devices from the Bluetooth settings of the phone.*  Power off/on the Bluetooth of the phone.*  Restart the app.4) If you want to turn off your watch at night or in an aircraft - DO NOT*  Press and HOLD the CONNECT button for >6s - this will put the watch into pairing mode and force you to re-pair it.*  Forget the device from the app - this will forget the device information and force you to re-pair it.*  Forget the device from IOS - this will forget the device information and force you to re-pair it.INSTEAD:*  Press and HOLD the CONNECT button until you hear the first beep (approx 3s).The Icons should all briefly flash, then the screen should clear and be entirely blank.5) If your watch is OFF and you want to turn it ON - DO NOT*  Press and HOLD the CONNECT button for >6s - this will put the watch into pairing mode and force you to re-pair it.*  Forget the device from the app - this will forget the device information and force you to re-pair it.*  Forget the device from IOS - this will forget the device information and force you to re-pair it.INSTEAD:*  Press and HOLD the CONNECT button until you hear the first beep (approx 3s).*  Tap the "LINK" icon in the app corresponding to the device in question..This should trigger a device reconnect.  If the reconnection does not succeed after several attempts, then:*  Power off/on the Bluetooth of the phone and tap the "LINK" icon again.*  Kill the app and re-launch it, then tap the "LINK" icon again.Only if all of the above fail, should you initiate the pairing process.So at the end the product doesn't even deserve a star, but the seller in my case was really nice 5 stars to the seller none to the product. Would definitively buy form them again just not this watch.

I bought this GPS on deal elsewhere. I was surprised by it being so deeply discounted being such a recent launch.After a couple of weeks using it I can see why.They propose a simple, no gimmick, product. The problem is that the user interface simply makes no sense.First, you have to active the GPS on every mode you use it. For instance, if you hold a button for a couple of seconds, it reads "GPS ON" but then you go to Bike mode and it blinks "Indoor", so you have to turn it on again (and every time you go to bike mode).As an occasional rider, I just want to know my speed and how much I rode. I assumed it would start measuring both automatically and pause when I stop. It doesn't.You have to go to the Chrono mode, start the chronograph, then go back to Bike mode and start the GPS again.Given that the GPS seems to turn itself off so often, I assumed that I didn't need to do anything once I was done riding my bike. Wrong again.The battery completely depleted in about 24 hours. I searched a forum and they said I had to hold the button that turns the GPS on/off for a couple of seconds so it turns itself off. By doing this, now it lasts many days in stand by mode.And also the manual is almost useless.How could they make something they claim to be simple so complicated?They have the chance to solve these issues, and improve the unit, with firmware updates. Much easier to find apps, and easier to keep track of apps that I'm not currently using.Having bluetooth on does drain my battery a bit, but not as much as I feared it would. I've had my pebble for about 5 months now and I don't know how I lived without it. The most useful aspect of the Pebble watch is as a triage device for your messages and calls. Scenario: you texted something to your girlfriend 10 minutes ago. Now your phone is in your pocket and your phone alerts you to a new message. Is it your mom with some urgent family news? Is it your boss saying you need to call him immediately? So you set down your coffee, fumble in your pocket, pull out your phone and unlock it to find- it's a text from your girlfriend that says "lol".So what the Pebble does is let you know immediately what the text is, what your new email is, who is calling you etc. so that you know if it's something you need to deal with immediately or that warrants a response.I know what you're saying, "But taking your phone out of your pocket or purse only takes like 7 seconds..."  True, but how many text messages do you get a year? Thirty per day would be around ten thousand per year. How many emails do you get? What about tweets or Facebook messages? Reminder and calendar alerts? Multiply that times 7 seconds and you can see how useful Pebble really is.Also, the Pebble has vibration, so if you are in a meeting, or in class, you can simply glance at your wrist to read your messages, without the conspicuous rudeness of pulling out your phone and reading it while someone is speaking to you.Of course, Pebble also has apps that can do other stuff: control your music, find your phone, etc. With the upcoming version 2.0 firmware apps will be able to do way more. And of course there are the hundreds of cool watch faces to choose from so the look of your Pebble stays fresh.My one negative on the watch is that it isn't very scratch resistant. If you get a Pebble, you should really get a clear screen protector from places like GadgetWraps.

The Pebble Steel just came out (which I just know I'm going to get) and I believe runs SDK 2.0 so you have more options as far as apps, not too mention it looks way more stylish.  The team who put this together looks like they really care about the product and it shows when you use it. There's a good amount of options out there, but Pebble stole my heart. I would recommend you check out a Youtube video of the creators, it'll give you more appreciation for the design process behind it.  Thank you!

I purchased this watch to pair with my Galaxy Note II phone so that I would not have to pull my phone out of my pocket so often when out and about, and not be paranoid about leaving it to charge when at home or in the office.My phone stays on silent at all times now, since any text message or call gives me a quite noticable (but silent) vibration on my wrist.  No need for the phone to ring.  And if I ever misplace my phone in the house, I just trigger the free "Ring my Phone" app and it rings at full volume regardless of the setting.I use three apps, all free: Glance, which provides an amazing information-rich customizable watchface (weather, time, date, numbers of missed calls, unread texts and voicemails - even a tiny number for the battery charge % on my phone); Notifier, which sends notifications for my apps to my watch (particularly my work email which is third-party); and the aforementioned Ring my Phone.  Glance also lets you pre-set six text messages that you can send to people.Just to test it, I left my charger at home when I went on a four-day trip out of town.  The watch stayed alive during the whole trip.  I've also used it plenty of times in wet conditions without any problems.

These things work well - meaning they do what they say they'll do - for a little while and then break.  The company has a totally dysfunctional "customer service" set up and all they can do, have months of very slow back and forth is send you a new one which also will break. If you want to know the basics of what this thing does then read some reviews.  I'm going to leave some feedback on what the reviews don't cover, mainly the 3rd party apps that you can install.  In short you can install 3rd party apps, they can range from apps that extend the basic functions like the music player or notifications, they can be simple games, even fitness trackers.  I was considering getting a dedicated fitness tracker at one point, but the price and limited functionality of current fitness trackers put me off, so I was pleasantly surprised to find the Pebble can do some of the same things.  I'm a fan of the user apps, while not all of the apps will be high quality, they are user submitted after all, you can write your own if you are so inclined.  The user interface isn't bad, you press the center button on the right as an advance/select button to drill down into menus and tick options with the top and bottom buttons on the right being for navigation or cycling through watch faces, the lone button on the left side is the back button.  The music control immediately picked up the 3rd party music player I use on my Android phone, PowerAmp without any headaches, however it would not show the song tittles like it would for the Google Play music player.  Also all of my phone notifications pass off to the Pebble about a second after they show up on my phone, I'll be able to leave my phone on silent from now on, which is a good thing because the ringer on my phone always scares me when it goes off. It is surprisingly novel to read the first few lines of an email and decide if I can let it pass or take action immediately, the Pebble is clearly a product of the busy lives that Millennials lead.I ordered a high quality screen protector because the poly-carbonate screen seems like it would be a scratch magnet.  Also I ordered a replacement watch band because I was expecting to hate the included silicone band, but it turns out I like the included band, it stretches a little so I can have it fit snug on my wrist without having to tighten it as far as it will go.  Also it came with a 30% charge in the box and is up to 80% after I left it plugged in for two hours, that tells me that the 150mA battery doesn't charge too quickly but instead charges quickly enough, it would probably be at a full charge from 0% in about 4 hours time.  You would probably get a days use out of half an hour to 40 minutes of charge.

The Pebble is a unique piece of technology. It has great capability and a great user interface. The display itself isn't that oversized like some of its competitors. It is comfortable to wear and all around a cool conversation starter. I highly recommend the Pebble to any watch or tech lover.

Let me start by saying I bought this product on a whim. I didn't have much confidence in it, thought it looked ugly, and I didn't think I'd like it. I was wrong. Once I took it out of the box it felt durable. Not great materials, but good. The Pebble feels like it can take a beating and I don't fear for it's well being like I do with my other watches. To my surprise the black Pebble looks great once it's on your wrist. It's comfortable and light weight. The screen is always on and if you tap  a button the screen lights up.The Pebble surprised me. It is not a luxurious watch, but it is fun and customizable. Hate the cheap and ugly band it comes with? You can change it. Bored with the watch faces it comes with? Go to mypebblefaces.com and download new ones. Think you chose the wrong color? Go here [...]The Pebble is a great watch. I would buy this product again and will recommend it to friends and family.
I only hope the iWatch has as many cool features and can do just as much if not more. the new os for it is great.

The watch has a nice sleek look, however, the positive attributes stop there.  With this watch, you can view your texts and can be alerted to an incoming call.  Other than that, you can't do much.  You cannot make a call or answer a call on the watch.  You can't write a message or text using this watch.  It does not appear that the technology associated with this watch has developed to the point where it's really of practical for most of us.
summary: Looks nice but can't do much...

summary: Very cool!! Bought it for my son

reviewText: This is a really good smartwatch that does deliver the goods.  I would not hesitate to recommend this for Iphone use.
summary: SMARTWATCH LIVES UP TO ITS NAME

reviewText: I managed to blackout drunk one night while wearing this watch. I had an after market band on it, but I woke up the next morning to find this thing in the sink, but not alone. It was submerged in a healthy amount of vomit with both bands broken off and missing the two little pieces that keep the band in place. I spent about and hour scrubbing this thing as hard as I could to get in ever nook and cranny to completely clean it and then let it soak in a bowl of soapy water for the rest of the day. Once it was spik and span again I proceeded to find if this watch was still ticking, and it was as it did the day I bought it. Afterwards I was able to run to Walmart and get a new band to place on it. I have a hard time believing that any other smart watch out on the market now could survive this and highly recommend this on for anyone looking for a durable smart watch.

PROs:All notifications on your wrist for either iOS or Android -- no more pulling out your phone during your meeting or whatever else (My primary selling point)Fun, cute simple games like asteroids, tetris, snake, other "Game and Watch Gallery" type of portsCan be useful to time workouts, runs, has a 7 minute workout appWater resistant up to a few feet, can shower with it, etc.Multiple day battery lifeBacklightFirmware is continuing to be updatedApp ecosystem is most robust for a watch that I know ofBluetooth 4.0 and LEDesign blends in well for most settingsCONs:Little bulky for my tasteBattery lasts 2-4 days in my uses, not 5-7 as statedApps can be hard to access, not a centralized system like on your smartphoneButtons are a bit hard to pressSome bugsNo way to respond to notifications or view past ones, although does support multiple notifications that you can scroll through, but only until you dismiss them
summary: Best available Smartwatch-- yet still for the early adopter / specific use cases.

reviewText: ....but now I'm wondering if this is worth it.  Yes, sometimes having notifications show up on your arm is handy...for me that is mostly when I'm home and I've left my phone somewhere else in the house.  But the limitations of this watch are upsetting. For one, not nearly enough cool watch faces.  No real apps.  No fully-featured alarm system (just barely functional). Special charge cable makes keeping it charged up a pain. Too expensive for what you get. This thing should be well under $100.  I can see no reason to buy the new Steel version of this.  Sad.So, after owning this for a spell, I have come to believe there is simply nothing useful in this swartwatch space.
summary: I have been a smart watch fan.....

reviewText: I got a black/black watch about 2 months ago and love it.  It's become my go-to travel watch since it looks great, is inexpensive, and allows me to switch time zones easily.  I also love being able to get messages while biking and skiing -- it makes communication with a large group during sporting activities much easier.

I waited last year to buy one because it appeared to be in its early stages. I finally bought mine about two months ago and love it!It is great to be able to see a text message on my wrist, rather than pulling out my phone. The same for CID information. So far I have not had any problems with it. Liked it so much I gave one to my son-in-law for his birthday. I have used the German web site to create several personal watch faces -- Special Forces for this old "snakeeater" and several firefighter ones for my firefighter son-in-law.I'm getting about 4 -5 days between charges with mine and I use it quite a bit. Many notifications from my iPhone -- news alerts, weather alerts, etc.Too bad there is not a slightly smaller one for my wife :-)

Love my Pebble.  This is sharp looking watch also.  I use it for tracking my cycling, but I like that it notifies me about incoming phone calls, I can read my text message and Facebook updates, when I want them.

Overall I'm happy with the product.  I didn't experience a battery problem as one other reviewer has.  My complaints are fairly minor and fixable.The good points:1. You don't have to reach into your pocket to see who is calling.  That's especially handy when you are sitting down in a meeting and your pockets are as full as mine.  You have the option to send the call to voicemail from your watch if the call isn't urgent.2. I find that I miss fewer calls in noisy environments since I can easily feel my watch vibrate.3. You can see text messages easily.4. It's extensible.  If you are so inclined, you can use the SDK to write your own watchface, though the iOS version isn't out as of this writing.  I thought I might add the moon sign to mine.There are a few things that need improvement.  Some of these may change as they provide software updates:1. Setting alarms requires a bit too many button presses.  In fairness, I'm not sure how you would fix this with the four buttons available.  Maybe a double press or pressing two at once.2. You can't set a timer yet.3. No battery indicator yet.
summary: Currently useful.  With updates could be more so.

reviewText: I bought my Pebble at the beginning over Kickstarter.Up to now, I found no problems with this smartwatch. I LOVE (!) it!!Especially since the last iOS 7 update.. now are working all the push notifications with all apps!
I got this for my husband and he loves it. He wears it and uses it all the time. We don't have anything to complain about.

Upgraded to this from Nike FuelbandProsEasy to setupSo much potentialNumber of apps and watchfaces increasing by the dayAbsolutely love the notifications on my watch instead of having to pull phone out to check (also a con, see below)Battery lifeWaterproof - so far so good in shower and poolIntegration with runkeeperConsStill early in developmentIts a very well known issue but notifications sometimes (understatement) drop from IOS (Deleted space like the recommend and try and clear background apps but still have issues with getting all notifications - IOS 7.04 Jailbroken)No activity monitor/pedometer integrated without having to be in exclusive app or companion running on phoneFinal PointLots of potential but I would wait until they integrate sensor on board in newer models. I returned mine due to the fact that their are no sensors, the notifications stopped working almost everyday. I moved on to a fitbit, but looking forward to the Apple iWatch!See my blog[...]
summary: So far so good - Lots and lots of potential

reviewText: the best smartwatch out on the market today and notifications are sent the correct way, battery life lasts a week on a charge.
It does everything it said it would.  I love it.  I would recommend this to anyone looking for a watch that alerts them.

This is the first product I have ever returned to Amazon: pinky swear! One star will have to do when zero is not possible. Impossibly dark screen, quirky and ill-conceived controls/apps. I own the Galaxy Gear and wanted a watch with similar functionality but without the constant need to touch/shake/rattle/roll to get the face to illuminate.

None of the apps designed for this watch works as they should, most causes it to hang. The screen is distorted (not flat / uneven) so when ever you look at the watch you feel it is not good enough to be a consumer product.Nothing really works except for multiple watch faces, and some of them display "data error" on the screen so that you cannot use them.This is something which should have never seen the market, it is still under developed.

reviewText: I got my first Pebble from Kickstart. It was so good and well liked, had to get another one for my daughter. After almost a year of use, I still oboe it. Have an expensive watch, that sits in the drawer. When I am in a meeting, the convenience of knowing who is calling or reading a text I received without the embarrassment of taking my phone out is priceless.

I bought this as a birthday gift for myself because I was intrigued by Pebble. Setting the phone up with my android phone was quick and easy. The next day though... the e-ink on the screen was a bit scrambled, but I found pressing the forward and back (or was it the top and bottom buttons on the right?) cleared the problem and I only had to do that once.It doesn't send me notifications for my work exchange mail, but other things (Gmail, SMS, Google Calendar) work great. Getting calls is funny because my watch will vibrate like crazy, even a few seconds AFTER I answer the phone. It can be a touch disconcerting when you are driving any your wrist starts buzzing, but overall I love this device.I had worried that keeping bluetooth on all day would kill my phone battery life, but that hasn't been the case. Actually because I'm not constantly checking my phone for messages and the like, by the end of the day I have pretty good battery life. I wasn't looking for an overkill type smartwatch like the Gear (which has a camera built in and you can talk to your wrist instead of your phone). I just wanted a watch that had a nifty watchface and can keep me alert to meetings I may have scheduled on my calendar.
summary: Nice to not have to check your phone every 5 minutes

reviewText: My son can now get text messages on his watch and change the pandora settings on his phone from his watch.  This is a real conversation starter and a lot of fun for an 11 year old.

My son loves it. It never fails usually his hands will be full when a call or some sort of message comes through and his phone will be in his pocket. Now he can see who is trying to get a hold of him and decide if it is important enough to address it.

Does everything it says it will. A mite fussy to set up and pair with your phone, but once done seems to work well. Battery life decent (5-7 Days) and apps reasonably varied. A very good first effort. Some day we really will have a "Dick Tracy", watch, but don't hold your breath!
The Pebble is great! It is so handy to have the apps right there on my wrist. I can't wait to see where this idea takes us.

I wear this watch everyday, and it is simply amazing!  It's wide range of functions make it useful for a broad range of people, and with 3rd party apps like PebbleTasker, PebbleCards, Glance and Pebble Notifier, it's versatility shines.  I use it all the time to set timers, and quickly check the texts I get. The ability to change the watchface, depending on your mood and how you want to present yourself, is a great plus.That being said, I think it really needs to mature for the average consumer.  With the software update (2.0) coming in the next few months, the pebble team will have polished most of the rough edges I've found with the current software.  Having development experience is a great plus since the sdk is open, and if you are a developer, or just like to code, I'd highly recommend getting your feet wet, because the api and documentation are wonderful.
Bought this for my son and his nephews. They do not like it. The concept is great. But its quality need  improvement.
we could never get this to work with our samsung galaxy 3Had to send it backDisappointing because this was a Christmas gift

i was a KIckstarter backer on this product.  Thought it would be a unique grown up toy.  I get lots of looks at the watch and comments from friends.  That's where it stops.  It works fine for cell calls and text messages, but leaves a lot to be desired on email.To date, I have received only two email alerts on the watch...then the fun begins.Try to reach someone at the company...forget about it.  there is no phone number...the company does not return emails.While i realize it is a start up, but they neglect the most important thing customer satisfaction. I love my product!!! it's such a fun device to use everyday at work or around the town. Thanks guys for such a great product

I really, really want to like the Pebble smartwatch.  I've been using it for three months now, almost on a daily basis in conjunction with an iPhone 5s.  I am running the most current firmware/software/etc.  It's just incredibly annoying that it loses connection with my phone so often.  Generally, twice a day I will have to go through some process that I still haven't completely figured out that includes turning bluetooth off and on for my phone; shutting down the pebble and restarting; restarting my phone, etc.When it works, it's enjoyable to use.  When it doesn't, it isn't that attractive of a piece of jewelry to wear.  I like that it has integration with things like map my run.  90% it works.  Sometimes it just freezes in the middle of a run.  They now have some other interesting apps like integration with evernote.  It's nice to look at, but in reality, I would always pull my phone out for something like this.I have one other problem that comes up from time to time.  For some reason, when it is paired with my iPhone, my iPhone can no longer make an audio notification for any app.  I've checked all the settings, etc and nothing seems to be wrong.  The only thing that works is unpairing the pebble and restarting the phone.  Not sure which device gets the blame for this, but it is annoying.So overall, I give the idea of a Pebble smart watch 4 stars and the execution 2 stars, giving it my total score of 3.I really hope apple eventually comes out with something that works better with an iPhone.I've paired the device with my wife's S4 for a couple of days.  It seems to work ok, but still loses pairing at least once a day.
summary: I like the idea of it more than the actual product

reviewText: This interesting idea was marred by the positioning of the watch as "e-Paper".  It was nothing of the sort - it is just monochrome LCD.  Don't be fooled - they are clearly trying to bank on the success of the Kindle Paperwhite.

I received this as a Christmas gift so I could silence my iPhone notifications forever and this product accomplishes that very well.Running firmware version 1.14.1Most of the negative criticisms I've read so far could be resolved if people spend more time studying the settings options both in the watch and on the phone.My negative comments on the watch are mostly very minor and should not discourage anyone from buying one.ProsA silent vibration on your wrist. The phone's vibration can be noisy especially on a table.Reading text messages and previewing E-mails is wonderful.E-Paper display is very easy to read and has a variable ambient light detector to change the brightness.Shake to activate the back light.Buttons instead of a touch screen. The feel of the buttons are very good.Do not disturb feature is available in settings- you can set the timeConsLimited documentation available for features and settings. You should spend time to figure out all the features.No Bluetooth disconnect notification. There is no way to know if you have lost your connection to your phone.The back light stays on only for 4 seconds at a time while you use it. There is no setting available to change this to make it last longer.The digital watch faces do not have a digital seconds indicator. Only the analog face has a seconds hand.E-mail notifications are only a preview. I wish I could read an entire e-mail if I wanted.The weather apps don't always maintain a live connection.
They took forever to update to 2.0 . when they did it stopped all connection to my android phone ,no tech support unless your a programer. Just wait for a better watch.

The last few updates have really made a big difference. The battery life is finally up to what was advertised! I charge once a week. You can now see multiple notifications, the two way apps are finally starting to come out, and they keep squashing bugs.

This seems to be a great concept, with an adequate implementation when it used to work, i.e. lots of bugs but it's new and coming from a bunch of amateurs, but what is going to kill it is that there is no support if/when it breaks.  I have the kickstarter model and it's dead, just a lump of plastic, and I can't get any sort of response from customer support other than an email with a ticket number.
summary: Great when it works, but it doesn't for long - NO CUSTOMER SUPPORT

reviewText: The case looks and feels cheaply made.  The four buttons don't always make contact when I press them.  The display resolution is OK, but just that.  It is certainly not up to the standards of a Kindle "paper display" and I was expecting lots better.  The band is unnecessarily thick.  This might have been done in the interest of stylishness and given the way the rest of the watch looks, why bother?  Granted, you can replace the band but...Physical characteristics aside, When I place my (pre) order many months ago there weren't any.  Today there are barely more than that.  You should check to make sure what you want is available and is usable.  For example, the is an app that controls music on your mobile device except there is no way to change the volume.  There are plenty of alternate clock faces and many are round with their sides cut off by the Pebble rectangular display.Some stuff does work. For example, text messages and caller ID displays just fine.  A few other things work, albeit with limited functionality as well.  The question is, do you want to have that stuff if it comes on a watch that looks and feels like a child's toy?UPDATE:  I must acknowledge Pebble Customer Service.  After a week they responded to my question about their return policy by sending me an RMA.  I will update the review again if I ever get my refund.

Simplistic in design and iOS and Android universality are what made the Pebble stand out more than all the other smartwatches. Rechargeable, water resistant and designed to fit standard watchbands, gives the Pebble even more flair. A one-of-a-kind watch that always have people noticing.

I like a lot about this watch and dislike a few things too. I've been dreaming of a smart watch for a while now and really wated to love this little guy. I do like the functionality, but the apps are kind of useless right now, I'm hoping they get better. It's a great watch, but I've found I often keep glancing at it even though my phone is right next to me. I assume I'll find it more useful when I travel, we shall see.
summary: I like it, don't love it

reviewText: UPDATE: After 3 months of ownership, I must lower my rating. While the watch is good and has much potential, Pebble support is incredibly poor. I state that it is nonexistent below and I wish there was a better word for how nonexistent. I have entered three support tickets to Pebble support. NONE of the tickets has even been acknowledged. I almost regret purchasing the watch because of the frustration with the lack of communication.WATCH THE SELLER. The max price of this watch should be $150. This is an item that resellers appear to purchase and then charge more than double the actual price for. If the watch is more than $150, just go to getpebble.com and buy direct.UPDATE: I have now had the Pebble Smartwatch for about 8 weeks. Here are my observations - firmware version 2. I would still purchase the watch today after my experiences.The good:The Pebble is mostly good at doing what it says. It can display any notification from my iPhone, and display weather and other information when running version 2. My experience with battery life is about 5 days because I have several apps sending notifications throughout a typical day. I do like the watch and the potential that is in the watch.I have silenced almost all notifications on my phone and prefer to receive those on the Pebble. This has made me more productive and increased my iPhone battery life by keeping the screen from being opened by me for every notification.Unlike the Pebble steel, the original plastic watch can take any appropriately sized strap. I swapped my strap for a quality zulu strap that is much more comfortable and fits my wrist better. there are many choices for an aftermarket strap.The bad:Pebble support is nonexistent. I submitted a ticket immediately after upgrading to version 2 about an issue I was experiencing. I have yet to receive a response two weeks later. I ended up solving my issue by resetting my watch to factory settings. I found this solution on Reddit, not the Pebble forums. Be prepared to search non-Pebble forums for answers to any issues you may have. If this seems daunting, do not buy the watch. It seems that users are typically on their own as Pebble does not appear to have a large support staff. Pebble leadership is also not very accomplished at PR or communication, but I understood that going in.The bluetooth connectivity has been spotty after an upgrade of the iPhone app to version 2.0.1. The watch does not reconnect reliably if you walk out of range with your phone (version 2.0 reconnected every time). To reconnect a simple click of connect to watch is required in the iPhone app. This is mostly an inconvenience, but frustrates me when it happens.
summary: Watch the seller - only buy if sold by Amazon.

reviewText: Pebble has a lot of bugs that need to be worked out and they don't offer live technical support nor do they respond to emails very well. If you do get a response, it will be generic at best. The watch didn't even come with a user guide. Just a watch and USB. You will need to download additional apps "httpebble" to get the weather to work and in some cases, this app. varies from watch face to watch face. After a week of frustration, I finally discovered some more satisfaction than originally expected. Once again, Pebble has some bugs when it comes to the iPhone, and don't expect any customer service. I was able to get multiple email addresses to notify to the Pebble. The bug in the programming is to set only one email address to "ON" in "Notifications" and use "Alert" Style. Apple is going to do it's best to cause difficulties with Pebble and Bluetooth with anticipation of launching the iWatch before the end of 2013. I hope the Pebble competition will keep the iWatch price in check.
