I wouldn't suggest paying more than $150 Since that's what they cost.  But I love mine it was a Christmas Present sure I didn't get it until recently but its been a month now and its working GREAT!  I wasn't super fond of the watch band that came with it but that's easily remedied with any 22mm watch band. The Pebble Smartwatch is an indispensable device for me.Starting with the hardware - beautiful, simple and eye catching, Pebble is lightweight and robust. The buttons have a solid click to them and the screen is wonderfully visible in bright sunlight, as advertised. I've also tested it while swimming and it seems to be watertight as advertised.Since I began using my Pebble there are a few things I never anticipated it would help me out with - namely two factor auth text messages from Google and discretely keeping up with text messages. The former is worth the value of the watch alone - two factor auth text messages are a massive pain given you have to pull out your phone, unlock it, etc. When they are directly on your wrist, they are practically frictionless. Additionally, mundane text messages that may have previously interrupted dinner or a good conversation can be quickly reviewed by peeking at my wrist.One of my biggest concerns about a smartwatch was the battery life - I'm consistently getting a week with Pebble. And quite frankly if I had to charge my watch on a daily basis, I wouldn't be interested. I'm hopeful that future updates make this even longer.It's also been great to see the progress in software updates that the Pebble folks have been putting out - they clearly want Pebble to get better over time and it shows. Excited to see the watch and the platform grow.
summary: Pebble delighted me in ways I couldn't have anticipated

reviewText: Been wearing this watch since they first started shipping to Kickstarter backers, and now can hardly imagine my daily routine without it! I've had my Kickstarter-edition Pebble working with my iPhone 4S for a few weeks now and can add my two cents.  Overall, I love getting texts and call notifications on my wrist.  I miss far fewer messages than in my pre-Pebble, pocket-vibrating days.  Other reviewers are right, though, that the bluetooth connection between watch and phone occasionally drops and then reconnects (usually when they separate by 25 or more feet and then reunite) and that caller ID with contact names rarely works.  I also love controlling music (play, pause, back one track, forward one track); this was really handy on a road trip recently.  And the ability to change faces is just plain fun.  I appreciate all those creative people out there designing watchfaces.  Thank you!!!  There are few apps available right now; the only one I use is a countdown timer.  Email notifications apparently work for iPhones now (post 8/1/13), but I don't want to be bothered with those.I got the Pebble, though, also to get calendar notifications.  Alas, because all notifications (except for texts and calls) turn off in the event of a disconnection, calendar notifications are not reliable.  You can restart calendar and other app notifications by toggling them off and then back on in "settings->notifications" on an iPhone, but I can't count on knowing when to do this or that I will remember to do it.  This flaw is nearly a deal-killer for me, since I really wanted calendar notifications to work.So why 4 stars?  I have a work-around that suits me just fine.  I use Google Calendar on my laptop and Calendars+ on my iPhone.  Instead of setting event alerts to "pop-up" or "alert," I set them to signal me via SMS.  (In "settings" under the gear in the upper-right corner of your Google Calendar, sign up under "mobile setup" to get SMS via Google.)  This means that my Google Calendar alerts reach me 99% of the time.  The one exception so far has been when the bluetooth connection between watch and phone disconnected and did not reconnect automatically; I don't know what happened.  My solution?  Shut down the watch and turn it back on.Early adopters have to deal with such annoyances, eh?  In a few months or years, perfection will arrive, in the form of either updated firmware from Pebble or a watch from some other maker.  For now, I can say confidently that my Pebble makes life a little better, even with its flaws.
summary: Not perfect but fun and useful, as long as Google Calendar SMS is enabled

I also see emails and can read them.With Glance there are some pre-programmed text messages you can send people... "on my way, OK, sounds good... etc." and you can add your own... Like, "I'm leaving the office, hope to be home for dinner soon."Without Glance, this is really a 1-way extension of what's on your phone with a few watch faces.  There are a good number of applications that make this watch useful to a wide variety of needs.  So far it has exceeded mine other than the heart rate thing.It's good for someone who doesn't want to keep looking at their phone or stay tethered to it. Oh, and it has a 1-yr warranty which is pretty awesome for this kind of thing.------ Update: About 5 days after getting the watch... I looked everywhere for a battery meter, there isn't one - until it starts to go down, and it's only visible when you're looking through the menus of the watch.  So, when you get your watch, charge it, and find there is no indicator, that's because you're OK, it doesn't need a charge yet.  I now have the standard battery icon in the top right of the screen.  So, I expect it'll last another day or 2, about a week on 1 charge as advertised... and I've played around with it a lot.I'm still enjoying it as much as day 1.  :)

reviewText: This was purchased as a tech toy. Smart watches are still in their infancy. Even so, this unit is well thought out, and even for its simple design, it does a fairly good job.The watch comes with a set of 'faces' (digital, not physical) which are different watch faces to tell time. You can download more via the companion application you have to install on your smart phone. Yes, you have to pair it with a phone to use it. The companion application offloads things like information retrieval (weather, GPS, etc) from the watch, reducing the electronic complexity in the watch itself.There are other applications you can download into the watch beyond the basic watch faces. There are 8 storage spaces in the watch to run them. Some may come in 2 parts, and this take two spaces. So it is no memory behemoth. You are not going to upload your MP3 collection into it. It doesn't even have speakers to play them anyway. Also of note: the watch does not run two programs at once. You run the one you want, switch to another and the first is shutdown.It does have a 'buzzer' motor built in. It can be used to tick off the hour, or used as an alarm. Very quiet and effective, unless you suffer from some nerve damage that leaves your arm numb to sensations like that.One application I use beyond the information tools, is a sleep monitor. It samples the watch's built in accelerometer while it is running, to get an idea if you are sound asleep, lightly asleep, or seemingly wake (tossing and turning). The companion app can then give you a chart in the morning of how you did. It also has a smart alarm function that will wake you up, theoretically at the best point within a wake up time range you set. This isn't a serious health application. But it is a good toy that gives you insight into you sleep patterns.Battery life is fair. It certainly beats a typical phone's battery. I charge my PEBBLE every four or five days, when it is down around 30 or 40 %.Construction is solid. You are NOT ever going to open this thing up to change the batter or explore. People who have done that end up with a badly 'damaged' watch that requires nasty glue jobs to get it back into workable shape. So, in essence this is a throw away toy. If it dies, you are not going to get it repaired (when outside of its warranty). But at its price, compared to other smart watches, it hurts a bit less to let it go.If the price is too steep to you, then yes, it is too steep. This is not a watch you will keep for years and years. There are far better watches you can buy, to tell time with. This is an early stage smart watch in a world where people think they must trade their cellular phone out for a new one every 2 years or so. It would be so nice if they made a smart watch with an expected 10 year life cycle, with replaceable parts. This isn't that.The requirement to tie it to your iOS or Android smart phone, reduces its value a bit. But then, if it could gather information all on its own, it would cost a heck of a lot more. So it is a good entry point to explore the ideas of what a smarter watch can be.

I just purchased my Pebble yesterday and I am still getting to know the capabilities.  So far, I'm amazed!  This is the best tech gadget I have purchased since the original iPhone.  Not to mention it is extremely comfortable and light weight.  I couldn't hold out any longer for apple to launch their wearable tech watch.  In the meantime, this smart watch will get me orientated to this technology.  They are ahead of the game as far as opening development for apps.  It is simplistic, and easy to comfortably navigate within a short period of time.  I don't know if we are getting extremely lazy, but I love the fact I don't have to pull my phone out of my pocket every time I hear a tone or a vibration.  The hands free notifications (email, phone call, and text) are worth the price alone.

Let's put it this way: I love it, and I believe this is the best smart watch by far in this current, first generation. Now, details.When you unbox, you are surprised that it does not look geeky. It does not look expensive though, but it does not look cheap either. It's actually different, more on the "modern stylish" side, and that's the expression that comes to my mind when I look at it. I'm fine with it. But there is one thing that is certain: you will get *a lot* of questions about it, from everyone in all social classes, especially if you use fancy watch faces. Everyone is curious, everyone looks at it.Charging is done using the supplied, proprietary cable. It connects using regular USB, but the watch side is a magnetic component. When you power it on, it will ask to pair with your phone. At least for Android, you must 1) turn on Bluetooth, 2) Pair the watch using your phone, 3) Activate the watch in the Accessibility section of Android Settings. Many people get lost because they don't know about this last step. Finally, open the Pebble app and you're good to go. After that, when you turn on Bluetooth on the phone and watch, it will connect automatically.Notifications work fine. Out of the box, Whatsapp, Facebook, Hangouts/SMS, Calendar are supported. Other apps can easily add support for Pebble using the supplied API. As someone with an Android app published, I was impressed with the ease of the API. It's very easy to program and the API is really lean and straightforward. I added support for my Android application in one night (learning and everything!) and I'm not a C guru by any means whatsoever.Battery lasts around a full week to 3 or 4 days depending on how much you use. Charging seems to be quick, around an hour (the manual states something like that).What I like to do the most is pair my phone with my car, and my phone with the Pebble. I can then control the car sound system using my watch, as well as receive, answer and end calls using the watch, all while using the car sound system. Everyone is impressed when I do this. It also adds a bit of safety, since it's much easier and quick to look who's calling with a glance at your watch, although I generally just refuse the calls because I don't feel comfortable driving and speaking at the same time. But it definitely adds a layer of safety if/when you do, by keeping your eyes on the road! :-)I can control my music without taking the phone out of my pocket, and without even turning it on.I also snorkel with this watch. My Android app displays tidal data, so I don't need to tell how insanely useful and insanely cool it was to check the tides using a waterproof watch! Just in case, I rinse with tap water after I finish. If I recall correctly, the manual says such thing, but don't remember. I also avoid pressing buttons when the watch is wet. I know many watches require that, but you may want to double check that. The quick start guide is very quick.There is a very friendly online community at getpebble dot com, both for users and developers. The documentation online is extensive.However, the best and worst feature of this watch is the screen: it's e-ink, so it reflects light received, doesn't emit any (unless you press the backlight button, but that's another point). This is awesome, and I can't understand why someone would even consider using an LCD watch in broad daylight. Just for you to know: it's brighter under the Sun. That's the whole difference! However, since reflective technology is still in its infancy, they kept the price down using a black and white e-ink with fairly limited resolution. Again, it's not monochromatic, it's black and white, as in 1 bit, on and off, for the pixels. There are advances in this area (Mirasol), but, considering the current stage of this business, I believe it was a fair tradeoff to make it widely available at a smaller cost. I consider this a sound decision, even if we prefer a color screen. There is also a problem regarding polarized light... Many people complain about slight color banding in the screen, but, fortunately, I don't have this problem. However, it is VERY pronounced if you're using polarized glasses, which happens with many LCD displays. It becomes all funky and psychedelic.So... I know there are other smart watches available, but all of them failed in my opinion for not getting the concept right. I promptly refuse the current crop of Android smart watches since they are too complex, and I don't need a full featured phone in my arm. I just want a second, glance able screen for my phone, that I can command remotely. For that the Pebble nails it! Also, other watches tend to be too big and cumbersome, reminding me of the Casio calculator watches. Because I love computer programming does not mean I want to dress in a stereotyped manner.To end this, you need to ask: do you need a smart watch? Don't dive into the hype, they are not for everyone. I researched this very well (as you can probably tell by now) and found that it simplifies my life. Controlling my music, telling me who is calling, reading emails and notifications that arrive, checking data while on the sea, and I'm sure I'll find my more.Finally, I'm anxiously waiting what the second generation of smart watches will bring. However, don't wait for it. The best thing right now is already available, it's useful, it's refreshing, and it will always be nice to tell that you lived the birth of this technology!I give it five stars (4.5 if I could) considering the current state of this technology. To paraphrase a famous quote, it's too bad it's not perfect, but then again what is?
summary: Excellent... for this first age of smartwatches

reviewText: I had no idea there were so many watch faces and apps out there for these amazing little pieces of technology.  The watch lens seems to be acrylic, so make sure to get a screen protector for it.  The version 2 for the firmware is coming out in early 2014.  It's possible to install the beta for it now.  Upgrading to version 2 really makes a difference!  This item is perfect for people who: 1) set reminders on their phones but somehow miss the message from the phone, 2) people who leave their phones (the watch will tell you when you are out of range with the right app installed), 3) if you are in situations when you want to be alerted to mail/texts but you don't want to rude by looking at your phone (like class, or meetings, etc.).

I was very hesitant spending $150 for a watch that was made by a small start up group, but I have been more than satisfied with not only the watch, but the development and effort that the Pebble team continues to put in.  Sure, there are a few bumps and the one time I contacted support, it took a little while, but I expect that from a small company.Here is what I love about my watch:- It is programmable.  I am a school teacher and I always wanted a watch that was synced to the school clocks and would count down to the end of each period.  With a little effort, I was able to write a program to do that, and that is not functionality I can get anywhere else.- I love the support for additional apps, like RunKeeper and FreeCaddie.  I start RunKeeper on my iPhone and I automatically see all the pacing information right on my watch.  It is like having a GPS watch built in.  The same is true for FreeCaddie if you golf.  I just put the phone in my bag and my watch gives me the information I need.- Notifications from the phone.  I love that I can put my phone away and still get notifications and emails.  This works well when I am at the pool and I put my phone in a waterproof case in my pocket.  I can't easily see my phone, but when a message comes in, I can still get the message.  It is also handy on my job since I don't want my kids seeing me pull my phone out of my pocket to check messages every few minutes.  While I do sometime experience issues with the messages not coming through, it is pretty rare under the new operating system for the watch.- Battery life is great.  I charge it about once a week, and I usually use a watch face that counts down seconds with vibrating patterns to signal the time remaining in class.Here is what is cool, but I don't really find all that useful:- Lots of different watch faces.  Yes, it is nice to have a custom watch face and be able to change it when ever you want, but if that is the only thing you are looking for, this is a little expensive for that.  Switching watch faces got old pretty quick.- Many of the apps that it has are cool, but again not as functional as other things.  For example, there are many step counter apps, but they are nowhere near as accurate as things like FitBit.  Other apps like GPS, pictures, etc. are all neat looking, but not really effective and beyond what the watch is really focused on doing.- Weather, stock, news apps and things like that.  Most of that information is not updated all that regularly, so I find it easier to just check that stuff on my phone.There is not much to complain about, but the few things that I would say are that the connectivity between the phone can sometimes be sporadic and you may miss notifications on your watch because of it. It is not often that messages stop (maybe once a month), but it happens and I think this will happen with a software that is constantly being updated and improved.

reviewText: Nowadays, when my phone rings, my wrist buzzes. When someone texts me, I don't look at my phone to find out what they said; I look at my watch. Why? I've got a Pebble - the "smartwatch." Pebble describes it as an "E-paper watch for iPhone and Android". The "e-paper" bit might get some thinking you're going to be reading books on it. You're definitely not, but it is a great display. So what do you get for your money? It's a watch, to start with. The face is 144x168 pixels, a large black/white e-paper display. I chose the black body and strap (you can get it in black, white, cherry red or grey). Open the box, and you're instructed to go to getpebble.com. That's a neat touch - no manual at all. The whole initial setup is done through its web page and then app. Open that page on your smartphone, and it directs you to the iPhone or Android app store, where you download a free app which connects via Bluetooth. Through that, you can send software updates (such as new watchfaces) and, more usefully, back-and-forth notifications when someone calls or texts. (You can also set it to notify you when you get an email. Don't do this unless you never get email.) The watchface is scratch-resistant (not -proof) and has an anti-glare coat; I find it very readable in all lights, except when it's dark. Then you have the options of an automatic backlight (adjusted to light levels), or being able to flick your wrist to activate the backlight. The strap feels like rubber; it's wide (to go with the watch) but not uncomfortable. Charging is via a USB lead terminating in a magnetic attachment to a pair of contacts on the left-hand side of the watch; I assume a micro-USB slot would have taken up too much internal space and created waterproofing problems (it is waterproof, at least for swimming). So don't lose that charger; you'll be needing it every four or five days (in my experience, though the makers claim up to seven.. probably if you have Bluetooth off) and it's unique. One bad thing: the interface doesn't show the battery level (even in the phone app), which can leave you in the lurch without warning. The charge level only shows when you're charging, and even then only in the menu, as opposed to standard watch, display.
summary: The Pebble Samrtwatch: "the watch that does what you need."

reviewText: Having used my Pebble for several months, it is hard to overstate its usefulness and practicality. There is no other electronic device closer to you than your watch, and the beauty of the Pebble is that all of its features work extremely well and help it to seamlessly integrate into your everyday tasks more than any other smartwatch.You almost need to wear one on a regular basis to fully appreciate what it can do for you, because it enables you to do things you couldn't do before and might not have thought of. Some of my favorite uses:1) Going for a run with my phone strapped to my arm and using the RunKeeper app on my Pebble. I can easily pause/resume my run, glance down at my wrist to see my speed and time elapsed (rather than having to awkwardly look and poke at my phone on my arm, especially in the sunshine).2) Being able to remotely control the music playing on my phone. Handy for when your hands are all wet/dirty and you don't want to touch your phone or it isn't right next to you, and especially for running with earphones. Since Pebble is waterproof, I even use it when I'm swimming to change songs when I'm in the pool.3) Being able to see immediately when I have a new text message, a new email, Facebook update, or when someone is trying to call me. I love being able to see at a glance who is calling me so that I don't need to take my phone out of my pocket to check (or worse yet, so that I don't miss the call entirely if I'm walking and don't feel it). Once I see who is calling, I can ignore the call without needing to take my phone out of my pocket. Of course, you can control which alerts get sent to your watch in the first place. How's that for minimizing phone-related distractions?!4) Inconspicuously being able to read an email or text message on my watch, rather than fiddling with my phone and looking like I'm not paying attention to anyone nearby.5) Changing watch faces for different occasions (especially using the Big Time face for practicality where the time is in huge font, or a cool look where the time is shown in text as "four thirty"). You could try a new one each day!6) I can simply flick my wrist to activate the backlight for reading the screen in the dark.7) What a great conversation starter -- if people don't come up to you and ask about it first, just about anyone would be impressed by its cool factor and what it can do. Whereas it would be pretty socially unacceptable to show off your Rolex to strangers, showing off your Pebble is cool, everybody loves it and has that genuine look of "wow, that's really awesome, now I want one!"The Pebble is also physically a good size, very light and comfortable to wear. The stock watchband is very comfortable and waterproof, but you can change it if you want something unique. If you're not used to wearing a watch, the Pebble won't feel like a large heavy object like some other watches (*cough* Samsung *cough*). With a week of battery life, you won't need to worry about forgetting to charge it daily either.Setup in the Pebble app and connecting it to your phone is a breeze. It works with Androids and iPhones, and gets software updates directly from Pebble as new features are introduced -- this is really a case where the product you buy today can get even better over time while you own it.If you're the type of person who explores more than the basic functions, Pebble also has you covered. Designing your own watch face is fairly straightforward and you can add all kinds of data feeds to your watch. Personally, I have my watch face show the weather and temperature, the time, when sunrise and sunset are, the date, the battery life percentage remaining on my phone and what my next appointment is in my calendar.I know a number of people who have Pebbles and we all love them! A highly recommended product!
summary: Pebble is easily the best smartwatch on the market!

reviewText: I bought my Pebble for the sports features, not so much for the everyday notifications (I don't normally wear a watch). I'm a runner, and I just couldn't justify spending 100s of dollars on a GPS watch when my phone already had a GPS. I use it all the time with Runkeeper; the integration works great.

Overall I'm happy with my Pebble watch. The battery life is awesome and it's always easy to read. It's starting to get some really great apps now too. Here are some of the problems I've had with it.1.) Connecting to your cell phone can take a really long time. It usually takes me three tries to get it to connect, it always starts working on the 3rd attempt. I wonder why.2.) The glass is very easily scratched! You definitely need a screen protector. I have two giant gouges and the funny thing is, I have no idea how or why. They just appeared. I'm sure I did something, but I don't remember it going through any trauma.3.) The charger isn't super great. The magnet that keeps it together is pretty week and you can't plug it into a wall to charge. You can only plug it in to a computer via USB to charge. It would be much more convenient if I could plug it in.4.) There aren't many good options for covers and cases. Maybe I'm just picky, I just wish there was a bigger variety. Most of them are stickers. If there were more snap on/snap offs to match different outfits and I'd be much happier.Overall, it's a good product. I'd somewhat recommend, just take note of some of it's downfalls.

reviewText: Applications do not seem to work well with this device.  It is almost completely dependent on a smart phone for its operation.

I got this watch because when I am seeing patients, I don't like to have to pull out my call to see if someone is calling from the ICU (answer immediately) or anywhere/who else (go to voicemail).  Also, because my pages are all text messages.  This awesome device lets me screen the calls/texts very inconspicuously. For calls I don't need to answer, I push the button by the "X" and they to to voicemail.  Texts scroll down to read them.  Once the initial phone set up is done, on the iPhone it works great, as the app just stays open, and does it's part of talking to the watch. Stays charged about 5 days.  And I love that with the Smartwatch+ app, I can see the weather without having to pull my phone out, which by the time I am headed out to my truck, the phone is tucked away in a pocket. (And now that I am trying the beta of the Pebble OS 2.0, I can use the Yahoo weather watchface not even have to have Smartwatch+ open on the phone).Coolness factor: one of the nurses at my hospital ask what jewelry store I got it at, because it is a deep glossy black I guess. The Black really does look good.More importantly, wearability/durability: after an errant pitch by my son smashed my old Casio, I tried a Timex, that beeped all the time when I was typing notes (I wear it on the palm side of my wrist, so I can look at it while counting pulse rate) and hurt my wrist typing, felt like a rock, and had the dates backwards. Was a PITA. This fits my wrist well in either position, is lightweight, and I barely notice it. Also, it wears in shower and handwashing just fine.  Durability: I don't plan on testing it, as it cost $150 here!  But it has absorbed minor bumping fine so far.Geek factor: I have already made several watchfaces for it. Gotta love it!Cons: most watchfaces are viewable without backlight on for me.  But the angle of viewing is such that for me to show it to someone else, I have to shake my wrist to activate the backlight so they can see it. But the beauty of it is that someone will probably build a timer app for it that will sell or be free in the Pebble App Store that is launching in Jan 2014.I think in the next few years as these and the inevitable iWatch and gWatch catch on, that people will expect their watches to do all this. reviewText: So I actually bought this for a present for a friend.  I almost did the kickstarter way back when, but I wasn't sure if the technology was really going to be that helpful. The software itself is still needing some development too, but it's functional now.I use it constantly though the day.  To check the time, sure.  Beyond that though, I get tons of emails, so it's really nice to glance at my wrist to just see who it was.  Same with calls and texts.  Reaching for your phone is not always easy or polite, and this watch gives you a great quick message for when you can't.I've always worn watches.  Most of  my life it was almost purely for decoration.  I can honestly say I'm using my watch now.  It may not be the most beautiful, but the functionality is so overwhelming, it's a solid buy.

Before I get to the good stuff, let me first bring up the bad. When I first got this watch, I was initially underwhelmed by it. I encountered pairing issues with my phone. I could not figure out how to install faces and apps. Once I did, I found that some apps caused the watch to lock up and require system recovery. The battery, while extremely good, does not have a "low charge" warning (instead, it has an icon that appears in the menu about 12 hours before it dies).That being said, The pairing issues went away with the last update, and my android phone started actually directing my scanned qr links to the pebble app when applicable. The apps that cause the Pebble to crash are few and far between, and the recovery process is very quick and painless, with no data loss. The screen is very tough, and has no marks or scratches after a month of running it into things. The water resistance is also worth noting, as I have showered with it every day since I got it, and it has been doing fine. I now get emails, texts, and call notifications, complete with vibration, on my wrist, meaning that I can leave my phone constantly on silent without missing anything. Most of the faces and apps are great, and I can change things instantly when I want a different look or feel. I can keep score, follow to-do lists, and if it comes down to it, use the back-light to light my path to the restroom in the middle of the night.Other android apps have also been enhancing my experience. Coffer lets me manage my pebble faces and apps so I can swap out even when my watch is full. HTTPebble gives me wrist access to information such as tides, exchange rates, moon phases, sunrize and sunset times, weather forecasts, and seconds since the Unix epoch. Apps like Glance display my phone's battery and current stock/mutual fund values, while bringing other information together onto one screen.Pebble has some small hurdles, but they are all fixable. I have yet to find a better watch, anywhere, and wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone willing to learn how to use it.
summary: This may be the best watch on the market

reviewText: I bought this at a store last September.  When I was first using it, it didn't work very well.  I wouldn't always get notifications, and it would suddenly die on me without warning.  There were very few apps, and I just rarely wore it.  Around November, and update came out that made it infinitely better.  I could now get all the notifications that appeared on my phone screen, and it was much more stable.  That was when I started falling in love with this.  On February 4, 2014, Pebble released an update that finally made this the watch it should have been from the beginning.  They have their own App store now, to get Pebble apps.  The notifications are greatly improved, and the range is very good (I can go from one floor to the next in my house and still have connection between the two devices).  Some of the third-party apps are iffy, and many lose the connection and have to be reset, but so far the only one that has really helped is a battery life app.  That's the one bad point with this watch; you don't get a notification that the battery is low until it's almost dead.  And even then you have to click to the settings screen to see the little icon, you don't see it on the main screen.  So you get up in the morning, check your settings, and oops, there's the low battery icon.  Now you can't go out with your watch because you have to leave it charging or it will die in an hour.  However, there are battery life apps that work directly with the watch (not with the phone) so I can easily check how much battery life is left.  Many of the third-party apps work with the phone (such as Foursquare and Smartwatch Pro), so if the phone happens to time out the bluetooth connection your app is dead.  But at least Pebble is on top of the game with their updates, and so far it is the best overall smart watch.  If the Galaxy watch was universal, it may give Pebble a run for its money, but for now if you don't have a Samsung phone this watch is the way to go.

I'm an Android user, and I've had the Pebble Watch for a month now, so I figured I'd leave my thoughts on it here. This watch has its good and its bad, just as any product does; several factors keep me from giving this a 5-star rating.Cons:- Most features that you see on the on [...] (where I got my pebble from) require a third party app, and they don't tell you which. I wish they had provided a list, or integrated options into their own app.- The default app only lets you download some basic watch faces (see above for additional features).- Watch face easily scratches; great for the office environment, but don't tinker around with it.- Better support under Android than iOs, mainly due to phone policies on apps talking to each other (sorry, iPhone users). Fix would be to integrate everything into a single app.Pros:- Once you get the apps installed, you can do some great stuff.- Long selection of music-playing apps that you can control from the watch (under Android, at least, I have 15 apps listed, including Audible, Netflix, Hulu Plus, and the standard Video Player).- Long battery life. Other devices rarely last 3 days, but the Pebble has lasted me a full 7 days before showing the low battery warningOverall, for the ability to control my phones status (silent/vibrate/normal through Phone Ringer), see notifications from any app I choose (Pebble Notifier), answer calls and mute them (PebbleDialer), or design my own watch face (Canvas for Pebble), this watch is great for the price. I DON'T need a second phone on my wrist, just a tool to see what's going on in my phone and control it a bit. Between the price and the battery life, I can live with picking and choosing which features I want and downloading those apps (for now).
summary: Great Smart Watch, Some Tinkering Required

reviewText: Firstly,  this watch did not impress me.  I like watches and at first I was excited to get this one because it is a "smart" watch.  Upon first touch, I immediately noticed that it was comprised of lower grade plastic.  Plastic push buttons, easily scratched plastic face, lower grade band--overall a lower grade build quality for the going price. I was not too impressed.  However, I pressed on and was determined to see what this new device could do once paired up to my Samsung Galaxy S 4.  "Maybe the functions outweigh the cheapness, I thought".To get this watch to work with the phone, I had to download the "PEBBLE APP" from Google .  In the activation process of the app, the user is required to permit a function called "accessibility" in the phone.  There was no way around this requirement.  So, to use the "smart" part of the phone this feature had to be enabled in order to continue with the app installation.  Instantly after the download the program and watch connected and determined that the phone needed a firmware update, which was performed.  So far so good.I was now receiving my e-mail on my watch screen. I could change my watch face. I could control my phone music through the watch buttons.  All of this was pretty cool and this functionality overshadowed the lackluster build quality.Well, here comes the depressing part.  I then went back to my phone to search the web and much to my shock and horror, the phone kept announcing the actions of going back and forward on internet searches.  This was a spoken voice in the loudest volume that my phone possesses.  I could not turn the volume down, nor stop the speach using "settings/accessibility" in the phone.  Upon quick research I found that others had the same problem with this loud, obnoxious announcing every move made on internet searches.  Nobody on the blog pages had a good, solid solution for this problem and how to stop it.  Some suggested unchecking all features of "accessibility/Talkback" on the phone and then removing this app from the phone entirely.  Well, I did uncheck the features and upon finishing, my phone spoke every app, button, etc. on each screen of the phone that I was on.  Then my phone locked up and I could not enter my security code.  For each number pressed, the voice said "dot".  My phone was taken back to the phone store.  The people there new nothing about the problems associated with a Pebble watch used with a Samsung Galaxy S 4. All they could do was to do a factory reset on my phone which eliminated my contacts and apps.So, upon arrival back home I promptly put the watch back into the box and shelved it hoping that the battery would eventually die in it.  I then reworked the phone.This watch has some issues worth investigating for certain phones/devices. For me, to use the watch just as a watch, and with no "smart" functionality just doesn't fit my bill.  It is rather big , for just a watch.  It is rather cheaply built , for just a watch.  Time will tell--maybe by waiting someone will make this watch work.
summary: Poor build quality, limited function, Pebble App requires Accessibility (Talkback)

I spend a lot of time with my phone in pockets or bags that can be inconvenient to get to when I get a text, email, or phone call.  I work and play outside a lot, often with gloves, so pulling my phone out every time I hear it chirp or ring is frustrating.  I use a Samsung Galaxy S3, so I looked at the Samsung Gear watch thinking it would be a great tool to have.  After reading reviews, and realizing that it isn't even water resistant, I decided it would not be a good choice, not to mention the price tag.  I also didn't really like the idea of another touchscreen that I couldn't use with gloves very well.  The Pebble seemed to be a good choice for me, seeing that it is waterproof, and not a touch screen.  I wasn't sure the size and style were going to all that desirable, but decided to give it a try.  After opening the package, I realized the size of the watch wasn't going to be a problem.  It is relatively slim, fits well on my wrist (though the band was apparently designed for people with much smaller wrists than mine), and looks good!  I've been wearing an analog dive watch for 7 years, so knowing that I can still use a traditional watch face is nice.  After getting to know the watch now, though, I don't use the analog face anymore, but prefer to use one that conveys much more information than the time.  For those that like to be kept up to date in places where cell phones are frowned upon (school, movie theater, meetings) this thing is great.  It vibrates on your wrist, so if your phone is silenced, or you are snowmobiling, or on a noisy jobsite, you can easily feel the vibration.Some things I like about the Pebble:It's size is quite reasonable for packing so much into it.The buttons are large and easy to use, even with gloves on.The e ink display is very visible in bright sunlightThe backlight turns on with a flick of the wristThere are MANY different apps for the Pebble.At the time I'm writing this, the Android App Store has just (within an hour ago) opened.....hopefully this is a pro.....Battery life seems to be pretty good.  I'm getting three to five days out of a charge, closer to five.I'm rough on things, and the screen has not suffered a single scratch yet.If you don't like the band, you can swap it out with any 22mm band.Couple things I'm not too fond of:It seems to disconnect and connect pretty often, even when sitting a few feet from the phone. I have a suspicion that this has more to do with my phone than the watch, though.I understand the magnetic charger is used to keep the watch waterproof, but it's just one more power cord to keep track of.....The app installation and use is not the most user friendly around, but I get by.Overall, the Pebble is great.  It definitely does everything I was hoping for , and more.  If you are looking for a flashy, colorful, touch screen, this probably isn't the watch you are looking for.  But this thing gets the job done, looks great, and is actually a lot of fun to use.

I received my Pebble in the mail after looking at the different smartwatches that were available.  I'd read a couple of articles, all of which pointed to the Pebble as being the one to buy.  I believe the story about it having come about through a kickstarter campaign is media-charming, as if that somehow makes it not a commercial enterprise (it is a commercial enterprise).  Its neat but not as neat as some might have you believe.After a day of using it, here are my observations.  They are my observations, your own mileage may vary...objects in watch screen may be closer than they...you get it.First, the watch came neatly packaged in a tight little box. Once opened, do not expect real instructions.  There's a quick start guide, some disclosure materials, a cable and the watch. The watch came with very little juice and wouldn't do anything until I plugged it in. Once plugged in, it charges pretty quickly and seems to be very economic with how it spends its power.The watch itself is a study in sleek black plastic.  I'm hoping the screen on it doesn't scratch but I can already tell you it attracts smudges like nobody's business.  I've had to clean it a half dozen times in the past day alone. It is light weight, attractive and will work equally well with jeans or a suit. It may seem to be a bit non-descript until someone realizes you're looking at emails on it and then it becomes a real conversation piece.Setup was pretty easy, mostly done by downloading your app and following directions on your phone or ipad. The watch has 8 slots for watch faces or apps. I have no idea how much memory is on the watch, but it is managed through the use of the slots. Separately, almost everything you do on the Pebble (aside from using it directly) is done on your smartphone or ipad.  Anything bought, saved, changed or moved is done on the smartphone or ipad and then is uploaded to the watch.  This happens in pretty close to real-time and there are enough watch faces that you can have a different one everyday for weeks on end.  There are quite simple applications available both at the Pebble site as well as the ITunes App Store though some are more useful than others.The positives are that the watch works, retains power, keeps accurate time and is interesting.  The bad news is that the face is dim (even when 'lit,' which is accomplished by simply jerking your wrist a little) and sometimes hard to read.  If you want to show it to someone, you have to take it off.  The angle of view works for the wearer, but NO ONE is contortionist enough to show it clearly to someone else while its still on your wrist.The next negative is that I haven't been able to figure out how to control the vibrate. I'd like to set the watch so it won't vibrate after (say) 11 so the next non-solicited email offering to sell me Canadian Viagra at 4 in the morning doesn't wake me up. You can hit 'Do Not Disturb,' if you remember to do so, but that takes remembering.There is no camera, touchscreen, interactivity between watch and phone/ipad.  Simply, it show some of the information that hits your cellphone but not all of it and then only to show.  The point being, I supposed, that the watch is telling you when to look at the cellphone.  All in, it delivers on its capabilities, but not on the ideas that those capabilities inspire. Its less a smart watch than a dumb monitor right now.  Its possible that may change in future generations but for now, its a relatively simple device for seeing what's going on in your phone without having to look at your phone.I'm not over- or under-whelmed.  I guess I'm just whelmed.  We'll see what next gen apps do with the platform.
summary: Review: Pebble Smartwatch  Exec Summary: Its OK, not great

First and foremost, I'd like to note that you should not buy this at amazon at this time. The asking price is ridiculous when you can just go to best buy and get it for $150. That is what I did, hence the reason I don't have a verified Amazon purchase.That said, the product itself is fantastic and I'm surprised about all these bad reviews.The phone I use my pebble with is an HTC One, AT&T.; Unlocked, and has a custom ROM.The watch looks very minimal and stylish if you ask me. The first thing I did was apply a screen protector. The reason being I use my hands a lot at work and could easily bump into things or scrape the display. I suggest if you do any manual labor or are just worried about an accident, buy a screen protector. (This coming from someone who won't use one on their phone.) I normally hate them but I'd rather use one on the exposed screen than suffer damage.That said, let's get into the watch itself.DISPLAY: The display is very pleasing. I noticed someone else commented that it is pixelated. Keep in mind this is a small form factor watch. It's not going to look fantastic. As a watch, though, it looks great.The display is not really the type of E-paper that most people would think of, it is not like a kindle. It's a lower power LCD. no touch screen. I've seen a lot of complaints about this, which I find dumb. The animations and transitions on this are far better than that of a kindle, which I care about more, considering what I use this for. Which, speaking of...SOFTWARE: I see a lot of people also complaining the software is buggy, another problem I never had. Upon opening the watch, I was given very clear instructions to download the app on the play store, after opening that app, my pebble started a firmware update. This is the ONE time I had a problem with the watch. I waited and waited with no indication of progress on the watch. Finally I pressed a button and cancelled the up date (from the watch) and reconnected with my phone. It updated again and worked fantastically from that point (there was a % indicator on the watch that time. So if you see that you're probably good.) The onboard software let's you receive SMS messages, phone calls, and email on the watch. You can't reply to email or SMS but you can read them. You can see who is calling and also answer phone calls from it though. I will note that my SMS messages never would show up on the watch, even though the test SMS worker. This was problematic. But an easy fix. I'll detail that later. It also has basic music control. It has native Pandora Apollo, and YouTube integration for music control, as well as a paid app (by a third party) called music boss on the play store which extends functionality. The native music player allows you to skip forward and backwards on track listing and play and pause your music. All worked fine excluding SMS.ADDITIONAL APPS: in addition to the main app, there are various third party apps you can install to your pebble. Most are free. A few cost money. I won't go into most of them, as a quick search in your own respective app store (iOS or Android) for 'pebble' should show you most of them. I will, however mention, that I was able to install the "Pebble Notifier" which in addition to fixing my SMS problem (and I should have noted, I use a third party SMS application, Textra, which might have affected the stock program from working), I can also set any other app I wanted to be notified on the watch face.HARDWARE:-Buttons - A little hard to press but I got used to it very quickly. I wear gloves at with and have little issue holding them down while it's on my wrist.Band: you can replace the band. I like the one that it comes with but that's mostly personal preference.Backlight: It has a backlight. The default setting is that it detects movement and will turn on automatically. (I believe the concept was for it to turn on when you look at your wrist. ) I keep this setting off because I move a lot and do not want the light to be turning on and off all the time.Charger: another slight caveat. The charger doesn't plug in. It's a magnetic strip with electrical contacts. It magnetizes in place so the contacts meet. The magnets are fairly weak however and it can fall off fairly easily. Someone said the band actually makes it worse and I agree. Make sure it's steady and won't move (in addition to being in a place it won't be bumped) if you decide to charge it with the band on. I do it this way and find it helps to keep the watch it self on something slightly raised up.Motor: The watch, as far as I can tell, has no speakers. It does have a vibrator in it though. When you recieve a text message, a phone call, or other notifications, the watch will buzz on your wrist. It's not annoying but enough so you will feel it. For me, it's perfect.I think that covers most the basics. Its a very handy watch if you don't want to be taking your phone out of your pocket all the time. I use it to adjust Pandora and see incoming texts and phone calls  it works wonderfully for that and has saved me time and gave me efficiency.If you want just a watch, there are cheaper alternatives. If you want a feature packed mini smartphone, there are better options for a smart watch. But if you want something affordable, simple, that can control and handle basics while looking stylish. This is your guy.And again. At best buy for $150. I think AT&T; has them now too. Thanks for reading!

Ordered the black Pebble in early Dec 13'. Order arrived within the prescribed time frame promised. It came packaged in a padded envelope and neatly boxed.Construction: Light weight plastic with some metal (buckle and side charging pins). The screen is scratch resistant (according to the website literature). The screen is ~1-inch (corner to corner). The larger button on left above the charging pins is a 'back-button'. There are three buttons not shown on the right. Think of them as scroll up (top), select (middle button), and scroll down (bottom). The band is made of rubber and is very comfortable. Over all the watch is very light weight...I caught myself looking to make sure it was still on it is so light. The watch charges over a standard USB port. There is no literature on the specific type of AC charger to use, so i'd caution anyone in using this method to charge the watch as it may not match the charging requirements of the watch itself.Software/Sync: I own an iPhone 4S with iOS7. The watch came with firmware 1.2 (? not sure if i'm using the correct terms-- firmware or software-not an IT guy!). I down loaded the free pebble app to my iPhone, once connected, it automatically walked me through the update process from 1.2 to 1.3., actually it was pretty seamless and a hands off process. Bluetooth established a handshake with my iPhone in seconds. I then selected the option to send test text and test call. both worked and the watch vibrated almost immediately. Packaged in the box were two short pamphlets, one with basic instructions and the other was all the FCC requirement information.Pebble can only receive data, save one, the music selection, which can start, stop and play music on your mobile device. Otherwise you can't text, email, or call from the watch. Think of it as an 'extension' "to" your phone as a remote control and as a notification system--albeit a limited extension as it can't manipulate apps on your phone--it can only use streams of data from it, e.g. GPS-data.  The phone must be in proximity to the Pebble (Bluetooth range varies) in order to function as a 'smart watch', otherwise it's only good as a watch...it tells time and date. There is tremendous potential here but that's a discussion beyond the scope of this review.Issues I encountered. First, there are other Pebble utilities (e.g. Smartwatch +, SmartWatch Pro, etc.)  that allow you access to weather features, maps, etc. But these are pay-utilities. In other word to really start enjoying the potential of this watch, you need to add these 'foundational utilities' in order to obtain the apps that make the watch more enjoyable to use as a tool. That said, some utilities/apps are pay and some are free, some are OEM type apps (approved for use on Pebble-tested), others are not (not tested or guaranteed). My opinion is that the smart watch needs to come with those baseline utilities/apps or at least make them available through the website. If its a third party vendor app, then sure, you may have to pay for those apps/services--I embrace capitalism, but in the most basic sense, the watch should come with baseline functional apps that showcase its potential. It just makes business sense.I personally ran into issues after the upgrade. My Pebble was constantly looking for a Bluetooth connection and when established, it was constantly in an "updating" mode for weather and GPS for when I ran (didn't work the only time I used it on an outdoor run which lasted for 47 mins), and lastly it never was able to correctly sync may battery status for my phone. So for example, if my phone was 100% charged, the Pebble would show 75% charged.Assuming you don't have a Samsung which has its own watch and assuming Apple doesn't come out with its own line of smart watches, Pebble can only improve in my opinion. It has a lot of potential, but it first needs to work out the basic bugs.5 starts for it potential, 3 stars however for its functionality vis-a-vis the need to purchase additional apps, and its glitchy-ness.
summary: To Pebble or Not to Pebble....Potential

reviewText: Wish I would have known just how limited the messaging and email capabilities were. This watch doesn't do what they say it will. A waste of my money !

I've owned a Pebble since x-mas, and I really love it; however, I love it for the wrong reasons. This device is simply fun to own. At most I enjoy changing and creating watch faces for it. In fact, that's really the only thing I use it for. Imagine owning a device that you can change the look of at will. If you get bored of a watch face, you download or create a new one.Now, on to the actual functionality and usability of the Pebble. As of now, there's simply not enough usage for the Pebble. It doesn't allow much of any useful interaction between it and the smartphone outside using it to control song play on your smartphone. For example, you can receive text notifications, but you can't reply to them. It doesn't even have built-in generic responses such as, "okay," "see you later," etc. There are also a number of apps for weather and battery notifications, but many of the watch faces include that information. Again, the watch faces are really the highlight of this device. Recently they've been releasing games for the Pebble. I don't understand why, as it's awkward to play a game on your wrist, and the not to mention that the button are a bit flimsy and cheap feeling. I can see them popping off from repeatedly being pressed. It's also a bit buggy. There are times when for any reason at all you won't get notifications, weather updates, etc. and a bluetooth resync is in order.So why did I give this device 4 stars you ask? Because the cool watch faces make it worth buying. As stated above, many watch faces include information such as weather and battery status. The Pebble store has hundreds and possibly thousands of faces to choose from. Love Star Wars? There are tons of Star Wars watch faces. Love the look of a Rolex watch? There's a Rolex watch face in the store. You can even make your own watch faces if you can't find one of interest. The best part is that you don't have to be a programmer. There's a website called http://www.watchface-generator.de/ that allows you to create your own faces and upload them to your Pebble. I only pair the two to transfer watch faces, and I do find it useful to have on when I'm teaching in class and can't get to my phone.As a consumer, you have to decide what your looking for in a smart watch. If you want something that acts like a true smart device, then get the Samsung Gear, or whatever Apple releases for IOS. If you're looking for a cool fun watch with limited smart technology, then go with the Pebble.

Sometimes, when you're the first out of the gate, you end up not having all the features and flash that your followers do, but considering this was kick-started and is in turn kick-starting the competition, I still stand by my little Pebble.It's come a good way since i purchased it, with the community providing great apps, and the Pebble team working on keeping the official Pebble app for iOS updated and increasing functionality.It's been rocky at times, but in the end, I have exactly what i want in a smart watch—a way to see the time, date, weather, and any alerts WITHOUT having to reach into my pocket.  It helps make the chaff of communications we all receive daily much more manageable.  And because you're not constantly turning your phone on and off, you're saving the battery life for more important things.Sure, I'd love a color display, and maybe a speaker built into it—but unlike it's followers, which may have some of those things, it's Platform Agnostic and Brand Agnostic—you can pair it with Android or iPhones and know there's a great community further tweaking and exploring the limitations of the Pebble Marketplace—it's not done evolving.There are also a wide variety of ways to customize the look, with snap-on faces, adhesive wraps, and band swaps.And it's waterproof, so you can shower with it.  (I've heard they no longer recommend it, but I think as long as you don't keep it in super-hot water for 30 mins, you're probably fine.  I shower with it daily and have never had a problem.For the money and how far it's come, it's a great SmartWatch for those who want to dive in and not worry about being locked into a brand or platform.

reviewText: Just got the Pebble this morning.  Setup was a breeze with my iPhone running iOS 7.  I read most of the reviews here on Amazon before buying the watch, and it looks like some of the doubters either received defective Pebbles or were just plain wrong.  The high points:Build Quality - my Pebble has no discernible manufacturing defects in the watch casing, as some others have observed with their Pebbles.  If you bought a Pebble from Amazon and there are nicks, scratches, or other defects in the watch casing, just send it back and get another one.  That's why we buy from Amazon people.  Easy returns and exchanges.Setup - I am into tech, but I did not have to draw on any serious knowledge of technology to set this thing up.  The Pebble folks have done a great job in making sure users are spoon-fed by the Pebble app and the watch during setup.  It.Was.Easy.Exchange Notifications - I read in some other reviews that users were upset that the Pebble purportedly does not receive email notifications from Microsoft Exchange accounts.  This is simply not true if you are using an iPhone running iOS 7.  I am receiving my work emails (Exchange server) just fine.  I do not have an Android phone, so if there is a problem there, I leave that to someone else to address.  But as to reviews claiming that iPhones with iOS 7 cannot receive Microsoft Exchange email notifications, THEY ARE FLAT OUT WRONG.Strap - I ordered a nicer replacement strap when I ordered my Pebble.  Replacing the strap was incredibly easy, and all I had to do was Google "replace Pebble watch strap" and view a short video.  The watch looks much nicer with the replacement strap.Slickwrap - I also ordered an Onyx brushed metal wrap for my Pebble.  Application took a little while to get right, but it was worth it.  Makes the watch look great.  IMPORTANT - the Slickwrap came with a screen protector film, which is a MUST with the Pebble.  The Pebble has a plastic screen that is very prone to scratching.  Applying a screen protector should be pretty much the first thing you do with your Pebble.I love the Pebble so far because it is exactly what I expected it to be - a device to, among other things, receive notifications from my iPhone and control my iPhone's music.  With the coming 2.0 firmware update, the watch is going to be able to do even more than that.  Right now I am running the SmartModernMod - Button Mod watch face from MyPebbleFaces.com, and it is very cool.  Weather, calendar, notifications, music control, etc.If you are looking for a second smartphone to wear on your wrist, then the Pebble is not for you.  That said, even now, Pebble does a lot more than just provide smartphone notifications, and the 2.0 firmware update is going to open things up for exciting developments in the future.  I am also looking forward to the GoPro Pebble app, as I have used my GoPro to video my younger son's tournament baseball games for years, and since I also manage his team, this will make it easier to turn the camera on and off between innings and let me focus on the game.In short, read the reviews, watch the videos, and read the information on Pebble's website.  If all of that describes a smartwatch that fits your needs and desires, then you will not be disappointing.

I purchased my Pebble through the original Kickstarter campaign, so I have had the watch for just about a whole year at this point.I do have to say I really love this watch. It gets a lot of attention, people are constantly asking about it. This isn't a motivator for me really, but it does show there is a real market for smart watches and the Pebble team had great timing.The Good:-The watch is easy to use-It is comfortable on your wrist-Easy to read indoors and out-Decent battery life-the battery usually lasts at least 5 days for me when I forget and let it run out of energyThe Bad:-You do need to remember to charge it-I have had some corrosion where the battery charger attaches, it wasn't too hard to clean it, but this really shouldn't have happened, this may be because I was a VERY early adopter and one would hope the refined manufacturing process would have addressed this by now-A kind of bad/but kindof my fault, I have one scratch on the watch face, which I felt when it happened, Gorilla Glass would be nice!The Could be better:-After a year the Pebble Team have just put out a new version of the software (Winter 2014) that is approaching what was promised upon creation of the project. Having developed software myself, I am sympathetic to how these kinds of projects can take longer than expected, but it sure would have been nice to see it move faster.If you are considering the Pebble, please be aware that it is a device designed to show you information on your wrist and there is no point in getting it you don't have an Android or iPhone to connect with. You can do a few interactions with it directly , but it is really more for showing useful information: one of my favorites is being able to read text-messages on my wrist and not need to reach for my phone unless they need a response.Many people who see it on my wrist ask if it is has a touch screen: no it is not, just the four buttons for interaction.I love the watch, I tend to abuse watches fairly severely and the Pebble has stood up to a fair amount of abuse, other than the single watch face scratch which was my fault, it appears pretty much brand new almost a whole year later! Highly recommended.

I go surfing with it twice a week and it still works perfectly.The smart watch seems a natural extension of the smart phone. I understand that some people don't "get" the idea of a smartwatch, so I'll explain why I wanted one. I have to stay connected and respond immediately as part of my job. I'm on work (and personal) chat and email continually throughout the day. If I'm in front of my computer, managing this is simple. But if I'm out and about I have to constantly reach for my phone to check notifications, many of which simply aren't important.Now I *could* (and have in the past) set up custom notifications so I know if the message is work or personal, chat or email, etc. But I've found this to be unwieldy and annoying. Also in many environments I simply don't hear/feel my phone notifications, or can't easily check them (driving).With the Pebble (or other smartwatch), I get my notifications on my wrist, which I can quickly and easily glance at without any reaching, clicking, unlocking, etc. I know instantly if I can ignore the message, or if I need to go to my phone, or to a computer, and take further action.Also, I regularly wear a watch and check the time frequently, so this serves that purpose as well.The Pebble is a watch first and foremost: it's waterproof to 50m (most other smartwatches are either water resistant or not even that), the display is easy to read and has many watchfaces available, and the battery lasts around a week (vs less than a day for most other current smartwatches). Most others have touchscreens but the Pebble only has buttons. No sound, but the vibration is very strong and impossible to miss (and discreet as opposed to sonic notifications). I find the fit to be comfortable and the size/protrusion are fine.Most of the one-star reviews I read on here were from Kickstarter supporters who were dissatisfied because their Pebbles were DOA or stopped working. I sympathize, and not being sure of Pebble's reliability I bought mine at Best Buy and got the extended (2-year) warranty for $20, so that solves the reliability issue.Out of the box Pebble will only handle notifications for a few of your phone's apps - default email, SMS, etc. If you're on Android you can download a number of companion apps that make it dead simple to receive all of your phone's notifications; from what I've read it's more difficult on iOS.My initial impression of the Pebble is excellent and I will update my review in the future.

This watch doesn't do everything, and it doesn't do everything it does do perfectly.  But it works well enough to be useful.  If you're looking to replicate the smartphone experience on your wrist, pick a different smartwatch.  But if you want something that will move some of the more mundane tasks off your smartphone and into a more readily accessible location, this is a good buy.As another reviewer has said, DO NOT pay more than $150 for this watch--if it's priced above that, you're just lining the pockets of a third-party reseller.  If Amazon isn't selling it, just go to getpebble.com.My job requires me to use a six-digit passcode on my iPhone (or carry a separate device for work emails).  The Pebble lets me triage emails and text messages to see whether it's worth pulling my phone out of my pocket.  Over the course of a day and a hundred emails, that's a pretty significant time saver.  That, in itself, would make this worthwhile for me.Having weather on the watchface (which will require you to download one of the multitude of watchfaces that offer this feature--I like Modern and Futura Weather) has also been great over the course of a blustery spring during which the temperature has been swinging like a drug-addled pendulum.  That said, I'd like the feature a lot better if it were drawing from a better source.  The watchface apps draw from, I believe, an open-source weather site that, for Washington D.C. and for the last couple of weeks, at least, has been between five and ten degrees off the actual temperature.  Still, having a ballpark and knowing if it's raining outside reduce the number of mornings I have to schlep back up to my apartment to get an umbrella.Your mileage may vary on the apps, but I have yet to find one that's terribly useful.  The Runkeeper companion screen (it's not really an app) is pretty useful for keeping track of how long, how far, and how fast you're running, if you're into that sort of thing.Pebble Cards has promise, but it's brutally slow.  Yelp seems decent except that I usually want more information than could fit on a watch face so I use my phone for that anyway.  Still, since app development uses a pretty common language and Pebble is all about experimentation and homebrew software, I expect we'll start seeing some clever uses of the tech over the next year.Also, it strikes me as borderline ridiculous that there's no built-in battery monitor--you will want to install one in one of your eight slots first thing.  The battery life has been decent--4-5 days seems to be about the limit for a charge, and I usually just charge it every other night.Again, make sure you understand what it can and can't do up front.  If you go in with reasonable expectations, the Pebble won't disappoint.

reviewText: At the time of writing it has been announced that at the end of January there will be the release of firmware 2.0 for the watch which allows back and forth communication between the watch and the phone to allow data to be shared. Right now, iOS cannot send data to the watch so programmers are having to circumvent this but using the music app to send data (with the exception of notifications, those work). It should also be noted that this was bought at the same time the new steel watch was being sold. The "upgrades" are a gorilla glass screen, metal features and a smaller bezel. For $100 more, this does not add much. If you want a metal face then pay for it but you don't need to worry about the screen scratching and thus the gorilla glass isn't really needed. I've had plenty of scrapes and bumps to test this out with. The screens are the same size so if the metal one looks bigger its only perception due to the bezel. Remember, you can always add a new watch band onto this model as long as it's 22mm, so pick a color and change the band and save some money.This section is iOS onlyPros:-all notifications can be pushed to the watch so the phone can always be silent-with update 1.31 it uses LE bluetooth so there isn't much battery drain. If you think ifs eating a lot of power try turning off wifi. That'll help-comfortable, the silicone band doesn't chafe-unlike metal backed watches the backing doesn't react with skin to produce as much odor even if worn continuously-low profile-speedy refresh times on the screen, even though it is e-paper, there is almost instantaneous updating of the screen. Most of the wait time is waiting for the app to send the notification to the watch-good back-light (defaulted to shake motion) allows for night use.-fully customize-able with apps or hand coding (plenty of tutorials and forums out there)-there is almost no processing to be done so it is very fast in comparison to other smart watches-waterproof to 50mcons:-no talk-back between the devices (to be fixed by Feb. with firmware)-no unified collection of apps (to be fixed by Feb. with new app/appstore) or way to manage updates-(technical) there is no current management of memory so you can have about 8 apps on the watch at a time (the app on the phone can send the app to the watch when needed) but this should be fixed with the Feb. update-(app based) the current app doesn't manage memory on the phone so you must continuously kill apps to keep data being sent to the watch. Good practice to learn to keep battery higher and background processes low. Once the apps get managed by the  new appstore by Feb. the memory management and allocation should get fixed.

reviewText: This can best be described as a Remote and another Display for your phone. The functionality rely's heavily on the phone to handle the work, and this just mainly just controls your phone and displays your information from your phone. (like displays emails, any notification from any app that might appear, it also shows you who's calling and allows you to accept or hangup)The watch has 8 "slots" where you can load up different watch faces and apps to it via an iphone or android app. You can store more than 8 on your phone and load and unload pretty easy.I mainly where this when during the workday, when I'm away from my desk. So that, when I'm not working, I don't have to see emails come in.  Also, you can use it to see whos calling and cancel the call real easy, rather than rooting through your pocket or bag.I love all the different watch faces. There are only a few cool apps that I've found, but more are constantly being added. For example, like the foursquare app lets you check-in from your wrist.the bluetooth works extremely well, the watch always seems to connect without any effort on my part.You can also trick this out with custom watch bands and skins. I really like the James Bond watch strap. It's a version of the22mm NATO strap http://www.amazon.com/s/ref=bl_sr_watches?ie=UTF8&field-brandtextbin;=22mm+NATO+strap&node;=377110011These are really easy to swap out, so I have 3 of them with different colors/styles.also, there are some great wraps like this one:http://www.amazon.com/Brushed-Onyx-Wrap-Pebble-Watch/dp/B00IAOS7PShighly recommend!

You may be saying to yourself...why do I need a smart watch when I can just pull out my phone? or...Why should I get a Pebble when there are more fancy smart watches out there?For one, sometimes pulling your phone out can be rude or not allowed. If you are on a date, in a meeting, at work, etc...or your phone may just be in a bag or in another room. The Pebble is also waterproof, which means you can swim with it, you can shower with it. What other way can you say you can read texts in the shower? You can also use the music controls to change songs if your phone is hooked up to a stereo or dock remotely, and with third-party apps you can adjust the volume as well. I also find that the vibration on the watch is always noticable, whereas sometimes moving around a lot you can't feel a phone vibrate in your pocket.The e-paper display means you won't need to be charging it by the end of the day like color-screen smart watches, and it only needs a charge every 5-7 days. Of course if you have a lot of third-party apps, you may not get quite as much so keep that in mind. The e-paper display also means that your watch face will always be there, unlike other smart watches that auto-shutoff to conserve battery. What's the point of wearing a watch with a blank screen? Another point about the battery is that I now silence and disable vibrate on my phone and rely solely on my watch for notifications now, which means I'm saving a little battery on my phone, surely enough to make up for the 5-10% battery usage that the bluetooth connection draws in a day.Along with multiple color Pebble watches, there are countless watch face designs to suit everybody: digital, analog, modern, classic, abstract, video game themed, etc and they install in a snap.By default you can read sms, email, phone call, Facebook, Google Talk/Hangouts, and calendar notifications, but with third-party apps you can get every notification from any app on your phone and with texts you can even send customized preset texts back. You can control music, and with third-party apps also volume and more music providers. There are also other apps for weather stocks, and more and half the fun is discovering them and tweaking everything.The fact that it's only $150 dollars doesn't hurt either. And BEWARE of people looking to take advantage of you. The Pebble is sold out on the official website but Best Buy has a TON of them. Don't give these people twice what the watch is worth, just head to your local Best Buy!The one thing I will say is that if you have an iPhone...you may want to pass on the Pebble. The iPhone is just not as compatible like Android phones are and you'll find you are missing some features and compatibility.
summary: Why a smart watch? Here's why.
