reviewText: I love this watch. It does everything I wanted and more. With all the apps it can only get better.

This watch is great. I can never hear notifications from my phone when its in my pocket and this allows me to see them all and decide whether I need to pull my phone out to respond. Its also helped break my habit to constantly check my phone when I am out, because I know immediately when I get an email, txt, or call.

Some bugs that go along with any first generation technology, but this is hands down the most useful watch I've ever owned. I love not having to take my phone out to check every little beep and ping. Also, the music remote control is great for when I'm driving in the car (when it works at least). It's not the fanciest smartwatch on the market currently, but I believe it's the most functional and useful. Those who aren't early adopters or aren't willing to deal with the inherent bugs in a first generation technology may want to wait for the next generation.
summary: An excellent first generation device for early adopters

reviewText: I ordered this watch and used it for 2 months. It stopped syncing with my bluetooth and I tried reseting it and deleting all of the apps on my iPhone and reinstalling them. Nothing worked. It is now shut off and is sitting in a drawer. It was one of the worst purchases I ever made on Amazon and I cannot return after 30 days of use.When it was working, it malfunctioned regularly. I would NOT recommend that anyone purchase this item.

Purchased this for my daughter for Christmas 2013, it is amazing. She wears it at school and is allowed to view her texts during lunch. It has saved us on many missed pick ups. The Pebble allows downloads and customizing which is amazing. The red is a great color and is not common if you want to start a trend. I highly recommend this unit. The seller sent the item quickly.

People ask me in meetings ALL the time now, "are you getting your email on your watch?!?!?  I have GOT to get one of those!"  It's probably a daily occurrence these days.Pebble is exactly what it is advertised to be, a smartwatch.  Do not misunderstand, the watch is EXTREMELY reliant on your smart phone, but who doesn't have a smart phone?  it has a very noticeable vibration mechanism for incoming calls, emails, texts, etc. and a recent update has made those notifications more customizable.  There are more downloadable watch faces than I can count AND you can make your own (I made one with a picture of my family in the background, even with the epaper display the picture looks really good).  You can control music, read emails, read texts, control incoming calls (answer, deny, etc), it has saved me from missing countless meetings and phone calls (left my cell phone at my desk or something).  I don't carry my cell phone around my house any longer because the range essentially reaches my entire house if my phone is in my kitchen (I have a 3000 sq foot, 2 story home for reference).It doesn't have a camera, it's not a color display, it's not really a device on it's own like the Samsung watch, that's a very different animal, so don't expect that.  What it does do however, it does extremely well.Again, couldn't be happier with the watch (got mine on Kickstarter so I've been wearing it for some time now) and wouldn't hesitate to buy as a cool gadget gift for a techy friend.Oh, also, battery life is excellent, even with the vibration notification happening regularly.
summary: Couldn't be Happier, GREAT gadget, but know what it is and exactly how it does what it does before you buy it!

The main point of the watch is bluetooth connectivity and it fails at that.  I only gave it 2 stars because of the independent apps in it.  I've owned the watch for about 2 weeks and the customer service is terrible.  They only have the ability to email and all they say is, "our engineers are working on an update and we found that there is a bug."  If there is no update in 1 more week I'm returning it and updating the review to 1 star. reviewText: My husband got these via Kickstarter, where we were promised the sun, moon, and stars.  We use Apple and while we understand that the watch has better functionality with Android than it does Apple, we did not get nearly what the creators promised.  If you invested in a company that did so poorly, the SEC would investigate.The only thing this watch does for me, besides tell time, is sometimes but not always show text messages and it IDs incoming calls.  My husband has better functionality because...let's just say his apple device is different than mine.Pebble does not acknowledge tweets.  If you send an error report, they reply with a canned response that doesn't address your specific problem.  They further warn you that sending more than one message about your malfunction will only delay their response.They just released a new operating system.  Pebble sent me 7 notifications in 2 days about it.  I was in Yosemite, with limited internet and phone connectivity.  Updating the watch's OS was not my priority.  One notification will suffice!  I revoked their permission to send me notifications.When I tried to update the OS after returning to the connected world, the update failed repeatedly.  My husband also had to try repeatedly but his at least happened.You have to charge this watch...great, I needed another device to charge.  This means I leave my $150 watch home frequently because it's charging.  Also when I first had the watch, I used a white watch face, which drained the battery in a couple days, not the five or six that Pebble promised.  Charging sucks a lot of power out of your ports and it is slow.  If the watch isn't fully charged it may die before you get it back on the juice.  Sometimes for me, the charge only lasted a few hours after being connected for many.  My husband had to buy a new charging port that runs off our house electricity to charge these watches.

reviewText: It works very well if you want text and phone notifications. If you want the apps to work, you would want to read my review!!When ordering this, be aware that this is a kickstarter backed project, which means it is still in the developing process and not as user friendly for non-computer nerds. Do this and it will save you hours of wondering why nothing works other than text and phone calls.2. The PEBBLE app have A LOT (yes a lot) of kinks! This is good if you are a developer or know how to make your own app but I am not that tech savvy. The pebble app is slow ...very very slow! TO AVOID SPENDING HOURS ON THIS SLOW APP, GO TO MYPEBBLEFACES. It is like itunes!3. mypebblefaces serves as a MUCH faster filter. Hours saved! I cannot emphasize that enough!Now, you can edit what you see on your screen such as music, calendar, reminders.. etc..Side note:My ordered my pebble from amazon and not amazon warehouse but I see that my item is definitely a returned item. There was no plastic protectors no twist ties and not neatly stored in its package. Don't let other reviews sway you to only order from amazon.Recommended Improvements:1. volume control integration for music2. faster and more organized pebble app downloads3. functional customer service. live support with a telephone number4. better setup instructions for applications

Swap it out. Tired of the wrist strap? Swap it out. Tired of the border around the screen? Slap a new face over it. The Pebble never gets stale.Battery life is also very impressive. After doing a lot of research on the latest smart watches and anticipating the release of any up and coming wearable technologies; I decided on the Pebble.My needs were clear before I purchased and they were as follows:1. The device needed to have a long battery life (at least 5 days)2. The device needed to provide silent notifications (Text, Reminders, Phone, Calendar, etc.)3. The device needed to work with an iOS device (e.g. Apple)4. The device needed to be a light weight product with a relatively low purchase price.It was important to outline my expectations before I purchased as I have seen a number of reviewers of various smart watches rate their device low due to an absent expected feature and the device manufacturer never intended to provide that certain feature.------My pebble came in early and I took the advice of others and ordered a Skinomi Screen protector as well as another watch band for comfort (Watch Experts - 22MM - Model number PU66).The packaging was good quality and it arrived without damage; after I installed the watch band and screen protector; I immediately charged my Pebble. It didn't take long to charge and the cable magnetically snapped into the Pebble very conveniently.  I've heard of some complaining about the strength of the magnet to hold in place and I found the cable to be very sufficient to charge the device without coming loose. My Pebble charged in about 1 hour with a 2.1 Amp adaptor.  For the first week, I was using an iPhone 4 and one week later, my company upgraded me to a iPhone 5c so I have experience with both devices.The Pebble connected to both the iPhone 4 and iPhone 5c without any problems.  You have to do some digging and you will find the iPhone 4 is limited in its functionality with the Pebble since the iPhone 4 does not have Bluetooth LE capabilities and the Notification Center and the Pebble require Bluetooth LE to fully function.  With that being said, I was still able to get Text & Phone notifications to populate into my Pebble.  Once I received my iPhone 5c, I was able to get everything to fully function; if a notification can display on the 'screen lock notification,' it can display on the Pebble.  I really liked the ability to get notifications on my watch as I do not notice them when my phone is in my pocket and have missed a number of important texts in the past.  This was my most needed attribute for purchasing a smart watch. Another unexpected feature is the distance of the bluetooth connection...I can have my phone downstairs and still receive notifications to the top floor of my house.  Many of the watch-face applications have a 'vibrate on bluetooth disconnect' which is handy to remember to bring your phone with you.  I travel a lot and almost forgot to bring my phone with me the other day.  I got about 45 feet away from my quarters and my watched vibrated letting me know that the connection to my phone was cut.  I knew immediately that I forgot my phone.  I also like the alarm feature on the watch and can set multiple alarms that do not bother my sleeping wife.  I also am fond of the built-in music controller as I find myself controlling my iPhone's music in my hotel room for convenience or while running on the treadmill.The Pebble Application: The Pebble App must be running for most of the watch features to work.  The app is getting better but it could stand some improvement as many of the apps are a novelty and do not work consistently; for example, to date I've tried ALL the GPS apps and they are very buggy and stop working after a brief period of time.  Most of the watch faces work flawlessly (my favorite is 'Real Weather').  There are a number of apps that are very useful so please don't think I'm communicating a black cloud over the app.  Some of the quality apps that I use a lot are: 'bike+', 'Runkeeper', 'Flight Track', 'Pebble Bucks', 'Pebble Cards', 'Battery Life', 'Multi Timer', 'Evernote', 'Package Trackr' and Weather. They are all fun to use and reliable.The screen is in greyscale and very sharp; the backlit portion functions well; however, I found the battery to drain much faster with it on (up to three days shorter).  It might be the way I walk and move as any quick motions of the wrist can turn the backlight on.  Since I don't need the light during the day, I have this feature off most of the time. The watch weight is light and not too big for my wrist which is important as I didn't want a lot of extra bulk on my arm.  I can easily get 5-7 days of life when I have the backlight feature disabled and 4 days with the backlight feature turned on.Finally, if you're keeping track of my expectations; I have one more expectation to comment on.  The device must be relatively low cost.  I purchased my Pebble for just under $135; I didn't go for the Pebble Steel as I wanted try the less expensive option first.  I am very pleased with the looks of the my black Pebble.  I never get compliments on my watches and have received a number of comments on its looks.  I shower with my watch with no problems (even with the screen protector).  This little gadget is a great addition for the frequent traveler.  It has so many plusses that they outweigh some of the buggy 3rd party apps.  I expect them to get better over time and encourage you to grab a Pebble for yourself.
summary: Outstanding Smartwatch for iOS! (1 month post purchase review)

reviewText: Part of the display quit working after a little over a year. There is a thick black line across the middle of the display where the pixels appear to be dead. We would be more than happy to troubleshoot with you, however, we cannot offer you a replacement unit as it is now outside the one-year warranty period.While we can't replace your Pebble, it's possible for you buy a refurbished Pebble if you are interested, or you can purchase a new Pebble at the regular price any time at our website.Refurbished Pebbles cost $100, plus whatever shipping method you choose (prices range between $5 and $50 depending on your location). Refurbished Pebbles are fully functional and covered by our warranty, but may have minor cosmetic blemishes. In most cases, the blemishes can be fixed with screen polishes like Displex.Why would I spend money on this product again knowing what I know now??????UPDATE:  when I left this review, the Pebble people immediately emailed me and made it right!  They sent me a new watch.  So I changed my review from one star to five.

reviewText: I'm really surprised at the price of the Pebble on Amazon, especially considering how inexpensive it is at Best Buy.  Almost $100 less expensive right now.I just got the watch a little over a week ago, and when I purchased it, I had already upgraded my iPhone to iOS7.At first, it was monumentally annoying because every time it would disconnect and reconnect, all the alerts except for phone alert would become disabled.However, earlier this week, Pebble released 1.13 of the firmware, and now, the alerts come through all the time, throughout multiple disconnects and reconnects.There really isn't that much else to say about it.  It works, gets alerts, and simplifies customization of which apps give you alerts.One thing it doesn't do is let you scroll through some slightly older notifications.  When a notification is gone, it's gone, and you have to go to the phone to find it.  But sometimes, I have my phone in a zippered waist pouch with an external battery attached, so it would just be easier to flip through older notifications on the Pebble.Would also be nice if the Pebble could initiate some actions on the phone.  Like Cookoo can send a location-check-in for facebook.  If Pebble could do action initiations, it would be better.All in all, the watch is waterproof, lasts more than a weekend without charging, consistently gets alerts, lights up with a shake of the wrist, and is easy and intuitive to use.

reviewText: I work a job where I don't always have my phone accessible. So, I was excited to have a way to know when there was important info coming to my phone. When the Pebble arrived, I found the watch and a charging cord and little else. I went to the website, and still gathered little information on how to make everything work. It took 2 days and many related web searches to figure out how to get the watch and the phone to sync. Then it took several attempts to get everything to actually work.  I will have to admit, the Pebble worked well for about 2 weeks. Since then, the reliability is not good. It won't hold a charge for more than a few hours and the screen is unreadable with lines running through it. I paid about $150.00 for the Pebble, and hate feeling like that is an expendable sum. I would not recommend the purchase of a Pebble, unless you like throwing your money to the wind.

Forget the other smarthwatches with cameras and color touchscreens (really? a touchscreen that's barely bigger than your fingertip?), the Pebble is THE smart watch. Designed from the start to blend in rather than stand out, it's waterproof, the battery lasts for a full week, and you use it just like a normal watch, with the buttons on the side.But that's where the similarities end. You can control your phone's music, add custom watchfaces, even read texts and see who's calling. And it's that last part that makes it. I can't tell you how much less I worry about missing a text or call with the Pebble. Before, I'd constantly have to switch my phone between vibrate (for classes) and ring (for walking around and at home). Now, I haven't taken my phone off vibrate since I got the pebble.Plus, smarthwatches are still new enough that they're a great conversation starter. Someone will notice you playing with your watch, do a double take, and then their eyes pop!I'll admit, I would like it if the screen was color and a bit higher resolution - but only if it stays as an e-ink screen. Because that's another benefit - you can still read it in the sun, and if it's dark, all you have to do is flick your wrist to activate the backlight!Overall, I love it. Would buy again!

This watch is not for everyone.  If you're looking to be like Dick Tracy, then look somewhere else.  I was looking for a watch that would let me get discreet notifications without having to pull out my phone every time.  It lets me triage what I have to answer and what can wait.  Battery life is great.  I'm getting about 4-5 days per charge.  It's a really light watch so it feels more like a silicone bracelet than a watch.I don't look at my phone nearly as often.  My kids are old enough to notice how often I look at my phone and know when I'm not paying attention to them.  When I'm not on call, I just place my phone on the counter and play with the kids.  Any notifications are triaged quickly and most of the time, I don't have to touch my phone.Changing watch faces is really easy - just press one button.  There are a couple of good apps that offer hundreds of different watch faces that you can download for free.  Downloading is really easy.  Change watch faces to fit your mood.I found that controlling my music from the watch is more convenient than I could have imagined.  Forward, back, and pause.  Anything else would be more easily done on your phone.  While driving, I just press a button without having to take my eyes off the road to go to the next song.Some reviewers have complained about the watch kicking off other bluetooth devices.  I did not find that to be the case.  My iphone 5 had no problem staying connected with both the Pebble and the car's bluetooth.A couple of minor complaints.  The resolution is the watch's weakest feature, but I will sacrifice some resolution for the long battery life.  Sometimes when the sun is shining at an angle to the watch, the light refracts and distorts the display a bit.One of the more pleasant effects since having the watch is that I no longer have the phantom vibration feeling in my leg thinking that my phone just vibrated.  Well worth the price.  Future versions can only improve on what is a fantastic watch thus far.

Otherwise it might be a little too much buzzing for your liking for example if you want a notification to show up without any buzzing like some whatsapp group notifications you're out of luck.The apps mostly work great and allows me to generate one time authentication codes for services supported by google's authenticator app, check into foursquare with spoon. Smartwatch+ allows me to see if I've got mail or texts and control my music all without having to remove my phone from my pocket.The coolest app would be swimio which allows me to track my laps in the pool. As an avid swimmer it is a great app if it actually makes it out of beta. Now it is still a little finicky and doesn't track my laps without any errors yet.As my phone is jailbroken it allows me to have notifications muted on the watch if I'm using the phone or removes the need for any passcode if my watch is within range of my phone which I think is a great feature.I get lots of notifications everyday and with all that buzzing it still manages to last 4 days on average before charging is requiredUltimately if you're willing to spend some time setting up your watch and are using an android or jailbroken iphone I would highly recommend this to you. It may not be super revolutionary yet but I think for less than $150 the amount of utility it provides is worth the price. If you're on an unjailbroken iphone you might get reduced utility but I would say that it is still a good buy. It is definitely the ecosystem to beat for smartwatches out there at this point of time.The only thing I feel is poor about this watch is the material of the face. Review of: Vantasy Classic Antique Roman Half Hunter Black Steel Metal Hollow Skeleton Pocket Watch.I purchased this watch because I wanted a mechanical pocket watch.  For the price I am amazed at the level of quality.  The weight is proper for a mechanical watch.  It does not feel cheap.  The watch cover face opens and closes very smooth.  The mechanics of cogs and mechanism can be viewed through the front and back.  The only error is the Roman Numeral four (4) is represented as IIII instead of IV.  I have not researched the history of watches from the 19th Century where perhaps this was common or not.  After receiving it I set the time and wound the spring.  I have monitored the time for twenty-four hours and the time has kept pace with digital time losing probably only seconds, if any.  Another positive factor is that the watch has a sweeping second hand.  That is a nice touch and was indicative of the more expensive pocket watches from days gone by.  The color is an antiqued brown for both the watch and chain fob.  For those interested in timepieces or for any other reason this watch is a good buy.

I didn't realize the total Zen of having an uncluttered, very clear, understated and functionally-oriented timepiece. Many other designs have their clarity compromised for chronometers, functions, or just style, and this one used the simplicity and functionality as style.I found it to be a great mid-size watch neither too big or small on an average wrist. The build quality is solid and crisp - the offset winder is really nice for not jabbing into a flexed wrist. The NATO strap is well made and the metal work on it is substantial. The case itself is brushed stainless with just the right understated look. The lume works for at least 4-5 hours in practice, with more brightness ont the hands than the numbers, as is standard. I thought i'd miss some kind of indiglo-type function, but that requires two hands to read the time and drains a battery. The flat, flush mineral crystal has not shown any tendency to scratch.The second hand is not quite aligned with the chapter marks - not a big deal. The large date window showing yesterday and today may seem silly but it really does help register the date more quickly.The screw-down crown is substantial and marked with the company logo, as is the strap buckle. All in all it looks like a watches sold for more than 3 times the price.And it's designed in Canada, one of the few.Basically, this watch could be priced $100 higher with no-one questioning that, so it is a no-brainer.

The band is comfortable after initial break-in.I would have given it 5 stars but the lume does not charge by normal daylight use.  It will charge by a flashlight and is very bright when you you charge it that way.  A 10 minute charge fades in less than 30 minutes.  If you need to have it visible at night, consider a different watch.

I bought this bag for an NFL game in an outdoor stadium. I was concerned about exposing my camera to inclement weather since camera bags are not allowed. I thought this bag would be great to offer protection from the elements if needed. I chose this particular bag over its competition because of the messenger bag strap. Since blankets and jackets have to be carried in, I wanted my hands free and trying to have a bag shoved in your armpit is just too cumbersome.The bag arrived today. It's of average quality and smells like PVC, which is to be expected. The messenger strap is nice, though I think it could stand to be a hair longer. Cross body, it hits me on between the belly and hip, rather than at the hip.The biggest complaint I have about this bag is that the zipper doesn't completely close the bag. A good 2" at least on both sides are left open. So the zipper will prevent most things from rolling out, but it doesn't completely seal the bag from the elements, nor will it keep small things from falling out.It's a strange design. Theoretically, I can see how you could stuff the bag a little more this way and it might put less stress on the zipper, but on the other hand, if it doesn't seal the bag, doesn't that defeat the purpose?As long as you're aware of that issue, it's a decent bag. But if you need your bag to be sealed, this isn't the one.We were successfully admitted to Lambeau Field under 2013 rules with these bags (one for my husband and one for me). In one, we fit 2 Snuggies rolled tightly, a hat, and gloves, and in the other we fit 2 scarves, another hat and gloves, medicine we needed, a windbreaker, a small camera, and a wallet, and had plenty of extra room for more items, if we had had them.

reviewText: I bought this watch to replace the Suunto vector that I have owned for 14 years.  It had finally started to leak and was no longer operational.  i have always liked Casios although I have never owned a triple sensor.  I paid close to $300 for it and it showed up in great condition and very timely.  Some of the features have left me missing the Suunto brand and I may switch back.  There are too many modes to scroll through to get through them all.  I have a whole sunset sunrise screen and a snooze alarm screen.  Really?  Is this a needed feature?  My Suunto had a light that could be turned on and it would stay on for an extended amount of time and even let you scroll through other screens to say set your alarm for the next day while lying in your sleeping bag after a long day.  The Suunto had a robust plastic body that shed plenty of bumps and drops without losing color.  The Casio seems to have a painted metal bezel that may chip and begin to show a worn look after a few adventures.  Lastly, it is atomic and keeps exact time, so for those of us that like to set the watch ahead to be on time, no such luck.  It tells the time it is told.  I do think hope that the solar feature will keep the battery going strong for a much longer time than the Suunto which was one of its cons.  Maybe the long light time on the Suunto comes with that price.  Bottom line, I still have a few test days left before I have to make a decision whether or not I will keep it.  Thank you Amazon.

reviewText: No complaints!  This is a great bag. It's relatively light weight and best of all the strap is wide enough that it grips and stays on my shoulder if I'm not wearing it cross body. I've considered buying a slightly smaller water bottle for a bit more space though.  The pockets and places to store little items are plentiful with two inside zippers and one small outside zipper.  The back snap pocket is perfect for frequently used items such as a phone.I'm thoroughly impressed by the water resistance of the outside; a heavy downpour caught me and the outside of my bag was drenched, but its contents was dry.  Finally, I'm surprised by how much I like the magnetic closure.  I worried it wouldn't be strong enough to keep the flap closed, but if the flap catches, the magnet draws it closed again.There's only one downside: The strap, while it doesn't loosen, rubs on my neck.  There isn't any padding along the entire strap which is fine when I wear a t-shirt or jacket, but it's a bit uncomfortable with a tanktop.Overall though, an outstanding bag!!  I highly recommend :)

if it's actually cashmere. The label says 100 percent cashmere, made in Scotland. It's soft and warm. I recently saw a real cashmere scarf somewhere for $100--same color, looked like the same scarf.

Beware of buying these scarves from sellers on Amazon and on ebay. They are not Cashmere but some type of synthetic material. I don't think most of the sellers realize this...but their supplier does, I'm sure! These scarves should be described as "Soft as Cashmere" or "Cashmere Like" but not saying "100% Cashmere" made in Scotland no less! Thousands of these have been sold so please beware. When I received mine I didn't think it looked like or felt like real Cashmere so I tested the tip of the fringe by burning it...it melted into a hard ball of plastic and smelled like plastic burning...not how real wool would smell or burn. reviewText: Many things you get from China are poorly made and you buy them understanding that you are trying to spend as little as possible with the hopes that it may JUST work.  This is not one of those items.  It feels very well made, looks very nice, and the closure works better than any other watch band I have had.  Especially given the price, if you need a watch band, just get this one.  I'm no expert and I can't say if it will fit every watch, but I bought the curved version and it fit my watch perfectly.  "Curved," for the record, seems to be referring to the taper of the band, wherein the links start largest at the watch face and grow smaller as they reach the closure.  The measurement given (mine was 22mm) refers to the part you need it to refer to - the watch face where you will pop out the spring bars that attach to the largest (22mm) links.  Don't worry about the curved version's size variation throwing you off.  Now, if I can just figure out how to replace the links to size it right (the links don't have arrows, unless I'm not seeing them).Update:  Scratch that.  The band just fell apart on me at work for no particular reason whatsoever, and it was a link I did not adjust or tinker with in any way.

I bought this watch mostly for long range rifle shooting.  It has every environmental input I need except wind speed/direction.  The temperature is off (usually 8-10 deg high), but my anemometer that I use to get the wind speed gives accurate temperature.  So that was not a problem to me.  Below I rated each feature 1-10:CLOCK  - 10: it works.2ND CLOCK  - 10: cool feature, especially if you travel to different time zones from home.TIMER  - 10: convenient compared to using a chronograph backwards.CHRONO  - 10: works as advertised.ALARM  - 10: works as advertised.WEATHER  - 8: cool feature and as accurate as a watch can be, I'd still check the weather channel though.THERMO  - 2: don't buy for this feature.  I guess it gives you a ball park idea of the temperature.ALTIMETER  - 9: big buying point for me and is pretty accurate.  It changes +/- 2-5 feet from day to day standing in the same spot in my house.  But 2-5 feet isn't a big deal.ALT TRACKER- 9: cool/useful feature (I set it for the altitude I zero'd my rifle at).  Same small problem as the Altimeter.BAROMETER  - 10: I haven't checked the accuracy of it, but it seems to be close.  For my application, I don't care about if it's off as long as it's consistently off (bc I only care about changes in barometric pressure, not the actual value).COMPASS  - 10: VERY accurate. It has 2 methods of calibrating that can be done in unison with each other for further accuracy.BACK LIGHT  - 9: It is dimmer than the average watch, but I never have a problem seeing it any time of day.HISTORY  - 10: Shows history of barometer & altimeter for over 24hrs with a graph of the data.MANUAL  - 10: Broken down Barney style for every function and setting.  Very detailed and easy to use.DURABILITY  - 9: I have not had it long enough to damage it, but my initial assessment is that if you don't beat it, it won't break for no good reason.OPTIONS  - 10: It has settings to change to every unit readable.  Temp - C/F; Time - 12h/24h; Date - DDMM/MMDD; Barometer - inhg/mb/hpa; Altimeter - feet/meters; Display - many, many possibilities.I couldn't be happier with this watch and would expect to pay $150+ for an equal watch.  I highly recommend it.  Plus I like how it looks, but you should make that opinion on your own.
